entries.zh: 天凤中，黄山宫有死龙，汉兵诛莽而世祖复兴，此易代之征也。
entries.en: During Wang Mang's Tianfeng reign a dead dragon appeared at Huangshan Palace; Han armies overthrew Mang and Guangwu restored the house—such a corpse foretells the turning of the cosmic mandate.
entries.literal: In the Tianfeng era, at Huangshan Palace there was a dead dragon; Han troops executed Mang and the Shizu restored the rise—this is a sign of change of mandate.

entries.zh: 至建安二十五年，魏文帝代汉。
entries.en: In Jian'an 220, Cao Pi of Wei ended the Han and took the throne for himself.
entries.literal: Down to the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an, Wei Wendi replaced Han.

entries.zh: 恒阴，中兴以来无录者。
entries.en: Cases of prolonged unbroken overcast have not been entered in the record since Guangwu restored the dynasty.
entries.literal: As for unbroken overcast, since the restoration there have been none recorded.

entries.zh: 永康元年八月，巴郡言黄龙见。
entries.en: In the eighth month of Yongkang 1 (167), Ba Commandery reported a yellow dragon sighting.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yongkang, Ba Commandery reported a yellow dragon seen.

entries.zh: 时，吏傅坚以郡欲上言，内白事以为走卒戏语，不可。
entries.en: When the commandery wanted to memorialize the event, clerk Fu Jian argued in an internal memo that it was nothing but barrack-yard gossip and should not be sent up.
entries.literal: At the time, the clerk Fu Jian, because the commandery wished to memorialize upward, on internal report of the matter held it to be runners' jesting talk and impermissible.

entries.zh: 太守不听，尝见坚语云：「时，民以天热，欲就池浴，见池水浊，因戏相恐，'此中有黄龙'，语遂行人间。
entries.en: The governor brushed him aside and later told Fu Jian what had really happened: "When the weather turned hot, people went to bathe in the pond; seeing the water muddy, they teased one another, 'There's a yellow dragon in here,' and the story spread among the townsfolk.
entries.literal: The governor would not listen; he once saw Jian and spoke, saying: "At the time, because the weather was hot, the people wished to bathe in the pool; seeing the pool water turbid, they in jest mutually frightened one another, 'Herein is a yellow dragon,' and the words then circulated among the people.

entries.zh: 闻郡欲以为美，故言。」
entries.en: Hearing that the commandery wished to take it as an auspicious sign, they spoke accordingly."
entries.literal: Hearing that the commandery wished to take it as auspicious, therefore they spoke."

entries.zh: 时，史以书帝纪。
entries.en: Nevertheless the court scribes entered the story in the reign annals as fact.
entries.literal: At the time, the scribes wrote it in the emperor's annals.

entries.zh: 桓帝时政治衰缺，而在所多言瑞应，皆此类也。
entries.en: Under Emperor Huan the state ran down, yet every region rushed to report felicitous omens; most were fabrications of this sort.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Huan government declined and was deficient, yet everywhere many spoke of auspicious responses—all were of this class.

entries.zh: 又先儒言：瑞兴非时，则为妖孽。
entries.en: The classics also warn that a "lucky" sign appearing at the wrong moment is in truth an ill omen.
entries.literal: Moreover the earlier scholars said: when auspicious signs arise out of season, then they are prodigies.

entries.zh: 而民讹言生龙语，皆龙薛也。
entries.en: Street talk that "dragons" had been born was only another species of bogus dragon omen.
entries.literal: And the people's false words giving birth to talk of dragons—all are dragon xue.

entries.zh: 志第十七 五行五
entries.en: Treatise 17: The Five Phases, Part Five.
entries.literal: Treatise Seventeen: The Five Phases, Part Five.

entries.zh: 光武帝建武二年正月甲子朔，日有蚀之，在危八度。
entries.en: On the new moon, jiazi, in the first month of Jianwu 2 (26 CE), a solar eclipse occurred at eight degrees within the lodge Wei.
entries.literal: On the jiazi new-moon day of the first month in the second year of Jianwu of Emperor Guangwu, there was a solar eclipse, at eight degrees in Wei.

entries.zh: 《日蚀说》曰：「日者，太阳之精，人君之象。
entries.en: The Treatise on Solar Eclipses reads: "The sun embodies supreme yang; it is the emblem of the sovereign.
entries.literal: The Treatise on Solar Eclipses says: "The sun is the essence of great yang, the image of the human ruler.

entries.zh: 君道有亏，有阴所乘，故蚀。
entries.en: When the ruler's conduct falls short, yin force overtakes the sun, and an eclipse follows.
entries.literal: The ruler's way having defect, yin rides upon it; therefore it eclipses.

entries.zh: 蚀者，阳不克也。」
entries.en: An eclipse means yang has lost its ascendancy."
entries.literal: Eclipse means yang does not overcome."

entries.zh: 其候杂说，《汉书·五行志》著之必矣。
entries.en: The assorted prognostic glosses are set out at length in the Han shu Treatise on the Five Phases.
entries.literal: As for the various predictive glosses, the Treatise on the Five Phases in the Han shu records them in full.

entries.zh: 儒说诸侯专权，则其应多在日所宿之国。
entries.en: Scholars hold that when regional lords seize unchecked power, the omen usually falls on the state whose celestial lodge the sun occupies.
entries.literal: Confucian explanation: when feudal lords monopolize power, then its responses are mostly in the state where the sun lodges.

entries.zh: 诸象附从，则多为王者事。
entries.en: When secondary portents cluster with the eclipse, they tend to concern the throne itself.
entries.literal: When various images attach and follow, then mostly they are matters of the king.

entries.zh: 人君改修其德，则咎害除。
entries.en: If the ruler mends his ways and cultivates virtue, the ill omen and its harm may be dispelled.
entries.literal: If the human ruler reforms and cultivates his virtue, then blame and harm are removed.

entries.zh: 是时，世祖初兴，天下贼乱未除。
entries.en: Guangwu had only just restored the dynasty; rebels still roamed the empire.
entries.literal: At this time the Shizu had first risen, and bandit turmoil under Heaven was not yet removed.

entries.zh: 虚、危，齐也。
entries.en: The lodges Xu and Wei correspond to the old territory of Qi.
entries.literal: Xu and Wei are Qi.

entries.zh: 贼张步拥兵据齐，上遣伏隆谕步，许降。
entries.en: The warlord Zhang Bu held Qi with an army; the emperor sent Fu Long to negotiate and accepted his offer to submit.
entries.literal: The bandit Zhang Bu held troops and occupied Qi; the sovereign sent Fu Long to instruct Bu, promising acceptance of surrender.

entries.zh: 旋复叛称王，至五年中乃破。
entries.en: He soon rebelled again, proclaimed himself king, and was not crushed until mid–Jianwu 5.
entries.literal: Soon he again rebelled and declared himself king; down to the middle of the fifth year he was then broken.

entries.zh: 三年五月乙卯晦，日有蚀之，在柳十四度。
entries.en: At month's end on yimao in the fifth month of Jianwu 3 (27), the sun was eclipsed at fourteen degrees in Liu.
entries.literal: On the last day yimao of the fifth month of the third year, there was a solar eclipse, at fourteen degrees in Liu.

entries.zh: 柳，河南也。
entries.en: Liu maps to the Henan region south of the Yellow River.
entries.literal: Liu is Henan south of the river.

entries.zh: 时，世祖在雒阳，赤眉降贼樊崇谋作乱，其七月发觉，皆伏诛。
entries.en: The emperor was at Luoyang when Fan Chong of the surrendered Red Eyebrows plotted a coup; the plot surfaced in the seventh month and the conspirators were put to death.
entries.literal: At the time the Shizu was in Luoyang; the surrendered Red Eyebrow bandit Fan Chong plotted rebellion; in the seventh month it was discovered, and all were executed.

entries.zh: 六年九月丙寅晦，日有蚀之。
entries.en: At month's end on bingyin in the ninth month of Jianwu 6 (30), a solar eclipse occurred.
entries.literal: On the last day bingyin of the ninth month of the sixth year, there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 史官不见，郡以闻。
entries.en: Court astronomers missed it; word came in from a commandery.
entries.literal: The clerks of history did not see it; a commandery reported it.

entries.zh: 在尾八度。
entries.en: The sun stood at eight degrees in Wei.
entries.literal: It was at eight degrees in Wei.

entries.zh: 七年三月癸亥晦，日有蚀之，在毕五度。
entries.en: At month's end on guihai in the third month of Jianwu 7 (31), an eclipse fell at five degrees in Bi.
entries.literal: On the last day guihai of the third month of the seventh year, there was a solar eclipse, at five degrees in Bi.

entries.zh: 毕为边兵。
entries.en: Bi presages warfare on the frontier.
entries.literal: Bi is border troops.

entries.zh: 秋，隗嚣反，侵安定。
entries.en: That autumn Wei Xiao rose in revolt and struck into Anding.
entries.literal: In autumn Wei Xiao rebelled and invaded Anding.

entries.zh: 冬，卢芳所置朔方、云中太守各举郡降。
entries.en: In winter the puppet governors of Shuofang and Yunzhong whom Lu Fang had appointed surrendered their commands.
entries.literal: In winter the Shuofang and Yunzhong governors installed by Lu Fang each raised their commanderies and surrendered.

entries.zh: 光武建武七年四月丙寅，日有晕抱，白虹贯晕，在毕八度。
entries.en: On bingyin in the fourth month of Jianwu 7 (31), the sun wore a double halo pierced by a white rainbow at eight degrees in Bi.
entries.literal: On the bingyin day of the fourth month of the seventh year of Jianwu of Guangwu, the sun had a halo with embrace; a white rainbow pierced the halo; it was at eight degrees in Bi.

entries.zh: 毕为边兵。
entries.en: Bi again betokened frontier arms.
entries.literal: Bi is border troops.

entries.zh: 秋，隗嚣反，侵安定。
entries.en: That autumn Wei Xiao rose and struck into Anding.
entries.literal: In autumn Wei Xiao rebelled and invaded Anding.

entries.zh: 十六年三月辛丑晦，日有蚀之，在昴七度。
entries.en: At month's end on xinchou in the third month of Jianwu 16 (40), the sun was eclipsed at seven degrees in Mao.
entries.literal: On the last day xinchou of the third month of the sixteenth year, there was a solar eclipse, at seven degrees in Mao.

entries.zh: 昂为狱事。
entries.en: Mao governs prisons and penal cases.
entries.literal: Mao is prison affairs.

entries.zh: 时诸郡太守坐度田不实，世祖怒，杀十余人，然后深悔之。
entries.en: Several commandery governors had falsified their land surveys; Guangwu flew into a rage and executed more than a dozen, then bitterly repented.
entries.literal: At the time various commandery governors sat guilty of untrue land measurement; the Shizu was angry and killed more than ten persons, afterward deeply regretting it.

entries.zh: 十七年二月乙未晦，日有蚀之，在胃九度。
entries.en: At month's end on yiwei in the second month of Jianwu 17 (41), an eclipse occurred at nine degrees in Wei.
entries.literal: On the last day yiwei of the second month of the seventeenth year, there was a solar eclipse, at nine degrees in Wei.

entries.zh: 胃为廪仓。
entries.en: Wei signifies the state granaries.
entries.literal: Wei is the granary.

entries.zh: 时诸郡新坐租之后，天下忧怖，以谷为言，故示象。
entries.en: Commanderies had just been fined for tax irregularities; the realm was anxious and talk ran to grain shortages—hence Heaven mirrored the distress in the sky.
entries.literal: At the time the various commanderies had newly suffered punishment over rent; all under Heaven was anxious and fearful, speaking in terms of grain; therefore it showed an image.

entries.zh: 或曰：胃，供养之官也。
entries.en: Others read Wei as the palace department that supplies the court.
entries.literal: Some say: Wei is the office of provision and support.

entries.zh: 其十月，废郭皇后，诏曰「不可以奉供养」。
entries.en: That tenth month Empress Guo was cast aside with an edict declaring her unfit to "maintain the ancestral sacrifices."
entries.literal: In that tenth month Empress Guo was deposed; an edict said "she cannot undertake provision and support."

entries.zh: 二十二年五月乙未晦，日有蚀之，在柳七度，京都宿也。
entries.en: At month's end on yiwei in the fifth month of Jianwu 22 (46), the sun was eclipsed at seven degrees in Liu—the lodge of the capital itself.
entries.literal: On the last day yiwei of the fifth month of the twenty-second year, there was a solar eclipse, at seven degrees in Liu, the capital's lodging.

entries.zh: 柳为上仓，祭祀谷也，近舆鬼，舆鬼为宗庙。
entries.en: Liu is the "upper granary" of ritual grain; it neighbors Yugi, the asterism of the ancestral shrine.
entries.literal: Liu is the upper granary, grain for sacrifice; it is near Yugi; Yugi is the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 十九年中，有司奏请立近帝四庙以祭之，有诏「庙处所未定，且就高庙袷祭之。」
entries.en: In the midst of the nineteenth year, responsible officials memorialized requesting to establish four temples to recent emperors to sacrifice to them; there was an edict: "The site of the temples is not yet fixed; for now perform the xia sacrifice at the High Temple."
entries.literal: In the midst of the nineteenth year, responsible officials memorialized requesting to establish four temples to recent emperors to sacrifice to them; there was an edict: "The site of the temples is not yet fixed; for now perform the xia sacrifice at the High Temple."

entries.zh: 至此三年，遂不立庙。
entries.en: Three years passed, and still no separate shrines were built.
entries.literal: From then three years passed, and temples were still not established.

entries.zh: 有简堕心，奉祖宗之道有阙，故示象也。
entries.en: The court had grown slack toward the ancestors; the rites owed to the imperial dead were neglected—hence the warning in the heavens.
entries.literal: There was neglect and slackness of mind; the way of honoring the ancestors had gaps; therefore it showed an image.

entries.zh: 二十五年三月戊申晦，日有蚀之，在毕十五度。
entries.en: At month's end on wushen in the third month of Jianwu 25 (49), an eclipse fell at fifteen degrees in Bi.
entries.literal: On the last day wushen of the third month of the twenty-fifth year, there was a solar eclipse, at fifteen degrees in Bi.

entries.zh: 毕为边兵。
entries.en: Again Bi pointed to frontier war.
entries.literal: Bi is border troops.

entries.zh: 其冬十月，以武谿蛮夷为寇害，伏波将军马援将兵击之。
entries.en: That winter, in the tenth month, Ma Yuan marched south against the Wuxi tribes who were plundering the border.
entries.literal: That winter in the tenth month, because the Wuxi Man and Yi were raiding harm, General Who Crosses the Waves Ma Yuan led troops to strike them.

entries.zh: 二十九年二月丁巳朔，日有蚀之，在东壁五度。
entries.en: On the new moon dingsi in the second month of Jianwu 29 (53), the sun was eclipsed at five degrees in Eastern Wall.
entries.literal: On the dingsi new-moon day of the second month of the twenty-ninth year, there was a solar eclipse, at five degrees in Eastern Wall.

entries.zh: 东壁为文章，一名娵訾之口。
entries.en: Eastern Wall governs letters and learning; it is also called the mouth of the Ju zi lunar mansion.
entries.literal: Eastern Wall is literary composition; one name is the mouth of Ju zi.

entries.zh: 先是皇子诸王各招来文章谈说之士，去年中，有人上奏：「诸王所招待者，或真伪杂，受刑罚者子孙，宜可分别。」
entries.en: The princes had been patronizing scholars and debaters; the year before, a memorial warned that their clients included descendants of convicted men and demanded a vetting process.
entries.literal: Earlier the imperial sons and various kings each summoned men of letters and disputers; in the previous year someone memorialized: "Those whom the kings entertain are sometimes mixed true and false; descendants of those who suffered punishment should be distinguished."

entries.zh: 于是上怒，诏捕诸王客，皆被以苛法，死者甚多。
entries.en: Enraged, Guangwu ordered a sweep of the princes' retainers; harsh statutes were applied and many died.
entries.literal: Thereupon the sovereign was angry, edicting to arrest the kings' guests; all were charged under harsh law, and the dead were very many.

entries.zh: 世祖不早为明设刑禁，一时治之过差，故天示象。
entries.en: Because he had not laid down clear rules in advance, the purge overshot its mark—so Heaven sent a sign.
entries.literal: The Shizu had not early set clear penal prohibitions; in one moment governance overshot; therefore Heaven showed an image.

entries.zh: 世祖于是改悔，遣使悉理侵枉也。
entries.en: He then relented and dispatched agents to redress every wrongful conviction.
entries.literal: The Shizu thereupon repented and sent envoys to fully rectify encroachments and wrongs.

entries.zh: 三十一年五月癸酉晦，日有蚀之，在柳五度，京都宿也。
entries.en: At month's end on guiyou in the fifth month of Jianwu 31 (55), an eclipse struck Liu at five degrees—the capital's own lodge.
entries.literal: On the last day guiyou of the fifth month of the thirty-first year, there was a solar eclipse, at five degrees in Liu, the capital's lodging.

entries.zh: 自二十一年示象至此十年，后二年，宫车晏驾。
entries.en: Ten years had passed since the omen of Jianwu 21; two years after this eclipse, Guangwu died.
entries.literal: From the twenty-first year's showing of image down to here ten years; after two years, the palace carriage delayed its departure (the emperor died).

entries.zh: 中元元年十一月甲子晦，日有蚀之，在斗二十度。
entries.en: At month's end on jiazi in the eleventh month of Zhongyuan 1 (56), the sun was eclipsed at twenty degrees in Dou.
entries.literal: On the last day jiazi of the eleventh month of the first year of Zhongyuan, there was a solar eclipse, at twenty degrees in Dou.

entries.zh: 斗为庙，主爵禄。
entries.en: Dou is the lodge of the ancestral shrine and of titles and stipends.
entries.literal: Dou is the temple; it governs enfeoffment and salary.

entries.zh: 儒说十一月甲子，时王日也，又为星纪，主爵禄，其占重。
entries.en: Scholars note that jiazi in the eleventh month is the "king" stem-branch day, and the month belongs to the Star Marker cycle—both tie to rank and revenue, so the omen weighed heavily.
entries.literal: Confucian explanation: eleventh month jiazi is the king day of the hour; it is also Star Marker; it governs enfeoffment and salary; its prognostication is weighty.

entries.zh: 明帝永平三年八月壬申晦，日有蚀之，在氐二度。
entries.en: At month's end on renshen in the eighth month of Yongping 3 (60), an eclipse occurred at two degrees in Di.
entries.literal: On the last day renshen of the eighth month of the third year of Yongping of Emperor Ming, there was a solar eclipse, at two degrees in Di.

entries.zh: 氐为宿宫。
entries.en: Di is the lodge of the ruler's sleeping quarters.
entries.literal: Di is the lodging palace.

entries.zh: 是时明帝作北宫。
entries.en: Emperor Ming was then raising the Northern Palace.
entries.literal: At this time Emperor Ming was building the Northern Palace.

entries.zh: 八年十月壬寅晦，日有蚀之，既，在斗十一度。
entries.en: At month's end on renyin in the tenth month of Yongping 8 (65), a total eclipse reached eleven degrees in Dou.
entries.literal: On the last day renyin of the eighth month of the eighth year, there was a solar eclipse; it was total, at eleven degrees in Dou.

entries.zh: 斗，吴也。
entries.en: Dou corresponds to the old state of Wu.
entries.literal: Dou is Wu.

entries.zh: 广陵于天文属吴。
entries.en: By celestial reckoning Guangling lies in the Wu sector.
entries.literal: Guangling in astronomical terms belongs to Wu.

entries.zh: 后二年，广陵王荆坐谋反自杀。
entries.en: Two years later Prince Jing of Guangling killed himself after a conviction for treason.
entries.literal: After two years Prince Jing of Guangling sat guilty of plotting rebellion and committed suicide.

entries.zh: 十三年十月甲辰晦，日有蚀之，在尾十七度。
entries.en: At month's end on jiachen in the tenth month of Yongping 13 (70), the sun was eclipsed at seventeen degrees in Wei.
entries.literal: On the last day jiachen of the tenth month of the thirteenth year, there was a solar eclipse, at seventeen degrees in Wei.

entries.zh: 十六年五月戊午晦，日有蚀之，在柳十五度。
entries.en: At month's end on wuwu in the fifth month of Yongping 16 (73), an eclipse fell at fifteen degrees in Liu.
entries.literal: On the last day wuwu of the fifth month of the sixteenth year, there was a solar eclipse, at fifteen degrees in Liu.

entries.zh: 儒说五月戊午，犹十一月甲子也，又宿在京都，其占重。
entries.en: Scholars liken wuwu in the fifth month to jiazi in the eleventh month, and Liu again marked the capital—so the portent was grave.
entries.literal: Confucian explanation: fifth month wuwu is like eleventh month jiazi; moreover the lodging is at the capital region; its prognostication is weighty.

entries.zh: 后二岁，宫车晏驾。
entries.en: Two years later Emperor Ming died.
entries.literal: After two years the palace carriage delayed its departure.

entries.zh: 十八年十一月甲辰晦，日有蚀之，在斗二十一度。
entries.en: At month's end on jiachen in the eleventh month of Yongping 18 (75), an eclipse occurred at twenty-one degrees in Dou.
entries.literal: On the last day jiachen of the eleventh month of the eighteenth year, there was a solar eclipse, at twenty-one degrees in Dou.

entries.zh: 是时，明帝既崩，马太后制爵禄，故阳不胜。
entries.en: Ming had just died, and Empress Dowager Ma held the power of appointments—yang, the masculine principle of rule, was eclipsed.
entries.literal: At this time Emperor Ming had already died; Empress Dowager Ma controlled enfeoffment and salary; therefore yang did not overcome.

entries.zh: 延光三年九月庚申晦，日有食之，在氐十五度。
entries.en: At month's end on gengshen in the ninth month of Yanguang 3 (124), an eclipse occurred at fifteen degrees in Di.
entries.literal: On the last day gengshen of the ninth month of the third year of Yanguang, there was a solar eclipse, at fifteen degrees in Di.

entries.zh: 氐为宿宫。
entries.en: Di is the lodge of the ruler's private apartments.
entries.literal: Di is the lodging palace.

entries.zh: 宫，中宫也。
entries.en: Here "palace" denotes the empress's domain at the center of the court.
entries.literal: Palace means the central palace.

entries.zh: 时上听中常侍江京、樊丰及阿母王圣等谗言，废皇太子。
entries.en: The emperor trusted Jiang Jing, Fan Feng, and his wet nurse Wang Sheng, believed their lies, and deposed the crown prince.
entries.literal: At the time the sovereign listened to the slanderous words of Regular Attendants Jiang Jing and Fan Feng and of his nurse Wang Sheng and others, and deposed the crown prince.

entries.zh: 四年三月戊午朔，日有蚀之，在胃十二度。
entries.en: On the new moon wuwu in the third month of Yanguang 4 (125), the sun was eclipsed at twelve degrees in Wei.
entries.literal: On the wuwu new-moon day of the third month of the fourth year, there was a solar eclipse, at twelve degrees in Wei.

entries.zh: 陇西、酒泉、朔方各以状上，史官不觉。
entries.en: Longxi, Jiuquan, and Shuofang all filed reports, yet the capital historians failed to note the eclipse.
entries.literal: Longxi, Jiuquan, and Shuofang each submitted situation reports upward; the clerks of history did not notice.

entries.zh: 志第十八 五行六
entries.en: Treatise 18: The Five Phases, Part Six.
entries.literal: Treatise Eighteen: The Five Phases, Part Six.

entries.zh: 〖临邑〗有沛庙。
entries.en: At Linyi stood a temple honoring the Marquis of Pei.
entries.literal: Linyi: it had a shrine to the Marquis of Pei.

entries.zh: 〖东莞〗有郓亭。左傳曰「公處鄆」。
entries.en: Dongguan held Yun Pavilion; the Zuo Tradition says, “The duke resided at Yun.”
entries.literal: Dongguan: it had Yun Pavilion. The Zuo Tradition says, “The duke resided at Yun.”

entries.zh: 有邳乡。
entries.en: Pi Township appears in the same note.
entries.literal: It had Pi Township.

entries.zh: 有公来山。
entries.en: Mount Gonglai rose in the county.
entries.literal: It had Mount Gonglai.

entries.zh: 或曰古浮来。左傳隱八年盟浮來，杜預曰邳來山之閒，號曰邳來。莊九年鮑叔受管仲，及堂阜而脱之。杜預曰：「東莞蒙陰縣西北有夷吾亭，或曰鮑叔解夷吾縛於此，因以爲名。」卽古堂阜也，東莞後爲郡。
entries.en: Some authorities identify the peak with old Fulai. The Zuo Tradition records a covenant at Fulai in Duke Yin 8, which Du Yu places between the Pilai mountains and says was called Pilai. In Duke Zhuang 9, Bao Shu received Guan Zhong and released him at Tangfu; Du Yu says, “Northwest of Mengyin county in Dongguan was Yiwu Pavilion; some say Bao Shu released Yiwu from his bonds here, and for this reason it was named.” This was old Tangfu, and Dongguan later became a commandery.
entries.literal: Some say it was ancient Fulai. In Duke Yin 8, the Zuo Tradition records a covenant at Fulai; Du Yu says it was between the Pilai mountains and was called Pilai. In Duke Zhuang 9, Bao Shu received Guan Zhong and released him when they reached Tangfu. Du Yu says, “Northwest of Mengyin county in Dongguan was Yiwu Pavilion; some say Bao Shu released Yiwu from his bonds here, and for this reason it was named.” This was ancient Tangfu; Dongguan later became a commandery.

entries.zh: 志第二十一 郡国三
entries.en: Treatise 21: “Commanderies and States,” Part Three.
entries.literal: Treatise twenty-one: Commanderies and States, part three.

entries.zh: 汉之初兴，承继大乱，兵不及戢，法度草创，略依秦制，后嗣因循。
entries.en: The dynasty emerged from utter turmoil: the armies had scarcely been stood down when statutes and offices were framed in haste, largely on Qin models, and succeeding reigns largely left that pattern in place.
entries.literal: When Han first arose, it followed upon great chaos; the troops had no time to be laid aside; laws and institutions were rudimentarily created; it roughly followed Qin institutions, and later rulers carried them on.

entries.zh: 至景帝，感吴楚之难，始抑损诸侯王。
entries.en: Emperor Jing, sobered by the revolt of Wu and Chu, began to pare back the power of the feudal kings.
entries.literal: Reaching Emperor Jing, moved by the disaster of Wu and Chu, he began to curtail the feudal kings.

entries.zh: 及至武帝，多所改作，然而奢广，民用匮乏。
entries.en: Emperor Wu refashioned much of the machinery of state, but that age's breadth and lavish spending drained the common people.
entries.literal: When it reached Emperor Wu, there were many changes and new creations, yet there was extravagance and expansion, and the people's resources were exhausted.

entries.zh: 世祖中兴，务从节约，并官省职，费减亿计，所以补复残缺，及身未改，而四海从风，中国安乐者也。
entries.en: When Guangwu restored the Han, he enforced austerity, merged bureaus and cut posts, and saved sums on the order of hundreds of millions of cash, mending what the wars had shattered. He held that course for life, and the realm fell into step; the heartland knew peace again.
entries.literal: The Founding Ancestor's restoration practiced compliance with thrift, merging offices and reducing posts; expenditures decreased by sums reckoned in the hundreds of millions; by this means patching and restoring what was broken and incomplete; throughout his life he did not alter it, yet within the Four Seas they followed like the wind, and the Central States were peaceful and happy.

entries.zh: 长史一人，千石。
entries.en: One chief clerk at one thousand bushels.
entries.literal: Chief clerk: one person, one thousand bushels.

entries.zh: 掾属三十一人。
entries.en: Thirty-one attendants and subordinates.
entries.literal: Attendants and subordinates: thirty-one persons.

entries.zh: 令史及御属三十六人。
entries.en: Thirty-six clerks and ministerial attendants.
entries.literal: Clerks and ministerial attendants: thirty-six persons.

entries.zh: 本注曰：世祖即位，以武帝故事置司直，居丞相府，助督录诸州，建武十八年省也。
entries.en: Guangwu revived Emperor Wu's office of the Straightener in the chancellor's compound to help supervise the provinces; it was cut in Jianwu 18.
entries.literal: Original commentary: the Founding Ancestor, when ascending the throne, by Emperor Wu's precedent established the Straightener, residing in the chancellor's mansion, assisting in supervising and recording the various provinces; in the eighteenth year of Jianwu it was abolished.

entries.zh: 初，武帝以卫青数征伐有功，以为大将军，欲尊宠之。
entries.en: Emperor Wu first made Wei Qing Grand General to reward his repeated victories and signal his eminence.
entries.literal: At first Emperor Wu, because Wei Qing repeatedly on campaigns had merit, made him Grand General, desiring to honor and favor him.

entries.zh: 以古尊官唯有三公，皆将军。始自秦、晋，以为卿号，故置大司马官号以冠之。
entries.en: Traditionally only the three dukes held supreme civil rank; generalships came from Qin and Jin as minister-level commands, so the court added the Grand Marshal title to crown that authority.
entries.literal: Because in antiquity the honored offices were only the three dukes, while generals beginning from Qin and Jin were taken as minister titles, therefore he established the Grand Marshal official title to crown them.

entries.zh: 其后霍光、王凤等皆然。
entries.en: Later Huo Guang, Wang Feng, and others held the same arrangement.
entries.literal: After that Huo Guang, Wang Feng, and others were all thus.

entries.zh: 成帝绥和元年，赐大司马印绶，罢将军官。
entries.en: In Suhe 1 (8 BCE) Emperor Cheng granted the Grand Marshal insignia and dropped the separate general's title.
entries.literal: In the first year of Emperor Cheng's Suihe era, he bestowed the Grand Marshal seal and ribbons and abolished the general's office.

entries.zh: 世祖中兴，吴汉以大将军为大司马，景丹为骠骑大将军，位在公下，及前、后、左、右杂号将军众多，皆主征伐，事讫皆罢。
entries.en: At Guangwu's restoration Wu Han held Grand General merged with Grand Marshal; Jing Dan was Charging Cavalry Grand General, still below ducal rank; many Front, Rear, Left, Right, and miscellaneous generals led field armies only to be disbanded when the fighting ended.
entries.literal: At the Founding Ancestor's restoration, Wu Han took Grand General as Grand Marshal; Jing Dan was Charging Cavalry Grand General, his position below a duke; and Front, Rear, Left, Right, and miscellaneous-title generals were numerous, all mastering campaigns; when the affairs were finished all were abolished.

entries.zh: 明帝初即位，以弟东平王苍有贤才，以为骠骑将军；
entries.en: Emperor Ming, seeing talent in his brother Prince Cang of Dongping, first named him Charging Cavalry General;
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming first ascended the throne, because his younger brother the Prince of Dongping, Cang, had worthy talent, he made him Charging Cavalry General;

entries.zh: 以王故，位在公上，数年后罢。
entries.en: his princely blood lifted him above the dukes until the office was dropped a few years later.
entries.literal: because he was a king, his position was above a duke; after several years it was abolished.

entries.zh: 章帝即位，西羌反，故以舅马防行车骑将军征之，还后罢。
entries.en: When the Western Qiang rose under Emperor Zhang, the emperor's uncle Ma Fang led them as acting Chariots and Cavalry General and relinquished the command afterward.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhang ascended the throne, the Western Qiang rebelled; therefore by his maternal uncle Ma Fang as acting Chariots and Cavalry General he campaigned against them; after returning it was abolished.

entries.zh: 和帝即位，以舅窦宪为车骑将军，征匈奴，位在公下；
entries.en: Emperor He sent his uncle Dou Xian against the Xiongnu as Chariots and Cavalry General, initially below ducal rank;
entries.literal: When Emperor He ascended the throne, by his maternal uncle Dou Xian as Chariots and Cavalry General he campaigned against the Xiongnu; his position was below a duke;

entries.zh: 还复有功，迁大将军，位在公上；
entries.en: further victories raised him to Grand General above the dukes;
entries.literal: after returning he again had merit, was promoted to Grand General, his position above a duke;

entries.zh: 复征西羌，还免官，罢。
entries.en: a later western campaign ended with his dismissal and the command's abolition.
entries.literal: again he campaigned against the Western Qiang; on returning he was dismissed from office and it was abolished.

entries.zh: 安帝即位，西羌寇乱，复以舅邓骘为车骑将军征之，还迁大将军，位如宪，数年复罢。
entries.en: Emperor An likewise used his uncle Deng Zhi to crush Qiang unrest as Chariots and Cavalry General, then as Grand General at Dou's former level until the post lapsed again.
entries.literal: When Emperor An ascended the throne, the Western Qiang raided and rebelled; again by his maternal uncle Deng Zhi as Chariots and Cavalry General he campaigned against them; on returning he was promoted to Grand General, his position like Dou Xian's; after several years it was again abolished.

entries.zh: 自安帝政治衰缺，始以嫡舅耿宝为大将军，常在京都。
entries.en: As An's government weakened, Geng Bao—his full maternal uncle—held Grand General as a resident capital post.
entries.literal: From Emperor An, governance declined and lacked; first by his full uncle Geng Bao as Grand General, he constantly was in the capital region.

entries.zh: 顺帝即位，又以皇后父、兄、弟相继为大将军，如三公焉。
entries.en: Shun continued the pattern, raising the empress's father and brothers in turn to Grand General, coequal with the three dukes.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shun ascended the throne, again by the empress's father, elder brother, and younger brother succeeding one another as Grand General, it was like the three dukes.

entries.zh: 昔周公作《周官》，分职著明，法度相持，王室虽微，犹能久存。
entries.en: Long ago the Duke of Zhou set down the Rites of Zhou, with every duty spelled out and institutions buttressing one another, so that even as royal power thinned, the dynasty endured.
entries.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou made the "Offices of Zhou," dividing duties so they were clear and manifest; laws and institutions supported one another; though the royal house was weak, still it was able to endure long.

entries.zh: 今其遗书，所以观周室牧民之德既至，又其有益来事之范，殆未有所穷也。
entries.en: What survives of that text still shows how thoroughly Zhou rule tended the people and offers a pattern for later ages that admits no easy final word.
entries.literal: Now its surviving documents, whereby one may observe that the Zhou house's virtue in shepherding the people had reached the utmost, and also that their model is beneficial to later affairs, probably cannot be exhausted.

entries.zh: 故新汲令王隆作《小学汉官篇》，诸文倜说，较略不究。
entries.en: Hence Wang Long, once magistrate of Xinji, composed the Elementary Han Offices—a work that wanders and abbreviates rather than exhausting the subject.
entries.literal: Therefore the magistrate of Xinji, Wang Long, composed the "Elementary Learning Han Offices Chapter"; the various texts were divergent and explanatory, comparatively summary and not thorough.

entries.zh: 唯班固著《百官公卿表》，记汉承秦置官本末，讫于王莽，差有条贯；
entries.en: Only Ban Gu's Table of Officials and Nobles traced how Han took over Qin offices from start to finish, down to Wang Mang, with something like a clear thread;
entries.literal: Only Ban Gu wrote the "Table of All Offices and Nobles," recording from beginning to end Han's inheriting Qin's establishment of offices, down to Wang Mang, somewhat having order and continuity;

entries.zh: 然皆孝武奢广之事，又职分未悉。
entries.en: yet his focus falls on Emperor Wu's expansion and luxury, and the boundaries of each post remain incompletely spelled out.
entries.literal: yet they are all matters of Emperor Wu's extravagance and expansion, moreover duties and divisions of office were not fully detailed.

entries.zh: 世祖节约之制，宜为常宪，故依其官簿，粗注职分，以为《百官志》。
entries.en: Guangwu's lean institutions deserve to stand as the enduring norm; this treatise follows his official register and sketches each post's remit—hence this Treatise on Officials.
entries.literal: The Founding Ancestor's system of thrift ought to be the constant statute; therefore relying on his roster of offices, coarsely annotating duties and divisions, making it the "Treatise on Officials."

entries.zh: 凡置官之本及中兴所省，无因复见者，既在《汉书·百官表》，不复悉载。
entries.en: Foundations of the bureaucracy and cuts made at the restoration that need no second telling already sit in the Hanshu table of offices, so they are not repeated here in full.
entries.literal: As for the root of establishing offices and what the restoration abolished, what has no cause to appear again, since it is already in the Hanshu "Table of Officials," is not again fully recorded.

entries.zh: 太傅，上公一人。
entries.en: Grand Tutor: one holder among the supreme dukes.
entries.literal: Grand Tutor: supreme duke, one person.

entries.zh: 本注曰：掌以善导，无常职。
entries.en: Commentary: He guides the sovereign toward good conduct and has no fixed portfolio.
entries.literal: Original commentary: he leads by good guidance; there are no fixed duties.

entries.zh: 世祖以卓茂为太傅，薨，因省。
entries.en: Guangwu named Zhuo Mao Grand Tutor; when Zhuo died, the title lapsed.
entries.literal: The Founding Ancestor appointed Zhuo Mao as Grand Tutor; when he died, therefore it was abolished.

entries.zh: 其后每帝初即位，辄置太傅录尚书事，薨，辄省。
entries.en: Thereafter each new sovereign would appoint a Grand Tutor to oversee the Masters of Writing; when that man died, the office vanished again.
entries.literal: After that, whenever each emperor first ascended the throne, he always established a Grand Tutor to record Masters of Writing affairs; when he died, it was always abolished.

entries.zh: 太尉，公一人。
entries.en: Grand Commandant: one at the rank of duke.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant: duke, one person.

entries.zh: 本注曰：掌四方兵事功课，岁尽即奏其殿最而行赏罚。
entries.en: He directs military affairs across the realm and, at year's end, ranks the regions for reward and punishment.
entries.literal: Original commentary: he holds military affairs in the four directions and merit assessment; when the year ends he reports the lowest and highest rankings and carries out rewards and punishments.

entries.zh: 凡郊祀之事，掌亚献；
entries.en: At suburban sacrifices he presents the second libation;
entries.literal: In matters of suburban sacrifice, he presents the second libation;

entries.zh: 大丧则告谥南郊。
entries.en: on a great imperial death he proclaims the posthumous title at the southern suburban altar.
entries.literal: in great mourning he proclaims the posthumous title at the southern suburban altar.

entries.zh: 凡国有大造大疑，则与司徒、司空通而论之。
entries.en: On momentous policy or unresolved state matters he deliberates jointly with the Minister of Education and the Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Whenever the state has great undertakings or great doubts, then with the Minister of Education and the Minister of Works he jointly discusses them.

entries.zh: 国有过事，则与二公通谏争之。
entries.en: When the sovereign errs, he joins the other two dukes in remonstrance.
entries.literal: If the state has faulty affairs, then with the two dukes he jointly remonstrates and contends.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，为大司马。
entries.en: Guangwu took power as Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: The Founding Ancestor, when ascending the throne, was Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 建武二十七年，改为太尉。
entries.en: In Jianwu 27 (51 CE) it became the Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu, it was changed to Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 司徒，公一人。
entries.en: Minister of Education: one at duke rank.
entries.literal: Minister of Education: duke, one person.

entries.zh: 本注曰：掌人民事。
entries.en: He oversees matters concerning the people.
entries.literal: Original commentary: he holds the people's affairs.

entries.zh: 凡教民孝悌、逊顺、谦俭，养生送死之事，则议其制，建其度。
entries.en: He frames policy for teaching filial piety, brotherly deference, humility, frugality, and for the people's welfare from birth to burial.
entries.literal: As for teaching the people filiality and fraternal duty, yielding and compliance, modesty and thrift, and matters of nurturing life and sending off the dead, then he discusses their regulations and establishes their measures.

entries.zh: 凡四方民事功课，岁尽则奏其殿最而行赏罚。
entries.en: He ranks regional civil administration yearly for rewards and punishments.
entries.literal: As for civil merit assessment in the four directions, when the year ends he reports the lowest and highest and carries out rewards and punishments.

entries.zh: 凡郊祀之事，掌省牲视濯，大丧则掌奉安梓宫。
entries.en: At suburban rites he inspects the sacrificial animal and the cleansing of vessels; at a state funeral he escorts and sets the imperial coffin.
entries.literal: In matters of suburban sacrifice, he inspects the victim and inspects the washing of vessels; in great mourning he presents and settles the catalpa palace-coffin.

entries.zh: 凡国有大疑大事，与太尉同。
entries.en: Great crises and weighty decisions mirror the Grand Commandant's role.
entries.literal: Whenever the state has great doubt or great affairs, it is the same as the Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，为大司徒，建武二十七年，去「大」。
entries.en: Guangwu began as Grand Minister of Education; Jianwu 27 dropped the prefix "grand."
entries.literal: The Founding Ancestor, when ascending the throne, was Grand Minister of Education; in the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu the word "grand" was removed.

entries.zh: 司空，公一人。
entries.en: Minister of Works: one at duke rank.
entries.literal: Minister of Works: duke, one person.

entries.zh: 本注曰：掌水土事。
entries.en: He is in charge of public works and hydraulic projects.
entries.literal: Original commentary: he holds water and earth affairs.

entries.zh: 凡营城起邑、浚沟洫、修坟防之事，则议其利，建其功。
entries.en: Walled cities, ditches, dikes, and levees come under his planning for utility and success.
entries.literal: Whenever there are matters of building walls and raising towns, dredging ditches and canals, or repairing mounds and dikes, then he discusses their benefit and establishes their merit.

entries.zh: 凡四方水土功课，岁尽则奏其殿最而行赏罚。
entries.en: He annually ranks regional hydraulic and earthworks performance.
entries.literal: As for water-and-earth merit assessment in the four directions, when the year ends he reports the lowest and highest and carries out rewards and punishments.

entries.zh: 凡郊祀之事，掌扫除、乐器，大丧则掌将校复土。
entries.en: He oversees purification, ritual music, and, at imperial burial, directs generals and colonels in the grave-filling rite.
entries.literal: In matters of suburban sacrifice, he holds sweeping and cleaning and ritual instruments; in great mourning he leads generals and colonels in back-filling the grave.

entries.zh: 凡国有大造大疑，谏争，与太尉同。
entries.en: On great projects and doubts he joins the Grand Commandant in debate and remonstrance.
entries.literal: Whenever the state has great undertakings or great doubts, remonstrance and contention are the same as the Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，为大司空，建武二十七年，去「大」。
entries.en: The Founding Ancestor, when ascending the throne, was Grand Minister of Works; in the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu the word "grand" was removed.
entries.literal: The Founding Ancestor, when ascending the throne, was Grand Minister of Works; in the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu the word "grand" was removed.

entries.zh: 明帝初置度辽将军，以卫南单于众新降有二心者，后数有不安，遂为常守。
entries.en: Emperor Ming first created the General Who Crosses the Liao to watch the newly submitted Southern Shanyu followers, who still wavered in allegiance; recurring unrest soon turned the post into a standing frontier command.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming first established the General Who Crosses the Liao, it was in order to guard the Southern Shanyu's people who had newly surrendered and harbored divided loyalty; afterward there were frequent disturbances, therefore it became a constant garrison.

entries.zh: 东观书云司马二人。
entries.en: The Eastern Pavilion Account records two majors for the post.
entries.literal: The Eastern Pavilion Account states there are two majors.

entries.zh: 志第二十四 百官一
entries.en: Treatise 24: Officials, Part One.
entries.literal: Treatise twenty-four: Officials, Part One.

entries.zh: 博士祭酒一人，六百石。
entries.en: One erudite libationer at six hundred bushels.
entries.literal: Erudite libationer, one person, six hundred bushels.

entries.zh: 本仆射，中兴转为祭酒。
entries.en: The head of the erudites was originally titled Pushe; after the restoration the office was renamed libationer (jijiu).
entries.literal: Originally Erudite Pushe; at restoration changed to libationer.

entries.zh: 胡广曰：「官名祭酒，皆一位之元长者也。
entries.en: Hu Guang explained: "The title jijiu marks the senior head of a bureau.
entries.literal: Hu Guang said: "The office title libationer designates the senior head of a single rank.

entries.zh: 古礼，宾客得主人馔，则老者一人举酒以祭于地，旧说以为示有先。」
entries.en: In ancient guest ritual the eldest would pour a libation to the ground to honor those who came before."
entries.literal: In ancient ritual, when guests received food from the host, the eldest among them would raise wine and offer it to the ground; older explanations hold that this showed regard for ancestors."

entries.zh: 博士十四人，比六百石。
entries.en: Fourteen court erudites at six hundred bushels equivalent.
entries.literal: Fourteen erudites, comparable to six hundred bushels.

entries.zh: 本注曰：《易》四，施、孟、梁丘、京氏。
entries.en: The Book of Changes is taught in four schools—Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing.
entries.literal: Original commentary: for the Changes, four traditions: Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing.

entries.zh: 《尚书》三，欧阳、大小夏侯氏。
entries.en: The Book of Documents has three lines—Ouyang and the elder and younger Xiahou traditions.
entries.literal: For the Documents, three: Ouyang, Greater and Lesser Xiahou.

entries.zh: 《诗》三，鲁、齐、韩氏。
entries.en: The Odes are represented by the Lu, Qi, and Han schools.
entries.literal: For the Odes, three: Lu, Qi, and Han.

entries.zh: 《礼》二，大小戴氏。
entries.en: The Rites survive in the elder and younger Dai recensions.
entries.literal: For the Rites, two: Greater and Lesser Dai.

entries.zh: 《春秋》二，《公羊》严、颜氏。
entries.en: The Spring and Autumn is taught in two Gongyang schools, the lineages of Master Yan Pengzu and Master Yan Anle.
entries.literal: For the Spring and Autumn, two: the Gongyang traditions of Yan and Yan.

entries.zh: 掌教弟子。
entries.en: They instruct the disciples enrolled at the academy.
entries.literal: They master teaching disciples.

entries.zh: 國有疑事，掌承問對。
entries.en: When policy questions arise, they supply learned answers on demand.
entries.literal: When the state has doubtful matters, they undertake to answer inquiries.

entries.zh: 本四百石，宣帝增秩。
entries.en: Their stipend began at four hundred bushels until Emperor Xuan raised it.
entries.literal: Originally four hundred bushels; Emperor Xuan increased the rank.

entries.zh: 汉官曰：「五十人，无常员。」
entries.en: The Offices of Han lists fifty men without a fixed quota."
entries.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Fifty men, no fixed quota."

entries.zh: 谒者仆射一人，比千石。
entries.en: One chief receptionist at one thousand bushels equivalent.
entries.literal: Shepherd of receptionists, one person, comparable to one thousand bushels.

entries.zh: 本注曰：为谒者台率，主谒者，天子出，奉引。
entries.en: He heads the reception corps, and when the emperor leaves the palace he leads the vanguard.
entries.literal: Original commentary: he is leader of the receptionists' bureau, commands receptionists; when the Son of Heaven goes out, he leads the procession.

entries.zh: 古重习武，有主射以督录之。
entries.en: Antiquity prized martial drill; a master archer supervised the corps.
entries.literal: In antiquity they valued martial practice; there was a master of archery to supervise and record them.

entries.zh: 故曰仆射。
entries.en: Hence the title pushe, "shepherd of archers."
entries.literal: Therefore it is called "shepherd" (pushe).

entries.zh: 蔡质汉仪曰：「见尚书令，对揖无敬。
entries.en: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "When they meet the Master of Writing, they exchange bows without full prostration,
entries.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "When meeting the Master of Writing, they bow facing each other without full obeisance.

entries.zh: 谒者见，执板拜之。」
entries.en: but bowed with tablets to receptionists."
entries.literal: When receptionists meet, they hold the tablet and bow."

entries.zh: 常侍谒者五人，比六百石。
entries.en: Five standing receptionists at six hundred bushels equivalent.
entries.literal: Constant attendant receptionists, five persons, comparable to six hundred bushels.

entries.zh: 本注曰：主殿上时节威仪。
entries.en: They regulate ritual pacing and demeanor during audiences.
entries.literal: Original commentary: they hold seasonal order and ceremony on the hall above.

entries.zh: 谒者三十人。
entries.en: Thirty receptionists serve in rotation.
entries.literal: Thirty receptionists.

entries.zh: 其给事谒者，四百石。
entries.en: Serving receptionists draw four hundred bushels.
entries.literal: Those who are serving receptionists, four hundred bushels.

entries.zh: 其灌谒者郎中，比三百石。
entries.en: Bathed receptionists acting as gentleman secretaries rank at three hundred bushels equivalent.
entries.literal: Those who are bathed receptionists and gentlemen secretaries, comparable to three hundred bushels.

entries.zh: 本注曰：掌宾赞受事，及上章报问。
entries.en: They greet envoys, take in petitions, and carry answers back to supplicants.
entries.literal: Original commentary: they hold guest protocol, receiving business, and submitting memorials and answering inquiries.

entries.zh: 将、大夫以下之丧，掌使吊。
entries.en: They carry the court’s condolences to the funerals of generals and officials of lower rank.
entries.literal: For mourning of generals and grandees downward, they are dispatched to offer condolence.

entries.zh: 本员七十人，中兴但三十人。
entries.en: Western Han filled seventy slots; the restored court cut the corps to thirty.
entries.literal: Originally the quota was seventy persons; at restoration only thirty.

entries.zh: 荀绰晋百官表注曰：「汉皆用孝廉年五十，威容严恪能宾者为之。
entries.en: Xun Chuo's Jin commentary on the offices says: "Han chose fifty-year-old filial and incorrupt men of grave bearing to serve as receptionists.
entries.literal: Xun Chuo's Jin Table of Offices commentary says: "Han always appointed filial and incorrupt men aged fifty, of stern bearing and dignified manner able to receive guests.

entries.zh: 明帝诏曰：『谒者乃尧之尊官，所以试舜宾于四门，四门穆穆者也。』
entries.en: Emperor Ming called the post one of Yao's great offices, the office that tested Shun at the four gates.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming's edict said: 'Receptionists were Yao's honored office, by which Shun was tested as guest at the four gates, and the four gates were reverent.

entries.zh: 昔燕太子使荆轲劫始皇，变起两楹之间，其后谒者持匕首刺腋，高祖偃武行文，故易之以板。」
entries.en: Formerly the crown prince of Yan sent Jing Ke to seize the First Emperor; the crisis arose between the two pillars, and afterward receptionists carried daggers at the armpit. Gaozu laid aside arms and promoted culture, and therefore replaced them with tablets."
entries.literal: Formerly the crown prince of Yan sent Jing Ke to seize the First Emperor; the crisis arose between the two pillars, and afterward a receptionist stabbed him in the armpit with a dagger. Emperor Gaozu laid aside arms and promoted culture, and therefore replaced daggers with tablets."

entries.zh: 初为灌谒者，满岁为给事谒者。
entries.en: A novice begins as a bathed receptionist and after one year graduates to serving receptionist.
entries.literal: At first they are bathed receptionists; when a full year is complete they become serving receptionists.

entries.zh: 高庙令一人，六百石。
entries.en: One keeper of Emperor Gaozu’s shrine at six hundred bushels.
entries.literal: Gaozu’s shrine director, one person, six hundred bushels.

entries.zh: 本注曰：守庙，掌案行扫除。
entries.en: He tends the shrine, inspects its precincts, and keeps them swept.
entries.literal: Original commentary: guards the shrine; masters inspection tours and sweeping.

entries.zh: 无丞。
entries.en: There is no deputy to this office.
entries.literal: No assistant.

entries.zh: 世祖庙令一人，六百石。
entries.en: One keeper of Guangwu’s shrine at six hundred bushels.
entries.literal: Founding Ancestor’s shrine director, one person, six hundred bushels.

entries.zh: 本注曰：如高庙。
entries.en: His duties mirror those at Gaozu’s shrine.
entries.literal: Original commentary: as for Gaozu’s shrine.

entries.zh: 五官中郎将一人，比二千石。
entries.en: One captain of the central gentlemen for the five bureaus at two thousand bushels equivalent.
entries.literal: Leader of gentlemen-of-the-house for the five offices, one person, comparable to two thousand bushels.

entries.zh: 本注曰：主五官郎。
entries.en: He leads the gentlemen attached to the five ministries.
entries.literal: Original commentary: he commands the gentlemen for the five offices.

entries.zh: 五官中郎，比六百石。
entries.en: Central gentlemen for the five bureaus at six hundred bushels equivalent.
entries.literal: Gentlemen of the house for the five offices at middle rank, comparable to six hundred bushels.

entries.zh: 本注曰：无员。
entries.en: There is no statutory head count.
entries.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

entries.zh: 胡广曰：「光禄大夫，本为中大夫，武帝元狩五年置谏大夫为光禄大夫，世祖中兴，以为谏议大夫。
entries.en: Hu Guang said: "The Household Grandee was originally the Middle Grandee; in the fifth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu remonstrating grandees were made household grandees, and at Guangwu's restoration they became remonstrating grandees.
entries.literal: Hu Guang said: "The Household Grandee was originally Middle Grandee. In the fifth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu remonstrating grandees were made household grandees; at Emperor Guangwu's restoration they became remonstrating grandees.

entries.zh: 又有太中、中散大夫。
entries.en: alongside palace and scattered grandees
entries.literal: There were also grandees within the palace and grandees of scattered attendance.

entries.zh: 此四等于古皆为天子之下大夫，视列国之上卿。」
entries.en: —four grades matching the ancient lower grandees of the ruler."
entries.literal: These four grades in antiquity were all the Son of Heaven's lower grandees, equivalent to the upper ministers of feudal states."

entries.zh: 汉官曰三十人。
entries.en: The Offices of Han sets the quota at thirty.
entries.literal: The Offices of Han says thirty men.

entries.zh: 郎年五十以屬五官，故曰六百石。
entries.en: Gentlemen aged fifty were attached to the Five Offices, so they were said to be six hundred shi.
entries.literal: Gentlemen aged fifty were attached to the Five Offices, so they were said to be six hundred shi.

entries.zh: 五官侍郎，比四百石。
entries.en: Attendant gentlemen for the five bureaus at four hundred bushels equivalent.
entries.literal: Gentlemen attendants for the five offices, comparable to four hundred bushels.

entries.zh: 本注曰：無員。
entries.en: There is no statutory head count.
entries.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

entries.zh: 五官郎中，比三百石。
entries.en: Secretary gentlemen for the five bureaus at three hundred bushels equivalent.
entries.literal: Gentlemen secretaries for the five offices, comparable to three hundred bushels.

entries.zh: 本注曰：无员。
entries.en: There is no statutory head count.
entries.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

entries.zh: 凡郎官皆主更直执戟，宿卫诸殿门，出充车骑。
entries.en: Gentlemen-of-the-house stand rotating halberd watch at palace doors and ride out as imperial escort.
entries.literal: All gentlemen-of-the-house chiefly rotate watch bearing halberds, night-watch at the various hall gates, and go out to act as chariots and cavalry escort.

entries.zh: 唯议郎不在直中。
entries.en: Advisory gentlemen alone are exempt from guard duty.
entries.literal: Only advisory gentlemen are not in the watch rotation.

entries.zh: 蔡质汉仪曰：「出府丞、长史、陵令，皆选仪容端正，任奉使者。」
entries.en: Cai Zhi required handsome, dignified men for assistants, chief clerks, and mausoleum directors sent out as envoys."
entries.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "For outgoing bureau assistants, chief clerks, and mausoleum directors, all are chosen for proper bearing and appearance, appointed as envoys on mission."

entries.zh: 右属光禄勋。
entries.en: The offices at right fall under the Minister of the Household.
entries.literal: Those on the right belong to the Minister of the Household.

entries.zh: 本注曰：职属光禄者，自五官将至羽林右监，凡七署。
entries.en: Household-line commands run from the captain of the five bureaus through the right Feathered Forest superintendent—seven bureaus in all.
entries.literal: Original commentary: offices subordinate to the Household, from the leader of gentlemen for the five offices down to the right superintendent of the Feathered Forest, in all seven bureaus.

entries.zh: 自奉车都尉至谒者，以文属焉。
entries.en: From chariot commandants through receptionists they count as civil adjuncts of the same ministry.
entries.literal: From commandant of the imperial chariot down to receptionists, by civil subordination they attach there.

entries.zh: 旧有左右曹，秩以二千石，上殿中，主受尚书奏事，平省之。
entries.en: Western Han also posted left and right palace secretaries at two thousand bushels to take memorials from the Masters of Writing for screening inside the hall.
entries.literal: Formerly there were left and right Cao at two-thousand-bushel rank, ascending to the hall, receiving Masters of Writing memorials and leveling and reviewing them.

entries.zh: 世祖省，使小黄门郎受事，车驾出，给黄门郎兼。
entries.en: Guangwu abolished those posts and had petty Yellow Gate gentlemen handle intake; on imperial progresses those same gentlemen double as escort.
entries.literal: The Founding Ancestor eliminated them, having petty gentlemen of the Yellow Gate receive business; when the chariot goes out, petty gentlemen of the Yellow Gate double in the duty.

entries.zh: 有请室令，车驾出，在前请所幸，徼车迎白，示重慎。
entries.en: A director of the petition chamber once rode ahead to learn the emperor’s intended route so patrol cars could announce it—an emblem of care.
entries.literal: There was a director of the petition chamber; when the chariot went out, he went ahead to request the intended destination, patrol chariots met him with the report, showing gravity and caution.

entries.zh: 中兴但以郎兼，事讫罢，又省车、户、骑凡三将，如淳曰：「主车曰车郎，主户卫曰户郎。」
entries.en: After the restoration gentlemen temporarily doubled these posts and were dismissed when duty ended; the chariot, household, and cavalry commanders were cut. Ru Chun glossed chariot gentlemen and household gentlemen."
entries.literal: At restoration only gentlemen doubled the posts, dismissed when the affair ended; also eliminated were the three generals of chariots, household guard, and cavalry. Ru Chun said: "Those mastering chariots were called chariot gentlemen; those mastering household guard were called household gentlemen."

entries.zh: 及羽林令。
entries.en: The Feathered Forest director remained.
entries.literal: Also the Director of Feathered Forest.

entries.zh: 宫掖门，每门司马一人，比千石。
entries.en: Every inner gate posts one major at one thousand bushels equivalent.
entries.literal: For palace and harem gates, each gate has one major, comparable to one thousand bushels.

entries.zh: 本注曰：南宫南屯司马，主平城门；
entries.en: The Southern Palace’s south camp major holds Pingcheng Gate;
entries.literal: Original commentary: South Regiment Major of the Southern Palace masters Pingcheng Gate;

entries.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏九人，卫士百二人。」
entries.en: The Offices of Han lists nine clerks and 102 guards."
entries.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Nine staff and one hundred two guards."

entries.zh: 古今注曰建武十三年九月，初开此门。
entries.en: Notes Ancient and Modern dates the gate's first opening to the ninth month of Jianwu 13.
entries.literal: Notes Ancient and Modern says: in the ninth month of the thirteenth year of Jianwu, this gate was first opened.

entries.zh: 宫门苍龙司马，主东门；
entries.en: The Azure Dragon palace gate commandant holds the east gate;
entries.literal: Palace Gate Azure Dragon Commandant masters the east gate;

entries.zh: 案雒阳宫门名为苍龙阙门。
entries.en: Luoyang's east palace gate was called the Azure Dragon Tower Gate.
entries.literal: On investigation the Luoyang palace gate is named Azure Dragon Tower Gate.

entries.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏六人，卫士四十人。」
entries.en: The Offices of Han gives the post six clerks and forty guards."
entries.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Six staff and forty guards."

entries.zh: 玄武司马，主玄武门；
entries.en: the Black Tortoise major holds Black Tortoise Gate;
entries.literal: Black Tortoise Major masters Black Tortoise Gate;

entries.zh: 北屯司马，主北门；
entries.en: the north camp major holds the north gate;
entries.literal: North Regiment Major masters the north gate;

entries.zh: 北宫朱爵司马，主南掖门；
entries.en: the Northern Palace’s Vermilion Sparrow major holds the south harem portal;
entries.literal: Vermilion Sparrow Major of the Northern Palace masters the south harem gate;

entries.zh: 东明司马，主东门；
entries.en: the Dawn-clarity major holds the east inner gate;
entries.literal: Dawn-clarity Major masters the east gate;

entries.zh: 朔平司马，主北门：凡七门。
entries.en: and the Pacified-north major holds the north inner gate—seven gates in all.
entries.literal: Pacified-north Major masters the north gate: in all seven gates.

entries.zh: 凡居宫中者，皆有口籍于门之所属。
entries.en: Everyone quartered inside carries a mouth tally filed with the gate that controls his passage.
entries.literal: All who dwell within the palace have mouth tallies registered with the gate to which they belong.

entries.zh: 宫名两字，为铁印文符，案省符乃内之。
entries.en: Each two-character gate name is cast on an iron tally; the seal must match before entry is granted.
entries.literal: The palace name of two characters is an iron-seal text tally; they inspect the tally and only then admit them.

entries.zh: 胡广曰：「符用木，长尺二寸，铁印以符之。」
entries.en: Hu Guang noted that the wooden tally was one foot two inches long and authenticated by an iron seal."
entries.literal: Hu Guang said: "The tally is of wood, one foot two inches long; an iron seal authenticates the tally."

entries.zh: 若外人以事当入，本官长史为封棨传；
entries.en: Official visitors must carry a wooden tally pass sealed by their agency's chief clerk;
entries.literal: If an outsider must enter on business, the chief clerk of his home office seals a tally pass;

entries.zh: 其有官位，出入令御者言其官。
entries.en: Ranked officials declare their title to the coachman when passing in or out.
entries.literal: If they have official rank, going out and in they order the charioteer to announce their office.

entries.zh: 前书武帝置期门，平帝更名虎贲。
entries.en: The Former Book records that Emperor Wu created the Gate of Expected Arrival and Emperor Ping renamed it the rapid guard.
entries.literal: The Former Book says Emperor Wu set up the Gate of Expected Arrival; Emperor Ping renamed it Tiger-Rank Guard.

entries.zh: 蔡质汉仪曰：「主虎贲千五百人，无常员，多至千人。
entries.en: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "They command 1,500 rapid guards, without a fixed quota, often up to a thousand.
entries.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "They command one thousand five hundred tiger-rank guards, no fixed quota, often up to one thousand.

entries.zh: 戴鹖冠，次右将府。」
entries.en: wearing pheasant caps and quartered next to the right general's office."
entries.literal: They wear pheasant caps and rank next to the right general's bureau."

entries.zh: 又虎贲旧作「虎奔」，言如虎之奔也，王莽以古有勇士孟贲，故名焉。
entries.en: The name was once written "tiger-run" for swiftness; Wang Mang linked it to the ancient warrior Meng Ben.
entries.literal: Formerly hu-ben was written "tiger-run," meaning to run like a tiger; Wang Mang, because antiquity had the warrior Meng Ben, therefore gave the name.

entries.zh: 孔安国曰「若虎贲兽」，言其甚猛。
entries.en: Kong Anguo said they were "like tiger-rank beasts," meaning they were very fierce.
entries.literal: Kong Anguo said "like the tiger-rank beast," meaning they are very fierce.

entries.zh: 羽林中郎将，比二千石。
entries.en: The captain of the Feathered Forest guard at two thousand bushels equivalent.
entries.literal: Leader of gentlemen-of-the-house for the feathered forest, comparable to two thousand bushels.

entries.zh: 本注曰：主羽林郎。
entries.en: He commands the Feathered Forest gentlemen.
entries.literal: Original commentary: he commands feathered-forest gentlemen.

entries.zh: 羽林郎，比三百石。
entries.en: Feathered Forest gentlemen at three hundred bushels equivalent.
entries.literal: Feathered-forest gentlemen, comparable to three hundred bushels.

entries.zh: 本注曰：无员。
entries.en: There is no statutory head count.
entries.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.

entries.zh: 掌宿卫侍从。
entries.en: They provide close escort and night security for the throne.
entries.literal: They hold night-watch attendance and following.

entries.zh: 常选汉阳、陇西、安定、北地、上郡、西河凡六郡良家补。
entries.en: Recruits are drawn in rotation from respectable households across six northwestern commanderies.
entries.literal: They are regularly selected from the six commanderies Hanyang, Longxi, Anding, Beidi, Shangjun, and Xihe, good families to fill the ranks.

entries.zh: 本武帝以便马从猎，还宿殿陛巖下室中，故号巖郎。
entries.en: Emperor Wu first rode light mounts on the hunt and billeted his escort under the hall steps, whence the nickname “gallery guard.”
entries.literal: Originally Emperor Wu used nimble mounts to follow the hunt, returning to lodge in the chamber beneath the palace steps, therefore they were called “step-gentlemen.”

entries.zh: 前书曰初置名建章营骑，后更名。
entries.en: The Former Book records that the corps was first titled Jianzhang camp cavalry and later renamed.
entries.literal: The Former Book says at first they were set up as Jianzhang camp cavalry, later renamed.

entries.zh: 出补三百石丞、尉。
entries.en: Veterans were posted out as three-hundred-bushel assistants and commandants.
entries.literal: On leaving service they are supplemented as three-hundred-bushel assistants and commandants.

entries.zh: 荀绰晋百官表注曰：「言其严厉整锐也。」
entries.en: Xun Chuo glossed the name as denoting stern discipline and sharp readiness."
entries.literal: Xun Chuo's Jin Table of Offices commentary says: "This means stern, severe, and sharp."

entries.zh: 案此则为岩郎，与志不同。
entries.en: This account treats them as gallery guards, which differs from the treatise elsewhere.
entries.literal: On investigation this refers to gallery gentlemen, differing from the treatise.

entries.zh: 蔡质汉仪曰：「羽林郎百二十八人，无常员，府次虎贲府。」
entries.en: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "128 Feathered Forest gentlemen without a fixed quota, quartered next to the rapid guard."
entries.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "One hundred twenty-eight Feathered Forest gentlemen, no fixed quota; the bureau ranks next to the Tiger-Rank Guard bureau."

entries.zh: 右属廷尉。
entries.en: The offices at right fall under the Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: Those on the right belong to the Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 本注曰：孝武帝以下，置中都官狱二十六所，各令长名世祖中兴皆省，唯廷尉及雒阳有诏狱。
entries.en: From Emperor Wu on the capital ran twenty-six separate prison bureaus, each with its own warden; Guangwu abolished them, leaving only the Minister of Justice’s jails and Luoyang’s imperial prison.
entries.literal: Original commentary: from Emperor Xiaowu downward, twenty-six capital-office prisons were established, each with a director or chief by name; at the Founding Ancestor’s restoration all were eliminated; only the Minister of Justice and Luoyang retained edict prisons.

entries.zh: 志第二十五 百官二
entries.en: Treatise 25: Officials, Part Two.
entries.literal: Treatise twenty-five: Officials, Part Two.

entries.zh: 尚书令一人，千石。
entries.en: The director of the Secretariat held rank at one thousand piculs.
entries.literal: One director of the masters of writing, one thousand piculs.

entries.zh: 本注曰：承秦所置，武帝用宦者，更为中书谒者令，成帝用士人，复故。
entries.en: The office dated to Qin; Emperor Wu had put eunuchs in charge under the title of palace secretary and usher; Emperor Cheng returned it to civil officials under the old name.
entries.literal: Original note says: Inherited from what Qin established; Emperor Wu used eunuchs and changed it to director of palace secretaries and ushers; Emperor Cheng used literati and restored the old.

entries.zh: 掌凡选署及奏下尚书曹文书众事。
entries.en: He handled appointments, routed memorials, and dispatched paperwork to the six secretariat bureaus.
entries.literal: He is in charge of all selections and appointments and of memorializing and issuing downward the documents and multitude of affairs of the masters-of-writing bureaus.

entries.zh: 右属少府。
entries.en: The offices listed above fell under the Privy Treasurer.
entries.literal: Those on the right belong to the Privy Treasurer.

entries.zh: 本注曰：职属少府者，自太医、上林凡四官。
entries.en: Only four bureaus still drew their substantive duties directly from the Privy Treasurer, beginning with the grand physician and Shanglin.
entries.literal: Original note says: As for offices whose duties belong to the Privy Treasurer, from the grand physician and Shanglin, in all four offices.

entries.zh: 自侍中至御史，皆以文属焉。
entries.en: From gentlemen-in-attendance through the censorate, they were administratively attached to his ministry.
entries.literal: From gentlemen-in-attendance down to censors, all are attached to him by document.

entries.zh: 承秦，凡山泽陂池之税，名曰禁钱，属少府。
entries.en: Since Qin, revenue from royal forests, lakes, and ponds had been called "forbidden cash" and went to the Privy Treasurer.
entries.literal: Inherited from Qin, as for taxes on mountains, marshes, dikes, and pools, the name is forbidden money; they belonged to the Privy Treasurer.

entries.zh: 世祖改属司农，考工转属太仆，都水属郡国。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu reassigned that income to the Minister of Finance, moved the directorate of works to the grand coachman, and devolved water conservancy to local government.
entries.literal: Emperor Guangwu changed them to belong to the Minister of Finance; the works of artificers was transferred to belong to the grand coachman; capital waterworks belonged to commanderies and kingdoms.

entries.zh: 孝武帝初置水衡都尉，秩比二千石，别主上林苑有离官燕休之处，世祖省之，并其职于少府。
entries.en: Emperor Wu had created the water-and-balances commandant at two thousand piculs to run Shanglin's lodges and resorts; Emperor Guangwu abolished the post and folded its duties back into the Privy Treasurer.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu at first established the chief commandant of waters and balances, rank comparable to two thousand piculs, separately in charge of Shanglin Park having detached palaces and places for feasting and rest; Emperor Guangwu abolished it and merged its duties into the Privy Treasurer.

entries.zh: 每立秋貙刘之日，辄暂置水衡都尉，事讫乃罢之。
entries.en: Each autumn, for the imperial hunt, the water-and-balances commandant was revived briefly and then disbanded when the rite ended.
entries.literal: Each time on the day of autumn's beginning of the chu and liu hunt, then temporarily the chief commandant of waters and balances is established; when the affair is finished, then it is abolished.

entries.zh: 少府本六丞，省五。
entries.en: The Privy Treasurer once had six assistants; five were cut.
entries.literal: The Privy Treasurer originally had six assistants; five were abolished.

entries.zh: 又省汤官、织室令，置丞。
entries.en: The liquor-office and weaving-chamber directors were dropped in favor of deputies only.
entries.literal: Further the soup-house director and weaving-chamber director were abolished, and assistants were established.

entries.zh: 又省上林十池监，胞人长丞，宦者、昆台、佽飞三令，二十一丞。
entries.en: Also struck were ten Shanglin pond stewards, the chief and deputy of the palace kitchen attendants, three eunuch-led directorates including Kun Terrace and the flying-archer guard, and twenty-one assistant posts.
entries.literal: Further abolished were ten pool overseers of Shanglin, the chief and assistant of the kitchen attendants, three directors of eunuchs, Kun Terrace, and flying archers, and twenty-one assistants.

entries.zh: 又省水衡属官令、长、丞、尉二十余人。
entries.en: Over twenty more ranks under the old water-and-balances establishment were eliminated.
entries.literal: Further more than twenty directors, chiefs, assistants, and commandants belonging to the water-and-balances subordinates were abolished.

entries.zh: 章和以下，中官稍广，加尝药、太官、御者、钩盾、尚方、考工、别作监，皆六百石，宦者为之，转为兼副，或省，故录本官。
entries.en: After the Zhanghe era the eunuch establishment grew: stewards over tasting, kitchens, equipage, parks, workshops, and separate ateliers at six hundred piculs, often held concurrently or later cut—hence this note preserves their original titles.
entries.literal: From the Zhanghe reign downward, inner officials gradually expanded; added were overseers of tasting medicine, grand provisioner, charioteers, hook-shield, imperial workshops, works of artificers, and separate works—all six hundred piculs, eunuchs holding them, changed to concurrent deputies, or abolished; therefore the original offices are recorded.

entries.zh: 尚书六人，六百石。
entries.en: There were six secretariat ministers at six hundred piculs each.
entries.literal: Six masters of writing, six hundred piculs.

entries.zh: 本注曰：成帝初署尚书四人，分为四曹：常侍曹尚书主公卿事，二千石曹尚书主郡国二千石事，民曹尚书主凡吏上书事，客曹尚书主外国夷狄事。
entries.en: Emperor Cheng had first set four bureau chiefs: one for nobles and ministers, one for commandery and kingdom officials at two thousand piculs, one for commoners' petitions, and one for foreign envoys and frontier peoples.
entries.literal: Original note says: At the beginning of Emperor Cheng's reign four masters of writing were appointed, divided into four bureaus: the regular-attendant bureau master of writing was in charge of affairs of dukes and ministers; the two-thousand-picul bureau master of writing was in charge of affairs of two-thousand-picul officials of commanderies and kingdoms; the people bureau master of writing was in charge of affairs of all clerks submitting memorials; the guest bureau master of writing was in charge of affairs of foreign states and barbarians.

entries.zh: 世祖承遵，后分二千石曹，又分客曹为南主客曹、北主客曹，凡六曹。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu kept that structure, then split the two-thousand-picul bureau and divided the guest bureau into southern and northern guest affairs, for six bureaus in all.
entries.literal: Emperor Guangwu inherited and followed; later the two-thousand-picul bureau was split, and the guest bureau was further split into south guest bureau and north guest bureau; in all six bureaus.

entries.zh: 左右丞各一人，四百石。
entries.en: Left and right assistants of the board each held four hundred piculs.
entries.literal: One left assistant and one right assistant, each four hundred piculs.

entries.zh: 本注曰：掌录文书期会。
entries.en: They kept the files and tracked deadlines for the six bureaus.
entries.literal: Original note says: They are in charge of recording documents and scheduled meetings.

entries.zh: 左丞主吏民章报及驺伯史。
entries.en: The left assistant handled petitions from officials and commoners and supervised the board's runners and senior clerks.
entries.literal: The left assistant is in charge of clerks' and commoners' memorial replies and of outriders and chief clerks.

entries.zh: 右丞假署印绶及纸笔墨诸财用库藏。
entries.en: The right assistant issued seals and ribbons on temporary authority and managed stationery and supply vaults.
entries.literal: The right assistant temporarily assigns seals and ribbons and paper, ink, brush, and the various goods and treasuries.

entries.zh: 侍郎三十六人，四百石。
entries.en: Thirty-six secretariat gentlemen attendants served at four hundred piculs.
entries.literal: Thirty-six gentleman attendants, four hundred piculs.

entries.zh: 本注曰：一曹有六人，主作文书起草。
entries.en: Each of the six bureaus had six of them to draft outgoing paperwork.
entries.literal: Original note says: Each bureau has six persons; they are in charge of drafting documents.

entries.zh: 令史十八人，二百石。
entries.en: Eighteen secretariat clerks held rank at two hundred piculs.
entries.literal: Eighteen clerks, two hundred piculs.

entries.zh: 本注曰：曹有三，主书。
entries.en: Each bureau had three clerks to manage correspondence.
entries.literal: Original note says: Each bureau has three; they are in charge of writing.

entries.zh: 后增剧曹三人，合二十一人。
entries.en: Three more were later added for the urgent-affairs desk, making twenty-one in total.
entries.literal: Later three were added for the urgent bureau, in all twenty-one.

entries.zh: 志第二十六 百官三
entries.en: Treatise 26: The Bureaucracy, Part Three.
entries.literal: Treatise twenty-six: Officials, part three.

entries.zh: 大长秋一人，二千石。
entries.en: The empress's chamberlain, the grand prolonger of autumn, held two thousand piculs.
entries.literal: One grand prolonger of autumn, two thousand piculs.

entries.zh: 本注曰：承秦将行，宦者。
entries.en: The office descended from the Qin "general who goes"; it was held by a eunuch.
entries.literal: Original note says: Inherited from Qin's general who goes; eunuchs.

entries.zh: 景帝更为大长秋，或用士人。
entries.en: Emperor Jing renamed it grand prolonger of autumn and occasionally appointed a civil official.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing changed it to grand prolonger of autumn; sometimes literati were used.

entries.zh: 中兴常用宦者，职掌奉宣中宫命。
entries.en: After the restoration eunuchs normally held the post and conveyed the empress's orders.
entries.literal: At the restoration eunuchs were commonly used; the duty is to receive and proclaim the commands of the middle palace.

entries.zh: 凡给赐宗亲，及宗亲当谒见者关通之，中宫出则从。
entries.en: He arranged stipends for the imperial clan, passed in kinsmen who sought audience, and accompanied the empress when she left the palace.
entries.literal: As for all grants and gifts to imperial kin, and imperial kin who ought to have audience, he links and communicates them; when the middle palace goes out, he follows.

entries.zh: 丞一人，六百石。
entries.en: He had one assistant at six hundred piculs.
entries.literal: One assistant, six hundred piculs.

entries.zh: 本注曰：宦者。
entries.en: The assistant was a eunuch.
entries.literal: Original note says: Eunuchs.

entries.zh: 将作大匠一人，二千石。
entries.en: The master of works was a single minister at two thousand piculs.
entries.literal: One master artisan, two thousand piculs.

entries.zh: 本注曰：承秦，曰将作少府，景帝改为将作大匠。
entries.en: The office came from Qin as the privy treasurer of works; Emperor Jing renamed it master of works.
entries.literal: Original note says: Inherited from Qin, called privy treasurer of works; Emperor Jing changed it to master artisan.

entries.zh: 掌修作宗庙、路寝、宫室、陵园木土之功，并树桐梓之类列于道侧。
entries.en: He built and repaired imperial temples, inner halls, palaces, and mausoleum parks, and lined roadsides with paulownia and catalpa.
entries.literal: He is in charge of repair and construction of ancestral temples, route resting chamber, palaces, and mausoleum parks, works of timber and earth, and also planting paulownia, catalpa, and the like arrayed beside the roads.

entries.zh: 丞一人，六百石。
entries.en: He had one assistant at six hundred piculs.
entries.literal: One assistant, six hundred piculs.

entries.zh: 太子门大夫，六百石。
entries.en: The crown prince's gate grandee held six hundred piculs.
entries.literal: Gate grandee of the heir, six hundred piculs.

entries.zh: 本注曰：《旧注》云职比郎将。
entries.en: An old commentary compares the post to a captain of the guard.
entries.literal: Original note says: The old note says duties are comparable to a captain of the guard.

entries.zh: 旧有左右户将，别主左右户直郎，建武以来省之。
entries.en: Formerly left and right household captains had commanded the door guards, but Emperor Guangwu abolished them.
entries.literal: Formerly there were left and right household generals, separately in charge of left and right household gentlemen on duty; from Jianwu onward they were abolished.

entries.zh: 司隶校尉一人，比二千石。
entries.en: The colonel director of retainers was ranked at two thousand piculs.
entries.literal: One colonel director of retainers, salary comparable to two thousand piculs.

entries.zh: 本注曰：孝武帝初置，持節，掌察举百官以下，及京师近郡犯法者。
entries.en: Emperor Wu first created the post with a credential baton to impeach capital officials and wrongdoers in the home commanderies around Luoyang.
entries.literal: Original note says: Emperor Wu at first established it; he held the staff of authority; he is in charge of investigating and reporting all officials downward and those who violate the law in the capital region and neighboring commanderies.

entries.zh: 元帝去節，成帝省，建武中复置，并领一州。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan stripped the baton; Emperor Cheng abolished the office; Emperor Guangwu restored it and added authority over one province.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan removed the staff; Emperor Cheng abolished it; in the Jianwu era it was restored and also headed one province.

entries.zh: 从事史十二人。
entries.en: He had twelve attendants.
entries.literal: Twelve attendant clerks.

entries.zh: 本注曰：都官从事，主察举百官犯法者。
entries.en: The capital-bureau attendant impeached metropolitan officials who broke the law.
entries.literal: Original note says: Capital bureau attendant: in charge of investigating and reporting officials who violate the law.

entries.zh: 功曹从事，主州选署及众事。
entries.en: The merit clerk handled provincial appointments and general administration.
entries.literal: Merit bureau attendant: in charge of provincial selections and appointments and the multitude of affairs.

entries.zh: 别驾从事，校尉行部则奉引，录众事。
entries.en: The separate-car attendant led the colonel's inspection tours and kept his records.
entries.literal: Separate-car attendant: when the colonel inspects departments, then he leads the train and records the multitude of affairs.

entries.zh: 簿曹从事，主財穀簿書。
entries.en: The accounts clerk managed fiscal ledgers and grain registers.
entries.literal: Ledger bureau attendant: in charge of ledgers of wealth, grain, and documents.

entries.zh: 其有军事，则置兵曹从事，主兵事。
entries.en: In wartime a military-affairs clerk was added to the staff.
entries.literal: If there is military affairs, then a military bureau attendant is established, in charge of military affairs.

entries.zh: 其餘部郡国从事，每郡国各一人，主督促文书，察举非法，皆州自辟除，故通為百石云。
entries.en: Each commandery and kingdom also had one provincial clerk to push paperwork and report abuses; provinces hired them locally, so they were loosely treated as hundred-picul posts.
entries.literal: As for the remaining department commandery-kingdom attendants, each commandery and kingdom each has one person, in charge of urging documents, investigating and reporting what is unlawful; all are personally recruited by the province; therefore collectively they are called one hundred piculs, it is said.

entries.zh: 假佐二十五人。
entries.en: There were twenty-five subordinate aides.
entries.literal: Twenty-five deputy assistants.
