entries.en: The edict approved it.
entries.literal: An edict approved this.

entries.zh: 大定十九年，奉上孝成皇帝諡號。
entries.en: In Dading 19 the court presented the posthumous title of Emperor Xiaocheng.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year of Dading, the honorific title of Emperor Xiaocheng was presented.

entries.zh: 元年十一月十六日，詔曰：「前君乃太祖之長孫，受太宗之遺命，嗣膺神器，十有五年。
entries.en: On the sixteenth day of the eleventh month of the first year an edict stated: 'The former ruler was the eldest grandson of Emperor Taizu; he received Emperor Taizong's testamentary mandate, succeeded to the throne, and reigned for fifteen years.
entries.literal: On the sixteenth day of the eleventh month of the first year, an edict stated: 'The former ruler was the eldest grandson of Emperor Taizu; he received the testamentary mandate of Emperor Taizong, succeeded to the sacred vessel, and reigned for fifteen years.

entries.zh: 垂拱仰成，委任勳戚，廢齊國以省徭賦，柔宋人而息兵戈，世格泰和，俗躋仁壽，混車書於南北，一尉候於東西。
entries.en: He ruled by deferring to accomplished ministers, entrusted affairs to meritorious kinsmen, abolished the Qi state to lighten corvée and taxes, treated the Song people gently and stilled the weapons of war; the age attained great peace, customs rose to benevolence and longevity, chariots and books were united north and south, and frontier posts were made one from east to west.
entries.literal: He ruled by deferring to accomplished ministers, entrusted affairs to meritorious kinsmen, abolished the Qi state to reduce corvée and taxes, treated the Song people gently and stilled the weapons of war; the age attained great peace, customs rose to benevolence and longevity, chariots and books were united north and south, and frontier posts were made one from east to west.

entries.zh: 晚雖淫刑，幾於恣意，冤施弟後，戮及良工，虐不及民，事猶可諫，過之至此，古或有焉。
entries.en: In his later years he used excessive punishments and came near to acting at will—wrongfully punishing his younger brother's widow and killing worthy craftsmen—yet his cruelty did not reach the common people, and the matter could still be remonstrated against; that excess reached this point is something even the ancients sometimes did.
entries.literal: In his later years, though he used excessive punishments and came near to acting at will—wrongfully punishing his younger brother's widow and killing worthy craftsmen—his cruelty did not reach the common people, and the matter could still be remonstrated against; that excess reached this point is something the ancients sometimes did.

entries.zh: 右丞相岐國王亮不務弼諧，反行篡弑，妄加黜廢，抑損徽稱。
entries.en: Chief Councillor on the right, Prince of Qi Liang, did not devote himself to harmonious assistance but instead carried out usurpation and regicide, recklessly imposing dismissal and degradation and diminishing the former ruler's posthumous title.
entries.literal: The Chief Councillor on the right, Prince of Qi Liang, did not devote himself to harmonious assistance but instead carried out usurpation and regicide, recklessly imposing dismissal and degradation and diminishing the former ruler's honorific title.

entries.zh: 遠近傷嗟，神人憤怒，天方悔禍，朕乃繼興，受天下之樂推，居域中之有大。
entries.en: Near and far mourned; spirits and men were enraged; Heaven was about to repent of the calamity, and I then succeeded, receiving the willing submission of all under Heaven and occupying the great position within the realm.
entries.literal: Near and far mourned and sighed; spirits and men were enraged; Heaven was about to repent of the calamity, and I then succeeded and arose, receiving the willing submission of all under Heaven and occupying the great position within the realm.

entries.zh: 將撥亂而反正，務在革非。
entries.en: I shall quell disorder and restore rectitude, striving above all to reform what is wrong.
entries.literal: I shall quell disorder and restore rectitude, striving above all to reform what is wrong.

entries.zh: 期事亡以如存，聿思盡禮。
entries.en: I expect to treat the dead as if they still lived and think constantly of fulfilling every rite.
entries.literal: I expect to treat the dead as if they still lived and think constantly of fulfilling every rite.

entries.zh: 宜上諡號曰閔宗武靈皇帝。」
entries.en: The posthumous title Emperor Minzong Wuling should be conferred.'
entries.literal: The honorific title Emperor Minzong Wuling should be conferred.'

entries.zh: 十八年，有司言：「本朝祖宗尊諡或十八字，或十四字，或十二字，或四字。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year the relevant offices stated: 'The posthumous titles of our dynasty's imperial ancestors are either eighteen, fourteen, twelve, or four characters in length.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, the relevant offices stated: 'The honorific titles of the imperial ancestors of our dynasty are either eighteen characters, fourteen characters, twelve characters, or four characters.

entries.zh: 今擬增上閔宗尊諡曰弘基纘武莊靖孝成皇帝，仍加諡悼皇后曰悼平皇后。」
entries.en: It is now proposed to augment Minzong's posthumous title to Emperor Hongji Zuowu Zhuangjing Xiaocheng, and to add for Empress Dao the title Empress Daoping.'
entries.literal: It is now proposed to augment Minzong's honorific title to Emperor Hongji Zuowu Zhuangjing Xiaocheng, and to add for Empress Dao the title Empress Daoping.'

entries.zh: 又言：「大定三年追尊睿宗皇帝禮儀，大安殿前立黃麾仗一千人，應天門外行仗二千人，皇帝服通天冠、絳紗袍，隨冊寶降自西階，搢圭，跪，捧冊寶授太尉。
entries.en: They stated again: 'In the Dading 3 ritual for posthumously honoring Emperor Ruizong, one thousand yellow-banner guards were stationed before Da'an Hall and two thousand outer guards before Yingtian Gate; the emperor wore the tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, followed the registers and seals down the western steps, inserted the jade tablet, knelt, and presented the registers and seals to the Grand Mentor.
entries.literal: They stated again: 'In the ritual for posthumously honoring Emperor Ruizong in the third year of Dading, one thousand yellow-banner guards were stationed before Da'an Hall and two thousand outer guards before Yingtian Gate; the emperor wore the tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, followed the registers and seals down the western steps, inserted the jade tablet, knelt, and presented the registers and seals to the Grand Mentor.

entries.zh: 今擬大安殿行禮，及依唐、周典故，降階捧冊寶授太尉。
entries.en: It is now proposed to perform the rite in Da'an Hall and, following Tang and Zhou precedent, to descend the steps, hold the registers and seals, and present them to the Grand Mentor.
entries.literal: It is now proposed to perform the rite in Da'an Hall and, following the precedents of Tang and Zhou, to descend the steps, hold the registers and seals, and present them to the Grand Mentor.

entries.zh: 所有冠冕儀仗擬依已行禮例。」
entries.en: Crowns, robes, and ceremonial escorts are to follow the ritual precedents already established.'
entries.literal: All crowns, robes, and ceremonial guards are proposed to follow the ritual precedents already carried out.'

entries.zh: 上命儀仗人數約量減之，餘略同前儀。
entries.en: The emperor ordered the ceremonial guard reduced by roughly half; otherwise the rite largely followed the previous one.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered that the number of ceremonial guards be reduced by roughly half; the remainder was largely the same as the previous rite.

entries.zh: 明年四月十日，奉上冊寶，升祔太廟。
entries.en: On the tenth day of the fourth month of the following year the court presented the registers and seals and enshrined him in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: On the tenth day of the fourth month of the following year, the registers and seals were presented and he was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 二十六年，敕再議閔宗廟號，禮官擬上「襄、威、敬、定、桓、烈、熙」七字，奉旨用「熙」字，乃以明年四月一日，遣官奏告太廟及閔宗本室，易新廟號。
entries.en: In year 26 an edict ordered further deliberation on Minzong's temple name; ritual officials proposed seven characters—'xiang,' 'wei,' 'jing,' 'ding,' 'huan,' 'lie,' and 'xi'—and by imperial order 'xi' was chosen; on the first day of the fourth month of the following year officials were sent to announce at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and at Minzong's own chamber, adopting the new temple name.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, an edict ordered further deliberation on Minzong's temple name; the ritual officials proposed seven characters—'xiang,' 'wei,' 'jing,' 'ding,' 'huan,' 'lie,' and 'xi'—and by imperial order the character 'xi' was adopted; on the first day of the fourth month of the following year officials were dispatched to present memorial announcements at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and at Minzong's own chamber, changing to the new temple name.

entries.zh: 上尊諡
entries.en: Posthumous Honorific Titles
entries.literal: Conferring Posthumous Honorific Titles

entries.zh: 太宗天會二年，立大聖皇帝廟于西京。
entries.en: In Taizong's second Tianhui year, a temple to the Great Sage Emperor was erected in the Western Capital.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianhui under Emperor Taizong, a temple to the Great Sage Emperor was established in the Western Capital.

entries.zh: 熙宗天眷二年九月，又以上京慶元宮為太祖皇帝原廟。
entries.en: In the ninth month of Xizong's second Tianjuan year, the Qingyuan Palace in the Upper Capital was also designated as the original shrine of Emperor Taizu.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Tianjuan under Emperor Xizong, the Qingyuan Palace in the Upper Capital was likewise made the original temple of Emperor Taizu.

entries.zh: 皇統七年，有司奏：「慶元宮門舊日景暉，殿日辰居，似非廟中之名，今宜改殿名曰世德。」
entries.en: In Huangtong 7, the responsible offices reported: "The Qingyuan Palace gate was once called Jinghui and its hall Chenju—names ill suited to an ancestral shrine. The hall should now be renamed Shide."
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Huangtong, the relevant offices memorialized: "Formerly the gate of Qingyuan Palace was called Jinghui and the hall Chenju—names that seem unsuitable for a temple; the hall should now be renamed Shide."

entries.zh: 是歲，東京禦容殿成。
entries.en: That same year, the Imperial Portrait Hall in the Eastern Capital was completed.
entries.literal: That year, the Imperial Portrait Hall in the Eastern Capital was completed.

entries.zh: 世宗大定二年十二月，詔以「會寧府國家興王之地，宜就慶元宮址建正殿九間，仍其舊號，以時薦享」。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of Shizong's second Dading year, an edict declared: "Huining Prefecture is where the dynasty first rose to kingship. A main hall of nine bays should be built on the Qingyuan Palace site, keeping its former name, with offerings presented each season."
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Dading under Emperor Shizong, an edict stated: "Huining Prefecture is the place where the state rose to kingship; a main hall of nine bays should be built on the site of Qingyuan Palace, retaining its former name, with seasonal offerings."

entries.zh: 海陵天德四年，有司言：「燕京興建太廟，複立原廟。
entries.en: In Hailing's fourth Tiande year, the responsible offices reported: "With the Grand Ancestral Temple rising in Yanjing, original shrines should be re-established as well.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tiande under Prince Hailing, the relevant offices stated: "The Grand Ancestral Temple is being built in Yanjing, and original temples are to be re-established.

entries.zh: 三代以前無原廟制，至漢惠帝始置廟于長安渭北，薦以時果，其後又置於豐、沛，不聞享薦之禮。
entries.en: Before the Three Dynasties there was no institution of original shrines. Emperor Huidi of Han was the first to establish temples north of the Wei at Chang'an, offering seasonal fruits; later shrines were also set up at Feng and Pei, but no full rites of sacrifice and offering are recorded for them.
entries.literal: Before the Three Dynasties there was no system of original temples; it was only under Emperor Huidi of Han that temples were first set up north of the Wei River at Chang'an, with seasonal fruits offered; later they were also set up at Feng and Pei, but no rites of offering and sacrifice are recorded.

entries.zh: 今兩都告享宜止於燕京所建原廟行事。」
entries.en: For the present, report offerings at the two capitals should be performed only at the original shrine built in Yanjing."
entries.literal: At present, report offerings at the two capitals should be conducted only at the original temple built in Yanjing."

entries.zh: 於是，名其宮曰衍慶，殿曰聖武，門曰崇聖。
entries.en: The palace was then named Yansqing, its hall Shengwu, and its gate Chongsheng.
entries.literal: Thereupon the palace was named Yansqing, the hall Shengwu, and the gate Chongsheng.

entries.zh: 大定十六年四月十九日，奉安世祖禦容，行朝謁之禮。
entries.en: On the nineteenth day of the fourth month of Dading 16, Emperor Shizu's portrait was installed and the pilgrimage audience rites were performed.
entries.literal: On the nineteenth day of the fourth month of the sixteenth year of Dading, the imperial portrait of Emperor Shizu was reverently installed and the rites of pilgrimage audience performed.

entries.zh: 皇帝前一日齋於內殿，皇太子齋于本宮，親王齋于本府，百官齋於其第。
entries.en: On the previous day the emperor observed purification in the inner hall, the crown prince in his palace, princes in their mansions, and officials at their residences.
entries.literal: The emperor observed purification in the inner hall on the previous day; the crown prince in his palace; princes in their mansions; officials at their residences.

entries.zh: 太廟令率其屬，于衍慶宮內外掃除，設親王百官拜位於殿庭，又設皇太子拜褥于親王百官位前。
entries.en: The director of the Grand Ancestral Temple led his staff in sweeping Yansqing Palace inside and out, arranged bowing stations for princes and all officials in the forecourt, and set the crown prince's kneeling mat before their stations.
entries.literal: The director of the Grand Ancestral Temple led his subordinates in sweeping inside and outside Yansqing Palace, set the bowing places of princes and all officials in the forecourt, and set the crown prince's kneeling mat before the places of princes and officials.

entries.zh: 宣徽院率其屬，于聖武門外之東設西向禦幄，靈星門東設皇太子幄次。
entries.en: The Palace Domestic Service led its staff in setting a west-facing imperial enclosure east of Shengwu Gate and the crown prince's enclosure east of Lingxing Gate.
entries.literal: The Palace Domestic Service led its subordinates in setting a west-facing imperial enclosure east of Shengwu Gate, and the crown prince's enclosure east of Lingxing Gate.

entries.zh: 其日，有司列仗衛于應天門，俟奉安禦容訖，有司於殿上並神御前設北向拜褥位，安置香爐香案並香酒器物等。
entries.en: That day the responsible offices arrayed guards at Yingtian Gate. When the portrait installation was complete, they set north-facing kneeling mats on the hall and before the spirit seat and arranged censers, incense tables, incense, wine, vessels, and the like.
entries.literal: That day the relevant offices arrayed guards at Yingtian Gate; when the installation of the portrait was complete, they set north-facing kneeling mats on the hall and before the spirit seat, and arranged censers, incense tables, incense, wine, vessels, and the like.

entries.zh: 皇太子比至車駕進發已前，公服乘馬，本宮官屬導從，至衍慶宮門西下馬，步入幄次。
entries.en: The crown prince arrived before the imperial procession set out, riding in court dress with his palace officials guiding and attending. West of Yansqing Palace gate he dismounted and entered his enclosure on foot.
entries.literal: The crown prince, arriving before the imperial procession set out, rode in formal dress with officials of his palace guiding and attending; west of Yansqing Palace gate he dismounted and entered his enclosure on foot.

entries.zh: 親王百官于衍慶宮門外西向立班。
entries.en: Princes and all officials formed west-facing ranks outside Yansqing Palace gate.
entries.literal: Princes and all officials formed west-facing ranks outside the gate of Yansqing Palace.

entries.zh: 俟車駕將至，典贊儀引皇太子出幄次，于親王百官班前奉迎。
entries.en: When the imperial procession was about to arrive, the master of ritual praise led the crown prince out of his enclosure to welcome it before the ranks of princes and officials.
entries.literal: When the imperial procession was about to arrive, the master of ritual praise led the crown prince out of his enclosure to welcome it before the ranks of princes and officials.

entries.zh: 導駕官，五品六品七品職官內差四十員于應天門外道南立班以俟。
entries.en: Forty officials of the fifth, sixth, and seventh ranks were selected as procession guides and formed ranks south of the road outside Yingtian Gate to await the emperor.
entries.literal: Forty officials of the fifth, sixth, and seventh ranks were selected from among those holding posts to serve as procession guides, forming ranks south of the road outside Yingtian Gate to await.

entries.zh: 皇帝服靴袍乘輦，從官傘扇侍衛如常儀。
entries.en: The emperor wore boots and robe and rode in the palanquin; attendant officials with umbrellas, fans, and guards followed the usual protocol.
entries.literal: The emperor wore boots and robe and rode in the palanquin; attendant officials with umbrellas, fans, and guards followed the usual rites.

entries.zh: 敕旨用大安輦、儀仗一千人。
entries.en: By imperial command the Da'an palanquin was used with a ceremonial guard of one thousand.
entries.literal: By imperial command the Da'an palanquin was used and one thousand ceremonial guards.

entries.zh: 出應天門，閣門通喝：「導駕官再拜。」
entries.en: Exiting Yingtian Gate, the Gate Department called out: "Procession guides, bow twice."
entries.literal: Exiting Yingtian Gate, the Gate Department called out: "Procession guides, bow twice."

entries.zh: 訖，閣門傳敕：「道駕官上馬。」
entries.en: When this was done, the Gate Department transmitted the command: "Procession guides, mount."
entries.literal: When finished, the Gate Department transmitted the command: "Procession guides, mount."

entries.zh: 分左右前導，至廟門外西偏下馬。
entries.en: They guided ahead on either side and dismounted west of the temple gate.
entries.literal: They guided ahead left and right; west of the temple gate they dismounted.

entries.zh: 車駕至衍慶宮門外稍西降輦。
entries.en: The imperial procession reached slightly west of Yansqing Palace's outer gate and the emperor descended from the palanquin.
entries.literal: The imperial procession reached slightly west of the outer gate of Yansqing Palace and the emperor descended from the palanquin.

entries.zh: 左右宣徽使前導，皇帝步入禦幄，簾降。
entries.en: The left and right commissioners of the Palace Domestic Service guided ahead; the emperor entered the imperial enclosure on foot and the curtain was lowered.
entries.literal: The left and right commissioners of the Palace Domestic Service guided ahead; the emperor entered the imperial enclosure on foot and the curtain was lowered.

entries.zh: 閣門先引親王、宰執、四品已上執事官，由東西偏門入，至殿庭分東西班相向立。
entries.en: The Gate Department first led in princes, chief councillors, and officiating officials of the fourth rank and above through the east and west side gates; in the forecourt they divided into east and west ranks facing each other.
entries.literal: The Gate Department first led in princes, chief councillors, and officiating officials of the fourth rank and above through the east and west side gates; in the forecourt they divided into east and west ranks facing each other.

entries.zh: 典贊儀引皇太子入，立於褥位之西，東向。
entries.en: The master of ritual praise led the crown prince in to stand west of the kneeling mat, facing east.
entries.literal: The master of ritual praise led the crown prince in; he stood west of the kneeling mat, facing east.

entries.zh: 進香進酒等執事官並升階，於殿上分東西向以次立。
entries.en: The officiating officials for presenting incense and wine all ascended the steps and stood in east and west ranks on the hall in order.
entries.literal: The officiating officials for presenting incense and wine all ascended the steps and on the hall stood in east and west ranks in order.

entries.zh: 宣徽使跪奏：「請皇帝行朝謁之禮。」
entries.en: The commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service knelt and reported: "We request that Your Majesty perform the pilgrimage audience rites."
entries.literal: The commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service knelt and reported: "We request that the emperor perform the rites of pilgrimage audience."

entries.zh: 簾卷，皇帝出幄。
entries.en: The curtain was raised and the emperor emerged from the enclosure.
entries.literal: The curtain was raised and the emperor emerged from the enclosure.

entries.zh: 宣徽使前導，至殿上褥位，北向立。
entries.en: The commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service guided him to the kneeling mat on the hall, where the emperor stood facing north.
entries.literal: The commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service guided ahead to the kneeling mat on the hall, where the emperor stood facing north.

entries.zh: 典贊儀引皇太子就褥位，閣門引親王宰執四品已上職事官回班，並北向立。
entries.en: The master of ritual praise led the crown prince to the kneeling mat; the Gate Department led princes, chief councillors, and duty officials of the fourth rank and above back to their ranks, all standing facing north.
entries.literal: The master of ritual praise led the crown prince to the kneeling mat; the Gate Department led princes, chief councillors, and duty officials of the fourth rank and above back to their ranks; all stood facing north.

entries.zh: 令中間歇空，不礙奏樂。
entries.en: They left an open space in the middle so the music would not be obstructed.
entries.literal: They left an open space in the middle so as not to obstruct the music.

entries.zh: 五品以下聖武門外、八品以下宮門外陪拜。
entries.en: Those of the fifth rank and below accompanied the bows outside Shengwu Gate; those of the eighth rank and below outside the palace gate.
entries.literal: Those of the fifth rank and below accompanied the bows outside Shengwu Gate; those of the eighth rank and below outside the palace gate.

entries.zh: 二宣徽使奏請，皇帝再拜，教坊樂作。
entries.en: The two commissioners of the Palace Domestic Service petitioned; the emperor bowed twice while the Court Music Office played.
entries.literal: The two commissioners of the Palace Domestic Service petitioned; the emperor bowed twice and the Court Music Office performed.

entries.zh: 皇太子已下群官皆再拜。
entries.en: The crown prince and all officials below him bowed twice.
entries.literal: The crown prince and all officials below him bowed twice.

entries.zh: 請皇帝詣神御前褥位，北向立，又請皇帝再拜，皇太子已下群官皆再拜。
entries.en: They requested that the emperor go to the kneeling mat before the spirit seat and stand facing north, then bow twice; the crown prince and all officials below him bowed twice as well.
entries.literal: They requested that the emperor go to the kneeling mat before the spirit seat and stand facing north; again they requested that the emperor bow twice, and the crown prince and all officials below him bowed twice.

entries.zh: 請皇帝跪 ，三上香，三奠酒，俯伏，興。
entries.en: They requested that the emperor kneel, offer incense three times, present wine three times, prostrate himself, and rise.
entries.literal: They requested that the emperor kneel, offer incense three times, present wine three times, prostrate himself, and rise.

entries.zh: 又請皇帝再拜，皇太子已下群官皆再拜，訖，皇帝復位。
entries.en: Again they requested that the emperor bow twice; the crown prince and all officials below him bowed twice. When this was done, the emperor returned to his place.
entries.literal: Again they requested that the emperor bow twice; the crown prince and all officials below him bowed twice; when finished, the emperor returned to his place.

entries.zh: 又請皇帝再拜，皇太子已下群官皆再拜。
entries.en: Again they requested that the emperor bow twice; the crown prince and all officials below him bowed twice.
entries.literal: Again they requested that the emperor bow twice; the crown prince and all officials below him bowed twice.

entries.zh: 宣徽使奏：「禮畢。」
entries.en: The commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service reported: "The rites are complete."
entries.literal: The commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service reported: "The rites are complete."

entries.zh: 已上擬八拜，宣徽院奏過，依舊例十二拜。
entries.en: The above proposed eight bows; the Palace Domestic Service reported this, and following old precedent twelve bows were used.
entries.literal: The above proposed eight bows; the Palace Domestic Service reported this and, following the old precedent, twelve bows were used.

entries.zh: 典贊儀引皇太子複立于褥位之西，東向。
entries.en: The master of ritual praise led the crown prince to stand again west of the kneeling mat, facing east.
entries.literal: The master of ritual praise led the crown prince to stand again west of the kneeling mat, facing east.

entries.zh: 閣門引親王宰執以下群官，東西相向立。
entries.en: The Gate Department led princes, chief councillors, and all officials below them to stand facing each other in east and west ranks.
entries.literal: The Gate Department led princes, chief councillors, and all officials below them to stand facing each other east and west.

entries.zh: 先引五品已下官出。
entries.en: They first led out officials of the fifth rank and below.
entries.literal: They first led out officials of the fifth rank and below.

entries.zh: 宣徽使前導，皇帝還禦幄，簾降。
entries.en: The commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service guided ahead; the emperor returned to the imperial enclosure and the curtain was lowered.
entries.literal: The commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service guided ahead; the emperor returned to the imperial enclosure and the curtain was lowered.

entries.zh: 典贊儀引皇太子，閣門分引殿庭百官，以次出。
entries.en: The master of ritual praise led the crown prince; the Gate Department led the officials in the forecourt out in separate groups, in order.
entries.literal: The master of ritual praise led the crown prince; the Gate Department led out the officials in the forecourt in separate groups, in order.

entries.zh: 宣徽使跪奏：「請皇帝還宮。」
entries.en: The commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service knelt and reported: "We request that Your Majesty return to the palace."
entries.literal: The commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service knelt and reported: "We request that the emperor return to the palace."

entries.zh: 簾卷，步出廟門外，升輦還宮，如來儀。
entries.en: The curtain was raised; he walked out beyond the temple gate, mounted the palanquin, and returned to the palace by the same protocol as on arrival.
entries.literal: The curtain was raised; he walked out beyond the temple gate, mounted the palanquin, and returned to the palace by the same rites as on arrival.

entries.zh: 十九年舉安禮同。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year the installation rite was the same.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year the installation rite was the same.

entries.zh: 初，太祖忌辰，皇帝至褥位立，再拜。
entries.en: Initially, on the anniversary of Emperor Taizu's death, the emperor came to the kneeling mat, stood, and bowed twice.
entries.literal: Initially, on the anniversary of Emperor Taizu's death, the emperor came to the kneeling mat, stood, and bowed twice.

entries.zh: 稍東，西向，詣香案前，又再拜。
entries.en: Slightly to the east, facing west, he went before the incense table and bowed twice again.
entries.literal: Slightly to the east, facing west, he went before the incense table and bowed twice again.

entries.zh: 上香訖，復位，又再拜。
entries.en: After offering incense he returned to his place and bowed twice again.
entries.literal: When incense was offered, he returned to his place and bowed twice again.

entries.zh: 進食、奠茶、辭神皆再拜而退。
entries.en: Presenting food, offering tea, and taking leave of the spirit were each performed with two bows before withdrawal.
entries.literal: Presenting food, offering tea, and taking leave of the spirit—all were performed with two bows and withdrawal.

entries.zh: 大定二十一年五月十二日，睿宗忌辰，有司更定儀禮。
entries.en: On the twelfth day of the fifth month of Dading 21, the anniversary of Emperor Ruizong's death, the responsible offices revised the ritual protocol.
entries.literal: On the twelfth day of the fifth month of the twenty-first year of Dading, the anniversary of Emperor Ruizong's death, the relevant offices revised the ritual protocol.

entries.zh: 前一日，宣徽院設禦幄於天興殿門外稍西。
entries.en: On the previous day the Palace Domestic Service set the imperial enclosure slightly west of Tianxing Hall's outer gate.
entries.literal: On the previous day the Palace Domestic Service set the imperial enclosure slightly west of the outer gate of Tianxing Hall.

entries.zh: 至日質明，皇太子親王百官具公服于衍慶宮門外立班，奉迎。
entries.en: At dawn that day, the crown prince, princes, and all officials in court dress formed ranks outside Yansqing Palace gate to welcome the emperor.
entries.literal: At dawn on the day, the crown prince, princes, and all officials in formal dress formed ranks outside the gate of Yansqing Palace to welcome him.

entries.zh: 皇帝乘馬至衍慶宮門外下馬，二宣徽使前導，步入宮門稍東。
entries.en: The emperor rode to Yansqing Palace gate and dismounted; the two commissioners of the Palace Domestic Service guided ahead as he entered the palace gate on foot, slightly to the east.
entries.literal: The emperor rode to outside the gate of Yansqing Palace and dismounted; the two commissioners of the Palace Domestic Service guided ahead; he entered the palace gate on foot slightly to the east.

entries.zh: 皇帝乘輦，傘扇侍衛如常儀，至天興殿門外稍西。
entries.en: The emperor rode in the palanquin with umbrellas, fans, and guards as usual to slightly west of Tianxing Hall's outer gate.
entries.literal: The emperor rode in the palanquin with umbrellas, fans, and guards as in the usual rites to slightly west of the outer gate of Tianxing Hall.

entries.zh: 皇帝降輦，入幄次，簾降，典贊儀引皇太子、閣門引親王宰執四品已上官由偏門入，至於殿庭，左右分班立定，二宣徽使導皇帝由天興門正門入，自東階升殿，詣褥位立定。
entries.en: The emperor descended from the palanquin and entered the enclosure; the curtain was lowered. The master of ritual praise led the crown prince; the Gate Department led princes, chief councillors, and officials of the fourth rank and above through the side gates to the forecourt, where they formed left and right ranks. The two commissioners guided the emperor through Tianxing Hall's main gate, up the east steps, to the kneeling mat.
entries.literal: The emperor descended from the palanquin, entered the enclosure, and the curtain was lowered; the master of ritual praise led the crown prince; the Gate Department led princes, chief councillors, and officials of the fourth rank and above through the side gates to the forecourt, where they formed left and right ranks; the two commissioners guided the emperor through the main gate of Tianxing Hall, ascended the east steps, and took his place at the kneeling mat.

entries.zh: 皇太子已下官合班，五品以下班於殿門外。
entries.en: Officials from the crown prince downward formed a combined rank; those of the fifth rank and below formed ranks outside the hall gate.
entries.literal: Officials from the crown prince downward formed a combined rank; those of the fifth rank and below formed ranks outside the hall gate.

entries.zh: 宣徽使奏：「請皇帝先再拜。
entries.en: The commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service reported: "We request that Your Majesty first bow twice.
entries.literal: The commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service reported: "We request that the emperor first bow twice.

entries.zh: 請詣侍神位立。」
entries.en: We request that you go to stand at the attendant spirit seat."
entries.literal: We request that you go to stand at the attendant spirit seat."

entries.zh: 俟有司置香案酒卓訖，請詣褥位，又再拜，三上香、奠酒，復位，再拜。
entries.en: When the responsible offices had set out the incense table and wine tables, they requested that he go to the kneeling mat, bow twice again, offer incense three times and present wine, return to his place, and bow twice.
entries.literal: When the relevant offices had set out the incense table and wine tables, they requested that he go to the kneeling mat, bow twice again, offer incense three times and present wine, return to his place, and bow twice.

entries.zh: 已上，皇太子以下皆陪拜。
entries.en: Throughout the above, from the crown prince downward all accompanied the bows.
entries.literal: In all the above, from the crown prince downward all accompanied the bows.

entries.zh: 再奏：「請詣稍東侍神位立。」
entries.en: They reported again: "We request that you go to stand at the attendant spirit seat slightly to the east."
entries.literal: They reported again: "We request that you go to stand at the attendant spirit seat slightly to the east."

entries.zh: 典贊儀引皇太子升殿赴褥位，先兩拜，奠酒再兩拜，降複褥位。
entries.en: The master of ritual praise led the crown prince up the hall to the kneeling mat; he bowed twice, presented wine and bowed twice again, then descended and returned to the kneeling mat.
entries.literal: The master of ritual praise led the crown prince up the hall to the kneeling mat; he first bowed twice, presented wine and bowed twice again, descended and returned to the kneeling mat.

entries.zh: 次閣門引終獻官趙王上殿行禮。
entries.en: Next the Gate Department led the Prince of Zhao, the final presenter, up the hall to perform the rites.
entries.literal: Next the Gate Department led the Prince of Zhao, the final presenter, up the hall to perform the rites.

entries.zh: 宣徽使奏：「請皇帝詣褥位。」
entries.en: The commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service reported: "We request that Your Majesty go to the kneeling mat."
entries.literal: The commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service reported: "We request that the emperor go to the kneeling mat."

entries.zh: 再兩拜。
entries.en: He bowed twice again.
entries.literal: He bowed twice again.

entries.zh: 皇太子以下官皆再拜。
entries.en: Officials from the crown prince downward all bowed twice.
entries.literal: Officials from the crown prince downward all bowed twice.

entries.zh: 禮畢，百官依前分班立。
entries.en: When the rites were complete, all officials stood in their former left and right ranks.
entries.literal: When the rites were complete, all officials stood in their former left and right ranks.

entries.zh: 皇帝出殿門外，入幄次，簾降，更衣。
entries.en: The emperor went outside the hall gate, entered the enclosure, the curtain was lowered, and he changed garments.
entries.literal: The emperor went outside the hall gate, entered the enclosure, the curtain was lowered, and he changed garments.

entries.zh: 次引皇太子以下官出宮門外立班。
entries.en: Next they led officials from the crown prince downward out beyond the palace gate to form ranks.
entries.literal: Next they led officials from the crown prince downward out beyond the palace gate to form ranks.

entries.zh: 皇帝乘輦，至宮門稍東降輦，步出宮門外，上馬還宮，導從侍衛如來儀。
entries.en: The emperor rode in the palanquin to slightly east of the palace gate and descended; he walked out beyond the palace gate, mounted, and returned to the palace with guides, attendants, and guards following the same protocol as on arrival.
entries.literal: The emperor rode in the palanquin to slightly east of the palace gate and descended; he walked out beyond the palace gate, mounted, and returned to the palace; guides, attendants, and guards followed the rites of arrival.

entries.zh: 皇太子以下官，俟車駕行然後退。
entries.en: Officials from the crown prince downward waited until the imperial procession had departed before withdrawing.
entries.literal: Officials from the crown prince downward waited until the imperial procession had set out before withdrawing.

entries.zh: 大定五年，奏旨：「太祖忌辰，衍慶宮薦享止用素食，諸京凡禦容所在皆同。
entries.en: In Dading 5, a memorial to the throne stated: "On the anniversary of Emperor Taizu's death, offerings at Yansqing Palace should use only vegetarian food; all capitals where imperial portraits are kept should follow the same rule.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Dading, a memorial to the throne stated: "On the anniversary of Emperor Taizu's death, offerings at Yansqing Palace should use only vegetarian food; all capitals where imperial portraits are kept should follow the same rule.

entries.zh: 又朔望皆行朝拜禮。」
entries.en: On the first and fifteenth of each month the court audience rites should also be performed."
entries.literal: On the first and fifteenth of each month the court audience rites should also be performed."

entries.zh: 六年，有司奏：「太祖皇帝忌辰，車駕親奠，百官陪拜。
entries.en: In the sixth year, the responsible offices memorialized: "On the anniversary of Emperor Taizu's death, the emperor presents offerings in person and all officials accompany the bows.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, the relevant offices memorialized: "On the anniversary of Emperor Taizu's death, the imperial procession presents offerings in person and all officials accompany the bows.

entries.zh: 今車駕巡幸，合以宰臣為班首，率百官詣衍慶宮行禮。」
entries.en: Now that the emperor is on tour, the chief minister should lead the rank and take all officials to Yansqing Palace to perform the rites."
entries.literal: Now that the imperial procession is on tour, the chief minister should serve as lead of the rank and lead all officials to Yansqing Palace to perform the rites."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The memorial was approved.
entries.literal: The memorial was approved.

entries.zh: 十六年，奉旨：「世祖、太宗忌辰，一體奉奠。」
entries.en: In the sixteenth year, by imperial command: "On the anniversaries of Emperors Shizu and Taizong, offerings should be presented together."
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, by imperial command: "On the anniversaries of Emperors Shizu and Taizong, offerings should be presented together."

entries.zh: 十八年八月，太祖忌辰 ，世祖、太宗同在一處致祭，有司言「歷代無一聖忌辰列聖預祭之典。」
entries.en: In the eighth month of the eighteenth year, on the anniversary of Emperor Taizu's death, Emperors Shizu and Taizong were sacrificed to at the same site. The responsible offices stated: "Through the ages there is no precedent for other sage-emperors to receive preliminary sacrifice on one sage-emperor's anniversary."
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the eighteenth year, on the anniversary of Emperor Taizu's death, Emperors Shizu and Taizong were sacrificed to at the same place; the relevant offices stated: "Through the ages there is no precedent for other sage-emperors to receive preliminary sacrifice on one sage-emperor's anniversary."

entries.zh: 擬議間，敕遣太子，一位行禮，並諸祭功臣。
entries.en: While deliberation was underway, an edict dispatched the crown prince to perform the rites for one seat and sacrifices to meritorious ministers as well.
entries.literal: While deliberation was underway, an edict dispatched the crown prince to perform the rites for one seat, and sacrifices to meritorious ministers as well.

entries.zh: 二十六年，以內外祖廟不同，定擬：「太廟每歲五享，山陵朔、望、忌辰及節辰祭奠並依前代典故外，衍慶宮自來車駕行幸，遇祖宗忌辰百官行禮，並詣京祖廟節辰、忌辰、朔、望拜奠，雖無典故參酌，恐合依舊，以盡崇奉之意。」
entries.en: In the twenty-sixth year, because the inner and outer ancestral temples differed, it was decided: "The Grand Ancestral Temple holds five offerings each year; at the mountain tombs, sacrifices on the first and fifteenth, anniversaries, and festival days follow precedents of former ages. Apart from these, at Yansqing Palace the emperor has always paid visits; on ancestral anniversaries all officials perform the rites, and at the capital ancestral temples they bow and present offerings on festival days, anniversaries, and the first and fifteenth—though there is no clear precedent, they should follow established practice to fulfill the intent of reverent veneration."
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, because the inner and outer ancestral temples differed, it was decided: "The Grand Ancestral Temple holds five offerings each year; at the mountain tombs, sacrifices on the first and fifteenth, anniversaries, and festival days follow precedents of former ages. Apart from these, at Yansqing Palace the imperial procession has always paid visits; on ancestral anniversaries all officials perform the rites, and at the capital ancestral temples they bow and present offerings on festival days, anniversaries, and the first and fifteenth—though there is no precedent to consult, it is feared they should follow the old practice to fulfill the intent of reverent veneration."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The proposal was approved.
entries.literal: The proposal was approved.

entries.zh: 十五年二月，有司言東京開覺寺藏睿宗皇帝皁衣展裹真容，敕遷本京祖廟奉祀，仍易袍色。
entries.en: In the second month of the fifteenth year, the responsible offices reported that Kaijue Temple in the Eastern Capital held the true portrait of Emperor Ruizong in black robes with outspread wrapping. An edict ordered it moved to the capital's ancestral temple for worship and the robe color changed.
entries.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year, the relevant offices stated that Kaijue Temple in the Eastern Capital held the true portrait of Emperor Ruizong in black robes with outspread wrapping; an edict ordered it transferred to the ancestral temple of the capital for worship, and the robe color changed.

entries.zh: 明年四月，詔依奉安睿宗禮，奉安世祖禦容于衍慶宮。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the following year, an edict directed that the imperial portrait of Emperor Shizu be installed in Yansqing Palace following the rites used for Emperor Ruizong.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the following year, an edict ordered that the imperial portrait of Emperor Shizu be reverently installed in Yansqing Palace according to the rites used for Emperor Ruizong.

entries.zh: 前期，有司備香案、酒果、教坊樂。
entries.en: Beforehand, the responsible offices prepared incense tables, wine and fruit, and musicians from the Court Music Office.
entries.literal: Beforehand, the relevant offices prepared incense tables, wine and fruit, and Court Music Office performers.

entries.zh: 至日質明，親王宰執率百官公服迎引至衍慶宮，凡用甲騎百人，傘二人，扇十二人、香輿八人、彩輿十六人、從者二十四人、執事官二人，弩手控鶴各五十人、贊者二人、禮直官二人，六品以下官三十員公服乘馬前導。
entries.en: At dawn that day, princes and chief councillors led all officials in court dress to welcome and escort the portrait to Yansqing Palace: one hundred armored horsemen, two umbrellas, twelve fan-bearers, eight incense-carriage bearers, sixteen colored-carriage bearers, twenty-four attendants, two officiating officials, fifty crossbowmen and fifty crane handlers, two announcers, two ritual protocol officers, and thirty officials of the sixth rank and below in court dress riding ahead as guides.
entries.literal: At dawn on the day, princes and chief councillors led all officials in formal dress to welcome and escort the portrait to Yansqing Palace—employing in all one hundred armored horsemen, two umbrellas, twelve fan-bearers, eight incense-carriage bearers, sixteen colored-carriage bearers, twenty-four attendants, two officiating officials, fifty crossbowmen and fifty crane handlers each, two announcers, two ritual protocol officers, and thirty officials of the sixth rank and below in formal dress riding ahead as guides.

entries.zh: 奉安訖，百官再拜，禮畢，退立宮門之外，迎駕朝謁。
entries.en: Once installation was complete, all officials bowed twice. The rite concluded; they withdrew to stand outside the palace gate to welcome the emperor for the pilgrimage audience.
entries.literal: When the installation was complete, all officials bowed twice; the rite concluded; they withdrew and stood outside the palace gate to welcome the emperor for the pilgrimage audience.

entries.zh: 十六年正月，有司奏：「奉敕議世祖皇帝禦容當於何處安置。
entries.en: In the first month of the sixteenth year, the responsible offices memorialized: "By imperial command we have deliberated where the imperial portrait of Emperor Shizu should be installed.
entries.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year, the relevant offices memorialized: "By imperial command we deliberated where the imperial portrait of Emperor Shizu should be installed.

entries.zh: 臣等參詳衍慶宮即漢之原廟，每遇太祖皇帝忌辰，百官朝拜。
entries.en: We find that Yansqing Palace is the Han-style original shrine; on each anniversary of Emperor Taizu's death all officials perform the court audience.
entries.literal: We have examined that Yansqing Palace is the Han-style original temple; on each anniversary of Emperor Taizu's death all officials perform the court audience.

entries.zh: 今世祖皇帝擇地修建殿位，庶可副嚴奉之意。」
entries.en: For Emperor Shizu, selecting a site and building a hall would fulfill the intent of reverent veneration."
entries.literal: For Emperor Shizu, selecting a site and building a hall would fulfill the intent of reverent veneration."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The memorial was approved.
entries.literal: The memorial was approved.

entries.zh: 乃敕于聖武殿東西興建世祖、太宗、睿宗殿位。
entries.en: An edict then ordered halls for Emperors Shizu, Taizong, and Ruizong built to the east and west of Shengwu Hall.
entries.literal: An edict then ordered halls for Emperors Shizu, Taizong, and Ruizong built to the east and west of Shengwu Hall.

entries.zh: 既而複欲擇地建太宗殿於歸仁館，有司言：「山陵太祖、太宗、睿宗共一兆域，太廟世祖、太祖、太宗、睿宗亦同堂異室。
entries.en: Later they again wished to build a hall for Emperor Taizong at Guiren Lodge. The responsible offices reported: "At the mountain tombs, Emperors Taizu, Taizong, and Ruizong share one burial precinct; in the Grand Ancestral Temple, Emperors Shizu, Taizu, Taizong, and Ruizong share one hall with separate chambers.
entries.literal: Later they again wished to choose a site and build a hall for Emperor Taizong at Guiren Lodge; the relevant offices stated: "At the mountain tombs, Emperors Taizu, Taizong, and Ruizong share one burial precinct; in the Grand Ancestral Temple, Emperors Shizu, Taizu, Taizong, and Ruizong also share one hall with separate chambers.

entries.zh: 今于歸仁館興建太宗殿位，似與山陵、太廟之制不同。」
entries.en: Building a separate hall for Emperor Taizong at Guiren Lodge now would seem inconsistent with the systems of the mountain tombs and Grand Ancestral Temple."
entries.literal: To build a hall for Emperor Taizong at Guiren Lodge now seems inconsistent with the systems of the mountain tombs and Grand Ancestral Temple."

entries.zh: 詔從前議，止于衍慶宮各建殿七間、閣五間、三門五間。
entries.en: An edict followed the earlier proposal: at Yansqing Palace alone, each emperor received a hall of seven bays, a pavilion of five bays, and triple gates of five bays.
entries.literal: An edict followed the earlier proposal: only at Yansqing Palace were halls of seven bays, pavilions of five bays, and triple gates of five bays built for each.

entries.zh: 乃定世祖殿曰廣德、閣曰燕昌，太宗殿曰丕承、閣曰光昭，睿宗殿曰天興、閣曰景福。
entries.en: Shizu's hall was named Guangde and his pavilion Yanchang; Taizong's hall Picheng and pavilion Guangzhao; Ruizong's hall Tianxing and pavilion Jingfu.
entries.literal: Thereupon Shizu's hall was named Guangde and his pavilion Yanchang; Taizong's hall Picheng and pavilion Guangzhao; Ruizong's hall Tianxing and pavilion Jingfu.

entries.zh: 十九年五月六日，奏告。
entries.en: On the sixth day of the fifth month of the nineteenth year, a report was made to the temple.
entries.literal: On the sixth day of the fifth month of the nineteenth year, a report was made to the temple.

entries.zh: 七日，奉安。
entries.en: On the seventh day, the installation rite was performed.
entries.literal: On the seventh day, the reverent installation was performed.

entries.zh: 執事禮官二人，每位香案一、祭器席一、拜褥二、盥洗一、大勺篚巾全。
entries.en: Two ritual officiants were assigned; for each seat there was one incense table, one mat of sacrificial vessels, two kneeling mats, one hand-washing station, and a complete set of ladles, baskets, and towels.
entries.literal: Two ritual officiants were assigned; for each seat, one incense table, one mat of sacrificial vessels, two kneeling mats, one hand-washing station, and a complete set of ladles, baskets, and towels.

entries.zh: 前一日，太廟令率其屬掃除宮內外，又各設神座於殿上，又設親王宰執以下百官拜位於殿庭。
entries.en: On the previous day, the director of the Grand Ancestral Temple led his staff in sweeping the palace inside and out, set spirit seats on the hall for each emperor, and arranged bowing stations in the forecourt for princes, chief councillors, and all officials below them.
entries.literal: On the previous day, the director of the Grand Ancestral Temple led his subordinates in sweeping inside and outside the palace, set out spirit seats on the hall for each, and set the bowing places in the forecourt for princes, chief councillors, and all officials below them.

entries.zh: 又設盥洗位於東階下，執罍篚者位於其後。
entries.en: A hand-washing station was also set below the east steps, with bearers of ewers and baskets stationed behind it.
entries.literal: A hand-washing station was also set below the east steps, with the bearers of ewers and baskets behind it.

entries.zh: 又於神位前各設北向拜褥位，並各設香案香爐匙合香酒花果器皿物等，依前來例。
entries.en: Before each spirit seat a north-facing kneeling mat was set, with incense tables, censers, spoons, boxes, incense, wine, fruit, flowers, vessels, and the like arranged for each according to precedent.
entries.literal: Before each spirit seat a north-facing kneeling mat was set, and for each an incense table, censer, spoons, boxes, incense, wine, fruit, flowers, vessels, and the like were set out according to precedent.

entries.zh: 又于聖武殿上設香案爐匙合香等，又于殿下各設腰輿一、舁士一十六人、傘子各二人、執扇各十二人、導從弩手各三十人。
entries.en: On Shengwu Hall incense tables, censers, spoons, boxes, and incense were also set out; below the hall each emperor had one sedan chair, sixteen bearers, two umbrellas, twelve fan-bearers, and thirty crossbowmen as guides and attendants.
entries.literal: On Shengwu Hall incense tables, censers, spoons, boxes, incense, and the like were also set out; below the hall for each was set one sedan chair, sixteen bearers, two umbrellas each, twelve fan-bearers each, and thirty crossbowmen as guides and attendants each.

entries.zh: 前一日，清齋，親王于本府，百官於其第。
entries.en: On the previous day they observed ritual purification—princes in their mansions, officials at their residences.
entries.literal: On the previous day they observed ritual purification: princes in their mansions, officials at their residences.

entries.zh: 行禮官執事人等習儀，就祠所清齋。
entries.en: The officiating ritual officials and attendants rehearsed the rites and observed purification at the shrine.
entries.literal: The officiating ritual officials and attendants rehearsed the rites and observed purification at the shrine.

entries.zh: 其日質明，禮官率太廟署官等詣崇聖閣奉世祖禦容，每匣用內侍二人、太祝一員，禮官、署官前導，置於聖武殿神座。
entries.en: At dawn that day, ritual officials led Grand Ancestral Temple staff to Chongsheng Pavilion to receive Emperor Shizu's portrait; each casket was borne by two palace attendants and one chief invoker, with ritual and temple officials guiding ahead to place it on the spirit seat in Shengwu Hall.
entries.literal: At dawn that day, ritual officials led Grand Ancestral Temple staff to Chongsheng Pavilion to receive the imperial portrait of Emperor Shizu; for each casket two palace attendants and one chief invoker were used; ritual and temple officials guided ahead and placed it on the spirit seat in Shengwu Hall.

entries.zh: 禮直官引親王宰執百官公服于殿庭班立，七品以下班於殿門之外，贊者曰：「拜。」
entries.en: The ritual protocol officer led princes, chief councillors, and all officials in court dress to form ranks in the forecourt; those of the seventh rank and below formed ranks outside the hall gate. The announcer called: "Bow."
entries.literal: The ritual protocol officer led princes, chief councillors, and all officials in formal dress to form ranks in the forecourt; those of the seventh rank and below formed ranks outside the hall gate; the announcer said: "Bow."

entries.zh: 在位官皆再拜。
entries.en: All officials in their stations bowed twice.
entries.literal: All officials in their places bowed twice.

entries.zh: 禮直官引班首詣罍洗，盥手訖，升殿，詣神座前跪上香，訖，少退，再拜。
entries.en: The ritual protocol officer led the rank lead to the ewer-washing station; after washing his hands he ascended, went before the spirit seat, knelt to offer incense, withdrew slightly, and bowed twice.
entries.literal: The ritual protocol officer led the lead of the rank to the ewer-washing station; when hand-washing was finished, he ascended, went before the spirit seat, knelt to offer incense, withdrew slightly, and bowed twice.

entries.zh: 禮直官引班首降殿復位，贊者曰：「拜。」
entries.en: The ritual protocol officer led the rank lead down from the hall to his station. The announcer called: "Bow."
entries.literal: The ritual protocol officer led the lead down from the hall to his place; the announcer said: "Bow."

entries.zh: 在位官皆再拜，訖，禮直官導世祖禦容升腰輿，儀衛依次序導從，至廣德殿，百官後從，至庭下班位立。
entries.en: All officials in their stations bowed twice. The ritual protocol officer then guided Emperor Shizu's portrait onto the sedan chair; ceremonial guards followed in order to Guangde Hall while all officials followed behind and formed ranks in the forecourt.
entries.literal: All officials in their places bowed twice; when finished, the ritual protocol officer guided the imperial portrait of Emperor Shizu onto the sedan chair; ceremonial guards followed in order to Guangde Hall; all officials followed behind; at the forecourt they formed ranks.

entries.zh: 禮官率太廟署官就腰輿內捧禦容，於殿上正面奉安訖，百官於階下，六品已下官於殿門外，立班。
entries.en: Ritual officials led Grand Ancestral Temple staff in bearing the portrait from the sedan chair and installing it reverently on the hall facing forward. Officials stood below the steps, those of the sixth rank and below outside the hall gate, in ranks.
entries.literal: Ritual officials led Grand Ancestral Temple staff in bearing the portrait from within the sedan chair; on the hall they reverently installed it facing forward; officials stood below the steps, those of the sixth rank and below outside the hall gate, in ranks.

entries.zh: 贊者曰：「再拜。」
entries.en: The announcer called: "Bow twice."
entries.literal: The announcer said: "Bow twice."

entries.zh: 在位官皆再拜。
entries.en: All officials in their stations bowed twice.
entries.literal: All officials in their places bowed twice.

entries.zh: 禮直官引班首盥洗，盥手訖，升殿，執事官等從升，詣禦容前，跪上香，奠酒，教坊樂作，少退再拜，訖，樂止。
entries.en: The ritual protocol officer led the rank lead to wash his hands, then ascend with the officiating officials. Before the portrait he knelt to offer incense and wine while the Court Music Office played; he withdrew slightly and bowed twice, and the music ceased.
entries.literal: The ritual protocol officer led the lead to wash; when hand-washing was finished, he ascended, officiating officials ascending with him; before the portrait he knelt to offer incense and present wine; the Court Music Office performed; he withdrew slightly and bowed twice; when finished, the music ceased.

entries.zh: 禮直官引班首降殿復位，贊者曰：「拜。」
entries.en: The ritual protocol officer led the rank lead down from the hall to his station. The announcer called: "Bow."
entries.literal: The ritual protocol officer led the lead down from the hall to his place; the announcer said: "Bow."

entries.zh: 在位官皆再拜。
entries.en: All officials in their stations bowed twice.
entries.literal: All officials in their places bowed twice.

entries.zh: 訖，禮官率太廟署官詣崇聖閣。
entries.en: When this was done, ritual officials led Grand Ancestral Temple staff to Chongsheng Pavilion.
entries.literal: When finished, ritual officials led Grand Ancestral Temple staff to Chongsheng Pavilion.

entries.zh: 太祝內侍捧太宗禦容，禮官導太宗禦容置於聖武殿，行禮畢，以次奉安於丕承殿，行禮並如上儀。
entries.en: Chief invokers and palace attendants bore Emperor Taizong's portrait; ritual officials guided it to Shengwu Hall. When the rites were complete, it was installed in turn at Picheng Hall with the same ceremonies as above.
entries.literal: Chief invokers and palace attendants bore the imperial portrait of Emperor Taizong; ritual officials guided it to Shengwu Hall; when the rites were complete, it was reverently installed in turn at Picheng Hall, the rites all as above.

entries.zh: 次睿宗禦容奉安於天興殿，禮亦如之。
entries.en: Next Emperor Ruizong's portrait was installed at Tianxing Hall with the same rites.
entries.literal: Next the imperial portrait of Emperor Ruizong was reverently installed at Tianxing Hall, the rites likewise.

entries.zh: 俟奉安禮畢，百官退。
entries.en: When the installation rites were complete, all officials withdrew.
entries.literal: When the installation rites were complete, all officials withdrew.

entries.zh: 禮官參酌唐《開元禮》，定擬釋奠儀數：文宣王、兗國公、鄒國公每位籩豆各十、犧尊一、象尊一、簠簋各二、俎二、祝板各一、皆設案。
entries.en: Drawing on the Tang dynasty's Kaiyuan Rites, the ritual officers laid down the prescribed offerings for the Confucian libation: Confucius as Cultured Sagely King, Yan Hui as Lord of Yan, and Mencius as Lord of Zou each received ten bian and ten dou vessels, one sacrificial wine vessel, one elephant-decorated vessel, two fu and gui grain stands, two meat boards, and one prayer tablet apiece, all arranged on dedicated tables.
entries.literal: The ritual officials, consulting the Tang Kaiyuan Rites, fixed the proposed numbers for the libation sacrifice: for the Cultured Sagely King, the Lord of Yan, and the Lord of Zou, each was allotted ten bian and ten dou, one sacrificial wine vessel, one elephant-decorated vessel, two fu and gui, two zu, and one prayer board each, all set on tables.

entries.zh: 七十二賢、二十一先儒，每位各籩一、豆一、爵一，兩廡各設象尊二。
entries.en: The seventy-two disciples and twenty-one earlier Confucians were each allotted one bian, one dou, and one jue; in each side hall stood two elephant-decorated wine vessels.
entries.literal: For the seventy-two worthies and twenty-one earlier Confucians, each had one bian, one dou, and one jue; in each side hall two elephant-decorated vessels were set out.

entries.zh: 總用籩、豆各一百二十三，簠簋各六，俎六，犧尊三，象尊七，爵九十四。
entries.en: The ceremony required 123 bian and 123 dou in total, along with six fu, six gui, six meat boards, three sacrificial wine vessels, seven elephant-decorated vessels, and ninety-four jue cups.
entries.literal: In all there were used 123 bian and 123 dou, six fu and six gui, six zu, three sacrificial wine vessels, seven elephant-decorated vessels, and ninety-four jue.

entries.zh: 其尊皆有坫。
entries.en: Every wine vessel stood on its own pedestal.
entries.literal: All the wine vessels had pedestals.

entries.zh: 罍二，洗二，篚勺各二，冪六。
entries.en: There were two lei jars, two wash basins, two sets of basket and ladle, and six covers.
entries.literal: Two lei, two wash basins, two baskets each with spoons, and six covers.

entries.zh: 正位並從祀藉尊、罍、俎、豆席，約用三十幅，尊席用葦，俎、豆席用莞。
entries.en: Mats for the main and collateral offerings—covering the wine vessels, lei, meat boards, and dou—required roughly thirty panels in all: reed mats for the wine vessels, cattail mats for the meat boards and dou stands.
entries.literal: For the main seat and collateral sacrifices, mats for the wine vessels, lei, zu, and dou required about thirty panels; reed mats for the wine vessels, cattail mats for the zu and dou.

entries.zh: 牲用羊、豕各三，酒二十瓶。
entries.en: The sacrificial victims were three sheep and three pigs; wine was provided in twenty bottles.
entries.literal: Victims were three sheep and three pigs; wine, twenty bottles.

entries.zh: 禮行三獻，以祭酒、司業、博士充。
entries.en: The ceremony followed the three-offering sequence, with the Director of Sacrificial Wine, the Libationer, and the Erudites serving as the offering officers.
entries.literal: The rite was performed with three offerings; the Director of Sacrificial Wine, the Libationer, and the Erudites filled the roles.

entries.zh: 分獻官二，讀祝官一，太官令一，捧祝官二，罍洗官一，爵洗官一，巾篚官二，禮直官十一，學生以儒服陪位。
entries.en: Two officials distributed the secondary offerings; one read the prayer; one Grand Steward of Sacrifices oversaw the kitchen; two bore the prayer tablets; one washed the lei, one washed the jue; two tended the towels and baskets; eleven ritual attendants stood by; and students in scholar's robes filled the accompanying ranks.
entries.literal: Two sub-offering officials, one prayer reader, one Grand Steward, two prayer bearers, one lei-washing official, one jue-washing official, two towel-and-basket officials, eleven ritual attendants; students in scholar robes took accompanying positions.

entries.zh: 樂用登歌，大樂令一員，本署官充，樂工三十九人。
entries.en: The ascending hymn was performed under one Grand Music Director drawn from the music office, with thirty-nine musicians.
entries.literal: Music used the ascending hymn; one Grand Music Director, filled from his own office, and thirty-nine musicians.

entries.zh: 迎神，三奏姑洗宮《來甯之曲》，辭曰：「上都隆化，廟堂作新。
entries.en: To welcome the spirit, the "Song of Coming Peace" in the Guxian mode was played three times; its words run: "The upper capital flourishes in transformation; the temple hall stands renewed.
entries.literal: To welcome the spirit, three performances of the Guxian-mode "Song of Coming Peace"; the text says: "The upper capital flourishes in transformation; the temple hall is made anew.

entries.zh: 神之來格，威儀具陳。
entries.en: As the spirit descends, every mark of majesty and ritual is set forth.
entries.literal: The spirit comes to lodge; majesty and ritual are fully displayed.

entries.zh: 穆穆凝旒，巍然聖真。
entries.en: Solemn and still beneath the hanging crown beads, the sagely presence towers in truth.
entries.literal: Solemn and still, the crown beads hang; towering is the sagely truth.

entries.zh: 斯文伊始，群方所視。」
entries.en: This culture is renewed at its source, and all the realm looks on."
entries.literal: This culture has just begun anew; all regions look upon it."

entries.zh: 初獻盥洗，姑洗宮《靜甯之曲》，辭曰：「偉矣素王，風猷至粹。
entries.en: For the first offering's ablution, the "Song of Quiet Peace" in the Guxian mode was sung; its words run: "Great is the Uncrowned King; his teachings and conduct are supremely pure.
entries.literal: At the first offering, hand-washing: the Guxian-mode "Song of Quiet Peace"; the text says: "Great is the Uncrowned King; his teachings and conduct are supremely pure.

entries.zh: 垂二千年，斯文不墜。
entries.en: For two thousand years his culture has never fallen away.
entries.literal: For two thousand years his culture has not fallen.

entries.zh: 涓辰維良，爰修祀事。
entries.en: On this chosen auspicious day we undertake the sacrificial rites.
entries.literal: This chosen day is truly auspicious; now we undertake the sacrificial affair.

entries.zh: 沃盥于庭，嚴禋禮備。」
entries.en: Ablution is poured in the courtyard; the solemn sacrificial rites stand complete."
entries.literal: Pouring ablution in the courtyard, the solemn sacrificial rites are complete."

entries.zh: 升階，南呂宮《肅甯之曲》，辭曰：「巍乎聖師，道全德隆。
entries.en: On ascending the steps, the "Song of Solemn Peace" in the Nanlü mode was sung; its words run: "Towering is the Sagely Master; his Way is complete and his virtue sublime.
entries.literal: Ascending the steps, the Nanlü-mode "Song of Solemn Peace"; the text says: "Towering is the Sagely Master; his Way is complete and his virtue sublime.

entries.zh: 修明五常，垂教無窮。
entries.en: He clarified the Five Constants and handed down teachings without end.
entries.literal: He clarified the Five Constants and handed down teaching without end.

entries.zh: 增崇儒宮，遹追遺風。
entries.en: The Confucian temple is raised in honor as we deeply pursue the legacy he left behind.
entries.literal: The Confucian temple is raised in honor; we deeply pursue the legacy wind.

entries.zh: 嚴祀申虔，登降有容。」
entries.en: The solemn sacrifice expresses our devotion; in ascent and descent all bear themselves with dignity."
entries.literal: The solemn sacrifice expresses devotion; ascending and descending with proper bearing."

entries.zh: 奠幣，姑洗宮《和甯之曲》，辭曰：「天生聖人，賢于堯舜。
entries.en: For the presentation of silks, the "Song of Harmonious Peace" in the Guxian mode was sung; its words run: "Heaven gave birth to a sage more worthy than Yao and Shun.
entries.literal: Presenting the silks, the Guxian-mode "Song of Harmonious Peace"; the text says: "Heaven gave birth to a sage, more worthy than Yao and Shun.

entries.zh: 仰之彌高，磨而不磷。
entries.en: The more one looks up to him, the higher he seems; the more one polishes against him, the harder he proves.
entries.literal: Look up and he grows higher; polish him and he does not wear thin.

entries.zh: 新廟告成，宮牆數仞。
entries.en: The new temple is declared complete, its academy walls rising many ren high.
entries.literal: The new temple is announced complete; the academy walls are many ren high.

entries.zh: 遣使陳祠，斯文複振。」
entries.en: Envoys are dispatched to present the sacrifice, and this culture is revived once more."
entries.literal: Envoys are dispatched to present the sacrifice; this culture is revived anew."

entries.zh: 降階，姑洗宮《安寧之曲》辭曰：「稟靈尼丘，垂芳闕里。
entries.en: On descending the steps, the "Song of Tranquil Peace" in the Guxian mode was sung; its words run: "He received his spirit at Ni Hill; his fragrance endures in Que Village.
entries.literal: Descending the steps, the Guxian-mode "Song of Tranquil Peace"; the text says: "He received his spirit at Ni Hill; his fragrance hangs over Que Village.

entries.zh: 生民以來，孰如夫子。
entries.en: Since humankind began, who has been like the Master?
entries.literal: Since the birth of the people, who is like the Master?

entries.zh: 新祠巋然，四方所視。
entries.en: The new shrine stands towering, and all four quarters look upon it.
entries.literal: The new shrine stands towering; all four quarters look upon it.

entries.zh: 酹觴告成，祗循典禮。」
entries.en: The libation cup is poured to announce completion as we reverently follow the canonical rites."
entries.literal: Libation of the cup announces completion; we reverently follow the canonical rites."

entries.zh: 兗國公酌獻，姑洗宮《輯甯之曲》，辭曰：「聖師之門，顏惟居上。
entries.en: For the Lord of Yan's offering pour, the "Song of Gathered Peace" in the Guxian mode was sung; its words run: "At the Sagely Master's gate, Yan alone stands foremost.
entries.literal: The Lord of Yan pours the offering; the Guxian-mode "Song of Gathered Peace"; the text says: "At the Sagely Master's gate, Yan alone stands foremost.

entries.zh: 其殆庶幾，是宜配饗。
entries.en: He nearly reached perfection; he is fit to share the sacrifice.
entries.literal: He nearly approached perfection; he is fit to share the sacrifice.

entries.zh: 桓圭袞衣，有嚴儀象。
entries.en: With the tall gui scepter and embroidered robes, his august image is displayed.
entries.literal: With the tall gui and embroidered robes, his august image is displayed.

entries.zh: 載之神祠，增光吾黨。」
entries.en: He is borne into the divine shrine, adding glory to our fellowship."
entries.literal: He is borne into the divine shrine, adding glory to our fellowship."

entries.zh: 鄒國公酌獻，姑洗宮《泰甯之曲》，辭曰：「有周之衰，王綱既墜。
entries.en: For the Lord of Zou's offering pour, the "Song of Great Peace" in the Guxian mode was sung; its words run: "When Zhou declined, the royal order had already collapsed.
entries.literal: The Lord of Zou pours the offering; the Guxian-mode "Song of Great Peace"; the text says: "When Zhou declined, the royal net had already fallen.

entries.zh: 是生真儒，宏才命世。
entries.en: Then was born the true Confucian, whose great talent was ordained for the age.
entries.literal: Then was born the true Confucian; his great talent was ordained for the age.

entries.zh: 言而為經，醇乎仁義。
entries.en: His words became the classics, pure in benevolence and righteousness.
entries.literal: His words became the classics; pure in benevolence and righteousness.

entries.zh: 力扶聖功，同垂萬祀。」
entries.en: He strove to uphold the sage's achievement, sharing in offerings for ten thousand generations."
entries.literal: He strove to uphold the sage's achievement, sharing in offerings for ten thousand generations."

entries.zh: 亞、終獻，姑洗宮《咸甯之曲》，辭曰：「於昭聖能，與天立極。
entries.en: For the second and final offerings, the "Song of Universal Peace" in the Guxian mode was sung; its words run: "How bright is the sage's power, establishing the cosmic pole with Heaven.
entries.literal: The second and final offerings; the Guxian-mode "Song of Universal Peace"; the text says: "How bright is the sage's power, establishing the pole with Heaven.

entries.zh: 有承其流，皇仁帝德。
entries.en: There are those who inherit his stream—imperial benevolence and sovereign virtue.
entries.literal: There are those who inherit his stream; imperial benevolence and sovereign virtue.

entries.zh: 豈伊立言，訓經王國。
entries.en: Was it only in establishing words that he instructed the royal realm through the classics?
entries.literal: Was it only in establishing words that he instructed the royal domain through the classics?

entries.zh: 煥我文明，典祀千億。」
entries.en: He brightens our culture and civilization; canonical sacrifices shall endure for a hundred million ages."
entries.literal: He brightens our culture and civilization; canonical sacrifices for a hundred million ages."

entries.zh: 送神，姑洗宮《來甯之曲》，辭曰：「吉蠲為饎，孔惠孔時。
entries.en: To send off the spirit, the "Song of Coming Peace" in the Guxian mode was sung again; its words run: "Auspicious purification makes the offering; greatly kind, greatly timely.
entries.literal: Sending off the spirit, the Guxian-mode "Song of Coming Peace"; the text says: "Auspicious purification makes the offering; greatly kind, greatly timely.

entries.zh: 正辭嘉言，神之格思。
entries.en: With correct words and fine phrases, the spirit comes to lodge here.
entries.literal: Correct words and fine phrases—the spirit comes to lodge here.

entries.zh: 是饗是宜，神保聿歸。
entries.en: This feast is fitting; may the spirit's blessing now return.
entries.literal: This is the feast, this is fitting; may the spirit's blessing now return.

entries.zh: 惟時肇祀，太平極致。」
entries.en: Only at this time do we inaugurate the sacrifice—the utmost of great peace."
entries.literal: Only at this time do we inaugurate the sacrifice; the utmost of great peace."

entries.zh: 皇統元年二月戊子，熙宗詣文宣王廟奠祭，北面再拜，顧儒臣曰：「為善不可不勉。
entries.en: On wuzi day in the second month of Huangtong 1, Emperor Xizong went to the Temple of the Cultured Sagely King to offer sacrifice, bowed twice facing north, turned to the Confucian officials and said: "One must not fail to exert oneself in doing good.
entries.literal: In Huangtong 1, second month, on wuzi day, Xizong went to the Temple of the Cultured Sagely King to offer sacrifice, bowed twice facing north, turned to the Confucian officials and said: "One must not fail to exert oneself in doing good.

entries.zh: 孔子雖無位，以其道可尊，使萬世高仰如此。」
entries.en: Although Confucius held no office, because his Way was worthy of honor, he has been revered so highly for ten thousand generations."
entries.literal: Although Confucius held no office, because his Way was worthy of honor, he has been revered so highly for ten thousand generations."

entries.zh: 大定十四年，國子監言：「歲春秋仲月上丁日，釋奠于文宣王，用本監官房錢六十貫，止造茶食等物，以大小楪排設，用留守司樂，以樂工為禮生，率倉場等官陪位，于古禮未合也。
entries.en: In Dading 14, the Directorate of Education said: "On the ding day of the second month in spring and autumn each year, a libation sacrifice is offered to the Cultured Sagely King; using sixty strings of cash from this directorate's official funds, only tea foods and the like are prepared and arranged on large and small dishes; the resident military music office supplies music, musicians serve as ritual attendants, and grain-store officials and the like take accompanying positions—this does not accord with ancient ritual.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Dading, the Directorate of Education said: "On the ding day of the second month in spring and autumn each year, a libation sacrifice is offered to the Cultured Sagely King; using sixty strings of cash from this directorate's official funds, only tea foods and the like are made, arranged on large and small dishes; the resident military music office supplies music, musicians serve as ritual attendants, and grain-store officials and the like take accompanying positions—this does not accord with ancient ritual.

entries.zh: 伏睹國家承平日久，典章文物當粲然備具，以光萬世。
entries.en: We observe that the state has long enjoyed peace, and its institutions and cultural artifacts ought to be fully and splendidly provided, to shine for ten thousand generations.
entries.literal: We have observed that the state has long enjoyed peace, and its institutions and cultural relics ought to be fully and splendidly provided, to illuminate ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 況京師為首善之地，四方之所觀仰，擬釋奠器物、行禮次序，合行下詳定。
entries.en: Moreover, as the capital is the foremost seat of excellence and a place watched by all quarters, the vessels for the libation sacrifice and the order of the rite should be referred downward for detailed determination.
entries.literal: Moreover, as the capital is the foremost region of excellence and a place observed by all quarters, the vessels for the libation sacrifice and the sequence of the rite should be referred downward for detailed fixing.

entries.zh: 兼兗國公親承聖教者也，鄒國公功扶聖教者也，當于宣聖像左右列之。
entries.en: Moreover, the Lord of Yan personally received the sage's teaching, and the Lord of Zou by merit supported the sage's teaching—they should be set to the left and right of the image of the Sagely Proclaimed One.
entries.literal: Moreover, the Lord of Yan personally received the sage's teaching, and the Lord of Zou by merit supported the sage's teaching—they should be arrayed to the left and right of the image of the Sagely Proclaimed One.

entries.zh: 今孟子以燕服在後堂，宣聖像側還虛一位，禮宜遷孟子像于宣聖右，與顏子相對，改塑冠冕，妝飾法服，一遵舊制。」
entries.en: Now Mencius, in everyday dress, is in the rear hall; beside the image of the Sagely Proclaimed One one place still stands empty; by ritual Mencius's image ought to be moved to the right of the Sagely Proclaimed One, facing Yanzi across from him, with crowns and caps remolded and ritual robes adorned, all following the old regulations."
entries.literal: Now Mencius, in everyday dress, is in the rear hall; beside the image of the Sagely Proclaimed One one place still stands empty; by ritual Mencius's image ought to be moved to the right of the Sagely Proclaimed One, facing Yanzi opposite, with crowns and caps remolded and ritual robes adorned, all following the old regulations."

entries.zh: 承安二年，春丁，章宗親祀，以親王攝亞、終獻，皇族陪祀，文武群臣助奠。
entries.en: In Chengan 2, on the spring ding day, Emperor Zhangzong performed the sacrifice in person; a prince of the blood stood in for the second and final offerings, members of the imperial clan accompanied the rite, and civil and military officials assisted in the presentation.
entries.literal: In the second year of Chengan, on the spring ding day, Emperor Zhangzong personally sacrificed; a prince of the blood stood in for the second and final offerings, the imperial clan accompanied the sacrifice, and civil and military officials assisted in the presentation.

entries.zh: 上親為贊文，舊封公者升為國公，侯者為國侯，郕伯以下皆封侯。
entries.en: The emperor personally composed the praise text; former lords were promoted to state lords, marquises to state marquises, and from the Earl of Cheng downward all received marquis titles.
entries.literal: The emperor personally composed the praise text; those formerly enfeoffed as lords were raised to state lords, marquises to state marquises, and from the Earl of Cheng downward all were enfeoffed as marquises.

entries.zh: 宣宗遷汴，建廟會朝門內，歲祀如儀，宣聖、顏、孟各羊一、豕一，餘同小祀，共用羊八，無豕。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, a temple was built inside the Gate of Assembly, and annual sacrifices followed the established regulations. Confucius, Yan Hui, and Mencius each received one sheep and one pig; the remainder followed the minor sacrifice format, eight sheep in all and no pigs.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, a temple was built inside the Gate of Assembly; annual sacrifices followed the regulations. For the Sagely Proclaimed, Yan, and Meng, each had one sheep and one pig; the rest followed the minor sacrifice, eight sheep in all and no pigs.

entries.zh: 其諸州釋奠並遵唐儀。
entries.en: In all prefectures the Confucian libation sacrifices likewise followed Tang ritual practice.
entries.literal: In all prefectures the libation sacrifices likewise followed Tang ritual.

entries.zh: 泰和六年，詔建昭烈武成王廟于闕庭之右，麗澤門內。
entries.en: In Taihe 6, an edict ordered the construction of the temple of the Illustrious Martial Accomplished King to the right of the palace courtyard, inside the Lizhe Gate.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, an edict ordered construction of the temple of the Illustrious Martial Accomplished King to the right of the palace courtyard, inside the Lizhe Gate.

entries.zh: 其制一遵唐舊，禮三獻，官以四品官已下，儀同中祀，用二月上戊。
entries.en: Its regulations entirely followed Tang precedent: the three-offering rite, officials of fourth rank and below, ceremony equal to a middle sacrifice, performed on the upper wu day of the second month.
entries.literal: Its regulations entirely followed Tang precedent: the rite of three offerings, officials of fourth rank and below, ceremony equal to a middle sacrifice, performed on the upper wu day of the second month.

entries.zh: 七年，完顏匡等言：「我朝創業功臣，禮宜配祀。」
entries.en: In the seventh year, Wanyan Kuang and others said: "The founding meritocrats of our dynasty ought by ritual to receive collateral sacrifice."
entries.literal: In the seventh year, Wanyan Kuang and others said: "The founding meritocrats of our dynasty ought by ritual to receive collateral sacrifice."

entries.zh: 於是，以秦王宗翰同子房配武成王，而降管仲以下。
entries.en: Thereupon Prince of Qin Zonghan was paired with Zifang to accompany the Martial Accomplished King, while Guan Zhong and those below were demoted.
entries.literal: Thereupon Prince of Qin Zonghan was paired with Zifang to accompany the Martial Accomplished King, while Guan Zhong and those below were demoted.

entries.zh: 又躋楚王宗雄、宗望、宗弼等侍武成王坐，韓信而下降立於廡。
entries.en: Prince of Chu Zongxiong, Zongwang, Zongbi, and others were further promoted to attend beside the Martial Accomplished King's seat; from Han Xin downward they stood in the side halls.
entries.literal: Further promoted were Prince of Chu Zongxiong, Zongwang, Zongbi, and others to attend beside the Martial Accomplished King's seat; from Han Xin downward they stood in the side halls.

entries.zh: 又黜王猛、慕容恪等二十餘人，而增金臣遼王斜也等。
entries.en: Wang Meng, Murong Ke, and more than twenty others were removed, while Jin officials such as Prince of Liao Xieye were added.
entries.literal: Wang Meng, Murong Ke, and more than twenty others were removed, while Jin officials such as Prince of Liao Xieye were added.

entries.zh: 其祭，武成王、宗翰、子房各羊一、豕一，餘共用羊八，無豕。
entries.en: At the sacrifice, the Martial Accomplished King, Zonghan, and Zifang each received one sheep and one pig; the remainder shared eight sheep in all, with no pigs.
entries.literal: At the sacrifice, the Martial Accomplished King, Zonghan, and Zifang each had one sheep and one pig; the rest shared eight sheep in all, with no pigs.

entries.zh: 宣宗遷汴，餘會朝門內闕庭之右營廟如制，春秋上戊之祭仍舊。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuanzong moved to Bian, a temple was built to the right of the palace courtyard inside the Gate of Assembly as prescribed; the spring and autumn upper-wu sacrifices continued as before.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong moved to Bian, a temple was built to the right of the palace courtyard inside the Gate of Assembly as prescribed; the spring and autumn upper-wu sacrifices continued as before.

entries.zh: 三年一祭，于仲春之月祭伏犧于陳州，神農於亳州，軒轅於坊州，少昊於兗州，顓頊於開州，高辛於歸德府，陶唐於平陽府，虞舜、夏禹、成湯於河中府，周文王、武王於京兆府。
entries.en: Sacrifices were held once every three years: in mid-spring Fuxi was honored at Chen Prefecture, Shennong at Bozhou, the Yellow Emperor at Fang Prefecture, Shaohao at Yan Prefecture, Zhuanxu at Kai Prefecture, Gaoxin at Guide Prefecture, Emperor Yao at Pingyang Prefecture, Shun, Yu, and Tang at Hezhong Prefecture, and Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou at Jingzhao Prefecture.
entries.literal: Sacrificed once every three years: in the middle spring month Fuxi was sacrificed to at Chen Prefecture, Shennong at Bozhou, Xuanyuan at Fang Prefecture, Shaohao at Yan Prefecture, Zhuanxu at Kai Prefecture, Gaoxin at Guide Prefecture, Taotang Yao at Pingyang Prefecture, Yu Shun, Xia Yu, and Cheng Tang at Hezhong Prefecture, and King Wen and King Wu of Zhou at Jingzhao Prefecture.

entries.zh: 泰和三年、尚書省奏：「太常寺言：'《開元禮》祭帝嚳、堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武、漢祖祝版請禦署。
entries.en: In Taihe 3 the Secretariat memorialized: "The Court of Imperial Sacrifices reports that under the Kaiyuan Rites, prayer boards for sacrifices to Di Ku, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Kings Wen and Wu, and the Han Founder require imperial endorsement.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taihe the Secretariat memorialized: "The Court of Imperial Sacrifices states: 'The Kaiyuan Rites require imperial endorsement on prayer boards for sacrifices to Di Ku, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, and the Han Founder.

entries.zh: 《開寶禮》犧、軒、顓頊、帝嚳、陶唐、女媧、成湯、文、武請禦署，自漢高祖以下二十七帝不署。
entries.en: The Kaibao Rites require imperial endorsement for Fu Xi, the Yellow Emperor, Zhuanxu, Di Ku, Emperor Yao, Nüwa, Tang, and Kings Wen and Wu; from Han Gaozu downward twenty-seven emperors are not endorsed.
entries.literal: The Kaibao Rites require imperial endorsement for Fu Xi, Xuanyuan, Zhuanxu, Di Ku, Taotang Yao, Nüwa, Cheng Tang, Wen, and Wu; from Han Gaozu downward twenty-seven emperors are not endorsed.

entries.zh: '平章政事鎰、左丞匡、太常博士溫蒂罕天興言：'方嶽之神各有所主，有國所賴，請禦署固宜。
entries.en: Grand Councilor Yi, Left Vice Director Kuang, and Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wentihaan Tianxing said: "The spirits of the regional mountains each have their domain, and the state relies upon them—requesting imperial endorsement is certainly fitting."
