entries.literal: Grand Councilor Yi, Left Vice Director Kuang, and Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wentihaan Tianxing said: 'The spirits of the regional mountains each have their domain; the state relies upon them—requesting imperial endorsement is certainly fitting.

entries.zh: 至於前古帝王，寥落杳茫，列於中祀亦已厚矣，不須禦署。
entries.en: As for the ancient emperors of former ages, remote and indistinct, ranking them among middle sacrifices is already generous; imperial endorsement is not required.
entries.literal: As for the ancient emperors of former ages, remote and indistinct, to rank them among middle sacrifices is already generous; imperial endorsement is not required.

entries.zh: '參知政事即康及鉉以為三皇、五帝、禹、湯、文、武皆垂世立教之君，唐、宋致祭皆禦署，而今降祝版不署，恐於禮未盡。
entries.en: Vice Grand Councilors Jikang and Quan held that the Three August Ones, Five Emperors, Yu, Tang, and Kings Wen and Wu were all rulers who handed down teaching for the ages; Tang and Song sacrifices all received imperial endorsement, and now to issue prayer boards without endorsement may fall short of ritual propriety.
entries.literal: Vice Grand Councilors Jikang and Quan held that the Three August Ones, Five Emperors, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu were all rulers who handed down teaching for the ages; Tang and Song sacrifices all received imperial endorsement, and now to issue prayer boards without endorsement may fall short of ritual propriety.

entries.zh: 不若止從外路祭社稷及釋奠文宣王例，不降祝版，而令學士院定撰祝文，頒各處為常制。」
entries.en: It would be better simply to follow the precedent of sacrifices to the Gods of Earth and Grain and the Confucian libation in the outer circuits—do not issue prayer boards, but have the Academy of Scholar-Officials compose the prayer texts and distribute them to each place as standing regulations."
entries.literal: It would be better simply to follow the precedent of sacrifices to Earth and Grain and the libation to the Cultured Sagely King in the outer circuits—do not issue prayer boards, but have the Academy of Scholar-Officials compose the prayer texts and distribute them to each place as standing regulations."

entries.zh: 敕命依期降祝板，而不請署。
entries.en: An edict ordered that prayer boards be issued on schedule, but without requesting imperial endorsement.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that prayer boards be issued on schedule, but without requesting endorsement.

entries.zh: 大定二十五年，有司言：「昔太祖征遼，策馬徑渡，江神助順，靈應昭著，宜修祠宇，加賜封爵。」
entries.en: In Dading 25, the responsible offices said: "In former days when the Grand Ancestor campaigned against Liao, he spurred his horse straight across; the river god aided his cause, and the spiritual response was manifest—a shrine should be repaired and enfeoffment bestowed."
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Dading, the responsible offices said: "In former days when the Grand Ancestor campaigned against Liao, he spurred his horse straight across; the river god aided his cause, and the spiritual response was manifest—a shrine should be repaired and enfeoffment bestowed."

entries.zh: 乃封神為興國應聖公，致祭如長白山儀，冊禮如保陵公故事。
entries.en: The spirit was then enfeoffed as Duke of the Sagely Response Who Establishes the State; sacrifices followed the Changbai Mountain rite, and the enfeoffment ceremony followed the precedent of the Lord Who Protects the Tombs.
entries.literal: The spirit was then enfeoffed as Duke of the Sagely Response Who Establishes the State; sacrifices followed the Changbai Mountain rite, and the enfeoffment ceremony followed the precedent of the Lord Who Protects the Tombs.

entries.zh: 其冊文雲：「昔我太祖武元皇帝，受天明命，掃遼季荒茀，成師以出，至於大江，浩浩洪流，不舟而濟，雖穆滿渡江面黿粱，光武濟河而水冰，自今觀之無足言矣！
entries.en: The enfeoffment text reads: "In former days our Grand Ancestor, the Martial Origin Emperor, received Heaven's bright mandate, swept away the Liao dynasty's wild wasteland, and led his army forth to the great river—a vast torrent, yet he crossed without boats. Though King Mu of Zhou crossed the river on a turtle bridge and Emperor Guangwu crossed the Yellow River on ice, viewed from today these are hardly worth mentioning!
entries.literal: The text of the book reads: "In former days our Grand Ancestor, the Martial Origin Emperor, received Heaven's bright mandate, swept away the Liao dynasty's wild wasteland, and led his army forth to the great river—a vast torrent, yet he crossed without boats. Though King Mu of Zhou crossed the river on a turtle bridge and Emperor Guangwu crossed the Yellow River on ice, viewed from today these are hardly worth mentioning!

entries.zh: 執徐之歲，四月孟夏，朕時邁舊邦，臨江永歎，仰藝祖之開基，佳江神之效靈，至止上都，議所以尊崇之典。
entries.en: In the year of Zhixu, in early summer of the fourth month, I journeyed to the old domain, stood by the river and sighed long, looked up to the founding ancestor's establishment of the realm, and admired the river god's manifestation of spirit; arriving at the Upper Capital, I discussed the regulations by which to honor him.
entries.literal: In the year of Zhixu, in the first month of summer in the fourth month, I then journeyed to the old domain, stood by the river and sighed long, looked up to the founding ancestor's establishment of the base, and admired the river god's manifestation of spirit; arriving at the Upper Capital, I discussed the regulations by which to honor him.

entries.zh: 蓋古者五嶽視三公，四瀆視諸侯，至有唐以來，遂享帝王之尊稱，非直後世彌文，而崇德報功理亦有當然者。
entries.en: For in antiquity the Five Peaks were regarded as equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and the Four Watercourses as equal to feudal lords; from the Tang onward they came to enjoy the exalted titles of emperors and kings—not merely later ages adding ornament, for honoring virtue and repaying merit has its proper rationale.
entries.literal: For in antiquity the Five Peaks were regarded as equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and the Four Watercourses as equal to feudal lords; from the Tang onward they came to enjoy the exalted titles of emperors and kings—not merely later ages adding ornament, for honoring virtue and repaying merit has its proper rationale.

entries.zh: 矧茲江源出於長白，經營帝鄉，實相興運，非錫以上公之號，則無以昭答神休。
entries.en: How much more this river, whose source issues from Changbai, passes through the imperial domain, and truly shares in the dynasty's rise—unless bestowed the title of upper duke, there is no way to manifest response to the spirit's blessing.
entries.literal: How much more this river, whose source issues from Changbai, passes through the imperial domain, and truly shares in the dynasty's rise—unless bestowed the title of upper duke, there is no way to manifest response to the spirit's blessing.

entries.zh: 今遣某官某。
entries.en: Now we dispatch a certain official.
entries.literal: Now we dispatch a certain official.

entries.zh: 持節備物冊命神為興國應聖公。
entries.en: Bearing credentials and complete regalia to enfeoff the spirit as Duke of the Sagely Response Who Establishes the State.
entries.literal: Bearing credentials and complete regalia to enfeoff the spirit as Duke of the Sagely Response Who Establishes the State.

entries.zh: 申命有司，歲時奉祀。
entries.en: We further command the responsible offices to offer seasonal sacrifices.
entries.literal: We further command the responsible offices to offer seasonal sacrifices.

entries.zh: 於戲！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 嚴廟貌，正封爵，禮亦至矣！
entries.en: The temple appearance is made solemn, the enfeoffment is made correct—the ritual has reached its fullness!
entries.literal: The temple appearance is made solemn, the enfeoffment is made correct—the ritual has reached its fullness!

entries.zh: 惟神其衍靈長之德，用輔我國家彌億年，神亦享廟食於無窮，豈不休哉！」
entries.en: May the spirit extend its long-lasting spiritual virtue to assist our state for a hundred million years; may the spirit also enjoy temple offerings without end—is it not glorious!"
entries.literal: May the spirit extend its long-lasting spiritual virtue to assist our state for a hundred million years; may the spirit also enjoy temple offerings without end—is it not glorious!"

entries.zh: 舊名旺國崖，太祖伐遼嘗駐蹕於此。
entries.en: Its former name was Wangguo Cliff; when the Grand Ancestor campaigned against Liao he once halted his carriage here.
entries.literal: Its former name was Wangguo Cliff; when the Grand Ancestor campaigned against Liao he once halted his carriage here.

entries.zh: 大定八年五月，更名靜寧山，後建廟。
entries.en: In the fifth month of Dading 8 it was renamed Tranquil Peace Mountain, and a temple was later built.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Dading it was renamed Tranquil Peace Mountain, and a temple was later built.

entries.zh: 明昌六年八月，以冕服玉冊，冊山神為鎮安公。
entries.en: In the eighth month of Mingchang 6, with crown robes and jade book, the mountain spirit was enfeoffed as Duke Who Pacifies the Realm.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year of Mingchang, with crown robes and jade book, the mountain spirit was enfeoffed as Duke Who Pacifies the Realm.

entries.zh: 冊文曰：「皇帝若曰：古之名山，鹹在祀典。
entries.en: The enfeoffment text reads: "The emperor says: The famous mountains of antiquity were all in the sacrificial canon.
entries.literal: The text of the book reads: "The emperor says: The famous mountains of antiquity were all in the sacrificial canon.

entries.zh: 軒皇之世，神靈所奉者七千。
entries.en: In the age of the Yellow Emperor, seven thousand were received in spirit worship.
entries.literal: In the age of the Yellow Emperor, seven thousand were received in spirit worship.

entries.zh: 虞氏之時，望秩每及於五載。
entries.en: In the time of the House of Yu, gazing upon and ranking them came every five years.
entries.literal: In the time of the House of Yu, gazing upon and ranking them came every five years.

entries.zh: 蓋惟有益於國，是以必報其功。
entries.en: For only what benefits the state must its merit be repaid.
entries.literal: For only what benefits the state must its merit be repaid.

entries.zh: 逮乎後王，申以徽冊，至於嶽鎮之外，亦或封爵之加。
entries.en: Down to later kings, splendid books were extended; beyond the mountain and city gods, enfeoffment was sometimes also added.
entries.literal: Down to later kings, splendid books were extended; beyond the mountain and city gods, enfeoffment was sometimes also added.

entries.zh: 故太白有神應之稱，而終南有廣惠之號。
entries.en: Thus Taibai received the title of Spirit Response, and Zhongnan the designation of Broad Beneficence.
entries.literal: Thus Taibai received the title of Spirit Response, and Zhongnan the designation of Broad Beneficence.

entries.zh: 禮由義起，事與時偕，載籍所傳，於今猶監，朕修和有夏，咸秩無文，眷茲靜寧，秀峙朔野，厓澤布氣，幽贊乎坤元，導風出雲，協符乎乾造。
entries.en: Rites arise from righteousness; affairs keep pace with the times—what the records transmit we still take as mirror. I cultivate harmony like the Xia; all ranks are without omission. Fond is this Tranquil Peace, towering splendid in the northern wilds; its cliffs and marshes spread qi, secretly assisting the earthly principle, guiding wind and issuing clouds, in accord with the heavenly creation.
entries.literal: Rites arise from righteousness; affairs keep pace with the times—what the records transmit we still take as mirror. I cultivate harmony like the Xia; all ranks are without omission. Fond is this Tranquil Peace, towering splendid in the northern wilds; its cliffs and marshes spread qi, secretly assisting the earthly principle, guiding wind and issuing clouds, in accord with the heavenly creation.

entries.zh: 一方之表，萬物所瞻，南直都畿，北維障徼，連延廣厚，寶藏攸興，盤固高明，謻宮斯奠。
entries.en: The marker of one region, upon which the myriad things gaze; south it faces the capital domain, north it buttresses the frontier barrier; continuous, vast, and thick, treasures rise from it; firm, lofty, and bright, the secluded palace is here established.
entries.literal: The marker of one region, upon which the myriad things gaze; south it faces the capital domain, north it buttresses the frontier barrier; continuous, vast, and thick, treasures rise from it; firm, lofty, and bright, the secluded palace is here established.

entries.zh: 昔有遼嘗恃以富國，迄大定更為之錫名。
entries.en: Formerly Liao once relied upon it to enrich the state; down to Dading it was again granted a bestowed name.
entries.literal: Formerly Liao once relied upon it to enrich the state; down to Dading it was again granted a bestowed name.

entries.zh: 洪惟世宗，功昭列聖，亦越顯考，德利生民。
entries.en: Great was Emperor Shizong, his merit manifest to the successive sages; also surpassing was my illustrious father, whose virtue benefited the living people.
entries.literal: Great was Emperor Shizong, his merit manifest to the successive sages; also surpassing was my illustrious father, whose virtue benefited the living people.

entries.zh: 爰即歲時，駕言臨幸，兵革不試，遠人輯寧。
entries.en: Then at the appointed season he drove forth to visit in person; weapons were not tested, and distant peoples were gathered in peace.
entries.literal: Then at the appointed season he drove forth to visit in person; weapons were not tested, and distant peoples were gathered in peace.

entries.zh: 雨暘常調，品匯蕃廡，此上帝無疆之貺，亦英靈有相之符。
entries.en: Rain and sunshine were constantly in harmony; all kinds flourished abundantly—this was the Supreme Lord's boundless gift, and also the sign of the heroic spirit's assistance.
entries.literal: Rain and sunshine were constantly in harmony; all kinds flourished abundantly—this was the Supreme Lord's boundless gift, and also the sign of the heroic spirit's assistance.

entries.zh: 比即輿情，載修故事。
entries.en: Now matching public sentiment, we again repair the old precedent.
entries.literal: Now matching public sentiment, we again repair the old precedent.

entries.zh: 顧先皇帝駐蹕之地，揖累世承平之風。
entries.en: Looking back to where the former emperor halted his carriage, we bow to the wind of peace handed down through successive generations.
entries.literal: Looking back to where the former emperor halted his carriage, we bow to the wind of peace handed down through successive generations.

entries.zh: 迓續遺休，式甄神祐，肆象德以畀號，仍班台而闡儀。
entries.en: Welcoming the continuation of the legacy blessing, we thereby discern the spirit's aid; we extend the emblem of virtue to bestow a title, and still distribute the altar to unfold the rites.
entries.literal: Welcoming the continuation of the legacy blessing, we thereby discern the spirit's aid; we extend the emblem of virtue to bestow a title, and still distribute the altar to unfold the rites.

entries.zh: 宇像一新，采章具舉。
entries.en: The temple images are made new; emblems and ornaments are fully displayed.
entries.literal: The temple images are made new; emblems and ornaments are fully displayed.

entries.zh: 今遣使某、副某，持節備物，冊命神為鎮安公，仍敕歲時奉祀。
entries.en: Now we dispatch envoy so-and-so and deputy so-and-so, bearing credentials and complete regalia, to enfeoff the spirit as Duke Who Pacifies the Realm, and further command seasonal sacrifices.
entries.literal: Now we dispatch envoy so-and-so and deputy so-and-so, bearing credentials and complete regalia, to enfeoff the spirit as Duke Who Pacifies the Realm, and further command seasonal sacrifices.

entries.zh: 於戲！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 容典焜燿，精明感通，惟永億年，翊我昌運。
entries.en: May the ceremonial splendor shine bright, spirit and clarity sense and connect—for ten thousand million years may it assist our flourishing fortune.
entries.literal: May the ceremonial splendor shine bright, spirit and clarity sense and connect—for ten thousand million years may it assist our flourishing fortune.

entries.zh: 神其受職，豈不偉歟？」
entries.en: May the spirit receive its charge—is it not magnificent?"
entries.literal: May the spirit receive its charge—is it not magnificent?"

entries.zh: 即麻達葛山也，章宗生於此。
entries.en: This is Madage Mountain; Emperor Zhangzong was born here.
entries.literal: This is Madage Mountain; Emperor Zhangzong was born here.

entries.zh: 世宗愛此山勢衍氣清，故命章宗名之。
entries.en: Emperor Shizong loved this mountain's spreading terrain and clear qi, and therefore had Zhangzong name it.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong loved this mountain's spreading terrain and clear qi, and therefore had Zhangzong name it.

entries.zh: 後更名胡土白山，建廟。
entries.en: Later it was renamed Hutubai Mountain and a temple was built.
entries.literal: Later it was renamed Hutubai Mountain and a temple was built.

entries.zh: 明昌四年八月，以冕服玉冊，封山神為瑞聖公。
entries.en: In the eighth month of Mingchang 4, with crown robes and jade book, the mountain spirit was enfeoffed as Duke of Auspicious Sageliness.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Mingchang, with crown robes and jade book, the mountain spirit was enfeoffed as Duke of Auspicious Sageliness.

entries.zh: 建廟，命撫州有司，春秋二仲，擇日致祭為常。
entries.en: A temple was built; the responsible offices of Fuzhou were commanded that in the second months of spring and autumn they choose days for sacrifice as the regular practice.
entries.literal: A temple was built; the responsible offices of Fuzhou were commanded that in the second months of spring and autumn they choose days for sacrifice as the regular practice.

entries.zh: 其冊文曰：「皇帝若曰：國家之興，命曆攸屬。
entries.en: The enfeoffment text reads: "The emperor says: When a state rises, the mandate and calendar belong to it.
entries.literal: The text of the book reads: "The emperor says: When a state rises, the mandate and calendar belong to it.

entries.zh: 天地元化，惟時合符。
entries.en: Heaven and earth's primal transformation accords with the time in perfect correspondence.
entries.literal: Heaven and earth's primal transformation accords with the time in perfect correspondence.

entries.zh: 山川百神，無不受職。
entries.en: Mountains, rivers, and the hundred spirits—none fail to receive their charge.
entries.literal: Mountains, rivers, and the hundred spirits—none fail to receive their charge.

entries.zh: 粹精薦瑞，明聖繼生。
entries.en: Pure essence presents auspicious omens; the bright sage succeeds in birth.
entries.literal: Pure essence presents auspicious omens; the bright sage succeeds in birth.

entries.zh: 著丕應於殊禎，啟昌期於幽贊。
entries.en: Manifesting great response in extraordinary blessings, opening a flourishing age through hidden assistance.
entries.literal: Manifesting great response in extraordinary blessings, opening a flourishing age through hidden assistance.

entries.zh: 裒對信猶之典，咸修望秩之文。
entries.en: Gathering the canon of trust and response, all repair the texts of gazing upon and ranking.
entries.literal: Gathering the canon of trust and response, all repair the texts of gazing upon and ranking.

entries.zh: 嘉乃名山，奠茲勝地，下綿乾分，上直樞輝。
entries.en: Praising this famous mountain, establishing this excellent site—below it extends the heavenly allotment, above it faces the pivot's radiance.
entries.literal: Praising this famous mountain, establishing this excellent site—below it extends the heavenly allotment, above it faces the pivot's radiance.

entries.zh: 盤析木之津，達中原之氣。
entries.en: Coiling at the ford of the Wood Star, it reaches the qi of the Central Plain.
entries.literal: Coiling at the ford of the Wood Star, it reaches the qi of the Central Plain.

entries.zh: 廓除氛昆，函毓泰和。
entries.en: Sweeping away miasma and turbidity, it embraces and nurtures great harmony.
entries.literal: Sweeping away miasma and turbidity, it embraces and nurtures great harmony.

entries.zh: 仰惟光烈昭垂，徽音如在，即高明而清暑，克靜壽以安仁。
entries.en: Looking up, the bright merit shines down; the fine reputation is as if present—approaching the lofty and bright to clear summer heat, achieving tranquil longevity and peaceful benevolence.
entries.literal: Looking up, the bright merit shines down; the fine reputation is as if present—approaching the lofty and bright to clear summer heat, achieving tranquil longevity and peaceful benevolence.

entries.zh: 周廬安寧，厚澤浹洽。
entries.en: The surrounding lodges are tranquil; thick favor permeates all.
entries.literal: The surrounding lodges are tranquil; thick favor permeates all.

entries.zh: 朕祗循祖武，順講時巡，感美號以興懷，佩聖謨而介福。
entries.en: I reverently follow the ancestors' martial way, comply with the seasonal tour, am moved by the fine title to stir the heart, and wear the sage's counsel to receive blessing.
entries.literal: I reverently follow the ancestors' martial way, comply with the seasonal tour, am moved by the fine title to stir the heart, and wear the sage's counsel to receive blessing.

entries.zh: 言念誕彌之初度，言由翊衛之效靈。
entries.en: Speaking, I recall the first anniversary of birth; speaking, it comes from the assisting guard's manifestation of spirit.
entries.literal: Speaking, I recall the first anniversary of birth; speaking, it comes from the assisting guard's manifestation of spirit.

entries.zh: 然猶祀秩無章，神居不屋，非所以盡報功崇德之義，副追始樂原之心。
entries.en: Yet still the sacrificial rank lacks regulation, the spirit dwells without a house—this is not the way to fulfill the meaning of repaying merit and honoring virtue, nor to match the heart that pursues the beginning and delights in the origin.
entries.literal: Yet still the sacrificial rank lacks regulation, the spirit dwells without a house—this is not the way to fulfill the meaning of repaying merit and honoring virtue, nor to match the heart that pursues the beginning and delights in the origin.

entries.zh: 爰飾名稱，載新祠宇。
entries.en: Therefore we adorn the title and renew the shrine.
entries.literal: Therefore we adorn the title and renew the shrine.

entries.zh: 勒忱辭於貞琰，涓良日於元龜，彰服采以辨威，潔庪縣而致祭。
entries.en: We inscribe sincere words on the steadfast tablet, select an auspicious day from the primal tortoise, display robes and emblems to distinguish majesty, and purify the spirit table to perform the sacrifice.
entries.literal: We inscribe sincere words on the steadfast tablet, select an auspicious day from the primal tortoise, display robes and emblems to distinguish majesty, and purify the spirit table to perform the sacrifice.

entries.zh: 闡揚茂實，敷繹多儀。
entries.en: We expound flourishing substance and unfold the many rites.
entries.literal: We expound flourishing substance and unfold the many rites.

entries.zh: 今遣使某、副某，持節備物，冊命神為瑞聖公，仍敕有司歲時奉祀。
entries.en: Now we dispatch envoy so-and-so and deputy so-and-so, bearing credentials and complete regalia, to enfeoff the spirit as Duke of Auspicious Sageliness, and further command the responsible offices to offer seasonal sacrifices.
entries.literal: Now we dispatch envoy so-and-so and deputy so-and-so, bearing credentials and complete regalia, to enfeoff the spirit as Duke of Auspicious Sageliness, and further command the responsible offices to offer seasonal sacrifices.

entries.zh: 於戲！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 尚其聰明，歆此誠意，孚休惟永，亦莫不寧。」
entries.en: May it be intelligent and perceptive, receive this sincere intent; may blessing and rest be everlasting—all will be at peace."
entries.literal: May it be intelligent and perceptive, receive this sincere intent; may blessing and rest be everlasting—all will be at peace."

entries.zh: 大定四年五月，不雨。
entries.en: In the fifth month of Dading 4, there was no rain.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Dading, there was no rain.

entries.zh: 命禮部尚書王競祈雨北嶽，以定州長貳官充亞、終獻。
entries.en: The Minister of Rites Wang Jing was ordered to pray for rain at the Northern Peak; the chief and deputy officials of Ding Prefecture served as second and final offering officers.
entries.literal: The Minister of Rites Wang Jing was ordered to pray for rain at the Northern Peak; the chief and deputy officials of Ding Prefecture served as second and final offering officers.

entries.zh: 又卜日於都門北郊，望祀嶽鎮海瀆，有司行事，禮用酒脯醢。
entries.en: A day was also divined at the northern suburb outside the capital gate for gazing sacrifices to the mountain and city gods and the seas and rivers; the responsible offices performed the rite, using wine, dried meat, and pickled meat.
entries.literal: A day was also divined at the northern suburb outside the capital gate for gazing sacrifices to the mountain and city gods and the seas and rivers; the responsible offices performed the rite, using wine, dried meat, and pickled meat.

entries.zh: 後七日不雨，祈太社、太稷。
entries.en: After seven days with no rain, prayers were made at the Grand Altars of Earth and Grain.
entries.literal: After seven days with no rain, prayers were made at the Grand Altars of Earth and Grain.

entries.zh: 又七日祈宗廟，不雨，仍從嶽鎮海瀆如初祈。
entries.en: After another seven days prayers were made at the ancestral temple; still no rain, and they again followed the mountain and city gods and seas and rivers as at the first prayer.
entries.literal: After another seven days prayers were made at the ancestral temple; still no rain, and they again followed the mountain and city gods and seas and rivers as at the first prayer.

entries.zh: 其設神座，實樽罍，如常儀。
entries.en: They set out spirit seats and filled the wine vessels, as in the regular rite.
entries.literal: They set out spirit seats and filled the wine vessels, as in the regular rite.

entries.zh: 其樽罍用瓢齊，擇甘瓠去柢以為尊。
entries.en: For the wine vessels they used gourd ladles; selecting sweet gourds, they removed the stems to make wine vessels.
entries.literal: For the wine vessels they used gourd ladles; selecting sweet gourds, they removed the stems to make wine vessels.

entries.zh: 祝版惟五嶽、宗廟、社稷禦署，餘則否。
entries.en: Prayer boards received imperial endorsement only for the Five Peaks, the ancestral temple, and the Gods of Earth and Grain; for the rest, no.
entries.literal: Prayer boards received imperial endorsement only for the Five Peaks, the ancestral temple, and Earth and Grain; for the rest, no.

entries.zh: 後十日不雨，乃徒市，禁屠殺，斷傘扇，造土龍以祈。
entries.en: After ten more days without rain, they moved the market, forbade slaughter, stopped umbrellas and fans, and made an earthen dragon to pray.
entries.literal: After ten more days without rain, they moved the market, forbade slaughter, stopped umbrellas and fans, and made an earthen dragon to pray.

entries.zh: 雨足則報祀，送龍水中。
entries.en: When rain was sufficient they offered the report sacrifice and sent the dragon into the water.
entries.literal: When rain was sufficient they offered the report sacrifice and sent the dragon into the water.

entries.zh: 十七年夏六月，京畿久雨，遵祈雨儀，命諸寺觀啟道場祈禱。
entries.en: In the sixth month of summer in the seventeenth year, the capital region had long rain; following the rain-prayer rites, all temples and monasteries were ordered to open ritual grounds for prayer.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of summer in the seventeenth year, the capital region had long rain; following the rain-prayer rites, all temples and monasteries were ordered to open ritual grounds for prayer.

entries.zh: 宣聖廟
entries.en: The Temple of the Sagely Proclaimed One
entries.literal: Temple of the Sagely Proclaimed

entries.zh: 皇帝即御座，鳴鞭、報時畢，殿前班小起居，至侍立位。
entries.en: Once the emperor had taken the throne, the time was announced and the whip sounded. The front-hall formation made the minor bow of respect and took up their standing-attendance posts.
entries.literal: The emperor took the imperial seat; when the whip was sounded and the time announced, the front hall formation performed the minor bow of respect and reached their standing-attendance positions.

entries.zh: 引臣僚合班入，至丹墀小起居，引宰執上殿，其餘臣僚分班出。
entries.en: Officials were led in as a combined formation to the court terrace for the minor bow of respect. The chief ministers were escorted up to the hall while the remaining officials filed out by formation.
entries.literal: Officials were led in as a combined formation to the red terrace for the minor bow of respect; the chief ministers were led up to the hall and the remaining officials filed out by formation.

entries.zh: 閣門使奏辭榜子。
entries.en: The Gate Office commissioner announced the farewell notice.
entries.literal: The Gate Office commissioner reported the farewell notice board.

entries.zh: 先引夏使左入，傍折通班畢，至丹墀再拜，不出班奏：「聖躬萬福。」
entries.en: The Western Xia envoy was led in first from the left. After passing through the formation, he came to the court terrace and bowed again, then reported without leaving formation: "May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings."
entries.literal: First the Xi Xia envoy was led in from the left; when he had turned aside through the formation, he came to the red terrace and bowed again, and without leaving formation reported: "May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings."

entries.zh: 又再拜。
entries.en: He bowed again.
entries.literal: He bowed again.

entries.zh: 揖使副鞠躬，使出班，戀闕致詞，復位，又再拜，唱：「各好去。」
entries.en: The envoy and deputy were prompted to bow. The envoy stepped out of formation to deliver the parting words expressing reluctance to leave the court, returned to his place, and bowed again. The herald called out: "Each of you, go in peace."
entries.literal: The envoy and deputy were prompted to bow; the envoy left formation and delivered the parting words of lingering regard for the court, returned to place, bowed again, and the herald called: "Each of you, go in peace."

entries.zh: 引右出。
entries.en: He was led out on the right.
entries.literal: He was led out on the right.

entries.zh: 次引高麗使，如上儀，亦引右出。
entries.en: Next the Goryeo envoy was received according to the same protocol and was also led out on the right.
entries.literal: Next the Goryeo envoy was led in by the same protocol and was also led out on the right.

entries.zh: 次引宋使副左入，傍折通班畢，至丹墀，依上通六拜，各祗候，平立。
entries.en: Next the Song envoy and deputy were led in from the left. After passing through the formation, they came to the court terrace and performed six prostrations in all as prescribed above. Each remained in attendance standing at ease.
entries.literal: Next the Song envoy and deputy were led in from the left; when they had turned aside through the formation, they came to the red terrace and, following the above, performed six prostrations in all; each attended in place and stood level.

entries.zh: 閣使賜衣馬，鞠躬，聞敕，再拜。
entries.en: The Gate commissioner granted robes and horses. They bowed, heard the edict, and bowed again.
entries.literal: The Gate commissioner granted robes and horses; they bowed, heard the edict, and bowed again.

entries.zh: 賜衣馬畢，平身，搢笏，單跪，受別錄物過盡，出笏，拜起，謝恩，舞蹈，五拜。
entries.en: When the robes and horses had been granted, they stood upright, tucked in their court tablets, and knelt on one knee to receive the separate recorded items until all had been presented. They then produced their tablets, bowed and rose, offered thanks for imperial favor, and performed the ritual dance and five prostrations.
entries.literal: When the granting of robes and horses was finished, they stood level, tucked in their tablets, knelt on one knee, received the separate recorded items until all had passed, produced their tablets, bowed and rose, thanked for grace, and performed the ritual dance and five prostrations.

entries.zh: 有敕賜酒食，舞蹈，五拜。
entries.en: When an edict granted wine and food, they performed the ritual dance and five prostrations.
entries.literal: An edict granted wine and food; they performed the ritual dance and five prostrations.

entries.zh: 引使副左上露階，齊揖入欄內，揖鞠躬，大使少前拜跪受書，起復位。
entries.en: The envoy and deputy were led up the open steps on the left. They bowed together and entered the railing. The chief envoy was prompted to bow, stepped forward, knelt and bowed to receive the letter, then rose and returned to his place.
entries.literal: The envoy and deputy were led up the open steps on the left; they bowed together and entered the railing; they were prompted to bow; the chief envoy stepped slightly forward, knelt and bowed to receive the letter, rose and returned to place.

entries.zh: 揖使副齊鞠躬，受傳達畢，齊退，引左下至丹墀，鞠躬，喝：「各好去。」
entries.en: The envoy and deputy were prompted to bow together. When the transmitted message had been received, they all withdrew. They were led down on the left to the court terrace, bowed, and the herald called out: "Each of you, go in peace."
entries.literal: The envoy and deputy were prompted to bow together; when the transmitted message had been received, all withdrew together; they were led down on the left to the red terrace, bowed, and the herald called: "Each of you, go in peace."

entries.zh: 引右出。
entries.en: They were led out on the right.
entries.literal: They were led out on the right.

entries.zh: 次引宰執下殿，禮畢。
entries.en: The chief ministers were then led down from the hall, and the ceremony was complete.
entries.literal: Next the chief ministers were led down from the hall and the ceremony was finished.

entries.zh: 熙宗時，夏使入見，改為大起居。
entries.en: During the reign of Emperor Xizong, the Western Xia envoy's audience was changed to use the major bow of respect.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Xizong, when the Xi Xia envoy had an audience, it was changed to the major bow of respect.

entries.zh: 定制以宋使列于三品班，高麗、夏列于五品班。
entries.en: Regulations fixed the Song envoy in the third-rank formation and the Goryeo and Western Xia envoys in the fifth-rank formation.
entries.literal: It was fixed by regulation that the Song envoy was ranked in the third-rank formation, and Goryeo and Xi Xia in the fifth-rank formation.

entries.zh: 皇統二年六月，定臣使辭見，臣僚服色拜數止從常朝起居，三國使班品如舊。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the second year of Huangtong, regulations fixed that for envoys' farewell audiences, officials' dress colors and number of bows followed only the regular court bow of respect, while the three states' envoys kept their former formation ranks.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Huangtong, it was fixed that for envoy-officials' farewell audiences, officials' dress colors and number of bows followed only the regular court minor bow of respect, while the three states' envoys' formation ranks remained as before.

entries.zh: 俟殿前班及臣僚小起居畢，宰執升殿，余臣分班畢，乃令行入見及朝辭之禮。
entries.en: Only after the front-hall formation and the officials' minor bow of respect were finished, the chief ministers had ascended the hall, and the remaining officials had taken their formations was the court ordered to proceed with the audience and farewell ceremonies.
entries.literal: Only after the front hall formation and the officials' minor bow of respect were finished, the chief ministers ascended the hall, and the remaining officials had finished filing by formation, were the audience and farewell ceremonies ordered to proceed.

entries.zh: 凡入見則宋使先，禮畢夏使入，禮畢而高麗使入。
entries.en: At audiences the Song envoy always came first. When his ceremony was finished, the Western Xia envoy entered, and when that was finished, the Goryeo envoy entered.
entries.literal: In general, at audiences the Song envoy came first; when his ceremony was finished the Xi Xia envoy entered; when that ceremony was finished the Goryeo envoy entered.

entries.zh: 其朝辭則夏使先，禮畢而高麗使入，禮畢而宋使入。
entries.en: At farewell audiences the Western Xia envoy came first. When his ceremony was finished, the Goryeo envoy entered, and when that was finished, the Song envoy entered.
entries.literal: At farewell audiences the Xi Xia envoy came first; when his ceremony was finished the Goryeo envoy entered; when that ceremony was finished the Song envoy entered.

entries.zh: 夏、高麗朝辭之賜，則遣使就賜于會同館。
entries.en: Grants at the Western Xia and Goryeo farewell audiences were sent by envoys to bestow at the Hall of Joint Harmony.
entries.literal: Grants at the Xi Xia and Goryeo farewell audiences were sent by envoys to bestow at the Hall of Joint Harmony.

entries.zh: 惟宋使之賜則庭授。
entries.en: Only the Song envoy's grants were conferred in the courtyard.
entries.literal: Only the Song envoy's grants were conferred in the courtyard.

entries.zh: 舊高麗使至闕皆有私進禮，大定五年，上以宋、夏使皆無此禮，而小國獨有之，不可。
entries.en: Formerly Goryeo envoys always presented private gifts upon reaching the capital. In the fifth year of Dading, the emperor said that Song and Western Xia envoys had no such practice while a small state alone maintained it, which was unacceptable.
entries.literal: Formerly Goryeo envoys upon reaching the capital all had private presentation gifts; in the fifth year of Dading, the emperor said that Song and Xi Xia envoys had no such ceremony while a small state alone had it, which was not permissible.

entries.zh: 遂命罷之。
entries.en: He then ordered the practice abolished.
entries.literal: He then ordered it abolished.

entries.zh: 六年，詔外國使初見、朝辭則于左掖門出入，朝賀，賜宴則由應天門東偏門出入。
entries.en: In the sixth year, an edict ordered that foreign envoys should use the Left Flank Gate for their first audience and farewell audience, but the eastern side gate of the Gate of Accepting Heaven for court congratulations and granted banquets.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered that foreign envoys for their first audience and farewell audience should enter and exit by the Left Flank Gate, while for court congratulations and granted banquets they should enter and exit by the eastern side gate of the Gate of Accepting Heaven.

entries.zh: 外國使入見儀
entries.en: Ceremonies for Foreign Emissaries' Audiences
entries.literal: Ceremonies for foreign emissaries' audiences

entries.zh: 古者軍輿之制，各有名物表識，以祀以封，以田以戎，所以別上下、明等威也。
entries.en: In antiquity, regulations governing military carriages assigned distinct names and identifying insignia to each type, whether for sacrifice, enfeoffment, the hunt, or war—so that rank and authority could be clearly distinguished.
entries.literal: In antiquity the regulations for military carriages each had named objects and identifying marks, for sacrifice and for enfeoffment, for the hunt and for war—thereby to distinguish superior and inferior and to make clear rank and authority.

entries.zh: 歷代相承，互有損益，或因時創始，或襲舊致文，奇巧日滋，浮靡益蕩。
entries.en: Successive dynasties inherited these practices, each altering them here and there; some devised new forms to suit the times, others preserved old models for the sake of display. Ingenuity grew ever more elaborate, and lavish excess spread ever wider.
entries.literal: Dynasties handed these down in succession, each adding or reducing something; some created new forms according to the times, others followed old models to achieve ornament; ingenious contrivances grew daily, and extravagant excess swelled ever more.

entries.zh: 加以後世便習騎乘，車用蓋寡，惟於郊廟祀享法駕導引，為一代令儀而不敢廢也。
entries.en: Later ages moreover grew accustomed to riding horseback, so that carriages fell largely out of use. They survived only in the imperial procession at suburban and temple sacrifices, where they remained the prescribed ceremonial of the dynasty—and even that ritual no one dared abolish.
entries.literal: Moreover, in later ages people grew accustomed to riding on horseback, and carriages came to be little used; only at suburban and temple sacrifices, when the imperial procession was led forth, did they remain the prescribed ritual of an age—and even that they did not dare abolish.

entries.zh: 其于先王經世立法之意，寥乎闊哉！
entries.en: As for the intent of the former kings in establishing institutions to govern the world—that purpose now seems remote indeed.
entries.literal: As for the intent of the former kings in establishing institutions to govern the world—how remote and vast it has become!

entries.zh: 金初得遼之儀物，既而克宋，於是乎有車輅之制。
entries.en: When the Jin first acquired the Liao ceremonial regalia and later conquered the Song, they then established regulations for state carriages.
entries.literal: When the Jin first came into possession of the Liao ritual objects, and thereafter conquered the Song, they then had regulations for carriages and chariots.

entries.zh: 熙宗幸燕，始用法駕。
entries.en: When Emperor Xizong visited Yan, he first employed the full imperial procession.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xizong visited Yan, he first employed the imperial procession.

entries.zh: 迨至世宗，製作乃定，班班乎古矣！
entries.en: By the reign of Emperor Shizong, the specifications were finally settled—splendid indeed, in the manner of antiquity!
entries.literal: By the time of Emperor Shizong, the manufacture was fixed, and splendid indeed like the ancients!

entries.zh: 考禮文，證國史，以見一代之制度雲。
entries.en: By examining ritual texts and verifying them against dynastic histories, one may discern the institutions of the age.
entries.literal: Examining ritual texts and verifying against dynastic histories, one may see the institutions of an age.

entries.zh: 一品，轅用銀螭頭，涼棚杆子、月板並許以銀裝飾。
entries.en: First rank: shafts might use silver dragon heads; cool-awning poles and moon boards might all be ornamented in silver.
entries.literal: First rank: shafts used silver dragon heads; cool-awning poles and moon boards were all permitted silver ornament.

entries.zh: 三品以上，螭頭不得施銀，涼棚杆子、月板亦聽用銀為飾。
entries.en: Third rank and above: dragon heads might not be silvered, but cool-awning poles and moon boards might still use silver ornament.
entries.literal: Third rank and above: dragon heads might not use silver, but cool-awning poles and moon boards were permitted silver ornament.

entries.zh: 五品以上，轅獅頭。
entries.en: Fifth rank and above: lion heads on the shafts.
entries.literal: Fifth rank and above: lion heads on the shafts.

entries.zh: 六品以下，轅雲頭。
entries.en: Sixth rank and below: cloud heads on the shafts.
entries.literal: Sixth rank and below: cloud heads on the shafts.

entries.zh: 庶人坐車平頭，止用一色黑油。
entries.en: Commoners' riding carriages had level tops and used only black oil in a single color.
entries.literal: Commoners' riding carriages had level tops and used only one color of black oil.

entries.zh: 親王鞍，塗金銀裹，仍鈒以開花。
entries.en: Princes' saddles were coated and wrapped in gilt silver and chased with openwork floral patterns.
entries.literal: Princes' saddles were coated and wrapped in gilt silver, still chased with openwork flowers.

entries.zh: 障泥用紫羅，飾以錦。
entries.en: Mud-guards were of purple brocade ornamented with brocade.
entries.literal: Mud-guards used purple brocade, ornamented with brocade.

entries.zh: 轡以塗金銀裝，束用絲結。
entries.en: Bridles were wrapped in gilt silver and bound with silk knots.
entries.literal: Bridles were wrapped in gilt silver, bound with silk knots.

entries.zh: 皇家小功以上、太皇太后皇太后大功以上、皇后期親以上、並一品官、及官職俱至三品以上者，障泥許用金花。
entries.en: Members of the imperial clan from lesser merit mourning upward, the Grand and Regular Empress Dowagers from greater merit mourning upward, the empress from close kin upward, and first-rank officials—or those whose offices all reached third rank and above—might use gold floral patterns on mud-guards.
entries.literal: For the imperial clan from lesser merit mourning upward, for the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager from greater merit mourning upward, for the empress from close kin upward, and for first-rank officials and those whose offices all reached third rank and above, mud-guards were permitted to use gold floral patterns.

entries.zh: 若經賜或禦球場內，不在禁限。
entries.en: Items bestowed by imperial grant or used within the imperial ball ground were exempt from these restrictions.
entries.literal: If bestowed by imperial grant or within the imperial ball ground, they were not within the prohibition.

entries.zh: 舊制，親王、宰執任外者，與大興尹，皆服小帽、束帶、銀鞍、絲鞭。
entries.en: Formerly, princes and chief ministers posted outside the capital, along with the Daxing magistrate, all wore small caps, belt bindings, silver saddles, and silk whips.
entries.literal: Under the old regulations, when princes and chief ministers served outside the capital, together with the Daxing magistrate, all wore small caps, belt bindings, silver saddles, and silk whips.

entries.zh: 大定中，世宗以京尹亦外官三品，而與親王無別，遂命不得禦銀鞍、絲鞭，惟同外三品例，襆頭、帶、展皁視事。
entries.en: During Dading, Emperor Shizong ruled that the capital magistrate, though a third-rank outside post, should not share princely privileges; he was barred from silver saddles and silk whips and followed the outside-third-rank norm of headwrap, belt, and black boots for official business.
entries.literal: In the Dading era Emperor Shizong held that the capital magistrate, though also an outside official of third rank, should not be treated like princes, and ordered that he might not use silver saddles or silk whips but only follow the outside-third-rank precedent of headwrap, belt, and black boots for conducting affairs.

entries.zh: 承安二年，制護衛銅裝鞍轡不得借人。
entries.en: In the second year of Cheng'an [1197], guard-service copper-fitted saddles and bridles were forbidden to be lent out.
entries.literal: In the second year of Cheng'an, it was decreed that guard-service copper-fitted saddles and bridles might not be lent to others.

entries.zh: 庶人馬鞍許用黑漆，以骨、角、鐵為飾，不得用玉較具及金、銀、犀、象飾鞍轡。
entries.en: Commoners' saddles might use black lacquer with bone, horn, or iron ornament, but not jade cheekpieces or gold, silver, rhinoceros, or ivory fittings.
entries.literal: Commoners' horse saddles were permitted black lacquer, with bone, horn, and iron for ornament, but might not use jade cheekpieces or gold, silver, rhinoceros, or ivory saddle and bridle ornament.

entries.zh: 初，太宗即位，始服赭黃，自後視百官朝禦袍帶。
entries.en: When Emperor Taizong first took the throne, he adopted ochre-yellow and thereafter received officials in court robe and belt.
entries.literal: At first, when Emperor Taizong took the throne, he first wore ochre-yellow; thereafter he viewed the hundred officials in court robe and belt.

entries.zh: 章宗即位，以世宗之喪，有司請禦純吉，不從，乃服淡黃袍、烏犀帶。
entries.en: At Emperor Zhangzong's accession, during mourning for Emperor Shizong, officials requested pure auspicious dress; he refused and wore a pale yellow robe with rhinoceros belt.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhangzong took the throne, because of Emperor Shizong's mourning, offices requested pure auspicious dress; he did not consent, and wore pale yellow robe and rhinoceros belt.

entries.zh: 常朝則服小帽、紅襴、偏帶或束帶。
entries.en: For routine audiences he wore a small cap, red lan robe, and side belt or bound belt.
entries.literal: For regular audiences he wore small cap, red lan robe, and side belt or bound belt.

entries.zh: 書袋之制。
entries.en: Regulations for Document Pouches
entries.literal: Regulations for document pouches.

entries.zh: 大定十六年，世宗以吏員與士民之服無別，潛入民間受賕轀獄，有司不能檢察，遂定懸書袋之制。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year of Dading [1176], Emperor Shizong found clerks indistinguishable from commoners, secretly taking bribes among the people beyond official inspection, and mandated suspended document pouches.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year of Dading Emperor Shizong, because clerks' dress was indistinguishable from scholars and populace and they secretly entered the populace taking bribes and were thrown into prison while offices could not inspect, the suspended document-pouch regulation was fixed.

entries.zh: 省、樞密院令、譯史用紫襜絲為之，台、六部、宗正、統軍司、檢察司以黑斜皮為之，寺、監、隨朝諸局、並州縣，並黃皮為之，各長七寸，闊二寸、厚半寸，並於束帶上懸帶，公退則懸於便服，違者所司糾之。
entries.en: Provincial offices, Privy Council orders, and translators used purple dan silk pouches; the Censorate, Six Ministries, Imperial Clan Court, Commandery Office, and Inspection Office used black slanted leather; temples, directorates, court bureaus, and local governments used yellow leather. Each pouch was seven cun long, two cun wide, and half a cun thick, suspended from the official belt and moved to informal dress after hours; violators were disciplined by the responsible office.
entries.literal: For provincial offices, Privy Council orders, and translators purple dan silk was used; for the Censorate, Six Ministries, Imperial Clan Court, Commandery Office, and Inspection Office black slanted leather; for temples, directorates, various bureaus attending court, and prefectures and counties, all yellow leather; each seven cun long, two cun wide, and half a cun thick; all suspended from the bound belt; after leaving office suspended on informal dress; violators were corrected by the responsible office.

entries.zh: 輿服上
entries.en: Carriages and Clothing, Part One
entries.literal: Carriages and clothing, part one

entries.zh: 昔者先王因人之知畏而作刑，因人之知恥而作法。
entries.en: In ancient times, the former kings instituted punishments in response to humanity's capacity for fear, and established laws in response to humanity's capacity for shame.
entries.literal: In antiquity the former kings, because people knew fear, established punishments; because people knew shame, they established laws.

entries.zh: 畏也、恥也，五性之良知，七情之大閑也。
entries.en: Fear and shame are the innate moral sense within the five inherent dispositions and the great boundary restraining the seven emotions.
entries.literal: Fear and shame are the innate knowledge of the five natures and the great restraint of the seven emotions.

entries.zh: 是故，刑以治已然，法以禁未然，畏以處小人，恥以遇君子。
entries.en: Thus punishments address what has already occurred, laws prevent what has not yet occurred, fear governs petty men, and shame governs noble men.
entries.literal: Therefore punishments govern what has already happened, laws restrain what has not yet happened, fear handles petty men, shame treats noble men.

entries.zh: 君子知恥，小人知畏，天下平矣！
entries.en: When the noble know shame and the petty know fear, the realm is at peace.
entries.literal: When noble men know shame and petty men know fear, all under Heaven is at peace!

entries.zh: 是故先王養其威而用之，畏可以教愛。
entries.en: Therefore the former kings cultivated their authority and put it to use, for fear can teach one to love.
entries.literal: Therefore the former kings nurtured their authority and employed it; fear can teach love.

entries.zh: 慎其法而行之，恥可以立廉。
entries.en: They handled their laws with care and enforced them, for shame can establish integrity.
entries.literal: They were careful with their laws and carried them out; shame can establish integrity.

entries.zh: 愛以興仁，廉以興義，仁義興，刑法不幾於措乎？
entries.en: Love engenders benevolence, integrity engenders righteousness; when benevolence and righteousness flourish, punishments and laws would nearly become unnecessary, would they not?
entries.literal: Love gives rise to benevolence, integrity gives rise to righteousness; when benevolence and righteousness flourish, would punishments and laws not nearly fall into disuse?

entries.zh: 金初，法制簡易，無輕重貴賤之別，刑、贖並行，此可施諸新國，非經世久遠之規也。
entries.en: In the early Jin, the legal system was rudimentary, with no gradations of severity or rank; physical punishment and commutation by payment operated side by side. Such measures might suit a newly founded state, but they were no model for enduring governance.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jin, legal institutions were simple and crude, with no distinction between light and heavy or noble and base; corporal punishment and ransoms were applied in parallel. This could be applied in a new state but was not a regulation for long-lasting governance of the world.

entries.zh: 天會以來，漸從吏議，皇統頒制，兼用古律。
entries.en: From the Tianhui period onward, policy gradually followed officials' counsel; under Huangtong, regulations were promulgated that incorporated elements of older penal codes.
entries.literal: From the Tianhui era onward, they gradually followed officials' recommendations; Huangtong promulgated regulations, using ancient statutes together.

entries.zh: 厥後，正隆又有《續降制書》。
entries.en: Later, under Zhenglong, there appeared the Continued Promulgated Regulatory Documents.
entries.literal: Thereafter, in Zhenglong there was again the Continued Promulgated Regulatory Documents.

entries.zh: 大定有《權宜條理》，有《重修制條》。
entries.en: The Dading era produced the Provisional Articles and Ordinances and the Recast Regulatory Articles.
entries.literal: In Dading there were the Provisional Articles and Ordinances and the Recast Regulatory Articles.

entries.zh: 明昌之世，《律義》、《敕條》並修，品式當浸備。
entries.en: During the Mingchang reign, the Legal Commentaries and Imperial Decree Articles were both revised, and the classification of offenses should have grown increasingly comprehensive.
entries.literal: In the Mingchang era, the Legal Commentaries and Imperial Decree Articles were both revised, and categories and forms should have gradually become complete.

entries.zh: 既而《泰和律義》成書，宜無遺憾。
entries.en: When the Tahe Legal Commentaries were finally completed, nothing should have been left wanting.
entries.literal: Subsequently the Tahe Legal Commentaries were completed as a book; there ought to have been no regrets.

entries.zh: 然國脈紓蹙，風俗醇樗，世道升降，君子觀一代之刑法，每有以先知焉。
entries.en: Yet as the dynasty's vital force waned and customs grew rustic, as the moral climate shifted, learned observers who studied a generation's penal code could often read in advance which way the realm was headed.
entries.literal: Yet the nation's life-thread was slack and constricted, customs were pure but blunt, the age's way rose and fell; noble men observing a generation's penal laws often had grounds for foreknowledge.

entries.zh: 金法以杖折徒，累及二百，州縣立威，甚者置刃於杖，虐於肉刑。
entries.en: Jin law permitted beating with staffs to substitute for penal servitude, with strokes accumulating to as many as two hundred; local officials used this to assert their authority, and in the worst cases they fitted blades to the staffs, making the punishment more brutal than dismemberment itself.
entries.literal: Jin law used the staff to commute penal servitude, accumulating up to two hundred strokes; prefectures and counties established authority, and in extreme cases they placed blades on the staff, more cruel than corporal punishment.

entries.zh: 季年，君臣好用筐篋故習，由是以深文傅致為能吏，以慘酷辦事為長才。
entries.en: In the dynasty's closing years, court and ministers alike fell back on petty corruption as custom; officials who twisted the law to secure convictions passed as men of ability, and those who handled cases with cruelty passed as men of outstanding talent.
entries.literal: In the dynasty's final years, ruler and ministers readily favored old habits of petty graft; thereby making severe legal construction the mark of a capable official and handling affairs with brutality the sign of great talent.

entries.zh: 百司奸贓真犯，此可決也，而微過亦然。
entries.en: Flagrant corruption among the bureaucracy warranted decisive punishment, yet even minor infractions were punished just as harshly.
entries.literal: For true offenses of corruption among the hundred offices this could be decided, yet minor faults were treated the same.

entries.zh: 風紀之臣，失糾皆決。
entries.en: Even censors responsible for discipline were beaten for any failure to correct wrongdoing.
entries.literal: Officials charged with upholding standards—any failure in correction was decided by corporal punishment.

entries.zh: 考滿，校其受決多寡以為殿最。
entries.en: At term's end, officials were ranked according to how many beating sentences they had imposed—more strokes meant a better evaluation.
entries.literal: At the end of their term of evaluation, they compared how many punishments each had received to determine ranking from lowest to highest.

entries.zh: 原其立法初意，欲以同疏戚、壹小大，使之咸就繩約於律令之中，莫不齊手並足以聽公上之所為，蓋秦人強主威之意也。
entries.en: The original intent behind their legislation was to erase distinctions of kinship and rank, to force everyone alike into the constraints of statute, to make all stand with hands level and feet aligned, awaiting whatever the throne commanded—essentially the Qin ideal of concentrating sovereign power.
entries.literal: Investigating the original intent of their legislation, they wished to make kinship bonds uniform, make great and small one, cause all to submit to constraint within statutes and ordinances, none not leveling hands and joining feet to heed what the public authority did—essentially the intent of Qin men to strengthen the ruler's authority.

entries.zh: 是以待宗室少恩，待大夫士少禮。
entries.en: Hence the court showed scant kindness toward the imperial clan and scant ritual deference toward the official elite.
entries.literal: Therefore they treated the imperial clan with little kindness and treated great officers and scholars with little ceremony.

entries.zh: 終金之代，忍恥以就功名，雖一時名士有所不免。
entries.en: Throughout the Jin dynasty, men endured humiliation to advance their careers, and even the most celebrated scholars of the age were not spared.
entries.literal: Throughout the Jin dynasty, men endured shame to pursue fame and achievement; even renowned figures of the day were not exempt.

entries.zh: 至於避辱遠引，罕聞其人。
entries.en: Men who withdrew from office to avoid disgrace were exceedingly rare.
entries.literal: As for avoiding disgrace and withdrawing far away, one rarely heard of such persons.

entries.zh: 殊不知君子無恥而犯義，則小人無畏而犯刑矣。
entries.en: They failed to see that when the noble lose their sense of shame and transgress moral duty, the petty lose their fear and transgress the penal code.
entries.literal: They did not realize that when noble men are without shame and violate righteousness, then petty men are without fear and violate punishments.

entries.zh: 是故論者於教愛立廉之道，往往致太息之意焉。
entries.en: For this reason, commentators who reflected on the path of teaching love and establishing integrity often could only sigh in regret.
entries.literal: Therefore commentators on the way of teaching love and establishing integrity often expressed deep sighs.

entries.zh: 雖然，世宗臨御，法司奏讞，或去律援經，或揆義制法。
entries.en: Nevertheless, under Emperor Shizong's reign, when legal offices reported cases for judgment, they sometimes set aside the code to appeal to the classics, and sometimes fashioned law by weighing moral principle.
entries.literal: Nevertheless, when Shizong took the throne, the legal offices reported cases for judgment; sometimes they departed from statutes and appealed to the classics, sometimes they measured meaning to formulate law.

entries.zh: 近古人君聽斷，言幾於道，鮮有及之者。
entries.en: Among rulers of recent antiquity in hearing and deciding cases, his pronouncements came close to the Way itself; few could equal him.
entries.literal: Among recent ancient rulers' hearing and deciding cases, his words nearly reached the Way; few could match him.

entries.zh: 章宗、宣宗嘗親民事，當寧裁決，寬猛出入雖時或過中，跡其矜恕之多，猶有祖風焉。
entries.en: Emperors Zhangzong and Xuanzong sometimes took civil cases in hand themselves, rendering judgment from the throne; though their leniency and severity occasionally overshot the mark, the record of their compassion and clemency still bore traces of their forebears' style.
entries.literal: Zhangzong and Xuanzong at times personally handled civil affairs, deciding cases at the imperial seat; leniency and severity in their departures sometimes exceeded the mean, yet tracing their many acts of compassion and pardon, there was still ancestral style.

entries.zh: 簡牘所存，可為高抬貴手者，《本紀》、《刑志》詳略互見云。
entries.en: What survives in the written record worthy of note may be found in the Basic Annals and this Treatise on Punishment, where detail and summary complement each other throughout.
entries.literal: What survives in documents that can be held up for high regard: the Basic Annals and the Treatise on Punishment show detail and summary complementing each other.

entries.zh: 金國舊俗，輕罪笞以柳篸，殺人及盜劫者，擊其腦殺之，沒其家貲，以十之四入官，其六償主，並以家人為奴婢。
entries.en: By Jin custom, minor offenses were punished with flogging using willow switches; murderers and robbers were struck on the head and killed, their household property confiscated, with four-tenths going to the state and six-tenths to compensate the victim, while all members of the household were enslaved.
entries.literal: Jin state's old custom: light offenses were flogged with willow switches; killers and robbers were struck on the brain and killed, their household property confiscated, four-tenths entering the government, six-tenths compensating the victim, and their household members all made slaves and maidservants.

entries.zh: 其親屬欲以馬牛雜物贖者從之。
entries.en: Relatives who wished to ransom them with horses, cattle, or other goods were permitted to do so.
entries.literal: If their kin wished to ransom them with horses, cattle, and miscellaneous goods, this was permitted.

entries.zh: 或重罪亦聽自贖，然恐無辨于齊民，則劓、刵以為別。
entries.en: Even serious offenses sometimes allowed self-ransom, but lest offenders be indistinguishable from ordinary folk, they were marked by cutting off the nose or ears.
entries.literal: Even serious offenses were sometimes permitted self-ransom, yet fearing no distinction from common people, they used nose-cutting and ear-cutting as marks of differentiation.

entries.zh: 其獄則掘地深廣數丈為之。
entries.en: Prisons were pits dug several zhang deep and wide in the earth.
entries.literal: Their prisons were made by digging earth several zhang deep and wide.

entries.zh: 太宗雖承太祖無變舊風之訓，亦稍用遼、宋法。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong, though he inherited Taizu's injunction to preserve old customs unchanged, also drew somewhat on Liao and Song legal practice.
entries.literal: Taizong, though inheriting Taizu's instruction not to change old customs, also slightly used Liao and Song law.

entries.zh: 天會七年，詔凡竊盜，但得物徒三年，十貫以上徒五年，刺字充下軍，三十貫以上終身，仍以贓滿盡命刺字於面，五十貫以上死，征償如舊制。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Tianhui, an edict decreed that any thief who obtained goods would serve three years at penal labor; ten strings or more warranted five years, tattooing, and assignment to the lower army; thirty strings or more meant lifelong servitude, with full-value thefts tattooed on the face; fifty strings or more meant death, with compensation collected as under the old system.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Tianhui, an edict: for all theft, if goods were obtained, penal servitude three years; ten strings or more, penal servitude five years, tattooed characters and assigned to the lower army; thirty strings or more, for life, and when stolen goods reached the full amount, ordered tattooed on the face; fifty strings or more, death, collection of compensation as in the old system.

entries.zh: 熙宗天眷元年十月，禁親王以下佩刀入宮。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the first year of Tianjuan under Emperor Xizong, imperial princes and those below them were forbidden to carry swords into the palace.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Tianjuan under Xizong, princes of the blood and below were forbidden to wear swords when entering the palace.

entries.zh: 衛禁之法，實自此始。
entries.en: Palace security regulations in fact date from this decree.
entries.literal: Palace guard prohibitions in fact began from this.

entries.zh: 三年，復取河南地，乃詔其民，約所用刑法皆從律文，罷獄卒酷毒刑具，以從寬恕。
entries.en: In the third year, after recovering the Henan region, the court issued an edict to its inhabitants that all criminal law applied there should follow statutory text, abolishing jailers' cruel instruments of torture in favor of lenient treatment.
entries.literal: In the third year, having recovered the Henan territory, they then issued an edict its people that the criminal law to be applied should all follow statutory text, abolishing jailers' cruel and poisonous instruments of punishment to follow leniency and pardon.

entries.zh: 至皇統間，詔諸臣，以本朝舊制，兼采隋、唐之制，參遼、宋之法。
entries.en: By the Huangtong period, ministers were commanded to compile law drawing on the dynasty's own old institutions, incorporating elements of Sui and Tang practice and referencing Liao and Song codes.
entries.literal: By the Huangtong period, they issued an edict the various ministers to take this dynasty's old system, together adopt Sui and Tang systems, and reference Liao and Song law.

entries.zh: 類以成書，名曰《皇統制》，頒行中外。
entries.en: These were classified into a completed code named the Huangtong Regulations and promulgated throughout the realm.
entries.literal: They were classified to complete a book, named the Huangtong Regulations, and promulgated within and without.

entries.zh: 時制，杖罪至百，則臀、背分決。
entries.en: Under that system, when a beating sentence reached one hundred strokes, the blows were divided between buttocks and back.
entries.literal: At that time the system was: for staff punishment up to one hundred strokes, buttocks and back were decided separately.

entries.zh: 及海陵庶人以脊近心腹，遂禁之，雖主決奴牌，亦論以違制。
entries.en: When the usurper Hailing took power, he forbade back strokes because the back lies near the vital organs; even when masters punished slaves by tablet, back strokes were treated as a violation of regulations.
entries.literal: When Hailing the commoner [usurper], because the back is near the heart and belly, then forbade it; even when masters decided punishment on slave tablets, it was still judged as violating regulations.

entries.zh: 又多變易舊制，至正隆間，著為《續降制書》，與《皇統制》並行焉。
entries.en: He also altered the old system in many respects; by the Zhenglong period these were codified as the Continued Promulgated Regulatory Documents, applied alongside the Huangtong Regulations.
entries.literal: He also changed the old system in many ways; by the Zhenglong period it was written as the Continued Promulgated Regulatory Documents, applied in parallel with the Huangtong Regulations.

entries.zh: 然二君任情用法，自有異於是者矣。
entries.en: Yet both rulers applied the law as whim dictated, often departing from what the codes prescribed.
entries.literal: Yet the two rulers applied law according to whim, naturally having differences from this.

entries.zh: 及世宗即位，以正隆之亂，盜賊公行，兵甲未息，一時制旨多從時宜，遂集為《軍前權宜條理》。
entries.en: When Shizong ascended the throne, amid the chaos of the Zhenglong period, with bandits roaming freely and warfare still unsettled, many temporary edicts followed expedient needs and were collected as the Provisional Articles and Ordinances Before the Army.
entries.literal: When Shizong took the throne, because of the Zhenglong turmoil, bandits walked openly, arms and armor had not ceased; temporary regulatory edicts mostly followed timely fitness, and were then collected as the Provisional Articles and Ordinances Before the Army.

entries.zh: 大定四年，尚書省奏：「大興民男子李十、婦人楊仙哥並以亂言當斬。」
entries.en: In the fourth year of Dading, the Secretariat reported: 'The Daxing commoners Li Shi, a man, and Yang Xian'ge, a woman, have both spoken disorderly words and should be beheaded.'
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Dading, the Secretariat memorialized: 'Daxing commoner, male Li Shi and woman Yang Xian'ge, both for disorderly speech should be beheaded.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「愚民不識典法，有司亦未嘗丁寧誥戒，豈可遽加極刑。」
entries.en: The emperor said: 'These foolish commoners do not know the law, and the responsible offices have never earnestly warned them—how can we hastily impose the death penalty?'
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'Foolish commoners do not know canonical law; the responsible offices also have never earnestly admonished and warned—how can we hastily apply extreme punishment?'

entries.zh: 以減死論。
entries.en: They were sentenced to commuted death instead.
entries.literal: They were sentenced with commuted death.

entries.zh: 五年，命有司復加刪定《條理》，與前《制書》兼用。
entries.en: In the fifth year, he ordered officials to revise the Articles and Ordinances again for use alongside the earlier Regulatory Documents.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, he ordered the responsible offices again to revise and fix the Articles and Ordinances, to be used together with the previous Regulatory Documents.

entries.zh: 七年，左藏庫夜有盜殺都監郭良臣盜金珠，求盜不得。
entries.en: In the seventh year, a thief broke into the Left Treasury at night, killed the director Guo Liangchen, and stole gold and pearls, but the culprit could not be found.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, at night in the Left Treasury there was a thief who killed Director Guo Liangchen and stole gold and pearls; the thief could not be found.

entries.zh: 命點檢司治之，執其可疑者八人鞫之，掠三人死，五人誣伏。
entries.en: The Inspection Office was ordered to investigate; eight suspects were seized and interrogated, three dying under torture and five falsely confessing.
entries.literal: He ordered the Inspection Office to handle it; they seized eight suspicious persons and interrogated them, torturing three to death, five falsely confessing.

entries.zh: 上疑之，命同知大興府事移剌道雜治。
entries.en: The emperor grew suspicious and ordered Yila Dao, associate administrator of Daxing Prefecture, to conduct a separate investigation.
entries.literal: The emperor was suspicious and ordered Associate Administrator of Daxing Prefecture Yila Dao to conduct a mixed investigation.

entries.zh: 既而親軍百夫長阿思缽鬻金於市，事覺，伏誅。
entries.en: Soon afterward an imperial guard centurion named Asibo was discovered selling gold in the market; the crime was exposed and he was executed.
entries.literal: Subsequently an imperial guard centurion Asibo sold gold in the market; the matter was discovered and he submitted to execution.

entries.zh: 上聞之曰：「箠楚之下，何求不得，奈何鞫獄者不以情求之乎？」
entries.en: On hearing this the emperor said: 'Under the rod and whip, what confession cannot be extracted? Why do interrogators not seek the truth according to the facts?'
entries.literal: On hearing this the emperor said: 'Under the rod and whip, what cannot be obtained? Why do those who interrogate prisoners not seek according to the facts?'

entries.zh: 賜死者錢人二百貫，不死者五十貫。
entries.en: He granted two hundred strings of cash to the families of the dead and fifty strings to the survivors.
entries.literal: He bestowed on the dead two hundred strings of cash per person, on those not dead fifty strings.

entries.zh: 於是禁護衛百夫長、五十夫長非直日不得帶刀入宮。
entries.en: Thereupon centurions and half-centurions of the guard were forbidden to carry swords into the palace except on their assigned duty days.
entries.literal: Thereupon he forbade guard centurions and half-centurions, unless on daily duty, from carrying swords into the palace.

entries.zh: 是歲，斷死囚二十人。
entries.en: That year, twenty prisoners were sentenced to death.
entries.literal: That year, twenty death-row prisoners were decided.

entries.zh: 八年，製品官犯賭博法，贓不滿五十貫者其法杖，聽贖。
entries.en: In the eighth year, regulations were issued that ranked officials who violated gambling laws, when the stakes did not reach fifty strings, would receive beating by law with commutation permitted.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, he regulated that officials of rank who violated the gambling law, when stolen goods did not reach fifty strings, should by law receive the staff, with redemption permitted.

entries.zh: 再犯者杖之。
entries.en: Repeat offenders were beaten.
entries.literal: Repeat offenders were staff-punished.

entries.zh: 且曰：「杖者所以罰小人也。
entries.en: He also said: 'The staff is the punishment reserved for petty men.
entries.literal: Moreover he said: 'The staff is what is used to punish petty men.

entries.zh: 既為職官，當先廉恥，既無廉恥，故以小人之罰罰之。」
entries.en: Since they hold office, they should possess integrity and shame; lacking both, they are punished with the penalty reserved for petty men.'
entries.literal: Since they are already office-holders, they should first have integrity and shame; since they have no integrity and shame, therefore they are punished with petty men's punishment.'

entries.zh: 九年，因御史臺奏獄事，上曰：「近聞法官或各執所見，或觀望宰執之意，自今制無正條者皆以律文為准。」
entries.en: In the ninth year, when the Censorate reported on prison affairs, the emperor said: 'I have lately heard that judges sometimes cling to their own views or watch for the chief ministers' intent—from now on, wherever regulations lack a proper article, the statutory text shall be the standard.'
entries.literal: In the ninth year, because the Censorate reported prison affairs, the emperor said: 'Recently I have heard that judges sometimes each cling to their own views, sometimes watch and wait for the chief ministers' intent—from now on where regulations have no proper article, all shall take statutory text as standard.'

entries.zh: 復命杖至百者臀、背分受，如舊法。
entries.en: He also restored the old rule that when a beating reached one hundred strokes, the blows were divided between buttocks and back.
entries.literal: He again ordered that when staff reached one hundred, buttocks and back should receive separately, as in the old law.

entries.zh: 已而，上謂宰臣曰：「朕念罪人杖不分受，恐至深重，乃令復舊。
entries.en: Shortly afterward, the emperor told his chief ministers: 'I had feared that when beating was not divided between buttocks and back, the injury would be too severe, and so I restored the old practice.
entries.literal: Shortly after, the emperor told the chief ministers: 'I considered that when criminals' staff was not received separately, I feared it would reach too deep and heavy, and therefore ordered restoration of the old way.

entries.zh: 今聞民間有不欲者，其令罷之。」
entries.en: Now I hear that the people do not want it—let it be abolished.'
entries.literal: Now I hear that among the people there are those who do not wish it—let this be ordered abolished.'

entries.zh: 十年，尚書省奏：「河中府張錦自言復父仇，法當死。」
entries.en: In the tenth year, the Secretariat reported: 'Zhang Jin of Hezhong Prefecture has declared that he avenged his father's death; by law he should die.'
entries.literal: In the tenth year, the Secretariat memorialized: 'Hezhong Prefecture's Zhang Jin himself stated he avenged his father's enmity; by law he should die.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「彼復父仇，又自言之，烈士也。
entries.en: The emperor said: 'He avenged his father and confessed it himself—he is a man of fierce integrity.
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'He avenged his father's enmity and moreover spoke of it himself—a man of fierce integrity.

entries.zh: 以減死論。」
entries.en: He was sentenced to commuted death instead.'
entries.literal: He was sentenced with commuted death.'

entries.zh: 十一年，詔諭有司曰：「應司獄廨舍須近獄安置，囚禁之事常親提控，其獄卒必選年深而信實者輪直。」
entries.en: In the eleventh year, an edict instructed officials: 'Prison offices must be located near the jail; imprisonment must be personally supervised; and jailers must be chosen from experienced, trustworthy men serving in rotation.'
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, an edict instructed the responsible offices: 'Prison offices' quarters must be placed near the prison; matters of imprisonment should be personally supervised in control; prison guards must be selected from those of long years who are trustworthy and sincere, rotating duty.'

entries.zh: 十二年，尚書省言：「內丘令蒲察台補自科部內錢立德政碑，復有其餘錢二百餘貫，罪當 除名。
entries.en: In the twelfth year, the Secretariat reported: 'Pucha Taibu, magistrate of Neiqiu, used departmental funds to erect a merit stele and kept over two hundred strings besides; the offense warrants dismissal from office.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, the Secretariat stated: 'Neiqiu magistrate Pucha Taibu, from funds within his department, erected a merit stele, and moreover had over two hundred strings remaining; the offense warrants dismissal from office.

entries.zh: 今遇赦當敘，仍免徵贓。」
entries.en: An amnesty now entitles him to reinstatement, with confiscation waived.'
entries.literal: Now encountering an amnesty he should be reappointed, and still be exempted from collecting stolen goods.'

entries.zh: 上以貪偽，勿敘，且曰：「乞取之贓，若有赦原，予者何辜？
entries.en: The emperor, deeming this greedy fraud, forbade reinstatement and said: 'If stolen goods obtained by extortion are pardoned by amnesty, what wrong have the victims done?
entries.literal: The emperor, because of greedy falsity, forbade reappointment, and moreover said: 'For stolen goods obtained by begging and taking, if there is amnesty and pardon, what guilt do the givers have?

entries.zh: 自今可並追還其主，惟應入官者免徵。」
entries.en: Henceforth such goods must all be returned to their owners; only what should go to the state may be exempted from collection.'
entries.literal: From now on all may together be pursued and returned to their owners; only what should enter the government is exempted from collection.'

entries.zh: 尚書省奏，盜有發塚者，上曰：「功臣墳墓亦有被發者，蓋無告捕之賞，故人無所畏。
entries.en: When the Secretariat reported tomb robberies, the emperor said: 'Even the graves of meritorious officials have been opened—probably because there is no reward for reporting and capturing them, so people have nothing to fear.
entries.literal: The Secretariat memorialized that there were thieves who opened tombs; the emperor said: 'Meritorious officials' graves also have been opened—probably because there is no reward for reporting and capturing, so people have nothing to fear.

entries.zh: 自今告得實者量與給賞。」
entries.en: Henceforth informants whose reports prove true shall receive rewards in proportion.'
entries.literal: From now on those who report and it is verified shall be given rewards in measured amount.'

entries.zh: 故咸平尹石抹阿沒剌以贓死於獄，上謂：「其不屍諸市已為厚幸。
entries.en: The former administrator of Xianping, Shimou Amela, died in prison for corruption; the emperor remarked: 'That his corpse was not exposed in the marketplace was already great leniency.
entries.literal: Former Xianping Administrator Shimou Amela died in prison for corruption; the emperor said: 'That his corpse was not exposed in the market was already thick favor.

entries.zh: 貧窮而為盜賊，蓋不得已。
entries.en: Men who turn to banditry out of poverty do so from necessity.
entries.literal: Being poor and becoming bandits and thieves is probably unavoidable necessity.

entries.zh: 三品職官以贓至死，愚亦甚矣！
entries.en: But for a third-rank official to die for corruption—how profoundly foolish!
entries.literal: A third-rank office-holder dying for corruption—how extremely foolish!

entries.zh: 其諸子可皆除名。」
entries.en: All his sons shall be dismissed from office.'
entries.literal: His various sons may all be dismissed from office.'

entries.zh: 先是，詔自今除名人子孫有在仕者並取奏裁。
entries.en: Earlier, an edict had decreed that henceforth the sons of dismissed officials who held office must all be submitted for imperial decision.
entries.literal: Earlier, an edict had stated that from now on dismissed persons' descendants who held office should all be submitted for imperial decision.

entries.zh: 十三年，詔立春後、立秋前，及大祭祀，月朔、望，上、下弦，二十四氣，雨未晴，夜未明，休暇並禁屠宰日，皆不聽決死刑，惟強盜則不待秋後。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year, an edict forbade capital sentences from after Beginning of Spring until before Beginning of Autumn, and also on days of great sacrifice, new and full moons, quarter moons, the twenty-four seasonal nodes, rainy days, before dawn, holidays, and days when slaughter was forbidden—except for armed robbers, who need not wait until autumn.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, an edict: after Beginning of Spring and before Beginning of Autumn, and great sacrifices, new and full moons, first and last quarters, the twenty-four qi, when rain had not cleared, when night had not brightened, rest days and forbidden slaughter days—all did not permit deciding capital punishment, except bandits and robbers who need not wait until after autumn.

entries.zh: 十五年，詔有司曰：「朕惟人命至重，而在制竊盜贓至五十貫者處死，自今可令至八十貫者處死。」
entries.en: In the fifteenth year, the emperor issued an edict to officials: 'I hold human life supremely precious; yet the regulations execute thieves when stolen goods reach fifty strings—from now on let the threshold be eighty strings.'
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year, an edict to the responsible offices: 'I consider human life supremely heavy; yet in the regulations, theft with stolen goods reaching fifty strings is punished with death—from now on it may be ordered that reaching eighty strings is punished with death.'

entries.zh: 十七年，陳言者乞設提刑司，以糾諸路刑獄之失。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year, memorialists requested establishing an office to supervise punishments and correct errors in prisons on the various circuits.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year, memorializers requested establishing a Office for Elevating Punishments to correct errors in penal prisons on the various circuits.

entries.zh: 尚書省議，以謂久恐滋弊。
entries.en: The Secretariat deliberated that such an office would breed abuses over time.
entries.literal: The Secretariat deliberated, considering that in the long run they feared breeding abuses.

entries.zh: 上乃命距京師數千里外懷冤上訴者，集其事以待選官就問。
entries.en: The emperor instead ordered that grievants appealing from thousands of li beyond the capital should have their cases collected pending dispatch of selected officials to investigate on site.
entries.literal: The emperor then ordered that those bearing grievances and appealing who were several thousand li from the capital should have their matters collected to await selection of officials to go and inquire.

entries.zh: 二十年，上見有蹂踐禾稼者，謂宰相曰：「今後有踐民田者杖六十，盜人穀者杖八十，並償其直。」
entries.en: In the twentieth year, seeing people trampling crops in the fields, the emperor told his chief ministers: 'Henceforth anyone who treads upon a farmer's fields shall receive sixty strokes of the staff, and anyone who steals another's grain shall receive eighty, and in both cases shall pay full compensation.'
