entries.literal: In the twentieth year, the emperor saw persons trampling crops and said to the chief ministers: 'Henceforth whoever tramples civilian fields shall receive sixty strokes of the staff; whoever steals another's grain shall receive eighty strokes, and in both cases shall compensate the full value.'

entries.zh: 二十一年，尚書省奏：「鞏州民馬俊妻安姐與管卓姦，俊以斧擊殺之，罪當死。」
entries.en: In the twenty-first year, the Department of State Affairs reported: 'A commoner of Gong Prefecture, Ma Jun, learned that his wife Anjie had committed adultery with Guan Zhuo and killed him with an axe—a capital offense.'
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year, the Department of State Affairs memorialized: 'Gong Prefecture commoner Ma Jun's wife Anjie committed adultery with Guan Zhuo; Jun struck and killed him with an axe—the offense warrants death.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「可減死一等，以戒敗風俗者。」
entries.en: The emperor said: 'Reduce the death sentence by one grade, as a warning to those who corrupt public morals.'
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'His death penalty may be reduced by one grade, to warn those who ruin custom and morals.'

entries.zh: 二十二年，上謂宰臣曰：「凡尚書省送大理寺文字，一斷便可聞奏。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year, the emperor told his chief ministers: 'Whenever the Department of State Affairs forwards a case to the Office of Imperial Justice, a single adjudication should suffice for reporting to the throne.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year, the emperor told the chief ministers: 'All documents the Department of State Affairs sends to the Office of Imperial Justice, once decided may immediately be reported to Us.

entries.zh: 如烏古論公說事，近取觀之，初送法寺如法裁斷，再送司直披詳，又送闔寺參詳，反覆三次，妄生情見，不得結絕。
entries.en: Consider the Wugulun Gong case, which We recently reviewed: it was first sent to the legal office for adjudication under the code, then to the reviewing censor for detailed scrutiny, then to the entire tribunal for joint deliberation—three rounds in all, during which discretionary interpretations were invented on every pass, and the case still could not be closed.
entries.literal: Take for example the Wugulun Gong affair—We recently examined it: first sent to the legal office for judgment according to law, again sent to the reviewing censor for detailed examination, again sent to the whole office for joint deliberation—back and forth three times, wantonly generating discretionary views, unable to bring closure.

entries.zh: 朕以國政不宜滯留，昨雖炙艾六百炷，未嘗一日不坐朝，欲使卿等知勤政也。
entries.en: We hold that state business must not be delayed; though yesterday We underwent six hundred moxibustion treatments, We did not miss a single day of court, precisely so that you would understand what diligent governance requires.
entries.literal: We hold that state affairs ought not linger; yesterday though We underwent moxibustion with six hundred cones, not one day did We fail to hold court, wishing to make you all know diligent governance.

entries.zh: 自今可止一次送寺，闔寺披詳，荀有情見即具以聞，毋使滯留也。」
entries.en: Henceforth send each case to the tribunal only once for full deliberation; if discretionary views arise, report them completely, but do not allow cases to stagnate.'
entries.literal: From now on send to the office only once; the whole office shall examine in detail—if there are discretionary views, report them fully; do not let matters linger.'

entries.zh: 二十三年，尚書省奏：「益都民範德年七十六，為劉祐毆殺。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year, the Department of State Affairs reported: 'Fan De, a seventy-six-year-old commoner of Yidu, was beaten to death by Liu You.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year, the Department of State Affairs memorialized: 'Yidu commoner Fan De, age seventy-six, was beaten to death by Liu You.

entries.zh: 祐法當死，以祐父母年俱七十餘，家無侍丁，上請。」
entries.en: You merited death under the law, but because both his parents were over seventy and the household had no adult son to support them, a petition for clemency was submitted.'
entries.literal: By law You merited death; because You's parents were both over seventy, and the household had no adult sons to serve them, they submitted a petition upward.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「范德與祐父母年相若，自當如父母相待，至毆殺之，難議末減，其論如法。」
entries.en: The emperor said: 'Fan De was about the same age as You's parents; You ought to have treated him with the deference owed to parents, yet You beat him to death—mitigation is difficult; adjudicate strictly according to law.'
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'Fan De and You's parents were of like age; he ought naturally to have treated them as parents—yet he beat one to death; it is hard to argue for final mitigation; decide according to law.'

entries.zh: 尚書省奏招討司官及禿裏乞取本部財物制，上曰：「遠人止可矜恤，若進貢不闕，更以兵邀之，強取財物，與盜何異？
entries.en: When the Department of State Affairs submitted regulations on pacification commissioners and Tuli envoys seizing local property, the emperor said: 'Frontier peoples deserve compassion; if their tribute obligations are met, to send troops to waylay them and seize their goods by force—how is that different from robbery?
entries.literal: The Department of State Affairs memorialized on regulations for pacification commissioners and Tuli begging to take local goods; the emperor said: 'Remote peoples should only be treated with compassion; if their tribute is not lacking, yet troops are further sent to intercept them and goods forcibly taken—how is this different from robbery?

entries.zh: 且或因而生事，何可不懲。」
entries.en: Moreover, such conduct could easily provoke disturbances—how can it go unpunished?'
entries.literal: Moreover it may thereby give rise to incidents—how can it go unpunished?'

entries.zh: 又曰：「朕所行制條，皆臣下所奏行者，天下事多，人力有限，豈能一一盡之。
entries.en: He added: 'The regulatory articles I promulgate are all measures officials have recommended; affairs across the realm are countless and human capacity finite—no ruler can anticipate every contingency.
entries.literal: He also said: 'The regulatory articles We promulgate are all matters officials memorialized should be enacted; affairs under Heaven are many, human capacity is limited—how can one exhaust them all?

entries.zh: 必因一事奏聞，方知有所窒礙，隨即更定。
entries.en: Only when a specific case is reported do we discover where the law proves obstructive, and we revise it at once.
entries.literal: Only when because of one matter a memorial is submitted does one know there is some obstruction, and immediately it is revised and fixed.

entries.zh: 今有聖旨、條理，復有制條，是使奸吏得以輕重也。」
entries.en: Yet now we have imperial edicts, administrative ordinances, and regulatory articles all at once—which only enables corrupt officials to manipulate penalties at will.'
entries.literal: Now there are imperial edicts, articles and ordinances, and again regulatory articles—this allows corrupt officials to manipulate light and heavy.'

entries.zh: 大興府民趙無事帶酒亂言，父千捕告，法當死。
entries.en: Zhao Wushi, a commoner of Daxing Prefecture, spoke treasonously while drunk; his father had him arrested and denounced him—a capital offense.
entries.literal: A Daxing Prefecture commoner Zhao Wushi, drunk, spoke wildly; his father had him arrested and reported—the offense warranted death.

entries.zh: 上曰：「為父不恤其子而告捕之，其正如此，人所甚難。
entries.en: The emperor said: 'For a father to set aside pity for his own son and turn him in—such rectitude is truly difficult for any person to achieve.
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'For a father not to pity his son yet arrest and report him—such righteousness is exceedingly hard for men.

entries.zh: 可特減死一等。」
entries.en: Reduce the death sentence by one grade as a special dispensation.'
entries.literal: His death penalty may be specially reduced by one grade.'

entries.zh: 武器署丞奕、直長骨赧坐受草畔子財，奕杖八十，骨赧笞二十，監察御史梁襄等坐失糾察罰俸一月。
entries.en: Weapons Office Deputy Director Yi and Section Chief Guhan were convicted of accepting bribes from Caobanzi; Yi was sentenced to eighty strokes of the staff and Guhan to twenty strokes of the bamboo, while Investigating Censor Liang Xiang and others, convicted of failing to investigate, were fined one month's salary.
entries.literal: Weapons Office deputy director Yi and section chief Guhan were convicted of accepting Caobanzi's bribes; Yi received eighty strokes of the staff, Guhan twenty strokes of the bamboo, investigating censor Liang Xiang and others were convicted of failing to investigate and were fined one month's salary.

entries.zh: 上曰：「監察，人君之耳目。
entries.en: The emperor said: 'Investigating censors are the monarch's eyes and ears.
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'Investigating censors are the ruler's eyes and ears.

entries.zh: 事由朕發，何以監察為？」
entries.en: If every case originates with me, what purpose do investigating censors serve?'
entries.literal: When matters originate from Us, what need is there for investigating censors?'

entries.zh: 上以法寺斷獄，以漢字譯女直字，會法又復各出情見，妄生穿鑿，徒致稽緩，遂詔罷情見。
entries.en: Because the legal office, when adjudicating cases, translated Jurchen records into Chinese and each judge then produced his own discretionary interpretation, inventing forced constructions that only delayed proceedings, the emperor decreed the abolition of discretionary views.
entries.literal: The emperor, because the legal office in adjudicating cases translated Jurchen script into Chinese characters, and when applying law each again issued separate discretionary views, wantonly forcing strained constructions, merely causing delay, then decreed abolition of discretionary views.

entries.zh: 二十五年二月，上以婦人在囚，輸作不便，而杖不分決，與殺無異，遂命免死輸作者，決杖二百而免輸作，以臀、背分決。
entries.en: In the second month of the twenty-fifth year, noting that imprisoned women could not conveniently perform penal labor and that undivided beating was tantamount to execution, the emperor ordered that those whose death sentences were commuted to penal labor should instead receive two hundred strokes divided between buttocks and back and be exempted from labor.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, second month, the emperor, because women in custody found penal labor inconvenient, and undivided beating was no different from killing, then ordered those commuted from death to penal labor to receive two hundred strokes and be exempted from penal labor, with buttocks and back divided for beating.

entries.zh: 時後族有犯罪者，尚書省引「八議」奏，上曰：「法者，公天下持平之器，若親者犯而從減，是使之恃此而橫恣也。
entries.en: When a member of the empress's clan committed an offense and the Department of State Affairs invoked the Eight Deliberations, the emperor said: 'Law is the instrument by which the realm is held in impartial balance; if kinsmen of the throne may offend yet receive leniency, they will rely upon that privilege to act with impunity.
entries.literal: At that time when a member of the empress's clan committed an offense, the Department of State Affairs cited the 'Eight Deliberations' in memorial; the emperor said: 'Law is the instrument that balances all under Heaven impartially; if relatives who offend receive reduction thereby, this makes them rely on it to act wantonly.

entries.zh: 昔漢文誅薄昭，有足取者。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen of Han put Bo Zhao to death, he showed the right way forward.
entries.literal: In former times Emperor Wen of Han executed Bo Zhao—there is something worth taking from that.

entries.zh: 前二十年時，後族濟州節度使烏林達鈔兀嘗犯大辟，朕未嘗宥。
entries.en: Twenty years ago, Wulin Da Chaowu of the empress's clan, then military governor of Jizhou, committed a capital offense, and I did not grant him clemency.
entries.literal: Twenty years ago, empress-clan Jizhou military governor Wulin Da Chaowu once committed the great penalty—We never pardoned him.

entries.zh: 今乃宥之，是開後世輕重出入之門也。」
entries.en: To pardon him now would open the door for future generations to manipulate the severity of punishment at will.'
entries.literal: Now to pardon him is to open the gate for future ages of manipulating light and heavy.'

entries.zh: 宰臣曰：「古所以議親，尊天子，別庶人也。」
entries.en: The chief ministers replied: 'The ancients instituted deliberation for kinship to honor the Son of Heaven and distinguish the imperial house from commoners.'
entries.literal: The chief ministers said: 'Anciently the reason for deliberating kin was to honor the Son of Heaven and distinguish the common people.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「外家自異於宗室，漢外戚權太重，至移國祚，朕所以不令諸王、公主有權也。
entries.en: The emperor replied: 'The maternal clan is naturally distinct from the imperial house; in Han times consort kin wielded such power that the throne itself was overturned—which is why I have refused to grant real authority to imperial princes and princesses.
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'The maternal clan is naturally distinct from the imperial house; Han consort kin held power too heavy, even to the shifting of the dynastic mandate—therefore We do not allow imperial princes and princesses to hold power.

entries.zh: 夫有功于國，議勳可也。
entries.en: Those who have rendered distinguished service to the state may claim deliberation for merit.
entries.literal: Now for merit toward the state, deliberating merit is acceptable.

entries.zh: 至若議賢，既曰賢矣，肯犯法乎？
entries.en: As for deliberation for worthiness—if a man is truly worthy, would he violate the law?
entries.literal: As for deliberating worthiness—as to worthiness, would one willing offend against law?

entries.zh: 脫或緣坐，則固當減請也。」
entries.en: If he is implicated only by association, then a petition for mitigation is entirely appropriate.'
entries.literal: If perchance by guilt through association, then one should properly petition for reduction.'

entries.zh: 二十六年，遂奏定太子妃大功以上親，及與皇家無服者、及賢而犯私罪者，皆不入議。
entries.en: In the twenty-sixth year, it was decreed that relatives of the crown prince's consort within the degree of great mourning, persons bearing no mourning obligation toward the imperial house, and those deemed worthy who commit private offenses—all were excluded from the Eight Deliberations.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, they then memorialized fixing that the crown prince's consort's kin within great mourning, and those without mourning obligation toward the imperial house, and the worthy who commit private offenses—all are not admitted to deliberation.

entries.zh: 上謂宰臣曰：「法有倫而不倫者，其改定之。」
entries.en: The emperor told his chief ministers: 'Where the law follows principle in some cases but violates it in others, revise it accordingly.'
entries.literal: The emperor told the chief ministers: 'Where law has principle yet lacks principle, revise and fix it.'

entries.zh: 監察御史陶鈞以攜妓游北苑，歌飲池島間，迫近殿廷，提控官石玠聞而發之。
entries.en: Investigating Censor Tao Jun was found to have escorted courtesans through the Northern Park, singing and drinking among its ponds and islets in proximity to the palace halls; Surveillance Officer Shi Jie heard of it and reported the affair.
entries.literal: Investigating censor Tao Jun, taking courtesans to roam the Northern Park, singing and drinking among ponds and islets, approaching near the palace precincts—surveillance officer Shi Jie heard and exposed it.

entries.zh: 鈞令其友閻恕 屬玠得緩。
entries.en: Tao Jun had his friend Yan Shu intercede with Shi Jie to secure lenient handling.
entries.literal: Jun had his friend Yan Shu ask Shi Jie to obtain leniency.

entries.zh: 既而事覺，法司奏，當徒二年半。
entries.en: When the affair came to light, the legal authorities recommended penal servitude of two and a half years.
entries.literal: When the matter came to light, the legal office memorialized that the penalty should be penal servitude two and a half years.

entries.zh: 詔以鈞耳目之官，攜妓入禁苑，無上下之分，杖六十，玠、恕皆坐之。
entries.en: An edict ruled that Tao Jun, as an imperial censor, had violated the distinction of rank by bringing courtesans into the forbidden park and sentenced him to sixty strokes of the staff; Shi Jie and Yan Shu were also convicted.
entries.literal: An edict held that Jun, as an organ of the ruler's senses, bringing courtesans into the forbidden park, showed no distinction of superior and subordinate—sixty strokes of the staff; Shi and Yan were both convicted as well.

entries.zh: 二十八年，上以制條拘於舊律，間有難解之詞，命刪修明白，使人皆曉之。
entries.en: In the twenty-eighth year, finding that regulatory articles were hobbled by archaic statutory language and contained passages difficult to understand, the emperor ordered them revised into clear language so that everyone could comprehend the law.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, the emperor, because regulatory articles were constrained by old statutes and occasionally had difficult-to-understand language, ordered deletion and revision to clarity so all people would understand.

entries.zh: 時濟南尹梁肅言，犯徒者當免杖。
entries.en: At that time Liang Su, administrator of Jinan, proposed that those sentenced to penal servitude should be exempted from beating.
entries.literal: At that time Jinan Administrator Liang Su stated that those who committed penal servitude should be exempted from the staff.

entries.zh: 朝廷以為今法已輕于古，恐滋奸惡，不從。
entries.en: The court held that current law was already more lenient than antiquity and feared encouraging wickedness, and did not adopt the proposal.
entries.literal: The court considered that present law was already lighter than antiquity, fearing it would breed wickedness and evil, and did not follow.

entries.zh: 嘗詔宰臣，朝廷每歲再遣審錄官，本以為民伸冤滯也，而所遣多不盡心，但文具而已。
entries.en: He once told his chief ministers: 'The court dispatches review officials twice each year precisely to redress the people's grievances, yet those dispatched mostly fail to apply themselves and merely go through the motions.'
entries.literal: He once issued an edict the chief ministers: 'The court each year twice dispatches review and record officials, originally to extend grievances and delays for the people, yet those dispatched mostly do not exhaust their hearts, but only go through the forms.'

entries.zh: 審錄之官，非止理問重刑，凡訴訟案牘，皆當閱實是非，囚徒不應囚繫則當釋放，官吏之罪即以狀聞，失糾察者嚴加懲斷，不以贖論。
entries.en: Review officials should not limit themselves to capital cases; they must examine the merits of all litigation, release prisoners who should not be held, report officials' offenses by memorial, and punish failures of oversight severely, without commutation.
entries.literal: Review and record officials should not only manage and inquire into heavy punishments; all litigation case documents should have their right and wrong examined in fact; prisoners who should not be imprisoned should be released; officials' offenses should be reported by memorial; those who fail in correction and inspection should be strictly punished and decided, not judged by ransom.

entries.zh: 又以監察御史體察東北路官吏，輒受訟牒，為不稱職，笞之五十。
entries.en: A surveillance censor investigating officials on the Northeast Circuit was beaten fifty strokes for improperly accepting litigation documents, deeming him unfit for office.
entries.literal: Also because a surveillance censor investigating Dongbei Road officials readily accepted litigation documents, as unfit for office, he was given fifty strokes of the staff.

entries.zh: 又謂宰臣曰：「比聞大理寺斷獄，雖無疑者亦經旬月，何耶？」
entries.en: He again told his chief ministers: 'I have lately heard that the Court of Judicial Review takes ten days or a month even for cases without doubt—why is this?'
entries.literal: He again told the chief ministers: 'Recently I have heard that the Court of Judicial Review decides cases—even those without doubt also take ten days or a month—why?'

entries.zh: 參知政事移剌道對曰：「在法，決死囚不過七日，徒刑五日，杖罪三日。」
entries.en: Vice Councilor Yila Dao replied: 'By law, capital cases must be decided within seven days, penal servitude within five, and beating offenses within three.'
entries.literal: Vice Councilor Yila Dao replied: 'By law, deciding death prisoners does not exceed seven days, penal servitude five days, staff offenses three days.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「法有程限，而輒違之，弛慢也。」
entries.en: The emperor said: 'The law sets time limits, yet they violate them at will—this is negligence.'
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'The law has time limits, yet they readily violate them—this is lax slowness.'

entries.zh: 罷朝，御批送尚書省曰：「凡法寺斷重輕罪各有期限，法官但犯皆的決，豈敢有違。
entries.en: After court, an imperial annotation was sent to the Secretariat: 'Every judicial office has time limits for deciding offenses of every severity; judges must render definitive judgments for every case—how dare they violate these limits?
entries.literal: After court was dismissed, an imperial annotation was sent to the Secretariat: 'All judicial offices deciding heavy and light offenses each have time limits; judges, for any offense, all have definite decisions—how would they dare violate?

entries.zh: 但以卿等所見不一，至於再三批送，其議定奏者書奏牘亦不下旬日，以致事多滯留，自今當勿復爾。」
entries.en: But because your views differ, cases are sent back repeatedly for reconsideration; even when deliberation is settled, drafting the memorial takes no less than ten days, causing many cases to linger—from now on this must cease.'
entries.literal: But because you all have differing views, reaching to repeated annotations and returns, those whose deliberation is settled and memorialized—even writing the memorial document is not less than ten days, causing many matters to linger and delay—from now on this should not happen again.'

entries.zh: 又曰：「故廣甯尹高楨為政尚猛，雖小過，有杖而殺之者。
entries.en: He also said: 'The former administrator of Guangning, Gao Zhen, governed with excessive severity, beating men to death even for minor faults.
entries.literal: He also said: 'Former Guangning Administrator Gao Zhen in governing still favored severity; even for small faults, there were those staff-beaten to death.

entries.zh: 即罪至於死而情或可恕，猶當念之，況其小過者乎？
entries.en: Even when an offense warrants death yet the circumstances may warrant mercy, one should still reflect carefully—how much more so for minor faults?
entries.literal: Even when the offense reaches death yet the circumstances may be pardonable, one should still reflect on it—how much more for small faults?

entries.zh: 人之性命安可輕哉！」
entries.en: How can human life be treated so lightly!'
entries.literal: How can human life be treated lightly!'

entries.zh: 上以正隆《續降制書》多任己意，傷於苛察。
entries.en: The emperor held that the Zhenglong Continued Promulgated Regulatory Documents too often followed personal whim and were excessively harsh.
entries.literal: The emperor considered that the Zhenglong Continued Promulgated Regulatory Documents mostly followed personal whim, harmful in harsh scrutiny.

entries.zh: 而與皇統之《制》並用，是非淆亂，莫知適從，奸吏因得上下其手。
entries.en: Used alongside the Huangtong Regulations, they created such confusion of standards that no one knew which code to follow, allowing corrupt officials to manipulate outcomes at will.
entries.literal: Yet they were used together with the Huangtong Regulations, right and wrong confused and mixed, none knowing what to follow; corrupt officials thereby could raise and lower their hands [manipulate outcomes].

entries.zh: 遂置局，命大理卿移剌綎總中外明法者共校正。
entries.en: Thereupon a bureau was established, and Chief of the Office of Imperial Justice Yila Su was charged with assembling legal experts from inside and outside the court to collate and revise the code.
entries.literal: Thereupon they established a bureau, appointing the chief of the Office of Imperial Justice Yila Su to gather those versed in law within and without the court jointly to collate and correct.

entries.zh: 乃以皇統、正隆之《制》及大定《軍前權宜條理》、後《續行條理》，倫其輕重，刪繁正失。
entries.en: They drew on the Huangtong and Zhenglong Regulations, the Dading Provisional Articles and Ordinances for Military Campaigns, and the later Continued Operational Articles and Ordinances, arranging punishments by severity while cutting redundancy and correcting errors.
entries.literal: Then taking the Huangtong and Zhenglong Regulations together with the Dading Provisional Articles and Ordinances for Military Campaigns and the later Continued Operational Articles and Ordinances, they arranged their light and heavy, cut redundancy and corrected errors.

entries.zh: 制有闕者以律文足之。
entries.en: Where the regulations were incomplete, they supplemented them with statutory provisions.
entries.literal: Where the regulations had gaps, they supplemented them with statutory text.

entries.zh: 制、律俱闕及疑而不能決者，則取旨畫定。
entries.en: Cases where both regulations and statutes were silent, or where doubt could not be resolved, were settled by obtaining the emperor's decision and issuing a definitive ruling.
entries.literal: Where both regulations and statutes lacked provision and doubt could not be resolved, they then obtained imperial intent and fixed it by decree.

entries.zh: 《軍前權宜條理》內有可以常行者亦為定法，余未應者亦別為一部存之。
entries.en: Provisions within the Provisional Articles and Ordinances for Military Campaigns that could be applied on a standing basis were incorporated into permanent law; those not yet applicable were preserved in a separate fascicle.
entries.literal: Within the Provisional Articles and Ordinances for Military Campaigns, those that could be regularly applied were also made fixed law; the remainder not yet applicable was also set apart as a separate fascicle and preserved.

entries.zh: 參以近所定徒杖減半之法，凡校定千一百九十條，分為十二卷，以《大定重修制條》為名，詔頒行焉。
entries.en: Incorporating the recently adopted rule halving penalties of penal servitude and beating, they finalized 1,190 articles in twelve fascicles under the title Recast Regulatory Articles of the Dading Era, and an edict ordered their promulgation throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Referencing also the recently fixed method of halving penal servitude and beating, in all they collated and fixed 1,190 articles, divided into twelve fascicles, named the Recast Regulatory Articles of the Dading Era, and an edict ordered their promulgation.

entries.zh: 金於食貨，其立法也周，其取民也審。
entries.en: In matters of food and goods, the Jin fashioned laws with care and drew revenue from the people with exacting precision.
entries.literal: For the Jin in food and goods, their lawmaking was comprehensive and their extraction from the people careful.

entries.zh: 太祖肇造，減遼租稅，規模遠矣。
entries.en: At the dynasty's founding, Taizu cut Liao-era rents and taxes, setting a far-sighted example from the start.
entries.literal: When Taizu first founded the dynasty, he reduced Liao rents and taxes—the vision was far-reaching indeed.

entries.zh: 熙宗、海陵之世，風氣日開，兼務遠略，君臣講求財用之制，切切然以是為先務。
entries.en: Under Xizong and Hailing the realm grew cosmopolitan; court and emperor together obsessed over fiscal institutions, making finance their foremost concern.
entries.literal: In the reigns of Xizong and Hailing, customs daily opened up; they pursued distant designs together, ruler and ministers alike discussing systems of fiscal use, urgently taking this as their foremost task.

entries.zh: 雖以世宗之賢，儲積之志曷嘗一日而忘之。
entries.en: Even the worthy Emperor Shizong never let a single day pass without thought for building up reserves.
entries.literal: Even given Shizong's worthiness, the will to accumulate reserves—when did he forget it even for a day?

entries.zh: 章宗彌文煟興，邊費亦廣，食貨之議不容不急。
entries.en: Zhangzong's reign saw cultural brilliance—and soaring frontier costs; debate over finance could hardly wait.
entries.literal: Under Zhangzong culture blazed and flourished, frontier expenses too grew wide; discussion of food and goods could not but be urgent.

entries.zh: 宣宗南遷，國土日蹙，汙池數罟，往往而然。
entries.en: After Xuanzong withdrew south, territory shrank daily; exhausted pools fished with net upon net became the norm.
entries.literal: When Xuanzong moved south, the realm daily contracted; stagnant pools with nets laid one upon another—this came to pass everywhere.

entries.zh: 考其立國以來，所謂食貨之法，犖犖大者曰租稅、銅錢、交鈔三者而已。
entries.en: Looking back from the dynasty's founding, the main pillars of economic policy were only three: land rent and tax, copper coinage, and paper notes.
entries.literal: Examining from the founding of the state, the so-called laws of food and goods, the outstanding great ones are only three: rent-tax, copper cash, and paper notes.

entries.zh: 三者之法數變而數窮。
entries.en: Each of these three policies changed again and again until every expedient was spent.
entries.literal: The laws of the three repeatedly changed until methods were exhausted.

entries.zh: 官田曰租，私田曰稅。
entries.en: Rent applied to state lands, tax to private holdings.
entries.literal: Official fields are called zu, private fields are called shui.

entries.zh: 租稅之外算其田園屋舍車馬牛羊樹藝之數，及其藏鏹多寡，征錢曰物力。
entries.en: Beyond rent and tax the state assessed gardens, dwellings, horses, livestock, orchards, and hidden hoards of silver, collecting a cash levy called the property assessment.
entries.literal: Beyond rent and tax they calculated gardens, houses, carriages, horses, cattle, sheep, planted trees, and the amount of hidden silver, levying money called wuli.

entries.zh: 物力之征，上自公卿大夫，下逮民庶，無苟免者。
entries.en: The property levy reached from highest ministers down to humble subjects—no one escaped on petty pretext.
entries.literal: In the collection of wuli, from dukes, ministers, and grandees down to the common populace, none received casual exemption.

entries.zh: 近臣出使外國，歸必增物力錢，以其受饋遺也。
entries.en: Court favorites returning from foreign missions invariably had their property assessments raised, on the ground that they had accepted gifts abroad.
entries.literal: Close ministers sent on missions abroad, on returning were always required to increase their wuli assessment, because they had received gifts.

entries.zh: 猛安謀克戶又有所謂牛頭稅者，宰臣有納此稅，庭陛間諮及其增減，則州縣徵求于小民蓋可知矣。
entries.en: Jurchen meng'an-mouke households also paid the so-called ox-head tax; when grand councilors themselves paid it and the emperor asked at court whether levies had risen or fallen, one may infer how county officials wrung the common people.
entries.literal: Meng'an mouke households further had what was called the ox-head tax; when chief ministers paid this tax, the throne inquired about its increase or decrease in the audience hall—then how the prefectures and counties squeezed the small folk may be known.

entries.zh: 故物力之外又有鋪馬、軍須、輸庸、司吏、河夫、桑皮故紙等錢，名目瑣細，不可殫述。
entries.en: Beyond the property tax came relay horses, military provisions, corvée, clerks' fees, river workers, mulberry bark, wastepaper charges, and countless other dues too numerous to list.
entries.literal: Thus beyond wuli there were further the horse relay, military supplies, corvée transport, clerk, river laborer, mulberry bark and scrap paper and other levies, categories minute and inexhaustible to recount.

entries.zh: 其為戶有數等，有課役戶、不課役戶、本戶、雜戶、正戶、監戶、官戶、奴婢戶、二稅戶。
entries.en: Households fell into many grades: liable for corvée, exempt, original, miscellaneous, regular, supervised, official, bond, and double-tax categories.
entries.literal: As to households there were several grades: duty-paying household, non-duty household, original household, miscellaneous household, regular household, supervised household, official household, slave household, double-tax household.

entries.zh: 有司始以三年一籍，後變為通檢，又為推排。
entries.en: Officials first took a household census every three years, then shifted to nationwide inspection, then to reassessment and re-ranking.
entries.literal: The authorities at first registered households once every three years, later changed to comprehensive inspection, then again to reorganization by assessment.

entries.zh: 凡戶隸州縣者，與隸猛安謀克，其輸納高下又各不同。
entries.en: Those registered under civil prefectures paid on different terms than those under meng'an-mouke units, and rates differed again between them.
entries.literal: All households subordinate to prefectures and counties, as against those subordinate to meng'an mouke—their payments high and low again each differed.

entries.zh: 法之初行，唯恐不密，言事者謂其厲民，即命罷之。
entries.en: When the policy first took force, officials dreaded any laxity; critics called it oppressive and the court at once ordered it stopped.
entries.literal: When the law first went into effect, they feared lest it not be strict; memorialists said it harried the people and they were immediately ordered to abolish it.

entries.zh: 罷之未久，會計者告用乏，又即舉行。
entries.en: Hardly had it been abolished when treasurers warned of shortages and it was hurriedly restored.
entries.literal: Not long after abolishing it, accountants reported supplies exhausted and it was immediately revived.

entries.zh: 其罷也志以便民，而民未見德。
entries.en: Abolition aimed to ease the burden, yet the people felt no relief.
entries.literal: In abolishing it the intent was to benefit the people, yet the people did not perceive grace.

entries.zh: 其行也志以足用，而用不加饒。
entries.en: Enforcement aimed to fill the treasury, yet revenue scarcely increased.
entries.literal: In enforcing it the intent was to fill needs, yet supplies did not grow more ample.

entries.zh: 一時君臣節用之言不絕告誡。
entries.en: For a time the throne and ministers never ceased preaching thrift.
entries.literal: For a time admonitions on frugality from ruler and ministers never ceased.

entries.zh: 嘗自計其國用，數亦浩瀚，若足支歷年者，郡縣稍遇歲侵，又遽不足，竟莫詰其故焉。
entries.en: They once tallied state expenditure—figures vast enough to seem adequate for years—yet a county touched by modest harvest failure would find funds suddenly wanting, and no one ever traced why.
entries.literal: They once calculated their state expenditures—the figures too were vast, as if enough to last years—yet when a prefecture or county met slight crop failure they were suddenly insufficient, and in the end no one examined the reason.

entries.zh: 世宗大定二年，詔免二稅戶為民。
entries.en: In Shizong's second year of Dading, double-tax households were freed as commoners.
entries.literal: In the second year of Dading under Shizong, an edict freed double-tax households as commoners.

entries.zh: 初，遼人佞佛尤甚，多以良民賜諸寺，分其稅一半輸官，一半輸寺，故謂之二稅戶。
entries.en: Under Liao, devotion to Buddhism led many free commoners to be granted to temples, paying tax half to the state and half to the monastery—hence the name double-tax households.
entries.literal: At first, Liao people were especially devoted to Buddhism; many free commoners were granted to monasteries, their tax half paid to government, half to the monastery—hence called double-tax households.

entries.zh: 遼亡，僧多匿其實，抑為賤，有援佐證以告者，有司各執以聞，上素知其事，故特免之。
entries.en: After Liao fell, monks often concealed the truth and kept them in servile status; petitioners with evidence were heard by each office; the emperor, long aware, specially freed them.
entries.literal: When Liao perished, monks mostly concealed the facts and kept them as lowly; those with supporting evidence who reported—each office held and reported; the emperor long knew this matter, so specially freed them.

entries.zh: 十七年五月，省奏：「咸平府路一千六百餘戶，自陳皆長白山星顯、禪春河女直人，遼時簽為獵戶，移居于此，號移典部，遂附契丹籍。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year the province reported: "More than 1,600 households on the Xianping route claimed to be Jurchen from Changbai Mountain and the Chanchun River, enrolled under Liao as hunter households, relocated here as the Yidian tribe, and registered as Khitan subjects.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year, the province reported: "More than 1,600 households on the Xianping route circuit state they are all Jurchen of Changbai Mountain Xingxian and Chanchun River; in Liao times enrolled as hunter households, moved here, called the Yidian tribe, and attached to Khitan registers.

entries.zh: 本朝義兵之興，首詣軍降，仍居本部，今乞厘正。」
entries.en: When our armies rose they were among the first to surrender and remained in their original units; they now ask to have their status corrected."
entries.literal: When our dynasty's righteous armies arose, they first came to the army to surrender and still dwelt in their original units; now they beg rectification."

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: The court approved their request.
entries.literal: An edict approved it.

entries.zh: 二十年，以上京路女直人戶，規避物力，自賣其奴婢，致耕田者少，遂以貧乏，詔定制禁之。
entries.en: In the twentieth year, Jurchen households on the Upper Capital route evaded property tax by selling bondsmen, leaving too few to farm and causing poverty; regulations were issued to forbid the practice.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, because Jurchen households on the Upper Capital route evaded property assessment by selling their slaves and bondservants, causing few to till fields and thus poverty, an edict fixed regulations forbidding it.

entries.zh: 又謂宰臣曰：「猛安謀克人戶，兄弟親屬若各隨所分土，與漢人錯居，每四五十戶結為保聚，農作時令相助濟，此亦勸相之道也。」
entries.en: He told the grand councilors: "If meng'an-mouke kin settle on allotted lands among Han neighbors in clusters of forty or fifty households, aiding one another at planting and harvest, that too is mutual encouragement."
entries.literal: He also told grand councilors: "Meng'an mouke households—if brothers and kin each follow their allotted land and live intermixed with Han Chinese, every forty or fifty households forming a security cluster, helping one another in farming seasons—this too is the way of encouraging mutual aid."

entries.zh: 二十一年六月，徙銀山側民於臨潢。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the twenty-first year, people from the Yinshan slopes were moved to Linhuang.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-first year, they moved people from the Yinshan slopes to Linhuang.

entries.zh: 又命避役之戶舉家逃於他所者，元貫及所寓司縣官同罪，為定制。
entries.en: Households fleeing corvée with whole families were ordered punished together with their original registration and host county officials—a fixed regulation.
entries.literal: They also ordered that households evading corvée who fled with whole families elsewhere—their original registration and the officials of the host prefecture or county shared guilt; this became fixed regulation.

entries.zh: 二十三年，定制，女直奴婢如有得力，本主許令婚娉者，須取問房親及村老給據，方許娉於良人。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year it was regulated that capable Jurchen bondwomen permitted to marry by their masters required kin and village-elder certificates before marrying free men.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year, regulations fixed: if Jurchen slave women were capable, and the master permitted marriage, they must inquire of kin and village elders for certificates before permitting marriage to free persons.

entries.zh: 是年八月，奏猛安謀克戶口、墾地、牛具之數。
entries.en: That August, meng'an-mouke household counts, reclaimed land, and ox teams were reported.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of that year, they reported meng'an mouke household counts, reclaimed land, and ox-team numbers.

entries.zh: 猛安二百二，謀克千八百七十八，戶六十一萬五千六百二十四，口六百一十五萬八千六百三十六，內正口四百八十一萬二千六百六十九，奴婢口一百三十四萬五千九百六十七。
entries.en: There were 202 meng'an, 1,878 mouke, 615,624 households, and 6,158,636 persons—including 4,812,669 free persons and 1,345,967 bond servants.
entries.literal: Meng'an 202, mouke 1,878, households 615,624, persons 6,158,636, of which regular persons 4,812,669, slave persons 1,345,967.

entries.zh: 墾田一百六十九萬三百八十頃有奇，牛具三十八萬四千七百七十一。
entries.en: Reclaimed land totaled more than 1,690,380 qing, with 384,771 ox teams.
entries.literal: Reclaimed fields 1,690,380-odd qing, ox teams 384,771.

entries.zh: 在都宗室將軍司，戶一百七十，口二萬八千七百九十，內正口九百八十二，奴婢口二萬七千八百八。
entries.en: The Capital Imperial Clan General Office had 170 households and 28,790 persons—982 free and 27,808 bond.
entries.literal: Capital Imperial Clan General Office: households 170, persons 28,790, of which regular 982, slave 27,808.

entries.zh: 墾田三千六百八十三頃七十五畝，牛具三百四。
entries.en: It held 3,683 qing 75 mu of reclaimed land and 304 ox teams.
entries.literal: Reclaimed fields 3,683 qing 75 mu, ox teams 304.

entries.zh: 迭剌、唐西二部五颭，戶五千五百八十五，口十三萬七千五百四十四，內正口十一萬九千四百六十三，奴婢口一萬八千八十一。
entries.en: The Diela and Tangxi divisions' five banners had 5,585 households and 137,544 persons—119,463 free and 18,081 bond.
entries.literal: Diela and Tangxi two divisions five banners: households 5,585, persons 137,544, of which regular 119,463, slave 18,081.

entries.zh: 墾田萬六千二十四頃一十七畝，牛具五千六十六。
entries.en: They held 16,024 qing 17 mu of reclaimed land and 5,066 ox teams.
entries.literal: Reclaimed fields 16,024 qing 17 mu, ox teams 5,066.

entries.zh: 二十五年，命宰臣禁有祿人一子、及農民避課役，為僧道者。
entries.en: In the twenty-fifth year, officials were ordered to forbid salaried officials' sons and farmers evading corvée from taking monastic orders.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, grand councilors were ordered to forbid salaried officials' sons and farmers evading corvée from becoming monks or Daoists.

entries.zh: 大定初，天下戶才三百余萬，至二十七年天下戶六百七十八萬九千四百四十九，口四千四百七十萬五千八十六。
entries.en: At the start of Dading the empire had barely three million households; by the twenty-seventh year it had 6,789,449 households and 44,705,086 persons.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Dading, empire-wide households were only a little over three million; by the twenty-seventh year empire-wide households were 6,789,449, persons 44,705,086.

entries.zh: 通檢，即《周禮》大司徒三年一大比，各登其鄉之眾寡、六畜、車輦，辨物行征之制也。
entries.en: Comprehensive inspection follows the Rites of Zhou: every three years the Grand Minister of Education took a great census, registering each district's population, livestock, and vehicles—the system for distinguishing goods and levying duties.
entries.literal: Comprehensive inspection is the Rites of Zhou Grand Minister of Education's great comparison every three years, each registering his district's numbers, six livestock, carriages and teams—the system of distinguishing goods and levying transit duties.

entries.zh: 金自國初占籍之後，至大定四年，承正隆師旅之餘，民之貧富變更，賦役不均，世宗下詔曰：「粵自國初，有司常行大比，於今四十年矣。
entries.en: From the dynasty's founding registers to the fourth year of Dading, after Zhenglong's wars wealth and poverty had shifted and levies grown uneven; Shizong decreed: "Since the founding, officials have held great censuses—forty years have passed.
entries.literal: From the Jin's initial occupation of registers after the founding, to the fourth year of Dading, inheriting the aftermath of Zhenglong armies, the people's rich and poor changed, levies and corvée uneven; Shizong issued an edict: "Since the founding, officials regularly conducted great comparisons—it has been forty years now.

entries.zh: 正隆時，兵役並興，調發無度，富者今貧不能自存，版籍所無者今為富室而猶倖免。
entries.en: Under Zhenglong, armies mobilized without limit—the once rich now could not survive, while the unregistered grew wealthy yet still escaped duty.
entries.literal: In Zhenglong times military service arose together, mobilization without measure; the rich are now poor and cannot support themselves, those absent from registers are now wealthy houses yet still escape by luck.

entries.zh: 是用遣信臣泰甯軍節度使張弘信等十三人，分路通檢天下物力而差定之，以革前弊，俾元元無不均之歎，以稱朕意。
entries.en: Thirteen trusted envoys led by Taining Army Commissioner Zhang Hongxin were sent on separate routes to inspect property empire-wide and fix gradations, reform abuses, and spare the people uneven burdens—as the emperor intended.
entries.literal: Therefore trusted ministers were sent—Taining Army Commissioner Zhang Hongxin and thirteen others—to conduct comprehensive inspection of empire-wide property by route and fix gradations, to reform prior abuses, so the masses have no uneven lament, matching Our intent.

entries.zh: 凡規措條理，命尚書省畫一以行。」
entries.en: All arrangements were ordered unified and implemented through the Ministry of Revenue."
entries.literal: All planning arrangements and regulations—the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to unify and implement."

entries.zh: 又命：「凡監戶事產，除官所撥賜之外，餘凡置到百姓有稅田宅。
entries.en: It was also ordered: "All supervised households' property, beyond official grants, and any taxable land or houses commoners acquired,
entries.literal: They also ordered: "All supervised households' estates—apart from what officials granted—whatever commoners acquired with taxable fields and houses,

entries.zh: 皆在通檢之數。」
entries.en: all fell within the comprehensive inspection."
entries.literal: all fall within comprehensive inspection's count."

entries.zh: 時諸使往往以苛酷多得物力為功，弘信檢山東州縣尤為酷暴，棣州防禦使完顏永元面責之曰：「朝廷以正隆後差調不均，故命使者均之。
entries.en: Envoys often treated harshness and inflated assessments as merit; Hongxin's inspection of Shandong was especially brutal; Di Prefecture Defense Commissioner Wanyan Yongyuan rebuked him: "The court sent you to equalize burdens after Zhenglong's uneven levies.
entries.literal: At the time envoys often took harsh severity and gaining much property assessment as merit; Hongxin inspecting Shandong prefectures and counties was especially cruel and violent; Di Prefecture Defense Commissioner Wanyan Yongyuan rebuked him to his face: "The court, because after Zhenglong corvée assignments were uneven, ordered envoys to equalize them.

entries.zh: 今乃殘暴，妄加民產業數倍，一有來申訴者，則血肉淋離，甚者即殞杖下，此何理也？」
entries.en: Instead you brutalize the people, multiplying assessments severalfold; appellants are beaten until flesh tears and some die under the rod—what justice is this?"
entries.literal: Now you are brutal and violent, recklessly multiplying people's estates several fold; whenever someone came to appeal, flesh and blood were torn streaming; the severe even died under the staff—what principle is this?"

entries.zh: 弘信不能對，故惟棣州稍平。
entries.en: Hongxin had no answer; only Di Prefecture remained relatively calm.
entries.literal: Hongxin could not reply; therefore only Di Prefecture was somewhat calm.

entries.zh: 五年，有司奏諸路通檢不均，詔再以戶口多寡、貧富輕重，適中定之。
entries.en: In the fifth year, uneven inspection across routes was reported; the court re-fixed gradations by household size and wealth.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, offices reported routes' comprehensive inspection uneven; an edict again fixed by household numbers, rich and poor, light and heavy—moderately determined.

entries.zh: 既而，又定通檢地土等第稅法。
entries.en: Land grades and tax rates for comprehensive inspection were then fixed.
entries.literal: Then they also fixed comprehensive inspection land grades and tax law.

entries.zh: 十五年九月，上以天下物力，自通檢以來十餘年，貧富變易，賦調輕重不均，遣濟南尹梁肅等二十六人，分路推排。
entries.en: In the ninth month of the fifteenth year, noting that wealth had shifted in the decade since comprehensive inspection and levies grown uneven, the emperor sent Jinan Prefect Liang Su and twenty-six others on separate routes to reassess and re-rank property.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the fifteenth year, the emperor said empire-wide property, since comprehensive inspection more than ten years, rich and poor changed, tax levies light and heavy uneven—sent Jinan Prefect Liang Su and twenty-six others to conduct reorganization by route.

entries.zh: 二十年四月，上謂宰臣曰：「猛安謀克戶，富貧差發不均，皆自謀克內科之，暗者惟胥吏之言是從，輕重不一。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the twentieth year the emperor told councilors: "Meng'an-mouke corvée falls unevenly because each mouke levies internally and the ignorant follow clerks' word—burdens vary wildly.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the twentieth year, the emperor told grand councilors: "Meng'an mouke households—rich and poor corvée assignments uneven—all levied within the mouke; the ignorant follow only clerks' words, light and heavy not uniform.

entries.zh: 自窩斡叛後，貧富反復，今當籍其夾戶，推其家貲，儻有軍役庶可均也。」
entries.en: Since Wowohan's rebellion fortunes have reversed; we should register dependent households and assess family wealth so military duties may be fairly shared."
entries.literal: Since Wowohan's rebellion, rich and poor reversed; now we should register their dependent households, assess family wealth—if there is military service perhaps it can be even."

entries.zh: 詔集百官議，右丞相克甯、平章政事安禮，樞密副使宗尹言：「女直人除猛安謀克僕從差使，余無差役。
entries.en: Officials were summoned to debate; Right Grand Councilor Kening, Grand Councilor Anli, and Privy Council Vice Commissioner Zongyin said: "Apart from meng'an-mouke attendant duties, Jurchen bear no other corvée.
entries.literal: An edict gathered the hundred officials to discuss; Right Grand Councilor Kening, Grand Councilor Anli, Privy Council Vice Commissioner Zongyin said: "Jurchen apart from meng'an mouke attendant assignments have no other corvée.

entries.zh: 今不推奴婢孳畜、地土數目，止驗產業科差為便。」
entries.en: Assessing only property for corvée, not counting bond servants, livestock, or land, would be simpler."
entries.literal: Now not assessing slaves, livestock, land numbers—only verifying property for corvée assignment is convenient."

entries.zh: 左丞相守道等言：「止驗財產，多寡分為四等，置籍以科差，庶得均也。」
entries.en: Left Grand Councilor Shoudao and others said: "Verify property alone, divide into four grades, register for corvée—that may achieve fairness."
entries.literal: Left Grand Councilor Shoudao and others said: "Only verify property, divide abundance into four grades, set registers for corvée—perhaps it can be even."

entries.zh: 左丞通、右丞道、都點檢襄言：「括其奴婢之數，則貧富自見，緩急有事科差，與一例科差者不同。
entries.en: Left Vice Councilor Tong, Right Vice Councilor Dao, and Chief Inspector Xiang said: "Count bond servants and wealth becomes visible; urgent and routine corvée differ from lump assessment.
entries.literal: Left Vice Councilor Tong, Right Vice Councilor Dao, Chief Inspector Xiang said: "Counting their slaves—then rich and poor show themselves; urgent and routine corvée differ from uniform lump assessment.

entries.zh: 請俟農隙，拘括地土牛具之數，各以所見上聞。」
entries.en: They asked to wait for the farming slack season, investigate land and ox teams, and report findings."
entries.literal: Request waiting for farming slack, investigating land and ox-team numbers, each reporting what they see."

entries.zh: 上曰：「一謀克戶之貧富，謀克豈不知。
entries.en: The emperor said: "Does not each mouke know its households' wealth?
entries.literal: The emperor said: "One mouke household's rich and poor—the mouke surely knows.

entries.zh: 一猛安所領八謀克，一例科差。
entries.en: Yet one meng'an levies eight mouke uniformly.
entries.literal: One meng'an commands eight mouke—uniform lump corvée.

entries.zh: 設如一謀無內，有奴婢二三百口者，有奴婢一二人者，科差與同，豈得平均。
entries.en: If one household has two or three hundred bond servants and another one or two, yet corvée is the same—how is that fair?
entries.literal: Suppose in one mouke within, some have two or three hundred slaves, some one or two slaves—corvée the same; how can it be even?

entries.zh: 正隆興兵時，朕之奴婢萬數，孳畜數千，而不差一人一馬，豈可謂平。
entries.en: When Zhenglong raised armies I had tens of thousands of bond servants and thousands of livestock yet levied not one man or horse—can that be called fair?
entries.literal: When Zhenglong raised armies, Our slaves numbered in the tens of thousands, livestock in the thousands, yet not one person or horse was levied—can this be called even?

entries.zh: 朕於庶事未嘗專行，與卿謀之。
entries.en: I never decide ordinary affairs alone but deliberate with you.
entries.literal: We in ordinary affairs have never acted alone, but deliberated with you.

entries.zh: 往年散置契丹戶，安禮極言恐擾動，朕決行之，果得安業。
entries.en: When I dispersed Khitan households, Anli warned of unrest; I carried it through and they settled peacefully.
entries.literal: In former years dispersing Khitan households, Anli strongly said he feared disturbance; We resolutely carried it out and indeed secured settled livelihoods.

entries.zh: 安禮雖盡忠，未審長策。
entries.en: Anli is loyal but lacks long-term vision.
entries.literal: Anli though utterly loyal did not discern long-term policy.

entries.zh: 其從左丞通等所見，拘括推排之。」
entries.en: Follow Left Vice Councilor Tong's view—investigate and reassess."
entries.literal: Follow Left Vice Councilor Tong and others' view—investigate and conduct reorganization by assessment."

entries.zh: 十二月，上謂宰臣曰：「猛安謀克多新強舊弱，差役不均，其令推排，當自中都路始。」
entries.en: In the twelfth month the emperor said: "Meng'an-mouke units mix new wealth with old poverty and corvée is uneven—begin reassessment on the Central Capital route."
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, the emperor told grand councilors: "Meng'an mouke mostly new strong and old weak, corvée uneven—order reorganization by assessment, starting from the Central Capital route."

entries.zh: 至二十二年八月，始詔令集耆老，推貧富，驗土地牛具奴婢之數，分為上中下三等。
entries.en: By the eighth month of the twenty-second year elders were gathered to assess wealth, verify land, ox teams, and bond servants, and divide households into upper, middle, and lower grades.
entries.literal: By the eighth month of the twenty-second year, they first decreed gathering elders, assessing rich and poor, verifying land, ox teams, and slave numbers, dividing into upper, middle, and lower three grades.

entries.zh: 以同知大興府事完顏烏裏也先推中都路，續遣戶部主事按帶等十四人與外官同分路推排。
entries.en: Associate Administrator of Daxing Prefecture Wanyan Wuliye led the Central Capital route; Revenue Bureau Administrator Andai and fourteen others joined outer officials on separate routes.
entries.literal: With Associate Administrator of Daxing Prefecture Wanyan Wuliye first assessing the Central Capital route, then sending Revenue Bureau Administrator Andai and fourteen others with outer officials to conduct reorganization by route.

entries.zh: 九月，詔：「毋令富者匿隱畜產，貧戶或有不敢養馬者。
entries.en: In the ninth month the court decreed: "The rich must not conceal livestock, nor should the poor fear keeping horses.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, an edict: "Do not let the rich conceal livestock; poor households perhaps dare not keep horses.

entries.zh: 昔海陵時，拘括馬畜，絕無等級，富者倖免，貧者盡拘入官，大為不均。
entries.en: Under Hailing, horse requisition ignored rank—the rich escaped and the poor lost all stock to the state, a gross injustice.
entries.literal: Formerly in Hailing's time, requisitioning horses and livestock had no grades; the rich luckily escaped, the poor all seized into government—greatly uneven.

entries.zh: 今並核實貧富造籍，有急即按籍取之，庶幾無不均之弊。」
entries.en: Now verify wealth, register livestock, and requisition by register in emergencies—thus avoiding uneven abuse."
entries.literal: Now verify rich and poor and make registers; when urgent take from registers—perhaps no uneven abuse."

entries.zh: 張汝弼、梁肅奏：「天下民戶通檢既定，設有產物移易，自應隨業輸納。
entries.en: Zhang Rubi and Liang Su reported: "Once comprehensive inspection is set, property transfers should pay tax according to the new holder's status.
entries.literal: Zhang Rubi and Liang Su reported: "Empire-wide household comprehensive inspection being fixed, if property changes hands, naturally should pay according to occupation.

entries.zh: 至於浮財，須有增耗，貧者自貧，富者自富，似不必屢推排也。」
entries.en: Floating wealth rises and falls—the poor stay poor, the rich remain rich—so repeated reassessment seems unnecessary."
entries.literal: As for floating wealth, there must be increase and decrease; the poor remain poor, the rich remain rich—seemingly no need for repeated reorganization."

entries.zh: 上曰：「宰執家多有新富者，故皆不願也。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "Councilors' families have grown newly rich—that is why you resist."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Grand councilors' families mostly have newly rich—therefore all are unwilling."

entries.zh: 肅對曰：「如臣者，能推排中都物力。
entries.en: Su replied: "As for me, I can reassess Central Capital property.
entries.literal: Su replied: "As for one like your servant, I can conduct reorganization of Central Capital property.

entries.zh: 臣以嘗為南使，先自添物力錢至六十餘貫，視其他奉使無如臣多者。
entries.en: I once served as envoy to the Song south and had my property assessment raised by more than sixty strings—more than any other envoy on record.
entries.literal: Your servant, having once served as envoy to the south, first added property assessment money to more than sixty strings—viewing other envoys, none had as much as your servant.

entries.zh: 但小民無知，法出奸生，數動搖則易駭。
entries.en: Yet common people are ignorant; new laws breed evasion, and frequent upheaval easily panics them.
entries.literal: But small folk are ignorant; when laws issue, treachery arises; frequent disturbance then easily terrifies.

entries.zh: 如唐、宋及遼時，或三二十年不測通比則有之。
entries.en: Under Tang, Song, and Liao, comprehensive censuses sometimes came only every twenty or thirty years.
entries.literal: As in Tang, Song, and Liao times, sometimes twenty or thirty years might pass without a comprehensive comparison—such cases existed.

entries.zh: 頻歲推排，似為難爾。」
entries.en: Annual reassessment seems hard to sustain."
entries.literal: Reorganization by assessment year after year seems difficult."

entries.zh: 二十六年，複以李晏等分路推排。
entries.en: In the twenty-sixth year Li Yan and others were again sent on separate routes to reassess property.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, again with Li Yan and others they conducted reorganization by route.

entries.zh: 二十七年，奏晏等所定物力之數。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year they reported the property assessments Yan's team had fixed.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, they reported the property assessment numbers Yan and others had fixed.

entries.zh: 上曰：「朕以元推天下物力錢三百五萬餘貫，除三百萬貫外，令減五萬餘貫。
entries.en: The emperor said: "The original empire-wide property assessment was over 3.5 million strings; I ordered all but three million reduced by more than fifty thousand.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "We originally assessed empire-wide property money at more than 3.5 million strings; apart from three million strings, We ordered a reduction of more than fifty thousand strings.

entries.zh: 今減不及數，複續收二萬餘貫，即是實二萬貫爾，而曰續收，何也？」
entries.en: The reduction fell short, yet you report another twenty thousand collected as 'continued collection'—that is simply twenty thousand new—why call it otherwise?"
entries.literal: Now the reduction did not reach the amount, yet again continued collection of more than twenty thousand strings—this is really twenty thousand strings, yet you call it continued collection—why?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「此謂舊脫漏而今首出者，及民地舊無力耕種，而今耕種者也。」
entries.en: They replied: "These are cases formerly omitted now first reported, and land the people could not farm before but cultivate now."
entries.literal: They replied: "This means those formerly omitted and now first appearing, and commoners' land formerly without strength to cultivate but now cultivated."

entries.zh: 上曰：「通檢舊數，止于視其營運息耗，與房地多寡，而加減之。
entries.en: The emperor said: "The old comprehensive inspection adjusted only business gains and losses and the amount of houses and land.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Comprehensive inspection's old numbers only looked at their business profit and loss, and houses and land more or less, and increased or decreased accordingly.

entries.zh: 彼人賣地，此人買之，皆舊數也。
entries.en: When one sells land and another buys, the total should remain the old figure.
entries.literal: That person sells land, this person buys it—all old numbers.

entries.zh: 至如營運。
entries.en: As for business operations,
entries.literal: As for business operations.

entries.zh: 此強則彼弱，強者增之，弱者減之而已。
entries.en: where one grows strong another weakens—raise the strong, lower the weak, and no more.
entries.literal: Where this is strong that is weak—the strong are increased, the weak decreased, that is all.

entries.zh: 且物力之數蓋是定差役之法，其大數不在多寡也。
entries.en: Property assessment exists to fix corvée obligations—the grand total should not turn on sheer quantity.
entries.literal: Moreover property assessment numbers are essentially the method for fixing corvée; the grand total lies not in more or less.

entries.zh: 朕恐實有營運富家所當出者，反分與貧者爾。」
entries.en: I fear what wealthy traders ought to pay is being shifted onto the poor instead."
entries.literal: We fear that what wealthy households with real business operations ought to pay is instead divided among the poor."

entries.zh: 國之有食貨，猶人之有飲食也。
entries.en: For a state, grain and goods are what food and drink are for a person.
entries.literal: A state has food and goods as a person has drink and food.

entries.zh: 人非飲食不生，國非食貨不立。
entries.en: A person cannot survive without nourishment, nor can a state endure without its economic foundation.
entries.literal: Without drink and food a person cannot live; without food and goods a state cannot stand.

entries.zh: 然燧人、庖犧能為飲食之道以教人，而不能使人無飲食之疾。
entries.en: Even Suiren and Fuxi could teach mankind how to prepare food and drink, yet they could not spare people every ill that diet brings.
entries.literal: Yet Suiren and Paoxi were able to teach people the ways of drink and food, yet could not make people free of ailments from drink and food.

entries.zh: 三王能為食貨之政以遺後世，而不能使後世無食貨之弊。
entries.en: The Three Kings could hand down sound policies on public finance, yet they could not keep later ages from the abuses those policies invite.
entries.literal: The Three Kings were able to bequeath to later ages policies on food and goods, yet could not make later ages free of abuses in food and goods.

entries.zh: 唯善養生者如不欲食啖，而飲食自不闕焉，故能適饑飽之宜，可以疾少而長壽。
entries.en: Only those who truly know how to care for the body eat as though indifferent to appetite, yet never go short of nourishment; they regulate hunger and fullness so well that they suffer few illnesses and live long.
entries.literal: Only one skilled in nurturing life is like one who does not desire to eat and chew, yet drink and food of themselves are not lacking, so he can suit the appropriate measure of hunger and satiety and thereby have few ailments and long life.

entries.zh: 善裕國者初不事貨殖，而食貨自不乏焉，故能制豐約之節，可以弊少而長治。
entries.en: A ruler who truly enriches his realm does not obsess over commercial profit, yet grain and goods remain abundant; he can modulate plenty and restraint so that abuses are few and governance endures.
entries.literal: One skilled in enriching a state at first does not engage in profit-seeking, yet food and goods of themselves are not scarce, so he can regulate abundance and restraint and thereby have few abuses and long good order.

entries.zh: 與敵國互市之所也。
entries.en: These were the designated sites for border trade with hostile states.
entries.literal: They are the places for mutual trade with enemy states.

entries.zh: 皆設場官，嚴厲禁，廣屋宇以通二國之貨，歲之所獲亦大有助於經用焉。
entries.en: Each market had its own superintendent, strict regulations, and ample warehouses to move goods between the two realms, and annual receipts substantially eased the state's budget.
entries.literal: At each one market officials were set up, prohibitions strictly enforced, and buildings expanded to circulate the goods of the two states; what was gained each year also greatly assisted state expenditures.

entries.zh: 熙宗皇統二年五月，許宋人之請，遂各置於兩界。
entries.en: In the fifth month of Xizong's Huangtong 2 (1142), the court granted the Song petition and set up markets on both sides of the frontier.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of Huangtong 2 under Emperor Xizong, the Song people's request was granted, and each side then established them on both borders.

entries.zh: 九月，命壽州、鄧州、鳳翔府等處皆置。
entries.en: In the ninth month the court ordered markets established at Shouzhou, Dengzhou, Fengxiang Prefecture, and other points.
entries.literal: In the ninth month orders were issued to establish them at Shouzhou, Dengzhou, Fengxiang Prefecture, and other places.

entries.zh: 海陵正隆四年正月，罷鳳翔府、唐、鄧、潁、蔡、鞏、洮等州並膠西縣所置者，而專置於泗州。
entries.en: In the first month of Hailing's Zhenglong 4 (1159), the court closed the markets at Fengxiang Prefecture and at Tang, Deng, Ying, Cai, Gong, Tao, and other prefectures, as well as Jiaoxi County, concentrating border trade at Sizhou alone.
entries.literal: In the first month of Zhenglong 4 under Prince Hailing, those established at Fengxiang Prefecture and the prefectures of Tang, Deng, Ying, Cai, Gong, and Tao, as well as Jiaoxi County, were abolished, and markets were set up only at Sizhou.

entries.zh: 尋伐宋，亦罷之。
entries.en: When war against the Song broke out soon after, those markets were closed as well.
entries.literal: Soon afterward, when campaigning against the Song, these too were abolished.

entries.zh: 五年八月，命榷場起赴南京。
entries.en: In the eighth month of year 5 the court ordered the border markets relocated to the Southern Capital.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of year 5 orders were issued for the monopoly markets to be moved to the Southern Capital.

entries.zh: 國初于西北招討司之燕子城、北羊城之間嘗置之，以易北方牧畜。
entries.en: Early in the dynasty a market had stood between Swallow City and North Sheep City under the Northwestern Pacification Commission, where Jin goods were traded for livestock from the northern steppe.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the dynasty they had once been placed between Swallow City and North Sheep City under the Northwestern Pacification Commission, to exchange for northern pastoral livestock.

entries.zh: 世宗大定三年，市馬于夏國之榷場。
entries.en: In Shizong's Dading 3 (1163) the court bought horses at the Western Xia border market.
entries.literal: In the third year of Dading under Emperor Shizong, horses were purchased at the Western Xia monopoly market.

entries.zh: 四年，以尚書省奏，複置泗、壽、蔡、唐、鄧、潁、密、鳳翔、秦、鞏、洮諸場。
entries.en: In the fourth year, acting on a memorial from the Department of State Affairs, the court reopened markets at Si, Shou, Cai, Tang, Deng, Ying, Mi, Fengxiang, Qin, Gong, and Tao.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, on a memorial from the Department of State Affairs, the markets at Si, Shou, Cai, Tang, Deng, Ying, Mi, Fengxiang, Qin, Gong, and Tao were all re-established.

entries.zh: 七年，禁秦州場不得賣米麵、及羊豕之臘、並可作軍器之物入外界。
entries.en: In the seventh year the Qinzhou market was barred from exporting rice, flour, cured meats, or any material that could be turned into weapons.
entries.literal: In the seventh year it was forbidden for the Qinzhou market to sell rice and flour, cured pork and mutton, or any goods that could be made into weapons to the outer realm.

entries.zh: 十七年二月，上謂宰臣曰：「宋人喜生事背盟，或與大石交通，恐枉害生靈，不可不備。
entries.en: In the second month of year seventeen the emperor told his ministers, "The Song delight in provocation and treaty-breaking and may even deal with the Kara-Khitai. Innocent lives could be lost if we are caught unprepared.
entries.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year the emperor told his ministers: "The Song are fond of stirring trouble and breaking treaties; they may also communicate with the Kara-Khitai. I fear innocent lives will be harmed in vain—we cannot fail to prepare.

entries.zh: 其陝西沿邊榷場可止留一處，餘悉罷之。
entries.en: Along the Shaanxi frontier only one border market should remain; all others are to be closed.
entries.literal: Of the monopoly markets along the Shaanxi border, only one may be retained; the rest are all to be abolished.

entries.zh: 令所司嚴察奸細。」
entries.en: Responsible offices were ordered to tighten scrutiny of spies and infiltrators."
entries.literal: Let the responsible offices strictly investigate spies."

entries.zh: 前此，以防奸細，罷西界蘭州、保安、綏德三榷場。
entries.en: Earlier, to block spies, the court had already closed the three western markets at Lanzhou, Bao'an, and Suide.
entries.literal: Earlier, to guard against spies, the three monopoly markets at Lanzhou, Bao'an, and Suide on the western frontier had been abolished.

entries.zh: 二十一年正月，夏國王李仁孝上表乞複置，以保安、蘭州無所產，而且稅少，惟於綏德為要地，可複設互市，命省臣議之。
entries.en: In the first month of year twenty-one Western Xia's King Li Renxiao petitioned for restoration, noting that Bao'an and Lanzhou yielded little produce and scant revenue, whereas Suide was a strategic site where border trade should resume; the court referred the matter to provincial ministers.
entries.literal: In the first month of the twenty-first year Western Xia King Li Renxiao submitted a memorial begging restoration, saying Bao'an and Lanzhou produced nothing and their tax receipts were slight, but Suide was a vital place where mutual trade could be re-established; provincial ministers were ordered to deliberate.

entries.zh: 宰臣以陝西鄰西夏，邊民私越境盜竊，緣有榷場，故奸人得往來，擬東勝可依舊設，陝西者並罷之。
entries.en: The chief ministers argued that with Western Xia on Shaanxi's border, frontier residents crossed illegally to steal, and open markets let agents move freely; they proposed keeping Dongsheng as before while closing every Shaanxi market.
entries.literal: The chief ministers held that Shaanxi bordered Western Xia, border people privately crossed to steal, and because monopoly markets existed traitors could come and go; they proposed that Dongsheng could be kept as before while all Shaanxi markets be abolished.

entries.zh: 上曰：「東勝與陝西道路隔絕，貿易不通，其令環州置一場。」
entries.en: The emperor replied, "Dongsheng and Shaanxi are too far apart for trade to flow; establish a market at Huanzhou instead."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Dongsheng and Shaanxi are cut off by roads and trade cannot pass; let a market be established at Huanzhou."

entries.zh: 尋於綏德州複置一場。
entries.en: A market at Suide Prefecture was reopened soon afterward.
entries.literal: Soon afterward one market was re-established at Suide Prefecture.

entries.zh: 金銀之稅。
entries.en: Tax on Gold and Silver
entries.literal: Tax on gold and silver.

entries.zh: 世宗大定五年，聽人射買寶山縣銀冶。
entries.en: In Shizong's Dading 5 (1165) the court allowed competitive bidding for the Baoshan County silver works.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Dading under Emperor Shizong, people were permitted to bid competitively for the Baoshan County silver smeltery.

entries.zh: 九年，御史台奏河南府以和買金銀，抑配百姓，且下其直。
entries.en: In the ninth year the Censorate reported that Henan Prefecture had used state gold-and-silver purchases to coerce the populace and cut payment below fair value.
entries.literal: In the ninth year the Censorate memorialized that Henan Prefecture used harmonized purchase of gold and silver, forcibly apportioned it among the people, and also lowered the price.

entries.zh: 上曰：「初，朕欲泉貨流通，故令行，豈可反害民乎？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "I ordered this to keep currency circulating. How can it end up harming the people instead?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "At first I wished currency to circulate, and therefore ordered this carried out—how can it instead harm the people?"

entries.zh: 遂罷之。
entries.en: The practice was abolished.
entries.literal: It was therefore abolished.

entries.zh: 十二年，詔金銀坑冶，恣民采，毋收稅。
entries.en: In the twelfth year an edict allowed free private mining of gold and silver without tax.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year an edict declared that gold and silver mines and smelters might be freely mined by the people without collecting tax.

entries.zh: 二十七年，尚書省奏：「聽民于農隙采銀，承納官課。」
entries.en: In year twenty-seven the Department of State Affairs memorialized, "Let the people mine silver in agricultural slack seasons and pay the official dues."
entries.literal: In year twenty-seven the Department of State Affairs memorialized, "Let the people mine silver in agricultural slack seasons and pay the official dues."

entries.zh: 明昌二年，天下見在金千二百餘鋌，銀五十五萬二千餘鋌。
entries.en: By Mingchang 2 (1191) circulating gold exceeded 1,200 ingots and silver more than 552,000 ingots empire-wide.
entries.literal: In Mingchang 2, gold in circulation throughout the realm exceeded 1,200 ingots and silver 552,000-odd ingots.

entries.zh: 三年，以提刑司言，封諸處銀冶，禁民采煉。
entries.en: In the third year, on the surveillance commission's advice, silver works were sealed nationwide and private mining forbidden.
entries.literal: In the third year, on a report from the surveillance commission, silver smelteries everywhere were sealed and private mining and smelting forbidden.

entries.zh: 五年，以御史台奏，請令民采煉隨處金銀銅冶，上命尚書省議之。
entries.en: In the fifth year the Censorate asked to reopen local gold, silver, and copper works to private operators; the emperor referred the matter to the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, on a Censorate memorial requesting that the people be allowed to mine and smelt gold, silver, and copper works wherever located, the emperor ordered the Department of State Affairs to deliberate.

entries.zh: 宰臣議謂：「國家承平日久，戶口增息，雖嘗禁之，而貧人苟求生計，聚眾私煉。
entries.en: The chief ministers argued, "The state has enjoyed long peace and the population has grown; although mining has been forbidden, poor people seeking a livelihood gather in groups to smelt in secret.
entries.literal: The chief ministers argued, "The state has enjoyed long peace and the population has grown; although mining has been forbidden, poor people seeking a livelihood gather in groups to smelt in secret.

entries.zh: 上有禁之之名。
entries.en: Prohibition existed in name only.
entries.literal: Above there is the name of prohibition.

entries.zh: 而無杜絕之實，故官無利而民多犯法。
entries.en: Yet smuggling continued unchecked, so the state gained nothing while commoners broke the law in droves.
entries.literal: Yet there is no reality of cutting it off; therefore the government gains no profit while the people frequently break the law.

entries.zh: 如令民射買，則貧民壯者為夫匠，老稚供雜役，各得均齊，而射買之家亦有餘利。
entries.en: Competitive bidding would let poor households deploy strong men as master smiths and elders and children as helpers, share work fairly, and still leave contractors a margin.
entries.literal: If the people are allowed competitive bidding, then among the poor the strong become master craftsmen, the old and young supply miscellaneous labor, each receives fair shares, and the bidding households also have surplus profit.

entries.zh: 如此，則可以久行。
entries.en: Such a system could be sustained long term.
entries.literal: Thus it can be carried on for long.

entries.zh: 比之官役顧工，糜費百端者，有間矣。」
entries.en: Compared with state-run operations that hire labor and waste resources in countless ways, there is a clear difference."
entries.literal: Compared with state-run operations that hire labor and waste resources in countless ways, there is a clear difference."

entries.zh: 遂定制，有冶之地，委謀克縣令籍數，召募射買。
entries.en: Regulations followed: wherever mines existed, mouke and county magistrates were to register sites and invite competitive bids.
entries.literal: Regulations were then fixed: wherever smelteries existed, mouke and county magistrates were entrusted to register numbers and summon competitive bids.

entries.zh: 禁權要、官吏、弓兵、裏胥皆不得與。
entries.en: Powerful families, officials, bow soldiers, and village clerks were barred from taking contracts.
entries.literal: It was forbidden for powerful families, officials, bow soldiers, and village clerks to participate.

entries.zh: 如舊場之例，令州府長官一員提控，提刑司訪察而禁治之。
entries.en: As with the old market system, one prefectural chief supervised each site while the surveillance commission investigated abuses.
entries.literal: Following the example of old markets, one prefectural chief was appointed to supervise, and the surveillance commission was to investigate and prohibit abuses.

entries.zh: 上曰：「此終非長策。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "This is no lasting solution."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "This is ultimately not a long-term policy."

entries.zh: 參知政事胥持國曰：「今姑聽如此，後有利然後設官可也。
entries.en: Vice Director Xu Chiguo replied, "Let it stand for now; once revenues justify it, the state can appoint officials.
entries.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Xu Chiguo said: "For now let it be heard thus; when there is profit afterward, officials may then be established.

entries.zh: 譬之酒酤，蓋先為坊場，從後官榷也。」
entries.en: It resembles the wine trade: private workshops come first, state monopoly later."
entries.literal: It is like wine sales—first establish workshops and markets, and afterward the state monopolizes."

entries.zh: 上亦以為然，遂從之。
entries.en: The emperor agreed, and the proposal was adopted.
entries.literal: The emperor also held this correct and followed it.

entries.zh: 墳山、西銀山之銀窟凡百一十有三。
entries.en: Fen Mountain and West Silver Mountain together held 113 silver mines.
entries.literal: Silver mines at Fen Mountain and West Silver Mountain numbered 113 in all.

entries.zh: 熙宗皇統二年十月，燕、西、東京、河東、河北、山東，汴京等路秋熟，命有司增價和糴。
entries.en: In the tenth month of Xizong's Huangtong 2 (1142), after the harvest in Yan, Western, Eastern Capital, Hedong, Hebei, Shandong, and Bianjing circuits, officials were ordered to buy grain at premium prices.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of Huangtong 2 under Emperor Xizong, when autumn crops ripened in the Yan, Western, Eastern Capital, Hedong, Hebei, Shandong, and Bianjing circuits, responsible offices were ordered to raise prices for harmonized grain purchase.

entries.zh: 世宗大定二年，以正隆之後倉廩久匱，遣太子少師完顏守道等，山東東、西路收糴軍糧，除戶口歲食外，盡令納官，給其直。
entries.en: In Shizong's Dading 2 (1162), with granaries depleted since the Zhenglong era, Junior Tutor Wanyan Shoudao was sent to eastern and western Shandong to buy army grain, requiring households to sell all surplus beyond annual rations at fair price.
entries.literal: In the second year of Dading under Emperor Shizong, because after Zhenglong the granaries had long been empty, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent Wanyan Shoudao and others were sent to the eastern and western Shandong circuits to purchase army grain; apart from each household's yearly food, all was ordered surrendered to the government and paid for.

entries.zh: 三年，謂宰臣曰：「國家經費甚大，向令山東和糴，止得四十五萬余石，未足為備。
entries.en: In the third year he told his ministers, "State expenses are enormous. The last Shandong purchase brought only 450,000-odd shi—not enough for reserves.
entries.literal: In the third year he told his ministers: "State expenditures are very great; the earlier order for Shandong harmonized purchase yielded only 450,000-odd shi—not enough as reserve.

entries.zh: 自古有水旱，所以無患者，由蓄積多也。
entries.en: Floods and droughts are as old as history; states escaped harm only when granaries were full.
entries.literal: From antiquity there have been flood and drought; the reason there was no harm was because accumulations were abundant.

entries.zh: 山東軍屯處須急為二年之儲，若遇水旱則用賑濟。
entries.en: Shandong garrison districts need two years' grain on hand at once for relief when disaster strikes.
entries.literal: Where army colonies stood in Shandong, a two-year reserve must urgently be made; if flood or drought occurs, use it for relief.

entries.zh: 自餘宿兵之郡，亦須糴以足之。
entries.en: Other provinces hosting troops must buy grain until stores are full.
entries.literal: The remaining prefectures where troops are stationed must also purchase grain to fill them.

entries.zh: 京師之用甚大，所須之儲，其敕戶部宜急為計。」
entries.en: The capital's needs are vast; the Revenue Ministry must plan reserves without delay."
entries.literal: The capital's consumption is very great; as for the required reserves, the Revenue Ministry should urgently devise plans."

entries.zh: 五年，責宰臣曰：「朕謂積貯為國本，當修倉廩以廣和糴。
entries.en: In the fifth year he rebuked his ministers: "Stored grain is the state's foundation. Repair granaries and expand government purchases.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he reproached his ministers: "I hold that stored grain is the foundation of the state; granaries should be repaired to expand harmonized purchase.

entries.zh: 今聞外路官文具而已。
entries.en: I hear outer-circuit officials treat this as paperwork only.
entries.literal: Now I hear that officials on outer circuits treat it as mere paperwork.

entries.zh: 卿等不留心，甚不稱委任之意。」
entries.en: Your inattention falls far short of what I entrusted to you."
entries.literal: You do not give it your attention—this greatly fails the intent of my commission."

entries.zh: 六年八月，敕有司，秋成之後，可于諸路廣糴，以備水旱。
entries.en: In the eighth month of year six an edict ordered broad post-harvest purchases on every circuit against flood and drought.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year an edict ordered responsible offices that after the autumn harvest, broad purchase might be made on all circuits to prepare for flood and drought.

entries.zh: 九年正月，諭宰臣曰：「朕觀宋人虛誕，恐不能久遵誓約。
entries.en: In the first month of year nine he warned his ministers, "The Song are unreliable; they may not keep the treaty for long.
entries.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he instructed his ministers: "I observe the Song are empty and deceitful; I fear they cannot long keep their sworn treaty.

entries.zh: 其令將臣謹飭邊備，以戒不虞。
entries.en: Order frontier commanders to tighten defenses against surprise attack.
entries.literal: Let generals and ministers strictly ready border defenses to guard against the unexpected.

entries.zh: 去歲河南豐，宜令所在廣糴，以實倉稟。
entries.en: Henan had a bumper harvest last year; every locality should buy grain widely and fill the granaries.
entries.literal: Last year Henan was abundant; each place should be ordered to purchase broadly and fill the granaries.

entries.zh: 詔州縣和糴，毋得抑配百姓。」
entries.en: An edict forbade counties and prefectures from coercing the populace during government grain purchases."
entries.literal: An edict declared that counties and prefectures conducting harmonized purchase must not forcibly apportion burdens on the people."

entries.zh: 十二年
entries.en: In the twelfth year
entries.literal: In the twelfth year

entries.zh: 世宗大定十四年，嘗定制，詔中外行之，其法尋廢。
entries.en: In Shizong's Dading 14 (1174) regulations were enacted empire-wide, but the system was soon abandoned.
