entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Dading under Emperor Shizong regulations were once fixed and an edict ordered them carried out within and without the court; the method was soon abandoned.

entries.zh: 章宗明昌元年八月，御史請複設，敕省臣詳議以聞。
entries.en: In the eighth month of Zhangzong's Mingchang 1 (1190) censors asked to restore the system; the court ordered provincial ministers to deliberate and report.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of Mingchang 1 under Emperor Zhangzong censors requested restoration; an edict ordered provincial ministers to deliberate in detail and report.

entries.zh: 省臣言：「大定舊制，豐年則增市價十之二以糴，儉歲則減市價十之一以出，平歲則已。
entries.en: Provincial ministers said, "Under the old Dading system, in abundant years grain was bought at two-tenths above market price; in lean years it was sold at one-tenth below market price; in normal years nothing was done.
entries.literal: Provincial ministers said, "Under the old Dading system, in abundant years grain was bought at two-tenths above market price; in lean years it was sold at one-tenth below market price; in normal years nothing was done.

entries.zh: 夫所以豐則增價以收者，恐物賤傷農。
entries.en: Prices were raised in good years lest cheap grain harm farmers.
entries.literal: The reason for raising price to buy in abundance is fear that cheap goods harm farmers.

entries.zh: 儉則減價以出者，恐物貴傷民。
entries.en: Prices were lowered in scarcity lest dear grain harm the people.
entries.literal: In scarcity price is reduced to sell out, fearing that dear goods harm the people.

entries.zh: 增之損之以平粟價，故謂常平，非謂使天下之民專仰給於此也。
entries.en: Raising and lowering prices stabilized grain markets—hence the name ever-normal—not a plan to make the entire populace depend on these granaries alone.
entries.literal: Raising and lowering to level grain prices is therefore called ever-normal—not meaning to make all people under heaven rely solely on this for sustenance.

entries.zh: 今天下生齒至眾，如欲計口使餘一年之儲，則不惟數多難辦，又慮出不以時而致腐敗也。
entries.en: With the empire's vast population, storing a full year's grain per capita would be unmanageable and risk spoilage if not released in time.
entries.literal: Now the population under heaven is extremely numerous; if one wished to calculate by mouth and leave a year's reserve for each, not only would the quantity be hard to manage, but one also fears that if not released in time it would rot.

entries.zh: 況複有司抑配之弊，殊非經久之計。
entries.en: Forced apportionment by local officials made the scheme unsustainable.
entries.literal: Moreover there is the abuse of offices forcibly apportioning burdens—this is truly no long-term plan.

entries.zh: 如計諸郡縣驗戶口例以月支三鬥為率，每口但儲三月，已及千萬數，亦足以平物價救荒凶矣。
entries.en: If each county stored three months' grain per capita at the standard three-dou monthly ration, totals would reach tens of millions of shi—enough to stabilize prices and relieve famine.
entries.literal: If one calculates by counties and prefectures verifying household registers at the rate of three dou monthly ration per person, storing only three months per mouth, the total already reaches tens of millions—this too suffices to level prices and relieve famine and disaster.

entries.zh: 若令諸處，自官兵三年食外，可充三月之食者免糴，其不及者俟豐年糴之，庶可久行也。
entries.en: Districts with three months' surplus beyond troop rations should be exempt from purchase; deficient districts should buy in good years—then the system could endure.
entries.literal: If each place, apart from three years' food for troops and officials, is exempt from purchase where three months' food can be filled, and where it falls short waits for abundant years to purchase, it may perhaps be carried on long.

entries.zh: 然立法之始貴在必行，其令提刑司各路計司兼領之，郡縣吏沮格者糾，能推行者加擢用。
entries.en: Effective enforcement was essential: the surveillance commission and circuit accounting offices should jointly oversee the system, obstructing clerks impeached and successful implementers promoted.
entries.literal: Yet at the beginning of legislation what is valued is certain enforcement: order the surveillance commission and circuit accounting offices jointly to oversee it; county and prefecture clerks who obstruct are to be impeached, those who can implement are to be promoted.

entries.zh: 若中都路年穀不熟之所，則依常平法，減其價三之一以糴。」
entries.en: Wherever the Central Capital circuit has a poor harvest, buy grain at one-third below market price according to the ever-normal granary method."
entries.literal: Wherever the Central Capital circuit has a poor harvest, buy grain at one-third below market price according to the ever-normal granary method."

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: The edict approved the plan.
entries.literal: An edict approved it.

entries.zh: 熙宗皇統三年三月，陝西旱饑，詔許富民入粟補官。
entries.en: In the third month of Xizong's Huangtong 3 (1143) drought and famine struck Shaanxi; wealthy households were allowed to buy offices with grain.
entries.literal: In the third month of Huangtong 3 under Emperor Xizong, Shaanxi suffered drought and famine; an edict permitted wealthy households to submit grain to supplement offices.

entries.zh: 世宗大定元年，以兵興歲歉，下令聽民進納補官。
entries.en: In Shizong's Dading 1 (1161) war and crop failure led the court to allow grain payments for offices.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dading under Emperor Shizong, because war arose and harvests failed, an order permitted the people to advance payments to supplement offices.

entries.zh: 又募能濟饑民者，視其人數為補官格。
entries.en: Those who relieved famine victims were also recruited, with office grades set by the number saved.
entries.literal: Those able to relieve famine victims were also recruited; according to the number of people saved, office-supplement grades were set.

entries.zh: 五年，上謂宰臣曰：「頃以邊事未定，財用闕乏，自東、南兩京外，命民進納補官，及賣僧、道、尼、女冠度牒，紫、褐衣師號，寺觀名額。
entries.en: In the fifth year the emperor told his ministers, "Recently, because border affairs were unsettled and finances were short, outside the Eastern and Southern Capitals we ordered the people to submit payments to receive office, and sold ordination certificates for monks, Daoists, nuns, and priestesses, purple and brown robe master titles, and temple and monastery name quotas.
entries.literal: In the fifth year the emperor told his ministers, "Recently, because border affairs were unsettled and finances were short, outside the Eastern and Southern Capitals we ordered the people to submit payments to receive office, and sold ordination certificates for monks, Daoists, nuns, and priestesses, purple and brown robe master titles, and temple and monastery name quotas.

entries.zh: 今邊鄙已寧，其悉罷之。
entries.en: With the frontier now calm, all these measures were abolished.
entries.literal: Now the borderlands are calm; let all these be abolished.

entries.zh: 慶壽寺、天長觀歲給度牒，每道折錢二十萬以賜之。」
entries.en: Qingshou Temple and Tianchang Abbey are given ordination certificates each year, each certificate being converted to 200,000 cash and granted to them."
entries.literal: Qingshou Temple and Tianchang Abbey are given ordination certificates each year, each certificate being converted to 200,000 cash and granted to them."

entries.zh: 明昌二年，敕山東、河北闕食之地，納粟補官有差。
entries.en: In Mingchang 2 graded rates for grain office purchases applied in famine-stricken parts of Shandong and Hebei.
entries.literal: In Mingchang 2 an edict ordered that in Shandong and Hebei where food was lacking, grain submission for office supplement had graded rates.

entries.zh: 承安二年，賣度牒、師號、寺觀額，複令人入粟補官。
entries.en: In Cheng'an 2 the court again sold certificates, master titles, and temple quotas and allowed grain office purchases.
entries.literal: In Cheng'an 2 ordination certificates, master titles, and monastery quotas were sold, and people were again permitted to submit grain for office supplement.

entries.zh: 三年，西京饑，詔賣度牒以濟之。
entries.en: In the third year famine in the Western Capital led the court to sell ordination certificates for relief.
entries.literal: In the third year the Western Capital suffered famine; an edict sold ordination certificates to relieve it.

entries.zh: 十二月，詔在都和糴以實倉廩，且使錢幣通流。
entries.en: In the twelfth month an edict ordered capital grain purchases to fill granaries and keep currency circulating.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month an edict ordered harmonized purchase in the capital to fill granaries and also circulate currency.

entries.zh: 又詔凡秋熟之郡，廣糴以備水旱。
entries.en: Another edict required every district with a good harvest to buy grain broadly against disaster.
entries.literal: Another edict declared that wherever the autumn harvest was good, broad purchase should prepare against flood and drought.

entries.zh: 十六年五月，諭左丞相紇石烈良弼曰：「西邊自來不備儲蓄，其令所在和糴，以備緩急。」
entries.en: In the fifth month of year sixteen he told Left Chancellor Heshenilie Liangbi, "The west has never stockpiled grain; order local purchases for emergencies."
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the sixteenth year he instructed Left Chancellor Heshenilie Liangbi: "The western frontier has never prepared reserves; order harmonized purchase in each place to prepare for emergencies."

entries.zh: 十七年春，尚書省奏：「先奉詔賑濟東京等路饑民，三路粟數不能給。」
entries.en: In the spring of year seventeen the Department reported, "Earlier we received an edict to relieve famine victims in the Eastern Capital and other circuits, but the grain of the three circuits cannot meet the need."
entries.literal: In the spring of year seventeen the Department reported, "Earlier we received an edict to relieve famine victims in the Eastern Capital and other circuits, but the grain of the three circuits cannot meet the need."

entries.zh: 上曰：「朕嘗諭卿等，豐年廣糴以備凶歉。
entries.en: The emperor said, "I told you to buy grain generously in good years against famine.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "I once instructed you to purchase broadly in abundant years to prepare for lean years.

entries.zh: 卿等皆言天下倉廩盈溢，今欲賑濟，乃雲不給。
entries.en: You all claimed granaries were overflowing; now you say there is nothing left for relief.
entries.literal: You all said the empire's granaries overflowed; now when relief is wanted, you say there is not enough.

entries.zh: 自古帝王皆以蓄積為國長計，朕之積粟豈欲獨用。
entries.en: Emperors since antiquity stored grain as a long-term policy. I did not stockpile it for myself alone.
entries.literal: From antiquity emperors and kings all took accumulation as the state's long-term plan—do I hoard grain to use it alone?

entries.zh: 即今不給，可於鄰道取之。
entries.en: If supplies run short now, draw from neighboring circuits.
entries.literal: If now it is not enough, take it from neighboring circuits.

entries.zh: 自今多備，當以為常。」
entries.en: Stockpile heavily from now on and make that the norm."
entries.literal: From now on prepare abundantly and make it the regular practice."

entries.zh: 四月，尚書省奏：「東京三路十二猛安尤闕食者，已賑之矣。
entries.en: In the fourth month the Department reported, "The neediest among the twelve meng'an in the three Eastern Capital circuits have already been relieved.
entries.literal: In the fourth month the Department reported, "The neediest among the twelve meng'an in the three Eastern Capital circuits have already been relieved.

entries.zh: 尚有未賑者。」
entries.en: There are still others who have not yet received relief."
entries.literal: There are still others who have not yet received relief."

entries.zh: 詔遣官詣複州、曷蘇館路，檢視富家，蓄積有餘增直以糴。
entries.en: Officials were sent to Fuzhou and the Hesuguan circuit to inspect wealthy households and buy surplus grain at premium prices.
entries.literal: An edict dispatched officials to Fuzhou and the Hesuguan circuit to inspect wealthy households; where accumulations were surplus, purchase at raised prices.

entries.zh: 令近地居民就往受糧。
entries.en: Nearby residents were to collect the grain on site.
entries.literal: Nearby residents were ordered to go and receive grain.

entries.zh: 十八年四月，命泰州所管諸猛安、西北路招討司所管奚猛安，咸平府慶雲縣寔松河等處遇豐年，多和糴。
entries.en: In the fourth month of year eighteen the court ordered meng'an under Taizhou and the Xi under the Northwestern Pacification Commission, and places such as Shisong River in Qingyun County, Xianping Prefecture, to buy grain heavily in good harvest years.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the eighteenth year orders were issued that all meng'an under Taizhou, Xi meng'an under the Northwestern Pacification Commission, and places such as Shisong River in Qingyun County, Xianping Prefecture, when harvests were abundant, conduct extensive harmonized purchase.

entries.zh: 章宗明昌二年七月，尚書省以泗州榷場自前關防不嚴，遂奏定從大定五年制，官為增修舍屋，倍設闌禁，委場官及提控所拘榷，以提刑司舉察。
entries.en: In the seventh month of Zhangzong's Mingchang 2 (1191) the Department of State Affairs noted lax controls at the Sizhou market and proposed adopting the Dading 5 rules: state-funded repairs, doubled checkpoints, supervision by market officials and control offices, and inspection by the surveillance commission.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of Mingchang 2 under Emperor Zhangzong, the Department of State Affairs reported that from earlier times border controls at the Sizhou monopoly market had not been strict, and memorialized to fix regulations following the Dading 5 system: officials were to enlarge and repair buildings, double the barriers, entrust market officials and control offices with monopoly supervision, and have the surveillance commission investigate.

entries.zh: 惟東勝、淨、慶州，來遠軍者仍舊，余皆修完之。
entries.en: Only Dongsheng, Jing, Qingzhou, and Laiyuan Army were left unchanged; all other sites were refurbished.
entries.literal: Only Dongsheng, Jing, Qingzhou, and Laiyuan Army were left as before; the rest were all repaired and completed.

entries.zh: 泗州場，大定間，歲獲五萬三千四百六十七貫，承安元年，增為十萬七千八百九十三貫六百五十三文。
entries.en: During the Dading era the Sizhou market yielded 53,467 strings annually; in Cheng'an 1 (1196) receipts rose to 107,893 strings and 653 cash.
entries.literal: The Sizhou market during the Dading period yielded 53,467 strings per year; in the first year of Cheng'an it rose to 107,893 strings 653 cash.

entries.zh: 所須雜物，泗州場歲供進新茶千胯、荔支五百斤、圓眼五百斤、金橘六千斤、橄欖五百斤、芭蕉幹三百個、蘇木千斤、溫柑七千個、橘子八千個、沙糖三百斤、生薑六百斤、梔子九十稱、犀象丹砂之類不與焉。
entries.en: Each year the Sizhou market also forwarded tribute goods: 1,000 bundles of fresh tea, 500 jin of lychee, 500 jin of longan, 6,000 jin of kumquat, 500 jin of olives, 300 dried plantains, 1,000 jin of sappanwood, 7,000 Wenzhou oranges, 8,000 oranges, 300 jin of sugar, 600 jin of ginger, and 90 sheng of gardenia—excluding rhinoceros horn, ivory, cinnabar, and similar luxuries.
entries.literal: Among required miscellaneous goods, the Sizhou market each year presented as tribute 1,000 bundles of new tea, 500 jin of lychee, 500 jin of longan, 6,000 jin of kumquat, 500 jin of olive, 300 dried plantains, 1,000 jin of sappanwood, 7,000 Wenzhou oranges, 8,000 oranges, 300 jin of sugar, 600 jin of ginger, and 90 sheng of gardenia—not including rhinoceros horn, ivory, cinnabar, and the like.

entries.zh: 宋亦歲得課四萬三千貫。
entries.en: The Song likewise collected 43,000 strings in annual duties.
entries.literal: The Song also gained 43,000 strings in revenue each year.

entries.zh: 秦州西子城場，大定間，歲獲三萬三千六百五十六貫，承安元年，歲獲十二萬二千九十九貫。
entries.en: During Dading the Qinzhou Xizi City market yielded 33,656 strings a year; in Cheng'an 1 receipts reached 122,099 strings.
entries.literal: The Qinzhou Xizi City market during Dading yielded 33,656 strings per year; in Cheng'an 1 it yielded 122,099 strings per year.

entries.zh: 承安二年，複置於保安、蘭州。
entries.en: In Cheng'an 2 (1197) markets at Bao'an and Lanzhou were reopened.
entries.literal: In Cheng'an 2 they were re-established at Bao'an and Lanzhou.

entries.zh: 三年九月，行樞密院奏：「斜出等告開榷場，擬於轄裏尼要安置。」
entries.en: In the ninth month of year three the Mobile Privy Council reported, "Xiechu and others have requested the opening of a border market; we propose placing it at a strategic point in Xialini."
entries.literal: In the ninth month of year three the Mobile Privy Council reported, "Xiechu and others have requested the opening of a border market; we propose placing it at a strategic point in Xialini."

entries.zh: 許自今年十一月貿易。
entries.en: Trade was authorized beginning in the eleventh month of that year.
entries.literal: Permission was granted for trade from the eleventh month of this year.

entries.zh: 尋定制，隨路榷場若以見錢入外界、與外人交易者，徒五年，三斤以上死。
entries.en: Regulations soon fixed that taking cash across the border or trading it with foreigners at any circuit market drew five years' penal servitude, and three jin or more meant death.
entries.literal: Soon regulations were fixed: at monopoly markets in each circuit, if cash coin was taken into the outer realm or traded with foreigners, penal servitude for five years; three jin or more meant death.

entries.zh: 宋界諸場，以伐宋皆罷。
entries.en: Every market on the Song frontier was closed when war against the Song resumed.
entries.literal: All markets on the Song border were abolished because of the campaign against the Song.

entries.zh: 泰和八年八月，以與宋和，宋人請如舊置之，遂複置於唐、鄧、壽、泗、息州及秦、鳳之地。
entries.en: In the eighth month of Taihe 8 (1208), after peace with the Song and a Song request to restore the old arrangement, markets reopened at Tang, Deng, Shou, Si, Xizhou, and in the Qin and Feng regions.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of Taihe 8, because peace was made with the Song and the Song requested restoration as before, markets were re-established at Tang, Deng, Shou, Si, Xizhou, and in the Qin and Feng regions.

entries.zh: 宣宗貞祐元年，秦州榷場為宋人所焚。
entries.en: In Xuanzong's Zhenyou 1 (1213), the Qinzhou market was burned by Song forces.
entries.literal: In Xuanzong's Zhenyou 1 (1213), the Qinzhou market was burned by Song forces.

entries.zh: 二年，陝西安撫副使烏古論袞州複開設之，歲所獲以十數萬計。
entries.en: In year two, Shaanxi Deputy Pacification Commissioner Wugulun Gunzhou reopened it, and annual receipts were counted in the hundreds of thousands.
entries.literal: In year two, Shaanxi Deputy Pacification Commissioner Wugulun Gunzhou reopened it, and annual receipts were counted in the hundreds of thousands.

entries.zh: 三年七月，議欲聽榷場互市用銀，而計數稅之。
entries.en: In the seventh month of year three, officials discussed allowing silver to be used in mutual trade at the border markets and taxing it by amount.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of year three, officials discussed allowing silver to be used in mutual trade at the border markets and taxing it by amount.

entries.zh: 上曰：「如此，是公使銀入外界也。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "If we do this, it is openly sending silver across the border."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "If we do this, it is openly sending silver across the border."

entries.zh: 平章盡忠、權參知政事德升曰：「賞賜之用莫如銀絹，而府庫不足以給之。
entries.en: Chief Minister Jinzhong and Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat Desheng said, "For rewards and grants nothing is better than silver and silk, but the treasury cannot supply enough.
entries.literal: Chief Minister Jinzhong and Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat Desheng said, "For rewards and grants nothing is better than silver and silk, but the treasury cannot supply enough.

entries.zh: 互市雖有禁，而私易者自如。
entries.en: Although mutual trade is forbidden, private traders do as they please.
entries.literal: Although mutual trade is forbidden, private traders do as they please.

entries.zh: 若稅之，則斂不及民而用可足。」
entries.en: If it is taxed, the levy will not reach the common people, and state needs can be met."
entries.literal: If it is taxed, the levy will not reach the common people, and state needs can be met."

entries.zh: 平章高琪曰：「小人敢犯，法不行爾，況許之乎？
entries.en: Chief Minister Gao Qi said, "Petty people dare to violate the law only because the law is not enforced. How much worse if we permit it?
entries.literal: Chief Minister Gao Qi said, "Petty people dare to violate the law only because the law is not enforced. How much worse if we permit it?

entries.zh: 今軍未息，而產銀之地皆在外界，不禁則公私指日罄矣！」
entries.en: Now the armies have not yet stood down, and all the silver-producing lands are outside our borders. If this is not banned, public and private silver will soon be exhausted!"
entries.literal: Now the armies have not yet stood down, and all the silver-producing lands are outside our borders. If this is not banned, public and private silver will soon be exhausted!"

entries.zh: 上曰：「當熟計之。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "This should be carefully considered."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "This should be carefully considered."

entries.zh: 興定元年，集賢諮議官呂鑒言：「嘗監息州榷場，每場獲布數千匹，銀數百兩，兵興之後皆失之。」
entries.en: In Xingding 1 (1217), Jixian Advisory Official Lu Jian said, "I once supervised the Xizhou market. Each market obtained several thousand bolts of cloth and several hundred taels of silver, but after the fighting began, all of this was lost."
entries.literal: In Xingding 1 (1217), Jixian Advisory Official Lu Jian said, "I once supervised the Xizhou market. Each market obtained several thousand bolts of cloth and several hundred taels of silver, but after the fighting began, all of this was lost."

entries.zh: 貞祐四年八月，言事者程淵言：「碭山諸縣陂湖，水至則畦為稻田，水退種麥，所收倍於陸地。
entries.en: In the eighth month of Zhenyou 4, memorialist Cheng Yuan said, "In the lake and embankment lands of Dangshan and other counties, when water arrives the beds become rice fields, and when the water recedes wheat is planted; their yields are double those of dry land.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of Zhenyou 4, memorialist Cheng Yuan said, "In the lake and embankment lands of Dangshan and other counties, when water arrives the beds become rice fields, and when the water recedes wheat is planted; their yields are double those of dry land.

entries.zh: 宜募人佃之，官取三之一，歲可得十萬石。」
entries.en: Tenants should be recruited for them, with the government taking one-third; each year 100,000 shi can be obtained."
entries.literal: Tenants should be recruited for them, with the government taking one-third; each year 100,000 shi can be obtained."

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: The edict approved the plan.
entries.literal: An edict approved it.

entries.zh: 興定五年五月，南陽令李國瑞創開水田四百餘頃，詔升職二等，仍錄其最狀遍諭諸道。
entries.en: In the fifth month of Xingding 5 Nanyang Magistrate Li Guorui opened over 400 qing of paddy and was promoted two grades; his record was circulated to all circuits.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of Xingding 5 Nanyang Magistrate Li Guorui newly opened more than 400 qing of paddy; an edict promoted him two grades and recorded his top achievement to announce throughout all circuits.

entries.zh: 凡銓注，必取求仕官解由，撮所陳行績資歷之要為銓頭，以定其能否？
entries.en: Every appointment required the candidate's discharge papers; the ministry distilled conduct, merit, and qualifications into a selection summary to judge fitness.
entries.literal: For every appointment one had to take the petitioning official's discharge certificate, extract the essentials of stated conduct, merit, and qualifications as the selection summary, and thereby determine fitness.

entries.zh: 其有犯公私罪贓汙者，謂之犯選格，則雖遇恩而不得與。
entries.en: Anyone guilty of public or private crimes or corruption violated selection criteria and could not participate even when an amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: Those who had committed public or private crimes or corruption were said to violate selection criteria; even when amnesties were granted they could not participate.

entries.zh: 舊制，犯追一官以至追四官，皆解任周年，而複仕之。
entries.en: Under the old rules, anyone demoted by one to four ranks had to leave office for a full year before serving again.
entries.literal: Under the old rules, offenders demoted by one rank up to four ranks all left office for a full year before being reappointed.

entries.zh: 承安二年，定制，每追一官則殿一年，凡罷職會赦當敘者，及降殿當除者，皆具罪以聞，而後仕之。
entries.en: In Cheng'an 2 (1197) the rule was set: each rank lost meant one year on the bench. Anyone dismissed who qualified for reinstatement at an amnesty, or whose bench term ended, had to report the full record of offenses before returning to office.
entries.literal: In the second year of Cheng'an regulations were fixed: for each rank demoted one year's bench penalty; whenever dismissed officials met amnesty conditions for reinstatement, or when bench penalties expired, the crimes were reported in full before reappointment.

entries.zh: 凡增課升至六品者，任回復降。
entries.en: Officials promoted to rank six for superior tax assessments were demoted again when their term ended.
entries.literal: All who were promoted to rank six for superior tax assessments were demoted again when their term ended.

entries.zh: 既廉升而再任覆察不同者，任回亦降。
entries.en: Those promoted on an integrity review who failed a repeat inspection on reappointment were demoted when their term ended as well.
entries.literal: Those promoted on integrity review whose repeat inspection on reappointment did not match were also demoted when their term ended.

entries.zh: 自進士、舉人、勞效、廕襲、恩例之外，入仕之途尚多，而所定之時不一。
entries.en: Beyond jinshi, juren, merit commendation, yin privilege, and grace appointments, many other paths to office existed, each fixed in a different reign.
entries.literal: Apart from jinshi, juren, merit commendation, yin privilege, and grace appointments, routes to office were still many, and the times when each was established were not uniform.

entries.zh: 若牌印、護衛、令史之出職，則皇統時所定者也。
entries.en: Posts such as seal officers, palace guards, and ministry clerks were established in the Huangtong era.
entries.literal: Offices such as seal officers, palace guards, and ministry clerks were fixed in the Huangtong period.

entries.zh: 檢法、知法、國史院書寫，則海陵庶人所置者也。
entries.en: Legal reviewers, legal specialists, and National History Academy scribes were offices created by Prince Hailing.
entries.literal: Legal reviewers, legal specialists, and National History Academy scribes were posts that the Prince of Hailing had created.

entries.zh: 若宗室將軍、宮中諸局承應人、宰相書表、太子護衛、妃護衛、王府祗候郎君、內侍、及宰相之子、並譯史、通事、省祗候郎君、親軍驍騎諸格，則定于世宗之時，及章宗所置之太常檢討、內侍寄祿官，皆仕進之門戶也。
entries.en: Imperial-clan generals, palace bureau attendants, chancellors' memorial scribes, crown-prince and consort guards, princely retainers, eunuchs, chancellors' sons, translators, interpreters, provincial attendants, and personal-guard and crack-cavalry categories were all set under Shizong; Zhangzong added Sacrifices examiners and salaried eunuch posts—each a doorway into office.
entries.literal: As for imperial-clan generals, attendants in the various palace bureaus, chancellors' memorial drafters, crown-prince guards, consort guards, princely household attendants, eunuchs, chancellors' sons, translators, interpreters, provincial attendants, and the categories of personal guards and crack cavalry—all fixed in Shizong's time—and the Sacrifices examiners and salaried eunuch posts that Zhangzong established, these were all gateways to advancement.

entries.zh: 凡門廕之制，天眷中，一品至八品皆不限所廕之人。
entries.en: Under the gate-yin system, in the Tianjuan era ranks one through eight placed no limit on who could receive yin privilege.
entries.literal: As for the system of gate yin privilege, in the Tianjuan period ranks one through eight were all unlimited as to whom could receive yin.

entries.zh: 貞元二年，定廕敘法，一品至七品皆限以數，而削八品用廕之制。
entries.en: In Zhenyuan 2 (1154) yin appointments were regulated: ranks one through seven were capped by number, and eighth-rank yin was abolished.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan the yin appointment law was fixed: ranks one through seven were all limited by number, and the eighth rank was cut from using yin.

entries.zh: 世宗大定四年五月，詔：「皇家袒免以上親，就廕者依格引試，中選者勿令當儤使。」
entries.en: In the fifth month of Dading 4 (1164) Shizong decreed: "Imperial kin within the upper-garment mourning circle who enter by yin shall sit the qualifying examination. Those who pass shall not be assigned corvée duty."
entries.literal: In the fifth month of Shizong's Dading 4 an edict stated: "Imperial kin within the upper-garment mourning circle who take yin shall be referred for examination according to regulations; those who pass shall not be assigned corvée duty."

entries.zh: 五年十月，制：「亡宋官當廕子孫者，並同亡遼官用廕。」
entries.en: In the tenth month of the fifth year (1165) a rule declared: "Descendants of deceased Song officials entitled to yin shall receive it on the same terms as descendants of deceased Liao officials."
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year a regulation stated: "Descendants of deceased Song officials entitled to yin shall all use yin on the same terms as descendants of deceased Liao officials."

entries.zh: 又曰：「教坊出身人，若任流內職者，與文武同用廕。
entries.en: It also said: "Music Bureau alumni who hold regular civil or military posts may use yin like other officials.
entries.literal: It also said: "Those from the Music Bureau who hold posts within the regular ranks may use yin like civil and military officials.

entries.zh: 自餘有勤勞者，賞賜而已。
entries.en: Everyone else with merit received rewards only.
entries.literal: All others with merit received rewards only.

entries.zh: 昔正隆時常使教坊輩典城牧民，朕甚不取。」
entries.en: Under Zhenglong the court often put Music Bureau people in charge of cities and subjects. I want no part of that."
entries.literal: In the past, during Zhenglong, Music Bureau people were often made to govern cities and shepherd the people; I greatly disapprove of this."

entries.zh: 又更定冒廕及取廕官罪賞格。
entries.en: The court also revised penalties and rewards for false yin claims and for officials who granted yin improperly.
entries.literal: Regulations were also revised for falsely claiming yin and for penalties and rewards regarding yin-granting officials.

entries.zh: 七年五月，命司天臺官四品以上官改授文武資者，並聽如太醫例廕。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the seventh year (1167) the court ruled that Astronomical Bureau officials of rank four and above reassigned to civil or military tracks might use yin on the same terms as medical officials.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year it was ordered that Astronomical Bureau officials of rank four and above who were reassigned to civil or military seniority might all use yin on the medical-official precedent.

entries.zh: 其制，凡正班，廕亦正班；
entries.en: The rule was: proper-rank holders granted proper-rank yin;
entries.literal: The rule was: for proper-rank posts, yin was also proper rank;

entries.zh: 雜班，廕雜班。
entries.en: mixed-rank holders granted mixed-rank yin.
entries.literal: for mixed-rank posts, yin was mixed rank.

entries.zh: 明昌元年，以上封事者乞六品官添廕，吏部言：「天眷中，八品用廕，不限所廕之人。
entries.en: In Mingchang 1 (1190) a sealed memorial asked for extra yin quotas for rank-six officials. The Ministry of Personnel replied: "In the Tianjuan era eighth-rank officials could grant yin without limit on recipients.
entries.literal: In the first year of Mingchang, on a sealed memorial someone requested added yin for rank-six officials. The Ministry of Personnel said: "In the Tianjuan period eighth rank used yin without limiting whom could receive it.

entries.zh: 貞元中，七品用廕，方限以數。
entries.en: In the Zhenyuan era seventh-rank yin was capped by number.
entries.literal: In the Zhenyuan period seventh rank used yin, and only then were numbers limited.

entries.zh: 當是時，文始於將仕，武始於進義，以上至七品儒林、忠顯，各七階，許廕一名。
entries.en: At that time the civil track began at Awaiting Assignment and the military at Advancing Righteousness. From there through rank-seven Rulin and Zhongxian—seven grades in all—one yin recipient was allowed.
entries.literal: At that time the civil track began at Awaiting Assignment and the military at Advancing Righteousness; from there up to rank-seven Rulin and Zhongxian, seven grades in all, one yin recipient was permitted.

entries.zh: 至六品承直、昭信，計九階，許廕二人。
entries.en: At rank-six Chengzhi and Zhaoxin—nine grades in all—two yin recipients were allowed.
entries.literal: At rank-six Chengzhi and Zhaoxin, nine grades in all, two yin recipients were permitted.

entries.zh: 自大定十四年，文武官從下各增二階，其七品視舊為九階，亦廕一人，至五品凡十七階，方廕二人，其五品至三品並無間越，唯六品不用廕。
entries.en: From Dading 14 (1174) civil and military ranks each gained two bottom grades. Seventh rank—nine grades by the old count—still allowed one yin; fifth rank, seventeen grades in all, allowed two. Fifth through third rank had no gaps, but sixth rank could not use yin.
entries.literal: From Dading 14 civil and military officials each gained two grades at the bottom; seventh rank, which by the old count was nine grades, also granted one yin; at fifth rank, seventeen grades in all, two yin were granted; from fifth through third rank there was no gap, but sixth rank did not use yin.

entries.zh: 乞依舊格，五品以上增廕一名，六品廕子孫兄弟二人，七品仍舊為格。」
entries.en: We ask to follow the old rules: add one yin quota from fifth rank upward; allow sixth rank two yin for sons, brothers, or nephews; leave seventh rank unchanged."
entries.literal: We ask to follow the old regulations: from fifth rank upward add one yin; at sixth rank grant yin to two sons, brothers, or nephews; at seventh rank keep the old rule."

entries.zh: 時又以舊格雖有己子許廕兄弟侄，蓋所以崇孝悌也。
entries.en: The court noted that although old rules let a son yield yin to brothers or nephews, that was meant to honor filial piety and fraternal duty.
entries.literal: At the time it was also noted that although the old regulations allowed one's own son to yield yin to brothers and nephews, this was meant to honor filial piety and brotherly duty.

entries.zh: 而新格禁之，遂聽讓廕。
entries.en: The new rules forbade it, so yielding yin was allowed instead.
entries.literal: The new regulations forbade this, so yielding yin was permitted.

entries.zh: 舊制，司天、太醫、內侍、長行雖至四品。
entries.en: Under the old rules, astronomical, medical, eunuch, and senior-attendant offices, though they could reach rank four,
entries.literal: Under the old rules, astronomical, medical, eunuch, and senior attendant offices, though they reached rank four,

entries.zh: 如非特恩換授文武官資者，不許用廕，以本人見允承應，難使系班故也。
entries.en: could not use yin unless specially reassigned to civil or military seniority, because the holder was still serving as an attendant and could not be tied to the regular rank roster.
entries.literal: unless specially favored and reassigned to civil or military seniority, were not permitted to use yin, because the holder was currently serving as an attendant and could not easily be tied to the rank roster.

entries.zh: 泰和二年，定制，以年老六十以上退、與患疾及身故者，雖至止官，擬令系班，除存習本業者聽廕一名，止一子者則不須習即廕。
entries.en: In Taihe 2 (1202) the rule was set: retirees over sixty, the seriously ill, and the deceased—though they had reached terminal rank—stayed on the roster. Those who kept practicing their trade could grant one yin; if there was only one son, he need not practice the trade to receive yin.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taihe regulations were fixed: those who retired at age sixty or above, or because of illness or death, though they had reached terminal rank, were to remain on the roster; except those who continued practicing their profession, one yin was permitted; if there was only one son, he need not practice the profession to receive yin.

entries.zh: 正隆元年，罷是制，止於密院台及六部吏人令史內選充。
entries.en: In Zhenglong 1 (1156) this system was abolished; clerks were chosen only from the Privy Council, Censorate, and six ministries.
entries.literal: In Zhenglong 1 this system was abolished; selection was limited to clerks of the Privy Council, Censorate, and six ministries.

entries.zh: 大定元年，世宗以胥吏既貪墨，委之外路幹事又不知大體，徒多擾動，至二年，罷吏人而複皇統選進士之制。
entries.en: In Dading 1 (1161) Shizong found clerks corrupt and their external assignments disruptive because they lacked broader judgment. In the second year (1162) he dismissed them and restored the Huangtong jinshi selection system.
entries.literal: In Dading 1 Shizong, because clerks were already corrupt and when sent on external assignments did not understand larger principles but only caused disturbance, by the second year clerks were dismissed and the Huangtong system of selecting jinshi was restored.

entries.zh: 承直郎以上者，一考正七品，除運判、節察判、軍刺同知。
entries.en: At Chengzhi Lang and above: one evaluation brought proper seventh rank as transport judge, circuit judge, or military commissioner deputy.
entries.literal: Those at Chengzhi Lang and above: after one evaluation proper seventh rank, appointed transport judge, circuit-intendant judge, or military commissioner deputy.

entries.zh: 兩考者從六品，除京運判、總府判、防禦同知。
entries.en: Two evaluations brought secondary sixth rank as capital transport judge, metropolitan prefectural judge, or defense commissioner deputy.
entries.literal: After two evaluations secondary sixth rank, appointed capital transport judge, metropolitan prefectural judge, or defense commissioner deputy.

entries.zh: 奉直大夫已上，一考者從六品，除同前。
entries.en: Fengzhi Grand Master and above: one evaluation brought secondary sixth rank with the same appointments as before.
entries.literal: Fengzhi Grand Master and above: after one evaluation secondary sixth rank, appointments as before.

entries.zh: 兩考從五品，除節運副、京總管府留守司判官。
entries.en: Two evaluations brought secondary fifth rank as circuit-transport deputy or capital metropolitan retention-office judge.
entries.literal: After two evaluations secondary fifth rank, appointed circuit-transport deputy or capital metropolitan prefectural retention-office judge.

entries.zh: 七年，以散階官至五品亦勾充，不願者聽。
entries.en: In the seventh year (1167) holders of honorary fifth rank could also be selected; unwilling candidates could decline.
entries.literal: In the seventh year those whose honorary rank reached fifth rank were also selected; those unwilling were permitted to decline.

entries.zh: 十一年，以進士官至承直者眾，遂不論官資但以榜次勾補。
entries.en: In the eleventh year (1171) so many jinshi had reached Chengzhi that selection followed examination rank alone, without regard to seniority.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, because many jinshi had reached Chengzhi, official seniority was no longer considered and selection followed only examination rank.

entries.zh: 二十七年，以外多闕官，論者以為資考所拘，難以升進，乃命不論官資，凡一考者與六品，次任降除正七品，第三任與六品，第四任升為從五品。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year (1187), with many vacancies outside the capital and critics arguing seniority rules blocked advancement, the court ignored seniority: one evaluation brought rank six; second term demotion to proper seventh; third term rank six again; fourth term secondary fifth.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, because outside the capital many offices were vacant and critics held that seniority requirements hindered advancement, it was ordered that regardless of seniority, after one evaluation rank six was granted; on the next term demoted to proper seventh rank; on the third term rank six again; on the fourth advanced to secondary fifth rank.

entries.zh: 兩考者與從五品，次任降除六品，第三、四任皆與從五品，五任升正五品。
entries.en: Two evaluations brought secondary fifth rank; second term demotion to rank six; third and fourth terms secondary fifth again; fifth term proper fifth.
entries.literal: After two evaluations secondary fifth rank; next term demoted to rank six; third and fourth terms both secondary fifth rank; fifth term advanced to proper fifth rank.

entries.zh: 承安二年，以習學知除、刑房知案、及兵興時邊關令史，三十月除隨朝闕。
entries.en: In Cheng'an 2 (1197) trainee case managers, criminal-section managers, and wartime frontier clerks received court-service vacancies after thirty months.
entries.literal: In Cheng'an 2, trainee case managers, criminal-section case managers, and frontier clerks during military campaigns—after thirty months appointed to court-service vacancies.

entries.zh: 泰和八年，以習學知除十五月以上，選充正知除。
entries.en: In Taihe 8 (1208) trainee case managers with fifteen months or more were selected as full case managers.
entries.literal: In Taihe 8, trainee case managers of fifteen months or more were selected as full case managers.

entries.zh: 一考後理算資考。
entries.en: After one evaluation seniority was calculated.
entries.literal: After one evaluation seniority was calculated.

entries.zh: 大安三年，以從榜次則各人所曆月日不齊，遂以吏部等差其所曆歲月多寡為次，收補知除，考滿則授隨朝職。
entries.en: In Da'an 3 (1211) examination rank alone left service months uneven, so the Ministry ranked candidates by years served, enrolled them as case managers, and after evaluation granted court-service posts.
entries.literal: In Da'an 3, because following examination rank left each person's months uneven, the Ministry of Personnel ranked them by differential in years served, enrolled them as case managers, and after evaluation granted court-service posts.

entries.zh: 文武選
entries.en: Civil and Military Selection
entries.literal: Civil and Military Selection

entries.zh: 凡宮中諸局分，大定元年，世宗謂諸局分承應人，班敘俸給涉於太濫，正隆時乃無出身，涉於太刻，又其官品不以勞逸為制，遂命更定之。
entries.en: In Dading 1 Emperor Shizong found palace bureau attendants overpaid under current rules yet too restricted under Zhenglong, with ranks ignoring workload, and ordered reform.
entries.literal: As for all palace bureaus, in Dading 1 Emperor Shizong said the class ranking and salaries of bureau attendants were too lavish; in the Zhenglong era there was no pathway to office, which was too harsh; moreover official grades were not set according to labor light or heavy—therefore he ordered revision.

entries.zh: 大定六年，諭有司曰：「宮中諸局分承應人，有年滿數差使者，往往苦於稽留，而卒不得。
entries.en: In Dading 6 he told the offices, "Palace bureau attendants who had completed their terms and were due for rotation were often delayed and in the end never transferred.
entries.literal: In Dading 6 he instructed the offices: "Palace bureau attendants who had completed their term and were due for rotation often suffered prolonged delay and in the end did not obtain it.

entries.zh: 其差者，複多不解文字而不幹，故公私不便。
entries.en: Assignees often could not read documents or perform competently, hampering both public and private business.
entries.literal: Those assigned were moreover mostly unable to read documents and incompetent, so public and private affairs were inconvenienced.

entries.zh: 今從願出局者聽，願留者各增其秩，依舊承應。
entries.en: Those who wished to leave could do so; those who stayed received higher rank and continued as attendants.
entries.literal: Now those wishing to leave the bureau were permitted; those wishing to stay each had rank increased and continued as attendants as before.

entries.zh: 其十人長，雖老願留者亦增秩，作長行承應，餘依例放還。」
entries.en: Ten-person chiefs who wished to remain despite age were promoted to senior attendants; the rest were released according to precedent."
entries.literal: Their ten-person chiefs, even if old and wishing to stay, also had rank increased and served as senior attendants; the rest were released according to precedent."

entries.zh: 七年，詔宰臣曰：「女直人自來諸局分不經收充祗候。
entries.en: In year 7 the emperor told ministers, "Jurchens have never been recruited into palace bureaus as attendants.
entries.literal: In year 7 an edict told the chief ministers: "Jurchens have never been recruited into palace bureaus as attendants.

entries.zh: 可自今除太醫、司天、內侍外、餘局分並令收充勾當。」
entries.en: From now on, apart from the Medical Bureau, Astronomy Bureau, and Palace Service, all other bureaus are ordered to recruit them for service."
entries.literal: From now on, apart from the Medical Bureau, Astronomy Bureau, and Palace Service, all other bureaus are ordered to recruit them for service."

entries.zh: 大定二年，戶部郎中曹望之言：「隨處胥吏猥多，乞減其半。」
entries.en: In Dading 2 (1162) Households Vice Director Cao Wangzhi said, "Subordinate clerks everywhere are excessively numerous; I beg to reduce them by half."
entries.literal: In Dading 2 the Households Bureau Vice Director Cao Wangzhi said: "Subordinate clerks everywhere are excessively numerous; I beg to reduce them by half."

entries.zh: 詔胥吏仍舊，但禁用貼書。
entries.en: The court kept clerk numbers unchanged but banned substitute scribes.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that subordinate clerks remain as before, but substitute scribes were forbidden.

entries.zh: 又命縣吏闕，則令推舉行止修舉為鄉里所重者充。
entries.en: County clerk vacancies were to be filled by recommending men of upright conduct respected locally.
entries.literal: It was also ordered that when county clerk posts were vacant, those of upright conduct respected in their communities were to be recommended to fill them.

entries.zh: 三年，以外路司吏久不升轉，往往交通豪右為奸，命與孔目官每三十月則一轉，移於它處。
entries.en: In year 3 (1163) circuit clerks who rarely rotated and colluded with local power brokers were ordered to transfer every thirty months alongside bureau-manager clerks.
entries.literal: In year 3, because circuit clerks long went without promotion and often colluded with powerful families to commit wrongdoing, it was ordered that with bureau-manager clerks they rotate every thirty months and transfer elsewhere.

entries.zh: 七年，敕隨朝司屬吏員通事譯史勾當過雜班月日，如到部者並不理算。
entries.en: In year 7 (1167) mixed-class service days for capital-agency clerks, interpreters, and translators did not count if they had only reached a ministry post.
entries.literal: In year 7 an edict ordered that for capital-agency clerks, interpreters, and translator-scribes who had served mixed-class days, if they had only reached a ministry these were not counted.

entries.zh: 又詔吏人但犯贓罪罷者，雖遇赦，而無特旨，不許複敘。
entries.en: Another edict barred reinstatement of clerks dismissed for corruption even during amnesties unless the throne issued a special order.
entries.literal: Another edict ordered that clerks dismissed for corruption offenses, even if an amnesty occurred, could not be reinstated without a special edict.

entries.zh: 又命京府州縣及轉運司胥吏之數，視其戶口與課之多寡，增減之。
entries.en: Clerk quotas in the capital, counties, and transport commissions were adjusted to household counts and tax yields.
entries.literal: It was also ordered that the numbers of subordinate clerks in the capital prefecture, counties, and transport commissions be increased or decreased according to households and tax yield.

entries.zh: 十二年，上謂宰臣曰：「外路司吏，止論名次上下，恐未得人。
entries.en: In year 12 (1172) the emperor told his ministers, "Ranking circuit clerks only by seniority might miss the best candidates.
entries.literal: In year 12 the emperor told the chief ministers: "Circuit clerks are ranked only by seniority; I fear the right men are not obtained.

entries.zh: 若其下有廉慎、熟閑吏事，委所屬保舉。
entries.en: Superiors were to recommend subordinates who were honest, prudent, and skilled in clerical work.
entries.literal: If among their subordinates there were those who were honest, cautious, and skilled in clerical affairs, let the superiors recommend them.

entries.zh: 試不中程式者，付隨朝近下局分承應，以待再試。
entries.en: Candidates who failed the exam format were posted to lower capital bureaus as attendants until they could retest.
entries.literal: Those who failed the examination format were assigned to lower capital bureaus as attendants, to await re-examination.

entries.zh: 彼既知不得免試，必當盡心以求進也。」
entries.en: Knowing they could not skip the exam, they would strive harder to advance."
entries.literal: Once they knew they could not avoid the examination, they would surely devote themselves fully to advance."

entries.zh: 右職吏員雜選
entries.en: Miscellaneous Selection of Military-Track Officials and Clerks
entries.literal: Miscellaneous Selection of Right-Track Officials and Clerks

entries.zh: 凡吏部選授之制，自太宗天會十二年，始法古立官，至天眷元年，頒新官制。
entries.en: The Ministry of Personnel's selection and appointment system began when Emperor Taizong, in Tianhui 12 (1134), restored offices on ancient models; by Tianjuan 1 (1138) a new official structure was issued.
entries.literal: As for the Ministry of Personnel's system of selection and appointment, from Emperor Taizong's twelfth year of Tianhui it began to model antiquity in establishing offices, and by the first year of Tianjuan a new official system was promulgated.

entries.zh: 及天德四年，始以河南、北選人並赴中京，吏部各置局銓注。
entries.en: In Tiande 4 (1152) candidates from the Henan and Hebei circuits were first required to report together at Zhongjing, where the Ministry of Personnel set up separate bureaus for certification and registration.
entries.literal: By the fourth year of Tiande, candidates from Henan and Hebei were first gathered together at the Central Capital, and the Ministry of Personnel established separate bureaus to review and register appointments.

entries.zh: 又命吏部尚書蕭賾定河南、北官通注格，以諸司橫班大解、並大將軍合注差人，依年例一就銓注，餘求仕人分四季擬授，遂為定制。
entries.en: Minister of Personnel Xiao Ze was also ordered to set unified registration rules for the Henan and Hebei circuits. Holders of horizontal-rank grand release from various agencies and eligible grand generals were certified in one annual batch; other office-seekers received seasonal draft appointments, and this became standard practice.
entries.literal: The Ministry of Personnel Director Xiao Ze was also ordered to fix the general registration regulations for Henan and Hebei offices; persons with horizontal-rank grand release from various agencies and grand generals eligible for joint registration were all reviewed and registered at once according to annual precedent, while remaining office-seekers received draft appointments in four seasons—this became the standing rule.

entries.zh: 貞元二年，命擬注時，依舊令，求仕官明數謂面授也，不許就本鄉，若衰病年老者毋授繁劇處。
entries.en: In Zhenyuan 2 (1154), draft nominations were again governed by the old rule that candidates declare their numbers for in-person assignment and could not take posts in their home districts; the frail, sick, or elderly were barred from demanding assignments.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, when drafting nominations it was ordered that under the old statutes office-seekers must state their numbers—meaning face-to-face appointment—and were not permitted to take posts in their home districts; if feeble, ill, or elderly, they were not to be given demanding posts.

entries.zh: 宣宗貞祐二年，以播越流離，官職多闕，權命河朔諸道宣撫司得擬七品以下，尋以所注吏部不知，季放之闕多至重複，乃奏罷之。
entries.en: In Zhenyou 2 (1214) under Emperor Xuanzong, with the court displaced and offices widely vacant, pacification commissions on the Hebei frontier were temporarily allowed to draft appointments through the seventh rank; because the Ministry of Personnel was not informed, seasonal vacancy lists soon duplicated, and the arrangement was abolished on memorial.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou under Emperor Xuanzong, because of displacement and wandering, many offices stood vacant; it was provisionally ordered that the pacification commissions of the Hebei circuits might draft appointments for the seventh rank and below; soon because the appointments were unknown to the Ministry of Personnel, seasonal releases of vacancies often reached duplication, and memorial was made to abolish this.

entries.zh: 時李英言：「兵興以來，百務煩冗，政在用人，舊雖有四善、十七最之法，而拔擢蔑聞，幾為徒設。
entries.en: At that time Li Ying said, "Since the wars began, affairs have multiplied and good government depends on appointing the right men. The old rules of four excellences and seventeen superlatives are barely used for promotion and have become nearly meaningless.
entries.literal: At that time Li Ying said: "Since warfare arose, the hundred affairs have been numerous and burdensome; governance lies in employing men. Although there were formerly the methods of four excellences and seventeen superlatives, promotion and advancement have scarcely been heard of—they have nearly become empty provisions.

entries.zh: 大定間，以監察御史及審錄官分詣諸路，考核以擬，號為得人，可依已試之效，庶幾使人自勵。」
entries.en: During the Dading era, censorial investigators and review officials toured the circuits to assess officials and draft nominations, with good results; that tested method should be revived so that men will strive to excel."
entries.literal: During Dading, censorial investigators and review-recording officials were sent separately to the various circuits to assess and draft nominations, acclaimed as obtaining the right men; one may rely on effects already tested, so that perhaps men will encourage themselves."

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: An edict approved.
entries.literal: An edict assented.

entries.zh: 三年，戶部郎中奧屯阿虎言：「諸色遷官並與女直一體，而有司不奉，妄生分別，以至上下相疑。」
entries.en: In the third year, Ministry of Revenue Director Aotun Ahu said, "Officials of every background should be treated like Jurchens when transferring posts, but the responsible offices ignore this, invent distinctions, and breed mutual suspicion."
entries.literal: In the third year, Households Bureau Director Aotun Ahu said: "Officials of all categories transferring posts are uniformly treated the same as Jurchens, yet the responsible offices do not comply and arbitrarily create distinctions, so that superiors and subordinates come to suspect one another."

entries.zh: 詔以違制禁之。
entries.en: An edict forbade the practice as a violation of regulations.
entries.literal: An edict forbade this as violation of regulations.

entries.zh: 初，宣宗之南遷也，詔吏部以秋冬于南京、春夏於中都置選，而赴調者憚於北行，率皆南來，遂並于南京設之。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuanzong moved south, the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to hold selection at Nanjing in autumn and winter and at Zhongdu in spring and summer; candidates feared traveling north and mostly reported to Nanjing, so selection was consolidated there.
entries.literal: Initially, when Emperor Xuanzong moved south, the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to hold selection in Nanjing in autumn and winter and at the Central Capital in spring and summer; but those reporting for assignment feared traveling north and mostly all came south, so selection was combined and established at Nanjing.

entries.zh: 三月，命汰不勝官者，令五品以上官公舉，今季赴部人內，先擇材幹者量緩急易之。
entries.en: In the third month, incompetent officials were ordered removed; fifth-rank officials and above were to recommend replacements publicly; among this season's candidates at the ministry, capable men were to be chosen first and assigned according to urgency.
entries.literal: In the third month, incompetent officials were ordered eliminated; officials of the fifth rank and above were to recommend publicly; among those arriving at the ministry this season, first select capable men and exchange them according to urgency.

entries.zh: 興定元年，詔有司議減冗員。
entries.en: In Xingding 1 (1217) the responsible offices were ordered to discuss cutting redundant posts.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xingding, the responsible offices were ordered to discuss reducing redundant personnel.

entries.zh: 又詔，自今吏部每季銓選，差女直、漢人監察各一員監視，又盡罷前犯罪降除截罷、及承應未滿解去而複為隨處官司委使者。
entries.en: Another edict required that each seasonal ministry selection be supervised by one Jurchen and one Han inspector, and abolished officials previously demoted or dismissed for crimes, as well as attendants who left before completing their terms yet were again commissioned by local offices.
entries.literal: Another edict [stated that] from now on at each season's selection and review by the Ministry of Personnel, one Jurchen and one Han inspector were to be dispatched to supervise; also completely abolish those previously demoted or dismissed for crimes, and attendants who left before completing their term yet again became agents commissioned by local offices everywhere.

entries.zh: 又定制，權依劇縣例俱作正七品，令隨朝七品、外路六品以上職事官，舉正七品以下職事官年未六十無公私罪堪任使者，歲一人，仍令兼領樞密院彈壓之職，以鎮軍人。
entries.en: Another rule, following demanding-county precedent, treated the posts as proper seventh rank; capital seventh-rank and outer-circuit sixth-rank functional officials were to recommend proper seventh-rank and below officials under sixty without offenses, one per year, who would also hold Privy Council authority to suppress disturbances and control troops.
entries.literal: Another standing rule provisionally followed the precedent of demanding counties, all treated as proper seventh rank; capital-attached seventh-rank and outer-circuit sixth-rank and above functional officials were to recommend functional officials of the proper seventh rank and below, under sixty years of age, without public or private offenses, capable of service—one per year—who were also to hold concurrently the Privy Council post of suppressing disturbances, to restrain soldiers.

entries.zh: 凡上司不得差占及淩辱決罰。
entries.en: Superiors could not requisition them or insult and punish them arbitrarily.
entries.literal: In general superiors might not requisition them or insult and punish them by decision.

entries.zh: 到任半年，委巡按官體訪具申籍記。
entries.en: After six months in office, touring inspectors investigated and filed full reports for the registry.
entries.literal: After half a year in office, touring inspectors were commissioned to investigate and report fully for registry.

entries.zh: 又半年覆察，考滿日分等升用。
entries.en: After another six months they were reinspected, and at term's end were promoted by grade.
entries.literal: After another half year they were re-inspected; on completion of the review term they were promoted in graded use.

entries.zh: 如六事備為上等，升職一等，四事為中等，減二資歷，其次下等減一資歷，不稱者截罷。
entries.en: If all six criteria were met, upper grade meant promotion one rank; four criteria meant middle grade and reduction of two seniority steps; the next lower grade meant one seniority step down; the unfit were dismissed outright.
entries.literal: If all six matters were complete, upper grade—promote one rank in office; four matters, middle grade—reduce two seniority grades; next, lower grade—reduce one seniority grade; if unfit, dismiss outright.

entries.zh: 右景祖子，與世祖、肅宗、穆宗凡九人。
entries.en: Listed at right: sons of the Illustrious Ancestor—nine men, counting Shizu, Suzong, and Muzong.
entries.literal: At right: sons of the Illustrious Ancestor—nine in all, with Shizu, Suzong, and Muzong.

entries.zh: 冶訶、魯補稱係出景祖，不稱誰子，不可以世，置之卷末。
entries.en: Yehe and Lubu are called collateral kin of the Illustrious Ancestor; neither is named as any man's son; their generations cannot be fixed, so both are placed at the scroll's end.
entries.literal: Yehe and Lubu are styled as collateral issue of the Illustrious Ancestor; neither is entered as anyone's son; they cannot be placed by generation and are set at the end of the scroll.

entries.zh: 右始祖子，與德帝凡二人。
entries.en: Listed at right: sons of the First Ancestor—two men, counting the Virtuous Emperor.
entries.literal: At right: sons of the First Ancestor—two in all, with the Virtuous Emperor.

entries.zh: 右世祖子，與康宗、太祖、太宗凡十一人。
entries.en: Listed at right: sons of Shizu—eleven men, counting Kangzong, Taizu, and Taizong.
entries.literal: At right: sons of Shizu—eleven in all, with Kangzong, Taizu, and Taizong.

entries.zh: 古者太史掌敘邦國之世次，辨其姓氏，別其昭穆，尚失。
entries.en: Even in ancient times the Grand Historian who ordered the ages of the realms, sorted clan names, and marked senior from junior lines could not keep the record whole.
entries.literal: In antiquity the Grand Historian kept the generations of the states, distinguished their surnames, and separated zhao from mu—and still there were lapses.

entries.zh: 金人初起完毅十二部，其後皆以部為氏，史臣記錄有稱「宗室」者，有稱完顏者。
entries.en: The Jin first gathered in the twelve Wanyi tribes, then took each tribe as a clan name. Court historians sometimes wrote "Imperial Clan", sometimes Wanyan.
entries.literal: When the Jin people first arose in the twelve tribes of Wanyi, afterward all took their tribe as surname; in the historians' records some are called "Imperial Clan", some Wanyan.

entries.zh: 稱完顏者。
entries.en: As for those called Wanyan:
entries.literal: Those called Wanyan.

entries.zh: 稱完顏者亦有二焉，有同姓完顏，蓋疏族，若石土門、迪古乃是也；
entries.en: "Wanyan" itself split two ways: same-surname Wanyan were really distant kin, men like Shitumen and Digunai;
entries.literal: Those called Wanyan also fall into two kinds: same-surname Wanyan, who were in fact collateral kin—Shitumen and Digunai are examples;

entries.zh: 有異姓完顏，蓋部人，若歡都是也。
entries.en: different-surname Wanyan were really tribesmen, men like Huandu.
entries.literal: and different-surname Wanyan, who were in fact men of the tribe—Huandu is an example.

entries.zh: 大定以前稱「宗室」，明昌以後避睿宗諱稱「內族」，其實一而已，書名不書氏，其制如此。
entries.en: Before Dading they were called "Imperial Clan"; after Mingchang, to avoid the taboo on Ruizong, "Inner Kin"—the same group in fact. Registers record personal names, not clan names; that was the rule.
entries.literal: Before the Dading era they were called "Imperial Clan"; after Mingchang, to avoid the taboo on Ruizong they were called "Inner Kin"—in substance one and the same. The annals give personal names, not clan names; such was the rule.

entries.zh: 宣宗詔宗室皆稱完顏，不復識別焉。
entries.en: Emperor Xuanzong ordered that all imperial kin take the name Wanyan, and the old distinctions ceased.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuanzong decreed that all of the imperial clan should be called Wanyan, and no further distinction was made.

entries.zh: 大定、泰和之間，袒免以上親皆有屬籍，以敘授官，大功以上，薨卒輟朝，親親之道行焉。
entries.en: From Dading through Taihe, relatives within tan-mian degree and nearer were entered in the clan rolls and ranked for appointment; when one within da-gong degree or nearer died, court paused in mourning—kinship was honored in deed.
entries.literal: Between Dading and Taihe, kin within the degree of tan-mian mourning and closer all had household registers, by which offices were assigned; for kin within the degree of da-gong mourning and closer, death halted court audiences—the way of cherishing kin was practiced.

entries.zh: 貞祐以後，譜牒散失，大概僅存，不可殫悉，今掇其可次第者著於篇。
entries.en: After Zhenyou the pedigree books were lost; a broken outline alone remains, too fragmentary to exhaust. Here I collect what can still be sequenced and place it in these pages.
entries.literal: After Zhenyou the genealogical registers were scattered and lost; only a rough outline survives, and it cannot be set forth in full. Now I gather what can be ordered by generation and set it down in this chapter.

entries.zh: 其上無所系、下無所承者，不能盡錄也。
entries.en: Lines that attach to nothing above and hand down to nothing below cannot be entered in full.
entries.literal: Those with no tie above and no succession below cannot all be recorded.

entries.zh: 元（本名常勝。胙王。）

entries.literal: Yuan (born Changsheng; Prince of Zuo).

entries.en: Listed at right: sons of Ruizong—two in all, with Shizong.
entries.literal: At right: sons of Ruizong—two in all, with Shizong.

entries.en: Listed at right: sons of Shizong—with Xianzong and Wei Shaowang, ten in all.
entries.literal: At right: sons of Shizong—with Xianzong and Wei Shaowang, ten in all.

entries.literal: Sagai (Guolun Hulu bojilie, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery).

entries.literal: Keng (Imperial Grandson; posthumous title Chonghuai).

entries.literal: Agunai (elder brother of the First Ancestor).

entries.zh: 不知世次
entries.en: Generation not known.
entries.literal: Generation not known.

entries.literal: Tabuye (Liao Grand Commandant).

entries.en: Hushimen (Flying Cavalry General-in-Chief).
entries.literal: Hushimen (Flying Cavalry General-in-Chief).

entries.zh: 鉤室
entries.en: Goushi.
entries.literal: Goushi.

entries.zh: 歡都，劾孫子。
entries.en: Huandu was Hesun's son.
entries.literal: Huandu was Hesun's son.

entries.zh: 世祖初，襲節度使。
entries.en: When Shizu first came to power, Huandu inherited the post of military governor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shizu's reign he inherited the office of military governor.

entries.zh: 而跋黑以屬尊，蓄異謀，不可制。
entries.en: Bahei, however, stood high in the lineage and nursed designs of his own; he could not be brought to heel.
entries.literal: But Bahei, by reason of senior kinship, harbored other designs and could not be controlled.

entries.zh: 諸部不肯受約束，相繼為變。
entries.en: Tribe after tribe refused obedience and rose in revolt.
entries.literal: The tribes would not accept restraint and rose in rebellion one after another.

entries.zh: 歡都入與謀議，出臨戰陣，未嘗去左右。
entries.en: Huandu came in to counsel and went out to command on the field; he never left Shizu's side.
entries.literal: Huandu went in to counsel on plans and went out to face the battle lines, never leaving Shizu's side.

entries.zh: 斡勒部人杯乃，自景祖時與其兄弟俱居安出虎水之北，及烏春作難，杯乃將與烏春合，間誘斡魯紺出水居人與之相結，欲先除去歡都。
entries.en: Beinai of the Wole clan had lived with his brothers north of the Anchu River since Jingzu's day. When Wuchun rebelled, Beinai was ready to join him and secretly won over the Woluguan water-folk, intending to destroy Huandu first.
entries.literal: Beinai of the Wole tribe, since Jingzu's time he and his brothers had all dwelt north of the Anchu River; when Wuchun made trouble, Beinai was about to join Wuchun and between whiles enticed the water-dwellers of Woluguan to link with him, wishing first to remove Huandu.

entries.zh: 會其家被火，陰約隸人不歌束，詭稱放火乃歡都、胡土二人，使注都來謂世祖曰：「不歌束來告曰'前日之火，歡都等縱之'。
entries.en: When his house burned, he secretly suborned the bondservant Bugesou to claim that Huandu and Hutu had set the blaze, and sent Zhudu to Shizu with the message: "Bugesou reports that the fire the other day was the work of Huandu and his party.
entries.literal: When his house caught fire, he secretly arranged with the bondservant Bugesou, falsely claiming the arsonists were Huandu and Hutu, and sent Zhudu to tell Shizu: "Bugesou comes to report that the fire of the other day was set by Huandu and the rest.

entries.zh: 若不棄舊好，其執縱火之人以來。」
entries.en: If you will not break the old bond of friendship, seize the arsonists and deliver them."
entries.literal: If you do not abandon the old friendship, seize those who set the fire and bring them."

entries.zh: 世祖疑之。
entries.en: Shizu was doubtful.
entries.literal: Shizu was suspicious.

entries.zh: 石盧斡勒勃堇曰：「杯乃兄弟也，豈以一二人之故，而與兄弟構怨乎。
entries.en: The Wole tribal chief Shilu Wole said: "Beinai is your brother. Would you for the sake of one or two men make an enemy of your own kin?
entries.literal: The tribal chief Shilu Wole said: "Beinai is your brother—would you for one or two men bear enmity against a brother?

entries.zh: 彼自取之，又將尤誰，不如與之便。」
entries.en: He brought this on himself. Whom else can he blame? Better to give way to him."
entries.literal: He brought it on himself—against whom will he complain? Better to yield to him."

entries.zh: 歡都被甲執戟而起曰：「彼為亂之人也，若取太師兄弟，則亦與之乎。
entries.en: Huandu buckled on armor, seized his halberd, and rose. "He is a rebel. If they demand the Grand Preceptor's brothers, will you surrender them as well?
entries.literal: Huandu donned armor, took up his halberd, and rose, saying: "He is a man of disorder. If they take the Grand Preceptor's brothers, will you hand them over too?

entries.zh: 今取我輩，我輩決不可往，若必用戰，當盡力致死。」
entries.en: If they demand us, we will never go. If it must come to war, we shall fight to the last man."
entries.literal: If they take us now, we absolutely will not go. If battle is necessary, we shall fight to the death."

entries.zh: 穆宗曰：「壯哉歡都，以我所見，正如此爾。」
entries.en: Muzong said: "How bold Huandu is! In my judgment he is entirely right."
entries.literal: Muzong said: "How stalwart is Huandu! From what I see, it is exactly so."

entries.zh: 贈歡都以馬，曰：「戰則乘此。」
entries.en: He gave Huandu a horse and said: "When you fight, ride this one."
entries.literal: He gifted Huandu a horse, saying: "In battle ride this."

entries.zh: 眾皆稱善。
entries.en: All approved.
entries.literal: All praised the decision.

entries.zh: 世祖乃往見杯乃，隔鱉刺水而與之言曰：「不歌束既告縱火由歡都等，謹當如約。
entries.en: Shizu then went to Beinai and, standing across the Biecih River, said: "Bugesou has named Huandu and the rest as the arsonists. I shall keep our agreement to the letter.
entries.literal: Shizu then went to see Beinai, and across the Biecih River spoke to him: "Since Bugesou has reported that the arson was by Huandu and the others, I shall strictly keep the agreement.

entries.zh: 當先遣不歌束來。」
entries.en: Send Bugesou to me first."
entries.literal: Bugesou must be sent first."

entries.zh: 不歌束至，世祖于馬前殺之，使杯乃見之。
entries.en: When Bugesou came, Shizu struck him down before his horse and made Beinai witness it.
entries.literal: When Bugesou arrived, Shizu killed him before his horse and had Beinai see it.

entries.zh: 既而聞之，放火者杯乃家人阿出胡山也，杯乃欲開此釁，故以誣歡都雲。
entries.en: It later came out that the fire had been set by Beinai's servant Achuhushan. Beinai had sought a pretext for strife and had framed Huandu.
entries.literal: Later it was learned that the one who set the fire was Beinai's household servant Achuhushan; Beinai wished to open this quarrel and therefore falsely accused Huandu.

entries.zh: 歡都事四君，出入四十年，征伐之際遇敵則先戰，廣廷大議多用其謀。
entries.en: Huandu served four sovereigns across forty years. In battle he always met the enemy first; in great council his counsel was often followed.
entries.literal: Huandu served four rulers, coming and going for forty years; on campaigns when he met the enemy he fought first; in broad court deliberations his counsel was often used.

entries.zh: 世祖嘗曰：「吾有歡都，則何事不成。」
entries.en: Shizu once said: "With Huandu at my side, what could I not accomplish?"
entries.literal: Shizu once said: "With Huandu at my side, what affair could fail?"

entries.zh: 肅宗時，委任冠於近僚。
entries.en: Under Suzong his trust outranked every courtier near the throne.
entries.literal: Under Suzong his commission ranked above the close attendants.

entries.zh: 穆宗嗣位，凡圖遼事皆專委之。
entries.en: When Muzong came to the throne, every matter touching Liao was placed solely in his hands.
entries.literal: When Muzong succeeded, all affairs concerning Liao were entrusted to him alone.

entries.zh: 康宗以為父叔舊人，尤加敬禮，多所補益。
entries.en: Kangzong treated him as a veteran of his father and uncles' generation, honored him the more, and drew great profit from his service.
entries.literal: Kangzong regarded him as an old companion of his father and uncles and showed him especial respect and courtesy, benefiting greatly from him.

entries.zh: 臘醅、麻產與世祖遇于野鵲水。
entries.en: Lapei and Machan met Shizu at the Wild Magpie River.
entries.literal: Lapei and Machan encountered Shizu at the Wild Magpie River.

entries.zh: 日已曛，惟從五六十騎，歡都入敵陣鏖擊之，左右出入者數四，世祖中創乃止。
entries.en: Dusk had fallen and Shizu had barely fifty or sixty riders. Huandu plunged into the enemy line and fought back and forth four times over before Shizu, wounded, called a halt.
entries.literal: The sun had set; Shizu had only fifty or sixty horsemen with him; Huandu charged into the enemy ranks and fought fiercely, going in and out several times; Shizu was wounded and only then did they stop.

entries.zh: 烏春、窩謀罕據活刺渾水，世祖既許之降，遂還軍。
entries.en: Wuchun and Womouhan held the Huocihun River. Shizu had already accepted their surrender and marched his army home.
entries.literal: Wuchun and Womouhan held the Huocihun River; Shizu had already promised them submission and therefore withdrew the army.

entries.zh: 於是騷臘勃堇、富者撻懶歡勝負不助軍，而騷臘、撻懶先曾與臘醅、麻產合，世祖欲因軍還而遂滅之，馳馬前進。
entries.en: The tribal chiefs Saola and Fuzhe Talan watched to see which side would win and withheld their support. Both had previously joined Lapei and Machan, so Shizu meant to destroy them on the march home and spurred his horse forward.
entries.literal: Thereupon the tribal chiefs Saola and Fuzhe Talan watched the outcome and did not aid the army. Saola and Talan had earlier joined with Lapei and Machan, so Shizu wished to destroy them on the army's return and spurred his horse forward.

entries.zh: 撻懶者，貞惠皇后之弟也。
entries.en: Talan was Empress Zhenhui's younger brother.
entries.literal: Talan was the younger brother of Empress Zhenhui.

entries.zh: 歡都下馬執轡而諫曰：「獨不念愛弟蒲陽溫與弟婦乎。」
entries.en: Huandu dismounted, seized the bridle, and pleaded: "Have you no thought for your beloved younger brother Puyangwen and his wife?"
entries.literal: Huandu dismounted, took the reins, and remonstrated: "Will you not think of your beloved younger brother Puyangwen and your younger brother's wife?"

entries.zh: 世祖感其言，遂止。
entries.en: Shizu was moved and drew rein.
entries.literal: Shizu was moved by his words and stopped.

entries.zh: 蒲陽溫者，漢語雲幼弟也。
entries.en: Puyangwen is the Jurchen name for "younger brother" in Chinese.
entries.literal: Puyangwen, in Chinese, means "younger brother."

entries.zh: 世祖母弟中穆宗最少，故雲然。
entries.en: Of Shizu's maternal brothers Muzong was the youngest, and so earned that name.
entries.literal: Among Shizu's maternal younger brothers Muzong was the youngest, and therefore he was so called.

entries.zh: 穆宗德歡都言，後以撻懶女曷羅哂妻其子谷神。
entries.en: Muzong remembered Huandu's counsel and later arranged for Talan's daughter Heluoshen to marry Huandu's son Gushen.
entries.literal: Muzong was grateful for Huandu's words; later he gave Talan's daughter Heluoshen in marriage to Huandu's son Gushen.

entries.zh: 太祖追麻產，歡都射中其首，遂獲之。
entries.en: When Taizu pursued Machan, Huandu struck him in the head with an arrow and took him prisoner.
entries.literal: Taizu pursued Machan; Huandu shot him in the head and he was captured.

entries.zh: 遼人命穆宗、太祖、辭不失、歡都俱為詳穩。
entries.en: Liao appointed Muzong, Taizu, Cibushi, and Huandu each to the office of xiangwen.
entries.literal: The Liao appointed Muzong, Taizu, Cibushi, and Huandu all as xiangwen.

entries.zh: 肅宗拒桓赧已再失利，世祖命歡都、冶訶，以本部謀克之兵助之。
entries.en: Suzong had twice been beaten by Huanhan. Shizu sent Huandu and Yehe with the commandery levies of their tribes to reinforce him.
entries.literal: Suzong in resisting Huanhan had already suffered defeat twice; Shizu ordered Huandu and Yehe to assist him with the commandery troops of their own tribes.

entries.zh: 冶訶與歡都常在世祖左右，居則與謀議，出則泣行陣，未嘗不在其間。
entries.en: Yehe and Huandu were always at Shizu's side, joining his councils in camp and taking their places in the battle line in the field. They were never absent from his affairs.
entries.literal: Yehe and Huandu were constantly at Shizu's side; at home they joined his deliberations, and in the field they took their places in the battle line, never absent from his affairs.

entries.zh: 天會十五年，贈銀青光祿大夫。
entries.en: In Tianhui 15 he was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver-Green Tally.
entries.literal: In Tianhui year 15 he was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver-Green Tally.

entries.zh: 明昌五年，贈特進，諡忠濟，與代國公歡都、特進劾者、開府儀同三司盆納、儀同三司拔達，俱配享世祖廟廷。
entries.en: In Mingchang 5 he was raised to Special Advancement with the posthumous name Zhongji, Loyal and Succoring, and together with Duke of Dai Huandu, Special Advancement Hezhe, Grand Master of the Palace Penna, and Bearer of the Triple Staff Bada was granted collateral sacrifice in Shizu's temple.
entries.literal: In Mingchang year 5 he was further enfeoffed as Special Advancement with the posthumous title Zhongji, "Loyal and Succoring," and together with Duke of Dai Huandu, Special Advancement Hezhe, Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Protocol Penna, and Bearer of the Triple Staff with Equal Protocol Bada, all received collateral sacrifice in Shizu's temple hall.

entries.zh: 贊曰：賢石魯與昭祖為友，歡都事景祖、世祖為之臣。
entries.en: The encomium reads: Virtuous Shilu was friend to Zhaozu; Huandu served Jingzu and Shizu as minister.
entries.literal: The encomium says: Virtuous Shilu was Zhaozu's friend; Huandu served Jingzu and Shizu as their minister.

entries.zh: 蓋金自景祖始大，諸部君臣之分始定，故傳異姓之臣，以歡都為首。
entries.en: From Jingzu's day Jin began its rise, and the lord-and-minister order among the tribes was first fixed. Hence among ministers of other surnames Huandu leads the roll.
entries.literal: Jin from Jingzu's time began to grow great, and the distinction between lord and minister among the tribes was first fixed; therefore in biographies of ministers of other surnames, Huandu stands first.

entries.zh: 冶訶雖宗室，與歡都同功，故列敘焉。
entries.en: Yehe, though of the imperial house, shared Huandu's merit, and is therefore set down here beside him.
entries.literal: Yehe, though of the imperial clan, shared merit with Huandu; therefore he is narrated here as well.

entries.zh: 斡善、斡脫以姑裏甸兵來歸，使斜缽勃堇撫定之。
entries.en: Woshan and Wotuo brought the Guli contingent in submission, and Shizu sent the tribal chief Xiebo to settle them.
entries.literal: Woshan and Wotuo brought the Guli troops to submit; Shizu sent the tribal chief Xiebo to pacify and settle them.

entries.zh: 蒲察部故石、拔石等，誘其眾入城，陷三百餘人。
entries.en: Gushi, Bashi, and others of the Pucha tribe lured the troops into a city and trapped more than three hundred men.
entries.literal: Gushi, Bashi, and others of the Pucha tribe enticed their forces into the city and trapped more than three hundred men.

entries.zh: 歡都為都統，往治斜缽失軍之狀，盡解斜缽所將軍、大破烏春、窩謀罕於斜堆，擒故石、拔石。
entries.en: Huandu was made commander-in-chief and sent to investigate Xiebo's loss of the force. He relieved Xiebo of his entire command, crushed Wuchun and Womouhan at Xiedui, and captured Gushi and Bashi.
entries.literal: Huandu served as commander-in-chief, investigated the circumstances of Xiebo's loss of the force, removed all the troops from Xiebo's command, routed Wuchun and Womouhan at Xiedui, and captured Gushi and Bashi.

entries.zh: 齊國建，阿魯補屯兵於汴城外。
entries.en: When the Qi puppet state was set up, Alubu encamped his troops outside Bian.
entries.literal: When the Qi state was established, Alubu garrisoned troops outside the walls of Bian.

entries.zh: 天會十五年，詔廢齊國，已執劉麟，阿魯補先入汴京備變。
entries.en: In Tianhui 15 an edict abolished Qi. Liu Lin was already in custody, and Alubu entered Bianjing first to guard against trouble.
entries.literal: In Tianhui year 15 an edict abolished the Qi state; Liu Lin had already been seized; Alubu entered Bianjing first to guard against disturbance.

entries.zh: 明年，除歸德尹。
entries.en: The following year he was appointed prefect of Guide.
entries.literal: The following year he was made prefect of Guide.

entries.zh: 割河南地與宋，入為燕京內省使。
entries.en: When the lands south of the river were ceded to Song, he entered service as Inner Secretariat envoy at Yanjing.
entries.literal: When the lands south of the river were ceded to Song, he entered the capital as Inner Secretariat envoy of Yanjing.

entries.zh: 宗弼複河南，阿魯補先濟河，撫定諸郡，再為歸德尹、河南路都統。
entries.en: When Zongbi recovered the south, Alubu crossed the river first, pacified the prefectures, and again became prefect of Guide and commander-in-chief of Henan.
entries.literal: When Zongbi recovered the lands south of the river, Alubu crossed the river first, pacified and settled the prefectures, and again became prefect of Guide and commander-in-chief of the Henan circuit.

entries.zh: 宋兵來取河南地，宗弼召阿魯補，與許州韓常、潁州大臭、陳州赤盞暉、皆會于汴，阿魯補以敵在近，獨不赴。
entries.en: Song troops came to recover the south. Zongbi summoned Alubu, Han Chang of Xuzhou, Dachou of Yingzhou, and Chisan Hui of Chenzhou to assemble at Bian. Alubu alone stayed away, for the enemy was at his gates.
entries.literal: Song troops came to recover the lands south of the river; Zongbi summoned Alubu, Han Chang of Xuzhou, Dachou of Yingzhou, and Chisan Hui of Chenzhou to assemble at Bian; Alubu, because the enemy was near, alone did not go.

entries.zh: 而宋將岳飛、劉光世等，果乘間襲取許潁三州，旁郡皆回應。
entries.en: Song generals Yue Fei, Liu Guangshi, and others did seize the moment, took Xu, Ying, and Chen, and neighboring districts rose in support.
entries.literal: Song generals Yue Fei, Liu Guangshi, and others indeed seized the opportunity to strike and take the three prefectures of Xu, Ying, and Chen; neighboring commanderies all responded in turn.

entries.zh: 其兵犯歸德者，阿魯補連擊敗之，複取亳、宿等州，河南平，阿魯補功最。
entries.en: The columns that threatened Guide he beat back again and again, retook Bo, Su, and other prefectures, and pacified the south—no man's service surpassed his.
entries.literal: Those of their troops that invaded Guide, Alubu repeatedly defeated; he recovered Bo, Su, and other prefectures; the south was pacified, and Alubu's merit was greatest.

entries.zh: 列傳第六 ○歡都子 謀演 冶訶子 阿魯補 骨赧 訛古乃 蒲查
entries.en: Biographies 6: Huandu and his son Mouyan; Yehe and his sons Alubu, Gunan, and Egunai; Sanda's son Pucha
entries.literal: Biographies 6: Huandu and his son Mouyan; Yehe and his sons Alubu, Gunan, and Egunai; Sanda's son Pucha

entries.zh: 列傳第七 太祖諸子 宗雋本名訛魯觀 宗傑本名沒里野 宗強本名阿魯，子 爽
entries.en: Biography 7. Sons of Taizu: Zong Juan, born Eluguan; Zong Jie, born Meiliye; Zong Qiang, born Alu—and Shuang his son.
entries.literal: Biography 7: Sons of the Taizu—Zong Juan (born Eluguan), Zong Jie (born Meiliye), Zong Qiang (born Alu); his son Shuang

entries.zh: （本名阿鄰）
entries.en: (born Alin)
entries.literal: (born Alin)

entries.zh: 可喜 阿瑣 宗敏本名阿魯補 元宗峻子，本名常勝
entries.en: Kexi, A Suo, Zong Min (born Alubu); Yuan, son of Zong Jun, born Changsheng.
entries.literal: Kexi, A Suo, Zong Min (born Alubu); Yuan, son of Zong Jun, born Changsheng.

entries.zh: 胙王元，景宣皇帝峻子也，本名常勝，為北京留守，弟查刺為安武軍節度使。
entries.en: Yuan, Prince of Zu, son of the Jingxuan Emperor Jun, was born Changsheng. He served as regent at the Northern Capital; his brother Chaci was military commissioner of the Anwu Army.
