entries.literal: Yuan, Prince of Zu, was a son of the Jingxuan Emperor Jun; his original name was Changsheng. He was Northern Capital regent; his younger brother Chaci was military commissioner of the Anwu Army.

entries.zh: 元子育，本名合住，大定二十七年，自南京副留守遷大宗正丞，兼勸農副使。
entries.en: Yuan’s son Yu, born Hezhu: in Dading year 27 he went from deputy regent at the Southern Capital to Grand Director of the Imperial Clan and Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture.
entries.literal: Yuan’s son Yu, original name Hezhu—in the twenty-seventh year of Dading he moved from deputy regent of the Southern Capital to Grand Director of the Imperial Clan, and concurrently Vice Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture.

entries.zh: 上問宰臣曰：「合住為人如何？」
entries.en: The emperor asked his chief ministers: "What manner of man is Hezhu?"
entries.literal: The emperor asked the chief ministers: "What sort of man is Hezhu?"

entries.zh: 平章政事襄、參政宗浩對曰：「為人清廉幹治。」
entries.en: Grand Councilor Xiang and Vice Councilor Zonghao answered: "Upright, frugal, and able in office."
entries.literal: Grand Councilor Xiang and Vice Councilor Zonghao replied: "In conduct he is clean, honest, and capable in administration."

entries.zh: 上曰：「乃父亦然。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "His father was the same."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "His father was likewise."

entries.zh: 又曰：「蒲陽溫胙王元，外若愚訥，臨事明敏過人。
entries.en: He went on: "Puyangwen—Prince of Zu Yuan—seemed slow and tongue-tied, yet in business he outshone everyone.
entries.literal: He added: "Puyangwen, Prince of Zu Yuan—outwardly dull and slow of speech, yet in affairs keener than other men.

entries.zh: 朕于兄弟間，于元尤款密。」
entries.en: Of all my brothers, none was dearer to me than Yuan."
entries.literal: Among my brothers, toward Yuan I was especially close and intimate."

entries.zh: 河南軍士孫進自稱「皇弟按察大王」，熙宗疑「皇弟」二字或在常勝也，使特思鞫之，無狀。
entries.en: Sun Jin, a soldier in Henan, called himself "Younger Brother, Inspector King." Xizong wondered whether "younger brother" meant Changsheng and set Tesi to question him; nothing was proved.
entries.literal: A soldier of the Henan army, Sun Jin, styled himself "Younger Brother, Inspector King"; Xizong suspected the words "younger brother" might point to Changsheng, and had Tesi interrogate him—no proof emerged.

entries.zh: 特思乃嘗疑海陵與唐括辯時時竊議，告之悼後者。
entries.en: Tesi had long suspected Hailing and Tangguo Bian of meeting in secret, and had told Empress Dowager Dao.
entries.literal: Tesi had once suspected that Hailing and Tangguo Bian from time to time met in secret counsel, and reported this to Empress Dowager Dao.

entries.zh: 海陵知熙宗有疑常勝心，因此可以除之，謂熙宗曰：「孫進反有端，不稱他人，乃稱皇弟大王。
entries.en: Hailing saw that Xizong already doubted Changsheng and that here was his chance. He told Xizong: "Sun Jin’s revolt has a thread to pull—he named no one else but Younger Brother the King.
entries.literal: Hailing knew Xizong already doubted Changsheng, and that by this he could remove him; he said to Xizong: "Sun Jin’s rebellion has a basis—he named no other man, only Younger Brother the King.

entries.zh: 陛下弟止有常勝、查刺。
entries.en: Your Majesty has only two brothers—Changsheng and Chaci.
entries.literal: Your Majesty’s brothers are only Changsheng and Chaci.

entries.zh: 特思鞫不以實，故出之矣。」
entries.en: Tesi’s inquiry did not get at the truth, and so he was let go."
entries.literal: Tesi’s interrogation did not bring out the truth, and so he was released."

entries.zh: 熙宗以為然，使唐括辯、蕭肄按問特思，特思自誣服，故出常勝罪。
entries.en: Xizong agreed and set Tangguo Bian and Xiao Yi to press Tesi; Tesi confessed under torture, and Changsheng was condemned.
entries.literal: Xizong thought it so, and had Tangguo Bian and Xiao Yi examine and question Tesi; Tesi falsely confessed, and thus the charge against Changsheng was established.

entries.zh: 於是，乃殺常勝及其弟查刺，並殺特思。
entries.en: Then they killed Changsheng and his brother Chaci, and killed Tesi too.
entries.literal: Thereupon they killed Changsheng and his brother Chaci, and killed Tesi as well.

entries.zh: 海陵乘此並擠阿楞殺之。
entries.en: Hailing used the moment to force Aleng’s death as well.
entries.literal: Hailing seized the moment and, pressing the case, had Aleng killed as well.

entries.zh: 阿楞弟撻楞，熙宗本無意殺之，海陵曰：「其兄既已伏誅，其弟安得獨存。」
entries.en: Aleng’s brother Taleng—Xizong had not meant to kill him. Hailing said: "The elder brother is already dead—can the younger live alone?"
entries.literal: Aleng’s younger brother Taleng—Xizong at first had no mind to kill him; Hailing said: "His elder brother has already suffered execution—how can the younger brother alone remain?"

entries.zh: 又殺之。
entries.en: They killed him as well.
entries.literal: They killed him too.

entries.zh: 熙宗以海陵為忠，愈益任之，而不知其詐也。
entries.en: Xizong thought Hailing faithful and relied on him ever more heavily, never seeing the fraud.
entries.literal: Xizong took Hailing for loyal and trusted him all the more, not knowing his deceit.

entries.zh: 皇統七年四月戊午，左副點檢蒲察阿虎特子尚主，進禮物，賜宴便殿。
entries.en: In the fourth month of Huangtong year 7, day wuwu: the son of Left Vice Director of the Palace Inspection Bureau Pucha Ahute married a princess and brought wedding gifts; the emperor gave a feast in the Informal Hall.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Huangtong, on the day wuwu of the fourth month, the son of Left Vice Director of the Palace Inspection Bureau Pucha Ahute married the princess and presented wedding gifts; a feast was granted in the Informal Hall.

entries.zh: 熙宗被酒，酌酒賜元，元不能飲，上怒，仗劍逼之，元逃去。
entries.en: Xizong, already drunk, poured wine and pressed it on Yuan. Yuan could not drink. The emperor flew into a rage, sword in hand, and drove at him; Yuan fled.
entries.literal: Xizong was drunk, poured wine and bestowed it on Yuan; Yuan could not drink—the sovereign grew angry, drew his sword and pressed him; Yuan fled.

entries.zh: 命左丞宗憲召元，宗憲與元俱去，上益怒，是時戶部尚書宗禮在側，使之跪，手殺之。
entries.en: He ordered Left Vice Director Zongxian to fetch Yuan; Zongxian left with him, and the emperor’s wrath only mounted. Minister of Revenue Zongli stood nearby—the emperor forced him to his knees and killed him himself.
entries.literal: He ordered Left Vice Director Zongxian to summon Yuan; Zongxian went off with Yuan together—the sovereign grew still angrier. At that time Minister of Revenue Zongli was at his side; he made him kneel and killed him with his own hand.

entries.zh: 海陵篡立，追封常勝、查刺、阿楞官爵，親臨葬所致祭。
entries.en: Once Hailing seized the throne he posthumously restored Changsheng, Chaci, and Aleng, and came in person to their graves to sacrifice.
entries.literal: When Hailing usurped the throne he posthumously restored the offices and titles of Changsheng, Chaci, and Aleng, and in person came to their burials to offer sacrifice.

entries.zh: 大定十三年六月丁巳，世宗召皇太子諸王，侍食於清輝殿，曰：「或稱海陵多能，何也。
entries.en: In the sixth month of Dading year 13, day dingsi: Shizong called the crown prince and the princes to dine with him in the Clear Splendor Hall and said: "Some praise Hailing as a man of many talents—why?
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dading, on the day dingsi of the sixth month, Shizong summoned the crown prince and the princes to attend him at meal in the Clear Splendor Hall, and said: "Some call Hailing greatly capable—why?

entries.zh: 海陵譎詐，睢盱殺人，空虛天下三分之二。
entries.en: Hailing was sly and murderous; he glared down the court and killed until a third of the realm stood empty.
entries.literal: Hailing was treacherous and false, glaring and killing men, and emptied two-thirds of the empire.

entries.zh: 太祖諸孫中，惟胙王元天性賢者也。」
entries.en: Of Taizu’s grandsons, only Prince of Zu Yuan was truly worthy by nature."
entries.literal: Among the Taizu’s grandsons, only Prince of Zu Yuan was gifted with a worthy nature by Heaven."

entries.zh: 海陵與唐括辯謀廢立，海陵曰：「若舉大事，誰當立者。」
entries.en: Hailing and Tangguo Bian plotted to depose the throne. Hailing asked: "If we raise a coup, whom should we set up?"
entries.literal: Hailing and Tangguo Bian plotted deposition and enthronement; Hailing said: "If we undertake a great affair, who ought to be enthroned?"

entries.zh: 海陵意謂己乃太祖長房之孫，當立。
entries.en: Hailing meant himself—grandson of Taizu in the senior house—to take the throne.
entries.literal: Hailing’s intent was that he himself, as a grandson of the Taizu of the senior line, ought to be enthroned.

entries.zh: 而辯與秉德初意不在海陵，常勝乃熙宗之弟，辯答曰：「無胙王常勝乎。」
entries.en: Bian and Bingde had not first thought of Hailing. Changsheng was Xizong’s own brother. Bian said: "What of the Prince of Zu, Changsheng?"
entries.literal: But Bian and Bingde at first had not had Hailing in mind; Changsheng was Xizong’s younger brother—Bian answered: "Is there not the Prince of Zu, Changsheng?"

entries.zh: 海陵複問其次，辯曰：「鄧王子阿楞。」
entries.en: Hailing pressed for the next choice. Bian said: "Aleng, son of the Prince of Deng."
entries.literal: Hailing asked again who came next; Bian said: "Prince of Deng’s son Aleng."

entries.zh: 海陵曰：「阿楞屬疏。」
entries.en: Hailing said: "Aleng is too far from the line."
entries.literal: Hailing said: "Aleng’s line is remote."

entries.zh: 由是海陵謂胙王有人望，不除之將不得立，故心忌常勝並阿楞。
entries.en: Thence Hailing reckoned the Prince of Zu held the people’s favor—without removing him he could not reign—and so he hated Changsheng and Aleng alike.
entries.literal: From this Hailing judged that the Prince of Zu had the people’s regard—unless he were removed he could not be enthroned; therefore in his heart he envied Changsheng together with Aleng.

entries.zh: 是時，阿楞方為奉國上將軍。
entries.en: Aleng was then General-in-Chief Who Upholds the State.
entries.literal: At that time Aleng was serving as General-in-Chief Who Upholds the State.

entries.zh: 爽，本名阿鄰。
entries.en: Shuang—born Alin.
entries.literal: Shuang, born Alin.

entries.zh: 天德三年，授世襲猛安。
entries.en: In Tiande year 3 he received a hereditary meng'an commission.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tiande he was granted a hereditary meng'an command.

entries.zh: 正隆二年，除橫海軍節度使，改安武軍，留京師奉朝請。
entries.en: Zhenglong year 2: appointed military commissioner of the Henghai Army, then of the Anwu Army, and kept at the capital on court attendance.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong he was made military commissioner of the Henghai Army, then transferred to the Anwu Army, remaining in the capital to attend court.

entries.zh: 海陵將伐宋，嚴酒禁，爽坐與其弟阿瑣，及從父兄京、徒單貞會飲，被杖，下遷歸化州刺史，奪猛安。
entries.en: When Hailing was about to march on Song he banned wine outright. Shuang had drunk with his brother A Suo and with his cousins Jing and Tushan Zhen; he was flogged, demoted to prefect of Guihua, and lost his meng'an.
entries.literal: As Hailing prepared to attack Song, liquor was strictly forbidden. Shuang was punished for drinking with his brother A Suo and his clansman cousins Jing and Tushan Zhen; he was beaten, demoted to prefect of Guihua, and stripped of his meng'an.

entries.zh: 未幾，複除安武軍節度使。
entries.en: Soon he was reappointed military commissioner of the Anwu Army.
entries.literal: Before long he was again appointed military commissioner of the Anwu Army.

entries.zh: 海陵渡淮，分遣使者翦滅宗室，爽憂懼不知所出。
entries.en: Hailing crossed the Huai and sent agents to purge the clan. Shuang was sick with fear and could see no way out.
entries.literal: When Hailing crossed the Huai, he dispatched envoys to cut down the imperial clan. Shuang was terrified and did not know what to do.

entries.zh: 會世宗即位東京，宗室璋推爽弟阿瑣行中都留守，遣人報爽。
entries.en: Shizong came to the throne at Dongjing. The clansman Zhang had A Suo, Shuang's younger brother, hold Zhongdu as acting protector and sent to inform Shuang.
entries.literal: When Shizong took the throne at Dongjing, the clansman Zhang urged A Suo, Shuang's brother, to act as temporary protector of Zhongdu and sent word to Shuang.

entries.zh: 爽棄妻子來奔，與弟忻州刺史可喜，俱至中都。
entries.en: Shuang left wife and children behind and fled to join him; with his brother Kexi, prefect of Xin, he entered Zhongdu.
entries.literal: Shuang abandoned wife and children and came over; with his brother Kexi, prefect of Xin, he reached Zhongdu together.

entries.zh: 東迎車駕，至梁魚務入見，世宗大悅，即除殿前馬步軍都指揮使。
entries.en: He rode east to meet the imperial train, was received at Liangyuwu, and Shizong rejoiced; at once Shuang was made commander of the Palace Horse and Foot Armies before the throne.
entries.literal: He went east to meet the imperial carriage, presented himself at Liangyuwu, and Shizong was greatly pleased; at once Shuang was made commander-in-chief of the palace horse and foot armies before the throne.

entries.zh: 封溫王，改秘書監。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed Prince Wen and appointed Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince Wen and made Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 母憂，尋起複，遷太子太保，進封壽王。
entries.en: When his mother died he left office, but was soon recalled, made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and advanced to Prince Shou.
entries.literal: On mourning for his mother he was soon recalled; promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and advanced to Prince Shou.

entries.zh: 及弑熙宗，使葛王宗敏。
entries.en: After he killed Xizong, he had the Prince of Ge summon Zong Min.
entries.literal: When he murdered Xizong, he dispatched Prince of Ge Zong Min.

entries.zh: 葛王者，世宗初封也。
entries.en: The Prince of Ge was the title Shizong had first received.
entries.literal: Prince of Ge—that was Shizong's initial enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 宗敏聞海陵召，疑懼不敢往。
entries.en: When Zong Min heard Hailing summon him, he was afraid and did not dare go.
entries.literal: Zong Min, hearing Hailing's summons, was doubtful and afraid and did not dare go.

entries.zh: 葛王曰：「叔父今不即往，至明日，如何與之相見。」
entries.en: The Prince of Ge said: "Uncle, if you do not go today, how will you meet him tomorrow?"
entries.literal: The Prince of Ge said: "Uncle, if you do not go at once today, when tomorrow comes how will you face him?"

entries.zh: 宗敏入宮，海陵欲殺之，尚猶豫，以問左右。
entries.en: Zong Min entered the palace. Hailing meant to kill him but still wavered, and asked his attendants what to do.
entries.literal: Zong Min entered the palace; Hailing wished to kill him but still hesitated, and questioned those at his side.

entries.zh: 烏帶曰：「彼太祖子也，不殺之，眾人必有異議，不如除之。」
entries.en: Wudai said: "He is Taizu’s own son. Leave him alive and the court will murmur—better cut him down."
entries.literal: Wudai said: "He is a son of the Taizu—if he is not killed, the multitude will surely raise objections; better to remove him."

entries.zh: 乃使僕散忽土殺之，忽土刃擊宗敏，宗敏左右走避，膚發血肉，狼藉遍地。
entries.en: He sent Pusan Hutu to do it. Hutu hacked at Zong Min; his attendants scattered. Flesh and blood lay heaped across the floor.
entries.literal: Thereupon he had Pusan Hutu kill him; Hutu struck Zong Min with his blade—Zong Min’s attendants fled aside, skin, hair, flesh, and blood strewn over the ground.

entries.zh: 葛王見殺宗敏，問於眾曰：「國王何罪而死？」
entries.en: The Prince of Ge saw Zong Min slain and asked those present: "What crime had the Kingdom Prince, that he should die?"
entries.literal: The Prince of Ge, seeing Zong Min killed, asked the assembly: "What crime had the Kingdom Prince that he should die?"

entries.zh: 烏帶曰：「天許大事，尚已行之，此蟣虱耳，何足道者。」
entries.en: Wudai said: "We have already done what Heaven approved—this is a flea. Why speak of it?"
entries.literal: Wudai said: "A Heaven-sanctioned great affair we have already carried through—this is a louse or nit; what is there worth speaking of?"

entries.zh: 天德三年，海陵追封宗敏為太師，進封爵。
entries.en: In Tiande year 3 Hailing posthumously made Zong Min Grand Preceptor and raised his title of nobility.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tiande, Hailing posthumously enfeoffed Zong Min as Grand Preceptor and advanced his noble rank.

entries.zh: 妃蒲察氏，進國號。
entries.en: His consort of the Pucha clan was raised in court rank.
entries.literal: His consort, of the Pucha clan, was advanced in state-title.

entries.zh: 封子撒合輦舒國公，賜名褒，進封王；
entries.en: His son Sahelian was made Duke of Shu, granted the name Bao, and later raised to prince;
entries.literal: His son Sahelian was enfeoffed Duke of Shu, given the name Bao, and advanced to prince;

entries.zh: 阿里罕封密國公。
entries.en: Alihan was enfeoffed Duke of Mi.
entries.literal: Alihan was enfeoffed Duke of Mi.

entries.zh: 正隆六年，契丹撒八反，海陵遣使殺諸宗室，阿里罕遂見殺。
entries.en: Zhenglong year 6: the Khitan Saba rose in revolt. Hailing sent agents to slaughter the clan, and Alihan was killed.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenglong the Khitan Saba rebelled; Hailing sent envoys to kill the members of the imperial clan, and Alihan was thereupon killed.

entries.zh: 大定間，詔複官爵。
entries.en: Under Dading an edict restored their offices and noble ranks.
entries.literal: In the Dading era an edict restored their offices and titles.

entries.zh: 頃之，世宗第五女蜀國公主下嫁唐括鼎，賜宴神龍殿，謂爽曰：「朕與卿兄弟，在正隆時，朝夕常懼不保，豈意今日賴爾兄弟之福，可以享安樂矣。」
entries.en: Not long after, Shizong's fifth daughter, the Princess of Shu, married Tangguo Ding; a feast was held in the Shenlong Hall. The emperor said to Shuang, "You and your brothers—in the Zhenglong years we woke each day afraid we would not live to see the next. Who dreamed that today, by your brothers' blessing, we could sit in ease?"
entries.literal: Before long, Shizong's fifth daughter, Princess of Shu, married Tangguo Ding; a banquet was given in the Shenlong Hall. The emperor said to Shuang: "You and your brothers—in the Zhenglong years we lived in daily fear that we might not survive. Who could have thought that today, through your brothers' fortune, we might enjoy peace and ease?"

entries.zh: 爽泣下，頓首謝。
entries.en: Shuang wept and bowed to the ground.
entries.literal: Shuang wept and bowed his head in thanks.

entries.zh: 未幾，判大宗正事，太子太保如故。
entries.en: Soon he was put in charge of the Imperial Clan Court while keeping his rank as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Before long he was assigned to preside over the Imperial Clan Court, retaining his title as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 顯宗長女鄴國公主下嫁烏古論誼，賜宴慶和殿，爽坐西向，迎夕照，面發赤似醉。
entries.en: The Xianzong's eldest daughter, Princess of Ye, married Wugulun Yi; a feast was given in the Qinghe Hall. Shuang sat facing west into the sunset; his face burned red as if he were drunk.
entries.literal: The Xianzong's eldest daughter, Princess of Ye, married Wugulun Yi; a banquet was given in the Qinghe Hall. Shuang sat facing west, catching the evening sun; his face flushed red as though drunk.

entries.zh: 上問曰：「卿醉邪？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "Are you drunk?"
entries.literal: The emperor asked, "Are you drunk?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「未也，臣面迎日色，非酒紅也。」
entries.en: He answered, "No, sire. I am facing the sun—that flush is not from wine."
entries.literal: He replied, "No, Your Majesty. My face catches the sunlight—it is not wine that reddens it."

entries.zh: 上悅，顧群臣曰：「此弟出言，未嘗不實，自小如此。」
entries.en: The emperor was pleased and told the ministers, "This brother of mine has never told a lie—not since he was a boy."
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased and said to the assembled ministers, "This younger brother of mine has never spoken falsely—he has been so since childhood."

entries.zh: 因謂顯宗兄弟曰：「汝等可以為法。」
entries.en: Then he said to the Xianzong and his brothers, "You would do well to be like him."
entries.literal: He then told the Xianzong and his brothers, "You may take him as your model."

entries.zh: 以爽貲用有闕，特賜錢一萬貫。
entries.en: Learning that Shuang's household was short, the emperor specially granted ten thousand strings of cash.
entries.literal: Because Shuang's private means were insufficient, ten thousand strings of cash were specially granted.

entries.zh: 二十三年，爽疾久不愈，敕有司曰：「榮王告滿百日，當給以王俸。」
entries.en: In year 23 Shuang's illness would not lift. An edict ran: "When Prince Rong's sick leave reaches one hundred days, grant him a prince's salary."
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year, Shuang's illness lingered. An edict instructed the offices: "When Prince Rong's sick leave reaches one hundred days, he shall receive a prince's stipend."

entries.zh: 大定二年正月甲戌，上謁山陵，可喜中道稱疾而歸。
entries.en: In the second year of Dading, on jiaxu of the first month, the emperor went to the imperial tombs. Kexi, midway, claimed illness and turned back.
entries.literal: Dading year 2, first month, day jiaxu—the emperor visited the imperial tombs; Kexi on the way pleaded illness and returned.

entries.zh: 乙亥夜，召斡論、惟忠、斡里朵、璋、布輝會其家，沃窟刺以兵赴之，璋曰：「今不高松軍，事不可成矣。」
entries.en: That night, on yihai, he called Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, Zhang, and Buhui to his home. Wokulu came with soldiers. Zhang said: "Without Gao Song's troops, this cannot be done."
entries.literal: On the night of yihai he summoned Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, Zhang, and Buhui to meet at his house; Wokulu came with troops; Zhang said: "Without Gao Song's army now, the affair cannot succeed."

entries.zh: 可喜、璋、布輝乃擒斡論、惟忠、斡里朵、沃窟刺，詣有司自首。
entries.en: Kexi, Zhang, and Buhui then seized Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, and Wokulu and surrendered themselves to the officials.
entries.literal: Kexi, Zhang, and Buhui thereupon seized Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, and Wokulu and went to the authorities to confess voluntarily.

entries.zh: 既下詔獄，可喜不肯自言其始謀，及與斡論面質，然後款伏。
entries.en: After they were committed to the imperial prison, Kexi would not admit the original plot of his own accord; only when he was confronted with Wolun did he confess everything.
entries.literal: Once they were placed in the imperial prison, Kexi would not speak of his initial plotting on his own; only when confronted face to face with Wolun did he then confess in full.

entries.zh: 上念兄弟少，太祖孫惟數人在，惻然傷之。
entries.en: The emperor thought how few brothers he had left, and that of Taizu's grandsons only a handful still lived—his heart ached for them.
entries.literal: The emperor reflected that brothers were few and only a handful of Taizu's grandsons remained—he was moved to sorrow.

entries.zh: 詔罪止可喜一身，其兄弟子孫皆不緣坐。
entries.en: An edict fixed guilt on Kexi alone; brothers, sons, and grandsons would not be punished by association.
entries.literal: An edict declared guilt rested on Kexi alone; his brothers, sons, and grandsons were none implicated by association.

entries.zh: 遂誅斡論、惟忠、斡里朵、沃窟刺等，其沃窟刺下謀克士卒皆釋之。
entries.en: Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, Wokulu, and the others were put to death; the company-command soldiers under Wokulu were all released.
entries.literal: Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, Wokulu, and the rest were then executed; the soldiers under Wokulu's subordinate company commands were all released.

entries.zh: 除璋彰化軍節度使，布輝浚州防禦使。
entries.en: Zhang was made military commissioner of Zhanghua; Buhui was made defender of Jun Prefecture.
entries.literal: Zhang was appointed military commissioner of Zhanghua Army; Buhui was made defender of Jun Prefecture.

entries.zh: 辛巳，詔天下。
entries.en: On xinsi an edict went out to all the realm.
entries.literal: On xinsi an edict was proclaimed throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 是日，賜扈從萬戶銀百兩，猛安五十兩，謀克絹十匹，甲士絹五匹、錢六貫，阿里喜以下賜各有差。
entries.en: That same day the escort wanhu received a hundred taels of silver, meng'an fifty taels, company commanders ten bolts of silk, and armored soldiers five bolts of silk plus six strings of cash; ranks below Ali Xi were rewarded in due measure.
entries.literal: That day, attendant-follower wanhu were granted a hundred taels of silver, meng'an fifty taels, company commanders ten bolts of silk, armored soldiers five bolts of silk and six strings of cash—those below Ali Xi received gifts in graded amounts.

entries.zh: 爽有疾，詔除其子符寶祗候思列為忠順軍節度副使。
entries.en: Shuang fell ill; an edict made his son Silie, a Sigil Guard Attendant, deputy military commissioner of the Zhongshun Army.
entries.literal: When Shuang fell ill, an edict appointed his son, Sigil Guard Attendant Silie, deputy military commissioner of the Zhongshun Army.

entries.zh: 爽入謝，上曰：「朕以卿疾，使卿子遷官，冀卿因喜而愈也。
entries.en: Shuang came to give thanks. The emperor said, "Your illness moved me to advance your son—I hoped gladness might ease you.
entries.literal: Shuang came in to give thanks. The emperor said: "Because of your illness I have promoted your son, hoping that joy may help you recover.

entries.zh: 思列年少，未閑政事，卿訓以義方，使有善可稱，別加升擢。」
entries.en: Silie is young and untried in government; teach him the right way so he may deserve praise, and I will raise him further."
entries.literal: Silie is young and not yet skilled in state affairs; instruct him in proper conduct so that he may earn praise, and I shall promote him further."

entries.zh: 爽疾少間，將從上如涼陘，賜錢千萬，進封英王，轉太子太傅。
entries.en: When Shuang was somewhat better and was to follow the emperor to Liangxi, he received ten million cash, was advanced to Prince Ying, and made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: When Shuang's illness eased somewhat and he was to accompany the emperor to Liangxi, ten million cash were granted; he was advanced to Prince Ying and made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 複世襲猛安，進封榮王，改太子太師。
entries.en: His hereditary meng'an was restored; he was advanced to Prince Rong and made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: His hereditary meng'an was restored; he was advanced to Prince Rong and made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 可喜，以宗室子，累官唐括部族節度使，降忻州刺史。
entries.en: Kexi, of the imperial clan, rose to military commissioner of the Tangguo tribal command, then was demoted to prefect of Xin.
entries.literal: Kexi, as a clansman, rose through offices to military commissioner of the Tangguo tribal command, then was reduced to prefect of Xin.

entries.zh: 海陵遣使殺之，可喜聞世宗即位，即棄州來歸，與其兄歸化州刺史阿鄰會於中都。
entries.en: Hailing sent men to kill him. Hearing that Shizong had taken the throne, Kexi abandoned his post and fled in; he met his elder brother Alin, prefect of Guihua, at Zhongdu.
entries.literal: Hailing sent agents to kill him. When Kexi heard that Shizong had taken the throne, he at once abandoned his prefecture and came over; he met his elder brother Alin, prefect of Guihua, at Zhongdu.

entries.zh: 是時，弟阿瑣權中都留守事，可喜謂阿鄰曰：「阿瑣愚戇，恐不能撫治，欲少留以助之。」
entries.en: A Suo was then acting protector of Zhongdu. Kexi said to Alin, "A Suo is slow and blunt; I doubt he can hold the city. Let me stay a while to help him."
entries.literal: At that time his brother A Suo was acting as temporary protector of Zhongdu. Kexi said to Alin, "A Suo is dull and rough; I fear he cannot govern well. I wish to remain a little while to assist him."

entries.zh: 阿鄰乃行。
entries.en: Alin went on.
entries.literal: Alin then departed.

entries.zh: 可喜留中都，聞世宗發東京，乃迎見於麻吉鋪。
entries.en: Kexi remained at Zhongdu; when he heard the emperor had left Dongjing, he went out to meet him at Majipu.
entries.literal: Kexi stayed in Zhongdu; when he heard that Shizong had set out from Dongjing, he went to meet him at Majipu.

entries.zh: 除兵部尚書，佩金牌，將兵往南京。
entries.en: He was made Minister of War, given a golden tablet, and marched toward Nanjing with troops.
entries.literal: He was made Minister of War, given a golden tablet, and sent with troops toward Nanjing.

entries.zh: 行至中都，聞南京已定，遂止。
entries.en: At Zhongdu he learned Nanjing was already settled, and stopped.
entries.literal: When he reached Zhongdu he heard that Nanjing was already secured, and halted.

entries.zh: 可喜材武過人，狠戾好亂，自乙太祖孫，頗有異志。
entries.en: Kexi was fierce in battle beyond others, cruel and eager for disorder; as a grandson of Taizu, he nursed no small designs.
entries.literal: Kexi was gifted in arms beyond the common run, cruel and bent on turmoil; as a grandson of Taizu in the yi generation, he harbored no small ambition.

entries.zh: 世宗初至中都，倥傯多事，扈從諸軍未暇行賞，或有怨言。
entries.en: When Shizong had just entered Zhongdu, business crowded him on every side; the troops who had escorted him had not yet been rewarded, and some grumbled.
entries.literal: When Shizong had just reached Zhongdu, affairs pressed on every side; the armies that had escorted him had not yet been rewarded, and some murmured in complaint.

entries.zh: 昭武大將軍斡論，正隆末，被詔佩金牌，取河南兵四百人，監完顏彀英軍於歸化，次彰德。
entries.en: Wolun, Grand General of Martial Illumination, late in the Zhenglong reign was ordered to wear the golden plaque, muster four hundred troops from Henan, and oversee Wanyan Gu Ying's forces at Guihua, stopping at Zhangde.
entries.literal: Grand General of Martial Illumination Wolun—at the end of the Zhenglong era, by edict wore the golden plaque, took four hundred Henan troops, supervised Wanyan Gu Ying's army at Guihua, and halted at Zhangde.

entries.zh: 會獨吉和尚持大定赦文至。
entries.en: Duji Heshang arrived with the amnesty proclamation of the Dading reign.
entries.literal: Duji Heshang arrived bearing the Dading amnesty.

entries.zh: 和尚使人招之，斡論不聽，率兵來迎，和尚亦以所將蒲輦兵，列陣待之。
entries.en: Heshang sent envoys to call him in; Wolun refused and marched to confront him. Heshang, for his part, drew up the Pulan troops he commanded and waited in battle array.
entries.literal: Heshang sent men to summon him; Wolun would not obey, led troops to meet him; Heshang likewise arrayed his Pulan troops in battle order to await him.

entries.zh: 斡論兵皆不肯戰，遂請降。
entries.en: Wolun's men would not fight at all, and so they asked to surrender.
entries.literal: Wolun's soldiers all refused to fight, and thereupon sought surrender.

entries.zh: 和尚邀之入相州，收其甲兵，置酒相勞，斡論托腹疾，不肯飲。
entries.en: Heshang brought him into Xiang Prefecture, disarmed his men, and set a feast to honor them. Wolun claimed a stomach ailment and would not drink.
entries.literal: Heshang invited him into Xiang Prefecture, collected their armor and weapons, set out wine to reward them; Wolun pleaded belly ailment and would not drink.

entries.zh: 至夜，已張燈，時時出門，與其心腹密謀，欲就執和尚。
entries.en: By night, with lamps already burning, he slipped out again and again to conspire with his closest followers—they meant to seize Heshang then and there.
entries.literal: When night came, lamps already lit, he went out the door from time to time and with his intimates secretly plotted to seize Heshang on the spot.

entries.zh: 稍具弓矢，和尚覺之，佯為不知，使其從者迫而伺之，斡論不得發。
entries.en: Bows and arrows were quietly readied. Heshang saw it but played ignorant, ordering his attendants to crowd in and watch; Wolun never found his opening.
entries.literal: They somewhat prepared bows and arrows; Heshang noticed but pretended not to know, and had his followers press close and watch; Wolun could not act.

entries.zh: 上至中都近郊，斡論上謁，上亦撫慰之。
entries.en: When the emperor came to the suburbs of the Central Capital, Wolun presented himself; the emperor received him with reassurance.
entries.literal: When the emperor reached the outskirts of the Central Capital, Wolun came to audience; the emperor also comforted him.

entries.zh: 斡論自慊，初無降志。
entries.en: Wolun was ill at ease with himself; he had never meant to submit in the first place.
entries.literal: Wolun felt ashamed—in the beginning he had had no mind to surrender.

entries.zh: 及河南統軍司令史斡里朵，為人狡險，憙圖事，斡論取兵于河南統軍使陁滿訛里也，斡里朵與俱來，俱不自安。
entries.en: Then there was Wolidu, clerk to the Henan frontier commander—a man sly, treacherous, and greedy for intrigue. Wolun had taken soldiers from the Henan frontier commissioner Tuoman E'eli; Wolidu came with them, and none of the party felt secure.
entries.literal: Moreover the Henan frontier army commander-in-chief's clerk Wolidu was deceitful and dangerous by nature, fond of plotting; Wolun had drawn troops from the Henan frontier army commissioner Tuoman E'eli—Wolidu came along with them, and all were ill at ease.

entries.zh: 同知延安尹李惟忠，與熙宗弑逆，構殺韓王亨，世宗疏斥之。
entries.en: Li Weizhong, Vice Director of Yan'an, had taken part in the plot that murdered Xizong and had engineered the death of Prince of Han Hen; Shizong had cast him aside.
entries.literal: Vice Director of Yan'an Yin Li Weizhong, with the regicide against Xizong, had framed and killed Prince of Han Hen; Shizong had kept him at a distance.

entries.zh: 同知中都留守璋，初自領其職，因而授之。
entries.en: Zhang, Vice Director of the Central Capital garrison, had first seized the office for himself; only later was the appointment made formal.
entries.literal: Vice Director of the Central Capital garrison Zhang—at first he had taken the post on his own authority, and it was afterward conferred on him.

entries.zh: 完顏布輝為副統，以罪解職，居京師。
entries.en: Wanyan Buhui had served as deputy commander-in-chief, lost his post for an offense, and was living in the capital.
entries.literal: Wanyan Buhui had been deputy commander-in-chief, was dismissed from office for a crime, and dwelt in the capital.

entries.zh: 於是可喜、斡論、李惟忠、斡里朵、璋、布輝謀，欲因扈從軍士怨望作亂。
entries.en: Then Kexi, Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, Zhang, and Buhui conspired to turn the grumbling of the emperor's escort troops into open rebellion.
entries.literal: Thereupon Kexi, Wolun, Li Weizhong, Wolidu, Zhang, and Buhui plotted, intending to exploit the resentments of the attendant-follower soldiers and raise a revolt.

entries.zh: 斡論曰：「押軍猛安沃窟刺，必不違我。」
entries.en: Wolun said: "The escort meng'an Wokulu will never go against me."
entries.literal: Wolun said: "The supervising army meng'an Wokulu will surely not oppose me."

entries.zh: 惟忠曰：「惟忠嘗為神翼軍總管，有兩銀牌尚在，可以矯發內藏賞士。
entries.en: Li Weizhong said: "I was once chief of the Divine Wing Army and still hold two silver plaques—I can forge orders to pay out the inner treasury's bounty to the troops.
entries.literal: Li Weizhong said: "Weizhong once served as chief of the Divine Wing Army; I still have two silver plaques, and can use them to falsely issue rewards from the inner storehouse to soldiers.

entries.zh: 萬戶高松與我舊，必見聽。」
entries.en: The wanhu Gao Song is an old friend of mine; he is bound to listen."
entries.literal: The wanhu Gao Song is an old associate of mine—he is sure to heed me."

entries.zh: 眾曰：「若得此軍，舉事無難矣。」
entries.en: The others said: "With that force in hand, the deed will not be hard."
entries.literal: The assembly said: "If we obtain this army, raising the affair will be no great difficulty."

entries.zh: 斡論往約沃窟刺，沃窟刺從之。
entries.en: Wolun went to win Wokulu over, and Wokulu consented.
entries.literal: Wolun went to arrange it with Wokulu, and Wokulu agreed.

entries.zh: 惟忠旆說高松，高松不聽，語在《松傳》。
entries.en: Li Weizhong went to win over Gao Song, but Gao Song refused—the story is told in the Biography of Song.
entries.literal: Li Weizhong went to persuade Gao Song; Gao Song would not listen—the account is in the Biography of Song.

entries.zh: 海陵伐宋，以左衛將軍蒲察沙離只同知中都留守事，佩金牌，守管簽。
entries.en: When Hailing attacked Song, Left Guard General Pucha Shalizhi was associate regent of the Central Capital, bearing the gold plaque and keeping charge of the seal.
entries.literal: When Hailing campaigned against Song, Left Guard General Pucha Shalizhi was made associate regent of the Central Capital, wore the gold plaque, and kept charge of the seal.

entries.zh: 世宗即位東京，阿瑣與璋等守城軍官烏林荅石家奴等，入留守府，殺沙離只、府判抹撚撒離喝。
entries.en: When Shizong took the throne at Dongjing, A Suo with Zhang and garrison officers including Wulindaxi Shijianu entered the regent's office and killed Shalizhi and vice-regent Manian Salihu.
entries.literal: When Shizong took the throne at Dongjing, A Suo with Zhang and the garrison officers Wulindaxi Shijianu and others entered the regent's office and killed Shalizhi and vice-regent Manian Salihu.

entries.zh: 眾以阿瑣行留守事，璋自署同知留守事，即遣謀克石家奴、烏林荅願、蒲察蒲查、大興少尹李天吉子磐等，奉表東京。
entries.en: The assembly put A Suo in charge as regent; Zhang styled himself associate regent and at once sent company commander Shijianu, Wulindaxi Yuan, Pucha Pucha, Li Tianji's son Pan of Daxing, and others to present a memorial at Dongjing.
entries.literal: The assembly had A Suo act as regent; Zhang appointed himself associate regent, and at once dispatched company commander Shijianu, Wulindaxi Yuan, Pucha Pucha, Daxing vice prefect Li Tianji's son Pan, and others to present a memorial at Dongjing.

entries.zh: 列傳第十三 ○盧彥倫子:璣
entries.en: Biography 13: Lu Yanlun; his son Ji
entries.literal: Biography 13 ○ Lu Yanlun, son: Ji

entries.zh: (子:亨嗣)
entries.en: (son: Hengsi)
entries.literal: (son: Hengsi)

entries.zh: 毛子廉 李三錫 孔敬宗 李師夔 沈璋 左企弓 虞仲文 曹勇義 康公弼 左泌弟:淵
entries.en: Mao Zilian; Li Sanxi; Kong Jingzong; Li Shikui; Shen Zhang; Zuo Qigong; Yu Zhongwen; Cao Yongyi; Kang Gongbi; Zuo Bi; his younger brother Yuan
entries.literal: Mao Zilian, Li Sanxi, Kong Jingzong, Li Shikui, Shen Zhang, Zuo Qigong, Yu Zhongwen, Cao Yongyi, Kang Gongbi, Zuo Bi, younger brother: Yuan

entries.zh: (子:光慶)
entries.en: (son: Guangqing)
entries.literal: (son: Guangqing)

entries.zh: 天會二年，知新城事。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianhui he was put in charge of Xincheng.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianhui he was made administrator of Xincheng.

entries.zh: 城邑初建，彥倫為經畫，民居、公宇皆有法。
entries.en: When the new town was first laid out, Yanlun planned it so that private homes and public buildings alike followed a coherent design.
entries.literal: As the town was first being built, Yanlun planned it, and both private dwellings and public offices were all laid out according to rule.

entries.zh: 改靜江軍節度留後，知鹹州煙火事。
entries.en: He was transferred to military commissioner designate of the Jingjiang Army and charged with beacon-fire affairs in Xian Prefecture.
entries.literal: He was changed to military commissioner designate of the Jingjiang Army and made overseer of beacon-fire affairs in Xian Prefecture.

entries.zh: 未幾，遷靜江軍節度使。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he was promoted to full military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army.
entries.literal: Before long he was promoted to military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army.

entries.zh: 天眷初，行少府監兼都水使者，充提點京城大內所，改利涉軍節度使。
entries.en: At the start of the Tianjuan era he served as acting director of the Palace Storehouse and concurrent commissioner of waterways, supervised the capital's inner-palace establishment, and was then made military commissioner of the Lishe Army.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianjuan he acted as director of the Palace Storehouse and concurrently commissioner of waterways, served as intendant of the capital inner palace office, and was changed to military commissioner of the Lishe Army.

entries.zh: 未閱月，還，複為提點大內所。
entries.en: Within a month he was back at court and again made intendant of the inner palace office.
entries.literal: Within less than a month he returned and again became intendant of the inner palace office.

entries.zh: 彥倫性機巧，能迎合悼合意，由是頗見寵用。
entries.en: Yanlun was clever by nature and skilled at winning Daohe's favor, and through this he rose to considerable trust and preferment.
entries.literal: Yanlun was by nature clever and able to cater to Dao-He's wishes; for this reason he came to be greatly favored and employed.

entries.zh: 歲餘，遷侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使，為宋國歲元使。
entries.en: A year later he was made commander-in-chief of the palace guard horse and foot armies and sent as the Jin envoy for the Song New Year audience.
entries.literal: After more than a year he was promoted to commander-in-chief of the palace guard horse and foot armies and served as Song New Year's envoy.

entries.zh: 改禮部尚書，加特進，封郇國公。
entries.en: He was appointed minister of rites, granted the extraordinary promotion rank, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xun.
entries.literal: He was changed to minister of rites, given the extraordinary promotion rank, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xun.

entries.zh: 天德二年，出為大名尹。
entries.en: In the second year of Tiande he was posted out as prefect of Daming.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tiande he went out as prefect of Daming.

entries.zh: 明年，詔彥倫營造燕京宮室，以疾卒，年六十九。
entries.en: The following year he was ordered to build the palaces at Yanjing. He died of illness at the age of sixty-nine.
entries.literal: The next year an edict ordered Yanlun to construct the palaces at Yanjing; he died of illness, aged sixty-nine.

entries.zh: 子璣。
entries.en: His son was Ji.
entries.literal: His son was Ji.

entries.zh: 璣字正甫，以廕補閤門祗候，累遷客省使，兼東上閤門使，改提點太醫、教坊、司天，充大定十五年宋主生日副使，遷同知宣徽院事。
entries.en: Ji, courtesy name Zhengfu, entered service by yin privilege as a privy-gate attendant. He rose through the posts of guest liaison commissioner and concurrent eastern upper privy-gate commissioner, then became intendant of the imperial medical service, music conservatory, and astronomical bureau. He served as deputy envoy for the Song emperor's birthday in the fifteenth year of Dading and was made vice director of the Privy Portal Office.
entries.literal: Ji, style Zhengfu, entered office by yin privilege as a privy-gate attendant. He was promoted repeatedly to guest liaison commissioner and concurrently eastern upper privy-gate commissioner, then was changed to intendant of the imperial medical service, music conservatory, and astronomical bureau. He served as deputy envoy for the Song emperor's birthday in the fifteenth year of Dading and was transferred to vice director of the Privy Portal Office.

entries.zh: 丁母憂，起複太府監，改開遠軍節度使，入為右宣徽使。
entries.en: After mourning his mother he was recalled as director of the Palace Storehouse, then made military commissioner of Kaiyuan Army and entered service as right privy portal commissioner.
entries.literal: Upon mourning for his mother, he was recalled to serve as director of the Palace Storehouse, was changed to military commissioner of Kaiyuan Army, and entered service as right privy portal commissioner.

entries.zh: 章宗即位，轉左宣徽使，致仕。
entries.en: When Zhangzong acceded, he was transferred to left privy portal commissioner and retired.
entries.literal: When Zhangzong acceded, he was transferred to left privy portal commissioner and retired from office.

entries.zh: 明昌四年，起複左宣徽使，改定武軍節度使，複為左宣徽使。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Mingchang he was recalled as left privy portal commissioner, made military commissioner of Dingwu Army, and again appointed left privy portal commissioner.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Mingchang he was recalled as left privy portal commissioner, changed to military commissioner of Dingwu Army, and again made left privy portal commissioner.

entries.zh: 是時，璣年已七十，詔許朝參得坐於廊下。
entries.en: By then Ji was already seventy, and an edict allowed him to take a seat in the corridor when he attended court.
entries.literal: At that time Ji was already seventy; an edict permitted him at court audience to be seated in the corridor.

entries.zh: 複致仕。
entries.en: He retired from office once more.
entries.literal: He again retired from office.

entries.zh: 泰和初，詔璣天壽節預宴。
entries.en: At the start of the Taihe era he was ordered to attend the emperor's birthday banquet.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, an edict summoned Ji to the Tian Shou festival banquet.

entries.zh: 二年，元妃李氏生皇子，滿三月，章宗以璣老而康強，命以所策杖為洗兒禮物。
entries.en: In the second year, when Primary Consort Li gave birth to a prince and the third month was reached, Zhangzong—seeing that Ji was old but still vigorous—commanded that the walking staff Ji used be presented as the gift for the infant-washing rite.
entries.literal: In the second year the primary consort Lady Li bore a prince; when three months were complete, Zhangzong, because Ji was old yet hale, ordered that the staff he leaned on be the gift for the washing-of-the-child ceremony.

entries.zh: 章宗幸玉泉山，詔璣與致仕宰相俱會食，許策杖給扶。
entries.en: When Zhangzong visited Jade Spring Mountain, he summoned Ji to dine with the retired chief ministers and allowed him a staff and aides to steady him.
entries.literal: Zhangzong visited Jade Spring Mountain and ordered Ji and retired chief ministers to dine together, permitting a staff and attendants to support him.

entries.zh: 後預天壽節，上命璣與大臣握槊戲，璣獲勝焉。
entries.en: On a later birthday celebration the emperor had Ji play shuo, a board game, against the chief ministers, and Ji won.
entries.literal: Later he attended the Tian Shou festival; the emperor ordered Ji and the great ministers to play shuo, a board game; Ji won.

entries.zh: 從上秋山，賜名馬。
entries.en: He accompanied the emperor on the autumn hunt in the hills and was given a fine horse.
entries.literal: He followed the emperor to the autumn mountain hunt and was granted a famous horse.

entries.zh: 上曰：「酬卿博直。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "This repays your blunt honesty at the shuo match."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "This rewards your forthright counsel in the shuo match."

entries.zh: 其眷遇如此。
entries.en: Such was the degree of favor he enjoyed.
entries.literal: Such was the favor shown him.

entries.zh: 泰和六年卒，年八十。
entries.en: He died in the sixth year of Taihe at the age of eighty.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe he died, aged eighty.

entries.zh: 子亨嗣。
entries.en: His son was Hengsi.
entries.literal: His son was Hengsi.

entries.zh: 亨嗣與弟亨益，盡友愛之道。
entries.en: Hengsi and his younger brother Hengyi were models of fraternal devotion.
entries.literal: Hengsi and his younger brother Hengyi fully practiced brotherly affection.

entries.zh: 亨嗣初以祖廕得官，大定十六年，父璣為同知宣徽院事，當廕子，亨嗣以讓弟亨益。
entries.en: Hengsi had first entered office through his grandfather's yin privilege. In the sixteenth year of Dading, when his father Ji became vice director of the Privy Portal Office and was entitled to pass office to a son, Hengsi yielded the privilege to his younger brother Hengyi.
entries.literal: Hengsi had first received office through his grandfather's privilege; in the sixteenth year of Dading his father Ji was vice director of the Privy Portal Office and was due a yin privilege for a son; Hengsi yielded it to his younger brother Hengyi.

entries.zh: 亨益早卒，子兟。
entries.en: Hengyi died young, leaving a son named Shen.
entries.literal: Hengyi died young; his son was Shen.

entries.zh: 兟幼稚，亨嗣盡以舊業田宅奴畜財物與之。
entries.en: Shen was still a child, so Hengsi turned over to him the entire family patrimony—fields, houses, slaves, livestock, and goods.
entries.literal: Shen was young; Hengsi gave him all the family's old estates, fields, houses, slaves, livestock, and goods.

entries.zh: 仲誨立朝峻整，容色莊重，世宗嘗曰：「朕見劉仲誨嘗若將切諫者。」
entries.en: Zhonghui was austere and composed at court, his bearing solemn. Emperor Shizong once said: "Whenever I see Liu Zhonghui, he looks ready to deliver a blunt remonstrance."
entries.literal: Zhonghui was stern and ordered at court, his bearing grave; Emperor Shizong once said: "When I see Liu Zhonghui it is as if he is about to offer a sharp remonstrance."

entries.zh: 其以剛嚴見知如此。
entries.en: Such was his reputation for stern integrity.
entries.literal: Thus he was known for stern integrity.

entries.zh: 入為禮部侍郎兼左諭德，遷太子詹事兼左諫議大夫。
entries.en: He entered the capital as Vice Director of Rites and Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Left Remonstrating Grand Master.
entries.literal: He entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and was transferred to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Left Remonstrating Grand Master.

entries.zh: 上曰：「東宮官屬，尤當選用正人，如行檢不修及不稱位者，具以名聞。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "The Eastern Palace staff must be men of integrity. Report by name anyone whose conduct is lax or who is unfit for his post."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Eastern Palace staff especially should be upright men; those whose conduct is not cultivated or who are unfit for their posts—report their names in full.

entries.zh: 又曰：「東宮講書或論議間，當以孝儉德行正身之事告之。」
entries.en: He added: "In lectures or discussions at the Eastern Palace, teach him filial piety, frugality, virtue, and self-discipline."
entries.literal: He also said: "When lecturing or debating in the Eastern Palace, tell him of filial piety, frugality, virtue, and correcting the person."

entries.zh: 頃之，東宮請增牧人及張設什用，上謂仲誨曰：「太子生於富貴，每教之恭儉。
entries.en: Soon the Eastern Palace requested more herdsmen and furnishings. The emperor told Zhonghui: "The crown prince was born to privilege—keep teaching him modesty and thrift.
entries.literal: Before long the Eastern Palace asked to increase herdsmen and expand furnishings; the emperor told Zhonghui: "The crown prince was born to wealth; teach him respect and frugality at every turn.

entries.zh: 朕服禦未嘗妄有增益，卿以此意諭之。」
entries.en: I have never indulged my wardrobe without cause—make that clear to him."
entries.literal: I have never rashly added to my robes; convey this meaning to him."

entries.zh: 改御史中丞。
entries.en: He was then appointed Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: He was changed to Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 複為太子詹事，遷吏部尚書，轉太子少師兼御史中丞。
entries.en: He again became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then Director of Personnel, and finally Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent with the additional post of Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: He again became Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and changed to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 坐失糾舉大長公主事，與侍御史李瑜各削一階。
entries.en: He was demoted for failing to impeach the Grand Princess; he and Attending Censor Li Yu each lost one rank.
entries.literal: He was punished for failing to impeach the Grand Princess; he and Attending Censor Li Yu each had one rank stripped.

entries.zh: 仲誨前後為東宮官且十五年，多進規戒，顯宗特加禮敬。
entries.en: Zhonghui had served in the Eastern Palace for some fifteen years in all, offering many admonitions, and Emperor Xianzong treated him with special deference.
entries.literal: Zhonghui had served as an Eastern Palace official for about fifteen years in all, often offering admonitions; Emperor Xianzong showed him special respect.

entries.zh: 大定十九年，卒。
entries.en: He died in Dading year 19.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year of Dading he died.

entries.zh: 十年，司空李德固孫引慶求襲其祖猛安，世宗曰：「德固無功，其猛安且闕之。
entries.en: In the tenth year Li Deguo's grandson Yinqing sought to inherit his grandfather's commander rank. The emperor said: "Deguo earned no merit; let that command remain vacant for now.
entries.literal: In the tenth year Minister of Works Li Deguo's grandson Yinqing sought to inherit his grandfather's commander rank; the emperor said: "Deguo had no merit; his commander rank shall remain vacant for now.

entries.zh: 漢人宰相惟韓企先最賢，他不及也。」
entries.en: Among Han grand chancellors only Han Qixian was truly worthy; none of the others matched him."
entries.literal: Among Han grand chancellors only Han Qixian was most worthy; the others did not equal him."

entries.zh: 十一年，將圖功臣像于衍慶宮，上曰：「丞相企先，本朝典章制度多出斯人之手，至於關決大政，與大臣謀議，不使外人知之，由是無人能知其功。
entries.en: In the eleventh year they planned to paint meritorious officials' portraits in the Yanqing Palace. The emperor said: "Grand Councillor Qixian drafted much of this dynasty's law and institutions. In great affairs he deliberated with ministers in secret, so no one could measure his achievement.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year they were to paint meritorious officials' portraits in the Yanqing Palace; the emperor said: "Grand Councillor Qixian—many of this dynasty's statutes came from this man's hand; in deciding great affairs he deliberated with ministers and would not let outsiders know, so no one could know his merit.

entries.zh: 前後漢人宰相無能及者，置功臣畫像中，亦足以示勸後人。」
entries.en: No Han grand councillor before or after could equal him. Placing his portrait among the meritorious ministers is enough to admonish those who come after."
entries.literal: No Han grand councillor before or after could equal him; placing his portrait among meritorious ministers is enough to admonish later men."

entries.zh: 十五年，諡簡懿。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he received the posthumous name Jianyi, meaning Simple and Virtuous.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was given the posthumous name Jianyi.

entries.zh: 韓鐸字振文，企先次子也。
entries.en: Han Duo, whose courtesy name was Zhenwen, was Qixian's second son.
entries.literal: Han Duo, courtesy name Zhenwen, was Qixian's second son.

entries.zh: 皇統末，以大臣子授武義將軍。
entries.en: Near the end of Huangtong, as a minister's son he was appointed General of Martial Righteousness.
entries.literal: At the end of Huangtong, as a minister's son he was made General of Martial Righteousness.

entries.zh: 熙宗聞其有儒學，賜進士第，除宣徽判官。
entries.en: When Xizong heard of his learning in the Confucian classics, he granted Duo the jinshi degree and made him a judge of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: Xizong hearing he had Confucian learning granted him the jinshi degree and made him Judge of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 再遷刑部員外郎，海陵遣中使諭之曰：「郎官，高選也。
entries.en: He was transferred again to Outer Director of the Ministry of Punishments. Hailing sent a palace envoy to tell him: "A bureau directorship is a high appointment.
entries.literal: He was transferred again to Outer Director of the Ministry of Punishments; Hailing sent a palace envoy to instruct him: "A bureau director is a high selection.

entries.zh: 汝勳賢之子，行已蒞官，能世其家，故以命汝。
entries.en: You are the son of a meritorious minister; your conduct already befits office and can carry on your family line, and that is why you are appointed.
entries.literal: You are the son of a meritorious worthy; your conduct has already reached office and can carry on the family, so you are appointed.

entries.zh: 苟能夙夜在公，當不次擢用，雖公相可到。」
entries.en: If you serve diligently day and night, you will be promoted out of turn—even the rank of grand councillor is within reach."
entries.literal: If you can be diligent from dawn to dusk in public affairs, you will be promoted out of turn—even grand councillor is attainable."

entries.zh: 鐸感奮，獄或有疑，據經議讞。
entries.en: Duo was deeply moved. When cases were doubtful he deliberated according to the classics and statutes.
entries.literal: Duo was stirred; when cases had doubts he deliberated on statutes.

entries.zh: 海陵伐宋，改兵部員外郎。
entries.en: During Hailing's campaign against Song he was transferred to Outer Director of the Ministry of War.
entries.literal: On Hailing's campaign against Song he was changed to Outer Director of the Ministry of War.

entries.zh: 大定初，遷本部郎中，累官河州防禦使，求養親，解去。
entries.en: Early in Dading he became Director in the same ministry, rose to Defender-in-Chief of Hezhou, then asked leave to care for his mother and resigned.
entries.literal: Early in Dading he was transferred to Director in the same ministry, rose to Defender-in-Chief of Hezhou, and requested leave to support his mother and resigned.

entries.zh: 召為左諫議大夫，遷中都路都轉運使。
entries.en: He was summoned as Left Remonstrating Grand Master and made Commissioner of Transport for the Central Capital circuit.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Left Remonstrating Grand Master and transferred to Commissioner of Transport for the Central Capital circuit.

entries.zh: 頃之，上謂宰臣曰：「韓鐸年高，不任繁劇，且其母老矣，可與之便郡。」
entries.en: Before long the emperor told his councillors: "Han Duo is advanced in years and cannot bear heavy duties, and his mother is old—give him a convenient prefecture."
entries.literal: Before long the emperor told the councillors: "Han Duo is aged and cannot bear heavy duties; moreover his mother is old—give him a convenient prefecture."

entries.zh: 於是改順天軍節度使。
entries.en: He was then made military commissioner of the Shuntian Army.
entries.literal: He was therefore changed to military commissioner of Shuntian Army.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 贊曰：太祖入燕，始用遼南、北面官僚制度。
entries.en: The commentator says: When Taizu entered Yan he first adopted the Liao southern and northern bureaucratic systems.
entries.literal: The commentator says: When Taizu entered Yan he first used the Liao southern and northern bureaucratic systems.

entries.zh: 是故劉彥宗、時立愛規為施設，不見於朝廷之上。
entries.en: Thus Liu Yanzong and Shi Liai planned and carried out measures that did not appear at the central court.
entries.literal: Therefore Liu Yanzong and Shi Liai planned and implemented arrangements not seen at the court level.

entries.zh: 軍旅之暇，治官政，庀民事，務農積穀，內供京師，外給轉餉，此其功也。
entries.en: In the intervals between campaigns they governed civil affairs, settled the people, promoted farming and stored grain, supplied the capital within and transport without—this was their achievement.
entries.literal: In intervals between campaigns they governed civil administration and arranged civilian affairs, promoted farming and stored grain, supplying the capital within and transport without—this was their achievement.

entries.zh: 韓企先入相兩朝，幾二十年，成功著業，世宗稱其賢焉。
entries.en: Han Qixian had served as grand chancellor through two reigns for nearly twenty years, leaving a record of solid achievement, and Emperor Shizong praised his excellence.
entries.literal: Han Qixian first served as grand chancellor through two reigns for nearly twenty years, achieved merit and established his work, and Emperor Shizong praised his worth.

entries.zh: 列傳第十六 ○劉彥宗子:萼
entries.en: Biographies 16: Liu Yanzong and his son E
entries.literal: Biographies 16: Liu Yanzong and his son E

entries.zh: (子:筈
entries.en: Liu Yanzong's son Kuo
entries.literal: Liu Yanzong's son Kuo

entries.zh: (子:仲誨))
entries.en: Kuo's son Zhonghui
entries.literal: Kuo's son Zhonghui

entries.zh: 劉頍 時立愛 韓企先子:鐸
entries.en: Liu Yi; Shi Liai; Han Qixian and his son Duo
entries.literal: Liu Yi; Shi Liai; Han Qixian and his son Duo

entries.zh: 夾谷清臣，本名阿不沙，胡里改路桓篤人也。
entries.en: Jiagu Qingchen, whose original name was A'busha, came from Huandu in the Huligai Circuit.
entries.literal: Jiagu Qingchen, original name A'busha, was a man of Huandu in the Huligai Circuit.

entries.zh: 姿狀雄偉，善騎射。
entries.en: He had a commanding physique and excelled at mounted archery.
entries.literal: His bearing was imposing and he was skilled at riding and archery.

entries.zh: 皇統八年，襲祖駁達猛安。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Huangtong (1148), he succeeded to his grandfather's hereditary meng'an at Bodafa.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Huangtong, he inherited his grandfather's Bodafa meng'an post.

entries.zh: 大定元年，聞世宗即位，率本部軍六千赴中都會之，以功遷昭武大將軍。
entries.en: When Shizong took the throne in the first year of Dading (1161), Qingchen led six thousand men of his unit to Zhongdu to rally to him and was promoted to Zhaowu Grand General for his service.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dading, hearing that Shizong had ascended the throne, he led six thousand troops of his command to Zhongdu to join him and, for his merit, was promoted to Zhaowu Grand General.

entries.zh: 從右副元帥紇石烈志甯為管押萬戶，接應左都監完顏思敬，逐窩斡餘黨，敗之柔遠，至抹拔里達悉獲之。
entries.en: He served under the Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Heshilie Zhining as supervising commander of ten thousand households, joined the Left Chief Inspector Wanyan Sijing in hunting down Wohe's remaining followers, routed them at Rouyuan, and ran them down to Mobali, where the entire force was taken.
entries.literal: Following the Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Heshilie Zhining as supervising commander of ten thousand households, he supported the Left Chief Inspector Wanyan Sijing in pursuing the remnant band of Wohe, defeated them at Rouyuan, and pursued them to Mobali, capturing them all.

entries.zh: 賊平，遷鎮國上將軍，知潁順軍事。
entries.en: After the rebellion was crushed, he was promoted to Zhenguo Grand General and put in charge of military affairs at Yingshun.
entries.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was transferred to Zhenguo Grand General and made responsible for Yingshun military affairs.

entries.zh: 會宋兵二萬襲陷汝州，殺刺史烏古孫麻發及漢軍二千。
entries.en: Song forces numbering twenty thousand then stormed and captured Ruzhou, killing the prefect Wugusun Mafa along with two thousand Han soldiers.
entries.literal: It happened that twenty thousand Song troops raided and seized Ruzhou, killing the prefect Wugusun Mafa and two thousand Han troops.

entries.zh: 河南統軍宗尹遣萬戶孛術魯定方與清臣等領騎兵四千往擊之。
entries.en: The Henan Commander-in-Chief Zong Yin dispatched Pusulu Dingfang, commander of ten thousand households, together with Qingchen and others at the head of four thousand horsemen to attack them.
entries.literal: The Henan Commander-in-Chief Zong Yin sent the commander of ten thousand households Pusulu Dingfang with Qingchen and others to lead four thousand cavalry to strike them.

entries.zh: 宋人棄城遁，遂複汝州。
entries.en: The Song troops abandoned the city and fled, and Ruzhou was retaken.
entries.literal: The Song men abandoned the city and fled, and Ruzhou was thereby recovered.

entries.zh: 三年五月，從志寧複取宿州，宋將李世輔大敗遁去，志寧複遣清臣等以兵追襲，又敗之。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the third year (1163), he followed Zhining in retaking Suzhou. After the Song general Li Shipu was routed and fled, Zhining sent Qingchen and others in pursuit, and they defeated the enemy again.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, following Zhining he recovered Suzhou; the Song general Li Shipu was greatly defeated and fled; Zhining again sent Qingchen and others with troops to pursue and strike them, and defeated them again.

entries.zh: 捷聞，授宿州防禦使。
entries.en: On report of the victory, he was appointed Defender of Suzhou.
entries.literal: When news of the victory arrived, he was appointed Defender of Suzhou.

entries.zh: 移博州，改西北路招討都監，遷烏古十壘部族節度使。
entries.en: He was moved to Bozhou, made Assistant Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit, and then promoted to Commissioner of the Wugu Shilei tribal command.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Bozhou, changed to Northwest Circuit Assistant Pacification Commissioner, and promoted to Commissioner of the Wugu Shilei Tribal Command.

entries.zh: 十二年，授右副都點檢，遷左副都點檢，出為陝西路統軍使，兼知京兆府事。
entries.en: In the twelfth year (1172) he was made Right Deputy Chief Inspector, then Left Deputy Chief Inspector, and sent out as Commander-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Circuit while also serving as administrator of Jingzhao Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Right Deputy Chief Inspector, transferred to Left Deputy Chief Inspector, and sent out as Shaanxi Circuit Commander-in-Chief, concurrently administering Jingzhao Prefecture affairs.

entries.zh: 朝辭，賜以金帶廄馬，仍諭之曰：「卿典禁兵，日侍左右，勤勞久矣，故以是授卿，宜益思勉。」
entries.en: When he took leave at court, the emperor bestowed a gold belt and imperial horses and told him: "You have long commanded the palace guard and attended me daily with tireless service; that is why I am sending you out—do not slacken your efforts."
entries.literal: At his court farewell he was granted a gold belt and stable horses, and was further instructed: "You have long commanded the forbidden troops and attended at my side day after day with devoted labor; therefore this is conferred on you—you should strive all the more."

entries.zh: 二十六年，改西京留守。
entries.en: In the twenty-sixth year (1186) he was appointed Garrison Commander of the Western Capital.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was changed to Western Capital Garrison Commander.

entries.zh: 閱三歲，遷樞密副使。
entries.en: Three years later he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: After three years he was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 明昌元年，初議出師，以本職充東北路兵馬都統制使，既而詔止之。
entries.en: In the first year of Mingchang (1190), when a campaign was first proposed, he was named Commander-in-Chief of Northeast Circuit forces in his current post, but an edict soon called the expedition off.
entries.literal: In the first year of Mingchang, when an expedition was first discussed, he was appointed in his present office as Commander-in-Chief of Northeast Circuit forces, but shortly an edict halted it.

entries.zh: 俄以其女為昭儀，眷倚益重。
entries.en: Before long his daughter was made a zhaoyi (imperial consort), and the emperor's reliance on him deepened.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward his daughter was made Lady of Brilliant Comportment, and imperial favor toward him grew heavier.

entries.zh: 二年，拜尚書左丞。
entries.en: In the second year (1191) he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: In the second year he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 頃之，進平章政事，封芮國公，賜同本朝人。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was promoted to Grand Councilor, enfeoffed as Duke of Rui, and granted the privileges of a native Jin subject.
entries.literal: Before long he was advanced to Grand Councilor, enfeoffed as Duke of Rui, and granted status equal to native Jin subjects.

entries.zh: 四年，遷右丞相，監修國史。
entries.en: In the fourth year (1193) he became Right Chancellor and was put in charge of compiling the national history.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Right Chancellor and made supervisor of the compilation of the national history.

entries.zh: 左丞相志甯疾甚，世宗臨問之，志寧薦襄「智勇兼濟，有經世才，他人莫及，異時任用，殆勝於臣」。
entries.en: When Left Chancellor Zhining fell gravely ill, Shizong visited him in person. Zhining recommended Xiang: "He combines wisdom and courage and has the talent to govern an age; no one else equals him, and if employed later he would likely surpass me."
entries.literal: Left Chancellor Zhining was gravely ill; Shizong visited him in person to inquire; Zhining recommended Xiang: "Combining wisdom and courage, possessing talent to order the age—no one else can match him; employed in future he would likely surpass me."

entries.zh: 即召授殿前左副都點檢。
entries.en: Xiang was immediately summoned and appointed Left Deputy Chief Inspector of the Hall Army.
entries.literal: He was immediately summoned and appointed Left Deputy Chief Inspector of the Hall Army.

entries.zh: 為宋生日使，宋方祈免親接國書，襄至，宋人屢來議，皆折之，迄成禮而還。
entries.en: As envoy for the Song emperor's birthday, when Song was petitioning to be excused from receiving the state letter in person, Xiang went. The Song side negotiated repeatedly, but he rebutted every proposal until the ceremony was completed and he returned.
entries.literal: He served as envoy for Song's birthday; Song was then petitioning to be excused from receiving the state letter in person; when Xiang arrived, Song men came repeatedly to negotiate and he refuted them all, until the rites were completed and he returned.

entries.zh: 授陝西路統軍使，賜之尚服、廄馬、鞍勒、佩刀。
entries.en: He was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Circuit and granted court robes, imperial horses, saddle and bridle, and a ceremonial sword.
entries.literal: He was appointed Shaanxi Circuit Commander-in-Chief and granted court robes, stable horses, saddle and bridle, and a waist sword.

entries.zh: 改河南統軍使。
entries.en: He was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of the Henan Circuit.
entries.literal: He was changed to Henan Circuit Commander-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 入為吏部尚書，轉都點檢，賜錢千萬。
entries.en: He was recalled to serve as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, then promoted to Chief Inspector and granted ten million in cash.
entries.literal: He entered the capital as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was transferred to Chief Inspector, and was granted ten million in cash.

entries.zh: 世宗謂宰執曰：「襄為人甚蘊藉，非直日，亦入宮規畫諸事，事有所付乃退，其公勤如此。
entries.en: Shizong told his chief administrators: "Xiang is deeply self-possessed. Even on days when he is not on duty he comes to the palace to discuss affairs and leaves only after matters are settled—such is his public diligence.
entries.literal: Shizong said to the chief administrators: "Xiang's character is very restrained; even on days when he is not on duty he enters the palace to plan various affairs and withdraws only when matters are entrusted—his public diligence is like this.

entries.zh: 若襄之才豈多得哉！」
entries.en: How rarely one finds talent like Xiang's!"
entries.literal: Talents like Xiang's—how could one obtain many!"

entries.zh: 擢御史大夫。
entries.en: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 逾月，拜尚書右丞，諭之曰：「卿在河南經制邊事，甚有統紀，及在吏部，至為點檢，尤奉公守法，朕甚嘉之。
entries.en: A month later he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. The emperor told him, "In Henan you kept border affairs in good order; in the Ministry of Personnel and as Chief Inspector you were scrupulously fair and law-abiding. I am deeply pleased with your service.
entries.literal: After more than a month, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and was addressed thus: "When you managed border affairs in Henan, you maintained excellent discipline; when you served in the Ministry of Personnel and later as Chief Inspector, you were especially devoted to public duty and observant of the law. I greatly commend this.

entries.zh: 近長憲台，亦以剛直聞，是用委以機政，其益勉之！」
entries.en: Since you recently headed the Censorate and are known for your uncompromising integrity, I am entrusting you with core state affairs. Apply yourself all the more!"
entries.literal: Recently, as head of the Censorate, you are also known for firm uprightness; for this reason I entrust you with state affairs—redouble your efforts!"

entries.zh: 未幾，進拜左丞。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was promoted to Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: Not long after, he was further promoted to Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 襄在外任，治有異效，至是朝廷以褒賞廉吏詔天下，列其名以示獎勵。
entries.en: While serving in provincial posts, Xiang had achieved outstanding results. The court now issued a nationwide edict honoring upright officials and named him among them as an example.
entries.literal: When Xiang served in external posts, his governance had remarkable results; at this time the court issued a proclamation throughout the realm praising upright officials, listing his name to show encouragement.

entries.zh: 二十三年，進拜平章政事，封蕭國公。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year he was promoted to Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was further promoted to Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao.

entries.zh: 世宗以金源郡王世嫡皇孫，將加王爵，詔擇國號。
entries.en: Because the Prince of Jinyuan was the principal imperial grandson, Shizong was about to confer a princely title on him, and an edict ordered a state name chosen for the enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Shizong, taking the Prince of Jinyuan as the principal imperial grandson, was about to confer princely rank, and an edict was issued to select a state name.

entries.zh: 襄曰：「為天下大計，必先正其本，原者本也，請封原。」
entries.en: Xiang said, "For the good of the empire we must first fix what is fundamental. Yuan means root—I propose the title Yuan."
entries.literal: Xiang said: "For the great plan of the realm, one must first set right the root; yuan means root—I request enfeoffment as Yuan."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The proposal was adopted.

entries.zh: 故事，諸部族節度使及其僚屬多用颭人，而頗有私縱不法者，議改用諸色人。
entries.en: By custom, commissioners of the tribal departments and their staffs often used Khitan, many of whom had abused their positions. Officials debated replacing them with men of other backgrounds.
entries.literal: By precedent, military commissioners of various tribal departments and their subordinates often employed Khitan, and there were many who privately indulged unlawful conduct; discussion turned to replacing them with people of various other categories.

entries.zh: 襄曰：「北邊雖無事，恆須經略之，若杜此門，其後有勞績，何以處之？
entries.en: Xiang said, "Even when the north is quiet we must still cultivate frontier talent. Close this avenue of advancement and we will have nowhere to reward future merit.
entries.literal: Xiang said: "Though the northern frontier is presently quiet, one must always manage it strategically; if this path is closed off, when someone later achieves merit, how will he be placed?

entries.zh: 請如舊。」
entries.en: Let the old practice stand."
entries.literal: I request keeping the former practice."

entries.zh: 他日，議及古有監軍之事。
entries.en: On another occasion the court discussed the old institution of army supervisors.
entries.literal: On another day, discussion turned to the ancient practice of army supervisors.

entries.zh: 襄曰：「漢、唐初無監軍，將得專任，故戰必勝，攻必克。
entries.en: Xiang said, "Early Han and Tang had no army supervisors. Generals held full command, so they fought to victory and stormed to success.
entries.literal: Xiang said: "In early Han and Tang there were no army supervisors; generals had full authority, hence in battle they always won and in attack they always prevailed.

entries.zh: 及叔世始以內臣監其軍，動為所制，故多敗而少功。
entries.en: Only in decadent times did inner-court officials begin supervising armies, tying the generals' hands and producing more defeats than victories.
entries.literal: In later ages palace officials began to supervise armies and generals were constantly constrained by them, hence many defeats and few achievements.

entries.zh: 若將得其人，監軍誠不必置。」
entries.en: Appoint the right commander and there is no need for supervisors at all."
entries.literal: If the right general is obtained, supervisors truly need not be appointed."

entries.zh: 並嘉納之。
entries.en: The emperor approved both recommendations.
entries.literal: Both suggestions were approved and adopted.

entries.zh: 詔受北部進貢。
entries.en: He was ordered to receive tribute from the northern frontier.
entries.literal: An edict was issued for him to receive tribute from the northern regions.

entries.zh: 使還，世宗問邊事，具圖以進，因上羈縻屬部、鎮服大石之策，詔悉行之。
entries.en: On his return Shizong questioned him about frontier affairs. Xiang submitted detailed maps and proposed policies to keep dependent tribes loyal and to hold the Dashi (Qara Khitai) in check. The emperor ordered all of it carried out.
entries.literal: When the envoy returned, Shizong asked about border affairs; he submitted detailed maps, and presented strategies for keeping subordinate tribes in submission and pacifying Dashi; an edict ordered all to be implemented.

entries.zh: 進拜右丞相，徙封戴。
entries.en: He was promoted to Right Chancellor and his fief was changed to Dai.
entries.literal: He was further promoted to Right Chancellor and transferred his fief to Dai.

entries.zh: 世宗不豫，與太尉徒單克甯、平章政事張汝霖宿內殿，同受顧命。
entries.en: When Shizong fell ill, Xiang stayed in the inner hall with Grand Commandant Tudan Kening and Grand Councilor Zhang Rulin and together received the emperor's deathbed charge.
entries.literal: When Shizong fell ill, together with Grand Commandant Tudan Kening and Grand Councilor Zhang Rulin he lodged in the inner hall and jointly received the final imperial charge.

entries.zh: 章宗初即政，議罷僧道奴婢。
entries.en: Soon after Zhangzong ascended the throne, the court debated abolishing the household slaves held by Buddhist and Daoist clergy.
entries.literal: When Zhangzong first took power, discussion arose about abolishing the slave attendants of Buddhist and Daoist clergy.

entries.zh: 太尉克甯奏曰：「此蓋成俗日久，若遽更之，於人情不安。
entries.en: Grand Commandant Kening argued, "This practice is deeply entrenched. To abolish it at once would unsettle public sentiment.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant Kening memorialized: "This has surely been custom for a long time; if changed abruptly, people's feelings would be unsettled.

entries.zh: 陛下如惡其數多，宜嚴立格法，以防濫度，則自少矣。」
entries.en: If Your Majesty finds their numbers excessive, set strict rules against indiscriminate ordination and the problem will shrink on its own."
entries.literal: If Your Majesty dislikes their great number, strict regulations should be established to guard against indiscriminate ordination, and they would naturally diminish."

entries.zh: 襄曰：「出家之人安用僕隸？
entries.en: Xiang replied, "What need have renunciants for servants?
entries.literal: Xiang said: "Why should those who leave home need servants?

entries.zh: 乞不問從初如何所得，悉放為良。
entries.en: Regardless of how they were acquired, release them all as free commoners.
entries.literal: I ask that regardless of how they were originally obtained, all be released as commoners.

entries.zh: 若寺觀物力元系奴婢之數推定者，併合除免。」
entries.en: Any temple endowment calculated from slave quotas should be abolished as well."
entries.literal: If monasteries and temples had their property and resources calculated on the basis of slave numbers, let that too be abolished together."

entries.zh: 詔從襄言。
entries.en: The emperor issued an edict adopting Xiang's proposal.
entries.literal: An edict followed Xiang's view.

entries.zh: 由是二稅戶多為良者。
entries.en: Many secondary tax households were thereby made free commoners.
entries.literal: Thereupon many secondary tax households became commoners.

entries.zh: 夾谷衡，本名阿里不，山東西路三土猛安益打把謀克人也。
entries.en: Jiagu Heng, whose original name was Alibu, came from the Santu Meng'an Yida baimouke in Shandong West Circuit.
entries.literal: Jiagu Heng, original name Alibu, was a man of the Santu Meng'an Yida baimouke in Shandong West Circuit.

entries.zh: 大定十三年，創設女直進士舉，衡中第四人，補東平府教授。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of Dading, when the Jurchen jinshi examination was first instituted, Heng placed fourth and was appointed professor at Dongping Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dading, when the Jurchen jinshi examination was first established, Heng placed fourth and was appointed professor at Dongping Prefecture.

entries.zh: 調范陽簿，選充國史院編修官，改應奉翰林文字。
entries.en: He was transferred to assistant magistrate of Fanyang, selected as a compiler in the National History Institute, and then made a Hanlin text attendant.
entries.literal: Transferred to Fanyang assistant magistrate; selected as compiler in the National History Institute; changed to Hanlin text attendant.

entries.zh: 世宗嘗謂宰臣曰：「女直進士中才傑之士蓋亦難得，如徒單鎰、夾穀衡、尼龐古鑒，皆有用材也。」
entries.en: Shizong once told his chief ministers, "Truly outstanding men among the Jurchen jinshi are hard to find, but men like Tudan Yi, Jiagu Heng, and Nipanggu Jian are all useful talent."
entries.literal: Shizong once told the chief ministers: "Outstanding talent among Jurchen jinshi is hard to come by; men like Tudan Yi, Jiagu Heng, and Nipanggu Jian are all useful material."

entries.zh: 遷修起居注。
entries.en: He was transferred to compiler of the Diary of Activity and Repose.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Compiler of the Diary of Activity and Repose.

entries.zh: 章宗立，為侍御史，轉右司員外郎，敷奏稱旨，升左司郎中。
entries.en: When Zhangzong took the throne, he became Attending Censor, then was transferred to Assistant Director of the Right Department. His memorials pleased the throne, and he was promoted to Director of the Left Department.
entries.literal: When Zhangzong ascended the throne, he became Attending Censor, then transferred to Assistant Director of the Right Department; his memorials pleased the throne, and he was promoted to Director of the Left Department.

entries.zh: 明昌二年，擢御史中丞，未幾，拜參知政事。
entries.en: In the second year of Mingchang he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, and before long was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: In the second year of Mingchang he was elevated to Vice Censor-in-Chief; before long he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 三年八月，以病，表乞致仕，詔撫慰不許。
entries.en: In the eighth month of the third year he submitted a memorial asking to retire on account of illness. An edict comforted him and refused the request.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, on account of illness he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; an edict comforted him and refused.

entries.zh: 夾谷清臣
entries.en: Jiagu Qingchen
entries.literal: Jiagu Qingchen

entries.zh: 天興元年正月，朝廷聞大兵入饒風，移兀典行省閿鄉，以備潼關。
entries.en: In the first month of Tianxing 1 (1232), the court learned that the Mongol army had entered Raofeng. Wudian's provincial headquarters was transferred to Minxiang to prepare the defense of Tong Pass.
entries.literal: In the first month of the first year of Tianxing, the court heard that the great army had entered Raofeng; Wudian's provincial headquarters was moved to Minxiang to prepare the defense of Tong Pass.

entries.zh: 徒單百家為關陝總帥，便宜行事。
entries.en: Tudan Baijia was appointed overall commander of the Guan-Shaan region with discretionary authority.
entries.literal: Tudan Baijia was made overall commander of Guan and Shaan, with discretionary authority.

entries.zh: 百家馳入陝，榜州民雲：「淮南透漏軍馬，慮其道由潼關，勢不能守，縣鎮遷入大城，糧斛輜重聚之陝州，近山者入山寨避兵。」
entries.en: Baijia rode posthaste into Shaanzhou and posted a notice to the people: "Enemy forces have broken through from Huainan. Fearing they may advance by way of Tong Pass, we cannot hold this position. Move from the county towns into the major cities; concentrate grain and baggage at Shaanzhou; those near the mountains should take refuge in stockaded strongholds."
