entries.literal: In every attack on an enemy one must seize his throat and strike his heart.

entries.zh: 夏口、東關，賊之心喉。
entries.en: Xiakou and Dongguan are precisely those vital points.
entries.literal: Xiakou and Dongguan are that foe’s heart and throat.

entries.zh: 若為陸軍以向皖城，引權東下，為水戰軍向夏口，乘其虛而擊之，此神兵從天而墮，破之必矣。」
entries.en: Send infantry toward Wancheng to tug Sun Quan downstream while your fleet thrusts at Xiakou and catches him thin—that is an assault from heaven itself.”
entries.literal: If you march a field army toward Wancheng and draw Sun Quan eastward, while a river force pushes toward Xiakou and hits him where he is weak, it will be like heavenly troops falling from the sky—you will surely break him.”

entries.zh: 天子並然之，復命帝屯於宛。
entries.en: The emperor endorsed it wholeheartedly and told him once more to hold Wan.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven deeply approved and again ordered the Emperor to encamp at Wan.

entries.zh: 初，蜀將孟達之降也，魏朝遇之甚厚。
entries.en: Earlier, when Shu’s general Meng Da defected, Wei showered him with favor.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Shu general Meng Da had surrendered, the Wei court treated him generously.

entries.zh: 帝以達言行傾巧不可任，驟諫不見聽，乃以達領新城太守，封侯，假節。
entries.en: He judged Da’s tongue treacherous and untrustworthy; repeated remonstrance failed, so Da received acting prefect of Xincheng, a marquisate, and the credential axe.
entries.literal: The Emperor deemed Da’s words and conduct slippery and unreliable; though he remonstrated repeatedly he was not heard, and Da was made acting prefect of Xincheng, enfeoffed as a marquis, and given the ceremonial axe.

entries.zh: 達於是連吳固蜀，潛圖中國。
entries.en: Da then stitched Wu to Shu and schemed against the heartland in secret.
entries.literal: Da then allied with Wu and Shu and secretly plotted against the central plains.

entries.zh: 蜀相諸葛亮惡其反覆，又慮其為患。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang despised his flip-flopping and dreaded the chaos he might unleash.
entries.literal: Shu’s chancellor Zhuge Liang despised his vacillation and also feared he would cause trouble.

entries.zh: 達與魏興太守申儀有隙，亮欲促其事，乃遣郭模詐降，過儀，因漏泄其謀。
entries.en: Da quarrelled with Shen Yi of Weixing; Liang hurried matters by sending Guo Mo under false colors past Yi to spill the conspiracy.
entries.literal: Da had a rift with Shen Yi, prefect of Weixing; Liang wished to hasten matters and sent Guo Mo feigning surrender, who passed through Yi and leaked the plot.

entries.zh: 達聞其謀漏泄，將舉兵。
entries.en: Once Da learned the secret was out, he prepared to rebel.
entries.literal: When Da heard his plot had leaked, he prepared to rise in arms.

entries.zh: 帝恐達速發，以書喻之曰：「將軍昔棄劉備，託身國家，國家委將軍以疆埸之任，任將軍以圖蜀之事，可謂心貫白日。
entries.en: Fearing a swift rising, he wrote: “You abandoned Liu Bei for us; we placed the border in your hands and tasked you with Shu—your loyalty blazes like noon.
entries.literal: The Emperor feared Da would move quickly and wrote to him: “General, you once abandoned Liu Bei and entrusted yourself to the state; the state entrusted you with the frontier and charged you with planning against Shu—your heart may be said to pierce the bright sun.

entries.zh: 蜀人愚智，莫不切齒於將軍。
entries.en: Every Shu soul, wise or dull, grinds teeth at your name.
entries.literal: Wise or foolish, everyone in Shu gnashes teeth at you.

entries.zh: 諸葛亮欲相破，惟苦無路耳。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang longs to ruin you yet lacked a lever until now.
entries.literal: Zhuge Liang wishes to destroy you but only lacks the means.

entries.zh: 模之所言，非小事也，亮豈輕之而令宣露，此殆易知耳。」
entries.en: Mo’s tale is no gossip—would Zhuge Liang broadcast it carelessly? The answer is plain.”
entries.literal: What Mo said is no trifle—would Liang treat it lightly and let it spread? This is easy to see.”

entries.zh: 達得書大喜，猶與不決。
entries.en: Da read the letter with delight yet still wavered.
entries.literal: Da received the letter and was greatly pleased, yet still hesitated.

entries.zh: 帝乃潛軍進討。
entries.en: He then stole forward with the army.
entries.literal: The Emperor then secretly advanced to attack.

entries.zh: 諸將言達與二賊交構，宜觀望而後動。
entries.en: His officers argued Da colluded with both enemies and urged caution.
entries.literal: The generals said Da was in league with the two foes and they should watch and wait before acting.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「達無信義，此其相疑之時也，當及其未定促決之。」
entries.en: He said, “Da knows no loyalty—this is the hour of mutual doubt; strike before his camp steadies.”
entries.literal: The Emperor said, “Da lacks good faith; this is when mutual suspicion reigns—we must strike before he is settled.”

entries.zh: 乃倍道兼行，八日到其城下。
entries.en: He forced the march and reached the walls in eight days.
entries.literal: He therefore doubled the march and in eight days reached the walls.

entries.zh: 吳蜀各遣其將向西城安橋、木闌塞以救達，帝分諸將以距之。
entries.en: Wu and Shu each rushed columns toward Xicheng, An Bridge, and Mulansai to rescue Da; he split commands to intercept them.
entries.literal: Wu and Shu each sent generals toward Xicheng, Anqiao, and Mulansai to relieve Da; the Emperor divided his generals to block them.

entries.zh: 太和元年六月，天子詔帝屯于宛，加督荊、豫二州諸軍事。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the first year of Taihe (227), the Son of Heaven ordered the emperor to garrison at Wan and additionally placed him in command of military affairs in Jing and Yu provinces.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Taihe (227), the Son of Heaven ordered the emperor to garrison at Wan and additionally placed him in command of military affairs in Jing and Yu provinces.

entries.zh: 初，申儀久在魏興，專威疆埸，輒承制刻印，多所假授。
entries.en: Shen Yi had dominated Weixing for years—running the border like a private fief, minting seals without sanction, and handing out titles at will.
entries.literal: Earlier, Shen Yi had long held Weixing, arrogated authority along the frontier, repeatedly carved seals on his own authority, and handed out many irregular appointments.

entries.zh: 達既誅，有自疑心。
entries.en: Once Meng Da fell, Shen Yi began to doubt his own safety.
entries.literal: After Da was put to death, Yi grew suspicious of his own position.

entries.zh: 時諸郡守以帝新克捷，奉禮求賀，皆聽之。
entries.en: County governors arrived with congratulations on his fresh triumph; he received every delegation.
entries.literal: At that time the various prefects, because the Emperor had just won a victory, brought gifts seeking congratulation; he accepted them all.

entries.zh: 帝使人諷儀，儀至，問承制狀，執之，歸于京師。
entries.en: He hinted until Shen Yi appeared at audience, pressed him on those self-made commissions, arrested him, and shipped him east.
entries.literal: The Emperor sent someone to sound out Yi; when Yi came to court he questioned him about his unauthorized appointments, seized him, and sent him to the capital.

entries.zh: 又徙孟達餘眾七千餘家於幽州。
entries.en: He resettled over seven thousand surviving households of Meng Da’s remnant followers in Youzhou.
entries.literal: He also relocated more than seven thousand households of Meng Da’s remnant followers to Youzhou.

entries.zh: 蜀將姚靜、鄭他等帥其屬七千餘人來降。
entries.en: Yao Jing and Zheng Ta of Shu marched in over seven thousand troops to defect.
entries.literal: Shu generals Yao Jing and Zheng Ta led their followers—more than seven thousand men—to surrender.

entries.zh: 時軍師杜襲、督軍薛悌皆言明年麥熟，亮必為寇，隴右無穀，宜及冬豫運。
entries.en: Du Xi and Xue Ti warned that next harvest Zhuge Liang would return while Longyou starved—haul grain before winter.
entries.literal: At that time army adviser Du Xi and supervisor Xue Ti both said that when the wheat ripened the next year Liang would surely raid again; Longyou lacked grain and supplies ought to be moved before winter.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「亮再出祁山，一攻陳倉，挫衄而反。
entries.en: He answered: “Twice from Qishan, once at Chencang—each time repulsed.
entries.literal: The Emperor said: “Liang has twice emerged from Qishan and once assaulted Chencang—each time he was beaten back.

entries.zh: 縱其後出，不復攻城，當求野戰，必在隴東，不在西也。
entries.en: Next time he will hunt open battle east of the Long ridges, not west.
entries.literal: Even if he comes out again he will not storm cities; he will seek a field battle east of Long, not west.

entries.zh: 亮每以糧少為恨，歸必積穀，以吾料之，非三稔不能動矣。」
entries.en: Grain gnaws at him—every retreat piles granaries. He cannot march for three full crops.”
entries.literal: Liang always lamented his shortage of grain; whenever he withdrew he stockpiled—by my reckoning he cannot move for three harvests.”

entries.zh: 於是表徙冀州農夫佃上邽，興京兆、天水、南安監冶。
entries.en: He filed to transplant Ji farmers onto Shanggui fields and to tool imperial armories in Jingzhao, Tianshui, and Nan’an.
entries.literal: He therefore memorialized to move tenant farmers from Ji Province up to Shanggui and to establish government foundries in Jingzhao, Tianshui, and Nan’an.

entries.zh: 是時大修宮室，加之以軍旅，百姓饑弊。
entries.en: Court architects ran wild while armies marched—the people starved under both burdens.
entries.literal: At that time palace construction was greatly expanded and military campaigns piled on; the common people were hungry and exhausted.

entries.zh: 帝將即戎，乃諫曰：「昔周公營洛邑，蕭何造未央，今宮室未備，臣之責也。
entries.en: When the emperor was about to go to war, he remonstrated, saying, "In the past, the Duke of Zhou built Luoyi, and Xiao He built Weiyang. Now that the palace buildings are not yet complete, it is my responsibility.
entries.literal: When the emperor was about to go to war, he remonstrated, saying, "In the past, the Duke of Zhou built Luoyi, and Xiao He built Weiyang. Now that the palace buildings are not yet complete, it is my responsibility.

entries.zh: 然自河以北，百姓困窮，外內有役，勢不並興，宜假絕內務，以救時急。」
entries.en: Yet north of the Yellow River, the people are impoverished; there are labor services both outside and inside, and the situation does not allow both to be undertaken at once. The inner works should be temporarily cut off, in order to save the current emergency."
entries.literal: Yet north of the Yellow River, the people are impoverished; there are labor services both outside and inside, and the situation does not allow both to be undertaken at once. The inner works should be temporarily cut off, in order to save the current emergency."

entries.zh: 景初二年，帥牛金、胡遵等步騎四萬，發自京都。
entries.en: Jingchu year two: forty thousand horse and foot under Niu Jin and Hu Zun left Luoyang.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jingchu (238) he led Niu Jin, Hu Zun, and others with forty thousand infantry and cavalry out of the capital.

entries.zh: 車駕送出西明門，詔弟孚、子師送過溫，賜以穀帛牛酒，敕郡守典農以下皆往會焉。
entries.en: The imperial carriage escorted him out through the Ximing Gate; an edict ordered his younger brother Fu and son Shi to see him past Wen, awarding grain, silk, cattle, and wine, and commanded the prefects and agricultural directors downward to assemble.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage escorted him through the Ximing Gate; an edict ordered his younger brother Fu and son Shi to see him past Wen, awarding grain, silk, cattle, and wine, and commanded the prefect and agricultural director downward to assemble.

entries.zh: 見父老故舊，讌飲累日。
entries.en: He lingered with hometown elders over cups for night after night.
entries.literal: He met elders and old friends and feasted for days on end.

entries.zh: 帝歎息，悵然有感，為歌曰：「天地開闢，日月重光。
entries.en: The emperor sighed and, moved with melancholy, made a song, saying, "Heaven and earth opened, sun and moon shone anew.
entries.literal: The emperor sighed and, moved with melancholy, made a song, saying, "Heaven and earth opened, sun and moon shone anew.

entries.zh: 遭遇際會，畢力遐方。
entries.en: Encountering the moment of meeting, I spend all strength in distant regions.
entries.literal: Encountering the moment of meeting, I spend all strength in distant regions.

entries.zh: 將掃羣穢，還過故鄉。
entries.en: I am about to sweep away the massed filth, and on return pass through my old home.
entries.literal: I am about to sweep away the massed filth, and on return pass through my old home.

entries.zh: 肅清萬里，總齊八荒。
entries.en: Purifying ten thousand li, I shall gather and order the eight wastes.
entries.literal: Purifying ten thousand li, I shall gather and order the eight wastes.

entries.zh: 告成歸老，待罪舞陽。」
entries.en: When success is reported, I will return old and await punishment at Wuyang."
entries.literal: When success is reported, I will return old and await punishment at Wuyang."

entries.zh: 遂進師，經孤竹，越碣石，次于遼水。
entries.en: The columns rolled past Guzhu and Jieshi to the Liao.
entries.literal: Thereupon he advanced the army, passed Guzhu, crossed Jieshi, and halted at the Liao River.

entries.zh: 文懿果遣步騎數萬，阻遼隧，堅壁而守，南北六七十里，以距帝。
entries.en: Gongsun Yuan plugged Liaosui with tens of thousands—palisades stretched seventy li along the narrows.
entries.literal: Wenyi indeed sent several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to block Liaosui, fortifying walls and holding sixty or seventy li north to south against the Emperor.

entries.zh: 帝盛兵多張旗幟出其南，賊盡銳赴之。
entries.en: Sima Yi feigned strength on the southern bank and drew the Liaodong army off.
entries.literal: The Emperor massed troops and unfurled many banners south of them; the rebels committed every elite regiment there.

entries.zh: 乃泛舟潛濟以出其北，與賊營相逼，沈舟焚梁，傍遼水作長圍，棄賊而向襄平。
entries.en: Under cover of dark water he slipped upstream, burned the crossings, pinned the Liao with earthworks, and ignored the camp for Xiangping.
entries.literal: He then floated boats and secretly crossed to their north, pressing against their camp—sank boats, burned bridges, threw a long cordon along the Liao, abandoned the enemy column, and marched on Xiangping.

entries.zh: 諸將言曰：「不攻賊而作圍，非所以示眾也。」
entries.en: The generals said, "To make a siege without attacking the enemy is not the way to show resolve to the troops."
entries.literal: The generals said, "To make a siege without attacking the enemy is not the way to show resolve to the troops."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「賊堅營高壘，欲以老吾兵也。
entries.en: The emperor said, "The enemy has made a firm camp and high ramparts because he wants to wear out our troops.
entries.literal: The emperor said, "The enemy has made a firm camp and high ramparts because he wants to wear out our troops.

entries.zh: 攻之，正入其計，此王邑所以恥過昆陽也。
entries.en: If we attack it, we fall exactly into his plan; this is why Wang Yi was shamed at Kunyang.
entries.literal: If we attack it, we fall exactly into his plan; this is why Wang Yi was shamed at Kunyang.

entries.zh: 古人曰，敵雖高壘，不得不與我戰者，攻其所必救也。
entries.en: The ancients said that even if the enemy has high ramparts, he cannot avoid fighting us if we attack what he must rescue.
entries.literal: The ancients said that even if the enemy has high ramparts, he cannot avoid fighting us if we attack what he must rescue.

entries.zh: 賊大眾在此，則巢窟虛矣。
entries.en: The enemy's main force is here, so their nest is empty.
entries.literal: The enemy's main force is here, so their nest is empty.

entries.zh: 我直指襄平，則人懷內懼，懼而求戰，破之必矣。」
entries.en: If I point straight at Xiangping, then the people will harbor internal fear; fearing, they will seek battle, and I will certainly defeat them."
entries.literal: If I point straight at Xiangping, then the people will harbor internal fear; fearing, they will seek battle, and I will certainly defeat them."

entries.zh: 遂整陣而過。
entries.en: He aligned divisions and slipped past.
entries.literal: Thereupon he dressed ranks and marched through.

entries.zh: 賊見兵出其後，果邀之。
entries.en: The Liaodong army wheeled about to cut him off.
entries.literal: When the rebels saw troops emerge behind them they indeed tried to intercept.

entries.zh: 帝謂諸將曰：「所以不攻其營，正欲致此，不可失也。」
entries.en: The emperor told the generals, "The reason I did not attack their camp was precisely because I wanted to bring this about. We must not lose it."
entries.literal: The emperor told the generals, "The reason I did not attack their camp was precisely because I wanted to bring this about. We must not lose it."

entries.zh: 乃縱兵逆擊，大破之，三戰皆捷。
entries.en: He hurled the lines forward and routed them thrice running.
entries.literal: He then unleashed troops in a counterattack and shattered them; three engagements brought three victories.

entries.zh: 賊保襄平，進軍圍之。
entries.en: They fled inside Xiangping; he tightened the ring.
entries.literal: The rebels held Xiangping; he advanced and invested it.

entries.zh: 會霖潦，大水平地數尺，三軍恐，欲移營。
entries.en: Monsoon floods drowned the plain; men clamored to move.
entries.literal: Seasonal rains poured; floodwaters stood several chi deep on level ground; the three armies feared and wished to shift camp.

entries.zh: 帝令軍中敢有言徙者斬。
entries.en: He threatened death for talk of redeployment.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered that whoever spoke of relocating be executed.

entries.zh: 都督令史張靜犯令，斬之，軍中乃定。
entries.en: Zhang Jing broke the rule and lost his head—the ranks fell silent.
entries.literal: Supervisory clerk Zhang Jing violated the order and was beheaded—only then did the army steady.

entries.zh: 賊恃水，樵牧自若。
entries.en: The defenders still sent out woodcutters as if dry.
entries.literal: The rebels trusted the water and gathered firewood and grazed cattle as usual.

entries.zh: 諸將欲取之，皆不聽。
entries.en: Staff urged raids on foragers; he refused each time.
entries.literal: The generals wished to seize those parties; he forbade every proposal.

entries.zh: 司馬陳珪曰：「昔攻上庸，八部並進，晝夜不息，故能一旬之半，拔堅城，斬孟達。
entries.en: Army officer Chen Gui said, "In the past, when we attacked Shangyong, eight divisions advanced together and did not rest day or night; therefore in half a ten-day period we were able to take a firm city and behead Meng Da.
entries.literal: Army officer Chen Gui said, "In the past, when we attacked Shangyong, eight divisions advanced together and did not rest day or night; therefore in half a ten-day period we were able to take a firm city and behead Meng Da.

entries.zh: 今者遠來而更安緩，愚竊惑焉。」
entries.en: Now we have come from afar and instead are calm and slow; foolishly, I am privately puzzled by it."
entries.literal: Now we have come from afar and instead are calm and slow; foolishly, I am privately puzzled by it."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「孟達眾少而食支一年，吾將士四倍于達而糧不淹月，以一月圖一年，安可不速？
entries.en: The emperor said, "Meng Da's men were few, and his food could support a year. My officers and soldiers are four times Da's, but our grain will not last a month. To plan for one year with one month, how could we not be quick?
entries.literal: The emperor said, "Meng Da's men were few, and his food could support a year. My officers and soldiers are four times Da's, but our grain will not last a month. To plan for one year with one month, how could we not be quick?

entries.zh: 以四擊一，正令半解，猶當為之。
entries.en: Using four to attack one, even if half deserted, we still had to do it.
entries.literal: Using four to attack one, even if half deserted, we still had to do it.

entries.zh: 是以不計死傷，與糧競也。
entries.en: For this reason we did not count death and injury; we were racing against grain.
entries.literal: For this reason we did not count death and injury; we were racing against grain.

entries.zh: 今賊眾我寡，賊飢我飽，水雨乃爾，功力不設，雖當促之，亦何所為。
entries.en: Now the enemy is many and we are few; the enemy is hungry and we are full. With rain and water like this, works cannot be set up. Even if we should hurry him, what would it accomplish?
entries.literal: Now the enemy is many and we are few; the enemy is hungry and we are full. With rain and water like this, works cannot be set up. Even if we should hurry him, what would it accomplish?

entries.zh: 自發京師，不憂賊攻，但恐賊走。
entries.en: Since leaving the capital, I have not worried that the enemy would attack; I only feared that the enemy would flee.
entries.literal: Since leaving the capital, I have not worried that the enemy would attack; I only feared that the enemy would flee.

entries.zh: 今賊糧垂盡，而圍落未合，掠其牛馬，抄其樵采，此故驅之走也。
entries.en: Now the enemy's grain is nearly exhausted, but the encirclement is not complete. To seize his cattle and horses and raid his woodcutters and gatherers would deliberately drive him to flee.
entries.literal: Now the enemy's grain is nearly exhausted, but the encirclement is not complete. To seize his cattle and horses and raid his woodcutters and gatherers would deliberately drive him to flee.

entries.zh: 夫兵者詭道，善因事變。
entries.en: War is the way of deception, and the skillful respond to changes in affairs.
entries.literal: War is the way of deception, and the skillful respond to changes in affairs.

entries.zh: 賊憑眾恃雨，故雖飢困，未肯束手，當示無能以安之。
entries.en: The enemy relies on numbers and trusts to the rain; therefore, though hungry and distressed, he is not yet willing to bind his hands. We should show inability in order to reassure him.
entries.literal: The enemy relies on numbers and trusts to the rain; therefore, though hungry and distressed, he is not yet willing to bind his hands. We should show inability in order to reassure him.

entries.zh: 取小利以驚之。
entries.en: To take small advantages and alarm him
entries.literal: To take small advantages and alarm him

entries.zh: 非計也。」
entries.en: is not a plan."
entries.literal: is not a plan."

entries.zh: 朝廷聞師遇雨，咸請召還。
entries.en: Luoyang heard mud and demanded withdrawal.
entries.literal: The court heard the army met rain and all petitioned recall.

entries.zh: 天子曰：「司馬公臨危制變，計日擒之矣。」
entries.en: The Son of Heaven said, "Sima Gong controls change in the face of danger; he will capture him on the calculated day."
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven said, "Sima Gong controls change in the face of danger; he will capture him on the calculated day."

entries.zh: 既而雨止，遂合圍。
entries.en: Skies cleared; the ring closed.
entries.literal: Soon the rain stopped and they completed the cordon.

entries.zh: 起土山地道，楯櫓鉤橦，發矢石雨下，晝夜攻之。
entries.en: They stacked siege mounds, bored mines, and hailed stone until the walls shook.
entries.literal: They piled earth hills and dug tunnels—shields, rams, hooks—arrows and stones rained in assault day and night.

entries.zh: 時有長星，色白，有芒鬣，自襄平城西南流于東北，墜於梁水，城中震慴。
entries.en: A white comet streaked from Xiangping’s southwest to the Liang—terror seized the town.
entries.literal: At that time a long comet appeared, white with bristling rays, flowing from southwest of Xiangping toward northeast, falling into the Liang River—the city shook with terror.

entries.zh: 文懿大懼，乃使其所署相國王建、御史大夫柳甫乞降，請解圍面縛。
entries.en: Yuan sent Wang Jian and Liu Fu pleading for the siege to lift so he could come out with bound hands.
entries.literal: Wenyi was terrified and sent his appointed Chancellor Wang Jian and Imperial Counselor Liu Fu to beg surrender, asking to lift the siege so he could bind himself.

entries.zh: 不許，執建等，皆斬之。
entries.en: Sima Yi refused—seized the envoys and took their heads.
entries.literal: He did not consent—seized Jian and the others and executed them all.

entries.zh: 檄告文懿曰：「昔楚鄭列國，而鄭伯猶肉袒牽羊而迎之。
entries.en: A proclamation informed Wenyì, saying, "In the past, Chu and Zheng were ranked states, yet the Earl of Zheng still bared his flesh, led a sheep, and went out to meet Chu.
entries.literal: A proclamation informed Wenyì, saying, "In the past, Chu and Zheng were ranked states, yet the Earl of Zheng still bared his flesh, led a sheep, and went out to meet Chu.

entries.zh: 孤為王人，位則上公，而建等欲孤解圍退舍，豈楚鄭之謂邪！
entries.en: I am a man of the king, and my rank is that of an upper duke, yet Jian and the others wanted me to lift the siege and withdraw. Is this what was meant by Chu and Zheng?
entries.literal: I am a man of the king, and my rank is that of an upper duke, yet Jian and the others wanted me to lift the siege and withdraw. Is this what was meant by Chu and Zheng?

entries.zh: 二人老耄，必傳言失旨，已相為斬之。
entries.en: The two men were old and confused and must have transmitted words contrary to their intent, so I have beheaded them for you.
entries.literal: The two men were old and confused and must have transmitted words contrary to their intent, so I have beheaded them for you.

entries.zh: 若意有未已，可更遣年少有明決者來。」
entries.en: If your intention is not yet exhausted, you may send another younger man with clarity and resolution."
entries.literal: If your intention is not yet exhausted, you may send another younger man with clarity and resolution."

entries.zh: 文懿復遣侍中衞演乞剋日送任。
entries.en: Yuan tried again—Wei Yan begging a hostage deadline.
entries.literal: Wenyi again sent attendant Wei Yan requesting a fixed day to deliver hostages.

entries.zh: 帝謂演曰：「軍事大要有五，能戰當戰，不能戰當守，不能守當走，餘二事惟有降與死耳。
entries.en: The emperor told Yan, "There are five essentials in military affairs: if one can fight, one should fight; if one cannot fight, one should defend; if one cannot defend, one should flee. The remaining two matters are only surrender and death.
entries.literal: The emperor told Yan, "There are five essentials in military affairs: if one can fight, one should fight; if one cannot fight, one should defend; if one cannot defend, one should flee. The remaining two matters are only surrender and death.

entries.zh: 汝不肯面縛，此為決就死也，不須送任。」
entries.en: You are unwilling to bind yourself face-forward; this means you have decided to go to death. There is no need to send hostages."
entries.literal: You are unwilling to bind yourself face-forward; this means you have decided to go to death. There is no need to send hostages."

entries.zh: 文懿攻南圍突出，帝縱兵擊敗之，斬于梁水之上星墜之所。
entries.en: Yuan rammed the southern sector; Sima Yi crushed him and struck off his head where the comet had plunged.
entries.literal: Wenyi assaulted the southern siege line trying to break out; the Emperor unleashed troops, defeated him, and beheaded him at the spot where the star fell above the Liang River.

entries.zh: 既入城，立兩標以別新舊焉。
entries.en: Inside the walls twin posts marked who belonged to the revolt.
entries.literal: After entering the city he erected two markers to separate new guilt from old inhabitants.

entries.zh: 男子年十五已上七千餘人皆殺之，以為京觀。
entries.en: Seven thousand males above fifteen died for the victory mound.
entries.literal: All males fifteen sui and older—more than seven thousand—were executed to form a burial mound.

entries.zh: 偽公卿已下皆伏誅，戮其將軍畢盛等二千餘人。
entries.en: Phony ministers died with two thousand officers including Bi Sheng.
entries.literal: All false dukes and ministers downward were executed; more than two thousand including general Bi Sheng were put to death.

entries.zh: 收戶四萬，口三十餘萬。
entries.en: Registers captured forty thousand households and three hundred thousand people.
entries.literal: Households registered numbered forty thousand; mouths exceeded three hundred thousand.

entries.zh: 初，文懿篡其叔父恭位而囚之。
entries.en: Yuan had seized Uncle Gong’s seat and jailed him.
entries.literal: Earlier Wenyi had usurped his uncle Gong’s position and imprisoned him.

entries.zh: 及將反，將軍綸直、賈範等苦諫，文懿皆殺之。
entries.en: On the eve of revolt Lun Zhi and Jia Fan pleaded—Yuan murdered them.
entries.literal: When about to rebel generals Lun Zhi and Jia Fan remonstrated bitterly—Wenyi executed them all.

entries.zh: 帝乃釋恭之囚，封直等之墓，顯其遺嗣。
entries.en: Sima Yi freed Gong, rebuilt martyrs’ graves, and ennobled their sons.
entries.literal: The Emperor then released Gong from prison, tended the tombs of Zhi and others, and honored their surviving heirs.

entries.zh: 令曰：「古之伐國，誅其鯨鯢而已，諸為文懿所詿誤者，皆原之。
entries.en: The order said, "In antiquity, when states were attacked, only their great criminals were executed. All those misled by Wenyì are pardoned.
entries.literal: The order said, "In antiquity, when states were attacked, only their great criminals were executed. All those misled by Wenyì are pardoned.

entries.zh: 中國人欲還舊鄉，恣聽之。」
entries.en: If people from the Central States wish to return to their old villages, let them do so freely."
entries.literal: If people from the Central States wish to return to their old villages, let them do so freely."

entries.zh: 時有兵士寒凍，乞襦，帝弗之與。
entries.en: Frozen troops begged quilts; he withheld them.
entries.literal: At that time soldiers freezing in the cold begged for padded jackets; the Emperor did not grant them.

entries.zh: 或曰：「幸多故襦，可以賜之。」
entries.en: Someone said, "Fortunately there are many old padded jackets; they can be given to them."
entries.literal: Someone said, "Fortunately there are many old padded jackets; they can be given to them."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「襦者官物，人臣無私施也。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Padded jackets are government property; a minister may not dispense them privately."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "Padded jackets are government property; a minister may not dispense them privately."

entries.zh: 乃奏軍人年六十已上者罷遣千餘人，將吏從軍死亡者致喪還家。
entries.en: He cashiered thousand greybeards and shipped coffins west.
entries.literal: He then memorialized to discharge over a thousand soldiers aged sixty and above and to send home the remains of officers who died on campaign.

entries.zh: 遂班師。
entries.en: Then he marched home.
entries.literal: Thereupon he withdrew the army.

entries.zh: 天子遣使者勞軍于薊，增封食昆陽，并前二縣。
entries.en: Envoys met him at Ji with fresh fiefs—Kunyang added to two older counties.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven dispatched envoys to reward the army at Ji, enlarged the grain income with Kunyang, together with the previous two counties.

entries.zh: 初，文懿聞魏師之出也，請救於孫權。
entries.en: Gongsun Yuan had cried to Sun Quan when Wei stirred.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Wenyi heard the Wei army had marched, he begged rescue from Sun Quan.

entries.zh: 權亦出兵遙為之聲援，遺文懿書曰：「司馬公善用兵，變化若神，所向無前，深為弟憂之。」
entries.en: Quan also sent troops from afar to make a show of support and sent Wenyì a letter, saying, "Sima Gong is good at using troops; his changes are like those of a spirit, and nothing stands before him wherever he turns. I am deeply worried for you, younger brother."
entries.literal: Quan also sent troops from afar to make a show of support and sent Wenyì a letter, saying, "Sima Gong is good at using troops; his changes are like those of a spirit, and nothing stands before him wherever he turns. I am deeply worried for you, younger brother."

entries.zh: 初，帝至襄平，夢天子枕其膝，曰：「視吾面。」
entries.en: Earlier, when the emperor reached Xiangping, he dreamed that the Son of Heaven rested his head on his knees and said, "Look at my face."
entries.literal: Earlier, when the emperor reached Xiangping, he dreamed that the Son of Heaven rested his head on his knees and said, "Look at my face."

entries.zh: 俛視有異於常，心惡之。
entries.en: Stooping to look, it differed from the ordinary, and his heart abhorred it.
entries.literal: Stooping to look it differed from the ordinary—his heart reviled it.

entries.zh: 先是，詔帝便道鎮關中；
entries.en: Orders already told him to guard Guanzhong by detour.
entries.literal: Earlier an edict had ordered the Emperor by convenient route to hold Guanzhong;

entries.zh: 及次白屋，有詔召帝，三日之間，詔書五至。
entries.en: At Baiwu five summons arrived in three days.
entries.literal: When halting at Baiwu edicts summoned the Emperor—within three days five edicts arrived.

entries.zh: 手詔曰：「間側息望到，到便直排閤入，視吾面。」
entries.en: The handwritten edict said, "I am lying on my side, breath held, hoping you arrive. When you arrive, push straight through the doors and enter; look at my face."
entries.literal: The handwritten edict said, "I am lying on my side, breath held, hoping you arrive. When you arrive, push straight through the doors and enter; look at my face."

entries.zh: 帝大遽，乃乘追鋒車晝夜兼行，自白屋四百餘里，一宿而至。
entries.en: Panic drove the relay carriage four hundred li overnight.
entries.literal: The Emperor was greatly alarmed and rode the pursuit-chariot day and night—more than four hundred li from Baiwu, arriving in one night.

entries.zh: 引入嘉福殿臥內，升御牀。
entries.en: He was led into the inner chamber of Jiafu Hall and helped onto the imperial couch.
entries.literal: He was conducted into the Jiafu Palace inner chamber and helped onto the imperial couch.

entries.zh: 帝流涕問疾，天子執帝手，目齊王曰：「以後事相託。
entries.en: The emperor wept and asked about his illness. The Son of Heaven took the emperor's hand, looked at the Prince of Qi, and said, "I entrust later affairs to you.
entries.literal: The emperor wept and asked about his illness. The Son of Heaven took the emperor's hand, looked at the Prince of Qi, and said, "I entrust later affairs to you.

entries.zh: 死乃復可忍，吾忍死待君，得相見，無所復恨矣。」
entries.en: Only now can I bear to die. I endured death waiting for you; having seen you, I have no further regret."
entries.literal: Only now can I bear to die. I endured death waiting for you; having seen you, I have no further regret."

entries.zh: 與大將軍曹爽並受遺詔輔少主。
entries.en: He and Cao Shuang sealed regency for the boy emperor.
entries.literal: Together with Grand General Cao Shuang he received testamentary edicts to aid the young lord.

entries.zh: 及齊王即帝位，遷侍中、持節、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，與爽各統兵三千人，共執朝政，更直殿中，乘輿入殿。
entries.en: When the Prince of Qi ascended the throne, Sima Yi was promoted to palace attendant, bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of all armies inside and outside the capital, and recorder of affairs of the Secretariat. He and Shuang each commanded three thousand troops, jointly held court government, took turns on duty in the palace, and entered the palace by carriage.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Qi ascended the throne, Sima Yi was promoted to palace attendant, bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of all armies inside and outside the capital, and recorder of affairs of the Secretariat. He and Shuang each commanded three thousand troops, jointly held court government, took turns on duty in the palace, and entered the palace by carriage.

entries.zh: 爽欲使尚書奏事先由己，乃言於天子，徙帝為大司馬。
entries.en: Shuang wanted memorials from the Secretariat to pass through him first, and therefore spoke to the Son of Heaven and transferred the emperor to be grand marshal.
entries.literal: Shuang wanted memorials from the Secretariat to pass through him first, and therefore spoke to the Son of Heaven and transferred the emperor to be grand marshal.

entries.zh: 朝議以為前後大司馬累薨於位，乃以帝為太傅，入殿不趨，贊拜不名，劍履上殿，如漢蕭何故事。
entries.en: Court discussion held that former grand marshals had repeatedly died in office, and so the emperor was made grand tutor instead. He entered the palace hall without hurrying, was announced in audiences without being named, and went up into the hall with sword and shoes, following the precedent of Xiao He of Han.
entries.literal: Court discussion held that former grand marshals had repeatedly died in office, and so the emperor was made grand tutor instead. He entered the palace hall without hurrying, was announced in audiences without being named, and went up into the hall with sword and shoes, following the precedent of Xiao He of Han.

entries.zh: 嫁娶喪葬取給於官，以世子師為散騎常侍，子弟三人為列侯，四人為騎都尉。
entries.en: Marriage and funeral expenses were supplied by the government; his heir Shi was made palace attendant cavalier, three sons and younger kinsmen were made listed marquises, and four were made cavalry commandants.
entries.literal: Marriage and funeral expenses were supplied by the government; his heir Shi was made palace attendant cavalier, three sons and younger kinsmen were made listed marquises, and four were made cavalry commandants.

entries.zh: 帝固讓子弟官不受。
entries.en: The emperor firmly declined the offices for his sons and younger kinsmen and did not accept them.
entries.literal: The emperor firmly declined the offices for his sons and younger kinsmen and did not accept them.

entries.zh: 正始元年春正月，東倭重譯納貢，焉耆、危須諸國，弱水以南，鮮卑名王，皆遣使來獻。
entries.en: In spring, the first month of the first year of Zhengshi (240), Eastern Wa sent tribute through multiple interpreters; Yanqi, Weixu, the states south of Ruoshui, and Xianbei titled kings all sent envoys to present offerings.
entries.literal: In spring, the first month of the first year of Zhengshi (240), Eastern Wa sent tribute through multiple interpreters; Yanqi, Weixu, the states south of Ruoshui, and Xianbei titled kings all sent envoys to present offerings.

entries.zh: 天子歸美宰輔，又增帝封邑。
entries.en: The court credited the ministers and fattened Sima Yi’s lands.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven attributed glory to the chief ministers and again enlarged the Emperor’s fief.

entries.zh: 初，魏明帝好修宮室，制度靡麗，百姓苦之。
entries.en: Mingdi’s terraces had bled the people.
entries.literal: Earlier Wei Mingdi loved constructing palaces—standards extravagant—the common people suffered.

entries.zh: 帝自遼東還，役者猶萬餘人，雕玩之物動以千計。
entries.en: Ten thousand corvée hands still carved gewgaws by the thousand.
entries.literal: When the Emperor returned from Liaodong laborers still numbered over ten thousand; carved trinkets mounted by thousands.

entries.zh: 至是皆奏罷之，節用務農，天下欣賴焉。
entries.en: He stopped the yards, urged ploughs—the empire sighed relief.
entries.literal: At this point all were memorialized to cease—economizing and promoting farming—the realm rejoiced and relied on him.

entries.zh: 二年夏五月，吳將全琮寇芍陂，朱然、孫倫圍樊城，諸葛瑾、步騭掠柤中，帝請自討之。
entries.en: Year two summer—Quan Zong hit Quebei, Zhu Ran and Sun Lun pinned Fan, Zhuge Jin and Bu Zhi ravaged Zhazhong—Sima Yi asked to ride south.
entries.literal: Summer fifth month second year—Wu general Quan Zong raided Quebei; Zhu Ran and Sun Lun besieged Fancheng; Zhuge Jin and Bu Zhi raided Zhazhong—the Emperor requested to campaign himself.

entries.zh: 議者咸言，賊遠來圍樊，不可卒拔。
entries.en: Court wise men argued Wu sat far off—Fan would not fall fast.
entries.literal: Discussants all said the rebels came from afar to besiege Fan—it cannot be quickly taken.

entries.zh: 挫於堅城之下，有自破之勢，宜長策以御之。
entries.en: Let prolonged defense drain them.
entries.literal: Frustrated beneath stout walls they tend toward self-collapse—a long strategy should answer them.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「邊城受敵而安坐廟堂，疆埸騷動，眾心疑惑，是社稷之大憂也。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "For border cities to receive the enemy while we sit at ease in the court, with the frontier in turmoil and people's minds doubtful, is a great anxiety for the altars of soil and grain."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "For border cities to receive the enemy while we sit at ease in the court, with the frontier in turmoil and people's minds doubtful, is a great anxiety for the altars of soil and grain."

entries.zh: 先是，吳遣將諸葛恪屯皖，邊鄙苦之，帝欲自擊恪。
entries.en: Zhuge Ke’s Wan garrison tormented the border—Sima Yi meant to lead the strike personally.
entries.literal: Earlier Wu had stationed Zhuge Ke at Wan; the frontier suffered; the Emperor wished to attack Ke himself.

entries.zh: 議者多以賊據堅城，積穀，欲引致官兵。
entries.en: Critics said Wu baited Wei toward granary walls.
entries.literal: Discussants mostly held that the rebels held a strong city and stored grain and wished to lure imperial troops.

entries.zh: 今懸軍遠攻，其救必至，進退不易，未見其便。
entries.en: A lone expedition invites rescue columns—movement becomes clumsy.
entries.literal: Now an isolated army campaigns deep—relief must arrive; advance and retreat are awkward—the advantage is unclear.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「賊之所長者水也，今攻其城，以觀其變。
entries.en: The emperor said, "What the enemy excels in is water. Now we will attack his city, in order to observe his response.
entries.literal: The emperor said, "What the enemy excels in is water. Now we will attack his city, in order to observe his response.

entries.zh: 若用其所長，棄城奔走，此為廟勝也。
entries.en: If he uses what he excels in and abandons the city to flee, this will be a victory in the temple calculations.
entries.literal: If he uses what he excels in and abandons the city to flee, this will be a victory in the temple calculations.

entries.zh: 若敢固守，湖水冬淺，船不得行，勢必棄水相救，由其所短，亦吾利也。」
entries.en: If he dares to hold firm, lake water is shallow in winter and boats cannot move; circumstances will force him to abandon water and come to the rescue, and by his weakness this will also be to my advantage."
entries.literal: If he dares to hold firm, lake water is shallow in winter and boats cannot move; circumstances will force him to abandon water and come to the rescue, and by his weakness this will also be to my advantage."

entries.zh: 尚書鄧颺、李勝等欲令曹爽建立功名，勸使伐蜀。
entries.en: Deng Yang and Li Sheng pushed Shuang toward a Shu raid for glory.
entries.literal: Ministers Deng Yang and Li Sheng wished Cao Shuang to earn merit and urged him to attack Shu.

entries.zh: 帝止之，不可，爽果無功而還。
entries.en: Sima Yi blocked it—Shuang marched anyway and limped home empty.
entries.literal: The Emperor stopped him—without success—Shuang indeed returned without achievement.

entries.zh: 冬十二月，天子詔帝朝會乘輿升殿。
entries.en: Winter: Sima Yi earned carriage access to the throne hall.
entries.literal: Winter twelfth month—the Son of Heaven issued an edict that at court assemblies the Emperor might ride the carriage onto the hall.

entries.zh: 曹爽用何晏、鄧颺、丁謐之謀，遷太后於永寧宮，專擅朝政，兄弟并典禁兵，多樹親黨，屢改制度。
entries.en: Shuang locked the dowager away, stacked brothers on the guards, rewrote laws with He Yan’s cabal.
entries.literal: Cao Shuang employed He Yan, Deng Yang, and Ding Mi’s plots—shifted the empress dowager to Yongning Palace, monopolized court governance, brothers jointly commanded palace guards, planted partisans widely, repeatedly altered institutions.

entries.zh: 帝不能禁，於是與爽有隙。
entries.en: Sima Yi could not brake him—rift opened.
entries.literal: The Emperor could not restrain him—thereupon grew estranged from Shuang.

entries.zh: 六月，乃督諸軍南征，車駕送出津陽門。
entries.en: Sixth month he took supreme command—throne carriage to Jinyang Gate.
entries.literal: Sixth month—thereupon he commanded all armies south; imperial carriage escorted him out Jinyang Gate.

entries.zh: 帝以南方暑溼，不宜持久，使輕騎挑之，然不敢動。
entries.en: Humid south forbade long stays—light horse baited Zhu Ran; Ran stayed put.
entries.literal: The Emperor considered the south hot and humid—not suited to long endurance—sent light cavalry to provoke them; Ran did not stir.

entries.zh: 於是休戰士，簡精銳，募先登，申號令，示必攻之勢。
entries.en: He rested men, culled shock troops, promised ladder gold, showed unstoppable assault.
entries.literal: Thereupon he rested troops, picked elite, recruited first-assault climbers, proclaimed orders, displayed inevitable assault posture.

entries.zh: 吳軍夜遁走，追至三州口，斬獲萬餘人，收其舟船軍資而還。
entries.en: Wu fled by dark—Sanzhou Ford piled ten thousand heads and captured hulls.
entries.literal: Wu army fled by night—pursued to Sanzhou kou, beheaded and captured over ten thousand, seized boats and military supplies and returned.

entries.zh: 天子遣侍中常侍勞軍于宛。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven dispatched a palace attendant and a regular attendant to reward the army at Wan.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven dispatched palace attendant and regular attendant to reward the army at Wan.

entries.zh: 四年秋九月，帝督諸軍擊諸葛恪，車駕送出津陽門。
entries.en: Autumn, ninth month, year four: full command against Zhuge Ke—throne carriage to Jinyang Gate.
entries.literal: Fourth year, autumn ninth month—the Emperor commanded all armies against Zhuge Ke; the imperial carriage escorted him out the Jinyang Gate.

entries.zh: 軍次於舒，恪焚燒積聚，棄城而遁。
entries.en: The army halted at Shu; Ke burned his stores, abandoned the city, and fled.
entries.literal: The army halted at Shu; Ke burned his stores, abandoned the city, and fled.

entries.zh: 秋七月，增封食郾、臨潁，并前四縣，邑萬戶，子弟十一人皆為列侯。
entries.en: That fall added Yan and Linying to four older counties—ten thousand taxable households—and eleven sons became column marquises.
entries.literal: In autumn’s seventh month his income was enlarged with Yan and Linying; together with the previous four counties his households totaled ten thousand, and eleven sons were all enfeoffed as full marquises.

entries.zh: 帝勳德日盛，而謙恭愈甚。
entries.en: Honors mounted while he grew more deferential.
entries.literal: The Emperor’s merit grew daily, yet his humility deepened.

entries.zh: 以太常常林鄉邑舊齒，見之每拜。
entries.en: He bowed to Chang Lin of the ministry whenever they crossed paths—hometown seniority demanded it.
entries.literal: Because Minister of Ceremonies Chang Lin was an elder townsman, whenever they met the Emperor bowed.

entries.zh: 恆戒子弟曰：「盛滿者道家之所忌，四時猶有推移，吾何德以堪之。
entries.en: He constantly warned his sons and younger kinsmen, saying, "Fullness and excess are what the Daoist tradition avoids; even the four seasons still have alternation. What virtue do I have to bear this?
entries.literal: He constantly warned his sons and younger kinsmen, saying, "Fullness and excess are what the Daoist tradition avoids; even the four seasons still have alternation. What virtue do I have to bear this?

entries.zh: 損之又損之，庶可以免乎！」
entries.en: Diminish it and diminish it again; perhaps then I can escape disaster!"
entries.literal: Diminish it and diminish it again; perhaps then I can escape disaster!"

entries.zh: 三年春，天子追封諡皇考京兆尹為舞陽成侯。
entries.en: Spring of year three brought a posthumous marquisate on his father Fang.
entries.literal: Third-year spring—the Son of Heaven posthumously titled his late father, Governor of Jingzhao, Marquis Cheng of Wuyang.

entries.zh: 三月，奏穿廣漕渠，引河入汴，溉東南諸陂，始大佃於淮北。
entries.en: He broke ground on the Guang canal, tapping the Yellow River into the Bian to flood Huai-north paddies.
entries.literal: Third month—he memorialized to cut the Guang transport canal, divert the Yellow River into the Bian, irrigate the southeastern reservoirs, and begin large-scale farming north of the Huai.

entries.zh: 帝以滅賊之要，在於積穀，乃大興屯守，廣開淮陽、百尺二渠，又修諸陂於潁之南北，萬餘頃。
entries.en: He bankrolled victory with dirt—Huaiyang and Baichi cuts, Ying basin dikes, ten thousand qing wet.
entries.literal: The Emperor held that destroying rebels hinged on grain—therefore he massively expanded garrison farms, widened the Huaiyang and Baichi canals, and repaired reservoirs north and south of the Ying—more than ten thousand qing.

entries.zh: [8]自是淮北倉庾相望，壽陽至於京師，[9]農官屯兵連屬焉。
entries.en: [8] From then on granaries lined the region north of the Huai; [9] from Shouyang to the capital, agricultural officials and colony troops were linked.
entries.literal: [8] From then on granaries lined the Huai north; [9] from Shouyang to the capital agricultural colonies and camps chained together.

entries.zh: 五年春正月，帝至自淮南，天子使持節勞軍。
entries.en: In the first month of spring of the fifth year the Emperor returned from Huainan; the Son of Heaven sent an envoy bearing the staff of authority to reward the army.
entries.literal: First month of spring in the fifth year—the Emperor returned from Huainan; the Son of Heaven sent an envoy with insignia to reward the army.

entries.zh: 六年秋八月，曹爽毀中壘中堅營，以兵屬其弟中領軍羲。
entries.en: Autumn eight, year six: Shuang stripped the inner ramparts and handed steel to brother Xi.
entries.literal: Sixth year, autumn eighth month—Cao Shuang dismantled the central bastion’s core camp and transferred troops to his younger brother Xi, Captain of the Central Army.

entries.zh: 帝以先帝舊制禁之，不可。
entries.en: He cited Mingdi’s bans—Shuang shrugged.
entries.literal: The Emperor cited late emperor regulations forbidding this—it was not accepted.

entries.zh: 七年春正月，吳寇柤中，夷夏萬餘家避寇北渡沔。
entries.en: Spring seven: Wu smashed Zhazhong—ten thousand families splashed north over the Han.
entries.literal: Seventh year spring first month—Wu raided Zhazhong; Yi and Han households north of ten thousand fled the bandits across the Han.

entries.zh: 帝以沔南近賊，若百姓奔還，必復致寇，宜權留之。
entries.en: He argued refugees must stay north—returning invited another plunge.
entries.literal: The Emperor held that south of the Han lay close to the foe—if commoners rushed back they would invite raid again—it was fitting temporarily to detain them.

entries.zh: 曹爽曰：「今不能修守沔南而留百姓，非長策也。」
entries.en: Cao Shuang said, "Now, if we cannot repair and defend south of the Mian yet leave the people there, it is not a long-term plan."
entries.literal: Cao Shuang said, "Now, if we cannot repair and defend south of the Mian yet leave the people there, it is not a long-term plan."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「不然。
entries.en: The emperor said, "It is not so.
entries.literal: The emperor said, "It is not so.

entries.zh: 凡物致之安地則安，危地則危。
entries.en: In general, when things are placed on secure ground, they are secure; when they are placed on dangerous ground, they are endangered.
entries.literal: In general, when things are placed on secure ground, they are secure; when they are placed on dangerous ground, they are endangered.

entries.zh: 故兵書曰『成敗，形也；
entries.en: Therefore the military books say, 'Success and failure are a matter of form;
entries.literal: Therefore the military books say, 'Success and failure are a matter of form;

entries.zh: 安危，勢也』。
entries.en: security and danger are a matter of configuration.'
entries.literal: security and danger are a matter of configuration.'

entries.zh: 形勢，御眾之要，不可以不審。
entries.en: Form and configuration are essentials in controlling the masses and cannot fail to be examined carefully.
entries.literal: Form and configuration are essentials in controlling the masses and cannot fail to be examined carefully.

entries.zh: 設令賊以二萬人斷沔水，三萬人與沔南諸軍相持，萬人陸梁柤中，將何以救之？」
entries.en: Suppose the enemy used twenty thousand men to cut off the Mian River, thirty thousand men to hold our various armies south of the Mian, and ten thousand men to range freely through Zhazhong. How would you rescue them?"
entries.literal: Suppose the enemy used twenty thousand men to cut off the Mian River, thirty thousand men to hold our various armies south of the Mian, and ten thousand men to range freely through Zhazhong. How would you rescue them?"

entries.zh: 爽不從，卒令還南。
entries.en: Shuang forced the migration south anyway.
entries.literal: Shuang did not follow—ultimately ordered them returned south.

entries.zh: 賊果襲破柤中，所失萬計。
entries.en: Wu shattered Zhazhong—myriad gone.
entries.literal: The bandits indeed struck and broke Zhazhong—losses numbered ten thousand.

entries.zh: 八年夏四月，夫人張氏薨。
entries.en: Eighth year summer: wife Zhang passed.
entries.literal: Summer fourth month eighth year—Lady Zhang died.

entries.zh: 五月，帝稱疾不與政事。
entries.en: He pleaded sick and vanished from council.
entries.literal: Fifth month—the Emperor claimed illness and withdrew from governance.

entries.zh: 時人為之謠曰：「何、鄧、丁，亂京城。」
entries.en: People of the time made a song about them, saying, "He, Deng, and Ding throw the capital into disorder."
entries.literal: People of the time made a song about them, saying, "He, Deng, and Ding throw the capital into disorder."

entries.zh: 九年春三月，黃門張當私出掖庭才人石英等十一人，與曹爽為伎人。
entries.en: Yellow Gate Zhang Dang secretly brought eleven palace talents including Shi Ying out of the inner court as entertainers for Cao Shuang.
entries.literal: Spring third month ninth year—Yellow Gate Zhang Dang secretly brought eleven palace talents including Shi Ying out of the forbidden precincts as entertainers for Cao Shuang.

entries.zh: 爽、晏謂帝疾篤，遂有無君之心，與當密謀，圖危社稷，期有日矣。
entries.en: They thought Sima Yi dying and schemed usurpation with Zhang Dang.
entries.literal: Shuang and Yan deemed the Emperor mortally ill—thereupon harbored disloyal intent—plotting secretly with Dang to endanger the altars—a date was set.

entries.zh: 帝亦潛為之備，爽之徒屬亦頗疑帝。
entries.en: Sima Yi armed in shadows while Shuang’s men sniffed trap.
entries.literal: The Emperor also secretly prepared; Shuang’s followers likewise suspected the Emperor.

entries.zh: 會河南尹李勝將莅荊州，來候帝。
entries.en: When the Governor of Henan, Li Sheng, was about to take up Jingzhou, he came to visit the emperor.
entries.literal: When Governor of Henan Li Sheng was about to take up Jingzhou he came to visit the Emperor.

entries.zh: 帝詐疾篤，使兩婢侍，持衣衣落，指口言渴，婢進粥，帝不持杯飲，粥皆流出霑胸。
entries.en: He staged palsy—maids, spilled porridge, sodden robes.
entries.literal: The Emperor feigned grave illness—had two maids attend—when dressing let clothes fall—pointed to mouth saying thirst—maids brought gruel—the Emperor could not hold cup—gruel spilled soaking chest.

entries.zh: 勝曰：「眾情謂明公舊風發動，何意尊體乃爾！」
entries.en: Sheng said, "Everyone thought Your Lordship's old wind illness had acted up. How could your honored body be like this!"
entries.literal: Sheng said, "Everyone thought Your Lordship's old wind illness had acted up. How could your honored body be like this!"

entries.zh: 帝使聲氣纔屬，說「年老枕疾，死在旦夕。
entries.en: The emperor made his voice and breath barely connect and said, "I am old and bedridden with illness; death is at morning or evening.
entries.literal: The emperor made his voice and breath barely connect and said, "I am old and bedridden with illness; death is at morning or evening.

entries.zh: 君當屈并州，并州近胡，善為之備。
entries.en: You are going to serve in Bingzhou. Bingzhou is close to the Hu; prepare well for it.
entries.literal: You are going to serve in Bingzhou. Bingzhou is close to the Hu; prepare well for it.

entries.zh: 恐不復相見，以子師、昭兄弟為託」。
entries.en: I fear we will not see each other again, so I entrust my sons Shi and Zhao, the brothers, to you."
entries.literal: I fear we will not see each other again, so I entrust my sons Shi and Zhao, the brothers, to you."

entries.zh: 勝曰：「當還忝本州，非并州。」
entries.en: Sheng said, "I am returning to serve in my home province, not Bingzhou."
entries.literal: Sheng said, "I am returning to serve in my home province, not Bingzhou."

entries.zh: 帝乃錯亂其辭曰：「君方到并州。」
entries.en: The emperor then deliberately confused his words and said, "You are just going to Bingzhou."
entries.literal: The emperor then deliberately confused his words and said, "You are just going to Bingzhou."

entries.zh: 勝復曰：「當忝荊州。」
entries.en: Sheng again said, "I am going to serve in Jingzhou."
entries.literal: Sheng again said, "I am going to serve in Jingzhou."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「年老意荒，不解君言。
entries.en: The emperor said, "In old age my mind is confused, and I did not understand your words.
entries.literal: The emperor said, "In old age my mind is confused, and I did not understand your words.

entries.zh: 今還為本州，盛德壯烈，好建功勳！」
entries.en: Now you are returning to your home province; with flourishing virtue and vigorous valor, build fine achievements!"
entries.literal: Now you are returning to your home province; with flourishing virtue and vigorous valor, build fine achievements!"

entries.zh: 勝退告爽曰：「司馬公尸居餘氣，形神已離，不足慮矣。」
entries.en: After Sheng withdrew, he told Shuang, "Sima Gong lies like a corpse with only remnant breath; his form and spirit have already separated. He is not worth worrying about."
entries.literal: After Sheng withdrew, he told Shuang, "Sima Gong lies like a corpse with only remnant breath; his form and spirit have already separated. He is not worth worrying about."

entries.zh: 他日，又言曰：「太傅不可復濟，令人愴然。」
entries.en: Another day, he also said, "The Grand Tutor can no longer be saved; it makes one grieve."
entries.literal: Another day, he also said, "The Grand Tutor can no longer be saved; it makes one grieve."

entries.zh: 故爽等不復設備。
entries.en: Shuang stood down his guard.
entries.literal: Therefore Shuang and others ceased preparing defenses.

entries.zh: 嘉平元年春正月甲午，天子謁高平陵，爽兄弟皆從。
entries.en: In spring, the first month, jiawu, of the first year of Jiaping (249), the Son of Heaven paid respects at Gaoping Mausoleum, and Shuang and his brothers all accompanied him.
entries.literal: In spring, the first month, jiawu, of the first year of Jiaping (249), the Son of Heaven paid respects at Gaoping Mausoleum, and Shuang and his brothers all accompanied him.

entries.zh: 是日，太白襲月。
entries.en: Metal star gnawed the moon that dawn.
entries.literal: That day Venus occulted the moon.

entries.zh: 帝于是奏永寧太后廢爽兄弟。
entries.en: Empress warrant arrived—strip Shuang brothers.
entries.literal: The Emperor thereupon memorialized Empress Dowager Yongning to depose Shuang brothers.

entries.zh: 時景帝為中護軍，將兵屯司馬門。
entries.en: Sima Shi held Sima Gate.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Jing served as Colonel Protecting the Army—commanded troops camped at Sima Gate.

entries.zh: 帝列陣闕下，經爽門。
entries.en: Sima Yi formed ranks below Duan—passed Shuang mansion.
entries.literal: The Emperor drew battle lines below the palace gate—passed Shuang’s gate.

entries.zh: 爽帳下督嚴世上樓，引弩將射帝，孫謙止之曰：「事未可知。」
entries.en: Yan Shi, a commander under Shuang, went up the tower and drew a crossbow to shoot the emperor, but Sun Qian stopped him, saying, "The matter cannot yet be known."
entries.literal: Yan Shi, a commander under Shuang, went up the tower and drew a crossbow to shoot the emperor, but Sun Qian stopped him, saying, "The matter cannot yet be known."

entries.zh: 三注三止，皆引其肘不得發。
entries.en: Three drawn bolts—three stays—never fired.
entries.literal: Three times he drew—three times stopped—all pulling his elbow unable to loose.

entries.zh: 大司農桓範出赴爽，蔣濟言於帝曰：「智囊往矣。」
entries.en: When Grand Minister of Agriculture Huan Fan left to join Shuang, Jiang Ji said to the emperor, "The wisdom bag has gone."
entries.literal: When Grand Minister of Agriculture Huan Fan left to join Shuang, Jiang Ji said to the emperor, "The wisdom bag has gone."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「爽與範內疏而智不及，駑馬戀短豆，必不能用也。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Shuang and Fan are inwardly estranged, and his wisdom is not equal to Fan's. A worn-out horse longs for short beans; he certainly will not use him."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "Shuang and Fan are inwardly estranged, and his wisdom is not equal to Fan's. A worn-out horse longs for short beans; he certainly will not use him."

entries.zh: 於是假司徒高柔節，行大將軍事，領爽營，謂柔曰：「君為周勃矣。」
entries.en: Thereupon he borrowed Situ Gao Rou's staff, made him acting general-in-chief, put him in command of Shuang's camp, and said to Rou, "You are Zhou Bo."
entries.literal: Thereupon he borrowed Situ Gao Rou's staff, made him acting general-in-chief, put him in command of Shuang's camp, and said to Rou, "You are Zhou Bo."

entries.zh: 命太僕王觀行中領軍，攝羲營。
entries.en: Wang Guan seized Xi’s guards.
entries.literal: He ordered Minister Coachman Wang Guan to act as Central Army colonel—take Xi’s camp.

entries.zh: 帝親帥太尉蔣濟等勒兵出迎天子，屯于洛水浮橋，上奏曰：「先帝詔陛下、秦王及臣升於御牀，握臣臂曰『深以後事為念』。
entries.en: The emperor personally led Grand Commandant Jiang Ji and others, drew up troops, went out to meet the Son of Heaven, encamped at the floating bridge over the Luo River, and memorialized, "The late emperor ordered Your Majesty, the Prince of Qin, and me to ascend the imperial couch, grasped my arm, and said, 'I am deeply mindful of later affairs.'
entries.literal: The emperor personally led Grand Commandant Jiang Ji and others, drew up troops, went out to meet the Son of Heaven, encamped at the floating bridge over the Luo River, and memorialized, "The late emperor ordered Your Majesty, the Prince of Qin, and me to ascend the imperial couch, grasped my arm, and said, 'I am deeply mindful of later affairs.'

entries.zh: 今大將軍爽背棄顧命，敗亂國典，內則僭擬，外專威權。
entries.en: Now General-in-Chief Shuang has turned his back on the charge left to him, thrown the institutions of the state into disorder, usurps forms within, and monopolizes authority without.
entries.literal: Now General-in-Chief Shuang has turned his back on the charge left to him, thrown the institutions of the state into disorder, usurps forms within, and monopolizes authority without.

entries.zh: 羣官要職，皆置所親；
entries.en: For the important offices among the assembled officials, he has installed only those close to him;
entries.literal: For the important offices among the assembled officials, he has installed only those close to him;

entries.zh: 宿衞舊人，並見斥黜。
entries.en: the old members of the palace guard have all been rejected and dismissed.
entries.literal: the old members of the palace guard have all been rejected and dismissed.

entries.zh: 根據槃互，縱恣日甚。
entries.en: His roots and bases intertwine, and his arrogance grows worse by the day.
entries.literal: His roots and bases intertwine, and his arrogance grows worse by the day.

entries.zh: 又以黃門張當為都監，專共交關，伺候神器。
entries.en: He has also made the Yellow Gates officer Zhang Dang metropolitan inspector, and they alone exchange connections and watch for the divine vessel.
entries.literal: He has also made the Yellow Gates officer Zhang Dang metropolitan inspector, and they alone exchange connections and watch for the divine vessel.

entries.zh: 天下洶洶，人懷危懼。
entries.en: All under Heaven is in turmoil, and people harbor danger and fear.
entries.literal: All under Heaven is in turmoil, and people harbor danger and fear.

entries.zh: 陛下便為寄坐，豈得久安？
entries.en: Your Majesty has thereby become one seated in dependency; how can you long be secure?
entries.literal: Your Majesty has thereby become one seated in dependency; how can you long be secure?

entries.zh: 此非先帝詔陛下及臣升御牀之本意也。
entries.en: This was not the original intent of the late emperor when he ordered Your Majesty and me to ascend the imperial couch.
entries.literal: This was not the original intent of the late emperor when he ordered Your Majesty and me to ascend the imperial couch.

entries.zh: 臣雖朽邁，敢忘前言。
entries.en: Though I am decayed and old, how would I dare forget the former words?
entries.literal: Though I am decayed and old, how would I dare forget the former words?

entries.zh: 昔趙高極意，秦是以亡；
entries.en: In the past, Zhao Gao fulfilled his will to the utmost, and Qin thereby perished;
entries.literal: In the past, Zhao Gao fulfilled his will to the utmost, and Qin thereby perished;

entries.zh: 呂霍早斷，漢祚永延。
entries.en: the Lu and Huo clans were cut off early, and the Han mandate was prolonged forever.
entries.literal: the Lu and Huo clans were cut off early, and the Han mandate was prolonged forever.

entries.zh: 此乃陛下之殷鑒，臣授命之秋也。
entries.en: This is Your Majesty's clear warning and the moment when I receive my command.
entries.literal: This is Your Majesty's clear warning and the moment when I receive my command.

entries.zh: 公卿羣臣皆以爽有無君之心，兄弟不宜典兵宿衞；
entries.en: The high ministers and assembled officials all consider Shuang to have a heart that recognizes no ruler, and that the brothers should not control troops and the palace guard;
entries.literal: The high ministers and assembled officials all consider Shuang to have a heart that recognizes no ruler, and that the brothers should not control troops and the palace guard;

entries.zh: 奏皇太后，皇太后敕如奏施行。
entries.en: they memorialized the Empress Dowager, and the Empress Dowager ordered that it be carried out as memorialized.
entries.literal: they memorialized the Empress Dowager, and the Empress Dowager ordered that it be carried out as memorialized.

entries.zh: 臣輒敕主者及黃門令罷爽、羲、訓吏兵，各以本官侯就第。
entries.en: I have therefore ordered the responsible officials and the Director of the Yellow Gates to remove Shuang, Xi, and Xun from their officials and troops, and for each, as a marquis with his original office, to go to his residence.
entries.literal: I have therefore ordered the responsible officials and the Director of the Yellow Gates to remove Shuang, Xi, and Xun from their officials and troops, and for each, as a marquis with his original office, to go to his residence.

entries.zh: 若稽留車駕，以軍法從事。
entries.en: If they delay the imperial carriage, handle them under military law.
entries.literal: If they delay the imperial carriage, handle them under military law.

entries.zh: 臣輒力疾將兵詣洛水浮橋，伺察非常。」
entries.en: I have therefore forced myself through illness and led troops to the floating bridge over the Luo River, to watch for the extraordinary."
entries.literal: I have therefore forced myself through illness and led troops to the floating bridge over the Luo River, to watch for the extraordinary."

entries.zh: 爽不通奏，留車駕宿伊水南，伐樹為鹿角，發屯兵數千人以守。
entries.en: Shuang did not transmit the memorial, detained the imperial carriage overnight south of the Yi River, felled trees for palisades, and called several thousand garrison troops to defend.
entries.literal: Shuang did not transmit memorial—detained imperial carriage south of Yi River overnight—felled trees for antlers—called several thousand garrison troops to defend.

entries.zh: 桓範果勸爽奉天子幸許昌，移檄徵天下兵。
entries.en: Fan beg march to Xuchang—levy realm.
entries.literal: Huan Fan indeed urged Shuang to escort Son of Heaven to Xuchang—issue proclamations summoning troops empire-wide.

entries.zh: 爽不能用，而夜遣侍中許允、尚書陳泰詣帝，觀望風旨。
entries.en: Shuang failed nerve—sent Xu Yun and Chen Tai to sniff terms.
entries.literal: Shuang could not use this—by night sent Palace Attendant Xu Yun and Minister Chen Tai to the Emperor—probe intentions.

entries.zh: 帝數其過失，事止免官。
entries.en: Sima Yi listed crimes—offer stripped posts.
entries.literal: The Emperor enumerated his faults—matter stopped at dismissal from office.

entries.zh: 泰還以報爽，勸之通奏。
entries.en: Chen Tai urged surrender memorial.
entries.literal: Tai returned reporting to Shuang—urged transmitting memorial.

entries.zh: 帝又遣爽所信殿中校尉尹大目諭爽，指洛水為誓，爽意信之。
entries.en: Yin Damu swore on Luo—Shuang believed.
entries.literal: The Emperor again sent Shuang’s trusted Palace Inspector Yin Damu to instruct Shuang—pointed to Luo River swearing oath—Shuang’s heart trusted.

entries.zh: 桓範等援引古今，諫說萬端。
entries.en: Fan pleaded classics till hoarse.
entries.literal: Huan Fan and others cited ancient and modern—remonstrated myriad ways.

entries.zh: 終不能從，乃曰：「司馬公正當欲奪吾權耳。
entries.en: In the end Shuang could not follow Fan, and then said, "Sima Gong merely wants to seize my authority.
entries.literal: In the end Shuang could not follow Fan, and then said, "Sima Gong merely wants to seize my authority.

entries.zh: 吾得以侯還第，不失為富家翁。」
entries.en: If I can return to my residence as a marquis, I will not fail to be a wealthy old gentleman."
entries.literal: If I can return to my residence as a marquis, I will not fail to be a wealthy old gentleman."

entries.zh: 範拊膺曰：「坐卿，滅吾族矣！」
entries.en: Fan beat his breast and said, "Because of you, my clan will be destroyed!"
entries.literal: Fan beat his breast and said, "Because of you, my clan will be destroyed!"

entries.zh: 遂通帝奏。
entries.en: Shuang folded—sent memorial.
entries.literal: Thereupon transmitted Emperor memorial.

entries.zh: 既而有司劾黃門張當，并發爽與何晏等反事，乃收爽兄弟及其黨與何晏、丁謐、鄧颺、畢軌、李勝、桓範等誅之。
entries.en: Indictments landed—Zhang Dang flipped—Shuang ring executed wholesale.
entries.literal: Soon judicial officials impeached Yellow Gate Zhang Dang—and uncovered Shuang with He Yan and others rebellion matter—thereupon seized Shuang brothers and faction He Yan, Ding Mi, Deng Yang, Bi Gui, Li Sheng, Huan Fan etc.—executed.

entries.zh: 蔣濟曰：「曹真之勳，不可以不祀。」
entries.en: Jiang Ji said, "Cao Zhen's merits cannot be left without sacrifice."
entries.literal: Jiang Ji said, "Cao Zhen's merits cannot be left without sacrifice."

entries.zh: 帝不聽。
entries.en: Sima Yi refused.
entries.literal: The Emperor did not listen.

entries.zh: 二月，天子以帝為丞相，增封潁川之繁昌、鄢陵、新汲、父城，并前八縣，邑二萬戶，奏事不名。
entries.en: February: chancellor, four Yingchuan counties stacked on eight—twenty thousand households—name suppressed on memorials.
entries.literal: Second month—the Son of Heaven made the Emperor Chancellor, enlarged his income with Fanchang, Yanling, Xinji, and Fucheng in Yingchuan—together eight counties previously—twenty thousand households—and memorialized without naming himself.

entries.zh: 固讓丞相。
entries.en: He refused the chancellor seal.
entries.literal: He firmly declined Chancellor.

entries.zh: 冬十二月，加九錫之禮，朝會不拜。
entries.en: Winter: Nine tins—stood straight at audience.
entries.literal: Winter twelfth month—the Nine Bestowals ritual was added—at court assemblies he did not bow.

entries.zh: 固讓九錫。
entries.en: He refused the nine insignia.
entries.literal: He firmly declined the Nine Bestowals.

entries.zh: 二年春正月，天子命帝立廟于洛陽，置左右長史，增掾屬、舍人滿十人，歲舉掾屬任御史、秀才各一人，增官騎百人，鼓吹十四人，封子肜平樂亭侯，倫安樂亭侯。
entries.en: Spring year two: Luoyang ancestral shrine, full clerical staff, ten advisors, yearly recommendations, hundred escorts, fourteen pipes—sons Rong and Lun petty marquises.
entries.literal: Second year spring first month—the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor to erect a temple in Luoyang, assign left and right senior clerks, enlarge aides and attendants to ten men fully, annually nominate one aide each for censor and xiucai, add one hundred official riders and fourteen musicians, enfeoff son Rong as marquis of Pingle ting and Lun as marquis of Anle ting.

entries.zh: 帝以久疾不任朝請，每有大事，天子親幸第以諮訪焉。
entries.en: Too ill for court—emperor rode to his gate for counsel.
entries.literal: The Emperor because of long illness could not attend court audiences—whenever great affairs arose the Son of Heaven personally visited his mansion for consultation.

entries.zh: 三年春正月，王淩詐言吳人塞涂水，請發兵以討之。
entries.en: Year three spring: Wang Ling lied Wu jammed Tu ford—begged arms.
entries.literal: Third year spring first month—Wang Ling falsely claimed Wu men blocked the Tu River—requested mobilizing troops to attack.

entries.zh: 帝潛知其計，不聽。
entries.en: Sima Yi saw through it—denied arms.
entries.literal: The Emperor secretly knew his scheme—did not consent.

entries.zh: 初，爽司馬魯芝、主簿楊綜斬關奔爽。
entries.en: Lu Zhi and Yang Zong had bolted to Shuang.
entries.literal: Earlier Shuang’s marshal Lu Zhi and clerk Yang Zong broke passes fleeing to Shuang.

entries.zh: 及爽之將歸罪也，芝、綜泣諫曰：「公居伊周之任，挾天子，杖天威，孰敢不從？
entries.en: When Shuang was about to return and submit to punishment, Zhi and Zong wept and remonstrated, saying, "You occupy the office of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, hold the Son of Heaven, and rely on Heaven's authority. Who would dare not follow?
entries.literal: When Shuang was about to return and submit to punishment, Zhi and Zong wept and remonstrated, saying, "You occupy the office of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, hold the Son of Heaven, and rely on Heaven's authority. Who would dare not follow?

entries.zh: 舍此而欲就東市，豈不痛哉！」
entries.en: To abandon this and want to go to the eastern market for execution, is it not painful!"
entries.literal: To abandon this and want to go to the eastern market for execution, is it not painful!"

entries.zh: 有司奏收芝、綜科罪，帝赦之，曰：「以勸事君者。」
entries.en: The responsible offices memorialized to arrest Zhi and Zong and assign crimes, but the emperor pardoned them, saying, "To encourage those who serve their lords."
entries.literal: The responsible offices memorialized to arrest Zhi and Zong and assign crimes, but the emperor pardoned them, saying, "To encourage those who serve their lords."

entries.zh: 兗州刺史令狐愚、、太尉王淩貳於帝，謀立楚王彪。
entries.en: The Inspector of Yanzhou, Linghu Yu, and Grand Commandant Wang Ling rebelled against the Emperor, plotting to install Prince Biao of Chu.
entries.literal: Inspector of Yanzhou Linghu Yu [sic—duplicate punctuation in source] and Grand Commandant Wang Ling rebelled against the Emperor—plotting to install Prince Biao of Chu.

entries.zh: 帝內忌而外寬，猜忌多權變。
entries.en: Inside jealous—outside mild—paranoia masked.
entries.literal: The Emperor inwardly jealous outwardly generous—suspicious—many stratagems.

entries.zh: 魏武察帝有雄豪志，聞有狼顧相，欲驗之。
entries.en: Cao Cao tested wolf-turn rumor.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu observed the Emperor bore heroic ambition—heard he had wolf-gaze physiognomy—wished to verify.

entries.zh: 乃召使前行，令反顧，面正向後而身不動。
entries.en: Ordered forward—snap neck—wolf stare.
entries.literal: Summoned ordering advance march—commanded turn head—face squared rear yet body unmoved.

entries.zh: 又嘗夢三馬同食一槽，甚惡焉。
entries.en: Dreamed three horses one trough—dread.
entries.literal: Also once dreamed three horses shared one trough—greatly loathed.

entries.zh: 因謂太子丕曰：「司馬懿非人臣也，必預汝家事。」
entries.en: He therefore said to Crown Prince Pi, "Sima Yi is no mere subject; he will certainly take part in your family affairs."
entries.literal: He therefore said to Crown Prince Pi, "Sima Yi is no mere subject; he will certainly take part in your family affairs."

entries.zh: 太子素與帝善，每相全佑，故免。
entries.en: Pi shielded him—survived.
entries.literal: Heir always friendly with Emperor—each time wholly protected—therefore spared.

entries.zh: 帝於是勤於吏職，夜以忘寢，至於芻牧之間，悉皆臨履，由是魏武意遂安。
entries.en: Burned ledgers nightly—Cao Cao relaxed.
entries.literal: Thereupon Emperor diligent in clerical duties—night forgot sleep—even fodder matters personally inspected—thereby Emperor Wu’s mind settled.

entries.zh: 及平公孫文懿，大行殺戮。
entries.en: When he pacified Gongsun Wenyi he carried out a great slaughter.
entries.literal: When pacifying Gongsun Wenyi greatly conducted slaughter.

entries.zh: 誅曹爽之際，支黨皆夷及三族，男女無少長，姑姊妹女子之適人者皆殺之，既而竟遷魏鼎云。
entries.en: Shuang purge erased kin—even married women—then stole Wei.
entries.literal: When executing Cao Shuang faction all branches extirpated three clans—male female none spared young old—aunts sisters daughters married all killed—thereafter indeed shifted Wei tripod.

entries.zh: 明帝時，王導侍坐。
entries.en: Emperor Ming of Jin held Wang Dao beside him.
entries.literal: During Emperor Ming’s reign Wang Dao attended seated.

entries.zh: 帝問前世所以得天下，導乃陳帝創業之始，及文帝末高貴鄉公事。
entries.en: Ming asked Jin’s rise—Wang Dao traced Sima Yi through Gaoguixiang coup.
entries.literal: Emperor asked how former age gained realm—Dao therefore narrated Emperor’s founding beginnings and Wen emperor end affair of Duke Gaoguixiang.

entries.zh: 明帝以面覆牀曰：「若如公言，晉祚復安得長遠！」
entries.en: Emperor Ming covered his face against the bed and said, "If it is as you say, how could the Jin mandate again be long-lasting!"
entries.literal: Emperor Ming covered his face against the bed and said, "If it is as you say, how could the Jin mandate again be long-lasting!"

entries.zh: 迹其猜忍，蓋有符於狼顧也。
entries.en: His cruelty matched wolf stare.
entries.literal: Tracing his suspicious cruelty fits wolf-gaze omen.

entries.zh: 夏四月，帝自帥中軍，汎舟沿流，九日而到甘城。
entries.en: Fourth month: central army by river—nine days to Gancheng.
entries.literal: Summer fourth month—the Emperor personally led the central army—boated downstream—nine days reaching Gancheng.

entries.zh: 淩計無所出，乃迎於武丘，面縛水次，曰：「淩若有罪，公當折簡召淩，何苦自來邪！」
entries.en: With no plan available, Wang Ling went out to meet him at Wuqiu, bound himself before him at the riverside, and said, "If I had committed a crime, you should have summoned me with a folded note. Why trouble yourself to come in person!"
entries.literal: With no plan available, Wang Ling went out to meet him at Wuqiu, bound himself before him at the riverside, and said, "If I had committed a crime, you should have summoned me with a folded note. Why trouble yourself to come in person!"

entries.zh: 帝曰：「以君非折簡之客故耳。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "It is only because you are not a guest for a folded note."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "It is only because you are not a guest for a folded note."

entries.zh: 即以淩歸于京師。
entries.en: Thereupon he took Wang Ling back to the capital.
entries.literal: Thereupon took Ling back toward capital.

entries.zh: 道經賈逵廟，淩呼曰：「賈梁道！
entries.en: As the road passed the shrine of Jia Kui, Wang Ling cried out, "Jia Liangdao!
entries.literal: As the road passed the shrine of Jia Kui, Wang Ling cried out, "Jia Liangdao!

entries.zh: 王淩是大魏之忠臣，惟爾有神知之。」
entries.en: Wang Ling is a loyal minister of Great Wei; only you, if you have spirit, know it."
entries.literal: Wang Ling is a loyal minister of Great Wei; only you, if you have spirit, know it."

entries.zh: 至項，仰鴆而死。
entries.en: At Xiang he swallowed poison.
entries.literal: Arriving at Xiang drank poison and died.

entries.zh: 收其餘黨，皆夷三族，并殺彪。
entries.en: Purged networks—three kin wipes—and Prince Biao.
entries.literal: Seized remainder faction—all extirpated three clans—and executed Biao.

entries.zh: 悉錄魏諸王公置于鄴，命有司監察，不得交關。
entries.en: Caged Wei royalty at Ye—wardens barred intrigue.
entries.literal: Registered all Wei princes and dukes at Ye—ordered officials supervise—no conspiracy.

entries.zh: 天子遣侍中韋誕持節勞軍于五池。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven sent Palace Attendant Wei Dan with a staff of authority to reward the army at Wuchi.
entries.literal: Son of Heaven dispatched Palace Attendant Wei Dan with insignia to reward army at Wuchi.

entries.zh: 帝至自甘城，天子又使兼大鴻臚、太僕庾嶷持節，策命帝為相國，封安平郡公，孫及兄子各一人為列侯，前後食邑五萬戶，侯者十九人。
entries.en: Second investiture: minister of state, Anping duke, nineteen marquis slots—fifty thousand households.
entries.literal: The Emperor returned from Gancheng. The Son of Heaven again ordered Yu Yi, concurrent Grand Herald and Minister Coachman, with a staff of authority, to appoint the Emperor Minister of State and enfeoff him as Duke of Anping Commandery; one grandson and one elder brother’s son each as a column marquis; food-fiefs totaling fifty thousand households; nineteen marquises in all.

entries.zh: 固讓相國、郡公不受。
entries.en: Refused duke and minister posts.
entries.literal: Firmly declined minister of state and commandery duke—did not accept.

entries.zh: 九月庚申，葬于河陰，諡曰文，後改諡宣文。
entries.en: Buried Heyin—first Wen then Xu Wen.
entries.literal: Ninth month gengshen—buried Heyin—posthumous title Wen—later altered Xu Wen.

entries.zh: 先是，預作終制，於首陽山為土藏，不墳不樹；
entries.en: Pre-dug Shouyang grave—flat earth—no mound trees;
entries.literal: Earlier prepared terminal instructions—earth tomb at Shouyang Mountain—no mound no trees;

entries.zh: 作顧命三篇，斂以時服，不設明器，後終者不得合葬。
entries.en: three wills—seasonal shroud—no mingqi—no later joint burial.
entries.literal: composed testament three chapters—shroud in seasonal clothes—no grave goods—later deceased may not joint bury.

entries.zh: 一如遺命。
entries.en: Burial obeyed will.
entries.literal: All accorded testament charge.

entries.zh: 晉國初建，追尊曰宣王。
entries.en: Jin raised him King Xuan.
entries.literal: When Jin state first founded posthumously honored King Xuan.

entries.zh: 武帝受禪，上尊號曰宣皇帝，陵曰高原，廟稱高祖。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he raised the honorific Emperor Xuan; the mausoleum was Gaoyuan; the temple name was Gaozu.
entries.literal: When Wu-di accepted abdication elevated honorific Emperor Xuan—mausoleum Gaoyuan—temple styled Gaozu.

entries.zh: 制曰：夫天地之大，黎元為本；
entries.en: Edict: realm rests on people;
entries.literal: Decree says: Vast as Heaven and Earth—the common people are root;

entries.zh: 邦國之貴，元首為先。
entries.en: state treasures ruler.
entries.literal: precious as state—sovereign comes first.

entries.zh: 治亂無常，興亡有運。
entries.en: Times turn—fate shifts.
entries.literal: Order and chaos lack constancy—rise and fall have fortune.

entries.zh: 是故五帝之上，居萬乘以為憂；
entries.en: Five emperors ruled anxious;
entries.literal: Therefore above Five Emperors—occupying myriad chariots they worried;

entries.zh: 三王已來，處其憂而為樂。
entries.en: three kings sought joy in care.
entries.literal: since Three Kings—they dwelt in worry yet found joy.

entries.zh: 競智力，爭利害，大小相吞，強弱相襲。
entries.en: Brains and blades—swallow or be swallowed.
entries.literal: Competed in wit and strength—contended profit—great swallowed small—strong struck weak.

entries.zh: 逮乎魏室，三方鼎峙，干戈不息，氛霧交飛。
entries.en: Wei era—three kingdoms—war-smoke.
entries.literal: Down to Wei house—three corners tripod—spears unceasing—miasma flew crossed.

entries.zh: 宣皇以天挺之姿，應期佐命，文以纘治，武以棱威。
entries.en: Xuan paired mandate—civil weave—martial awe.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan with Heaven-endowed bearing answered period assisting mandate—literature to continue rule—military to grind awe.

entries.zh: 用人如在己，求賢若不及；
entries.en: He treated appointments like personal errands and chased worthy men as if always too late.
entries.literal: Employing men as if himself—seeking worth as if falling short;

entries.zh: 情深阻而莫測，性寬綽而能容。
entries.en: His feelings ran dark and impossible to read; his manner stayed broad enough to absorb insult.
entries.literal: emotion deep and obstructed unfathomable—nature broad yet containing.

entries.zh: 和光同塵，與時舒卷，戢鱗潛翼，思屬風雲。
entries.en: Merged dust—hid claws—waited storm.
entries.literal: Blended gleam with dust—rolled with seasons—folded scales hid wings—thought attached wind cloud.

entries.zh: 飾忠于已詐之心，延安于將危之命。
entries.en: Feigned loyalty—bought time.
entries.literal: Displayed loyalty from treacherous heart—extended peace with perilous mandate.

entries.zh: 觀其雄略內斷，英猷外決，殄公孫於百日，擒孟達於盈旬，自以兵動若神，謀無再計矣。
entries.en: Observe his inner heroic resolve and outer brilliant plans: he wiped out Gongsun in a hundred days and captured Meng Da within a full ten-day span; he thought his troop movements godlike and his stratagems in need of no second plan.
entries.literal: Observe his heroic decisiveness within brilliant scheme without—extinguished Gongsun in hundred days—captured Meng Da within full ten-day span—self-thought soldier movement godlike—stratagem needed no second plan.

entries.zh: 既而擁眾西舉，與諸葛相持。
entries.en: West face Zhuge—stalemate.
entries.literal: Yet massed hosts west rising—with Zhuge Liang stalemate.

entries.zh: 抑其甲兵，本無鬭志，遺其巾幗，方發憤心。
entries.en: Women’s ribbons—shame battle.
