entries.literal: Restrained armor weapons—originally lacked battle will—sent women’s scarves—then roused angry heart.

entries.zh: 杖節當門，雄圖頓屈，請戰千里，詐欲示威。
entries.en: When a staff of authority blocked the gate, his grand design was abruptly bent; requesting battle from a thousand li away, he feigned a wish to display might.
entries.literal: Staff insignia blocked gate—grand plan abruptly bent—requested battle thousand li—feigned wishing display might.

entries.zh: 且秦蜀之人，勇懦非敵，夷險之路，勞逸不同，以此爭功，其利可見。
entries.en: Shu vs Wei terrain uneven odds.
entries.literal: Moreover Qin-Shu people brave coward unmatched—barrier roads labor ease different—using this contest merit advantage visible.

entries.zh: 而返閉軍固壘，莫敢爭鋒，生怯實而未前，死疑虛而猶遁，良將之道，失在斯乎！
entries.en: Stalled behind walls—cowardice mistaken prudence!
entries.literal: Yet returned closing army fortifying ramparts—none dared contend edge—alive cowardice solid yet not advancing—dead doubt empty yet still fleeing—good general’s way failure lies here!

entries.zh: 文帝之世，輔翼權重，許昌同蕭何之委，崇華甚霍光之寄。
entries.en: Regency rivaled Xiao He-Huo Guang.
entries.literal: During Wen emperor’s reign wings authority heavy—Xuchang same as Xiao He’s commission—Chonghua deeper than Huo Guang’s trust.

entries.zh: 當謂竭誠盡節，伊傅可齊。
entries.en: Should match Yi Yin purity.
entries.literal: Should have exhausted loyalty utmost fidelity—Yi Yin Fu Yue parallel.

entries.zh: 及明帝將終，棟樑是屬，受遺二主，佐命三朝，既承忍死之託，曾無殉生之報。
entries.en: Two deathbeds—three reigns—no martyr payment.
entries.literal: When Ming emperor near end pillar beam entrusted—received testament two lords—aided mandate three courts—already undertook endure-death trust—never offered die-for-lord repayment.

entries.zh: 天子在外，內起甲兵，陵土未乾，遽相誅戮，貞臣之體，寧若此乎！
entries.en: Emperor absent—Luoyang coup—fresh tomb—bloodbath—loyalty?
entries.literal: Son of Heaven outside—armor rose within—imperial mound earth not dry—suddenly mutual slaughter—upright minister’s bearing—could it be thus!

entries.zh: 盡善之方，以斯為惑。
entries.en: Perfection veils doubt.
entries.literal: Perfect governance method—here lies confusion.

entries.zh: 夫征討之策，豈東智而西愚？
entries.en: Wise east foolish west?
entries.literal: Could expedition strategy east wise west foolish?

entries.zh: 輔佐之心，何前忠而後亂？
entries.en: Same heart?
entries.literal: Assistant heart why earlier loyal later turbulent?

entries.zh: 故晉明掩面，恥欺偽以成功；
entries.en: Ming hid eyes—shamed fraud victory;
entries.literal: Therefore Jin Ming covered face—ashamed deceit achieving success;

entries.zh: 石勒肆言，笑姦回以定業。
entries.en: Shi Le mocked Jin hypocrisy.
entries.literal: Shi Le unrestrained speech—laughed treacherous twist fixing enterprise.

entries.zh: 古人有云，「積善三年，知之者少；
entries.en: An ancient said, "Accumulate goodness for three years, and few know of it;
entries.literal: An ancient said, "Accumulate goodness for three years, and few know of it;

entries.zh: 為惡一日，聞于天下」，可不謂然乎！
entries.en: do evil for one day, and it is heard throughout the world." Can this not be called true!
entries.literal: do evil for one day, and it is heard throughout the world." Can this not be called true!

entries.zh: 雖自隱過當年，而終見嗤後代。
entries.en: Hidden sins mocked later.
entries.literal: Although concealed faults that year—finally mocked later generations.

entries.zh: 亦猶竊鍾掩耳，以眾人為不聞；
entries.en: Like the bell thief plugging his ears—
entries.literal: Also like stealing bell covering ears—thinking crowd hears not;

entries.zh: 銳意盜金，謂市中為莫覩。
entries.en: gold thief blind.
entries.literal: keen stealing gold—thinking market blind.

entries.zh: 故知貪于近者則遺遠，溺于利者則傷名；
entries.en: Greed for what is near forfeits what is far;
entries.literal: Thus know greed near abandons far—drowning profit harms name;

entries.zh: 若不損己以益人，則當禍人而福己。
entries.en: hurt others gain self.
entries.literal: if not diminish self benefit others—then harm others bless self.

entries.zh: 順理而舉易為力，背時而動難為功。
entries.en: Move with the pattern and effort comes easily;
entries.literal: Follow pattern raising easy force—oppose season moving hard merit.

entries.zh: 況以未成之晉基，逼有餘之魏祚？
entries.en: How much more when Jin’s foundation was still unbuilt and it pressed against a Wei mandate that yet had life in it?
entries.literal: Moreover unfinished Jin foundation pressing ample Wei mandate?

entries.zh: 雖復道格區宇，德被蒼生，而天未啟時，寶位猶阻，非可以智競，不可以力爭，雖則慶流後昆，而身終於北面矣。
entries.en: Heaven withheld throne—died Wei subject.
entries.literal: Although again Way spanning realm virtue covering dark-green generation—Heaven not yet opened hour treasure throne still blocked—not by wisdom compete—not by strength contend—although blessing flows later generations—person ended facing north.

entries.zh: 六月，帝寢疾，夢賈逵、王淩為祟，甚惡之。
entries.en: Summer sixth: nightmares of Jia Kui and Wang Ling.
entries.literal: Sixth month—Emperor bedridden illness—dreamed Jia Kui and Wang Ling haunted him—greatly loathed.

entries.zh: 秋八月戊寅，崩於京師，時年七十三。
entries.en: Died Luoyang seventy-three.
entries.literal: Autumn eighth month wuyin—perished at capital—aged seventy-three.

entries.zh: 天子素服臨弔，喪葬威儀依漢霍光故事，追贈相國、郡公。
entries.en: The emperor wore mourning and oversaw rites on the Huo Guang model—then piled minister of state and duke honors on the dead.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven wore unpatterned mourning dress and attended the obsequies—burial majesty followed Han Huo Guang precedent—and posthumously gifted minister of state and commandery duke.

entries.zh: 弟孚表陳先志，辭郡公及轀輬車。
entries.en: Sima Fu cited Sima Yi’s will—refusing ducal rank and the ornate burial cart.
entries.literal: Younger brother Fu memorialized his late brother’s wishes—declining commandery duke rank and the imperial hearse.

entries.zh: 都督雍梁二州諸軍事 據三國志魏志以下僅稱魏志、蜀志或吳志。
entries.en: Commander of military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces. Based on Records of the Three Kingdoms, Wei zhi—hereafter cited only as Wei zhi, Shu zhi, or Wu zhi.
entries.literal: Commanded Yong-Liang two provinces military affairs—according to Records of Three Kingdoms Wei

entries.zh: 陳留王紀，梁州置於景元四年十二月，在此後三十餘年。
entries.en: Annals of the Prince of Chenliu: Liang province was established in the twelfth month of the fourth year of Jingyuan, more than thirty years later than this.
entries.literal: Prince of Chenliu annals—Liang province established twelfth month fourth year Jingyuan—more than thirty years later.

entries.zh: 司馬懿督二州係代曹真，景初三年趙儼代懿，魏志曹真傳、趙儼傳都作「雍涼」。
entries.en: Sima Yi's command over the two provinces followed his replacement of Cao Zhen; in the third year of Jingchu, Zhao Yan replaced Yi, and both the Wei zhi biographies of Cao Zhen and Zhao Yan write "Yong and Liang."
entries.literal: Sima Yi's command over the two provinces followed his replacement of Cao Zhen; in the third year of Jingchu, Zhao Yan replaced Yi, and both the Wei zhi biographies of Cao Zhen and Zhao Yan write "Yong and Liang."

entries.zh: 疑當從魏志。
entries.en: Editors conclude the text should align with the Wei zhi.
entries.literal: The doubtful passage ought to follow the Wei Records.

entries.zh: 諡曰文後改諡宣文 各本皆作「諡曰文貞，後改諡文宣」。
entries.en: For "posthumously named Wen and later changed to Xuanwen," all editions write "posthumously named Wenzhen and later changed to Wenxuan."
entries.literal: For "posthumously named Wen and later changed to Xuanwen," all editions write "posthumously named Wenzhen and later changed to Wenxuan."

entries.zh: 考異：「按禮志，魏朝初諡宣帝為文侯，景帝為武侯。
entries.en: The Kaoyi says, "According to the Treatise on Rites, when the Wei court first gave posthumous names, Emperor Xuan was named Marquis Wen and Emperor Jing was named Marquis Wu.
entries.literal: The Kaoyi says, "According to the Treatise on Rites, when the Wei court first gave posthumous names, Emperor Xuan was named Marquis Wen and Emperor Jing was named Marquis Wu.

entries.zh: 文王表不宜與二祖同，於是改諡宣文、忠武。
entries.en: King Wen memorialized that they should not be the same as the two ancestors, and therefore the posthumous names were changed to Xuanwen and Zhongwu.
entries.literal: King Wen memorialized that they should not be the same as the two ancestors, and therefore the posthumous names were changed to Xuanwen and Zhongwu.

entries.zh: 然則初諡文，無『貞』字也。
entries.en: Thus the initial posthumous name was Wen, and did not have the graph 'zhen'.
entries.literal: Thus the initial posthumous name was Wen, and did not have the graph 'zhen'.

entries.zh: 禮志及文帝紀並稱舞陽宣文侯，宋書禮志同。
entries.en: The Treatise on Rites and the Basic Annals of Emperor Wen both call him Marquis Xuanwen of Wuyang, and the Treatise on Rites in the Song shu is the same.
entries.literal: The Treatise on Rites and the Basic Annals of Emperor Wen both call him Marquis Xuanwen of Wuyang, and the Treatise on Rites in the Song shu is the same.

entries.zh: 此云『文宣』，亦轉寫之誤。」
entries.en: Here saying 'Wenxuan' is also a copying error."
entries.literal: Here saying 'Wenxuan' is also a copying error."

entries.zh: 今據改。
entries.en: Corrected per collation.
entries.literal: Now emended accordingly.

entries.zh: 武都氐王苻雙強端帥其屬六千餘人來降 據蜀志張嶷傳、華陽國志七，武都氐王苻健降蜀，其弟率眾就魏。
entries.en: According to the Shu zhi biography of Zhang Yi and Huayang guozhi 7, the Jinshu names Fu Shuang and Qiang Duan as Wudu Di kings leading more than six thousand followers to surrender; those sources instead have Wudu Di king Fu Jian surrender to Shu while his younger brother led a host to Wei.
entries.literal: Di kings of Wudu Fu Shuang and Qiang Duān leading followers—according to Shu Records Zhang Yi biography and Huayang guozhi 7 Wudu Di king Fu Jian surrendered to Shu while his younger brother led crowds to Wei.

entries.zh: 苻雙並非氐王，疑「王」字衍。
entries.en: Fu Shuang was not a Di king, so the graph "king" is suspected to be intrusive.
entries.literal: Fu Shuang was not a Di king, so the graph "king" is suspected to be intrusive.

entries.zh: 景皇帝諱師，字子元，宣帝長子也。
entries.en: Emperor Jing, whose personal name was Shi and courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan of Jin.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing, taboo name Shi, courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 雅有風彩，沈毅多大略。
entries.en: He carried himself with quiet distinction, steady and resolute, with a strategist’s breadth of mind.
entries.literal: He had refined bearing and presence, was deep and resolute, and possessed great strategic vision.

entries.zh: 少流美譽，與夏侯玄、何晏齊名。
entries.en: While still young he was widely praised, and his name stood alongside those of Xiahou Xuan and He Yan.
entries.literal: In youth he enjoyed a fine reputation, and was ranked with Xiahou Xuan and He Yan.

entries.zh: 晏常稱曰：「惟幾也能成天下之務，司馬子元是也。」
entries.en: He Yan used to say, "It takes someone who senses the moment before it turns to carry the weight of the realm—and that man is Sima Ziyuan."
entries.literal: He Yan often declared, "Only one who apprehends subtle turning points can accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven; Sima Ziyuan is such a man."

entries.zh: 魏景初中，拜散騎常侍，累遷中護軍。
entries.en: During Wei’s Jingchu years he received appointment as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and rose step by step to Central Protector of the Army.
entries.literal: In the Jingchu era of Wei, he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and eventually promoted to Central Protector of the Army.

entries.zh: 為選用之法，舉不越功，吏無私焉。
entries.en: He set rules for appointments so that promotions matched real achievement, and his staff could not trade on personal connections.
entries.literal: He established methods for selection and appointment; recommendations did not exceed actual merit, and clerks practiced no private favoritism.

entries.zh: 宣穆皇后崩，居喪以至孝聞。
entries.en: After Empress Dowager Xuanmu’s death, he kept mourning with such scrupulous grief that word of his filial piety spread everywhere.
entries.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuanmu died, he observed mourning for her and was famed for extreme filial devotion.

entries.zh: 宣帝之將誅曹爽，深謀秘策，獨與帝潛畫，文帝弗之知也。
entries.en: As Sima Yi readied the strike against Cao Shuang, he laid his plans in the deepest secrecy—working them out alone with Sima Shi—while Sima Zhao was kept entirely in the dark.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan was about to execute Cao Shuang, with deep plots and secret stratagems he secretly planned only with the Emperor (Sima Shi); Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao) did not know of it.

entries.zh: 將發夕乃告之，既而使人覘之，帝寢如常，而文帝不能安席。
entries.en: Sima Yi waited until the night before the coup to inform his son; when he sent men to watch Sima Shi’s quarters, Shi slept soundly as on any other night, while Sima Zhao tossed and could not settle.
entries.literal: On the eve of launching the action he was told; then someone was sent to spy on him—the Emperor slept as usual, but Emperor Wen could not find rest on his mat.

entries.zh: 晨會兵司馬門，鎮靜內外，置陣甚整。
entries.en: At daybreak he drew up his forces at the Sima Gate, steadying the palace inside and out and arraying them with flawless discipline.
entries.literal: At dawn he assembled troops at the Sima Gate, calming inside and outside, and deployed formations in very good order.

entries.zh: 宣帝曰：「此子竟可也。」
entries.en: Sima Yi said, "This boy will do after all."
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan said, "This son is indeed capable."

entries.zh: 初，帝陰養死士三千，散在人間，至是一朝而集，眾莫知所出也。
entries.en: Earlier, Sima Shi had quietly kept three thousand devoted fighters dispersed through the capital; now they materialized overnight, and no one could guess where they had sprung from.
entries.literal: At the outset the Emperor had secretly maintained three thousand bravos, scattered among the people; at this moment they gathered in a single morning, and the multitude did not know whence they had come.

entries.zh: 事平，以功封長平鄉侯，食邑千戶，尋加衛將軍。
entries.en: After the coup succeeded he was rewarded with the village marquisate of Changping and a thousand-household fief, and before long was named General of the Guard as well.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled, by merit he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Changping with a fief of one thousand households; soon he was additionally appointed General of the Guard.

entries.zh: 及宣帝薨，議者咸云「伊尹既卒，伊陟嗣事」，天子命帝以撫軍大將軍輔政。
entries.en: At Sima Yi’s death, court opinion echoed the old line—“When Yi Yin passed away, his son Yi Zhi carried on the task”—and the Wei emperor appointed Sima Shi General Who Pacifies the Army to assist in government.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, those who deliberated all said, "After Yi Yin died, Yi Zhi succeeded to his duties," and the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor as General Who Stabilizes the Army and Great General to assist in government.

entries.zh: 魏嘉平四年春正月，遷大將軍，加侍中，持節、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。
entries.en: In the first month of spring, Wei’s fourth year of Jiaping, he advanced to Great General, was given the concurrent post of Palace Attendant, received the imperial baton, took overall command of central and frontier forces, and assumed control of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring in the fourth year of Jiaping of Wei, he was promoted to Great General, added as Palace Attendant, bearing credentials, supervising all military affairs of the central command and the regions, and recording Director of the Secretariat business.

entries.zh: 命百官舉賢才，明少長，恤窮獨，理廢滯。
entries.en: He instructed every office to put forward able men, to sort seniority fairly, to relieve the widowed and alone, and to clear the backlog of neglected business.
entries.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to recommend worthy talent, clarify precedence of young and old, show pity to the destitute and solitary, and straighten out stalled appointments.

entries.zh: 諸葛誕、毌丘儉、王昶、陳泰、胡遵都督四方，王基、州泰、鄧艾、石苞典州郡，盧毓、李豐裳選舉，傅嘏、虞松參計謀，鐘會、夏侯玄、王肅、陳本、孟康、趙酆、張緝預朝議，四海傾注，朝野肅然。
entries.en: Zhuge Dan, Guanqiu Jian, Wang Chang, Chen Tai, and Hu Zun held regional commands; Wang Ji, Zhou Tai, Deng Ai, and Shi Bao ran the provinces; Lu Yu and Li Feng handled personnel; Fu Gu and Yu Song shaped policy; Zhong Hui, Xiahou Xuan, Wang Su, Chen Ben, Meng Kang, Zhao Feng, and Zhang Ji sat in on the great councils. The empire fixed its hopes on them, and court and countryside grew solemn.
entries.literal: Zhuge Dan, Guanqiu Jian, Wang Chang, Chen Tai, and Hu Zun supervised the four quarters; Wang Ji, Zhou Tai, Deng Ai, and Shi Bao administered prefectures and commanderies; Lu Yu and Li Feng oversaw selection and appointment; Fu Gu and Yu Song joined in planning stratagems; Zhong Hui, Xiahou Xuan, Wang Su, Chen Ben, Meng Kang, Zhao Feng, and Zhang Ji took part in court deliberations; the four seas turned their gaze upon them, and court and countryside stood in solemn awe.

entries.zh: 或有請改易制度者，帝曰：「'不識不知，順帝之則'，詩人之美也。
entries.en: When voices rose for sweeping institutional change, Sima Shi answered, "The Odes praise the ruler who does not meddle for show but simply follows the pattern Heaven set for the sage-kings.
entries.literal: When some requested changes to institutions, the Emperor said: "'Not knowing, not perceiving, following the norms of the Di'—that is what the poets praise.

entries.zh: 三祖典制，所宜遵奉；
entries.en: The precedents left by the three Wei founders are what we are bound to honor;
entries.literal: The regulations of the three founding ancestors are what ought to be obeyed and upheld;

entries.zh: 自非軍事，不得妄有改革。」
entries.en: and apart from what war demands, nothing should be changed on a whim."
entries.literal: unless it be military affairs, one must not recklessly carry out reforms."

entries.zh: 二年春正月，有彗星見於吳楚之分，西北竟天。
entries.en: In the first month of spring, the second year, a comet blazed across the Wu–Chu sector of the sky from the northwest to the horizon.
entries.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, there was a comet appearing in the Wu-Chu division, in the northwest filling the sky.

entries.zh: 鎮東大將軍毌丘儉、揚州刺史文欽舉兵作亂，矯太后令移檄郡國，為壇盟於西門之外，各遣子四人質于吳以請救。
entries.en: Guanqiu Jian, Grand General Who Guards the East, and Wen Qin, Yangzhou’s inspector, rose in revolt, forged a rescript in the Dowager’s name, sent manifestos across the commanderies, swore a blood oath on a platform west of the walls, and each sent four sons east as hostages to beg Wu for aid.
entries.literal: General Who Guards the East Guanqiu Jian and Inspector of Yangzhou Wen Qin raised troops and made rebellion, falsely issuing an empress dowager order and circulating proclamations through commanderies and principalities; they made an altar covenant outside the west gate, each sending four sons as hostages to Wu to request rescue.

entries.zh: 二月，儉、欽帥眾六萬，渡淮而西。
entries.en: In the second month they marched sixty thousand men across the Huai and drove west.
entries.literal: In the second month, Jian and Qin led a host of sixty thousand, crossed the Huai and went west.

entries.zh: 帝會公卿謀征討計，朝議多謂可遣諸將擊之，王肅及尚書傅嘏、中書侍郎鐘會勸帝自行。
entries.en: Sima Shi called the high ministers to plan the campaign; most favored sending subordinate generals, but Wang Su, Fu Gu of the Secretariat, and Zhong Hui of the Palace Secretariat pressed him to take the field himself.
entries.literal: The Emperor convened dukes and ministers to plan punitive expedition strategy; court deliberation mostly said one could dispatch various generals to strike them, but Wang Su and Director of the Secretariat Fu Gu and Palace Secretariat Gentleman Zhong Hui urged the Emperor to go in person.

entries.zh: 戊午，帝統中軍步騎十餘萬以征之。
entries.en: On wuwu he led well over a hundred thousand central-army horse and foot against the rebels.
entries.literal: On wuwu, the Emperor commanded the central army infantry and cavalry of more than one hundred thousand to campaign against them.

entries.zh: 倍道兼行，召三方兵，大會于陳許之郊。
entries.en: He forced the march, called in contingents from three directions, and massed them on the Chen–Xu plain.
entries.literal: Doubling roads and marching together, he summoned troops from three directions and held a great assembly on the outskirts of Chen and Xu.

entries.zh: 甲申，次於隱橋，儉將史招、李績相次來降。
entries.en: On jiashen he encamped at Yinqiao, where Jian’s officers Shi Zhao and Li Ji surrendered in quick succession.
entries.literal: On jiashen, he halted at Yinqiao; Jian's generals Shi Zhao and Li Ji came to surrender one after another.

entries.zh: 儉、欽移入項城，帝遣荊州刺史王基進據南頓以逼儉。
entries.en: When the rebels pulled into Xiangcheng, Sima Shi ordered Jingzhou Inspector Wang Ji to seize Nandun and pin Jian in place.
entries.literal: Jian and Qin shifted into Xiangcheng; the Emperor sent Inspector of Jingzhou Wang Ji to advance and occupy Nandun in order to press Jian.

entries.zh: 帝深壁高壘，以待東軍之集。
entries.en: He dug in behind high walls and waited for the eastern columns to assemble.
entries.literal: The Emperor deepened walls and raised high ramparts, in order to await the gathering of eastern troops.

entries.zh: 諸將請進軍攻其城，帝曰：「諸君得其一，未知其二。
entries.en: The generals requested advancing the army to attack the city. Sima Shi said, "You gentlemen have grasped one point, but do not yet know the second.
entries.literal: The generals requested advancing the army to attack the city. Sima Shi said, "You gentlemen have grasped one point, but do not yet know the second.

entries.zh: 淮南將士本無反志。
entries.en: The Huainan rank and file never wanted this rebellion.
entries.literal: The Huainan officers and soldiers fundamentally had no rebellious intent.

entries.zh: 且儉、欽欲蹈縱橫之跡，習儀秦之說，謂遠近必應。
entries.en: Jian and Wen Qin fancy themselves wandering strategists in the mold of Su Qin and Zhang Yi; they expect the whole region to rise at their call.
entries.literal: Moreover Jian and Qin wish to tread the traces of the vertical-horizontal persuaders, practice the doctrines of Yi and Qin, and think that near and far will surely respond.

entries.zh: 而事起之日，淮北不從，史招、李績前後瓦解。
entries.en: When the revolt broke, the north bank of the Huai refused to move, and Shi Zhao and Li Ji melted away in turn.
entries.literal: Yet on the day the affair arose, north of the Huai they did not follow; Shi Zhao and Li Ji before and after disintegrated.

entries.zh: 內乖外叛，自知必敗，困獸思鬥，速戰更合其志。
entries.en: Betrayed within and without, they know they are finished; like beasts at bay they will fight—and a hasty battle is exactly what they want.
entries.literal: Inner discord and outer rebellion—they know themselves they must be defeated; a cornered beast thinks of fighting; swift battle further fits their intent.

entries.zh: 雖云必克，傷人亦多。
entries.en: We might win a rush attack, but the butcher’s bill would be steep.
entries.literal: Although it is said one must surely overcome, the wounded will also be many.

entries.zh: 且儉等欺誑將士，詭變萬端，小與持久，詐情自露，此不戰而克之也。」
entries.en: Moreover, Guanqiu Jian and the others deceive and mislead their officers and soldiers, changing deceitfully in a myriad ways. Stay with them a little longer, and their fraudulent situation will reveal itself; this is conquering them without battle."
entries.literal: Moreover, Guanqiu Jian and the others deceive and mislead their officers and soldiers, changing deceitfully in a myriad ways. Stay with them a little longer, and their fraudulent situation will reveal itself; this is conquering them without battle."

entries.zh: 乃遣諸葛誕督豫州諸軍自安風向壽春，征東將軍胡遵督青、徐諸軍出譙宋之間，絕其歸路。
entries.en: He sent Zhuge Dan with the Yu columns from Anfeng toward Shouchun and Hu Zun with Qing–Xu forces through the Qiao–Song corridor to sever their retreat.
entries.literal: Thereupon he dispatched Zhuge Dan to supervise Yu Province troops from Anfeng toward Shouchun, and General Who Conquers the East Hu Zun to supervise Qing and Xu troops out between Qiao and Song, cutting off their return route.

entries.zh: 帝屯汝陽，遣競州刺史鄧艾督太山諸軍進屯樂嘉，示弱以誘之。
entries.en: Sima Shi camped at Ruyang and ordered Yanzhou Inspector Deng Ai to push the Taishan contingents forward to Lejia and feign weakness as bait.
entries.literal: The Emperor encamped at Ruyang and sent Inspector of Yan Province Deng Ai to supervise Taishan troops to advance and encamp at Lejia, showing weakness in order to lure them.

entries.zh: 欽進軍將攻艾，帝潛軍銜枚，輕造樂嘉，與欽相遇。
entries.en: When Wen Qin advanced on Deng Ai, Sima Shi slipped an army forward with bits in the horses’ mouths, raced to Lejia, and met Wen Qin head-on.
entries.literal: Qin advanced the army about to attack Ai; the Emperor secretly moved troops with mouth-gags, lightly went to Lejia, and encountered Qin.

entries.zh: 欽子鴦，年十八，勇冠三軍，謂欽曰：「及其未定，請登城鼓噪，擊之可破也。」
entries.en: Qin's son Yang was eighteen, and his courage topped the three armies. He said to Qin, "Before they are settled, please climb the wall, beat the drums, and shout; attacking them can break them."
entries.literal: Qin's son Yang was eighteen, and his courage topped the three armies. He said to Qin, "Before they are settled, please climb the wall, beat the drums, and shout; attacking them can break them."

entries.zh: 既謀而行，三噪而欽不能應，鴦退，相與引而東。
entries.en: They put the plan in motion, but after three rounds of shouting Wen Qin never moved; Yang fell back, and father and son drew off toward the east.
entries.literal: Having planned then acting, three clamors yet Qin could not respond; Yang withdrew, together they led away eastward.

entries.zh: 帝謂諸將曰：「欽走矣。」
entries.en: Sima Shi told the generals, "Qin has fled."
entries.literal: Sima Shi told the generals, "Qin has fled."

entries.zh: 命發銳軍以追之。
entries.en: He ordered the elite vanguard forward in pursuit.
entries.literal: He ordered to dispatch picked troops to pursue them.

entries.zh: 諸將皆曰：「欽舊將，鴦少而銳，引軍內入，未有失利，必不走也。」
entries.en: The generals all said, "Qin is an old general, and Yang is young and sharp. They led the army deep inside and have not yet suffered defeat; they surely will not flee."
entries.literal: The generals all said, "Qin is an old general, and Yang is young and sharp. They led the army deep inside and have not yet suffered defeat; they surely will not flee."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「一鼓作氣，再而衰，三而竭。
entries.en: Sima Shi said, "With one drumbeat, spirit rises; with the second it declines; with the third it is exhausted.
entries.literal: Sima Shi said, "With one drumbeat, spirit rises; with the second it declines; with the third it is exhausted.

entries.zh: 鴦三鼓，欽不應，其勢已屈，不走何待？」
entries.en: Yang beat the drum three times, and Qin did not respond; their force is already bent. If they do not flee, what are they waiting for?"
entries.literal: Yang beat the drum three times, and Qin did not respond; their force is already bent. If they do not flee, what are they waiting for?"

entries.zh: 欽將遁，鴦曰：「不先折其勢，不得去也。」
entries.en: When Qin was about to flee, Yang said, "If we do not first break their force, we cannot leave."
entries.literal: When Qin was about to flee, Yang said, "If we do not first break their force, we cannot leave."

entries.zh: 乃與驍騎十餘摧鋒陷陣，所向皆披靡，遂引去。
entries.en: He led a dozen picked horsemen in a spearhead charge that scattered every line before him, then broke off and withdrew.
entries.literal: Then with more than ten swift cavalry he shattered the vanguard and broke formations; wherever he went all were swept aside; then he led away.

entries.zh: 帝遣左長史司馬璉督驍騎八千翼而追之，使將軍樂林等督步兵繼其後。
entries.en: Sima Shi sent his left chief clerk Sima Lian with eight thousand horse to sweep around Wen Qin’s flank and told generals such as Yue Lin to bring the footsoldiers up behind.
entries.literal: The Emperor sent Left Chief Clerk Sima Lian to supervise eight thousand swift cavalry to flank and pursue them, and ordered generals such as Yue Lin to supervise infantry to follow their rear.

entries.zh: 比至沙陽，頻陷欽陣，弩矢雨下，欽蒙盾而馳。
entries.en: By Shayang they had torn through Wen Qin’s lines again and again; bolts fell like rain, and Wen Qin crouched under his shield and spurred on.
entries.literal: By the time they reached Shayang, repeatedly they broke Qin's formations; crossbow bolts rained down; Qin covered himself with a shield and galloped.

entries.zh: 大破其軍。
entries.en: They shattered his army.
entries.literal: Greatly defeated his army.

entries.zh: 眾皆投戈而降，欽父子與麾下走保項。
entries.en: The men threw down their weapons and yielded; Wen Qin and his son raced with their remaining followers to the refuge of Xiang.
entries.literal: The host all cast aside halberds and surrendered; Qin father and son with those under their command fled to protect Xiang.

entries.zh: 儉聞欽敗，棄眾宵遁淮南。
entries.en: Guanqiu Jian, hearing of Wen Qin’s rout, abandoned his army and fled south into Huainan by night.
entries.literal: When Jian heard Qin was defeated, he abandoned the host and fled by night to Huainan.

entries.zh: 安風津都尉追儉，斬之，傳首京都。
entries.en: The commandant at Anfeng Ford ran him down, struck off his head, and sent it to the capital by post-horse.
entries.literal: The Commandant of Anfeng Ford pursued Jian, beheaded him, and sent the head by relay to the capital.

entries.zh: 欽遂奔吳，淮南平。
entries.en: Wen Qin escaped into Wu, and the Huainan rebellion was over.
entries.literal: Qin then fled to Wu; Huainan was pacified.

entries.zh: 四年春二月丁丑，天子復命帝如前，又固讓。
entries.en: On dingchou in the second month of spring, the fourth year, the emperor repeated the old honors; Sima Zhao refused again.
entries.literal: Fourth year, spring, second month, day dingchou, the Son of Heaven again ordered the Emperor as before; again firmly declined.

entries.zh: 三月，詔大將軍府增置司馬一人，從事中郎二人，舍人十人。
entries.en: In the third month an edict added one major, two retainers, and ten gentlemen to the grand general’s staff.
entries.literal: Third month, edict: Great General's mansion additionally establish one Major, two Retainers, ten Gentlemen.

entries.zh: 夏，帝將伐蜀，乃謀眾曰：「自定壽春已來，息役六年，治兵繕甲，以擬二虜。
entries.en: That summer, as he readied the Shu expedition, he told his council, "Six years have passed since Shouchun fell—six years we have spent forging arms to meet Wu and Shu.
entries.literal: Summer, the Emperor was about to campaign against Shu; then he consulted the host saying: "Since settling Shouchun, we have rested corvée six years, drilled troops and repaired armor, in order to target the two bandits.

entries.zh: 略計取吳，作戰船，通水道，當用千餘萬功，此十萬人百數十日事也。
entries.en: A Wu campaign—building hulls and dredging channels—would swallow ten million man-days; a hundred thousand laborers would need months on end.
entries.literal: Roughly calculating taking Wu, building war boats, opening water routes, ought to use more than ten million man-days of work; this is a matter of one hundred several tens of days for one hundred thousand men.

entries.zh: 又南土下濕，必生疾疫。
entries.en: The southern marshes breed sickness; an army would wilt there.
entries.literal: Moreover southern soil is low and damp; surely sickness and pestilence will arise.

entries.zh: 今宜先取蜀，三年之後，在巴蜀順流之勢，水陸並進，此滅虞定虢，吞韓並魏之勢也。
entries.en: Better to take Shu first; three years later, riding the Yangzi current from Ba and Shu, we can move by water and land together—the old stratagem of swallowing the neighbor to fatten the conqueror.
entries.literal: Now it is fitting first to take Shu; after three years, with Ba-Shu's down-current momentum, water and land advancing together—this is the momentum of destroying Yu and settling Guo, swallowing Han and annexing Wei.

entries.zh: 計蜀戰士九萬，居守成都及備他郡不下四萬，然則餘眾不過五萬。
entries.en: Shu lists ninety thousand troops, but forty thousand must hold Chengdu and the outlying commanderies—no more than fifty thousand can meet us in the field.
entries.literal: Calculating Shu warriors ninety thousand; dwelling to guard Chengdu and garrison other commanderies not less than forty thousand; then the remaining host does not exceed fifty thousand.

entries.zh: 今絆姜維於遝中，使不得東顧，直指駱穀，出其空虛之地，以襲漢中。
entries.en: Pin Jiang Wei in Taozhong so he cannot shift east, then drive straight through Luogu into the empty heart of Hanzhong.
entries.literal: Now pin Jiang Wei in Taozhong, causing him not to be able to look east; point straight to Luogu Valley, emerge in their empty hollow ground, to raid Hanzhong.

entries.zh: 彼若嬰城守險，兵勢必散，首尾離絕。
entries.en: If they hug the walls and cling to the defiles, their strength will splinter and van detach from van.
entries.literal: If they gird the city and guard the peril, military momentum must scatter; head and tail are cut off.

entries.zh: 舉大眾以屠城，散銳卒以略野，劍閣不暇守險，關頭不能自存。
entries.en: Mass the army to storm the towns, send flying columns to scour the open country, and Jiange will have no time to hold the narrows while the Guan passes collapse on their own.
entries.literal: Raise a great host to slaughter the city; scatter picked troops to sweep the wilds; Jiange will have no leisure to guard the peril; Guantou cannot preserve itself.

entries.zh: 以劉禪之暗，而邊城外破，士女內震，其亡可知也。」
entries.en: Liu Shan is a dull tool; once the frontier cracks and panic seizes the capital, his fall is a foregone conclusion."
entries.literal: With Liu Shan's darkness, and border cities broken from without, gentlemen and ladies within shaken, its perishing can be known.

entries.zh: 征西將軍鄧艾以為未有釁，屢陳異議。
entries.en: Deng Ai, the western commander, argued there was no opening yet and kept filing objections.
entries.literal: General Who Conquers the West Deng Ai thought there was not yet a crack, repeatedly presented divergent opinions.

entries.zh: 帝患之，使主簿師纂為艾司馬以喻之，艾乃奉命。
entries.en: Annoyed by Deng Ai’s foot-dragging, Sima Zhao made his chief clerk Shi Zuan Deng Ai’s major to talk sense into him; Deng then accepted the order.
entries.literal: The Emperor worried about it, ordered Chief Clerk Shi Zuan to become Ai's Major in order to instruct him; Ai then received the command.

entries.zh: 於是征四方之兵十八萬，使鄧艾自狄道攻姜維於遝中，雍州刺史諸葛緒自祁山軍于武街，絕維歸路，鎮西將軍鐘會帥前將軍李輔、征蜀護軍胡烈等自駱穀襲漢中。
entries.en: He raised a hundred and eighty thousand men from every quarter: Deng Ai moved from Didao against Jiang Wei in Taozhong; Yongzhou Inspector Zhuge Xu marched from Qishan to Wujie to sever Jiang Wei’s retreat; Zhong Hui, General Who Guards the West, led Li Fu, Hu Lie, and the rest through Luogu against Hanzhong.
entries.literal: Thereupon conscripted troops of the four quarters one hundred eighty thousand, ordered Deng Ai from Didao to attack Jiang Wei in Taozhong, Inspector of Yongzhou Zhuge Xu from Qishan to encamp at Wujie, cutting off Jiang Wei's return route, General Who Guards the West Zhong Hui leading Former General Li Fu, Shu Campaign Protector Hu Lie, and others from Luogu Valley to raid Hanzhong.

entries.zh: 秋八月，軍發洛陽，大賚將士，陳師誓眾。
entries.en: In the eighth month of autumn the host left Luoyang after rich gifts to the ranks, a full review, and oaths to the army.
entries.literal: Autumn, eighth month, the army set out from Luoyang, greatly rewarded officers and soldiers, arrayed the host and swore the multitude.

entries.zh: 將軍鄧敦謂蜀未可討，帝斬以徇。
entries.en: General Deng Dun said Shu was not ripe for attack; Sima Zhao struck off his head as a warning.
entries.literal: General Deng Dun said Shu could not be punished; the Emperor beheaded him to display.

entries.zh: 九月，又使天水太守王頎攻維營，隴西太守牽弘邀其前，金城太守楊頎趣甘松。
entries.en: In the ninth month he sent Tianshui’s Wang Qi against Jiang Wei’s camp, Longxi’s Qian Hong to block his van, and Jincheng’s Yang Qi toward Gansong.
entries.literal: Ninth month, again ordered Tianshui Grand Administrator Wang Qi to attack Wei's camp, Longxi Grand Administrator Qian Hong to intercept his front, Jincheng Grand Administrator Yang Qi to hurry to Gansong.

entries.zh: 鐘會分為二隊，入自斜谷，使李輔圍王含于樂城，又使步將易愷攻蔣斌于漢城。
entries.en: Zhong Hui split his force, entered by Xie Valley, set Li Fu to invest Wang Han at Lecheng, and sent Yi Kai against Jiang Bin at Hancheng.
entries.literal: Zhong Hui divided into two columns, entered from Xie Valley, ordered Li Fu to besiege Wang Han at Lecheng, also ordered infantry general Yi Kai to attack Jiang Bin at Hancheng.

entries.zh: 會直指陽安，護軍胡烈攻陷關城。
entries.en: Zhong Hui drove straight on Yang’an while Protector Hu Lie stormed the pass fort.
entries.literal: Hui pointed straight to Yang'an; Protector Hu Lie attacked and took Guancheng.

entries.zh: 姜維聞之，引還，王頎追敗維于強川。
entries.en: Jiang Wei wheeled about; Wang Qi ran him down at Qiangchuan and broke his column.
entries.literal: When Jiang Wei heard it, he led back; Wang Qi pursued and defeated Wei at Qiangchuan.

entries.zh: 維與張翼、廖化合軍守劍閣，鐘會攻之。
entries.en: Jiang Wei joined Zhang Yi and Liao Hua to hold Jiange; Zhong Hui laid siege.
entries.literal: Wei joined Zhang Yi and Liao Hua combining armies to guard Jiange; Zhong Hui attacked it.

entries.zh: 冬十月，天子以諸侯獻捷交至，乃申前命曰：
entries.en: In the tenth winter month, as victory dispatches from the lords piled in, the emperor renewed his earlier charge, saying:
entries.literal: Winter, tenth month, the Son of Heaven because the nobles' presented victories arrived in succession, then reiterated the former command saying:

entries.zh: 咸熙元年春正月，檻車征艾。
entries.en: In the first month of spring, Xianxi year 1, Deng Ai was summoned back in a prison cart.
entries.literal: First year of Xianxi, spring, first month, caged cart summoned Ai.

entries.zh: 乙丑，帝奉天子西征，次於長安。
entries.en: On yichou he escorted the emperor west and encamped at Chang’an.
entries.literal: On yichou, the Emperor escorting the Son of Heaven west campaigned, halted at Chang'an.

entries.zh: 是時魏諸王侯悉在鄴城，命從事中郎山濤行軍司事，鎮於鄴，遣護軍賈充持節、督諸軍，據漢中。
entries.en: With every Wei prince gathered at Yecheng, he put Shan Tao in charge of rear-area command there and sent Jia Chong with baton to oversee the armies holding Hanzhong.
entries.literal: At this time Wei various princes and marquises were all at Yecheng; he ordered Retainer Shan Tao to conduct army affairs, garrisoning at Yecheng; sent Army Protector Jia Chong bearing credentials, supervising the various armies, occupying Hanzhong.

entries.zh: 鐘會遂反於蜀，監軍衛瓘、右將軍胡烈攻會，斬之。
entries.en: Zhong Hui rose in Shu; Wei Guan and Hu Lie struck him down and took his head.
entries.literal: Zhong Hui then rebelled in Shu; Army Supervisor Wei Guan, General of the Right Hu Lie attacked Hui, beheaded him.

entries.zh: 初，會之伐蜀也，西曹屬邵悌言於帝曰：「鐘會難信，不可令行。」
entries.en: At first, when Zhong Hui was attacking Shu, Shao Ti, subordinate of the Western Bureau, said to Sima Zhao, "Zhong Hui is hard to trust; he must not be allowed to go."
entries.literal: At first, when Zhong Hui was attacking Shu, Shao Ti, subordinate of the Western Bureau, said to Sima Zhao, "Zhong Hui is hard to trust; he must not be allowed to go."

entries.zh: 帝笑曰：「取蜀如指掌，而眾人皆言不可，唯會與吾意同。
entries.en: Sima Zhao had only smiled and said, "Shu will fall as easily as reading one’s palm, though everyone else doubted—only Zhong Hui shared my view.
entries.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "Taking Shu is like pointing at the palm; yet the host of men all say it cannot be done; only Hui and Our intent agree.

entries.zh: 滅蜀之後，中國將士，人自思歸，蜀之遺黎，猶懷震恐，縱有異志，無能為也。」
entries.en: After Shu fell, every northern soldier would pine for home and the Shu populace would still quake with fear—even if someone harbored treason, he could do nothing with it."
entries.literal: After extinguishing Shu, central state's officers and soldiers, each person thinks of returning; Shu's surviving common people still cherish trembling fear; even if they had different intent, they have no ability to act.

entries.zh: 卒如所量。
entries.en: Events proved him exactly right.
entries.literal: In the end it was as he had measured.

entries.zh: 丙辰，帝至自長安。
entries.en: On bingchen he returned from Chang’an to the capital.
entries.literal: On bingchen, the Emperor arrived from Chang'an.

entries.zh: 三月己卯，進帝爵為王，增封並前二十郡。
entries.en: On jimao in the third month he was raised from duke to king with twenty commanderies in all, old grants and new.
entries.literal: Third month, day jimao, advanced the Emperor's noble rank to king, increased fief together with the previous twenty commanderies.

entries.zh: 夏五月癸未，天子追加舞陽宣文侯為晉宣王，舞陽忠武侯為晉景王。
entries.en: On guiwei in the fifth month of summer the emperor posthumously raised Sima Yi to Prince Xuan of Jin and Sima Shi to Prince Jing of Jin.
entries.literal: Summer, fifth month, day guiwei, the Son of Heaven posthumously added Wuyang Marquis Xuanwen as Jin King Xuan, Wuyang Marquis Zhongwu as Jin King Jing.

entries.zh: 秋七月，帝奏司空荀顗定禮儀，中護軍賈充正法律，尚書僕射裴秀議官制，太保鄭沖總而裁焉。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn he charged Xun Yi with the rites, Jia Chong with the laws, Pei Xiu with the bureaucracy, and Zheng Chong as coordinator over all.
entries.literal: Autumn, seventh month, the Emperor memorialized Minister of Works Xun Yi to fix rites and ceremonies, Central Army Protector Jia Chong to rectify laws and statutes, Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Xiu to deliberate official system, Grand Guardian Zheng Chong overall to judge them.

entries.zh: 始建五等爵。
entries.en: He began the institution of the five orders of nobility.
entries.literal: For the first time established the five ranks of nobility.

entries.zh: 冬十月丁亥，奏遣吳人相國參軍徐劭、散騎常侍水曹屬孫彧使吳，喻孫皓以平蜀之事，致馬錦等物，以示威懷。
entries.en: On dinghai in the tenth winter month he memorialized to send Xu Shao and Sun Yu—Wu natives in his service—to Wu with horses and brocade, to tell Sun Hao of Shu’s fall and to blend threat with kindness.
entries.literal: Winter, tenth month, day dinghai, memorialized to send Wu man Chancellor of State Army Advisor Xu Shao, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Water Bureau Subordinate Sun Yu as envoys to Wu, informing Sun Hao of the affair of pacifying Shu, presenting horses, brocade, and such objects, in order to show awe and cherishing.

entries.zh: 丙午，天子命中撫軍新昌鄉侯炎為晉世子。
entries.en: On bingwu the emperor named Sima Yan, the Central Stabilizing General and Marquis of Xinchang township, heir apparent of Jin.
entries.literal: On bingwu, the Son of Heaven ordered Central General Who Stabilizes the Army, village marquis of Xinchang Yan, to be Jin heir apparent.

entries.zh: 公卿將校皆詣府喻旨，帝以禮辭讓。
entries.en: The high ministers and commanders crowded his gate with the edict; he declined again by formal courtesy.
entries.literal: Dukes, ministers, generals, and colonels all went to the mansion to explain the intent; the Emperor by rite declined.

entries.zh: 司空鄭沖率群官勸進曰：「伏見嘉命顯至，竊聞明公固讓，沖等眷眷，實有愚心。
entries.en: Minister of Works Zheng Chong led the assembled officials in urging advancement, saying, "We humbly see that the fine command has manifestly arrived, and privately hear that your enlightened lordship firmly declines it. Chong and the others are full of concern and truly have a foolish thought.
entries.literal: Minister of Works Zheng Chong led the assembled officials in urging advancement, saying, "We humbly see that the fine command has manifestly arrived, and privately hear that your enlightened lordship firmly declines it. Chong and the others are full of concern and truly have a foolish thought.

entries.zh: 以為聖王作制，百代同風，褒德賞功，有自來矣。
entries.en: The sage kings set precedent for every age: to honor merit is the way of antiquity itself.
entries.literal: We consider that the sage king makes institutions; a hundred generations share one wind; praising virtue and rewarding merit has had its source from of old.

entries.zh: 昔伊尹，有莘氏之媵臣耳，一佐成湯，遂荷阿衡之號。
entries.en: Yi Yin began as a mere attendant of Youxin; one service to Tang won him the name Ah Heng.
entries.literal: In the past Yi Yin was only Youxin's accompanying minister; once he assisted Cheng Tang, then he bore the title of Ah Heng.

entries.zh: 周公藉已成之勢，據既安之業，光宅曲阜，奄有龜蒙。
entries.en: The Duke of Zhou took power already won and a realm already calm, then made Qufu his seat and held Gui and Meng.
entries.literal: The Duke of Zhou leaned on already completed power, occupied already secure enterprise, brightly dwelt at Qufu, covered Gui and Meng.

entries.zh: 呂尚，磻溪之漁者也，一朝指麾，乃封營丘。
entries.en: Lü Shang was a fisherman by Pan Creek; one morning’s command won him Yingqiu.
entries.literal: Lü Shang was a fisherman of Panxi; one morning directing and waving, then was enfeoffed at Yingqiu.

entries.zh: 自是以來，功薄而賞厚者，不可勝數，然賢哲之士，猶以為美談。
entries.en: Since then thin merit has often drawn rich reward—yet wise men still praise those tales.
entries.literal: From this onward, those whose merit was thin yet reward was thick cannot be counted; yet worthy and wise gentlemen still take them as fine tales.

entries.zh: 況自先相國以來，世有明德，翼輔魏室，以綏天下，朝無秕政，人無謗言。
entries.en: From the former Chancellor of State onward, each generation has aided Wei with shining virtue until the court is clean of chaff and the people free of slander.
entries.literal: Moreover since the former Chancellor of State, generation after generation there has been bright virtue, winging and assisting the Wei house, thereby pacifying all under Heaven; court has no chaff government, men have no slanderous words.

entries.zh: 前者明公西征靈州，北臨沙漠，榆中以西，望風震服，羌戎來馳，回首內向，東誅叛逆，全軍獨克。
entries.en: You marched west to Lingzhou and north to the sands; west of Yuzhong every tribe trembled into submission; Qiang and Rong wheeled their horses toward the throne; in the east you cut down rebels alone and whole.
entries.literal: Formerly the enlightened lord west campaigned Lingzhou, north faced the desert; west of Yuzhong, gazing at the wind trembled and submitted; Qiang and Rong came galloping, turned head inward; east punished rebels and traitors, whole army alone overcame.

entries.zh: 禽闔閭之將，虜輕銳之卒以萬萬計，威加南海，名懾三越，宇內康寧，苛慝不作。
entries.en: You took Wu’s generals and tens of thousands of their best troops, spread terror to the Southern Sea and the three Yues, and brought peace so that cruelty died away.
entries.literal: Captured Helü's generals, took light keen soldiers by the ten thousands counted; awe added to South Sea, name overawed the three Yues; within the four seas peaceful and tranquil, harsh evil did not arise.

entries.zh: 是以時俗畏懷，東夷獻舞。
entries.en: The age stands in awe; even the eastern Yi send dancers to your court.
entries.literal: Therefore the age's customs feared and cherished; eastern Yi presented dance.

entries.zh: 故聖上覽乃昔以來禮典舊章，開國光宅，顯茲太原。
entries.en: Therefore the sage Son of Heaven has weighed the old statutes and opened a bright fief for you at Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Therefore the sage superior surveys thence past rites and canons, old regulations, opens state and bright dwelling, displays this Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 明公宜承奉聖旨，受茲介福，允當天人。
entries.en: You should accept the imperial word, take this great blessing, and satisfy both Heaven and the people.
entries.literal: The enlightened lord ought to receive and follow the sage decree, receive this great blessing, truly meet Heaven and men.

entries.zh: 元功盛勳，光光如彼；
entries.en: Your founding merit shines so bright;
entries.literal: Founding merit and blazing achievement, blazingly thus;

entries.zh: 國土嘉祚，巍巍如此。
entries.en: the fief and fortune offered you stand so high.
entries.literal: State soil and fine blessing, thus lofty.

entries.zh: 內外協同，靡愆靡違。
entries.en: Within and without all move as one, without fault or breach.
entries.literal: Inner and outer join in harmony; none fault, none violate.

entries.zh: 由斯征伐，則可朝服濟江，掃除吳會，西塞江源，望祀岷山。
entries.en: With that you may cross the Yangzi in court dress, sweep Wu clean, seal the river’s upper course, and offer the rite on Mount Min.
entries.literal: From this campaigning, then can in court robes cross the Yangtze, sweep and clear Wu and Hui, west block Yangtze's source, gaze-sacrifice Mount Min.

entries.zh: 回戈弭節，以麾天下，遠無不服，邇無不肅。
entries.en: Then lay by spear and still the reins to command the realm until the far submit and the near stand in awe.
entries.literal: Turn halberd and still the baton, thereby to command all under Heaven; far none not submit, near none not solemn.

entries.zh: 令大魏之德，光于唐虞；
entries.en: Great Wei’s virtue will outshine Tang and Yu;
entries.literal: Let great Wei's virtue shine on Tang and Yu;

entries.zh: 明公盛勳，超于桓文。
entries.en: and your merit will rise above Huan and Wen.
entries.literal: the enlightened lord's blazing merit surpasses Huan and Wen.

entries.zh: 然後臨滄海而謝支伯，登箕山而揖許由，豈不盛乎！
entries.en: Then you might stand by the eastern sea as kings of old did before worthy recluses, or climb Mount Ji to salute Xu You—what could be more glorious!
entries.literal: Then facing the dark sea and thanking Zhibo, ascending Mount Ji and bowing to Xu You—is it not grand!

entries.zh: 至公至平，誰與為鄰，何必勤勤小讓也哉。」
entries.en: With utmost publicness and utmost fairness, who can be your neighbor? Why must you earnestly make this small refusal?"
entries.literal: With utmost publicness and utmost fairness, who can be your neighbor? Why must you earnestly make this small refusal?"

entries.zh: 帝乃受命。
entries.en: Sima Zhao then accepted.
entries.literal: The Emperor then received the command.

entries.zh: 十一月，鄧艾帥萬餘人自陰平逾絕險至江由，破蜀將諸葛瞻於綿竹，斬瞻，傳首。
entries.en: In the eleventh month Deng Ai took ten thousand men over the sheer track from Yinping to Jiangyou, crushed Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu, struck off his head, and sent it east by post.
entries.literal: Eleventh month, Deng Ai led more than ten thousand from Yinping crossing extreme peril to reach Jiangyou, defeated Shu general Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu, beheaded Zhan, sent the head by relay.

entries.zh: 進軍雒縣，劉禪降。
entries.en: He pushed on to Luo county, and Liu Shan yielded.
entries.literal: Advanced the army to Luo county; Liu Shan surrendered.

entries.zh: 天子命晉公以相國總百揆，於是上節傳，去侍中、大都督、錄尚書之號焉。
entries.en: The emperor named the Duke of Jin chancellor with full authority over the government; Sima Zhao thereupon returned his batons and dropped the concurrent titles of Palace Attendant, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and overseer of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven ordered the Duke of Jin by Chancellor of State to overall command the hundred handles; thereupon he submitted credentials and tallies, removed Palace Attendant, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and recording Director of the Secretariat titles.

entries.zh: 表鄧艾為太尉，鐘會為司徒。
entries.en: He recommended Deng Ai for Grand Commandant and Zhong Hui for Minister of Education.
entries.literal: He memorialized Deng Ai as Grand Commandant, Zhong Hui as Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 會潛謀叛逆，因密使譖艾。
entries.en: Zhong Hui plotted revolt in secret and sent agents to traduce Deng Ai.
entries.literal: Hui secretly plotted rebellion, thereby secretly sent to slander Ai.

entries.zh: 丁卯，遣太僕劉原告于太廟。
entries.en: On dingmao he dispatched grand coachman Liu Yuan to report to the imperial temple.
entries.literal: On dingmao he sent grand coachman Liu Yuan to announce the matter in the grand temple.

entries.zh: 封魏帝爲陳留王，邑萬戶，居於鄴宮；
entries.en: The last Wei sovereign became king of Chenliu with a fief of ten thousand households, residing at Ye.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed the Wei emperor as king of Chenliu, with ten thousand households, dwelling in the Ye palace;

entries.zh: 魏氏諸王皆爲縣侯。
entries.en: Every other Wei prince was reduced to county marquis.
entries.literal: All kings of the house of Wei were made county marquises.

entries.zh: 追尊宣王爲宣皇帝，景王爲景皇帝，文王爲文皇帝，宣王妃張氏爲宣穆皇后。
entries.en: He posthumously honored King Xuan as Emperor Xuan, King Jing as Emperor Jing, and King Wen as Emperor Wen, and honored Lady Zhang, consort of King Xuan, as Empress Xuanmu.
entries.literal: He posthumously honored king Xuan as emperor Xuan, king Jing as emperor Jing, king Wen as emperor Wen, and king Xuan’s consort, lady Zhang, as empress Xuanmu.

entries.zh: 尊太妃王氏曰皇太后，宮曰崇化。
entries.en: Lady Wang, the grand consort, became empress dowager with her palace named Chonghua.
entries.literal: He honored grand consort Wang as empress dowager, her residence titled Chonghua.

entries.zh: 封皇叔祖父孚爲安平王，皇叔父幹爲平原王，亮爲扶風王，伷爲東莞王，駿爲汝陰王，肜爲梁王，倫爲琅邪王，皇弟攸爲齊王，鑒爲樂安王，機爲燕王，[1]皇從伯父望爲義陽王，皇從叔父輔爲渤海王，晃爲下邳王，瑰爲太原王，珪爲高陽王，衡爲常山王，子文爲沛王，[2]泰爲隴西王，權爲彭城王，綏爲范陽王，遂爲濟南王，遜爲譙王，睦爲中山王，陵爲北海王，斌爲陳王，皇從父兄洪爲河間王，皇從父弟楙爲東平王。
entries.en: He enfeoffed his granduncle Sima Fu as king of Anping; his uncles Sima Gan as king of Pingyuan, Liang as king of Fufeng, Zhou as king of Dongguan, Jun as king of Ruyin, Tong as king of Liang, and Lun as king of Langye; his younger brother You as king of Qi, Jian as king of Lean, and Ji as king of Yan; [1] his father's elder cousin Wang as king of Yiyang; his father's younger cousins Fu as king of Bohai, Huang as king of Xiapi, Gui as king of Taiyuan, Gui as king of Gaoyang, Heng as king of Changshan, Ziwen as king of Pei, [2] Tai as king of Longxi, Quan as king of Pengcheng, Sui as king of Fanyang, Sui as king of Jinan, Xun as king of Qiao, Mu as king of Zhongshan, Ling as king of Beihai, and Bin as king of Chen; his elder cousin Hong as king of Hejian; and his younger cousin Mao as king of Dongping.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed his granduncle Sima Fu as king of Anping, his uncles Sima Gan as king of Pingyuan, Liang as king of Fufeng, Zhou as king of Dongguan, Jun as king of Ru'yin, Tong as king of Liang, Lun as king of Langye, his younger brother You as king of Qi, Jian as king of Le'an, Ji as king of Yan, [1] his cousin once removed Wang as king of Yiyang, his father's younger cousins Fu as king of Bohai, Huang as king of Xiapi, Gui as king of Taiyuan, Gui as king of Gaoyang, Heng as king of Changshan, Ziwen as king of Pei, [2] Tai as king of Longxi, Quan as king of Pengcheng, Sui as king of Fanyang, Sui as king of Jinan, Xun as king of Qiao, Mu as king of Zhongshan, Ling as king of Beihai, and Bin as king of Chen, his cousin Hong as king of Hejian, and his cousin Mao as king of Dongping.

entries.zh: 以驃騎將軍石苞爲大司馬，封樂陵公，車騎將軍陳騫爲高平公，衛將軍賈充爲車騎將軍、魯公，尚書令裴秀爲鉅鹿公，侍中荀勖爲濟北公，太保鄭沖爲太傅、壽光公，太尉王祥爲太保、睢陵公，丞相何曾爲太尉、朗陵公，御史大夫王沈爲驃騎將軍、博陵公，司空荀顗爲臨淮公，鎮北大將軍衛瓘爲菑陽公。
entries.en: He appointed Shi Bao, general of swift cavalry, grand marshal and duke of Leling; Chen Qian duke of Gaoping; Jia Chong general of chariots and cavalry and duke of Lu; Pei Xiu duke of Julu; Xun Xu duke of Jibei; Zheng Chong grand tutor and duke of Shouguang; Wang Xiang grand guardian and duke of Suiling; He Zeng grand commandant and duke of Langling; Wang Chen general of swift cavalry and duke of Boling; Xun Yi duke of Linhuai; and Wei Guan duke of Ziyang.
entries.literal: He appointed Shi Bao, general of swift cavalry, as grand marshal with enfeoffment as duke of Leling; Chen Qian, general of chariots and cavalry, as duke of Gaoping; Jia Chong, guard general, as general of chariots and cavalry and duke of Lu; Pei Xiu, supervisor of the masters of writing, as duke of Julu; Xun Xu, palace attendant, as duke of Jibei; Zheng Chong, grand guardian, as grand tutor and duke of Shouguang; Wang Xiang, grand commandant, as grand protector and duke of Suiling; He Zeng, chancellor, as grand commandant and duke of Langling; Wang Chen, imperial counselor, as general of swift cavalry and duke of Boling; Xun Yi, minister of works, as duke of Linhuai; Wei Guan, great general who guards the north, as duke of Ziyang.

entries.zh: 其餘增封進爵各有差，文武普增位二等。
entries.en: Others were promoted in title by degrees, and the whole bureaucracy gained two steps in rank.
entries.literal: The rest received increased fiefs and advanced noble ranks each according to difference; civil and military officials were universally advanced two grades in rank.

entries.zh: 改景初曆爲太始曆，臘以酉，社以丑。
entries.en: The calendar was renamed from Jingchu to Taishi; the year-end rite was fixed in you and the soil altar in chou.
entries.literal: He changed the Jingchu calendar to the Taishi calendar, with year-end sacrifice in the you hour and earth god in the chou hour.

entries.zh: 二月，以雍州隴右五郡及涼州之金城、梁州之陰平置秦州。
entries.en: In the second month he carved out Qin province, combining the five Longyou commanderies under Yong with Jincheng from the Hexi frontier and Yinping from the Hanzhong basin.
entries.literal: In the second month Qin province was established from the five commanderies of Yongzhou west of the Long Range, together with Jincheng commandery from the northwest frontier and Yinping commandery from the Hanzhong uplands.

entries.zh: 辛巳，白龍二見於趙國。
entries.en: On xinsi two white dragons appeared in Zhao.
entries.literal: On the day xinsi two white dragons were seen in the principality of Zhao.

entries.zh: 青、徐、兗三州水，遣使振恤之。
entries.en: Flooding struck Qing, Xu, and Yan; the court dispatched inspectors with grain and aid.
entries.literal: The provinces of Qing, Xu, and Yan suffered floods; envoys were sent to relieve them.

entries.zh: 壬寅，以尚書左僕射羊祜都督荊州諸軍事，征東大將軍衛瓘都督青州諸軍事，東莞王伷鎮東大將軍、都督徐州諸軍事。
entries.en: On renyin Yang Hu took command on the Jing front, Wei Guan on the Qing front, and Sima Zhou of Dongguan became commander-in-chief on the Xu front.
entries.literal: On the day renyin, Yang Hu, senior vice-director of the masters of the left, was appointed to supervise all military affairs of Jing province; Wei Guan, great general who campaigns east, was appointed to supervise all military affairs of Qing province; king Zhou of Dongguan was made great general who guards the east and supervisor of all military affairs of Xu province.

entries.zh: 丁亥，詔曰：「古者歲書群吏之能否，三年而誅賞之。
entries.en: On dinghai, an edict said, "In antiquity, each year the ability or inability of the assembled clerks was written down, and after three years they were punished or rewarded.
entries.literal: On the day dinghai an edict said: “In antiquity the year’s record set down whether host of clerks could or could not perform their duties; after three years they were executed or rewarded.

entries.zh: 諸令史前後，但簡遣疏劣，而無有勸進，非黜陟之謂也。
entries.en: So far prefects had only purged the useless without promoting the able—that was not true evaluation.
entries.literal: Among the clerks of the various prefectures, hitherto only the slack and inferior were winnowed out and dismissed, while there was no encouragement of advancement—this is not what demotion and promotion mean.

entries.zh: 其條勤能有稱尤異者，歲以爲常。
entries.en: Any clerk praised year after year for diligence and talent should be entered on a standing honor roll.
entries.literal: Let those whose diligence and ability win praise as outstanding be recorded annually as a constant rule.

entries.zh: 吾將議其功勞。」
entries.en: The throne will then weigh rewards for proven service.”
entries.literal: I shall deliberate their merit and labor.”

entries.zh: 己未，詔蜀相諸葛亮孫京隨才署吏。
entries.en: On jiwei, Zhuge Liang's grandson Zhuge Jing was assigned an office suited to his talents.
entries.literal: On jiwei, an edict ordered that Zhuge Jing, grandson of Zhuge Liang, chancellor of Shu, be appointed to office according to his abilities.

entries.zh: 十二月，吳夏口督、前將軍孫秀帥眾來奔，拜驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，封會稽公。
entries.en: In the twelfth month: Sun Xiu, Wu’s Xiakou commander, defected with his army and received a ducal title and swift-cavalry command.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month Sun Xiu, Wu’s commander at Xiakou and former forward general, led his troops to defect; he was appointed general of swift cavalry with independent command equal to the three excellencies and enfeoffed as duke of Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 戊辰，復置鎮軍官。
entries.en: On wuchen the “guard the army” office was revived.
entries.literal: On the day wuchen the post of general who guards the army was restored.

entries.zh: 三月，孫皓帥眾趨壽陽，遣大司馬望屯淮北以距之。
entries.en: Third month: Sun Hao marched on Shouyang; grand marshal Sima Wang took station north of the Huai to meet him.
entries.literal: In the third month Sun Hao led his host toward Shouyang; the grand marshal Wang was sent to encamp north of the Huai to block him.

entries.zh: 丙戌，司空、鉅鹿公裴秀薨。
entries.en: On bingxu [13] Pei Xiu, minister of works, died.
entries.literal: On the day bingxu [13] Pei Xiu, minister of works and duke of Julu, died.

entries.zh: 癸巳，以中護軍王業爲尚書左僕射，高陽王珪爲尚書右僕射。
entries.en: Guisi: Wang Ye, Central Protector of the Army, was made left vice-director of the Secretariat, and Sima Gui, King of Gaoyang, was made right vice-director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: On the day guisi Wang Ye, central protector, was appointed senior vice-director of the masters of the left, and king Gui of Gaoyang senior vice-director of the masters of the right.

entries.zh: 孫秀部將何崇帥眾五千人來降。
entries.en: Sun Xiu’s officer He Chong brought five thousand soldiers over to Jin.
entries.literal: He Chong, a subordinate general under Sun Xiu, led five thousand men to surrender.

entries.zh: 秋七月癸酉，以車騎將軍賈充爲都督秦、涼二州諸軍事。
entries.en: Seventh month, guiyou: Jia Chong took joint command of Qin and Liang.
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day guiyou, Jia Chong, general of chariots and cavalry, was appointed supervisor of all military affairs of Qin and Liang provinces.

entries.zh: 吳將陶璜等圍交趾，太守楊稷與鬱林太守毛炅及日南等三郡降於吳。
entries.en: Tao Huang’s Wu army penned Jiaozhi until Yang Ji, Mao Jiong, and the coast surrendered.
entries.literal: Wu generals including Tao Huang besieged Jiaozhi; prefect Yang Ji together with Mao Jiong of Yulin and the three commanderies of Rinan and others surrendered to Wu.

entries.zh: 八月丙戌，以征東大將軍衛瓘爲征北大將軍、都督幽州諸軍事。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on bingxu, Wei Guan was moved from General-in-chief Who Campaigns East to General-in-chief Who Campaigns North and given command of Youzhou military affairs.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on bingxu, Wei Guan, General-in-chief Who Campaigns East, was made General-in-chief Who Campaigns North and Area Commander of military affairs in Youzhou.

entries.zh: 丙申，城陽王憲薨。
entries.en: On bingshen, Prince Xian of Chengyang died.
entries.literal: On bingshen, Xian, Prince of Chengyang, died.

entries.zh: 分益州之南中四郡置寧州，曲赦四郡殊死已下。
entries.en: The four Nanzhong commanderies were detached from Yizhou to form Ningzhou, and a special amnesty there covered capital offenders and below.
entries.literal: The four Nanzhong commanderies of Yizhou were separated to establish Ningzhou, and within the four commanderies those sentenced to death and below were specially pardoned.

entries.zh: 十二月丁亥，追尊宣帝廟曰高祖，景帝曰世宗，文帝曰太祖。
entries.en: Dinghai: Xuan, Jing, and Wen received temple names Gaozu, Shizong, and Taizu.
entries.literal: On the day dinghai of the twelfth month posthumous temple names were raised: emperor Xuan as Gaozu, emperor Jing as Shizong, emperor Wen as Taizu.

entries.zh: 是月大疫，洛陽死者太半。
entries.en: A plague carried off over half of Luoyang that month.
entries.literal: That month a great pestilence struck; more than half died in Luoyang.

entries.zh: 封裴頠爲鉅鹿公。
entries.en: Pei Wei received the Julu ducal title.
entries.literal: Pei Wei was enfeoffed as duke of Julu.

entries.zh: 三年春正月丙子朔，日有蝕之。
entries.en: In the third year, spring, first month, on the bingzi new moon, the sun was eclipsed.
entries.literal: In the third year, spring, first month, on the bingzi new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun.

entries.zh: 立皇子裕爲始平王，安平穆王隆弟敦爲安平王。
entries.en: The emperor made his son Yu prince of Shiping and made Dun, younger brother of Long, Prince Mu of Anping, prince of Anping.
entries.literal: The imperial son Yu was established as Prince of Shiping, and Dun, younger brother of Long, Prince Mu of Anping, was established as Prince of Anping.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「宗室戚屬，國之枝葉，欲令奉率德義，爲天下式。
entries.en: An edict declared: "The imperial kin are the state's branches and leaves; they should uphold virtue and righteousness and serve as models for the realm.
entries.literal: An edict said: "The imperial clan and kin by marriage are the branches and leaves of the state; I wish to have them uphold and lead in virtue and righteousness, becoming a model for the realm.

entries.zh: 然處富貴而能慎行者寡，召穆公糾合兄弟而賦唐棣之詩，此姬氏所以本枝百世也。
entries.en: Yet few men in wealth and rank remain careful. Lord Mu of Shao gathered his brothers and sang Tangdi; by such means the Ji clan preserved root and branch for generations.
entries.literal: Yet few who occupy wealth and rank can conduct themselves cautiously; Lord Mu of Shao gathered his brothers and composed the poem Tangdi, and this was how the Ji lineage kept root and branch for a hundred generations.

entries.zh: 今以衛將軍、扶風王亮爲宗師，所當施行，皆諮之於宗師也。」
entries.en: I now appoint Liang, Prince of Fufeng and Guards General, as Master of the Clan; all clan measures are to be referred to him."
entries.literal: Now I make the Guards General, Liang, Prince of Fufeng, Master of the Clan; all measures to be carried out shall be consulted with the Master of the Clan."

entries.zh: 庚寅，始平王裕薨。
entries.en: On gengyin, Prince Yu of Shiping died.
entries.literal: On gengyin, Yu, Prince of Shiping, died.

entries.zh: 有星孛於西方。
entries.en: A comet appeared in the west.
entries.literal: There was a broom star in the west.

entries.zh: 使征北大將軍衛瓘討鮮卑力微。
entries.en: Wei Guan, General-in-chief Who Campaigns North, was sent against the Xianbei leader Liwei.
entries.literal: He sent Wei Guan, General-in-chief Who Campaigns North, to campaign against Liwei of the Xianbei.

entries.zh: 三月，平虜護軍文淑討叛虜樹機能等，並破之。
entries.en: Third month: Wen Shu, Protector-general Who Pacifies the Captives, defeated the rebel forces of Shujineng and the others.
entries.literal: In the third month, Wen Shu, Protector-general Who Pacifies the Captives, campaigned against the rebel captives Shujineng and the others and defeated them all.

entries.zh: 有星孛于胃。
entries.en: A comet trailed through the Wei mansion.
entries.literal: A broom star appeared in the asterism Wei.

entries.zh: 乙未，帝將射雉，慮損麥苗而止。
entries.en: Yiwei: he canceled a hunt lest arrows trample the wheat.
entries.literal: On the day yiwei the emperor was about to shoot pheasants but stopped, fearing damage to the wheat.

entries.zh: 冬十月，以征北大將軍衛瓘爲尚書令。
entries.en: Winter: northern commander Wei Guan took over the secretariat.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month Wei Guan, great general who campaigns north, was appointed supervisor of the masters of writing.

entries.zh: 揚州刺史應綽伐吳皖城，斬首五千級，焚穀米百八十萬斛。
entries.en: Ying Chuo stormed Wu’s Wan stronghold, counted five thousand kills, and torched nearly two million hu of enemy stores.
entries.literal: Ying Chuo, inspector of Yang province, attacked Wu’s fortress at Wan, took five thousand heads, and burned one million eight hundred thousand hu of grain and rice.

entries.zh: 八月癸亥，徙扶風王亮爲汝南王，東莞王伷爲琅邪王，汝陰王駿爲扶風王，琅邪王倫爲趙王，渤海王輔爲太原王，太原王顒爲河間王，北海王陵爲任城王，陳王斌爲西河王，汝南王柬爲南陽王，濟南王耽爲中山王，河間王威爲章武王。
entries.en: Guihai: a wholesale rotation of princely fiefs—Liang to Runan, Zhou to Langye, Jun to Fufeng, Lun to Zhao, Fu of Bohai to Taiyuan, Yong of Taiyuan to Hejian, Ling of Beihai to Rencheng, Bin of Chen to Xihe, Jian of Runan to Nanyang, Dan of Jinan to Zhongshan, and Wei of Hejian to Zhangwu.
entries.literal: On the day guihai of the eighth month king Liang of Fufeng was transferred to king of Runan, king Zhou of Dongguan to king of Langye, king Jun of Ru'yin to king of Fufeng, king Lun of Langye to king of Zhao, king Fu of Bohai to king of Taiyuan, king Yong of Taiyuan to king of Hejian, king Ling of Beihai to king of Rencheng, king Bin of Chen to king of Xihe, king Jian of Runan to king of Nanyang, king Dan of Jinan to king of Zhongshan, king Wei of Hejian to king of Zhangwu.

entries.zh: 立皇子瑋爲始平王，允爲濮陽王，該爲新都王，遐爲清河王，鉅平侯羊祜爲南城侯。
entries.en: The imperial sons Wei, Yun, Gai, and Xia were made kings of Shiping, Puyang, Xindu, and Qinghe, while Yang Hu traded Juping for the Nancheng marquisate.
entries.literal: He established the imperial son Wei as king of Shiping, Yun as king of Puyang, Gai as king of Xindu, Xia as king of Qinghe, and marquis Yang Hu of Juping as marquis of Nancheng.

entries.zh: 以汝南王亮爲鎮南大將軍。
entries.en: Sima Liang of Runan took southern command.
entries.literal: King Liang of Runan was appointed great general who guards the south.

entries.zh: 大風拔樹，暴寒且冰，郡國五隕霜，傷穀。
entries.en: Gales, sudden frost, and ice [19] damaged crops in five provinces.
entries.literal: Great winds uprooted trees; violent cold brought ice [19]; five commanderies reported killing frost that injured the grain.

entries.zh: 十一月辛巳，太醫司馬程據獻雉頭裘，帝以奇技異服典禮所禁，焚之於殿前。
entries.en: Xinsi: Cheng Ju, marshal of the imperial physicians, offered a pheasant-skin cloak; the emperor burned it as illegal luxury.
entries.literal: On the day xinsi of the eleventh month Cheng Ju, court physician, presented a pheasant-head fur robe; the emperor, because strange skills and exotic garments are forbidden by ritual canon, burned it before the hall.

entries.zh: 甲申，敕內外敢有犯者罪之。
entries.en: Jiashen: a decree threatened punishment for anyone peddling such finery.
entries.literal: On the day jiashen he ordered that inside and outside any who dared violate the rule be punished.

entries.zh: 吳昭武將軍劉翻、厲武將軍祖始來降。
entries.en: Wu generals Liu Fan and Zu Shi crossed with their commands.
entries.literal: Wu’s general who displays martial power Liu Fan and general who displays stern martial power Zu Shi came to surrender.

entries.zh: 辛卯，以尚書杜預都督荊州諸軍事。
entries.en: Xinmao: Du Yu took supreme command on the Jing front.
entries.literal: On the day xinmao Du Yu of the masters of writing was appointed supervisor of all military affairs of Jing province.

entries.zh: 征南大將軍羊祜卒。
entries.en: Yang Hu, the southern expedition commander, died.
entries.literal: Yang Hu, great general who campaigns south, died.

entries.zh: 十一月，大舉伐吳，遣鎮軍將軍、琅邪王伷出涂中，[24]安東將軍王渾出江西，建威將軍王戎出武昌，平南將軍胡奮出夏口，鎮南大將軍杜預出江陵，龍驤將軍王濬、廣武將軍唐彬率巴蜀之卒浮江而下，東西凡二十餘萬。
entries.en: In the eleventh month: the conquest of Wu opened on every vector—Sima Zhou from Tu, Wang Hun from the north bank, Wang Rong, Hu Fen, Du Yu, and a river fleet under Wang Jun and Tang Bin—over two hundred thousand soldiers [24].
entries.literal: In the eleventh month a great campaign was launched against Wu: Sima Zhou, general who guards the army and king of Langye, went out from Tu; Wang Hun, general who guards the east, from west of the river; Wang Rong, general who displays might, from Wuchang; Hu Fen, general who pacifies the south, from Xiakou; Du Yu, great general who guards the south, from Jiangling; Wang Jun, general who displays dragon prowess, and Tang Bin, general who displays martial breadth, led Ba–Shu troops down the Yangzi—more than two hundred thousand men on the eastern and western axes combined [24].

entries.zh: 以太尉賈充爲大都督，行冠軍將軍楊濟爲副，總統眾軍。
entries.en: Jia Chong, Grand Commandant, was made Grand Commander-in-chief; Yang Ji, acting General Who Displays Champion Prowess, served as his deputy, and together they commanded all the armies.
entries.literal: Grand commandant Jia Chong was made supreme commander, with acting general who displays champion prowess Yang Ji as deputy, commanding all hosts.

entries.zh: 二月戊午，王濬、唐彬等克丹楊城。
entries.en: Second month, wuwu: the river fleet seized Danyang.
entries.literal: On the day wuwu of the second month Wang Jun, Tang Bin, and others took Danyang city.

entries.zh: 庚申，又克西陵，殺西陵都督、鎮軍將軍留憲，[25]征南將軍成璩，西陵監鄭廣。
entries.en: Gengshen: Xiling fell; Liu Xian, Cheng Qu, and Zheng Guang died defending it [25].
entries.literal: On the day gengshen they also took Xiling, killing Xiling commander and general who guards the army Liu Xian [25], general who campaigns south Cheng Qu, and Xiling intendant Zheng Guang.

entries.zh: 壬戌，濬又克夷道樂鄉城，殺夷道監陸晏、水軍都督陸景。
entries.en: Renxu: Wang Jun pushed to Yidao and Lexiang and killed Lu Yan and Lu Jing.
entries.literal: On the day renxu Jun further took Yidao and Lexiang towns, killing Yidao intendant Lu Yan and commander of the navy Lu Jing.

entries.zh: 甲戌，杜預克江陵，斬吳江陵督伍延；
entries.en: Jiaxu: Du Yu entered Jiangling and executed Wu Yan;
entries.literal: On the day jiaxu Du Yu took Jiangling and beheaded Wu’s Jiangling commander Wu Yan;

entries.zh: 平南將軍胡奮克江安。
entries.en: Hu Fen secured Jiang’an.
entries.literal: General who pacifies the south Hu Fen took Jiang’an.

entries.zh: 於是諸軍並進，樂鄉、荊門諸戍相次來降。
entries.en: Fort after fort—Lexiang, Jingmen—raised white flags.
entries.literal: Thereupon all armies advanced together, and the garrisons at Lexiang, Jingmen, and others surrendered in succession.

entries.zh: 乙亥，以濬爲都督益、梁二州諸軍事，復下詔曰：「濬、彬東下，掃除巴丘，與胡奮、王戎共平夏口、武昌，順流長騖，直造秣陵，與奮、戎審量其宜。
entries.en: On yihai, Wang Jun was made commander-in-chief of military affairs in Yi and Liang provinces, and an edict was again issued, saying, "Jun and Bin shall go east, sweep away Baqiu, and together with Hu Fen and Wang Rong pacify Xiakou and Wuchang, drive swiftly down the current, and go straight to Moling; with Fen and Rong, carefully measure what is appropriate.
entries.literal: On the day yihai Wang Jun was appointed supervisor of all military affairs of Yi and Liang provinces, and an edict further said: “When Jun and Bin sail east, clear Baqiu, join Hu Fen and Wang Rong to pacify Xiakou and Wuchang, then drive straight down the stream to Moling with Fen and Rong coordinating as fits.

entries.zh: 杜預當鎮靜零、桂，懷輯衡陽。
entries.en: Du Yu was to hold the southern Jing pocket and win over Hengyang.
entries.literal: Du Yu shall keep calm over Ling and Gui and soothe Hengyang.

entries.zh: 大兵既過，荊州南境固當傳檄而定，預當分萬人給濬，七千給彬。
entries.en: After the main thrust, Du Yu was to feed ten thousand troops to Wang Jun and seven thousand to Tang Bin.
entries.literal: Once the great army has passed, the southern marches of Jing ought to be settled by proclamation alone; Yu shall detach ten thousand men to Jun and seven thousand to Bin.

entries.zh: 夏口既平，奮宜以七千人給濬。
entries.en: When Xiakou fell, Hu Fen was to shift seven thousand soldiers to Wang Jun.
entries.literal: Once Xiakou is pacified, Fen should give seven thousand men to Jun.

entries.zh: 武昌既了，戎當以六千人增彬。
entries.en: After Wuchang, Wang Rong was to reinforce Tang Bin with six thousand.
entries.literal: Once Wuchang is settled, Rong should add six thousand men to Bin.

entries.zh: 太尉充移屯項，總督諸方。」
entries.en: Jia Chong would move headquarters to Xiang and coordinate all theaters.”
entries.literal: Grand commandant Chong shall shift his camp to Xiang and oversee every front.”

entries.zh: 濬進破夏口、武昌，遂泛舟東下，所至皆平。
entries.en: Wang Jun smashed the river defenses and swept downstream unopposed.
entries.literal: Jun advanced, broke Xiakou and Wuchang, then sailed east; wherever he went it was pacified.

entries.zh: 王渾、周浚與吳丞相張悌戰于版橋，大破之，斬悌及其將孫震、沈瑩，傳首洛陽。
entries.en: At Banqiao Wang Hun and Zhou Jun killed Zhang Ti and his generals Sun Zhen and Shen Ying and shipped the heads north.
entries.literal: Wang Hun, Zhou Jun, and Wu chancellor Zhang Ti fought at Banqiao; they crushed him, beheaded Ti and his generals Sun Zhen and Shen Ying, and sent the heads to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 孫皓窮蹙請降，送璽綬於琅邪王伷。
entries.en: Sun Hao capitulated, handing the imperial seal to Sima Zhou.
entries.literal: Sun Hao, driven to extremity, asked to surrender and sent the seal and cord to king Zhou of Langye.

entries.zh: 丙寅，帝臨軒大會，引皓升殿，群臣咸稱萬歲。
entries.en: Bingyin [29]: the emperor came to the hall for a great assembly, led Sun Hao up into the hall, and the ministers all cried 'ten thousand years.'
entries.literal: On the day bingyin [29] the emperor came to the gallery for a great assembly, led Hao up the hall, and the host of ministers cried “ten thousand years.”

entries.zh: 丁卯，薦酃淥酒于太廟。
entries.en: Dingmao: Linglu wine was poured for the ancestors.
entries.literal: On the day dingmao fine wine from Linglu was offered in the grand temple.

entries.zh: 郡國六雹，傷秋稼。
entries.en: Six more provinces reported hail damage.
entries.literal: Six commanderies and principalities were struck by hail that injured the autumn crop.

entries.zh: 庚午，詔諸士卒年六十以上罷歸于家。
entries.en: Gengwu: veterans over sixty were sent home.
entries.literal: On the day gengwu an edict ordered soldiers aged sixty and above dismissed home.

entries.zh: 庚辰，以王濬爲輔國大將軍、襄陽侯，杜預當陽侯，王戎安豐侯，唐彬上庸侯，賈充、琅邪王伷以下增封。
entries.en: Gengchen: Wang Jun was made great general who assists the state and marquis of Xiangyang, Du Yu marquis of Dangyang, Wang Rong marquis of Anfeng, Tang Bin marquis of Shangyong, and Jia Chong, Sima Zhou the king of Langye, and those below them received increased fiefs.
entries.literal: On the day gengchen Wang Jun was made great general who assists the state and marquis of Xiangyang, Du Yu marquis of Dangyang, Wang Rong marquis of Anfeng, Tang Bin marquis of Shangyong, and Jia Chong, king Zhou of Langye, and those below received increased fiefs.

entries.zh: 於是論功行封，賜公卿以下帛各有差。
entries.en: Silks followed to the whole bureaucracy graded by service.
entries.literal: Thereupon merit was weighed and enfeoffments granted, and silks were bestowed on the dukes and ministers downward, each according to difference.

entries.zh: 三年春正月丁丑，罷秦州，并雍州。
entries.en: Taikang 3, spring, first month, dingchou: Qin province was abolished and merged into Yong province.
entries.literal: In the third year, spring, first month, on the day dingchou, Qin province was abolished and merged into Yong.

entries.zh: 甲午，以尚書張華都督幽州諸軍事。
entries.en: Jiawu: Zhang Hua, a master of writing, was appointed commander of all military affairs in You province.
entries.literal: On the day jiawu Zhang Hua of the masters of writing was appointed supervisor of all military affairs of You province.

entries.zh: 冬十二月甲申，以司空齊王攸爲大司馬、督青州諸軍事，鎮東大將軍、琅邪王伷爲撫軍大將軍，[32]汝南王亮爲太尉，光祿大夫山濤爲司徒，尚書令衛瓘爲司空。
entries.en: Winter, twelfth month, jiashen: Sima You, King of Qi and Minister of Works, was made Grand Marshal and supervisor of all military affairs in Qing province; Sima Zhou, Great General Who Garrisons the East and King of Langye, was made Great General Who Pacifies the Army; [32] Sima Liang, King of Runan, was made Grand Commandant; Shan Tao, Grand Master of Brilliant Prosperity, was made Minister over the Masses; and Wei Guan, Director of the Secretariat, was made Minister of Works.
entries.literal: On the day jiashen of winter, twelfth month, Sima You, king of Qi and minister of works, was made grand marshal and supervisor of all military affairs of Qing province; Sima Zhou, great general who guards the east and king of Langye, was made great general who pacifies the army [32]; Sima Liang, king of Runan, grand commandant; Shan Tao, grand officer of brilliant prosperity, steward of the masters of the people; Wei Guan, supervisor of the masters of writing, minister of works.

entries.zh: 丙申，詔四方水旱甚者無出田租。
entries.en: Bingshen: disaster counties were forgiven their grain rent.
entries.literal: On the day bingshen an edict ordered that regions suffering severe flood or drought pay no field rent.

entries.zh: 八月，鄯善國遣子入侍，假其歸義侯。
entries.en: Eighth month: Shanshan sent a son to serve at court, and he was provisionally made marquis who returns to righteousness.
entries.literal: In the eighth month the state of Shanshan sent a son as hostage at court and he was given the acting title marquis who returns to righteousness.

entries.zh: 以隴西王泰爲尚書右僕射。
entries.en: Sima Tai of Longxi joined the secretariat as right vice-president.
entries.literal: King Tai of Longxi was appointed senior vice-director of the masters of the right.

entries.zh: 冬十一月壬子，以隴西王泰都督關中諸軍事。
entries.en: Renzi: Sima Tai took command of Guanzhong.
entries.literal: On the day renzi of winter, eleventh month, king Tai of Longxi was appointed supervisor of all military affairs within the passes.

entries.zh: 六年春正月甲申朔，[36]以比歲不登，免租貸宿負。
entries.en: Taikang 6, new moon jiashen [36]: years of poor harvests brought rent remission and canceled grain loans.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, spring, first month, on the first day jiashen [36], because harvests had failed for successive years, rent was remitted and old granary debts forgiven.

entries.zh: 戊辰，以征南大將軍王渾爲尚書左僕射，尚書褚䂮都督揚州諸軍事，楊濟都督荊州諸軍事。
entries.en: Wuchen: Wang Hun, Great General Who Campaigns South, was made left vice-director of the Secretariat; Chu Xian of the Secretariat was made commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Yang province; and Yang Ji was made commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Jing province.
entries.literal: On the day wuchen Wang Hun, great general who campaigns south, was appointed senior vice-director of the masters of the left; Chu Xian of the masters of writing supervisor of all military affairs of Yang province; Yang Ji supervisor of all military affairs of Jing province.

entries.zh: 是歲，東夷絕遠三十餘國、西南夷二十餘國來獻。
entries.en: Embassies arrived from thirty-plus eastern and twenty-plus southwestern tribes.
entries.literal: That year more than thirty distant eastern Yi states and more than twenty southwestern Yi states came to present tribute.

entries.zh: 虜奚軻男女十萬口來降。
entries.en: A hundred thousand Xike tribespeople submitted to Jin.
entries.literal: One hundred thousand persons, men and women, of the Xike tribe came to surrender.

entries.zh: 太熙元年春正月辛酉朔，改元。
entries.en: In Taixi 1, spring, first month, on the xinyou new moon, the reign title was changed.
