entries.literal: In Taixi 1, spring, first month, on the xinyou new moon, the reign period was changed.

entries.zh: 己巳，以尚書左僕射王渾爲司徒，司空衛瓘爲太保。
entries.en: On jisi, Wang Hun was promoted from Left Supervisor of the Secretariat to Minister over the Masses, and Wei Guan from Minister of Works to Grand Protector.
entries.literal: On jisi, Wang Hun, Left Supervisor of the Secretariat, was made Minister over the Masses, and Wei Guan, Minister of Works, was made Grand Protector.

entries.en: Manuscripts mark editorial note [40] here.
entries.literal: [40] The received text carries commentary marker [40] at this point.

entries.zh: 帝宇量弘厚，造次必於仁恕；
entries.en: He was large-spirited and humane even under pressure.
entries.literal: The emperor’s bearing was broad and his capacity magnanimous; even in haste he acted with benevolence and forgiveness.

entries.zh: 容納讜正，未嘗失色於人；
entries.en: He heard hard truths without losing his temper.
entries.literal: He accepted blunt counsel and never showed anger on his face toward others.

entries.zh: 明達善謀，能斷大事，故得撫寧萬國，綏靜四方。
entries.en: His judgment pacified the realm.
entries.literal: He was perspicacious, skilled in planning, and able to decide great matters, and therefore could soothe and stabilize the myriad regions and bring quiet to the four quarters.

entries.zh: 承魏氏奢侈刻弊之後，百姓思古之遺風，乃厲以恭儉，敦以寡慾。
entries.en: After Wei’s luxury and cruelty, he modeled austerity and restraint.
entries.literal: Following the Wei dynasty’s extravagance and harsh exactions, the hundred surnames longed for the surviving air of antiquity; he therefore enforced reverence and frugality and pressed for few desires.

entries.zh: 有司嘗奏御牛青絲紖斷，詔以青麻代之。
entries.en: When clerks noted the palace ox’s silk lead had broken, he told them to use hemp instead.
entries.literal: Once the offices memorialized that the imperial ox’s blue silk halter had snapped; he ordered hemp substituted.

entries.zh: 臨朝寬裕，法度有恆。
entries.en: His sessions were calm and the code steady.
entries.literal: In court he was lenient and law and measure remained constant.

entries.zh: 高陽許允既爲文帝所殺，允子奇爲太常丞。
entries.en: Xu Yun, whom Wen had executed, left a son Qi in the ritual office.
entries.literal: Xu Yun of Gaoyang had already been killed by emperor Wen; Yun’s son Qi served as assistant director of the grand master of ceremonies.

entries.zh: 帝將有事於太廟，朝議以奇受害之門，不欲接近左右，請出爲長史。
entries.en: Ministers wanted Qi barred from the rite as a victim’s son.
entries.literal: When the emperor was about to perform business in the grand temple, court discussion held that Qi came from a house that had suffered harm and should not be kept near the throne, requesting he be sent out as senior clerk.

entries.zh: 帝乃追述允夙望，稱奇之才，擢爲祠部郎，時論稱其夷曠。
entries.en: The emperor overruled them, praised Qi, and raised him—critics called it magnanimous.
entries.literal: The emperor then recalled Xu Yun’s old repute, praised Qi’s talent, promoted him to director in the sacrifices bureau, and opinion of the time praised his fairness and breadth.

entries.zh: 平吳之後，天下乂安，遂怠於政術，耽於遊宴，寵愛后黨，親貴當權，舊臣不得專任，彝章紊廢，請謁行矣。
entries.en: Peace bred complacency: harem kin and favorites took the reins while law grew slack.
entries.literal: After Wu was pacified, all under heaven was at peace; thereupon he slackened in governing methods, indulged in roaming feasts, doted on the empress’s kin, let close nobles hold power, no longer gave old ministers sole responsibility, canonical regulations fell into disorder, and soliciting favor became the way.

entries.zh: 爰至末年，知惠帝弗克負荷，然恃皇孫聰睿，故無廢立之心。
entries.en: Late in life he saw Hui’s weakness but pinned hope on a bright grandson.
entries.literal: By his last years he knew that emperor Hui could not bear the burden, yet he trusted in the imperial grandson’s cleverness and therefore had no mind to change the heir.

entries.zh: 復慮非賈后所生，終致危敗，遂與腹心共圖後事。
entries.en: He worried Jia’s lack of maternity would doom the line and schemed with confidants.
entries.literal: He again feared that because the child was not born of empress Jia, disaster would ultimately follow, and therefore plotted the aftermath with his intimates.

entries.zh: 說者紛然，久而不定，竟用王佑之謀，遣太子母弟秦王柬都督關中，楚王瑋、淮南王允並鎮守要害，以強帝室。
entries.en: Opinions were confused and remained unsettled for a long time. In the end, he adopted Wang You’s plan, sending Jian, King of Qin and the crown prince’s younger full brother, to command Guanzhong, while Wei, King of Chu, and Yun, King of Huainan, both guarded strategic points in order to strengthen the imperial house.
entries.literal: Opinions flew thick and long without settlement; in the end he adopted Wang You’s plan, sending the crown prince’s younger uterine brother, king Jian of Qin, to command Guanzhong, while kings Wei of Chu and Yun of Huainan jointly guarded critical points to strengthen the imperial house.

entries.zh: 又恐楊氏之偪，復以佑爲北軍中候，以典禁兵。
entries.en: To check the Yangs he gave Wang You the northern-army baton.
entries.literal: Fearing pressure from the Yang clan, he again made Wang You inspector of the northern armies to command the palace guard.

entries.zh: 既而寢疾彌留，至於大漸，佐命元勳，皆已先沒，群臣惶惑，計無所從。
entries.en: When death neared, his great generals were gone and the court panicked.
entries.literal: Soon he lay gravely ill; as he approached the final crisis, the founding ministers had all predeceased him, and the host of officials were frightened and at a loss.

entries.zh: 會帝小差，有詔以汝南王亮輔政，又欲令朝士之有名望年少者數人佐之，楊駿祕而不宣。
entries.en: A brief rally produced orders for Sima Liang and young worthies—Yang Jun hid the edict.
entries.literal: When the emperor briefly improved, an edict ordered king Liang of Runan to assist the government, and he also wished to have several young courtiers of high repute assist him, but Yang Jun suppressed the edict and did not proclaim it.

entries.zh: 帝復尋至迷亂，楊后輒爲詔以駿輔政，促亮進發。
entries.en: Empress Yang forged a regency for Yang Jun.
entries.literal: The emperor relapsed into confusion; empress Yang then forged an edict making Yang Jun regent and urging Liang to hurry to the capital.

entries.zh: 帝尋小間，問汝南王來未，意欲見之，有所付託。
entries.en: In a lucid moment he asked for Sima Liang.
entries.literal: The emperor briefly cleared and asked whether the king of Runan had arrived, intending to see him and entrust something.

entries.zh: 左右答言未至，帝遂困篤。
entries.en: Told Liang had not come, he sank back into coma.
entries.literal: Those at his side answered that he had not yet arrived, and the emperor thereupon sank into critical illness.

entries.zh: 中朝之亂，實始於斯矣。
entries.en: The mid-realm disasters trace to this bedside failure.
entries.literal: The turmoil at court truly began from this.

entries.zh: 制曰：武皇承基，誕膺天命，握圖御宇，敷化導民，以佚代勞，以治易亂。
entries.en: The court’s summation runs thus: Emperor Wu inherited the enterprise, claimed Heaven’s charge, mastered the realm’s map, and turned exhaustion and disorder into rest and rule.
entries.literal: The official rescript states: The Martial Emperor received the foundation, truly bore heaven’s mandate, grasped the chart and ruled the realm, spread transformation and guided the people, replacing toil with ease and exchanging chaos for order.

entries.zh: 絕縑綸之貢，去雕琢之飾，制奢俗以變儉約，止澆風而反淳朴。
entries.en: He banned luxury tribute and chased the court back toward plain living.
entries.literal: He cut off the tribute of fine silks, removed carved and polished ornament, curbed extravagant custom toward frugality, and checked dissolute winds to return to simplicity.

entries.zh: 雅好直言，留心采擢，劉毅、裴楷以質直見容，嵇紹、許奇雖仇讎不棄。
entries.en: He welcomed Liu Yi, Pei Kai, Ji Shao, and Xu Qi despite awkward pedigrees.
entries.literal: He loved straight words and attended to selection; Liu Yi and Pei Kai were tolerated for blunt honesty, Ji Shao and Xu Qi were not cast aside though they were sons of enemies.

entries.zh: 仁以御物，寬而得眾，宏略大度，有帝王之量焉。
entries.en: He ruled with humane breadth worthy of a founder.
entries.literal: With kindness he governed things, with leniency he won the multitude; he had grand strategy and large tolerance—the measure of a true emperor.

entries.zh: 於時民和俗靜，家給人足，聿修武用，思啟封疆。
entries.en: The realm prospered while he sharpened the sword for expansion.
entries.literal: At that time the people were harmonious and customs quiet, households had enough and persons sufficed; he repaired military readiness and thought to open the frontiers.

entries.zh: 決神算於深衷，斷雄圖於議表。
entries.en: He decided great strategy in council and in his own mind.
entries.literal: He settled divine calculations in his secret heart and cut heroic plans from memorial debate.

entries.zh: 馬隆西伐，王濬南征，師不延時，獯虜削跡，兵無血刃，揚越爲墟。
entries.en: Ma Long and Wang Jun finished the frontier and the south without prolonged war.
entries.literal: Ma Long campaigned west; Wang Jun marched south—the armies did not tarry, the savage tribes were erased, blades scarcely drew blood, and Yang and Yue became wastes.

entries.zh: 通上代之不通，服前王之未服。
entries.en: He finished what past dynasties could not.
entries.literal: He opened what former ages could not open and submitted what former kings had not submitted.

entries.zh: 禎祥顯應，風教肅清，天人之功成矣，霸王之業大矣。
entries.en: Omens and morale alike proclaimed a golden age.
entries.literal: Auspicious omens responded clearly, wind and instruction were sternly pure; the merit of heaven and man was achieved, the enterprise of hegemon-king was great.

entries.zh: 雖登封之禮，讓而不爲，驕泰之心，因斯以起。
entries.en: He modestly skipped the Feng sacrifice yet grew complacent.
entries.literal: Although he yielded and did not perform the Mount Tai enfeoffment rite, a mind of pride and ease arose from this.

entries.zh: 見土地之廣，謂萬葉而無虞；
entries.en: He mistook vast territory for perpetual safety;
entries.literal: Seeing the breadth of the land, he supposed myriad generations would need no caution;

entries.zh: 睹天下之安，謂千年而永治。
entries.en: he mistook quiet rule for an eternal guarantee.
entries.literal: beholding the peace of the realm, he thought a thousand years of good order assured.

entries.zh: 不知處廣以思狹，則廣可長廣；
entries.en: Breadth lasts only if one remembers how easily it narrows;
entries.literal: He did not know that dwelling in breadth while thinking of narrow straits can keep breadth long broad;

entries.zh: 居治而忘危，則治無常治。
entries.en: peace lasts only if peril stays in mind.
entries.literal: that sitting in order while forgetting peril means order is not constant order.

entries.zh: 加之建立非所，委寄失才，志欲就於升平，行先迎於禍亂。
entries.en: Wrong heirs and wrong ministers turned pursuit of stability into invitation to chaos.
entries.literal: Add to this that establishment was not in the right place, commissions missed the right men—his aim sought rising peace, yet his acts first invited calamity.

entries.zh: 是猶將適越者指沙漠以遵途，欲登山者涉舟航而覓路，所趣逾遠，所尚轉難，南北倍殊，高下相反，求其至也，不亦難乎！
entries.en: His choices were as absurd as sailing to a mountaintop.
entries.literal: It is like one who would go to Yue pointing at the desert for a road, or one who would climb a mountain crossing by boat to seek a path—the goal grows farther, the object harder, south and north doubly wrong, high and low reversed; to seek arrival—is it not hard!

entries.zh: 況以新集易動之基，而無久安難拔之慮，故賈充凶豎，懷姦志以擁權；
entries.en: On shaky foundations Jia Chong hoarded authority;
entries.literal: Moreover, on a newly gathered, easily shaken base, without long-term plans against stubborn peril, therefore Jia Chong, a vicious fellow, harbored treachery and clutched power;

entries.zh: 楊駿豺狼，苞禍心以專輔。
entries.en: Yang Jun seized the regency with predatory intent.
entries.literal: Yang Jun, a jackal-wolf, wrapped a baleful heart and monopolized assistance.

entries.zh: 及乎宮車晚出，諒闇未周，藩翰變親以成疏，連兵競滅其本；
entries.en: Before the tomb closed, princely armies turned on one another;
entries.literal: When at last the palace coach departed late and the mourning curtains had not yet completed their round, the screen princes turned kin into strangers and linked armies to destroy their own root;

entries.zh: 棟梁回忠而起僞，擁眾各舉其威。
entries.en: Former pillars of state feigned loyalty while raising private armies.
entries.literal: beams and pillars turned loyalty into treachery and each raised hosts to vaunt his might.

entries.zh: 曾未數年，綱紀大亂，海內版蕩，宗廟播遷。
entries.en: Within years the realm shattered and the altars fled.
entries.literal: In not a few years the great net was wildly tangled, the seas within the passes were in turmoil, and the ancestral temples were driven to flight.

entries.zh: 帝道王猷，反居文身之俗；
entries.en: Civilization collapsed into barbarous custom;
entries.literal: Imperial way and kingly norm fell among folk who tattoo their bodies;

entries.zh: 神州赤縣，翻成被髮之鄉。
entries.en: the heartland became a steppe frontier.
entries.literal: the divine land of red counties overturned into a realm of disheveled hair.

entries.zh: 棄所大以資人，掩其小而自託，爲天下笑，其故何哉﹖良由失慎於前，所以貽患於後。
entries.en: He gave away the store and became history’s cautionary tale.
entries.literal: He cast aside what was great to enrich others, covered what was small and trusted to it—was he not laughed at by the world? The reason is truly that losing caution earlier planted calamity later.

entries.zh: 且知子者賢父，知臣者明君；
entries.en: The wise father knows his son, the wise ruler his minister;
entries.literal: Moreover, he who knows a son is a worthy father; he who knows a minister is an enlightened lord.

entries.zh: 子不肖則家亡，臣不忠則國亂；
entries.en: Bad sons ruin families, disloyal ministers ruin states;
entries.literal: If a son is not worthy the house perishes; if a minister is not loyal the state is in chaos.

entries.zh: 國亂不可以安也，家亡不可以全也。
entries.en: Neither state nor house survives that rot.
entries.literal: A state in chaos cannot be made tranquil; a house perishing cannot be kept whole.

entries.zh: 是以君子防其始，聖人閑其端。
entries.en: The wise seal trouble at the source.
entries.literal: Therefore the gentleman guards the beginning, the sage blocks the opening.

entries.zh: 而世祖惑荀勖之姦謀，迷王渾之僞策，心屢移於眾口，事不定於己圖。
entries.en: Shizu listened to Xun Xu and Wang Hun and let rumor steer him.
entries.literal: Yet Shizu was deluded by Xun Xu’s treacherous counsel, misled by Wang Hun’s false strategy, his heart repeatedly swayed by many mouths, affairs unsettled by his own deliberation.

entries.zh: 元海當除而不除，卒令擾亂區夏；
entries.en: He spared Liu Yuan and reaped rebellion;
entries.literal: Yuanhai ought to have been removed and was not removed, ultimately letting him disturb the central plain;

entries.zh: 惠帝可廢而不廢，終使傾覆洪基。
entries.en: He kept a feeble heir and lost the dynasty.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui could have been deposed and was not deposed, finally overturning the great foundation.

entries.zh: 夫全一人者德之輕，拯天下者功之重，棄一子者忍之小，安社稷者孝之大；
entries.en: Saving the state outweighs sparing one prince;
entries.literal: To preserve one man is a small virtue; to save the realm is a weighty merit; to cast off one child is a small hardness; to secure the altars is the great filial piety.

entries.zh: 況乎資三世而成業，延二孽以喪之，所謂取輕德而捨重功，畏小忍而忘大孝。
entries.en: to waste three reigns’ work for two poisonous branches was to pick the lesser good.
entries.literal: How much more when he had completed an enterprise through three reigns yet prolonged two baleful shoots to destroy it—what is called taking light virtue and discarding heavy merit, fearing small hardness and forgetting great filial piety.

entries.zh: 聖賢之道，豈若斯乎！
entries.en: That is not the way of the sages.
entries.literal: Can the way of sages and worthies be like this!

entries.zh: 雖則善始於初，而乖令終於末，所以殷勤史策，不能無慷慨焉。
entries.en: A splendid start and a ruinous end invite the historian’s regret.
entries.literal: Although he had a good beginning at first, he missed a fitting end at the last; therefore the histories linger here and must sigh.

entries.zh: 斬吳江陵都督伍延 「伍延」，各本皆作「王延」。
entries.en: For beheading Wu’s Jiangling commander Wu Yan, editions all write "Wang Yan" for "Wu Yan."
entries.literal: Regarding beheading Wu’s Jiangling commander Wu Yan: editions all write Wang Yan instead of Wu Yan.

entries.zh: 按：本書杜預傳、吳志孫皓傳、冊府一二一、通鑑八一皆作「伍延」，今據改。
entries.en: Note: Du Yu’s biography in this book, Wu zhi, Sun Hao biography, Cefu 121, and Tongjian 81 all write "Wu Yan"; it is now corrected accordingly.
entries.literal: Comment: Du Yu’s biography, Wu zhi, Cefu yuangui 121, and Zizhi tongjian 81 all have Wu Yan; emend accordingly.

entries.zh: 參周校及洪頤烜諸史考異。
entries.en: See Zhou and Hong for discussion.
entries.literal: See Zhou’s collation and Hong Yixuan’s Zhu shi kaoyi.

entries.zh: 武皇帝諱炎，字安世，文帝長子也。
entries.en: The emperor honored posthumously as Wu bore the personal name Yan and the courtesy name Anshi; he was the firstborn son of Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao).
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor's taboo name was Yan, his style name Anshi; he was the eldest son of Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 寬惠仁厚，沈深有度量。
entries.en: Broad-minded, humane, and gentle by nature, he was grave and self-contained, with the measured bearing of a true ruler.
entries.literal: He was generous, kind, and humane in his magnanimity, deep and reserved, with breadth of mind.

entries.zh: 魏嘉平中，封北平亭侯，歷給事中、奉車都尉、中壘將軍，加散騎常侍，累遷中護軍、假節。
entries.en: During Wei’s Jiaping years he received the Beipingting marquisate and rose through a string of palace and guard posts—gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary—until he became central protector, bearing the credential staff.
entries.literal: In the Jiaping era of Wei he was enfeoffed as marquis of Beipingting, then served successively as gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, with additional appointment as regular palace attendant of cavalier, and was repeatedly promoted to central protector with plenary authority.

entries.zh: 迎常道鄉公於東武陽，遷中撫軍，進封新昌鄉侯。
entries.en: At Dongwuyang he received the duke of Changdaoxiang, was named central commander of the army, and was promoted to marquis of Xinchang.
entries.literal: He welcomed the duke of Changdaoxiang at Dongwuyang, was transferred to central commander of the army, and advanced to enfeoffment as marquis of Xinchang.

entries.zh: 及晉國建，立爲世子，拜撫軍大將軍，開府、副貳相國。
entries.en: When the Jin state was founded, he was established as heir apparent, appointed Great General Who Pacifies the Army with an office of his own, and made second-in-command assisting the Minister of State.
entries.literal: When the state of Jin was founded he was established as heir apparent, appointed great general who pacifies the army with independent command, and served as deputy to the minister of state.

entries.zh: 秋八月壬午，立廣陵王遹爲皇太子，以中書監何劭爲太子太師，吏部尚書王戎爲太子太傅，衛將軍楊濟爲太子太保。
entries.en: In autumn, on the renwu day of the eighth month, Sima Yu, prince of Guangling, was named crown prince; He Shao became his grand preceptor, Wang Rong his grand tutor, and Yang Ji his grand guardian.
entries.literal: In autumn, on the renwu day of the eighth month, Prince Sima You of Guangling was established as crown prince; Director of the Secretariat He Shao was made grand preceptor of the heir apparent; Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Rong was made grand tutor of the heir apparent; General of the Guards Yang Ji was made grand guardian of the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 遣南中郎將石崇、射聲校尉胡奕、長水校尉趙俊、揚烈將軍趙歡將屯兵四出。
entries.en: Shi Chong, Hu Yi, Zhao Jun, and Zhao Huan were sent out at the head of garrison forces in every direction.
entries.literal: General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Household Shi Chong, Colonel of the Sound of Shooting Hu Yi, Colonel of the Long River Zhao Jun, and General Who Displays Ferocity Zhao Huan were dispatched leading garrison troops in four directions.

entries.zh: 六月，賈后矯詔使楚王瑋殺太宰、汝南王亮，太保、菑陽公衛瓘。
entries.en: In the sixth month Empress Jia forged orders that sent Prince Wei of Chu to murder Prince Liang of Runan, the grand steward, and Duke Wei Guan of Ziyang, the grand guardian.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, Empress Jia forged an edict causing Prince Wei of Chu to kill Grand Steward, Prince Liang of Runan, and Grand Guardian, Duke Wei Guan of Ziyang.

entries.zh: 乙丑，以瑋擅害亮、瓘，殺之。
entries.en: On the yichou day Prince Wei was executed for having murdered Liang and Guan without authorization.
entries.literal: On the yichou day, because Wei had on his own authority harmed Liang and Guan, he was killed.

entries.zh: 曲赦洛陽。
entries.en: Luoyang received a limited amnesty.
entries.literal: A partial amnesty was proclaimed for Luoyang.

entries.zh: 以廣陵王師劉寔爲太子太保，司空、隴西王泰錄尚書事。
entries.en: Liu Shi became grand guardian to the crown prince, and Prince Tai of Longxi, still minister of works, took charge of secretariat business.
entries.literal: Preceptor to the Prince of Guangling, Liu Shi, was made grand guardian of the heir apparent; Minister of Works, Prince Tai of Longxi, recorded the affairs of the secretariat.

entries.zh: 永平元年春正月乙酉朔，臨朝，不設樂。
entries.en: On the yiyou new moon of the first month of spring in Yongping 1, the emperor held court without music.
entries.literal: In spring, in the first month of the first year of Yongping, on the yiyou new moon, he attended court and did not set out music.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「朕夙遭不造，淹恤在疚。
entries.en: An edict ran: “From boyhood I have known bereavement I did not choose; mourning has long weighed upon me.
entries.literal: An edict stated: “I from early on have encountered ill fortune not of my making; prolonged grief dwells in affliction.

entries.zh: 賴祖宗遺靈，宰輔忠賢，得以眇身託于群后之上。
entries.en: Thanks to the spirits of my forebears and to loyal, capable ministers, this slight frame has been set above the princes of the blood.
entries.literal: Relying on the lingering numen of ancestors and forebears, and on the chief ministers’ loyalty and worthiness, I have been able to entrust my insignificant person above the host of lords.

entries.zh: 昧於大道，不明于訓，戰戰兢兢，夕惕若厲。
entries.en: I am dim to the great Way, slow to take instruction, and I tremble through the day, alert at night as though disaster were at hand.
entries.literal: Dark regarding the great way, unclear in instruction, trembling with fear, in the evening watchful as if in danger.

entries.zh: 乃者哀迷之際，三事股肱，惟社稷之重，率遵翼室之典，猶欲長奉先皇之制，是以有永熙之號。
entries.en: In the confusion after my father’s death, the chief ministers, mindful of the altars of state, followed precedent for a minor on the throne and meant to keep his late Majesty’s institutions; that is why the reign was called Yongxi.
entries.literal: Recently, amid the confusion of mourning, the three high ministers, the thighs and arms, considering the weight of altars and grain, all followed the canons of aiding the chamber, and still wished long to uphold the late emperor’s regulations; therefore there was the era name Yongxi.

entries.zh: 然日月踰邁，已涉新年，開元易紀，禮之舊章。
entries.en: Yet the seasons have turned, a new year has begun, and ritual expects a fresh reign title at such a renewal.
entries.literal: Yet sun and moon pass beyond; already we have entered a new year; to open the first month and change the era tally is the old pattern of ritual.

entries.zh: 其改永熙二年爲永平元年。」
entries.en: Let the second year of Yongxi be renamed the first year of Yongping.”
entries.literal: Let the second year of Yongxi be changed to the first year of Yongping.”

entries.zh: 又詔子弟及群官並不得謁陵。
entries.en: A further edict forbade imperial clansmen and officials to visit the imperial tombs.
entries.literal: Another edict: imperial sons and younger brothers and all officials alike were not permitted to visit the mausoleum.

entries.zh: 丙午，皇太子冠，丁未，見于太廟。
entries.en: The crown prince came of age with the capping ceremony one day and was presented at the ancestral temple the next.
entries.literal: On the bingwu day the crown prince underwent capping; on the dingwei day he appeared in the Grand Temple.

entries.zh: 八月庚申，以趙王倫爲征東將軍、都督徐兗二州諸軍事；
entries.en: Prince Lun of Zhao was named general who conquers the east and given joint command over Xu and Yan;
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on the gengshen day, Prince Lun of Zhao was made general who conquers the east and area commander for military affairs in Xu and Yan provinces;

entries.zh: 河間王顒爲北中郎將，鎮鄴；
entries.en: Prince Yong of Hejian became a northern camp general and garrisoned Ye;
entries.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian was made general of the northern gentlemen of the household and stationed at Ye;

entries.zh: 太子太師何劭爲都督豫州諸軍事，鎮許昌。
entries.en: He Shao, the heir apparent’s grand preceptor, took command in Yu Province from a base at Xuchang.
entries.literal: Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent He Shao was made area commander for military affairs in Yu Province and stationed at Xuchang.

entries.zh: 徙長沙王乂爲常山王。
entries.en: Prince Yi of Changsha was re-enfeoffed as prince of Changshan.
entries.literal: Prince Yi of Changsha was transferred to be prince of Changshan.

entries.zh: 己巳，進西陽公羕爵爲王。
entries.en: Duke Yang of Xiyang was raised to princely rank.
entries.literal: On the jisi day, Duke Yang of Xiyang was advanced in noble rank to prince.

entries.zh: 辛未，立隴西世子越爲東海王。
entries.en: Yue, heir of the house of Longxi, was created prince of Donghai.
entries.literal: On the xinwei day, heir apparent Yue of Longxi was established as prince of Donghai.

entries.zh: 夏四月癸亥，以征東將軍、梁王肜爲征西大將軍、都督關西諸軍事，太子少傅阮坦爲平東將軍、監青徐二州諸軍事。
entries.en: Prince Rong of Liang was shifted from the eastern to the western theater as area commander beyond the passes, while Ruan Tan was sent to pacify the east and oversee the armies of Qing and Xu.
entries.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the guihai day, General Who Conquers the East, Prince Xiong of Liang, was made general-in-chief who conquers the west and area commander for all military affairs west of the passes; Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent Ruan Tan was made general who pacifies the east and overseer of military affairs in Qing and Xu provinces.

entries.zh: 己巳，以太子太傅王戎爲尚書右僕射。
entries.en: Wang Rong moved from tutoring the heir apparent to the right vice directorship of the secretariat.
entries.literal: On the jisi day, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent Wang Rong was made right vice director of the secretariat.

entries.zh: 三月辛卯，誅太傅楊駿，駿弟衛將軍珧，太子太保濟，中護軍張劭，散騎常侍段廣、楊邈，左將軍劉預，河南尹李斌，中書令蔣俊，東夷校尉文淑，尚書武茂，皆夷三族。
entries.en: In the third month Yang Jun and his entire faction were put to death: his brother Yang Yao, Yang Ji, Zhang Shao, Duan Guang, Yang Miao, Liu Yu, Li Bin, Jiang Jun, Wen Shu, and Wu Mao, with every branch of their families extirpated.
entries.literal: In the third month, on the xinmao day, Grand Tutor Yang Jun was executed; Jun’s younger brother General of the Guards Yang Yao, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent Yang Ji, Central Protector of the Army Zhang Shao, Cavalier Attendants-in-Ordinary Duan Guang and Yang Miao, General of the Left Liu Yu, Intendant of Henan Li Bin, Director of the Secretariat Jiang Jun, Colonel of Eastern Yi Tribes Wen Shu, and Minister Wu Mao—all were exterminated to the third degree of kin.

entries.zh: 壬辰，大赦，改元。
entries.en: A general amnesty followed, and the reign title was changed again.
entries.literal: On the renchen day a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

entries.zh: 賈后矯詔廢皇太后爲庶人，徙于金墉城，告于天地宗廟。
entries.en: Empress Jia forged an edict that stripped the empress dowager of her title, confined her in the Jinyong fortress, and had the act proclaimed to Heaven, Earth, and the imperial shrines.
entries.literal: Empress Jia forged an edict deposing the empress dowager to commoner status, transferring her to the Jinyong Fortress, and reported it to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples.

entries.zh: 誅太后母龐氏。
entries.en: The dowager’s mother, Lady Pang, was executed.
entries.literal: The empress dowager’s mother, the Lady Pang, was executed.

entries.zh: 壬寅，徵大司馬、汝南王亮爲太宰，與太保衛瓘輔政。
entries.en: Prince Liang of Runan was recalled from the grand marshal’s post to serve as grand steward alongside Grand Guardian Wei Guan as coregent.
entries.literal: On the renyin day, Grand Marshal, Prince Liang of Runan, was summoned to be grand steward, and together with Grand Guardian Wei Guan assisted the government.

entries.zh: 以秦王柬爲大將軍，東平王楙爲撫軍大將軍，鎮南將軍、楚王瑋爲衛將軍，領北軍中候，下邳王晃爲尚書令，東安公繇爲尚書左僕射，進封東安王。
entries.en: Prince Jian of Qin took the supreme military command; Prince Mao of Dongping became general who soothes the army; Prince Wei of Chu became general of the guards and colonel of the northern camp; Prince Huang of Xiapi headed the secretariat; Duke Yao of Dong’an became its senior deputy and was raised to prince of Dong’an.
entries.literal: Prince Jian of Qin was made general-in-chief; Prince Mao of Dongping was made general-in-chief who soothes the army; General Who Guards the South, Prince Wei of Chu, was made general of the guards, heading the colonel of the northern armies; Prince Huang of Xiapi was made director of the secretariat; Duke Yao of Dong’an was made left vice director of the secretariat and advanced in enfeoffment to prince of Dong’an.

entries.zh: 督將侯者千八十一人。
entries.en: One thousand eighty-one officers of commander rank or above were ennobled as marquises.
entries.literal: Supervisors and generals who were marquises numbered one thousand eighty-one persons.

entries.zh: 庚戌，免東安王繇及東平王楙，繇徙帶方。
entries.en: Princes Yao and Mao were stripped of their posts, and Yao was banished to Daifang on the Korean frontier.
entries.literal: On the gengxu day, Prince Yao of Dong’an and Prince Mao of Dongping were dismissed from office; Yao was transferred to Daifang.

entries.zh: 冬十月辛酉，以司空石鑒爲太尉，前鎮西將軍、隴西王泰爲司空。
entries.en: In the tenth month, Shi Jian rose from minister of works to grand commandant, while Prince Tai of Longxi, lately general who had guarded the west, took the ministry of works.
entries.literal: In winter, on the xinyou day of the tenth month, Minister of Works Shi Jian was made grand commandant; former General Who Guards the West, Prince Tai of Longxi, was made minister of works.

entries.zh: 二月甲寅，賜王公已下帛各有差。
entries.en: In the second month, princes, dukes, and officials down the scale received graded gifts of silk.
entries.literal: In the second month, on the jiayin day, silk was granted to princes, dukes, and downward, each according to rank.

entries.zh: 癸酉，鎮南將軍楚王瑋、鎮東將軍淮南王允來朝。
entries.en: Prince Wei of Chu, who held the southern command, and Prince Yun of Huainan, who held the eastern command, arrived for audience at court.
entries.literal: On the guiyou day, General Who Guards the South, Prince Sima Wei of Chu, and General Who Guards the East, Prince Sima Yun of Huainan, came to court audience.

entries.zh: 戊寅，復置祕書監官。
entries.en: The directorship of the Palace Library was restored.
entries.literal: On the wuyin day, the office of director of the Palace Library was re-established.

entries.zh: 九月甲午，大將軍、秦王柬薨。
entries.en: On jiawu in the ninth month, Sima Jian, Prince of Qin and Great General, died.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on jiawu, Jian, Prince of Qin and Great General, died.

entries.zh: 辛丑，徵征西大將軍、梁王肜爲衛將軍、錄尚書事，以趙王倫爲征西大將軍、都督雍梁二州諸軍事。
entries.en: On xinchou, Sima Rong, Prince of Liang and Great General Who Conquers the West, was recalled as General of the Guards and manager of Secretariat affairs. Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, became Great General Who Conquers the West and commander of military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces.
entries.literal: On xinchou, Rong, Prince of Liang and Great General Who Conquers the West, was summoned to be General of the Guards and manager of Secretariat affairs; Lun, Prince of Zhao, was made Great General Who Conquers the West and commander-in-chief of military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces.

entries.zh: 六年春正月，大赦。
entries.en: In the first month of spring in the sixth year, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: In spring, in the first month of the sixth year, there was a great amnesty.

entries.zh: 司空、下邳王晃薨。
entries.en: Sima Huang, Prince of Xiapi and Minister of Works, died.
entries.literal: Huang, Prince of Xiapi and Minister of Works, died.

entries.zh: 以中書監張華爲司空，太尉、隴西王泰爲尚書令，衛將軍、梁王肜爲太子太保。
entries.en: Zhang Hua, Director of the Secretariat, was appointed Minister of Works; Sima Tai, Prince of Longxi and Grand Commandant, became Director of the Secretariat; and Sima Rong, Prince of Liang and General of the Guards, became Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: Zhang Hua, Director of the Secretariat, was made Minister of Works; Tai, Prince of Longxi and Grand Commandant, was made Director of the Secretariat; Rong, Prince of Liang and General of the Guards, was made Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 丁丑，地震。
entries.en: On dingchou, an earthquake occurred.
entries.literal: On dingchou, there was an earthquake.

entries.zh: 五月，荊、揚二州大水。
entries.en: Jing and Yang provinces were overwhelmed by flood in the fifth month.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, Jing and Yang provinces suffered great flooding.

entries.zh: 匈奴郝散弟度元帥馮翊、北地馬蘭羌、盧水胡反，攻北地，太守張損死之。
entries.en: Du Yuan, Hao San’s brother, led Qiang and Lushui Hu allies from Fengyi and Beidi in revolt, stormed Beidi, and killed Prefect Zhang Sun in the fighting.
entries.literal: Hao San’s younger brother of the Xiongnu, Du Yuan, led the Fengyi, Beidi Malan Qiang, and Lushui Hu in rebellion, attacked Beidi, and Prefect Zhang Sun died in it.

entries.zh: 馮翊太守歐陽建與度元戰，建敗績。
entries.en: Ouyang Jian, prefect of Fengyi, met Du Yuan in battle and suffered a rout.
entries.literal: Fengyi Prefect Ouyang Jian battled with Du Yuan; Jian was defeated.

entries.zh: 徵征西大將軍、趙王倫爲車騎將軍，以太子太保、梁王肜爲征西大將軍、都督雍梁二州諸軍事，鎮關中。
entries.en: Prince Lun of Zhao was recalled from the western command to the capital post of general of chariots and cavalry, while Prince Rong of Liang took his place as general-in-chief in the west with authority over Yong and Liang and a mandate to hold the Guanzhong frontier.
entries.literal: General-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Lun of Zhao, was summoned to be general of chariots and cavalry; Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Prince Rong of Liang, was made general-in-chief who conquers the west and area commander for military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces, garrisoning within the passes.

entries.zh: 十一月丙子，遣安西將軍夏侯駿、建威將軍周處等討萬年，梁王肜屯好畤。
entries.en: Xiahou Jun and Zhou Chu were sent against Qi Wannian in the eleventh month while Prince Rong of Liang held a supporting camp at Haozhi.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on the bingzi day, General Who Pacifies the West Xiahou Jun, General Who Establishes Might Zhou Chu, and others were dispatched to attack Wannian; Prince Rong of Liang encamped at Haozhi.

entries.zh: 關中饑，大疫。
entries.en: Famine and plague ravaged the Guanzhong heartland.
entries.literal: Within the passes there was famine and great pestilence.

entries.zh: 九月，以尚書右僕射王戎爲司徒，太子太師何劭爲尚書左僕射。
entries.en: Wang Rong advanced from right vice director to minister of education, and He Shao from the heir apparent’s grand preceptor to left vice director of the secretariat in the ninth month.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Rong was made minister of education; Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent He Shao was made left vice director of the secretariat.

entries.zh: 夏四月辛卯，日有蝕之。
entries.en: Another solar eclipse occurred on the xinmao day in the fourth month.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the xinmao day, there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 癸巳，梁王肜、趙王倫矯詔廢賈后爲庶人，司空張華、尚書僕射裴頠皆遇害，侍中賈謐及黨與數十人皆伏誅。
entries.en: On the guisi day Princes Xiong and Lun forged an edict that deposed Empress Jia; Zhang Hua and Pei Wei were killed, and Jia Mi with dozens of his partisans went to the execution ground.
entries.literal: On the guisi day, Prince Xiong of Liang and Prince Lun of Zhao forged an edict deposing Empress Jia to commoner status; Minister of Works Zhang Hua and Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Wei both met harm and died; Palace Attendant Jia Mi and several tens of his faction were all executed.

entries.zh: 甲午，倫矯詔大赦，自爲相國、都督中外諸軍，如宣文輔魏故事，追復故皇太子位。
entries.en: The next day Prince Lun forged a general amnesty, named himself chancellor and commander-in-chief on the model of Sima Yi and Sima Zhao, and posthumously reinstated the murdered crown prince.
entries.literal: On the jiawu day, Lun forged an edict for a general amnesty, made himself chancellor of state and area commander for all military affairs within and without, according to the old precedent of Xuan and Wen assisting Wei, and posthumously restored the former crown prince’s position.

entries.zh: 丁酉，以梁王肜爲太宰，左光祿大夫何劭爲司徒，右光祿大夫劉寔爲司空，淮南王允爲驃騎將軍。
entries.en: Prince Xiong became grand steward, He Shao minister of education, Liu Shi minister of works, and Prince Yun of Huainan general of agile cavalry on the dingyou day.
entries.literal: On the dingyou day, Prince Xiong of Liang was made grand steward; Left Household Grandee He Shao was made minister of education; Right Household Grandee Liu Shi was made minister of works; Prince Yun of Huainan was made general of agile cavalry.

entries.zh: 己亥，趙王倫矯詔害賈庶人于金墉城。
entries.en: On the jihai day Prince Lun had the deposed Empress Jia killed inside the Jinyong fortress.
entries.literal: On the jihai day, Prince Lun of Zhao forged an edict and harmed the commoner Jia at the Jinyong Fortress.

entries.zh: 永康元年春正月癸亥朔，大赦，改元。
entries.en: The new moon of the first month of Yongkang brought a general amnesty and a new reign title.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongkang, spring, first month, on the guihai new moon, a general amnesty; the era name was changed.

entries.zh: 己卯，日有蝕之。
entries.en: The sun was eclipsed on the jimao day.
entries.literal: On the jimao day, there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 丙子，皇孫𧇃卒。
entries.en: On the bingzi day the imperial grandson died.
entries.literal: On the bingzi day, the imperial grandson 𧇃 died.

entries.zh: 秋八月，以尚書裴頠爲尚書僕射。
entries.en: In the eighth month Pei Wei advanced from ordinary minister to vice director of the secretariat.
entries.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Minister Pei Wei was made vice director of the secretariat.

entries.zh: 十二月壬戌，廢皇太子遹爲庶人，及其三子幽于金墉城，殺太子母謝氏。
entries.en: On the renxu day in the twelfth month Crown Prince Sima Yu was stripped of his title and imprisoned with his three sons in the Jinyong fortress, while his mother Lady Xie was put to death.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on the renxu day, Crown Prince You was deposed to commoner status; together with his three sons he was confined in the Jinyong Fortress; the crown prince’s mother, the Lady Xie, was killed.

entries.zh: 三月，尉氏雨血，妖星見于南方。
entries.en: Weishi was said to have been drenched in blood-red rain, and an ominous star shone in the southern sky.
entries.literal: In the third month, in Weishi it rained blood; a prodigy star appeared in the south.

entries.zh: 癸未，賈后矯詔害庶人遹于許昌。
entries.en: On the guiwei day Empress Jia used forged orders to murder the deposed heir Sima You at Xuchang.
entries.literal: On the guiwei day, Empress Jia forged an edict and harmed the commoner You at Xuchang.

entries.zh: 六月壬寅，葬愍懷太子于顯平陵。
entries.en: Crown Prince You, posthumously titled the Lamented Heir, was laid to rest at Xianping mausoleum on the renyin day.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on the renyin day, the Lamented Heir Apparent was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 撫軍將軍、清河王遐薨。
entries.en: Prince Xia of Qinghe, who held the title general who soothes the army, died.
entries.literal: General Who Soothes the Army, Prince Xia of Qinghe, died.

entries.zh: 癸卯，震崇陽陵標。
entries.en: Lightning shattered the stele at Emperor Wu’s Chongyang mausoleum on the guimao day.
entries.literal: On the guimao day, Chongyang Mausoleum’s marker was struck by lightning.

entries.zh: 永寧元年春正月乙丑，趙王倫篡帝位。
entries.en: On the yichou day in the first month of Yongning, Prince Lun of Zhao seized the throne.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongning, spring, first month, on the yichou day, Prince Lun of Zhao usurped the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 丙寅，遷帝于金墉城，號曰太上皇，改金墉曰永昌宮。
entries.en: The next day the true emperor was bundled off to the Jinyong fortress as a nominal “supreme emperor,” and the compound was renamed Yongchang Palace.
entries.literal: On the bingyin day, the emperor was moved to the Jinyong Fortress, titled supreme emperor; Jinyong was changed to Yongchang Palace.

entries.zh: 廢皇太孫臧爲濮陽王。
entries.en: The heir’s son Sima Zang was demoted to prince of Puyang.
entries.literal: The imperial grandson-heir Zang was deposed to be prince of Puyang.

entries.zh: 五星經天，縱橫無常。
entries.en: All five naked-eye planets were seen wheeling across the daytime sky in disorderly paths.
entries.literal: The five planets crossed the sky, vertically and horizontally without constancy.

entries.zh: 癸酉，倫害濮陽王臧。
entries.en: Prince Lun had Sima Zang, now prince of Puyang, murdered on the guiyou day.
entries.literal: On the guiyou day, Lun killed Prince Zang of Puyang.

entries.zh: 略陽流人李特殺趙廞，傳首京師。
entries.en: The refugee leader Li Te slew Zhao Xin and forwarded his head to Luoyang.
entries.literal: Lüeyang migrant Li Te killed Zhao Xin and sent his head to the capital.

entries.zh: 秋八月，淮南王允舉兵討趙王倫，不克，允及其二子秦王郁、漢王迪皆遇害。
entries.en: In the eighth month of autumn, Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan, raised troops against Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, but failed. Yun and his sons Yu, Prince of Qin, and Di, Prince of Han, were all killed.
entries.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, Yun, Prince of Huainan, raised troops to attack Lun, Prince of Zhao, but could not succeed; Yun and his two sons, Yu, Prince of Qin, and Di, Prince of Han, were all killed.

entries.zh: 曲赦洛陽。
entries.en: A special pardon was granted in Luoyang.
entries.literal: A special pardon was issued for Luoyang.

entries.zh: 平東將軍、彭城王植薨。
entries.en: Sima Zhi, Prince of Pengcheng and General Who Pacifies the East, died.
entries.literal: Zhi, Prince of Pengcheng and General Who Pacifies the East, died.

entries.zh: 改封吳王晏爲賓徒縣王。
entries.en: Sima Yan, Prince of Wu, was redesignated Prince of Bintu county.
entries.literal: Yan, Prince of Wu, was reassigned as Prince of Bintu county.

entries.zh: 以齊王冏爲平東將軍，鎮許昌；
entries.en: Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and stationed at Xuchang;
entries.literal: Jiong, Prince of Qi, was made General Who Pacifies the East and stationed at Xuchang;

entries.zh: 光祿大夫陳準爲太尉、錄尚書事。
entries.en: Chen Zhun, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, became Grand Commandant and manager of Secretariat affairs.
entries.literal: Chen Zhun, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, was made Grand Commandant and manager of Secretariat affairs.

entries.zh: 五月己巳，立皇孫臧爲皇太孫，尚爲襄陽王。
entries.en: Sima Zang was named heir apparent’s son and successor, while his brother Shang was created prince of Xiangyang, on the jisi day in the fifth month.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on the jisi day, Imperial Grandson Zang was established as imperial grandson-heir; Shang was made prince of Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 三月，平東將軍、齊王冏起兵以討倫，傳檄州郡，屯于陽翟。
entries.en: In the third month Prince Jiong of Qi, general who pacifies the east, mobilized against Prince Lun, circulated a call to arms through every province, and camped at Yangzhai.
entries.literal: In the third month, General Who Pacifies the East, Prince Jiong of Qi, raised troops to attack Lun, transmitted proclamations to the provinces and commanderies, and encamped at Yangzhai.

entries.zh: 征北大將軍、成都王穎，征西大將軍、河間王顒，常山王乂，豫州刺史李毅，兗州刺史王彥，南中郎將、新野公歆，皆舉兵應之，眾數十萬。
entries.en: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu and Grand General Who Campaigns North; Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian and Grand General Who Campaigns West; Sima Yi, Prince of Changshan; Li Yi, inspector of Yu Province; Wang Yan, inspector of Yan Province; and Xin, Duke of Xinye and General of the Southern Gentlemen-of-the-Household, all raised armies in response, mustering several hundred thousand men.
entries.literal: General-in-chief who conquers the north, Prince Ying of Chengdu; general-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Yong of Hejian; Prince Yi of Changshan; Inspector of Yu Province Li Yi; Inspector of Yan Province Wang Yan; General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Household, Duke Xin of Xinye—all raised troops in response; the hosts numbered several hundred thousand.

entries.zh: 倫遣其將閭和出伊闕，張泓、孫輔出堮阪以距冏，孫會、士猗、許超出黃橋以距穎。
entries.en: Prince Lun sent Lü He through the Yique pass, Zhang Hong and Sun Fu over the E ridge to block Prince Jiong, and Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao from Huang Bridge to stop Prince Ying.
entries.literal: Lun dispatched his generals Lü He out of Yique, Zhang Hong and Sun Fu out of E Slope to resist Jiong, and Sun Hui, Shi Yi, and Xu Chao out of Huang Bridge to resist Ying.

entries.zh: 及穎將趙驤、石超戰于湨水，會等大敗，棄軍走。
entries.en: At the Ju River, Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao, serving Prince Ying, routed Sun Hui’s army, which broke and ran.
entries.literal: When Ying’s generals Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao battled at the Ju River, Hui and the others were greatly defeated and abandoned the army and fled.

entries.zh: 癸亥，詔曰：「朕以不德，纂承皇統，遠不能光濟大業，靖綏四方；
entries.en: On the guihai day an edict began: “Lacking virtue, I yet inherited the throne, and I have not been able to extend the great enterprise or bring peace to the four quarters of the realm;
entries.literal: On the guihai day, an edict stated: “I, lacking virtue, have succeeded to the imperial line; afar I have been unable to brighten and aid the great enterprise and pacify and soothe the four directions;

entries.zh: 近不能開明刑威，式遏姦宄，至使逆臣孫秀敢肆凶虐，窺間王室，遂奉趙王倫饕據天位。
entries.en: Near at hand I failed to make law and majesty clear enough to stop treason, so the rebel Sun Xiu could brutalize the court, tear at the royal house, and help Prince Lun of Zhao seize the throne by force.
entries.literal: Near I have been unable to open and clarify punishments and might and check villainy and treachery, so that the rebellious minister Sun Xiu dared unleash cruelty and violence, spy on and divide the royal house, and thereupon supporting Prince Lun of Zhao greedily seized the heavenly position.

entries.zh: 鎮東大將軍、齊王冏，征北大將軍、成都王穎，征西大將軍、河間王顒，並以明德茂親，忠規允著，首建大策，匡救國難。
entries.en: General-in-chief who guards the east Prince Jiong of Qi, general-in-chief who conquers the north Prince Ying of Chengdu, and general-in-chief who conquers the west Prince Yong of Hejian are men of shining virtue and eminent kinship whose loyal counsel stood the test; they first devised the great plan that delivered the state from disaster.
entries.literal: General-in-chief who guards the east, Prince Jiong of Qi; general-in-chief who conquers the north, Prince Ying of Chengdu; general-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Yong of Hejian—all with bright virtue as flourishing kin, loyal plans truly manifest, first established the great strategy and rectified and saved the state’s crisis.

entries.zh: 尚書漼共立大謀，左衛將軍王輿與群公卿士，協同謀略，親勒本營，斬秀及其二子。
entries.en: Minister Cui framed the decisive plot; Wang Yu, general of the left guards, with the high ministers acting in concert, led their household troops into the palace and slew Sun Xiu together with his two sons.
entries.literal: Minister Cui together established the great plan; General of the Left Guards Wang Yu, together with the host of dukes, ministers, and gentlemen, coordinated in stratagem, personally commanded the original camp, and beheaded Xiu and his two sons.

entries.zh: 前趙王倫爲秀所誤，與其子等已詣金墉迎朕幽宮，旋軫閶闔。
entries.en: The former Prince Lun of Zhao was deceived by Sun Xiu; he and his sons had already reached the Jinyong compound to bring me out of confinement and were turning their carriages toward the Changhe Gate.
entries.literal: The former Prince Lun of Zhao was misled by Xiu; together with his sons and others he had already gone to Jinyong to welcome me from the hidden palace, turning the carriage at Changhe.

entries.zh: 豈在予一人獨饗其慶，宗廟社稷實有賴焉。」
entries.en: How could the blessing rest on me alone? The ancestral shrines and the altars of soil and grain have truly depended on them.”
entries.literal: How could it be that I alone partake of the blessing? The ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain truly have relied on this.”

entries.zh: 於是大赦，改元，孤寡賜穀五斛，大酺五日。
entries.en: With the edict closed, the court ordered a general amnesty, a new reign title, five hu of grain for every widow, widower, and orphan, and five days of public feasting.
entries.literal: Thereupon a general amnesty; the era name was changed; widowers, widows, and orphans were granted grain, five hu; great feasting for five days.

entries.zh: 誅趙王倫、義陽王威、九門侯質等及倫之黨與。
entries.en: Prince Lun, Prince Wei of Yiyang, Marquis Zhi of the Nine Gates, and the rest of Lun’s clique were put to death.
entries.literal: Prince Lun of Zhao, Prince Wei of Yiyang, Marquis Zhi of Jiumen, and others, and Lun’s factional followers, were executed.

entries.zh: 夏四月，歲星晝見。
entries.en: Jupiter shone visible in broad daylight during the fourth month.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the year star was seen in daytime.

entries.zh: 冏將何勖、盧播擊張泓於陽翟，大破之，斬孫輔等。
entries.en: He Xu and Lu Bo, under Prince Jiong, crushed Zhang Hong at Yangzhai and executed Sun Fu among others.
entries.literal: Jiong’s generals He Xu and Lu Bo attacked Zhang Hong at Yangzhai, greatly defeated him, and beheaded Sun Fu and others.

entries.zh: 辛酉，左衛將軍王輿與尚書、淮陵王漼勒兵入宮，禽倫黨孫秀、孫會、許超、士猗、駱休等，皆斬之。
entries.en: On the xinyou day Wang Yu and Prince Cui of Huailing forced the palace gates, seized Lun’s confederates Sun Xiu, Sun Hui, Xu Chao, Shi Yi, Luo Xiu, and others, and put them all to the sword.
entries.literal: On the xinyou day, General of the Left Guards Wang Yu, together with the minister, Prince Cui of Huailing, led troops into the palace, captured Lun’s faction Sun Xiu, Sun Hui, Xu Chao, Shi Yi, Luo Xiu, and others; all were beheaded.

entries.zh: 逐倫歸第，即日乘輿反正。
entries.en: Prince Lun was sent home under guard, and the emperor was restored to the throne that same day.
entries.literal: They expelled Lun to return to his residence; that same day the imperial carriage returned to rectitude.

entries.zh: 群臣頓首謝罪，帝曰：「非諸卿之過也。」
entries.en: The ministers prostrated themselves in apology, but the emperor told them, “None of this was your doing.”
entries.literal: The host of ministers knocked their heads in admitting guilt; the emperor said, “It is not the fault of you various ministers.”

entries.zh: 六月戊辰，大赦，增吏位二等。
entries.en: The wuchen day in the sixth month brought a general amnesty and a two-grade promotion for every official.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on the wuchen day, a general amnesty; officials’ ranks were increased two grades.

entries.zh: 復封賓徒王晏爲吳王。
entries.en: Prince Yan of Bintu was restored to the old Wu princedom.
entries.literal: Prince Yan of Bintu was again enfeoffed as prince of Wu.

entries.zh: 庚午，東萊王蕤、左衛將軍王輿謀廢齊王冏，事泄，蕤廢爲庶人，輿伏誅，夷三族。
entries.en: Prince Rui of Donglai and Wang Yu conspired to topple Prince Jiong; when the plot surfaced, Rui was reduced to commoner rank while Wang Yu and three degrees of his kin were executed.
entries.literal: On the gengwu day, Prince Rui of Donglai and General of the Left Guards Wang Yu plotted to depose Prince Jiong of Qi; the affair leaked; Rui was deposed to commoner status; Yu submitted to execution; three clans were exterminated.

entries.zh: 甲戌，以齊王冏爲大司馬、都督中外諸軍事，成都王穎爲大將軍、錄尚書事，河間王顒爲太尉。
entries.en: Prince Jiong became grand marshal and commander-in-chief, Prince Ying general-in-chief with charge of the secretariat, and Prince Yong grand commandant on the jiaxu day.
entries.literal: On the jiaxu day, Prince Jiong of Qi was made grand marshal and area commander for all military affairs within and without; Prince Ying of Chengdu was made general-in-chief and recorder of secretariat affairs; Prince Yong of Hejian was made grand commandant.

entries.zh: 罷丞相，復置司徒官。
entries.en: The chancellorship was abolished and the ministry of education revived.
entries.literal: The chancellor was abolished; the office of minister of education was re-established.

entries.zh: 己卯，以梁王肜爲太宰，領司徒。
entries.en: Prince Rong of Liang was named grand steward while retaining the ministry of education on the jimao day.
entries.literal: On the jimao day, Prince Xiong of Liang was made grand steward, concurrently heading the ministry of education.

entries.zh: 封齊王冏功臣葛旟牟平公，路季小黃公，衛毅平陰公，劉真安鄉公，韓泰封丘公。
entries.en: Prince Jiong of Qi's meritorious followers were enfeoffed: Ge Yu as Duke of Mouping, Lu Ji as Duke of Xiaohuang, Wei Yi as Duke of Pingyin, Liu Zhen as Duke of Anxiang, and Han Tai as Duke of Fengqiu.
entries.literal: Prince Jiong of Qi’s meritorious subjects Ge Yu was enfeoffed duke of Mouping, Lu Ji duke of Xiaohuang, Wei Yi duke of Pingyin, Liu Zhen duke of Anxiang, and Han Tai duke of Fengqiu.

entries.zh: 秋七月甲午，立吳王晏子國爲漢王，復封常山王乂爲長沙王。
entries.en: On the jiawu day in the seventh month Sima Guo, son of Prince Yan of Wu, was created prince of Han, and Prince Yi was moved back from Changshan to the Changsha princedom.
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the jiawu day, Prince Yan of Wu’s son Guo was established as prince of Han; Prince Yi of Changshan was again enfeoffed as prince of Changsha.

entries.zh: 五月，立襄陽王尚爲皇太孫。
entries.en: In the fifth month Prince Shang of Xiangyang was named heir to the throne.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, Prince Shang of Xiangyang was established as imperial grandson-heir.

entries.zh: 十二月，司空何劭薨。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, He Shao, Minister of Works, died.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, He Shao, Minister of Works, died.

entries.zh: 封齊王冏子冰爲樂安王，英爲濟陽王，超爲淮南王。
entries.en: The sons of Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, were enfeoffed: Bing as Prince of Le’an, Ying as Prince of Jiyang, and Chao as Prince of Huainan.
entries.literal: Bing, son of Jiong, Prince of Qi, was enfeoffed as Prince of Le’an, Ying as Prince of Jiyang, and Chao as Prince of Huainan.

entries.zh: 五月乙酉，侍中、太宰、領司徒、梁王肜薨。
entries.en: On yiyou in the fifth month, Sima Rong, Prince of Liang, who served as Palace Attendant, Grand Zai, and acting Minister over the Masses, died.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on yiyou, Rong, Prince of Liang, Palace Attendant, Grand Steward, and acting Minister over the Masses, died.

entries.zh: 以右光祿大夫劉寔爲太傅。
entries.en: Liu Shi, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness of the Right, was appointed Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: Liu Shi, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness of the Right, was made Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 太尉、河間王顒遣將衙博擊李特於蜀，爲特所敗。
entries.en: Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian and Grand Commandant, sent the general Ya Bo to attack Li Te in Shu, but Li Te defeated him.
entries.literal: Yong, Prince of Hejian and Grand Commandant, sent the general Ya Bo to attack Li Te in Shu, and he was defeated by Te.

entries.zh: 特遂陷梓潼、巴西，害廣漢太守張微，自號大將軍。
entries.en: Li Te then captured Zitong and Baxi, killed Zhang Wei, Administrator of Guanghan, and assumed the title Great General.
entries.literal: Te then captured Zitong and Baxi, killed Zhang Wei, Administrator of Guanghan, and styled himself Great General.

entries.zh: 癸卯，以清河王遐子覃爲皇太子，賜孤寡帛，大酺五日。
entries.en: On guimao, Tan, son of Sima Xia, Prince of Qinghe, was made crown prince. Silk was given to the bereft and unsupported, and a public feast was held for five days.
entries.literal: On guimao, Tan, son of Xia, Prince of Qinghe, was made imperial heir; silk was bestowed on widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless, and a great feast was held for five days.

entries.zh: 以齊王冏爲太師，東海王越爲司空。
entries.en: Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, was appointed Grand Preceptor, and Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Jiong, Prince of Qi, was made Grand Preceptor, and Yue, Prince of Donghai, was made Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 太安元年春正月庚子，安東將軍、譙王隨薨。
entries.en: Prince Sui of Qiao, general who pacifies the east, died on the gengzi day in the first month of Tai’an.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tai’an, spring, first month, on the gengzi day, General Who Pacifies the East, Prince Sui of Qiao, died.

entries.zh: 秋七月，中書令卞粹、侍中馮蓀、河南尹李含等貳於長沙王乂，乂疑而害之。
entries.en: In the seventh month Prince Yi suspected Bian Cui, Feng Sun, Li Han, and others of divided loyalty and had them killed.
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Director of the Secretariat Bian Cui, Palace Attendant Feng Sun, Intendant of Henan Li Han, and others were double-minded toward Prince Yi of Changsha; Yi suspected them and harmed them.

entries.zh: 二年春正月甲子朔，赦五歲刑。
entries.en: The new year opened with remission of all penal labor sentences up to five years.
entries.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, on the jiazi new moon, five-year sentences were amnestied.

entries.zh: 八月，河間王顒、成都王穎舉兵討長沙王乂，帝以乂爲大都督，帥軍禦之。
entries.en: In the eighth month Princes Yong and Ying marched against Prince Yi of Changsha, whom the emperor named supreme commander to meet them in the field.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, Prince Yong of Hejian and Prince Ying of Chengdu raised troops to attack Prince Yi of Changsha; the emperor made Yi grand commander-in-chief to lead the army in resisting them.

entries.zh: 永興元年春正月丙午，尚書令樂廣卒。
entries.en: On bingwu in the first month of spring in Yongxing 1, Le Guang, Director of the Secretariat, died.
entries.literal: In spring, in the first month of the first year of Yongxing, on bingwu, Le Guang, Director of the Secretariat, died.

entries.zh: 成都王穎自鄴諷于帝，乃大赦，改元爲永安。
entries.en: From Ye, Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, pressured the emperor by suggestion; a general amnesty followed, and the era name was changed to Yongan.
entries.literal: Ying, Prince of Chengdu, from Ye hinted to the emperor, and so there was a great amnesty and the era name was changed to Yongan.

entries.zh: 帝逼于河間王顒，密詔雍州刺史劉沈、秦州刺史皇甫重以討之。
entries.en: Pressed by Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, the emperor secretly ordered Liu Shen, Inspector of Yongzhou, and Huangfu Zhong, Inspector of Qinzhou, to attack him.
entries.literal: The emperor was pressured by Yong, Prince of Hejian, and secretly ordered Liu Shen, Inspector of Yongzhou, and Huangfu Zhong, Inspector of Qinzhou, to attack him.

entries.zh: 沈舉兵攻長安，爲顒所敗。
entries.en: Liu Shen raised troops against Chang’an, but Sima Yong defeated him.
entries.literal: Shen raised troops and attacked Chang’an, but was defeated by Yong.

entries.zh: 張方大掠洛中，還長安。
entries.en: Zhang Fang plundered Luoyang heavily and returned to Chang’an.
entries.literal: Zhang Fang greatly plundered the Luoyang area and returned to Chang’an.

entries.zh: 於是軍中大餒，人相食。
entries.en: The army then suffered severe famine, and people resorted to cannibalism.
entries.literal: At this, the army suffered great hunger, and people ate one another.

entries.zh: 以成都王穎爲丞相。
entries.en: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, was made Chancellor.
entries.literal: Ying, Prince of Chengdu, was made Chancellor.

entries.zh: 穎遣從事中郎成夔等以兵五萬屯十二城門，殿中宿所忌者，穎皆殺之，以三部兵代宿衛。
entries.en: Ying sent Cheng Kui and others with fifty thousand troops to garrison the twelve city gates. He killed everyone on palace duty whom he suspected and replaced the palace guard with troops from the Three Divisions.
entries.literal: Ying sent Attendant Gentleman Cheng Kui and others with fifty thousand troops to camp at the twelve city gates; all those on palace duty whom Ying feared, he killed, replacing the palace guards with troops from the Three Divisions.

entries.zh: 河間王顒表請立成都王穎爲太弟。
entries.en: Prince Yong asked the throne to name Prince Ying of Chengdu as heir apparent.
entries.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian submitted a memorial requesting that Prince Ying of Chengdu be established as imperial younger brother and heir.

entries.zh: 戊申，詔曰：「朕以不德，纂承鴻緒，于茲十有五載。
entries.en: On the wushen day an edict began: “Fifteen years have passed since I, unworthy, inherited the great mandate.
entries.literal: On the wushen day an edict stated: “I, lacking virtue, have succeeded to the vast line; here now fifteen years.

entries.zh: 禍亂滔天，姦逆仍起，至乃幽廢重宮，宗廟圮絕。
entries.en: Disaster has mounted to the skies, rebels have followed one after another, I was cast into the inner palace in disgrace, and the sacrifices nearly failed altogether.
entries.literal: Calamity and rebellion have swelled to Heaven; traitors have arisen in succession, so that I was even confined and deposed in the deep palace, and the ancestral temples were cut off.

entries.zh: 成都王穎溫仁惠和，克平暴亂。
entries.en: Prince Ying of Chengdu is gentle, generous, and just, and he has crushed the violence that tore the realm.
entries.literal: Prince Ying of Chengdu is warm, humane, kind, and harmonious, and has been able to pacify violence and chaos.

entries.zh: 其以穎爲皇太弟、都督中外諸軍事，丞相如故。」
entries.en: Let him therefore be named imperial younger brother and heir, commander of every army, while retaining the chancellorship.”
entries.literal: Let Ying be made imperial younger brother and heir, area commander for all military affairs within and without, and remain chancellor as before.”

entries.zh: 大赦，賜鰥寡高年帛三匹，大酺五日。
entries.en: A general amnesty followed, three bolts of silk went to each destitute elder, and the capital celebrated for five days.
entries.literal: A general amnesty; widowers, widows, and the aged were granted three bolts of silk; great feasting for five days.

entries.zh: 丙辰，盜竊太廟服器。
entries.en: Robbers plundered the ritual regalia from the Grand Temple on bingchen.
entries.literal: On the bingchen day thieves stole the vestments and vessels of the Grand Temple.

entries.zh: 以太尉顒爲太宰，太傅劉寔爲太尉。
entries.en: Prince Yong moved from grand commandant to grand steward, and Liu Shi from grand tutor to grand commandant.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant Yong was made grand steward; Grand Tutor Liu Shi was made grand commandant.

entries.zh: 顒遣其將張方，穎遣其將陸機、牽秀、石超等來逼京師。
entries.en: Zhang Fang came at the head of Prince Yong’s host, while Lu Ji, Qian Xiu, and Shi Chao advanced for Prince Ying against Luoyang.
entries.literal: Yong dispatched his general Zhang Fang; Ying dispatched his generals Lu Ji, Qian Xiu, Shi Chao, and others to press the capital.

entries.zh: 乙丑，帝幸十三里橋，遣將軍皇甫商距方于宜陽。
entries.en: The emperor rode to the Thirteen-Li bridge and ordered Huangfu Shang to hold Zhang Fang at Yiyang on the yichou day.
entries.literal: On the yichou day the emperor visited the bridge at Thirteen Li and sent General Huangfu Shang to block Zhang Fang at Yiyang.

entries.zh: 己巳，帝旋軍于宣武場。
entries.en: By the jisi day the imperial camp had withdrawn to the Xuanwu parade ground.
entries.literal: On the jisi day the emperor wheeled the army back to the Xuanwu drill ground.

entries.zh: 庚午，舍于石樓。
entries.en: He spent the gengwu night at the Stone Tower.
entries.literal: On the gengwu day he lodged at the Stone Tower.

entries.zh: 天中裂，無雲而雷。
entries.en: A fissure seemed to open in the heavens, and thunder rolled under a cloudless sky.
entries.literal: The sky split midway; without clouds there was thunder.

entries.zh: 冬十月壬寅，帝旋于宮。
entries.en: The sovereign re-entered the palace on renyin in the tenth month.
entries.literal: In winter, on the renyin day of the tenth month, the emperor returned to the palace.

entries.zh: 石超焚緱氏，服御無遺。
entries.en: Shi Chao put Gongshi to the torch and destroyed almost every piece of the imperial train.
entries.literal: Shi Chao burned Gongshi, leaving nothing of the imperial baggage.

entries.zh: 丁未，破牽秀、范陽王虓于東陽門外。
entries.en: Outside the Dongyang Gate the loyalists broke Qian Xiu and Prince Xiao of Fanyang on dingwei.
entries.literal: On the dingwei day Qian Xiu and Prince Xiao of Fanyang were defeated outside the Dongyang Gate.

entries.zh: 戊申，破陸機于建春門，石超走，斬其大將賈崇等十六人，懸首銅駝街。
entries.en: At the Jianchun Gate on wushen Lu Ji’s line collapsed, Shi Chao bolted, and sixteen of his senior commanders including Jia Chong were executed, their heads displayed along Copper Camel Street.
entries.literal: On the wushen day Lu Ji was defeated at the Jianchun Gate; Shi Chao fled; sixteen of his chief generals including Jia Chong were beheaded and their heads hung along Copper Camel Street.

entries.zh: 張方退屯十三里橋。
entries.en: Zhang Fang pulled back to the Thirteen-Li bridge.
entries.literal: Zhang Fang withdrew and encamped at the Thirteen-Li bridge.

entries.zh: 秋七月丙申朔，右衛將軍陳眕以詔召百僚入殿中，因勒兵討成都王穎。
entries.en: On the bingshen new moon of autumn’s seventh month, General of the Right Guards Chen Zhen used an edict to summon the hundred officials into the palace hall, then led troops against Prince Ying of Chengdu.
entries.literal: In autumn, on the bingshen new moon of the seventh month, General of the Right Guards Chen Zhen used an edict to summon the hundred officials into the palace, then led troops to attack Prince Ying of Chengdu.

entries.zh: 戊戌，大赦，復皇后羊氏及皇太子覃。
entries.en: Empress Yang and Crown Prince Tan were restored on wuxu under a general amnesty.
entries.literal: On the wuxu day a general amnesty restored Empress Yang and Crown Prince Tan.

entries.zh: 己亥，司徒王戎、東海王越、高密王簡、平昌公模、吳王晏、豫章王熾、襄陽王範、右僕射荀藩等奉帝北征。
entries.en: On jihai Wang Rong, Prince Yue, Prince Jian, Sima Mo, Prince Yan, Prince Chi, Prince Fan, and Xun Fan convoyed the emperor north.
entries.literal: On the jihai day Minister of Education Wang Rong, Prince Yue of Donghai, Prince Jian of Gaomi, Duke Mo of Pingchang, Prince Yan of Wu, Prince Chi of Yuzhang, Prince Fan of Xiangyang, and Right Vice Director Xun Fan and others escorted the emperor on a northern expedition.

entries.zh: 至安陽，眾十餘萬，穎遣其將石超距戰。
entries.en: The army swelled past a hundred thousand at Anyang, where Prince Ying sent Shi Chao to bar the road.
entries.literal: When they reached Anyang the host exceeded one hundred thousand; Ying dispatched his general Shi Chao to resist in battle.

entries.zh: 己未，六軍敗績于蕩陰，矢及乘輿，百官分散，侍中嵇紹死之。
entries.en: At Dangyin on jiwei the imperial army collapsed, arrows riddled the imperial coach, the courtiers fled, and Ji Shao died shielding the throne.
entries.literal: On the jiwei day the six armies were defeated at Dangyin; arrows reached the imperial carriage; the hundred officials scattered; Palace Attendant Ji Shao died in the engagement.

entries.zh: 帝傷頰，中三矢，亡六璽。
entries.en: The sovereign took three hits in the cheek and lost six of the dynasty’s jade seals in the rout.
entries.literal: The emperor was wounded in the cheek, struck by three arrows, and lost six of the imperial seals.

entries.zh: 帝遂幸超軍，餒甚，超進水，左右奉秋桃。
entries.en: Starving, he fell into Shi Chao’s lines; Chao gave him water while attendants found late peaches.
entries.literal: The emperor thereupon visited Chao’s camp, was extremely hungry; Chao advanced water, and attendants offered autumn peaches.

entries.zh: 超遣弟熙奉帝之鄴，穎帥群官迎謁道左。
entries.en: Shi Chao’s brother Shi Xi escorted the emperor toward Ye, where Prince Ying knelt with his entire staff along the road.
entries.literal: Chao sent his younger brother Xi to convoy the emperor to Ye; Ying led the host of officials to bow in welcome by the roadside.

entries.zh: 帝下輿涕泣，其夕幸于穎軍。
entries.en: He stepped down from the coach in tears and spent the night in Prince Ying’s encampment.
entries.literal: The emperor alighted from the carriage weeping; that evening he lodged in Ying’s camp.

entries.zh: 穎府有九錫之儀，陳留王送貂蟬文衣鶡尾，明日，乃備法駕幸于鄴，唯豫章王熾、司徒王戎、僕射荀藩從。
entries.en: Prince Ying’s compound already displayed the nine-bestowal regalia; the prince of Chenliu sent the full accoutrements of investiture, and on the following day the emperor entered Ye with complete state panoply, attended only by Prince Chi, Wang Rong, and Xun Fan.
entries.literal: Ying’s headquarters held the regalia for the nine bestowals; the Prince of Chenliu presented sable-cicada insignia, patterned robes, and pheasant-tail pennants; the next day the full imperial equipage was prepared and proceeded to Ye; only Prince Chi of Yuzhang, Minister Wang Rong, and Vice Director Xun Fan accompanied.

entries.zh: 庚申，大赦，改元爲建武。
entries.en: The reign was renamed Jianwu on gengshen amid another general amnesty.
entries.literal: On the gengshen day a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Jianwu.

entries.zh: 八月戊辰，穎殺東安王繇。
entries.en: Prince Yao of Dong’an was executed by Prince Ying on wuchen in the eighth month.
entries.literal: On the wuchen day of the eighth month Ying killed Prince Yao of Dong’an.

entries.zh: 張方復入洛陽，廢皇后羊氏及皇太子覃。
entries.en: Zhang Fang returned to Luoyang and stripped the empress and crown prince of their titles once more.
entries.literal: Zhang Fang again entered Luoyang and deposed Empress Yang and Crown Prince Tan.

entries.zh: 匈奴左賢王劉元海反於離石，自號大單于。
entries.en: Liu Yuan, the Xiongnu worthy king of the left who is known as Yuanhai, rose at Lishi and proclaimed himself great chanyu.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu Worthy King of the Left Liu Yuan (Yuanhai) rebelled at Lishi and styled himself great chanyu.

entries.zh: 安北將軍王浚遣烏丸騎攻成都王穎于鄴，大敗之。
entries.en: Wang Jun, general who pacifies the north, hurled Wuhuan horse against Prince Ying at Ye and shattered his army.
entries.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Wang Jun sent Wuhuan cavalry against Prince Ying of Chengdu at Ye and greatly defeated him.

entries.zh: 穎與帝單車走洛陽，服御分散，倉卒上下無齎，侍中黃門被囊中齎私錢三千，詔貸用。
entries.en: Prince Ying and the emperor bolted toward Luoyang in one cart, servants and luggage lost along the way; court eunuchs lent three thousand cash from their belts under emergency warrant.
entries.literal: Ying and the emperor fled in a single carriage toward Luoyang; attendants and baggage were scattered; in haste high and low had no provisions; palace attendants and yellow gates carried three thousand cash of private money in satchels, and an edict authorized borrowing it.

entries.zh: 所在買飯以供，宮人止食于道中客舍。
entries.en: They bought meals from wayside kitchens, and the palace ladies slept in posting houses.
entries.literal: Wherever they stopped they bought rice to supply him; palace women ate only at roadside inns.

entries.zh: 宮人有持升餘糠米飯及燥蒜鹽豉以進帝，帝噉之，御中黃門布被。
entries.en: One maid offered a bowl of gritty rice with dried garlic and salted beans; he ate it and slept under a eunuch’s quilt.
entries.literal: A palace woman brought more than a sheng of coarse rice, dried garlic, salted beans, and fermented black beans for the emperor; the emperor ate them; he used a eunuch’s cotton quilt.

entries.zh: 次獲嘉，市粗米飯，盛以瓦盆，帝噉兩盂。
entries.en: At Huojia he bought two bowls of rough rice from a street vendor in a clay dish.
entries.literal: Halting at Huojia, they bought coarse rice in the market, served in an earthen bowl; the emperor ate two bowls.

entries.zh: 有老父獻蒸雞，帝受之。
entries.en: An old man presented a steamed chicken, which the emperor accepted.
entries.literal: An old man presented a steamed chicken, and the emperor accepted it.

entries.zh: 至溫，將謁陵，帝喪履，納從者之履，下拜流涕，左右皆歔欷。
entries.en: At Wen, intending to worship at the tombs, he lost his shoes, borrowed a guard’s pair, and wept so bitterly that every retainer wept with him.
entries.literal: When they reached Wen, about to visit the mausoleum, the emperor lost his shoes, put on a follower’s footwear, descended to bow with streaming tears, and those at his side sobbed.

entries.zh: 及濟河，張方帥騎三千，以陽燧青蓋車奉迎。
entries.en: Zhang Fang met him mid-river with three thousand riders and a chariot hung with a bronze fire mirror and blue canopy.
entries.literal: When they crossed the river, Zhang Fang led three thousand horsemen to welcome him with a sun-mirror canopy carriage.

entries.zh: 方拜謁，帝躬止之。
entries.en: Zhang Fang kowtowed, but the emperor raised him with his own hands.
entries.literal: Fang bowed in audience; the emperor in person stopped him.

entries.zh: 辛巳，大赦，賞從者各有差。
entries.en: A general amnesty on xinsi came with graded rewards for everyone who had stayed with the throne.
entries.literal: On the xinsi day a general amnesty was proclaimed; followers were rewarded each according to grade.

entries.zh: 十二月丁亥，詔曰：「天禍晉邦，冢嗣莫繼。
entries.en: On the dinghai day in the twelfth month an edict began: “Heaven scourges Jin, and no son of mine survives to succeed.
entries.literal: On the dinghai day of the twelfth month an edict stated: “Heaven has punished the Jin state; no heir succeeds.

entries.zh: 成都王穎自在儲貳，政績虧損，四海失望，不可承重，其以王還第。
entries.en: Prince Ying proved unfit while heir apparent and has forfeited the trust of the realm, so he must be stripped of the succession and sent home to his fief.
entries.literal: Prince Ying of Chengdu, while heir, failed in government; within the four seas hope was disappointed; he cannot bear the heavy charge; let him return to his residence as a prince.

entries.zh: 豫章王熾先帝愛子，令問日新，四海注意，今以爲皇太弟，以隆我晉邦。
entries.en: Prince Chi of Yuzhang, the late emperor’s favorite, grows in reputation every day, and he shall be named imperial younger brother and heir to steady the house of Jin.
entries.literal: Prince Chi of Yuzhang was the late emperor’s beloved son; his fair fame grows daily; within the four seas all eyes turn to him; now let him be made imperial younger brother and heir to uplift our Jin state.

entries.zh: 以司空越爲太傅，與太宰顒夾輔朕躬。
entries.en: Minister of Works Prince Yue is appointed grand tutor to work beside Grand Steward Yong in guiding the throne.
entries.literal: Let Minister of Works Yue be made grand tutor, together with Grand Steward Yong to flank and assist my person.

entries.zh: 司徒王戎參錄朝政，光祿大夫王衍爲尚書左僕射。
entries.en: Wang Rong shall join in supervising policy, and Wang Yan shall take the left vice directorship of the secretariat.
entries.literal: Let Minister of Education Wang Rong participate in recording court governance; Household Grandee Wang Yan is made left vice director of the secretariat.

entries.zh: 安南將軍虓、安北將軍浚、平北將軍騰各守本鎮。
entries.en: Generals Xiao, Jun, and Teng are ordered to hold their existing commands.
entries.literal: General Who Pacifies the South Xiao, General Who Pacifies the North Jun, and General Who Pacifies the North Teng each guard their original garrisons.

entries.zh: 高密王簡爲鎮南將軍，領司隸校尉，權鎮洛陽；
entries.en: Prince Jian of Gaomi becomes general who guards the south and acting metropolitan superintendent at Luoyang.
entries.literal: Prince Jian of Gaomi is made general who guards the south, concurrently metropolitan superintendent, acting in authority at Luoyang;

entries.zh: 東中郎將模爲寧北將軍、都督冀州，鎮于鄴；
entries.en: Sima Mo moves to general who guards the north with Ji Province command, based at Ye.
entries.literal: General of the Household Gentlemen of the East Mo is made general who guards the north and area commander for Ji Province, stationed at Ye;

entries.zh: 鎮南大將軍劉弘領荊州，以鎮南土。
entries.en: Liu Hong, general-in-chief who guards the south, keeps order in Jing Province.
entries.literal: General-in-chief Who Guards the South Liu Hong holds Jing Province to secure the south.

entries.zh: 周馥、繆胤各還本部，百官皆復職。
entries.en: Zhou Fu and Miao Yin go back to their posts, and every minister returns to duty.
entries.literal: Zhou Fu and Miao Yin each return to their original commands; the hundred officials all resume their posts.

entries.zh: 齊王冏前應還第，長沙王乂輕陷重刑，封其子紹爲樂平縣王，以奉其嗣。
entries.en: Prince Jiong ought long ago to have been sent to his domain, and Prince Yi suffered a cruel death, so enfeoff his son Shao as prince of Leping to preserve his line.
entries.literal: Prince Jiong of Qi should earlier have returned to his residence; Prince Yi of Changsha was lightly subjected to heavy punishment; enfeoff his son Shao as prince of Leping county to continue his line.

entries.zh: 自頃戎車屢征，勞費人力，供御之物皆減三分之二，戶調田租三分減一。
entries.en: Because armies have marched again and again, palace supplies are cut by two-thirds, and the poll tax and land rent are each reduced by a third.
entries.literal: Recently war-chariots have repeatedly marched, exhausting men and resources; articles for the imperial household are all reduced by two-thirds; household levies and field rent are each reduced by one-third.

entries.zh: 蠲除苛政，愛人務本。
entries.en: Harsh statutes are swept away so the people may return to their fields.
entries.literal: Harsh government is remitted; the people are cherished and the root is sought.

entries.zh: 清通之後，當還東京。」
entries.en: Once peace is restored, the court will return to Luoyang.”
entries.literal: After the realm is cleared and at peace, we shall return to the eastern capital.”

entries.zh: 大赦，改元。
entries.en: The edict ended with a general amnesty and a new reign title.
entries.literal: A general amnesty; the era name was changed.

entries.zh: 以河間王顒都督中外諸軍事。
entries.en: Prince Yong of Hejian received overall command of every army.
entries.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian was made area commander for all military affairs within and without.

entries.zh: 六月甲子，侍中、司徒、安豐侯王戎薨。
entries.en: On jiazi in the sixth month, Wang Rong, Palace Attendant, Minister over the Masses, and Marquis of Anfeng, died.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on jiazi, Wang Rong, Palace Attendant, Minister over the Masses, and Marquis of Anfeng, died.

entries.zh: 隴西太守韓稚攻秦州刺史張輔，殺之。
entries.en: Han Zhi, Administrator of Longxi, attacked and killed Zhang Fu, Inspector of Qinzhou.
entries.literal: Han Zhi, Administrator of Longxi, attacked Zhang Fu, Inspector of Qinzhou, and killed him.

entries.zh: 李雄僭即帝位，國號蜀。
entries.en: Li Xiong usurped the imperial title and named his state Shu.
entries.literal: Li Xiong usurped the imperial position and named his state Shu.

entries.zh: 壬辰，祁弘等與刁默戰，默大敗，顒、穎走南山，奔于宛。
entries.en: On renchen Qi Hong and the others battled Diao Mo; Mo was greatly defeated; Princes Yong and Ying fled to the southern mountains and ran to Wan.
entries.literal: On the renchen day Qi Hong and others battled Diao Mo; Mo was greatly defeated; Yong and Ying fled to the southern mountains and ran to Wan.

entries.zh: 弘等所部鮮卑大掠長安，殺二萬餘人。
entries.en: Qi Hong’s Xianbei troopers sacked Chang’an and killed more than twenty thousand.
entries.literal: The Xianbei under Qi Hong’s command greatly plundered Chang’an and killed more than twenty thousand persons.

entries.zh: 是日，日光四散，赤如血。
entries.en: That day the sun’s light scattered blood-red in every quarter.
entries.literal: That day sunlight scattered in four directions, red as blood.

entries.zh: 甲午又如之。
entries.en: The same crimson light returned on jiawu.
entries.literal: On the jiawu day it was again so.

entries.zh: 九月，頓丘太守馮嵩執成都王穎，送之于鄴。
entries.en: Feng Song of Dunqiu captured Prince Ying and sent him to Ye.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, Dunqiu Prefect Feng Song seized Prince Ying of Chengdu and sent him to Ye.

entries.zh: 進東嬴公騰爵爲東燕王，平昌公模爲南陽王。
entries.en: Sima Teng became prince of Dongyan and Sima Mo prince of Nanyang.
entries.literal: Duke Teng of Dongying was advanced in rank to prince of Dongyan; Duke Mo of Pingchang was made prince of Nanyang.

entries.zh: 冬十月，司空、范陽王虓薨。
entries.en: Prince Xiao of Fanyang, minister of works, died in the tenth month.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Minister of Works, Prince Xiao of Fanyang, died.

entries.zh: 虓長史劉輿害成都王穎。
entries.en: Liu Yu, Prince Xiao’s chief clerk, killed Prince Ying.
entries.literal: Xiao’s chief clerk Liu Yu harmed Prince Ying of Chengdu.

entries.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
entries.en: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.
entries.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.

entries.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
entries.en: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.

entries.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.

entries.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。
entries.en: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.
entries.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.

entries.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。
entries.en: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.
