entries.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.

entries.zh: 元康二年，拜員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: In 292 he received appointment as supernumerary gentleman cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yuankang he was appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary.

entries.zh: 累遷左將軍，從討成都王穎。
entries.en: He rose step by step to general of the left and marched with the army that moved against Sima Ying, prince of Chengdu.
entries.literal: By stages he was promoted to General of the Left and followed in the campaign against the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying.

entries.zh: 蕩陰之敗也，叔父東安王繇爲穎所害。
entries.en: When the imperial forces were shattered at Dangyin, his uncle Sima Yao, prince of Dong'an, fell victim to Ying's purge.
entries.literal: At the defeat at Dangyin, his uncle the Prince of Dong'an, Yao, was killed by Ying.

entries.zh: 帝懼禍及，將出奔。
entries.en: Fearing the blow would soon strike him too, he prepared to slip away from the capital.
entries.literal: The emperor feared disaster reaching him and intended to flee.

entries.zh: 其夜月正明，而禁衛嚴警，帝無由得去，甚窘迫。
entries.en: The moon shone clear that night, yet the inner-palace cordon was so tight that he could find no way out and grew desperate.
entries.literal: That night the moon was just bright, but the palace guards were strictly alert; the emperor had no means to depart and was very pressed.

entries.zh: 有頃，雲霧晦冥，雷雨暴至，徼者皆馳，因得潛出。
entries.en: Presently clouds swallowed the moon, a sudden storm broke, and the sentries scattered for shelter, which gave him the opening to steal out unseen.
entries.literal: After a while, clouds and mist were dark and gloomy; violent rain and thunder arrived; the patrolmen all ran; thereby he was able secretly to go out.

entries.zh: 穎先令諸關無得出貴人，帝旣至河陽，爲津吏所止。
entries.en: Ying had barred every pass to people of rank; when he reached the Heyang ferry a petty official held him up.
entries.literal: Ying had first ordered the various passes not to allow nobles to exit; when the emperor had reached Heyang, he was stopped by the ferry clerk.

entries.zh: 從者宋典後來，以策鞭帝馬而笑曰：「舍長！
entries.en: His follower Song Dian rode up behind him, tapped his mount with a riding crop, and called out with a laugh, "Innkeeper!
entries.literal: Follower Song Dian came afterward, with a whip struck the emperor's horse and laughed, saying: "Hostel chief!

entries.zh: 官禁貴人，汝亦被拘邪！」
entries.en: The authorities are detaining grandees—have they got you as well!"
entries.literal: The officials forbid nobles; are you also detained!"

entries.zh: 吏乃聽過。
entries.en: The clerk, fooled by the act, waved them through.
entries.literal: The clerk then allowed passage.

entries.zh: 至洛陽，迎太妃俱歸國。
entries.en: He reached Luoyang, fetched his mother the grand consort, and escorted her home to his princedom.
entries.literal: Arriving at Luoyang, he welcomed the Grand Consort and together returned to the state.

entries.zh: 三月，徵征西將軍戴若思、鎮北將軍劉隗還衛京都。
entries.en: In the third month Dai Ruosi and Liu Wei were recalled from the front to defend the capital.
entries.literal: In the third month he summoned General Who Conquers the West Dai Ruosi, General Who Guards the North Liu Wei to return and guard the capital region.

entries.zh: 以司空王導爲前鋒大都督，以戴若思爲驃騎將軍，丹陽諸郡皆加軍號。
entries.en: Wang Dao was named commander of the vanguard, Dai Ruosi became general of agile cavalry, and every Danyang county received a military designation.
entries.literal: He appointed Minister of Works Wang Dao as Vanguard Grand Area Commander-in-Chief; appointed Dai Ruosi as General of Agile Cavalry; Danyang various commanderies all were added military titles.

entries.zh: 加僕射周顗尚書左僕射，領軍王邃尚書右僕射。
entries.en: Zhou Yi was promoted to left vice director of the secretariat and Wang Sui, the army commandant, to right vice director.
entries.literal: He added Vice Director Zhou Yi as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; Army Commandant Wang Sui as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 以太子右衛率周筵行冠軍將軍，統兵三千討沈充。
entries.en: Zhou Yan, leader of the crown prince's right guard, was given the brevet rank of general who takes the championship and three thousand men to move against Shen Chong.
entries.literal: He appointed the heir apparent's right guard leader Zhou Yan to act as General Who Takes the Championship, commanding three thousand troops to campaign against Shen Chong.

entries.zh: 甲午，封皇子昱爲琅邪王。
entries.en: On the jiawu day the emperor's son Sima Yu was invested as prince of Langye.
entries.literal: On jiawu he enfeoffed the imperial son Yu as Prince of Langye.

entries.zh: 劉隗軍于金城，右將軍周札守石頭，帝親被甲徇六師於郊外。
entries.en: Liu Wei took position at Jincheng, Zhou Zha, general of the right, held Stone City, and the emperor buckled on his armor and rode through the six hosts outside the walls.
entries.literal: Liu Wei encamped at Jincheng; General of the Right Zhou Zha guarded Stone Rampart; the emperor personally donned armor and inspected the six armies beyond the suburbs.

entries.zh: 遣平南將軍陶侃領江州，安南將軍甘卓領荊州，各帥所統以躡敦後。
entries.en: He ordered Tao Kan, the general who pacifies the south, to take charge of Jiangzhou and Gan Zhuo, the general who guards the south, of Jingzhou, each marching to fall on Wang Dun from behind.
entries.literal: He dispatched General Who Pacifies the South Tao Kan to take Jiangzhou, General Who Guards the South Gan Zhuo to take Jingzhou, each leading what they commanded to follow on Dun's rear.

entries.zh: 初，《玄石圖》有「牛繼馬後」，故宣帝深忌牛氏，遂爲二榼，共一口，以貯酒焉，帝先飲佳者，而以毒酒鴆其將牛金。
entries.en: The Dark Stone Chart once warned that "an ox would follow the horse"; Emperor Xuan therefore feared the Niu surname, set out paired flasks with a single spout, drank the good wine himself, and poisoned his general Niu Jin from the other.
entries.literal: Formerly, in the Dark Stone Chart there was "the ox follows the horse"; therefore Emperor Xuan deeply dreaded the Niu clan; then made two flasks, sharing one mouth, to store wine therein; the emperor first drank the fine, but with poisoned wine zhenned his general Niu Jin.

entries.zh: 而恭王妃夏侯氏竟通小吏牛氏而生元帝，亦有符云。
entries.en: Yet Lady Xiahou, consort of King Gong, took up with a minor clerk surnamed Niu and bore Emperor Yuan—another omen fulfilled, men said.
entries.literal: Yet King Gong's consort Lady Xiahou in the end connected with clerk Niu and bore Yuan Emperor; there was also a tally saying so.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：晉氏不虞，自中流外，五胡扛鼎，七廟隳尊，滔天方駕，則民懷其舊德者矣。
entries.en: The historians write: Jin could not guard against calamity from within; beyond the heartland the Five Hu seized the cauldron, the imperial shrines were cast down, and rebellion rose like a flood—so the people clung to the memory of better days.
entries.literal: The historians say: The Jin clan did not foresee it; from midstream outward, the five Hu shouldered the tripod, the seven temples toppled their honor; flooding Heaven side by side—then the people cherished its old virtue.

entries.zh: 昔光武以數郡加名，元皇以一州臨極，豈武宣餘化猶暢于琅邪，文景垂仁傳芳于南頓，所謂後乎天時，先諸人事者也。
entries.en: Guangwu rose from a handful of commanderies, while Emperor Yuan ruled from a single province—perhaps the lingering influence of King Wu and Emperor Xuan still flowed at Langye, and the kindness of Han Wendi and Jingdi still lingered at Nandun: fate came late, but human effort came first.
entries.literal: Formerly Guangwu by several commanderies added fame; Yuan Huang by one province faced the extreme—was it that Wu and Xuan's remaining transformation still flowed at Langye, Wen and Jing's hanging benevolence transmitted fragrance at Nandun—what is called behind Heaven's timing, ahead of the multitude of human affairs.

entries.zh: 馳章獻號，高蓋成陰，星斗呈祥，金陵表慶。
entries.en: Memorials flew in offering the throne, noble coaches crowded the roads like a forest, the stars showed blessing, and Jinling proclaimed good fortune.
entries.literal: Galloping memorials presented titles; high canopies became shade; stars and constellations showed auspice; Jinling displayed celebration.

entries.zh: 陶士行擁三州之旅，郢外以安；
entries.en: Tao Kan held three provinces' troops and the country beyond Jing grew calm;
entries.literal: Tao Shixing embraced three provinces' hosts; outside Ying thereby was pacified;

entries.zh: 王茂弘爲分陝之計，江東可立。
entries.en: Wang Dao laid plans like the ancient "divided Shaan" partnership, and the lower Yangzi could stand as a realm.
entries.literal: Wang Maohong made the divided-Shaan plan; east of the river could be established.

entries.zh: 或高旌未拂，而遐心斯偃，回首朝陽，仰希乾棟，帝猶六讓不居，七辭而不免也。
entries.en: Before his banners had swept the north, distant hearts already bowed; all eyes turned to the rising sun and looked for a pillar of state—yet even after six refusals of the throne and seven pleas to be spared, he could not escape taking it.
entries.literal: Perhaps high banners not yet waved, yet distant hearts thereby lay low; turning the head toward the morning sun, looking up hoping for the Qian ridgepole—yet the emperor still six times yielded not to dwell, seven times declined yet could not avoid.

entries.zh: 布帳綀帷，詳刑簡化，抑揚前軌，光啓中興。
entries.en: Plain curtains and gauze screens, careful justice and lean government—he trimmed the excesses of the past and lit the torch of the restoration.
entries.literal: Cloth curtains and pongee hangings; detailed punishments, simplified transformation; suppressing and raising former tracks, broadly opening restoration.

entries.zh: 古首私家不蓄甲兵，大臣不爲威福，王之常制，以訓股肱。
entries.en: The ancients said that private houses must not hoard arms and that ministers must not wield arbitrary power—such is the king's standing rule for teaching his servants.
entries.literal: From of old it has been said: private families do not store armor and weapons; great ministers do not make awesomeness and fortune—this is the king's constant regulation, whereby to instruct thigh and arm.

entries.zh: 中宗失馭強臣，自亡齊斧，兩京胡羯，風埃相望。
entries.en: Zhongzong failed to bridle mighty vassals and so lost the regal axe himself; the twin capitals fell to Hu and Jie, and dust of war stretched from plain to plain.
entries.literal: Zhongzong lost control of strong ministers, himself lost the Qi axe; two capitals Hu and Jie, wind and dust face each other.

entries.zh: 雖復《六月》之駕無聞，而《鴻雁》之歌方遠，享國無幾，哀哉！
entries.en: He never heard the war-chariots of the "Sixth Month" ode, and the lament of "Wild Geese" still rang far off; his reign was brief—how pitiful!
entries.literal: Although again the "Sixth Month" chariot was unheard of, yet the "Wild Geese" song was still distant; enjoying the state not many—alas!

entries.zh: 二月，葬元帝于建平陵，帝徒跣至于陵所。
entries.en: In the second month Emperor Yuan was laid in the Jianping tombs; the new emperor walked the last miles barefoot behind the bier.
entries.literal: In the second month they buried Yuan Emperor at Jianping Mausoleum; the emperor barefoot went to the mausoleum site.

entries.zh: 以特進華恒爲驃騎將軍、都督石頭水陸軍事。
entries.en: Hua Heng, holding the title specially advanced, was named general of agile cavalry and commander of land and river forces at Stone City.
entries.literal: He appointed Specially Advanced Hua Heng as General of Agile Cavalry, Area Commander-in-Chief of Stone Rampart water and land military affairs.

entries.zh: 乙丑，黃霧四塞。
entries.en: On the yichou day yellow fog closed in on every side.
entries.literal: On yichou yellow fog filled the four directions.

entries.zh: 丙寅，隕霜。
entries.en: Frost fell on the bingyin day.
entries.literal: On bingyin frost fell.

entries.zh: 壬申，又隕霜，殺穀。
entries.en: On renshen frost struck again and blighted the crops.
entries.literal: On renshen again frost fell, killing grain.

entries.zh: 元皇帝諱睿，字景文，宣帝曾孫，琅邪恭王覲之子也。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan, whose personal name was Rui and courtesy name Jingwen, was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan of Jin and the son of Sima Jin, Prince Gong of Langye.
entries.literal: The Emperor Yuan's taboo name was Rui, his courtesy name Jingwen; he was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan and the son of Jin, Prince Gong of Langye.

entries.zh: 咸寧二年生於洛陽，有神光之異，一室盡明，所藉槁如始刈。
entries.en: He was born in Luoyang in 276, amid a strange glow that lit the whole chamber and left the bedding straw looking freshly mown.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xianning he was born in Luoyang; there was a divine radiance anomaly; one room was entirely bright; the straw on which he lay was as if newly cut.

entries.zh: 及長，白豪生於日角之左，隆準龍顏，目有精曜，顧眄煒如也。
entries.en: As a man he bore a white filament beside the auspicious bump on his forehead, the high-bridged "dragon" profile of a ruler, and eyes so bright that every turn of his gaze seemed to flash with light.
entries.literal: When grown, a white hair grew to the left of his sun-corner; high bridge nose and dragon countenance; his eyes had refined brilliance; his glances were radiant.

entries.zh: 年十五，嗣位琅邪王。
entries.en: At fifteen he inherited the title of Prince of Langye.
entries.literal: At age fifteen he succeeded to the position of Prince of Langye.

entries.zh: 幼有令問。
entries.en: Even as a boy he was already known for an excellent name.
entries.literal: In youth he had a fine reputation.

entries.zh: 及惠皇之際，王室多故，帝每恭儉退讓，以免於禍。
entries.en: Under Emperor Hui, when the house of Jin was rocked by one crisis after another, he habitually kept to modesty, frugality, and deference so as to stay clear of disaster.
entries.literal: When it came to the time of Emperor Hui, the royal house had many troubles; the emperor each time was respectful, frugal, yielding, in order to avoid calamity.

entries.zh: 沈敏有度量，不顯灼然之迹，故時人未之識焉。
entries.en: He was steady, astute, and large-minded, yet never advertised his abilities, so his contemporaries failed to see the ruler in him.
entries.literal: Deep and keen, with capacity for tolerance, he did not display glaring traces; therefore people of the time did not recognize him.

entries.zh: 惟侍中嵇紹異之，謂人曰：「琅邪王毛骨非常，殆非人臣之相也。」
entries.en: Only Ji Shao, the palace attendant, saw something different in him and told others, "The Prince of Langye has a presence no ordinary man possesses; that is hardly the look of someone born to serve another."
entries.literal: Only Attendant-in-ordinary Ji Shao thought him strange, saying to people: "The Prince of Langye's bearing is extraordinary; probably it is not the appearance of a subject."

entries.zh: 夏四月癸卯，石季龍寇歷陽，加司徒王導大司馬、假黃鉞、都督征討諸軍事，以禦之。
entries.en: When Shi Hu struck Liyang in the fourth month of summer, Wang Dao was named grand marshal, given the yellow battle-ax, and placed in supreme command of the armies raised to meet him.
entries.literal: Summer, fourth month, day guimao, Shi Jilong raided Liyang; Minister of Education Wang Dao was added Grand Marshal, yellow battle-ax, area commander of all punitive campaign military affairs, in order to resist him.

entries.zh: 癸丑，帝觀兵于廣莫門，分命諸將，遣將軍劉仕救歷陽，平西將軍趙胤屯慈湖，龍驤將軍路永戍牛渚，建武將軍王允之戍蕪湖。
entries.en: On the guichou day the sovereign reviewed the host at Guangmo Gate and issued dispositions: Liu Shi was sent to relieve Liyang, Zhao Yin to hold Cihu, Lu Yong to guard Niuzhu, and Wang Yunzhi to secure Wuhu.
entries.literal: Day guichou, the emperor reviewed troops at Guangmo Gate, separately ordered various generals, sent General Liu Shi to relieve Liyang, General Who Pacifies the West Zhao Yin to encamp at Cihu, Soaring Dragon General Lu Yong to garrison Niuzhu, General Who Establishes Might Wang Yunzhi to garrison Wuhu.

entries.zh: 司空郗鑒使廣陵相陳光帥衆衛京師，賊退向襄陽。
entries.en: Xi Jian, minister of works, ordered Chen Guang of Guangling to march on the capital as a screen, and the invaders drew back toward Xiangyang.
entries.literal: Minister of Works Xi Jian ordered Chancellor of Guangling Chen Guang to lead troops to guard the capital; the bandits retreated toward Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 戊午，解嚴。
entries.en: On the wuwu day the capital stood down from full mobilization.
entries.literal: Day wuwu, martial law was lifted.

entries.zh: 石季龍將石遇寇中廬，南中郎將王國退保襄陽。
entries.en: Shi Yu, serving Shi Hu, struck Zhonglu, and Wang Guo, South Gentlemen of the Household General, fell back to defend Xiangyang.
entries.literal: Shi Jilong's general Shi Yu raided Zhonglu; South Gentlemen of the Household General Wang Guo retreated to protect Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 咸康元年春正月庚午朔，帝加元服，大赦，改元，增文武位一等，大酺三日，賜鰥寡孤獨不能自存者米，人五斛。
entries.en: At the new moon on gengwu in the first month of the Xiankang era the emperor came of age. He proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the new reign title, promoted officials by one rank, ordered three days of public feasting, and gave five hu of grain to every indigent widower, widow, orphan, or solitary without kin.
entries.literal: Xiankang first year, spring, first month, first day gengwu, the emperor added capping robes, great amnesty, changed era name, increased civil and military ranks one grade, great feast three days, granted rice to widowers, widows, orphans, and solitary who could not preserve themselves, five hu per person.

entries.zh: 九月，巴東太守楊謙擊李勢將申陽，走之，獲其將樂高。
entries.en: In the ninth month Yang Qian, prefect of Badong, attacked Shen Yang, a general of Li Shi, drove him off, and took Yue Gao prisoner.
entries.literal: Ninth month, Administrator of Badong Yang Qian struck Li Shi's general Shen Yang, routed him, captured his general Yue Gao.

entries.zh: 丙申，立皇子聃爲皇太子。
entries.en: On the bingshen day the emperor's son Sima Dan was invested as crown prince.
entries.literal: Day bingshen, established imperial son Dan as heir apparent.

entries.zh: 成皇帝諱衍，字世根，明帝長子也。
entries.en: Emperor Cheng, personal name Yan, courtesy name Shigen, was the eldest son of Emperor Ming.
entries.literal: The taboo name of Emperor Cheng was Yan, his courtesy name Shigen, and he was the eldest son of Emperor Ming.

entries.zh: 太寧三年三月戊辰，立爲皇太子。
entries.en: On the wuchen day of the third month in the third year of the Taining era (325 CE), he was invested as crown prince.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taining, third month, day wuchen, he was established as heir apparent.

entries.zh: 閏月戊子，明帝崩。
entries.en: On the wuzi day of the intercalary month, Emperor Ming died.
entries.literal: Intercalary month, day wuzi, Emperor Ming died.

entries.zh: 己丑，太子卽皇帝位，大赦，增文武位二等，賜鰥寡孤老帛，人二匹，尊皇后庾氏爲皇太后。
entries.en: On the jichou day the crown prince ascended the throne. He declared a general amnesty, promoted civil and military officials by two ranks, gave two bolts of silk each to widowers, widows, orphans, and the elderly, and elevated Empress Yu to the title of empress dowager.
entries.literal: Day jichou, the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, a general amnesty was proclaimed, civil and military ranks were raised two grades, widowers, widows, orphans, and the aged were granted silk, two bolts per person, and Empress Yu was honored as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 魏文帝黃初四年三月癸卯，月犯心大星。
entries.en: On guimao in the third month of Huangchu 4 under Emperor Wen of Wei (Cao Pi), the moon transgressed Antares, the bright star of the Heart mansion.
entries.literal: In the third month of the fourth Huangchu year of Emperor Wen of Wei, on the day guimao, the Moon transgressed the great star of the Heart [lodge].

entries.zh: 占曰：「心為天王位，王者惡之。」
entries.en: The prognostication reads: “The Heart asterism marks Heaven’s throne—sovereigns dread such a sign.”
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “The Heart is the seat of the Celestial King; the king finds it ill-omened.

entries.zh: 六月甲申，太白晝見。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on jiashen, Venus appeared in broad daylight.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jiashen, the Great White [Venus] was seen in daytime.

entries.zh: 案劉向《五紀論》曰：「太白少陰，弱，不得專行，故以己未為界，不得經天而行。
entries.en: Examining Liu Xiang’s Treatise on the Five Regulators, it says, "Venus is Lesser Yin; being weak, it cannot travel independently. Therefore it takes jiwei as the boundary and may not cross the sky in its course.
entries.literal: Investigating [this], Liu Xiang’s “Treatise on the Five Regulators” says: “The Great White is Lesser Yin; being weak, it cannot travel alone; therefore with jiwei as the boundary, it must not cross the sky [by day].

entries.zh: 經天則晝見，其占為兵喪，為不臣，為更王；
entries.en: If it crosses the sky, then it appears by day; its prognostication is war and mourning, disloyal ministers, and a changed king;
entries.literal: When it crosses the sky, then it is seen by day; its interpretation is military losses, disloyal subjects, and change of king;

entries.zh: 強國弱，小國強。」
entries.en: strong states become weak, and small states become strong."
entries.literal: strong states weaken, small states strengthen.

entries.zh: 是時孫權受魏爵號，而稱兵距守。
entries.en: Sun Quan had accepted Wei’s patent of nobility yet still mobilized armies and stood on the defensive.
entries.literal: At this time Sun Quan accepted titles from Wei, yet raised troops and held out on the defensive.

entries.zh: 其十二月丙子，月犯心大星。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on bingzi, the moon again crossed Antares in the Heart.
entries.literal: That twelfth month, on the day bingzi, the Moon transgressed the great star of the Heart.

entries.zh: 占同上。
entries.en: The diviners cited the same gloss as above.
entries.literal: The interpretation is the same as above.

entries.zh: 五年十月乙卯，太白晝見。
entries.en: In the tenth month of Huangchu 5, on yimao, Venus appeared in daylight.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, tenth month, on the day yimao, the Great White was seen in daytime.

entries.zh: 占同上。
entries.en: The prognostication matched the foregoing.
entries.literal: The interpretation is the same as above.

entries.zh: 又歲星入太微逆行，積百四十九日乃出。
entries.en: Jupiter also entered the Supreme Palace and traced a retrograde arc, lingering one hundred forty-nine days before departing.
entries.literal: Moreover the Year Star [Jupiter] entered the Supreme Palace enclosure and moved retrograde; it accumulated one hundred forty-nine days there before emerging.

entries.zh: 占曰：「五星入太微，從右入三十日以上，人主有大憂。」
entries.en: The gloss runs: “If the five planets enter the Supreme Palace from the right and remain upward of thirty days, the sovereign faces grave distress.”
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “When the Five Planets enter the Supreme Palace, entering from the right and staying thirty days or more, the ruler has great sorrow.

entries.zh: 一曰：「有赦至。」
entries.en: A variant reading adds: “A general amnesty is coming.”
entries.literal: Another saying: “An amnesty will arrive.

entries.zh: 七年五月，帝崩，明帝即位，大赦天下。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the seventh year the emperor died; Emperor Ming took the throne and issued an empire-wide amnesty.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year the emperor died; Emperor Ming succeeded and proclaimed a great amnesty for all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 六年五月壬戌，熒惑入太微，至壬申，興歲星相及，俱犯右執法，至癸酉乃出。
entries.en: On renxu in the fifth month of the sixth year Mars entered the Supreme Palace; by renshen it had closed with Jupiter, both crossing the Right Enforcer asterism, and they exited on guiyou.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, fifth month, on the day renxu, Spark-Delight [Mars] entered the Supreme Palace; by renshen it came together with the Year Star [Jupiter], both transgressing the Right Enforcer; on guiyou they emerged.

entries.zh: 占曰：「從右入三十日以上，人主有大憂。」
entries.en: The interpretation states: “Remaining from the right beyond thirty days brings great sorrow to the sovereign.”
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “Entering from the right and staying thirty days or more, the ruler has great sorrow.

entries.zh: 又曰：「月、五星犯左右執法，大臣有憂。」
entries.en: It also said, "When the moon or the five planets trespass against the Left or Right Enforcer, great ministers will have anxiety."
entries.literal: It also says: “When the Moon or the Five Planets transgress the Left or Right Enforcer, great ministers have sorrow.

entries.zh: 一曰：「執法者誅，金、火尤甚。」
entries.en: A further gloss adds that “execution reaches the officials who ‘enforce the law,’ worst when Venus or Mars is involved.”
entries.literal: Another saying: “The enforcers are executed; metal and fire [planets] make it especially severe.

entries.zh: 十一月，皇子東武陽王鑒薨。
entries.en: In the eleventh month the imperial son, Prince Jian of Dongwuyang, passed away.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month the imperial son, Prince Jian of Dongwuyang, died.

entries.zh: 七年正月，驃騎將軍曹洪免為庶人。
entries.en: The following first month General of Agile Cavalry Cao Hong was stripped of rank and reduced to common status.
entries.literal: In the first month of the seventh year Cao Hong, General of Agile Cavalry, was dismissed and made a commoner.

entries.zh: 四月，征南大將軍夏侯尚薨。
entries.en: In the fourth month Xiahou Shang, general who conquered the south, died.
entries.literal: In the fourth month Xiahou Shang, General Who Conquers the South, died.

entries.zh: 五月，帝崩。
entries.en: In the fifth month the emperor died.
entries.literal: In the fifth month the emperor died.

entries.zh: 《蜀記》稱明帝問黃權曰：「天下鼎立，何地為正？」
entries.en: The Records of Shu says that Emperor Ming asked Huang Quan, "With the realm standing like a tripod, which land is legitimate?"
entries.literal: The “Records of Shu” relates that Emperor Ming asked Huang Quan: “The realm stands tripod-wise—which region holds the true legitimacy?

entries.zh: 對曰：「當驗天文。
entries.en: Quan replied, "It should be verified by celestial patterns.
entries.literal: He replied: “One must verify it against astronomy.

entries.zh: 往者熒惑守心而文帝崩，吳、蜀無事，此其徵也。」
entries.en: Formerly Mars guarded Heart and Emperor Wen collapsed, while Wu and Shu had no incident; this is the proof."
entries.literal: Formerly Spark-Delight stationed at the Heart and Emperor Wen died, yet Wu and Shu were untroubled—this was its proof.

entries.zh: 案三國史並無熒惑守心之文，疑是入太微。
entries.en: Scrutiny shows none of the Three Kingdoms annals records Mars ‘stationing at the Heart’; the event was probably entry into the Supreme Palace.
entries.literal: Investigating the histories of the three states, there is no text of Spark-Delight stationing at the Heart; it is suspected that [the planet] entered the Supreme Palace.

entries.zh: 八月，吳遂圍江夏，寇襄陽，大將軍宣帝救襄陽，斬吳將張霸等，兵喪更王之應也。
entries.en: In the eighth month Wu besieged Jiangxia and struck Xiangyang; General-in-Chief Xuandi (Sima Yi) rescued Xiangyang and slew Wu generals such as Zhang Ba, matching the omens of war, mourning, and shifting sovereignty.
entries.literal: In the eighth month Wu then besieged Jiangxia, raided Xiangyang, and Grand Marshal Xuandi relieved Xiangyang, beheading Wu generals including Zhang Ba—the response of military losses and change of ruler.

entries.zh: 少帝正始元年四月戊午，月犯昴東頭第一星。
entries.en: On wuwu in the fourth month of Zhengshi 1 of the Young Emperor the moon clipped the easternmost star of the Hairy Head.
entries.literal: On wuwu in the fourth month of Zhengshi 1 of the Young Emperor the Moon transgressed the first star at the eastern end of the Hairy Head [Pleiades region].

entries.zh: 十月庚寅，月又犯昴北斗四星。
entries.en: On gengyin in the tenth month the moon transited both the Hairy Head and four stars of the Northern Dipper.
entries.literal: On gengyin in the tenth month the Moon again transgressed the Hairy Head and the four stars of the Northern Dipper.

entries.zh: 占曰：「月犯昴，胡不安。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "When the moon trespasses against Mao, the Hu will be unsettled."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “When the Moon transgresses the Hairy Head, the Hu are restless.

entries.zh: 二年六月，鮮卑阿妙兒等寇西方，敦煌太守王延破之，斬二萬餘級。
entries.en: In the second year’s sixth month Xianbei bands led by Amiao’er struck the western marches; Dunhuang prefect Wang Yan routed them, claiming over twenty thousand heads.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the second year Xianbei under Amiao’er and others raided the west; prefect Wang Yan of Dunhuang defeated them and beheaded more than twenty thousand.

entries.zh: 三年，又斬鮮卑大師及千餘級。
entries.en: The third year saw another victory that took the Xianbei commander’s head plus more than a thousand others.
entries.literal: In the third year another campaign severed the Xianbei commander’s head and over a thousand others.

entries.zh: 二年九月癸酉，月犯輿鬼西北星。
entries.en: On guiyou in the second year’s ninth month the moon crossed the Ghosts’ northwest star.
entries.literal: On guiyou in the ninth month of the second year the Moon transgressed the northwest star of the Ghosts.

entries.zh: 三年二月丁未，又犯西南星。
entries.en: On dingwei in the third year’s second month it struck the Ghosts’ southwest star.
entries.literal: On dingwei in the third year’s second month it again transgressed the southwest star.

entries.zh: 占曰：「有錢令。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "There will be a money ordinance."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be an ordinance on coinage.

entries.zh: 一曰：「大臣憂。」
entries.en: A variant gloss adds: “High ministers face peril.”
entries.literal: Another saying: “Great ministers will suffer.

entries.zh: 三年三月，太尉滿寵薨。
entries.en: Grand Commandant Man Chong died in the third month of the third year.
entries.literal: In the third month of the third year Grand Commandant Man Chong died.

entries.zh: 四年正月，帝加元服，賜群臣錢各有差。
entries.en: The fourth year’s first month saw the emperor’s capping ceremony and graded cash gifts to his officials.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the emperor assumed the capping [adult rite] and bestowed cash on the various ministers in graded amounts.

entries.zh: 四年十月、十一月，月再犯井鉞。
entries.en: During the fourth year’s tenth and eleventh months the moon crossed the Well’s axe twice.
entries.literal: In the tenth and eleventh months of the fourth year the Moon twice transgressed the Well’s Battle-Axe.

entries.zh: 是月，宣帝討諸葛恪，恪棄城走。
entries.en: That month Xuandi attacked Zhuge Ke, who deserted his walls and ran.
entries.literal: That same month Xuandi campaigned against Zhuge Ke, who abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 五年二月，曹爽征蜀。
entries.en: Cao Shuang led a Shu expedition in the fifth year’s second month.
entries.literal: In the second month of the fifth year Cao Shuang campaigned against Shu.

entries.zh: 五年十一月癸巳，填星犯亢距星。
entries.en: On guisi in the fifth year’s eleventh month Saturn crossed the Neck’s separator stars.
entries.literal: On guisi in the eleventh month of the fifth year the Station Star transgressed the separator stars of the Neck [lodge].

entries.zh: 占曰：「諸侯有失國者。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "Among the feudal lords there will be one who loses his state."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “Among the feudal lords there will be one who loses his state.

entries.zh: 七年七月丁丑，月犯左角。
entries.en: On dingchou in the seventh year’s seventh month the moon crossed the Horn’s left horn-star.
entries.literal: On dingchou in the seventh month of the seventh year the Moon transgressed the left horn [of the Horn lodge].

entries.zh: 占曰：「天下有兵，左將軍死。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "There will be war under Heaven, and the Left General will die."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “Under Heaven there will be soldiers; the general of the left will die.

entries.zh: 七月乙亥，熒惑犯畢距星。
entries.en: On yihai in the seventh month Mars crossed the Net’s separator star.
entries.literal: On yihai in the seventh month Spark-Delight transgressed the separator star of the Net.

entries.zh: 占曰；
entries.en: The prognostication reads:
entries.literal: The omen-text says:

entries.zh: 「有邊兵。」
entries.en: "There will be frontier troops."
entries.literal: There will be troops on the frontier.

entries.zh: 一曰：「刑罰用。」
entries.en: One reading said, "Punishments will be used."
entries.literal: Another saying: “Punishments will be applied.

entries.zh: 九年正月辛亥，月犯亢南星。
entries.en: On xinhai in the ninth year’s first month the moon crossed the Neck’s southern star.
entries.literal: On xinhai in the first month of the ninth year the Moon transgressed the southern star of the Neck.

entries.zh: 占曰：「兵起。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "War will arise."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “Arms will arise.

entries.zh: 一曰：「將軍死。」
entries.en: One reading said, "The general will die."
entries.literal: Another saying: “A general will die.

entries.zh: 七月癸丑，填星犯楗閉。
entries.en: On guichou in the seventh month Saturn crossed Key-and-Bolt.
entries.literal: On guichou in the seventh month the Station Star transgressed Key-and-Bolt.

entries.zh: 占曰：「王者不宜出宮下殿。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "The king should not leave the palace or descend from the hall."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “The king should not leave the palace or descend the hall.

entries.zh: 嘉平元年，天子謁陵，宣帝奏誅曹爽等。
entries.en: Jiaping 1 saw the emperor tend the tombs while Xuandi procured orders to purge Cao Shuang’s faction.
entries.literal: In the first Jiaping year the Son of Heaven visited the imperial tombs; Xuandi memorialized to execute Cao Shuang and his party.

entries.zh: 天子野宿，於是失勢。
entries.en: Forced to camp outside the capital, the emperor forfeited real power.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven lodged in the field encampment; thereby he lost authority.

entries.zh: 惠帝元康三年四月，熒惑守太微六十日。
entries.en: Emperor Hui’s Yuan-kang 3 fourth month held Mars sixty days inside the Supreme Palace.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of Yuan-kang 3 of Emperor Hui Spark-Delight stationed in the Supreme Palace for sixty days.

entries.zh: 占曰：「諸侯三公謀其上，必有斬臣。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "Feudal lords and the Three Dukes plot against their superior; there will certainly be ministers who are beheaded."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “Marquises and the Three Dukes plot against their ruler; there must be executed ministers.

entries.zh: 一曰：「天子亡國。」
entries.en: One reading said, "The Son of Heaven loses the state."
entries.literal: Another saying: “The Son of Heaven loses his state.

entries.zh: 是春太白守畢，至是百餘日。
entries.en: The same spring Venus lodged in the Net for over a hundred days.
entries.literal: That spring the Great White stationed at the Net, and by then it had remained more than a hundred days.

entries.zh: 占曰：「有急令之憂。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "There will be anxiety from urgent ordinances."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be fear of sudden edicts.

entries.zh: 一曰：「相死。」
entries.en: One reading said, "The chancellor will die."
entries.literal: Another saying: “The minister will die.

entries.zh: 又為邊境不安。
entries.en: It further signals disturbed borders.
entries.literal: It also means uneasy frontiers.

entries.zh: 後賈后陷殺太子。
entries.en: Empress Jia later destroyed the crown prince by false accusation.
entries.literal: Afterward Empress Jia framed and murdered the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 六年十月乙未，太白晝見。
entries.en: On yiwei in the sixth year’s tenth month Venus appeared by daylight.
entries.literal: On yiwei in the tenth month of the sixth year the Great White was seen in daytime.

entries.zh: 九年六月，熒惑守心。
entries.en: The ninth year’s sixth month again placed Mars on the Heart.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year Spark-Delight stationed at the Heart.

entries.zh: 占曰：「王者惡之。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "The king hates it."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “The king finds it ill-omened.

entries.zh: 八月，熒惑入羽林。
entries.en: That August Mars entered the imperial guard stars.
entries.literal: In the eighth month Spark-Delight entered the Forbidden Guards asterism.

entries.zh: 占曰：「禁兵大起。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "The palace troops will greatly rise."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “Palace troops will rise in force.

entries.zh: 其後，帝見廢為太上皇，俄而三王起兵討趙王倫，倫悉遣中軍兵相距累月。
entries.en: The emperor was soon reduced to Retired Emperor; then the three princes rose against Sima Lun, who threw the central corps against them for months.
entries.literal: Thereafter the emperor was deposed as Retired Emperor; presently the Three Princes raised troops against Prince Zhao Lun, who dispatched the central army to oppose them for months on end.

entries.zh: 永康元年三月，中台星坼，太白晝見。
entries.en: Yongkang 1’s third month saw the asterism of the high ministers fracture while Venus shone in daylight.
entries.literal: In the third month of Yongkang 1 the central terrace stars split, and the Great White appeared by day.

entries.zh: 占曰：「台星失常，三公憂。
entries.en: The prognostication said, "When the Terrace Stars lose their norm, the Three Dukes will have anxiety.
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “When terrace stars lose their norm, the Three Dukes grieve.

entries.zh: 太白晝見，為不臣。」
entries.en: When Venus appears by day, it means disloyal ministers."
entries.literal: The Great White seen by daylight means disloyal subjects.

entries.zh: 是月，賈后殺太子，趙王倫尋廢殺後，斬司空張華。
entries.en: That month Empress Jia slew the heir; Sima Lun rapidly ousted and killed her and executed Zhang Hua.
entries.literal: That month Empress Jia killed the heir apparent; Prince Zhao Lun soon deposed and murdered the empress and beheaded Minister of Works Zhang Hua.

entries.zh: 其五月，熒惑入南斗。
entries.en: The fifth month brought Mars into the Southern Dipper.
entries.literal: That fifth month Spark-Delight entered the Southern Dipper.

entries.zh: 占曰：「宰相死，兵大起。
entries.en: The prognostication said, "The chancellor will die, and war will greatly arise.
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “The chief minister will die; troops rise on a grand scale.

entries.zh: 斗，又吳分野。」
entries.en: Dipper is also Wu’s allotment."
entries.literal: The Dipper also marks Wu’s celestial field.

entries.zh: 是時，趙王倫為相，明年，篡位，三王興師誅之。
entries.en: Sima Lun held the premiership, seized the throne the following year, then fell to princely coalitions.
entries.literal: At that time Prince Zhao Lun was chancellor; the next year he usurped the throne, and princes raised armies and executed him.

entries.zh: 太安二年，石冰破揚州。
entries.en: Tai’an 2 saw Shi Bing overrun Yangzhou.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tai’an Shi Bing captured Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 其八月，熒惑入箕。
entries.en: That August Mars entered the Winnowing Basket.
entries.literal: That eighth month Spark-Delight entered the Winnowing Basket.

entries.zh: 占曰：「人主失位，兵起。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "The ruler of men loses his position, and war arises."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “The ruler loses his throne; troops arise.

entries.zh: 明年趙王倫篡位，改元。
entries.en: The following year Sima Lun seized the throne and altered the reign title.
entries.literal: The next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne and changed the era name.

entries.zh: 二年二月，太白出西方，逆行入東井。
entries.en: The second year’s second month brought Venus out in the west, retrograding into the Eastern Well.
entries.literal: In the second month of the second year the Great White emerged in the west and moved retrograde into the Eastern Well.

entries.zh: 占曰：「國失政，大臣為亂。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "The state loses its government, and great ministers make disorder."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “The state loses good government; great ministers make rebellion.

entries.zh: 是時，齊王冏起兵討趙王倫，倫滅，冏擁兵不朝，專權淫奢，明年，誅死。
entries.en: Prince Qi’s coalition destroyed Lun, yet Jiong quartered troops outside the capital, ruled tyrannically, and was killed the next year.
entries.literal: At that time Prince Qi Jiong raised troops against Prince Zhao Lun; Lun was destroyed, but Jiong kept his army from court, monopolized power, and indulged in arrogance and luxury; the next year he was executed.

entries.zh: 少帝正始元年十月乙酉，彗星見西方，在尾，長三丈，拂牽牛，犯太白。
entries.en: Wei Zhengshi comet in Tail.
entries.literal: On yiyou in the tenth month of Zhengshi 1 of Shaodi a comet appeared in the west at Tail three zhang long, brushing the Herdsman and transgressing the Great White.

entries.zh: 十一月甲子，進犯羽林。
entries.en: November comet entered Forbidden Guards.
entries.literal: On jiazi in the eleventh month it advanced to strike the Forbidden Guards.

entries.zh: 占曰：「尾為燕，又為吳，牛亦吳越之分。
entries.en: The prognostication said, "Tail is Yan and also Wu, and Ox is also the allotment of Wu-Yue.
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “Tail is Yan and also Wu; Ox likewise marks Wu-Yue.

entries.zh: 太白為上將，羽林中軍兵。
entries.en: Venus is the supreme general, and the Feathered Forest is the central army.
entries.literal: The Great White is the upper general; Forbidden Guards are central troops.

entries.zh: 為吳越有喪，中軍兵動。」
entries.en: It means Wu-Yue will have mourning, and the central army will move."
entries.literal: Wu-Yue will mourn while central armies stir.

entries.zh: 二年五月，吳遣三將寇邊。
entries.en: Year two May Wu raided borders.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the second year Wu dispatched three generals to raid the frontier.

entries.zh: 吳太子登卒。
entries.en: Wu heir Deng died.
entries.literal: Crown Prince Deng of Wu died.

entries.zh: 六月，宣帝討諸葛恪於皖。
entries.en: June Sima Yi attacked Zhuge Ke.
entries.literal: In the sixth month Xuandi campaigned against Zhuge Ke at Wan.

entries.zh: 太尉滿寵薨。
entries.en: Man Chong, Grand Commandant, passed away.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant Man Chong died.

entries.zh: 六年八月戊午，彗星見七星，長二尺，色白，進至張，積二十三日滅。
entries.en: Zhengshi 6 eighth month: comet in the Seven Stars.
entries.literal: On wuwu in the sixth year’s eighth month a comet appeared in the Seven Stars two feet long, white, advancing to Zhang, vanishing after twenty-three days.

entries.zh: 七年十一月癸亥，又見軫，長一尺，積百五十六日滅。
entries.en: Seventh year November comet in Chariot.
entries.literal: On guihai in the eleventh month of the seventh year it again appeared in the Chariot one foot long, lasting 156 days.

entries.zh: 九年三月，又見昴，長六尺，色青白，芒西南指。
entries.en: Ninth year third month comet in Mao.
entries.literal: In the third month of the ninth year it again appeared in the Hairy Head six feet long, bluish white, tail pointing southwest.

entries.zh: 七月，又見翼，長二尺，進至軫，積四十二日滅。
entries.en: July comet Wings to Chariot.
entries.literal: In the seventh month it again appeared in Wings two feet long, reaching the Chariot, disappearing after forty-two days.

entries.zh: 案占曰：「七星張為周分野，翼軫為楚，昴為趙魏。
entries.en: Examining the prognostication, it said, "Seven Stars and Extended Net are the allotment of Zhou; Wings and Chariot are Chu; Mao is Zhao and Wei.
entries.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Seven Stars and Zhang are Zhou’s field; Wings and Chariot are Chu; Mao is Zhao and Wei.

entries.zh: 彗所以除舊布新，主兵喪也。」
entries.en: Comets are how the old is removed and the new spread; they govern war and mourning."
entries.literal: Comets purge old and spread new; they preside over armies and mourning.

entries.zh: 嘉平元年，宣帝誅曹爽兄弟及其党與，皆夷三族，京師嚴兵。
entries.en: Jiaping 1 Sima Yi purged Cao Shuang.
entries.literal: In Jiaping 1 Xuandi executed Cao Shuang’s brothers and faction to the third kin, tightening arms at the capital.

entries.zh: 三年，誅楚王彪，又襲王淩於淮南。
entries.en: Year three killed Cao Biao and crushed Wang Ling.
entries.literal: In the third year he executed Prince Chu Biao and struck Wang Ling in Huainan.

entries.zh: 淮南，東楚也。
entries.en: Huainan matches Chu.
entries.literal: Huainan is eastern Chu.

entries.zh: 魏諸王幽於鄴。
entries.en: Wei imperial kin were caged at Ye.
entries.literal: Wei princes were confined at Ye.

entries.zh: 太熙元年四月，客星在紫宮。
entries.en: Taixi 1 April guest star in Purple Palace.
entries.literal: In Taixi 1 fourth month a guest star stood in Purple Forbidden.

entries.zh: 占曰：「為兵喪。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "It means war and mourning."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “There will be armies and mourning.

entries.zh: 太康未，武帝耽宴遊，多疾病。
entries.en: Late Taikang Wu feasted into illness.
entries.literal: Near Taikang’s end Emperor Wu indulged feasting and fell chronically ill.

entries.zh: 是月己酉，帝崩。
entries.en: Jiyou that month ended Emperor Wu.
entries.literal: That month on jiyou the emperor died.

entries.zh: 永平元年，賈后誅楊駿及其黨與，皆夷三族，楊太后亦見弑。
entries.en: Yongping purge slew Yang clan.
entries.literal: In Yongping 1 Empress Jia executed Yang Jun and faction to third kin—even Empress Dowager Yang was murdered.

entries.zh: 又誅汝南王亮、太保衛瓘、楚王瑋，王室兵喪之應也。
entries.en: Further kin slaughter followed.
entries.literal: She also killed Prince Runan Liang, Grand Guardian Wei Guan, Prince Chu Wei—responses of martial mourning for the royal house.

entries.zh: 惠帝元康五年四月，有星孛於奎，至軒轅、太微，經三台、太陵。
entries.en: Yuan-kang 5 comet crossed capital stars.
entries.literal: In Yuan-kang 5 fourth month a broom star appeared in Striding Legs reaching Chariot and Supreme Palace crossing Three Steps and Great Mound.

entries.zh: 占曰：「奎為魯，又為庫兵，軒轅為後宮，太微天子庭，三台為三司，太陵有積尸死喪之事。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "Legs is Lu and also arsenal troops; Xuanyuan is the rear palace; the Supreme Palace is the Son of Heaven’s court; the Three Terraces are the Three Offices; Great Mound has affairs of piled corpses, death, and mourning."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “Striding Legs is Lu and armory stores; Chariot Shaft is harem; Supreme Palace the court; Three Steps the Three Dukes; Great Mound holds piled corpses and death.

entries.zh: 其後武庫火，西羌反。
entries.en: Armory fire and Qiang revolt.
entries.literal: Afterward the arsenal burned and Qiang rebelled west.

entries.zh: 後五年，司空張華遇禍，賈后廢死，魯公賈謐誅。
entries.en: Later Zhang Hua and Jia clan fell.
entries.literal: Five years later Minister of Works Zhang Hua met disaster; Empress Jia was deposed and killed; Duke Lu Jia Mi executed.

entries.zh: 又明年，趙王倫篡位。
entries.en: Next year Sima Lun seized throne.
entries.literal: The next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped.

entries.zh: 於是三王興兵討倫，兵士戰死十餘萬人。
entries.en: Princely coalition slaughtered tens of thousands.
entries.literal: Then the Three Princes rose against Lun—over a hundred thousand soldiers died.

entries.zh: 永康元年三月，妖星見南方。
entries.en: Yongkang 1 March southern astral demon.
entries.literal: In Yongkang 1 third month an evil star appeared in the south.

entries.zh: 占曰：「妖星出，天下大兵將起。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "When a baleful star emerges, great war under Heaven is about to arise."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “When evil stars emerge great armies will arise.

entries.zh: 是月賈后殺太子，趙王倫尋廢殺后，斬司空張華，又廢帝自立。
entries.en: Jia killed heir; Lun purged court.
entries.literal: That month Empress Jia killed the heir; Prince Zhao Lun soon deposed and murdered her, executed Zhang Hua, and enthroned himself.

entries.zh: 於是三王並起，迭總天權。
entries.en: Princes vied for power.
entries.literal: Then three princes rose, trading supreme authority.

entries.zh: 其十二月，彗星出牽牛之西，指天市。
entries.en: December comet Herdsman to market.
entries.literal: That twelfth month a comet emerged west of Herdsman pointing at Celestial Market.

entries.zh: 占曰：「牛者七政始，彗出之，改元易號之象也。
entries.en: The prognostication said, "Ox is the beginning of the seven regulators; when a comet emerges from it, it is the image of changing the era and altering the title.
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “Ox begins the seven regulators; a comet there means changing era and reign title.

entries.zh: 天市一名天府，一名天子旗，帝坐在其中。」
entries.en: The Celestial Market is also called the Celestial Treasury and also the Son of Heaven’s Banner; the imperial seat is within it."
entries.literal: Celestial Market is also called Celestial Treasury and Son of Heaven’s banner—the throne sits within.

entries.zh: 明年，趙王倫篡位，改元，尋為大兵所滅。
entries.en: Lun’s coup collapsed.
entries.literal: The next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped, changed the era, then fell to great armies.

entries.zh: 二年四月，彗星見齊分。
entries.en: Year two April Qi comet.
entries.literal: In the second year’s fourth month a comet appeared in Qi field.

entries.zh: 占曰：「齊有兵喪。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "Qi will have war and mourning."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “Qi will suffer armies and mourning.

entries.zh: 是時，齊王冏起兵討趙王倫。
entries.en: Qi prince attacked Lun.
entries.literal: Then Prince Qi Jiong rose against Prince Zhao Lun.

entries.zh: 倫滅，冏擁兵不朝，專權淫奢。
entries.en: Jiong tyrannized Luoyang.
entries.literal: After Lun fell Jiong kept armies outside court, monopolizing power in arrogance and luxury.

entries.zh: 明年，誅死。
entries.en: Jiong executed next year.
entries.literal: The next year he was executed.

entries.zh: 太安元年四月，彗星晝見。
entries.en: Tai’an 1 April daytime comet.
entries.literal: In Tai’an 1 fourth month a comet appeared by day.

entries.zh: 二年三月，彗星見東方，指三台。
entries.en: Tai’an 2 March eastern comet.
entries.literal: In Tai’an 2 third month a comet appeared in the east pointing at Three Steps.

entries.zh: 占曰：「兵喪之象。
entries.en: The prognostication said, "It is the image of war and mourning.
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “Image of armies and mourning.

entries.zh: 三台為三公。」
entries.en: The Three Terraces are the Three Dukes."
entries.literal: Three Steps mean Three Dukes.

entries.zh: 三年正月，東海王越執太尉、長沙王乂，張方又殺之。
entries.en: Yue arrested Yi; Fang killed him.
entries.literal: In the third year’s first month Prince Donghai Yue seized Grand Commandant Prince Changsha Yi and Zhang Fang murdered him.

entries.zh: 魏明帝景初二年，宣帝圍公孫文懿于襄平。
entries.en: In the second year of Jingchu under Emperor Ming of Wei, Sima Yi besieged Gongsun Yuan at Xiangping.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jingchu under Emperor Ming of Wei, Emperor Xuan besieged Gongsun Yuan at Xiangping.

entries.zh: 八月丙寅夜，有大流星長數十丈，白色有芒鬣，從首山東北流，墜襄平城東南。
entries.en: On the night of bingyin in the eighth month, a great meteor tens of zhang long, white with a bristled tail, streamed northeast from Mount Shou and fell southeast of the city of Xiangping.
entries.literal: On bingyin night in the eighth month a great meteor tens of zhang long, white with a maned tail, flowed northeast from Mount Shou and fell southeast of Xiangping city.

entries.zh: 占曰：「圍城而有流星來走城上及墜城中者破。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "When a city is besieged and a meteor comes and runs above the city or falls within the city, it is broken."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “When besieging a city, meteors flying onto the walls or inside mean the city breaks.

entries.zh: 又曰：「星墜，當其下有戰場。」
entries.en: It also said, "When a star falls, beneath it there will be a battlefield."
entries.literal: It also says: “Where stars fall becomes a battlefield.

entries.zh: 又曰：「凡星所墜，國易姓。」
entries.en: It also said, "Wherever a star falls, the state changes surnames."
entries.literal: It also says: “Whatever land stars fall upon changes surname.

entries.zh: 九月，文懿突圍走，至星墜所被斬，屠城，坑其眾。
entries.en: In the ninth month Wenyi broke out of the siege, fled to where the star had fallen, and was beheaded; the city was slaughtered and his multitude buried alive.
entries.literal: In September Yuan broke out, fled to the fall site, was beheaded, the city slaughtered and buried alive.

entries.zh: 武帝泰始四年七月，星隕如雨，皆西流。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu, stars fell like rain, all streaming westward.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu, stars fell like rain, all streaming westward.

entries.zh: 占曰：「星隕為百姓叛。
entries.en: The prognostication said, "Falling stars mean the common people rebel.
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “Star falls mean commoners rebel.

entries.zh: 西流，吳人歸晉之象也。」
entries.en: Flowing west is the image of the people of Wu returning to Jin."
entries.literal: Westward flow meant Wu men submitting to Jin.

entries.zh: 二年，吳夏口督孫秀率部曲二千餘人來降。
entries.en: Sun Xiu defected to Jin.
entries.literal: In the second year Wu’s Xiakou commander Sun Xiu led more than two thousand retainers (buqu) to defect.

entries.zh: 惠帝元康四年九月甲午，枉矢東北行，竟天。
entries.en: On jiawu in the ninth month of the fourth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui, Crooked Arrow crossed the sky to the northeast.
entries.literal: On jiawu in the ninth month of the fourth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui, Crooked Arrow streaked northeast across the whole sky.

entries.zh: 六年六月丙午夜，有枉矢自斗魁東南行。
entries.en: Sixth year Crooked Arrow from Dipper.
entries.literal: On bingwu midnight in the sixth year Crooked Arrow issued from Dipper handle southeastward.

entries.zh: 案占曰：「以亂伐亂。
entries.en: Examining the prognostication, it said, "Using disorder to attack disorder.
entries.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Chaos attacks chaos.

entries.zh: 北斗主執殺，出斗魁，居中執殺者，不直之象也。」
entries.en: Northern Dipper governs holding and killing; when it emerges from the bowl of Dipper and the one who holds and kills occupies the center, it is the image of injustice."
entries.literal: The Northern Dipper governs holding and killing; emerging from the Dipper bowl, the one who holds and kills occupying the center, is the image of injustice.

entries.zh: 是後，趙王殺張、裴，廢賈后，以理太子之冤，因自篡盜，以至屠滅，以亂伐亂之應也。
entries.en: Sima Lun’s purge mirrored omen.
entries.literal: Afterward Prince Zhao slew Zhang and Pei, deposed Empress Jia to redress the heir—then seized power himself until extinction—chaos answering chaos.

entries.zh: 一曰，氐帥齊萬年反之應也。
entries.en: Alternate gloss: Qi Wannian.
entries.literal: Another reading ties it to Di chieftain Qi Wannian’s rebellion.

entries.zh: 懷帝永嘉元年九月辛卯，有大星如日，自西南流于東北，小者如斗，相隨，天盡赤，聲如雷。
entries.en: On xinmao in the ninth month of the first year of Yongjia under Emperor Huai, a giant bolide crossed from southwest to northeast, followed by smaller dipper-sized stars, with the whole sky red and thunderous.
entries.literal: On xinmao in the ninth month of the first year of Yongjia under Emperor Huai, a great star as bright as the sun streamed from southwest to northeast; lesser stars like dippers followed it, the sky turned entirely red, and the sound was like thunder.

entries.zh: 占曰：「流星為貴使，星大者使大。」
entries.en: The prognostication said, "A meteor is a noble envoy; when the star is large, the envoy is great."
entries.literal: The omen-text says: “Meteors are noble envoys—great stars mean great envoys.

entries.zh: 是年五月，汲桑殺東燕王騰，遂據河北。
entries.en: Ji Sang killed Sima Teng.
entries.literal: That May Ji Sang killed Prince Teng of Eastern Yan and seized Hebei.

entries.zh: 十一月，始遣和郁為征北將軍，鎮鄴西。
entries.en: Court posted He Yu north.
entries.literal: In November He Yu first dispatched north as general—stationed west of Ye.

entries.zh: 田甄等大破汲桑，斬于樂陵。
entries.en: Tian Zhen slew Ji Sang.
entries.literal: Tian Zhen crushed Ji Sang at Leling.

entries.zh: 於是以甄為汲郡太守，弟蘭钜鹿太守。
entries.en: Zhen brothers rewarded.
entries.literal: Zhen became Ji Administrator and brother Lan Julu prefect.

entries.zh: 小星相隨者，小將別帥之象也。
entries.en: Small meteors minor leaders.
entries.literal: Lesser stars following meant lesser commanders’ omens.

entries.zh: 司馬越忿魏郡以東平原以南皆党于桑，以賞甄等，於是侵掠赤地。
entries.en: Sima Yue, angry that the lands east of Wei commandery and south of Pingyuan had sided with Sang, used rewards to Zhen and then raided until the ground was scorched.
entries.literal: Sima Yue resented Wei commandery east of Wei plain south allying with Sang—rewarded Zhen—then raided until land scorched.

entries.zh: 有聲如雷，忿怒之象也。
entries.en: Thunder meant wrath.
entries.literal: Thunder noise signified rage.

entries.zh: 四年十月庚子，大星西北墜，有聲。
entries.en: Fourth year giant meteor.
entries.literal: On gengzi in the fourth year’s tenth month a great star fell northwest with noise.

entries.zh: 尋而帝蒙塵於平陽。
entries.en: Emperor captured at Pingyang.
entries.literal: Soon the emperor suffered shame at Pingyang.

entries.zh: 月五星犯列舍經星變附見
entries.en: The Moon and the Five Planets Transgressing the Lodges and Classical Stars, with Supplementary Notes on Celestial Portents.
entries.literal: Transgressions of the Moon and the Five Planets against the Lodges and Classical Stars; appended observations on anomalies.

entries.zh: 昔者元胎無象，太素流形，對越在天，以爲元首，則記所謂冬居營窟，夏居橧巢，飲血茹毛，未有麻絲者也。
entries.en: In the earliest age, before form coalesced from undivided simplicity, people already looked toward heaven as their sovereign; the old annals picture them wintering in earthen dens, summering in treetop huts, living on raw flesh and blood, long before cloth ever softened their lives.
entries.literal: In antiquity the primordial embryo had no image; Grand Simplicity flowed into forms; facing and answering what is on high, they took it as the supreme head—then the records say they dwelt in burrows in winter and nests in summer, drank blood and ate fur, and had not yet hemp or silk.

entries.zh: 及燧人鑽火，庖犧出震，風宗下武，炎胤昌基，畫野無聞，其歸一揆。
entries.en: Then Suiren struck fire from wood, Fuxi rose in the east like thunder, wind and flame passed their line down to martial kings, and the royal house widened its base; we hear nothing yet of surveying fields into squares, but every step still aimed at the same single standard of rule.
entries.literal: When Suiren drilled fire, Paoxi emerged in the Zhen (east) trigram; the Feng lineage descended to the martial kings, and the Yan heirs broadened the foundation; dividing the wilds is not heard of—their return is one measure.

entries.zh: 黃帝則東海南江，登空躡岱，至於崑峰振轡，崆山訪道，[1]存諸汗竹，不可厚誣。
entries.en: The Yellow Emperor pressed east to the sea and south along the great streams, climbed Kongsang and crossed Mount Tai, climbed Kunlun to tighten his reins and sought the Way on Kongshan; the fact is inked on bamboo that has soaked in human sweat, and it would be perverse to dismiss it as mere legend.
entries.literal: As for the Yellow Emperor: east to the sea, south to the great rivers; ascending hollow (Kong) and treading Dai; reaching Kun peaks to shake the reins, Kongshan to inquire of the Way—[1] it is preserved on sweating bamboo strips and cannot be heavily slandered.

entries.zh: 高陽任地依神，帝嚳順天行義。
entries.en: Zhuanxu, the High Yang line, grounded his power in the land and the spirits; Emperor Ku shaped policy by heaven's pattern and the moral law.
entries.literal: Gaoyang relied on earth and depended on spirits; Emperor Ku followed heaven and practiced righteousness.

entries.zh: 東踰蟠木，西濟流沙，北至幽陵，南撫交阯，日月所經，舟車所至，莫匪王臣，不踰茲域。
entries.en: Their sway ran east past the curling forest, west across the shifting sands, north to the cold marches, south to the Red River delta—every place the sun and moon lit and every road a wheel could find lay inside the ring of royal subjects, and nothing beyond that ring counted as theirs.
entries.literal: East they crossed Panmu, west they forded the flowing sands, north they reached Youling, south they soothed Jiaozhi; wherever sun and moon passed, wherever boat and cart could reach, none were not the king's subjects—they did not overstep this domain.

entries.zh: 帝堯時，禹平水土，以爲九州。
entries.en: Under Emperor Yao, Yu drained the flood and settled the soil, and from that labor the Nine Provinces took their shape.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Yao, Yu pacified the waters and earth, and thereby made the nine provinces.

entries.zh: 虞舜登庸，厥功彌劭，表提類而分區宇，判山河而考疆域，冀北創并部之名，燕齊起幽營之號，則書所謂肇十有二州，封十有二山者也。
entries.en: Once Shun took office, his achievement only deepened: he sorted kinds of terrain, carved the realm into regions, traced ranges and rivers to fix true borders, split the northern Ji plain to name the Bing command, and gave Yan and Qi the new titles of You and Ying—exactly the twelve provinces and twelve sacred peaks the classics say he first ordained.
entries.literal: When Shun of Yu ascended to employment, his merit grew ever greater; he displayed categories and divided the regional cosmos, adjudicated mountains and rivers and examined boundaries; north of Ji he created the name of the Bing department; in Yan and Qi he raised the designations of You and Ying—this is what the documents call initiating twelve provinces and enfeoffing twelve mountains.

entries.zh: 夏功在于唐堯，殷因無所損益。
entries.en: The Xia built on the work of Yao of Tang; the Shang inherited that map and left its proportions unchanged.
entries.literal: The Xia's achievement lay in Tang-Yao; the Yin inherited and had nothing to diminish or increase.

entries.zh: 周武克商，自豐徂鎬。
entries.en: When King Wu of Zhou overthrew the Shang, he moved the seat of power from Feng to Hao.
entries.literal: King Wu of Zhou conquered Shang, from Feng going to Hao.

entries.zh: 至成王時，改作禹貢，徐梁入於青雍，冀野析於幽并。
entries.en: Under King Cheng the court rewrote the "Tribute of Yu" grid: Xu and Liang were folded into Qing and Yong, while the old Ji heartland was carved into new You and Bing sectors.
entries.literal: By the time of King Cheng, they revised and made the Tribute of Yu; Xu and Liang were absorbed into Qing and Yong; the wilds of Ji were split into You and Bing.

entries.zh: 職方掌天下之土，以周厥利；
entries.en: The Bureau of Domains held the register of every soil under heaven, weighing what each tract could yield;
entries.literal: The Office of Regions grasped the soil of all under heaven, in order to complete its advantages;

entries.zh: 保章辯九州之野，皆有分星。
entries.en: The star-masters matched each of the Nine Provinces to its own stretch of sky, every region with its allotted constellation.
entries.literal: The Star-Clerk distinguished the wilds of the nine provinces; each had apportioned stars.

entries.zh: 東南曰揚州，正南曰荊州，河南曰豫州，正東曰青州，河東曰兗州，正西曰雍州，東北曰幽州，河內曰冀州，正北曰并州。
entries.en: The southeast quarter was Yangzhou, the south face Jingzhou, the ground south of the Yellow River Yuzhou, the east face Qingzhou, the ground east of the river Yanzhou, the west face Yongzhou, the northeast Youzhou, the inner bend of the river Jizhou, and the north face Bingzhou.
entries.literal: The southeast is called Yangzhou, the due south Jingzhou, south of the river Yuzhou, the due east Qingzhou, east of the river Yanzhou, the due west Yongzhou, the northeast Youzhou, within the river Jizhou, the due north Bingzhou.

entries.zh: 始皇初并天下，懲{乂心}戰國，削罷列侯，分天下爲三十六郡。
entries.en: The First Emperor, fresh from unifying the realm and determined not to repeat Warring States chaos, stripped the old enfeoffed nobles of power and carved the empire into thirty-six commanderies.
entries.literal: When the First Emperor first united all under heaven, chastened by the Warring States, he cut away and abolished the ranked feudal lords and divided all under heaven into thirty-six commanderies.

entries.zh: 〈三川、河東、南陽、南郡、九江、鄣郡、會稽、潁川、碭郡、泗水、薛郡、東郡、琅邪、齊郡、上谷、漁陽、右北平、遼西、遼東、代郡、鉅鹿、邯鄲、上黨、太原、雲中、九原、雁門、上郡、隴西、北地、漢中、巴郡、蜀郡、黔中、長沙，凡三十五郡，與內史爲三十六郡也。〉
entries.en: 〈The thirty-five commanderies were Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Nanjun, Jiujiang, Zhang, Kuaiji, Yingchuan, Dang, Sishui, Xue, Dong, Langye, Qi, Shanggu, Yuyang, Right Beiping, Liaoxi, Liaodong, Dai, Julu, Handan, Shangdang, Taiyuan, Yunzhong, Jiuyuan, Yanmen, Shang, Longxi, Beidi, Hanzhong, Ba, Shu, Qianzhong, and Changsha; together with the metropolitan intendant's district, they made thirty-six commanderies.〉
entries.literal: 〈Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Nanjun, Jiujiang, Zhang commandery, Kuaiji, Yingchuan, Dang commandery, Sishui, Xue commandery, Dong commandery, Langye, Qi commandery, Shanggu, Yuyang, Right Beiping, Liaoxi, Liaodong, Dai commandery, Julu, Handan, Shangdang, Taiyuan, Yunzhong, Jiuyuan, Yanmen, Shang commandery, Longxi, Beidi, Hanzhong, Ba commandery, Shu commandery, Qianzhong, Changsha—in all thirty-five commanderies, which together with the metropolitan intendant made thirty-six commanderies.〉

entries.zh: 於是興師踰江，平取百越，又置閩中、南海、桂林、象郡，凡四十郡，郡一守焉。
entries.en: He then sent armies south of the Yangtze, crushed the Yue peoples, and added Minzhong, Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang, bringing the whole system to forty commanderies, each overseen by a single appointed governor.
entries.literal: Thereupon they raised armies and crossed the rivers, pacified and took the Hundred Yue, and further established Minzhong, Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang commanderies—in all forty commanderies, each commandery having one governor.

entries.zh: 其地則西臨洮而北沙漠，東縈西帶，皆臨大海。
entries.en: The new realm ran west to the Tao River and north to the sands, while east and south it looped like a sash until every outer edge touched the sea.
entries.literal: As for the territory: west it bordered Tao and north the desert; east winding, west belting—all bordered the great sea.

entries.zh: 漢祖龍興，革秦之弊，分內史爲三部，更置郡國二十有三，
entries.en: When the Han founder seized the mandate, he undid Qin's excesses, split the old inner intendant into three metropolitan circuits, and added twenty-three new commanderies and princely kingdoms,
entries.literal: The Han progenitor rose like a dragon, reformed the Qin's abuses, divided the metropolitan intendant into three parts, and further established twenty-three commanderies and kingdoms,

entries.zh: 〈桂陽、江夏、豫章、河內、魏郡、東海、楚國、平原、梁國、定襄、泰山、汝南、淮陽、千乘、東萊、燕國、清河、信都、常山、中山、渤海、廣漢、涿郡，合二十三也。
entries.en: 〈These were Guiyang, Jiangxia, Yuzhang, Henei, Wei, Donghai, Chu, Pingyuan, Liang, Dingxiang, Taishan, Runan, Huaiyang, Qiansheng, Donglai, Yan, Qinghe, Xindu, Changshan, Zhongshan, Bohai, Guanghan, and Zhuo, twenty-three in all.
entries.literal: 〈Guiyang, Jiangxia, Yuzhang, Henei, Wei commandery, Donghai, Chu kingdom, Pingyuan, Liang kingdom, Dingxiang, Taishan, Runan, Huaiyang, Qiansheng, Donglai, Yan kingdom, Qinghe, Xindu, Changshan, Zhongshan, Bohai, Guanghan, Zhuo commandery—together twenty-three.

entries.zh: 三內史者，河上、渭南、中地也。
entries.en: The three inner districts were Heshang south of the bend, Weinan, and the central capital belt.
entries.literal: The three metropolitan intendants are: Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi.

entries.zh: 地理志曰：高祖增二十六，武帝改河上、渭南、中地以爲京兆、馮翊、扶風，是爲三輔也。〉
entries.en: The Treatise on Geography says: Gaozu added twenty-six; Emperor Wu changed Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi into Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng—these are the Three Adjuncts.〉
entries.literal: The Treatise on Geography says: Gaozu added twenty-six; Emperor Wu changed Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi into Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng—this is the Three Adjuncts.〉

entries.zh: 文增厥九，
entries.en: Emperor Wen of Han added nine more,
entries.literal: Wen added thereto nine,

entries.zh: 〈廣平、城陽、淄川、濟南、膠西、膠東、河間、廬江、衡山，武帝改衡山曰「六安」。〉
entries.en: 〈Guangping, Chengyang, Zichuan, Jinan, Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Hejian, Lujiang, and Hengshan—the last of which Emperor Wu renamed "Liu'an."〉
entries.literal: 〈Guangping, Chengyang, Zichuan, Jinan, Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Hejian, Lujiang, Hengshan—Emperor Wu changed Hengshan to "Liu'an."〉

entries.zh: 景加其四。
entries.en: Emperor Jing added four more.
entries.literal: Jing added four of them.

entries.zh: 〈濟北、濟陰、山陽、北海也。
entries.en: 〈Jibei, Jiyin, Shanyang, and Beihai.
entries.literal: 〈Jibei, Jiyin, Shanyang, and Beihai.

entries.zh: 宣改濟北曰東平。〉
entries.en: Emperor Xuan renamed Jibei as Dongping.〉
entries.literal: Xuan changed Jibei to Dongping.〉

entries.zh: 武帝開越攘胡，初置十七，
entries.en: Emperor Wu campaigned south against Yue and north against the steppe peoples, and his first expansion added seventeen commanderies,
entries.literal: Emperor Wu opened the Yue and pushed back the Hu, at first establishing seventeen,

entries.zh: 〈南海、蒼梧、鬱林、合浦、交阯、九真、日南、珠崖、儋耳九郡，平西南夷置牂柯、越巂、沈黎、汶山、犍爲、益州六郡，西置武都郡，又分立零陵郡，合十七郡。〉
entries.en: 〈nine southern coast commands from Nanhai to Dan'er, six carved from the southwest Yi heartland, Wudu on the western flank, and a split Lingling—seventeen new units in that push.〉
entries.literal: 〈Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, Hepu, Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, Rinan, Zhuya, Dan'er—nine commanderies; pacifying the southwestern Yi, established Zangke, Yuexi, Chenli, Wenshan, Qianwei, Yizhou—six commanderies; west established Wudu commandery; again separately established Lingling commandery—together seventeen commanderies.〉

entries.zh: 拓土分疆，又增十四。
entries.en: Further conquests widened the map by fourteen more commanderies.
entries.literal: Expanding soil and dividing boundaries, again added fourteen.

entries.zh: 〈弘農、臨淮、西河、朔方、酒泉、陳留、安定、天水、玄菟、樂浪、廣陵、敦煌、武威、張掖。〉
entries.en: 〈The fourteen interior and frontier commanderies were Hongnong, Linhuai, Xihe, Shuofang, Jiuquan, Chenliu, Anding, Tianshui, Xuantu, Lelang, Guangling, Dunhuang, Wuwei, and Zhangye.〉
entries.literal: 〈Hongnong, Linhuai, Xihe, Shuofang, Jiuquan, Chenliu, Anding, Tianshui, Xuantu, Lelang, Guangling, Dunhuang, Wuwei, Zhangye.〉

entries.zh: 昭帝少事，又增其一。
entries.en: Under the short reign of Emperor Zhao the court added only one more.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhao had few undertakings, again added one thereof.

entries.zh: 〈金城也。〉
entries.en: 〈Jincheng commandery.〉
entries.literal: 〈Jincheng.〉

entries.zh: 至平帝元始二年，凡新置郡國七十有一，與秦四十，合一百一十有一。
entries.en: By the second year of Yuanshi under Emperor Ping, Han had founded seventy-one new units; added to Qin's forty, the roster stood at one hundred eleven.
entries.literal: Down to Emperor Ping's Yuanshi second year, in all newly established commanderies and kingdoms were seventy-one; together with Qin's forty, altogether one hundred eleven.

entries.zh: 改雍曰涼，改梁曰益，又置徐州，復夏舊號，南置交阯，北有朔方，凡爲十三部。
entries.en: Yong was changed to Liang, Liang to Yi; Xuzhou was further established; Xia's old designations were restored; Jiaozhi was set up in the south and Shuofang in the north—thirteen departments in all.
entries.literal: Changed Yong to Liang, changed Liang to Yi, further established Xuzhou, restored Xia's old designations, south established Jiaozhi, north had Shuofang—in all became thirteen departments.

entries.zh: 〈涼、益、荊、揚、青、豫、兗、徐、幽、并、冀十一州，交阯、朔方二刺史，合十三部。〉
entries.en: 〈Eleven provinces from Liang to Ji plus two special zones, Jiaozhi and Shuofang, each with its own regional commissioner—thirteen departments in all.〉
entries.literal: 〈Liang, Yi, Jing, Yang, Qing, Yu, Yan, Xu, You, Bing, Ji—eleven provinces; Jiaozhi, Shuofang—two regional inspectors; together thirteen departments.〉

entries.zh: 光武投戈之歲，在彫秏之辰，郡國蕭條，并省者八。
entries.en: When Guangwu laid down the sword, the realm was gaunt from war; eight redundant commanderies were folded away in the general retrenchment.
entries.literal: In the year Guangwu cast aside the spear, it was a time of wasting exhaustion; commanderies and kingdoms were desolate; those merged and abolished were eight.

entries.zh: 〈城陽、淄川、高密、膠東、六安、真定、泗水、廣陽。〉
entries.en: 〈Chengyang, Zichuan, Gaomi, Jiaodong, Liu'an, Zhending, Sishui, and Guangyang were the eight struck from the map.〉
entries.literal: 〈Chengyang, Zichuan, Gaomi, Jiaodong, Liu'an, Zhending, Sishui, Guangyang.〉

entries.zh: 建武十一年，省州牧，復爲刺史，員十三人，各掌一州。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Jianwu the court abolished the provincial governorships, restored classic regional censors, and fixed their number at thirteen, one to each major province.
entries.literal: Jianwu eleventh year, abolished provincial shepherds, again became censors; establishment thirteen men, each grasping one province.

entries.zh: 明帝置一，
entries.en: Emperor Ming added one seat,
entries.literal: Mingdi established one,

entries.zh: 〈永昌也。〉
entries.en: 〈Yongchang in the far southwest.〉
entries.literal: 〈Yongchang.〉

entries.zh: 章帝置二，
entries.en: Emperor Zhang added two commands,
entries.literal: Zhangdi established two,

entries.zh: 〈任城、吳郡。〉
entries.en: 〈Rencheng and Wu commandery.〉
entries.literal: 〈Rencheng, Wu commandery.〉

entries.zh: 和順改作，其名有九。
entries.en: Under Emperors He and Shun names were altered; there were nine of them.
entries.literal: He and Shun altered and made; their names were nine.

entries.zh: 〈和置濟北、廣陽，順改淮陽爲陳，改楚爲彭城，濟東爲東平，臨淮爲下邳，千乘爲六安，信都爲安平，天水爲漢陽。〉
entries.en: 〈Emperor He revived Jibei and Guangyang; Emperor Shun renamed Huaiyang as Chen, the old Chu core as Pengcheng, Jidong as Dongping, Linhuai as Xiapi, Qiansheng as Liu'an, Xindu as Anping, and Tianshui as Hanyang.〉
entries.literal: 〈He established Jibei and Guangyang; Shun changed Huaiyang to Chen, changed Chu to Pengcheng, Jidong to Dongping, Linhuai to Xiapi, Qiansheng to Liu'an, Xindu to Anping, Tianshui to Hanyang.〉

entries.zh: 省朔方刺史，合之於司隸，凡十三部，
entries.en: Shuofang's inspectorate was folded into the capital superintendent's zone, leaving thirteen departments in the Eastern Han scheme,
entries.literal: Abolished the Shuofang regional inspector, merged it into the Metropolitan Superintendent; in all thirteen departments,

entries.zh: 〈其與西漢不同者，司隸校尉部郡治河南，朔方隸於并部。〉
entries.en: 〈Unlike Western Han, the metropolitan belt was administered from Henan, while Shuofang answered to the Bing inspector rather than standing alone.〉
entries.literal: 〈Where it differs from Western Han: the Metropolitan Superintendent's commandery-administered region takes Henan as its seat; Shuofang is subordinate to Bing department.〉

entries.zh: 而郡國百有八焉。
entries.en: The Eastern Han roster thus held one hundred eight commanderies and kingdoms.
entries.literal: And commanderies and kingdoms were one hundred eight.

entries.zh: 〈省前漢八，分置五，改舊名七，因舊九十六，少前漢三也。〉
entries.en: 〈Eight Western Han units were cut, five new ones split off, seven were simply renamed, ninety-six kept their old titles—three fewer than the old Han total.〉
entries.literal: 〈Abolished eight of Former Han, split and established five, changed old names seven, continued old ninety-six—three fewer than Former Han.〉

entries.zh: 桓靈頗增於前，復置六郡。
entries.en: Under Emperors Huan and Ling the court added six commanderies beyond the earlier baseline.
entries.literal: Huan and Ling somewhat increased over before, again established six commanderies.

entries.zh: 〈桓，高陽、高涼、博陵；
entries.en: 〈Emperor Huan created Gaoyang, Gaoliang, and Boling;
entries.literal: 〈Huan: Gaoyang, Gaoliang, Boling;

entries.zh: 靈，南安、鄱陽、廬陵。〉
entries.en: Emperor Ling added Nan'an, Poyang, and Luling.〉
entries.literal: Ling: Nan'an, Poyang, Luling.〉

entries.zh: 魏武定霸，三方鼎立，生靈版蕩，關洛荒蕪，所置者十二，
entries.en: When Wei Wu settled his hegemony, the three sides stood like a tripod, the people were thrown into turmoil, the passes and Luo region lay desolate, and those he established were twelve,
entries.literal: Wei Wu settled hegemony; the three sides stood like a tripod; living beings were on tablet-like upheaval; Guan and Luo were desolate; those established were twelve,

entries.zh: 〈新興、樂平、西平、新平、略陽、陰平、帶方、譙、樂陵、章武、南鄉、襄陽。〉
entries.en: 〈Xinxing, Leping, Xiping, Xinping, Lueyang, Yinping, Daifang, Qiao, Leling, Zhangwu, Nanxiang, and Xiangyang.〉
entries.literal: 〈Xinxing, Leping, Xiping, Xinping, Lueyang, Yinping, Daifang, Qiao, Leling, Zhangwu, Nanxiang, Xiangyang.〉

entries.zh: 所省者七，
entries.en: Seven older commands were struck at the same time,
entries.literal: Those abolished were seven,

entries.zh: 〈上郡、朔方、五原、雲中、定襄、漁陽、廬江。〉
entries.en: 〈Shang, Shuofang, Wuyuan, Yunzhong, Dingxiang, Yuyang, and Lujiang were the seven removed.〉
entries.literal: 〈Shang commandery, Shuofang, Wuyuan, Yunzhong, Dingxiang, Yuyang, Lujiang.〉

entries.zh: 而文帝置七，
entries.en: Emperor Wen of Wei then added seven more,
entries.literal: And Wendi established seven,

entries.zh: 〈朝歌、陽平、弋陽、魏興、新城、義陽、[2]安豐。〉
entries.en: 〈Zhaoge, Yangping, the Ru-nan Yiyang, Weixing, Xincheng, the Huai-line Yiyang, and Anfeng.〉
entries.literal: 〈Zhaoge, Yangping, the Ru-nan Yiyang, Weixing, Xincheng, the Huai-line Yiyang, and Anfeng.〉

entries.zh: 明及少帝增二，
entries.en: Emperor Ming and the first boy emperor each added one commandery—two in all,
entries.literal: Ming and the Lesser Emperor added two,

entries.zh: 〈明，上庸也；
entries.en: 〈Mingdi restored Shangyong;
entries.literal: 〈Ming: Shangyong;

entries.zh: 少，平陽也。〉
entries.en: the boy emperor added Pingyang.〉
entries.literal: Lesser: Pingyang.〉

entries.zh: 得漢郡者五十四焉。
entries.en: Wei thus held fifty-four commanderies inherited from Han.
entries.literal: Those obtaining Han commanderies were fifty-four.

entries.zh: 蜀先主於漢建安之間初置郡九，
entries.en: Between the Jian'an years, Liu Bei in Shu-Han first carved out nine commanderies,
entries.literal: Shu's First Sovereign, in the interval of Han's Jian'an, first established nine commanderies,

entries.zh: 〈巴東、巴西、梓潼、江陽、汶山、漢嘉、朱提、宕渠、涪陵。〉
entries.en: 〈Badong, Baxi, Zitong, Jiangyang, Wenshan, Hanjia, Zhuti, Dangqu, and Fuling.〉
entries.literal: 〈Badong, Baxi, Zitong, Jiangyang, Wenshan, Hanjia, Zhuti, Dangqu, Fuling.〉

entries.zh: 後主增二，
entries.en: Liu Shan later added two more,
entries.literal: The Later Sovereign added two,

entries.zh: 〈雲南、興古。〉
entries.en: 〈Yunnan and Xingu in the far south.〉
entries.literal: 〈Yunnan, Xingu.〉

entries.zh: 得漢郡者十有一焉。
entries.en: Shu ultimately held eleven Han-era commanderies.
entries.literal: Those obtaining Han commanderies were eleven.

entries.zh: 吳主大皇帝初置郡五，
entries.en: Sun Quan, Wu's Great Emperor, first founded five commanderies,
entries.literal: The Wu ruler, the Great Emperor, first established five commanderies,

entries.zh: 〈臨賀、武昌、珠崖、新安、廬陵南部。〉
entries.en: 〈Linhe, Wuchang, Zhuya, Xin'an, and the southern annex of Luling.〉
entries.literal: 〈Linhe, Wuchang, Zhuya, Xin'an, southern Luling.〉

entries.zh: 少帝、景帝各四，
entries.en: Sun Liang and Sun Xiu each added four commanderies,
entries.literal: The Lesser Emperor and Emperor Jing each four,

entries.zh: 〈少，臨川、臨海、衡陽、湘東。
entries.en: 〈Sun Liang created Linchuan, Linhai, Hengyang, and Xiangdong;
entries.literal: 〈Lesser: Linchuan, Linhai, Hengyang, Xiangdong.

entries.zh: 景，天門、建安、建平、合浦北部。〉
entries.en: Sun Xiu added Tianmen, Jian'an, Jianping, and northern Hepu.〉
entries.literal: Jing: Tianmen, Jian'an, Jianping, northern Hepu.〉

entries.zh: 歸命侯亦置十有二郡，
entries.en: Sun Hao, the "Marquis Who Surrendered His Mandate," still ordered twelve more commanderies founded,
entries.literal: The Marquis Who Submits to Fate also established twelve commanderies,

entries.zh: 〈始安、始興、邵陵、安成、新昌、武平、九德、吳興、東陽、桂林、滎陽、宜都。〉
entries.en: 〈Shi'an, Shixing, Shaoling, Ancheng, Xinchang, Wuping, Jiude, Wuxing, Dongyang, Guilin, Yingyang, and Yidu.〉
entries.literal: 〈Shi'an, Shixing, Shaoling, Ancheng, Xinchang, Wuping, Jiude, Wuxing, Dongyang, Guilin, Yingyang, Yidu.〉

entries.zh: 得漢郡者十有八焉。
entries.en: Wu in the end controlled eighteen commanderies that had once belonged to Han.
entries.literal: Those obtaining Han commanderies were eighteen.

entries.zh: 及宣帝、景帝之崩，並從權制。
entries.en: The deaths of Sima Yi and Sima Shi were handled under the same shortened schedule.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan and Emperor Jing died, each likewise followed the expedient code.

entries.zh: 文帝之崩，國內服三日。
entries.en: When Sima Zhao died, the whole state wore mourning for three days and no more.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the realm observed mourning for three days only.

entries.zh: 武帝亦遵漢魏之典，既葬除喪，然猶深衣素冠，降席撤膳。
entries.en: Emperor Sima Yan kept the Han–Wei rule of ending court mourning at burial, but he still dressed in plain hemp deep robes, set aside brocade cushions, and ate only coarse fare.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu likewise followed Han and Wei precedent: once the burial ended he set aside formal mourning, yet still wore plain deep garments and an undyed cap, lowered his mat, and withdrew rich food from his table.

entries.zh: 太宰司馬孚、太傅鄭沖、太保王祥、太尉何曾、司徒領中領軍司馬望、司空荀顗、車騎將軍賈充、尚書令裴秀、尚書僕射武陔、都護大將軍郭建、侍中郭綏、中書監荀勖、中軍將軍羊祜等奏曰：「臣聞禮典軌度，豐殺隨時，虞夏商周，咸不相襲，蓋有由也。
entries.en: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Grand Guardian Wang Xiang, Grand Commandant He Ceng, Minister of Education concurrently Central Army commander Sima Wang, Minister of Works Xun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Prefect of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Wu Yan, Chief Protector and Grand General Guo Jian, Palace Attendant Guo Sui, Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, and others memorialized: 'We have heard that ritual canons and measures wax or wane with the times; the houses of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou never blindly copied one another—each had its reasons.
entries.literal: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Grand Guardian Wang Xiang, Grand Commandant He Ceng, Minister of Education concurrently Central Army commander Sima Wang, Minister of Works Xun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Prefect of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Wu Yan, Chief Protector and Grand General Guo Jian, Palace Attendant Guo Sui, Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, and others memorialized: 'We have heard that ritual canons and measures wax or wane with the times; the houses of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou never blindly copied one another—each had its reasons.

entries.zh: 大晉紹承漢魏，有革有因，期於足以興化而已，故未得皆返太素，同規上古也。
entries.en: Great Jin inherits Han and Wei with some reforms and some continuities, aiming only to lift custom where it must; therefore it cannot yet return wholesale to pristine antiquity or match high antiquity in a single stroke.
