entries.literal: Great Jin inherits Han and Wei with some reforms and some continuities, aiming only to lift custom where it must; therefore it cannot yet return wholesale to pristine antiquity or match high antiquity in a single stroke.

entries.zh: 陛下既以俯遵漢魏降喪之典，以濟時務，而躬蹈大孝，情過乎哀，素冠深衣，降席撤膳，雖武丁行之于殷世，曾閔履之於布衣，未足以逾。
entries.en: Your Majesty has already bowed to Han and Wei's lowered mourning canons to meet pressing affairs, yet you personally tread the utmost filial path; your feeling overshoots moderation—plain cap, deep garments, lowered mat, curtailed meals—even King Wuding in the Yin age or Zengzi and Min Ziqian as commoners did not surpass this.
entries.literal: Your Majesty has already bowed to Han and Wei's lowered mourning canons to meet pressing affairs, yet you personally tread the utmost filial path; your feeling overshoots moderation—plain cap, deep garments, lowered mat, curtailed meals—even King Wuding in the Yin age or Zengzi and Min Ziqian as commoners did not surpass this.

entries.zh: 方今荊蠻未夷，庶政未乂，萬機事殷，動勞神慮，豈遑全遂聖旨，以從至情。
entries.en: Now the southern tribes are not yet pacified, government is not yet ordered, and myriad threads of business press upon you, taxing mind and spirit—how could you wholly indulge sage intent and the utmost of private feeling?
entries.literal: Now the southern tribes are not yet pacified, government is not yet ordered, and myriad threads of business press upon you, taxing mind and spirit—how could you wholly indulge sage intent and the utmost of private feeling?

entries.zh: 臣等以為陛下宜割情以康時濟俗，輒敕御府易服，內省改坐，太官復膳，諸所施行，皆如舊制。」
entries.en: We your servants therefore believe Your Majesty should cut private feeling to heal the age and aid custom; we dare order the Palace Treasury to exchange garments, the inner apartments to restore seating, the Grand Provisioner to restore full meals, and every other measure to follow the standing regulations.'
entries.literal: We your servants therefore believe Your Majesty should cut private feeling to heal the age and aid custom; we dare order the Palace Treasury to exchange garments, the inner apartments to restore seating, the Grand Provisioner to restore full meals, and every other measure to follow the standing regulations.'

entries.zh: 詔曰：「每感念幽冥，而不得終苴絰於草土，以存此痛，況當食稻衣錦，誠詭然激切其心，非所以相解也。
entries.en: The edict replied: 'Whenever I brood on the shades below and realize I cannot finish wearing straw cord on the burial mound to keep this pain alive—how much more to eat polished rice and wear brocade—indeed it stabs the heart; that is no way to console myself.
entries.literal: The edict replied: 'Whenever I brood on the shades below and realize I cannot finish wearing straw cord on the burial mound to keep this pain alive—how much more to eat polished rice and wear brocade—indeed it stabs the heart; that is no way to console myself.

entries.zh: 吾本諸生家，傳禮來久，何心一旦便易此情於所天！
entries.en: I was born to a house of scholars; the rites have been handed down among us a long time—how could my heart one morning cast off this feeling toward him who is my heaven!
entries.literal: I was born to a house of scholars; the rites have been handed down among us a long time—how could my heart one morning cast off this feeling toward him who is my heaven!

entries.zh: 相從已多，可試省孔子答宰我之言，無事紛紜也。
entries.en: You have followed me long; try reviewing Confucius's answer to Zai Wo—do not fuss at me again and again.
entries.literal: You have followed me long; try reviewing Confucius's answer to Zai Wo—do not fuss at me again and again.

entries.zh: 言及悲剝，柰何！
entries.en: When words touch grief it tears the heart—what can be done!
entries.literal: When words touch grief it tears the heart—what can be done!

entries.zh: 柰何！」
entries.en: What can be done!'
entries.literal: What can be done!'

entries.zh: 孚等重奏：「伏讀聖詔，感以悲懷，輒思仲尼所以抑宰我之問，聖思所以不能已已，甚深甚篤。
entries.en: Fu and the others rememorialized: 'We have read the sage edict and are moved to grief; we reflect on why Confucius checked Zai Wo's question—the sage mind cannot stop itself; the feeling is very deep and very earnest.
entries.literal: Fu and the others rememorialized: 'We have read the sage edict and are moved to grief; we reflect on why Confucius checked Zai Wo's question—the sage mind cannot stop itself; the feeling is very deep and very earnest.

entries.zh: 然今者干戈未戢，武事未偃，萬機至重，天下至眾。
entries.en: Yet now weapons are not yet stilled, military affairs not yet rested, the myriad threads are weightiest, and all under Heaven is most numerous.
entries.literal: Yet now weapons are not yet stilled, military affairs not yet rested, the myriad threads are weightiest, and all under Heaven is most numerous.

entries.zh: 陛下以萬乘之尊，履布衣之禮，服粗席稿，水飲疏食，殷憂內盈，毀悴外表。
entries.en: Your Majesty in the honor of ten thousand chariots treads the rites of a commoner—coarse mat and straw padding, drinking water and eating coarse food, sorrow swelling within, emaciation showing without.
entries.literal: Your Majesty in the honor of ten thousand chariots treads the rites of a commoner—coarse mat and straw padding, drinking water and eating coarse food, sorrow swelling within, emaciation showing without.

entries.zh: 而躬勤萬機，坐而待旦，降心接下，仄不遑食，所以勞力者如斯之甚。
entries.en: Yet you personally toil at myriad threads of state, sit awaiting dawn, humble your heart to receive subordinates, and lean so far you have no leisure to eat—such labor of strength is extreme.
entries.literal: Yet you personally toil at myriad threads of state, sit awaiting dawn, humble your heart to receive subordinates, and lean so far you have no leisure to eat—such labor of strength is extreme.

entries.zh: 是以臣等悚息不寧，誠懼神氣用損，以疚大事。
entries.en: Therefore we your servants tremble and breathe uneasily, truly fearing that spirit will be depleted and the great affair harmed.
entries.literal: Therefore we your servants tremble and breathe uneasily, truly fearing that spirit will be depleted and the great affair harmed.

entries.zh: 輒敕有司，改坐復常，率由舊典。
entries.en: We dare order the relevant offices to restore your seat and routine, following the old canons.
entries.literal: We dare order the relevant offices to restore your seat and routine, following the old canons.

entries.zh: 惟陛下察納愚款，以慰皇太后之心。」
entries.en: Only let Your Majesty examine and accept our foolish sincerity, so as to console the heart of the Empress Dowager.'
entries.literal: Only let Your Majesty examine and accept our foolish sincerity, so as to console the heart of the Empress Dowager.'

entries.zh: 又詔曰：「重覽奏議，益以悲剝，不能自勝，柰何！
entries.en: Another edict said: 'Rereading your memorials only deepens the tearing grief; I cannot master myself—what can be done!
entries.literal: Another edict said: 'Rereading your memorials only deepens the tearing grief; I cannot master myself—what can be done!

entries.zh: 柰何！
entries.en: What can be done!
entries.literal: What can be done!

entries.zh: 三年之喪，自古達禮，誠聖人稱情立衷，明恕而行也。
entries.en: Three years' mourning has from antiquity been the penetrating rite of the realm; truly the sages weighed human feeling, set the inner mean, and acted with enlightened forbearance.
entries.literal: Three years' mourning has from antiquity been the penetrating rite of the realm; truly the sages weighed human feeling, set the inner mean, and acted with enlightened forbearance.

entries.zh: 神靈日遠，無所訴告，雖薄於情，食旨服美，所不堪也。
entries.en: The spirits grow daily more distant; there is nowhere to cry complaint—though the outward show be slight, to taste rich food and wear fine cloth is unbearable.
entries.literal: The spirits grow daily more distant; there is nowhere to cry complaint—though the outward show be slight, to taste rich food and wear fine cloth is unbearable.

entries.zh: 不宜反覆，重傷其心，言用斷絕，柰何！
entries.en: You ought not go back and forth and doubly wound this heart; I break off words—what can be done!
entries.literal: You ought not go back and forth and doubly wound this heart; I break off words—what can be done!

entries.zh: 柰何！」
entries.en: What can be done!'
entries.literal: What can be done!'

entries.zh: 帝遂以此禮終三年。
entries.en: With that he carried the full three-year vigil despite every plea.
entries.literal: The emperor therefore observed mourning to the full three years under this rite.

entries.zh: 後居太后之喪亦如之。
entries.en: He repeated the same austerity when the empress dowager died.
entries.literal: Later, when mourning the Empress Dowager, he did the same.

entries.zh: 魏武以正月崩，魏文以其年七月設妓樂百戲，是則魏不以喪廢樂也。
entries.en: Cao Cao died in the first month; Cao Pi still staged troupes and acrobats that seventh month—so Wei never treated mourning as a reason to silence the bands.
entries.literal: Wei Wu died in the first month; Wei Wen in that year's seventh month set singing-girls and the hundred entertainments—therefore Wei did not cancel music because of mourning.

entries.zh: 武帝以來，國有大喪，輒廢樂終三年。
entries.en: Under Emperor Sima Yan, every dynastic bereavement silenced the orchestras for three years.
entries.literal: From Emperor Wu onward, whenever the state had great mourning, court music was suspended for the full three years.

entries.zh: 惠帝太安元年，太子喪未除，及元會亦廢樂。
entries.en: In Emperor Hui's Taian era, while the heir still wore mourning, the Yuan-day levee went without music.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taian under Emperor Hui, the crown prince's mourning was not yet removed—yet for the New Year court assembly music was likewise suspended.

entries.zh: 穆帝永和中，為中原山陵未修復，頻年元會廢樂。
entries.en: Yonghe years saw the New Year court go silent while Luoyang's tombs lay in ruins.
entries.literal: During Yonghe under Emperor Mu, because the imperial tombs on the Central Plain were not yet repaired, for successive years the Yuan assembly suspended music.

entries.zh: 是時太后臨朝，后父褚裒薨，元會又廢樂也。
entries.en: The regent's father Chu Pou died that same span, so the levee stayed mute again.
entries.literal: At that time the empress dowager presided at court; the empress's father Chu Pou died—the Yuan assembly again suspended music.

entries.zh: 孝武太元六年，為皇后王氏喪，亦廢樂。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, during mourning for Empress Wang, music was likewise suspended.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, during mourning for Empress Wang, music was likewise suspended.

entries.zh: 孝武崩，太傅錄尚書會稽王道子議：「山陵之後，通婚嫁不得作樂，以一期為斷。」
entries.en: When Xiaowu died, Grand Tutor concurrently recording Masters of Writing the Prince of Guiji, Sima Daozi, debated: 'After the imperial tomb is closed, weddings may proceed but without music—take one full cycle as the limit.'"
entries.literal: When Xiaowu died, Grand Tutor concurrently recording Masters of Writing the Prince of Guiji, Sima Daozi, debated: 'After the imperial tomb is closed, weddings may proceed but without music—take one full cycle as the limit.'"

entries.zh: 泰始四年，皇太后崩。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Taishi, the Empress Dowager died.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi, the Empress Dowager died.

entries.zh: 有司奏：「前代故事，倚廬中施白縑帳、蓐、素床，以布巾裹塊草，軺輦、版輿、細犢車皆施縑裏。」
entries.en: The responsible offices memorialized, "Former-generation precedents set white silk curtains, mats, and a plain bed in the leaning hut, wrapped clods and grass in a cloth kerchief, and applied silk linings to the light carriage, plank carriage, and small-calf cart."
entries.literal: The responsible offices memorialized, "Former-generation precedents set white silk curtains, mats, and a plain bed in the leaning hut, wrapped clods and grass in a cloth kerchief, and applied silk linings to the light carriage, plank carriage, and small-calf cart."

entries.zh: 詔不聽，但令以布衣車而已，其餘居喪之制，不改禮文。
entries.en: He refused the silks but allowed plain carts only, leaving every other mourning rule as written in the canon.
entries.literal: The edict did not consent; it ordered only plain-cloth carts; as for the rest of the dwelling-in-mourning system, it did not alter the ritual text.

entries.zh: 有司又奏：「大行皇太后當以四月二十五日安厝。
entries.en: The responsible offices again memorialized, "The deceased Empress Dowager should be interred on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month.
entries.literal: The responsible offices again memorialized, "The deceased Empress Dowager should be interred on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month.

entries.zh: 故事，虞著衰服，既虞而除。
entries.en: According to precedent, at the yu sacrifice one wears mourning dress, and after the yu sacrifice one removes it.
entries.literal: According to precedent, at the yu sacrifice one wears mourning dress, and after the yu sacrifice one removes it.

entries.zh: 其內外官僚皆就朝晡臨位，御除服訖，各還所次除衰服。」
entries.en: Let the officials inside and outside all go to their mourning positions at morning and afternoon, and when the imperial removal of dress is complete, each return to his quarters and remove mourning dress."
entries.literal: Let the officials inside and outside all go to their mourning positions at morning and afternoon, and when the imperial removal of dress is complete, each return to his quarters and remove mourning dress."

entries.zh: 詔曰：「夫三年之喪，天下之達禮也。
entries.en: An edict said, "The three-year mourning is the universally observed ritual throughout all under Heaven.
entries.literal: An edict said, "The three-year mourning is the universally observed ritual throughout all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 受終身之愛，而無數年之報，柰何葬而便即吉，情所不忍也。」
entries.en: Having received a lifetime of love, yet making no repayment of several years: how could one be buried and then immediately return to felicity? My feeling cannot bear it."
entries.literal: Having received a lifetime of love, yet making no repayment of several years: how could one be buried and then immediately return to felicity? My feeling cannot bear it."

entries.zh: 有司又奏：「世有險易，道有洿隆，所遇之時異，誠有由然，非忽禮也。
entries.en: The responsible offices again memorialized, "Ages have danger and ease, and the Way has hollows and heights. That the times encountered differ truly has reasons; it is not disregard for ritual.
entries.literal: The responsible offices again memorialized, "Ages have danger and ease, and the Way has hollows and heights. That the times encountered differ truly has reasons; it is not disregard for ritual.

entries.zh: 方今戎馬未散，王事至殷，更須聽斷，以熙庶績。
entries.en: At present, war horses have not yet dispersed, and royal affairs are extremely urgent. It is further necessary to hear and decide matters, in order to brighten the many tasks.
entries.literal: At present, war horses have not yet dispersed, and royal affairs are extremely urgent. It is further necessary to hear and decide matters, in order to brighten the many tasks.

entries.zh: 昔周康王始登翌室，猶戴冕臨朝。
entries.en: Formerly, when King Kang of Zhou first ascended the next chamber, he still wore the cap and robe and attended court.
entries.literal: Formerly, when King Kang of Zhou first ascended the next chamber, he still wore the cap and robe and attended court.

entries.zh: 降于漢魏，既葬除釋，諒闇之禮，自遠代而廢矣。
entries.en: Down to Han and Wei, after burial mourning was removed and released, and the ritual of liang'an had been abandoned since distant ages.
entries.literal: Down to Han and Wei, after burial mourning was removed and released, and the ritual of liang'an had been abandoned since distant ages.

entries.zh: 惟陛下割高宗之制，從當時之宜。」
entries.en: We only ask Your Majesty to cut back the system of Gaozong and follow what is fitting to the present time."
entries.literal: We only ask Your Majesty to cut back the system of Gaozong and follow what is fitting to the present time."

entries.zh: 詔曰：「夫三年之喪，所以盡情致禮，葬已便除，所不堪也。
entries.en: An edict said, "The three-year mourning is how one exhausts feeling and brings ritual to completion. To remove it once burial is finished is what I cannot bear.
entries.literal: An edict said, "The three-year mourning is how one exhausts feeling and brings ritual to completion. To remove it once burial is finished is what I cannot bear.

entries.zh: 當敘吾哀懷，言用斷絕，柰何！
entries.en: When I try to express my grief, words are cut off. What can I do!
entries.literal: When I try to express my grief, words are cut off. What can I do!

entries.zh: 柰何！」
entries.en: What can I do!"
entries.literal: What can I do!"

entries.zh: 有司又固請。
entries.en: The bureaus petitioned again, harder.
entries.literal: The offices again firmly requested.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「不能篤孝，勿以毀傷為憂也。
entries.en: An edict said, "If I cannot be deeply filial, do not take self-injury as a worry.
entries.literal: An edict said, "If I cannot be deeply filial, do not take self-injury as a worry.

entries.zh: 誠知衣服末事耳，然今思存草土，率當以吉物奪之，乃所以重傷至心，非見念也。
entries.en: I truly know that clothing is a minor matter. Yet now, when my thoughts are to remain with grass and earth, to take it away by means of auspicious things is precisely to wound the utmost heart again; it is not thinking of me.
entries.literal: I truly know that clothing is a minor matter. Yet now, when my thoughts are to remain with grass and earth, to take it away by means of auspicious things is precisely to wound the utmost heart again; it is not thinking of me.

entries.zh: 每代禮典質文皆不同耳，何為限以近制，使達喪闕然乎！」
entries.en: In each age, ritual codes differ in substance and refinement. Why restrict me by a recent system and make the universal mourning deficient!"
entries.literal: In each age, ritual codes differ in substance and refinement. Why restrict me by a recent system and make the universal mourning deficient!"

entries.zh: 群臣又固請，帝流涕久之乃許。
entries.en: Ministers pressed until he wept long and yielded.
entries.literal: The many ministers again firmly requested; the emperor wept a long time and then consented.

entries.zh: 文明皇后崩及武元楊后崩，天下將吏發哀三日止。
entries.en: When Empress Dowager Yuan died and when Empress Yang the consort of Wu died, officers empire-wide wailed three days only.
entries.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming died and when Empress Wu-Yuan Yang died, officers throughout the realm raised mourning for three days and then stopped.

entries.zh: 穆帝崩，哀帝立。
entries.en: Emperor Ai succeeded when Emperor Mu passed.
entries.literal: When Emperor Mu died, Emperor Ai was enthroned.

entries.zh: 帝于穆帝為從父昆弟，穆帝舅褚歆有表，中書答表朝廷無其儀，詔下議。
entries.en: Ai was Mu's cousin; Mu's uncle Chu Xin asked how to mourn; the Secretariat said no rule existed and the throne sent the case to debate.
entries.literal: The emperor toward Emperor Mu was a father's-brother's son; Emperor Mu's maternal uncle Chu Xin submitted a memorial; the Secretariat replied to the memorial that the court had no such precedent, and an edict sent the matter down for deliberation.

entries.zh: 尚書僕射江虨等四人並云，閔僖兄弟也，而為父子，則哀帝應為帝嗣。
entries.en: Jiang Pin and four others cited Duke Min and Duke Xi of Lu—brothers treated as father and son—and argued Ai should continue Cheng's line.
entries.literal: Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Jiang Pin and four others together said: 'Duke Min and Duke Xi were brothers yet treated as father and son—therefore Emperor Ai ought to follow the emperor's line of succession.'

entries.zh: 衛軍王述等二十五人云「成帝不私親愛，越授天倫，康帝受命顯宗。
entries.en: Guard General Wang Shu and twenty-five others said, "Emperor Cheng did not privately favor his own loved ones, but passed beyond natural kinship in conferring the succession, and Emperor Kang received the command from Xianzong.
entries.literal: Guard General Wang Shu and twenty-five others said, "Emperor Cheng did not privately favor his own loved ones, but passed beyond natural kinship in conferring the succession, and Emperor Kang received the command from Xianzong.

entries.zh: 社稷之重，已移所授，纂承之序，宜繼康皇。」
entries.en: The weight of the altars of soil and grain had already moved to the one who received it, and in the sequence of succession it is fitting to continue Emperor Kang."
entries.literal: The weight of the altars of soil and grain had already moved to the one who received it, and in the sequence of succession it is fitting to continue Emperor Kang."

entries.zh: 尚書謝奉等六人云：「繼體之正，宜本天屬，考之人情，宜繼顯宗也。」
entries.en: Xie Feng of the Secretariat and six others said, "The correctness of inheriting the body should be rooted in Heaven-given kinship. Examining it according to human feeling, it is fitting to continue Xianzong."
entries.literal: Xie Feng of the Secretariat and six others said, "The correctness of inheriting the body should be rooted in Heaven-given kinship. Examining it according to human feeling, it is fitting to continue Xianzong."

entries.zh: 詔從述等議，上繼顯宗。
entries.en: The edict sided with Wang Shu and made Ai heir to Emperor Yuan.
entries.literal: The edict followed Wang Shu and the others' debate and ordered succession to continue Emperor Yuan.

entries.zh: 寧康二年七月，簡文帝崩再周而遇閏。
entries.en: In the second year of Ningkang, in the seventh month, Emperor Jianwen died just as the second mourning round collided with an intercalary month.
entries.literal: In the second year of Ningkang, in the seventh month Emperor Jianwen died—the second full mourning cycle met an intercalary month.

entries.zh: 博士謝攸、孔粲議：「魯襄二十八年十二月乙未，楚子卒，實閏月而言十二月者，附正於前月也。
entries.en: Erudites Xie You and Kong Can deliberated, "In the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xiang of Lu, in the twelfth month, yiwei, the viscount of Chu died. It was actually an intercalary month, but saying twelfth month attached the regular designation to the preceding month.
entries.literal: Erudites Xie You and Kong Can deliberated, "In the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xiang of Lu, in the twelfth month, yiwei, the viscount of Chu died. It was actually an intercalary month, but saying twelfth month attached the regular designation to the preceding month.

entries.zh: 喪事先遠，則應用博士吳商之言，以閏月祥。」
entries.en: For mourning affairs, one first chooses what is distant; therefore one should use the words of Erudite Wu Shang and hold the xiang sacrifice in the intercalary month."
entries.literal: For mourning affairs, one first chooses what is distant; therefore one should use the words of Erudite Wu Shang and hold the xiang sacrifice in the intercalary month."

entries.zh: 尚書僕射謝安、中領軍王劭、散騎常侍鄭襲、右衛將軍殷康、驍騎將軍袁宏、散騎侍郎殷茂、中書郎車胤、左丞劉遵、吏部郎劉耽意皆同。
entries.en: Xie An, Wang Shao, Zheng Xi, Yin Kang, Yuan Hong, Yin Mao, Che Yin, Liu Zun, and Liu Dan concurred.
entries.literal: Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Xie An, Central Army commander Wang Shao, Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Zheng Xi, General of the Right Guard Yin Kang, General of Swift Cavalry Yuan Hong, Cavalier Gentleman Yin Mao, Palace Secretariat Secretary Che Yin, Left Assistant Liu Zun, Personnel Section chief Liu Dan—all agreed.

entries.zh: 康曰：「過七月而未及八月，豈可謂之逾期。
entries.en: Yin Kang said, "To pass the seventh month but not yet reach the eighth: how could this be called exceeding the term?
entries.literal: Yin Kang said, "To pass the seventh month but not yet reach the eighth: how could this be called exceeding the term?

entries.zh: 必所不了，則當從其重者。」
entries.en: If it truly cannot be settled, then one should follow the weightier option."
entries.literal: If it truly cannot be settled, then one should follow the weightier option."

entries.zh: 宏曰：「假值閏十二月而不取者，此則歲未終，固不可得矣。
entries.en: Yuan Hong said, "If it happened to be an intercalary twelfth month and one did not take it, then the year would not yet be complete, and this certainly could not be done.
entries.literal: Yuan Hong said, "If it happened to be an intercalary twelfth month and one did not take it, then the year would not yet be complete, and this certainly could not be done.

entries.zh: 《漢書》以閏為後九月，明其同體也。」
entries.en: The Han shu treats an intercalary month as a later ninth month, showing that it is of the same body."
entries.literal: The Han shu treats an intercalary month as a later ninth month, showing that it is of the same body."

entries.zh: 襲曰：「中宗、肅祖皆以閏月崩，祥除之變皆用閏之後月。
entries.en: Zheng Xi said, "Zhongzong and Suzong both died in intercalary months, and in the changes of xiang sacrifice and removal, all used the month after the intercalary month.
entries.literal: Zheng Xi said, "Zhongzong and Suzong both died in intercalary months, and in the changes of xiang sacrifice and removal, all used the month after the intercalary month.

entries.zh: 先朝尚用閏之後月，今閏附七月，取之何疑，亦合遠日申情之言。
entries.en: The former court still used the month after the intercalary month. Now the intercalary month is attached to the seventh month; what doubt is there in taking it? This also accords with the statement that a distant day extends the feeling.
entries.literal: The former court still used the month after the intercalary month. Now the intercalary month is attached to the seventh month; what doubt is there in taking it? This also accords with the statement that a distant day extends the feeling.

entries.zh: 又閏是後七而非八也，豈逾月之嫌乎！」
entries.en: Moreover, the intercalary month is after the seventh and is not the eighth; how could there be suspicion of exceeding the month!"
entries.literal: Moreover, the intercalary month is after the seventh and is not the eighth; how could there be suspicion of exceeding the month!"

entries.zh: 尚書令王彪之、侍中王混、中丞譙王恬、右丞戴謐等議異，彪之曰：「吳商中才小官，非名賢碩儒、公輔重臣、為時所準則者。
entries.en: Director of the Secretariat Wang Biaozhi, Palace Attendant Wang Hun, Censor-in-Chief Prince Tian of Qiao, Right Assistant Director Dai Mi, and others deliberated differently. Biaozhi said, "Wu Shang was a man of middling talent and a minor official, not a famous worthy, great classicist, high minister, or weighty servant whom the age should take as a standard.
entries.literal: Director of the Secretariat Wang Biaozhi, Palace Attendant Wang Hun, Censor-in-Chief Prince Tian of Qiao, Right Assistant Director Dai Mi, and others deliberated differently. Biaozhi said, "Wu Shang was a man of middling talent and a minor official, not a famous worthy, great classicist, high minister, or weighty servant whom the age should take as a standard.

entries.zh: 又取閏無證據，直攬遠日之義，越祥忌，限外取，不合卜遠之理。
entries.en: Moreover, taking the intercalary month has no evidence. It merely seizes on the meaning of the distant day, passes beyond the xiang taboo, and takes something outside the limit; this does not accord with the principle of divining the distant day.
entries.literal: Moreover, taking the intercalary month has no evidence. It merely seizes on the meaning of the distant day, passes beyond the xiang taboo, and takes something outside the limit; this does not accord with the principle of divining the distant day.

entries.zh: 又丞相桓公嘗論云，《禮》二十五月大祥。
entries.en: Furthermore, Chancellor Huan once argued that according to ritual the great xiang sacrifice is in the twenty-fifth month.
entries.literal: Furthermore, Chancellor Huan once argued that according to ritual the great xiang sacrifice is in the twenty-fifth month.

entries.zh: 何緣越期取閏，乃二十六月乎？」
entries.en: On what basis would one pass beyond the term and take the intercalary month, making it the twenty-sixth month?"
entries.literal: On what basis would one pass beyond the term and take the intercalary month, making it the twenty-sixth month?"

entries.zh: 於是啟曰：「或以閏附七月，宜用閏月除者。
entries.en: Thereupon they submitted, "Some consider that because the intercalary month is attached to the seventh month, the intercalary month should be used for removal.
entries.literal: Thereupon they submitted, "Some consider that because the intercalary month is attached to the seventh month, the intercalary month should be used for removal.

entries.zh: 或以閏名雖除七月，而實以三旬別為一月，故應以七月除者。
entries.en: Others consider that although the intercalary month is named as attached to the seventh month, in reality the three ten-day periods separately make one month, and therefore the seventh month should be used for removal.
entries.literal: Others consider that although the intercalary month is named as attached to the seventh month, in reality the three ten-day periods separately make one month, and therefore the seventh month should be used for removal.

entries.zh: 臣等與中軍將軍沖參詳，一代大禮，宜準經典。
entries.en: We your servants, together with General of the Central Army Chong, have examined the matter in detail. A great ritual of one age should take the classics as its standard.
entries.literal: We your servants, together with General of the Central Army Chong, have examined the matter in detail. A great ritual of one age should take the classics as its standard.

entries.zh: 三年之喪，十三月而練，二十五月而畢，《禮》之明文也。

entries.zh: 武帝楊悼皇后既母養懷帝，后遇難時，懷帝尚幼，及即位，中詔述后恩愛。
entries.en: Empress Yang had raised the future Emperor Huai; when she was killed he was still a child, and on enthronement he issued a palace rescript praising her care.
entries.literal: Empress Yang Dao of Emperor Wu had already mother-nurtured Emperor Huai; when she later met violent death, Emperor Huai was still young; when he ascended, an inner edict recounted the empress's kindness and love.

entries.zh: 及后祖載，群官議帝應為追制服，或以庶母慈己，依禮制小功五月，或以謂慈母服如母服齊衰者，眾議不同。
entries.en: At her cortège the ministries split: some wanted retroactive weeds, some cited a nurturing concubine's xiao gong, some equated her to a legal mother in qi-cui.
entries.literal: When later her funeral train departed, the many offices debated whether the emperor ought wear retroactive mourning—or some said because a concubine-mother had loved him, by ritual he should wear xiao gong five months—or some said foster-mother mourning like a mother's qi-cui—the many opinions differed.

entries.zh: 閭丘沖議云：「楊后母養聖上，蓋以曲情。
entries.en: Luqiu Chong debated: 'Empress Yang mother-nurtured the sage ascendant—generally out of special affection.
entries.literal: Luqiu Chong debated: 'Empress Yang mother-nurtured the sage ascendant—generally out of special affection.

entries.zh: 今以恩禮追崇，不配世祖廟。
entries.en: Now by kindness and ritual we posthumously honor her—not pairing her in Emperor Shizu's temple.
entries.literal: Now by kindness and ritual we posthumously honor her—not pairing her in Emperor Shizu's temple.

entries.zh: 王者無慈養之服，謂宜祖載之日，可三朝素服發哀而已。」
entries.en: For kings there is no garment for 'foster nurturing'; I say on the day of the funeral train, three court sessions in plain dress to raise mourning is enough.'
entries.literal: For kings there is no garment for 'foster nurturing'; I say on the day of the funeral train, three court sessions in plain dress to raise mourning is enough.'

entries.zh: 於是從之。

entries.zh: 孝武甯康中，崇德太后褚氏崩。
entries.en: During Ningkang, Empress Dowager Chongde of the Chu clan died.
entries.literal: In Emperor Xiaowu's Ningkang era, Empress Dowager Chongde née Chu died.

entries.zh: 后於帝為從嫂，或疑其服。
entries.en: To the reigning emperor she was a sister-in-law, so ministers argued the garment.
entries.literal: Toward the emperor she was his elder brother's wife—some doubted the mourning grade.

entries.zh: 博士徐藻議，以為：「資父事君而敬同。
entries.en: Erudite Xu Zao debated, holding that 'nurturing a father and serving a lord share the same reverence.
entries.literal: Erudite Xu Zao debated, holding that 'nurturing a father and serving a lord share the same reverence.

entries.zh: 又，禮，其夫屬父道者，其妻皆母道也。
entries.en: Moreover by ritual: when a husband falls under the 'father's way,' his wives all fall under the 'mother's way.'
entries.literal: Moreover by ritual: when a husband falls under the 'father's way,' his wives all fall under the 'mother's way.'

entries.zh: 則夫屬君道，妻亦后道矣。
entries.en: Then when the husband falls under the 'lord's way,' the wife likewise falls under the 'empress's way.'
entries.literal: Then when the husband falls under the 'lord's way,' the wife likewise falls under the 'empress's way.'

entries.zh: 服后宜以資母之義。
entries.en: For the empress dowager one ought by the meaning of a nurturing mother.
entries.literal: For the empress dowager one ought by the meaning of a nurturing mother.

entries.zh: 魯譏逆祀，以明尊尊。
entries.en: Lu reproached inverted sacrifice—to clarify honoring the honored.

entries.zh: 今上躬奉康、穆、哀皇及靖后之祀，致敬同於所天。

entries.literal: Now the sovereign personally attends sacrifice to Emperors Kang, Mu, and Ai and to Empress Jing—pays utmost reverence the same as to Heaven.

entries.en: Chenliu memorialized that the Duke of Yan was the king's natural father; once the king had been given to continue Emperor Ming's line, the duke counted only as a congfu relative. Officials proposed qi-grade mourning with no reduction for intimacy or rank.
entries.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Chenliu state reported—the Duke of Yan is the king's father—the king went out to serve Emperor Ming's sacrifices—now toward the king [the duke] is congfu kin—the offices memorialized [the duke] ought wear qi (one full cycle) mourning—not lowering by kin distance or honor base.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「王奉魏氏，所承者重，不得服其私親。」
entries.en: Edict stated: "The king carries Wei house—the inheritance is weighty—may not wear for private kin."
entries.literal: Edict stated: "The king carries Wei house—the inheritance is weighty—may not wear for private kin."

entries.zh: 穆帝時，東海國言，哀王薨逾年，嗣王乃來繼，不復追服，群臣皆已反吉，國妃亦宜同除。
entries.en: Later, under Emperor Mu, Donghai argued that King Ai had been dead more than a year before the heir arrived, so no retroactive mourning was worn; ministers had all returned to felicity garb, and the princess-consort should shed weeds as well.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Mu, Donghai state reported—King Ai died over a year—then the successor king came to continue—did not retroactively wear mourning—all ministers already returned auspicious—the state's royal consort likewise ought remove together.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「朝廷所以從權制者，以王事奪之，非為變禮也。

entries.literal: Edict stated: "Why the court followed expedient regulation—because royal affairs seized them—not to alter the rites.

entries.en: Women's transmitting weight—right meaning is great—if following expedient regulation—where will right rest!"
entries.literal: Women's transmitting weight—right meaning is great—if following expedient regulation—where will right rest!"

entries.zh: 於是國妃終三年之禮。
entries.en: The princess-consort therefore observed the full three-year mourning.

entries.literal: Cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Xie Heng held: "For a feudal lord's heir apparent, sworn presentation versus not yet sworn—the honored base and bodily tie differ.

entries.literal: The Mourning Garments [canon] states mourning for the eldest legitimate son's long shang means not yet sworn; once sworn then it is not [counted as] shang."

entries.en: When a male can guard altars of soil and grain and a female can uphold the wifely way—in years when completion is possible yet matters already accomplished—therefore may be without shang—it does not mean infant teeth.

entries.literal: All shangs that ought be weighted—great officers add no garment—yet to make the supremacy alone bear the weight—never before heard."

entries.en: Director of the Palace Library Zhi Yu said: "The heir apparent from birth is raised with adult rites—then shang principle is removed.
entries.literal: Director of the Palace Library Zhi Yu said: "The heir apparent from birth is raised with adult rites—then shang principle is removed.

entries.literal: The grand heir likewise forms one body with the lord and transmits weight—garments follow from position achieved, wholly not by age.

entries.zh: 天子無服殤之義，絕期故也。」
entries.en: The Son of Heaven has no principle of wearing [mourning for] shang—because [such ties] are cut off at one full cycle (qi)."
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven has no principle of wearing [mourning for] shang—because [such ties] are cut off at one full cycle (qi)."

entries.zh: 漢魏故事，大喪及大臣之喪，執紼者輓歌。

entries.literal: Han-Wei precedent: great mourning and great ministers' mourning—those holding tow-ropes sang dirges.

entries.en: The New Rites traced those laments to corvée labor songs under Emperor Wu—voices sharp with grief—and showed how they had hardened into funeral practice.
entries.literal: The New Rites held dirges arose from Han Emperor Wu's corvée people's labor songs—sound mournful and piercing—thereupon taken as seeing-off-the-end rite.

entries.zh: 雖音曲摧愴，非經典所制，違禮設銜枚之義。

entries.literal: Though melody is crushing-grief—not fashioned by classics—contravenes the rites' meaning of mouth-plugs.

entries.en: Mid-wail for the dead, nothing should parade under the label of "song."
entries.literal: Just now in wailing longing—not fitting to take 'song' as name.

entries.zh: 除，不輓歌。
entries.en: The reform abolished pulling-dirges altogether.
entries.literal: Removed—no dirges.

entries.zh: 摯虞以為：「輓歌因倡和而為摧愴之聲，銜枚所以全哀，此亦以感眾。
entries.en: Zhi Yu held: "Dirges through lead-and-chorus become crushing sounds—mouth-plugs thereby preserve mourning—this too thereby moves the crowd.

entries.zh: 宜定新禮如舊。」

entries.en: Under Emperor Wu in the eleventh month an edict read: "When princes, dukes, or great ministers die, those who owe three audiences of mourning shall have no music for over a month; those who owe one audience shall have no music for three days."
entries.literal: Under Emperor Wu in the eleventh month an edict read: "When princes, dukes, or great ministers die, those who owe three audiences of mourning shall have no music for over a month; those who owe one audience shall have no music for three days."

entries.zh: 元帝姨廣昌鄉君喪，未葬，中丞熊遠表云：「案《禮》『君于卿大夫，比葬不食肉，比卒哭不舉樂』，惻隱之心未忍行吉事故也。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan's maternal aunt the Lady of Guangchang village died, before burial Palace Secretary Xiong Yuan memorialized: "The Rites say the lord toward ministers and great officers—before burial does not eat meat, before the end of wailing does not raise music—because pitying hearts cannot yet bear auspicious business.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan's maternal aunt the Lady of Guangchang village died, before burial Palace Secretary Xiong Yuan memorialized: "The Rites say the lord toward ministers and great officers—before burial does not eat meat, before the end of wailing does not raise music—because pitying hearts cannot yet bear auspicious business.

entries.zh: 被尚書符，冬至後二日小會。
entries.en: A Secretariat directive scheduled a small court gathering two days after the winter solstice.
entries.literal: A Secretariat directive scheduled a small court gathering two days after the winter solstice.

entries.zh: 臣以為廣昌鄉君喪殯日，聖恩垂悼。

entries.literal: Your servant holds that on the Lady of Guangchang's encoffining day sagely grace should show condolence.

entries.zh: 禮，大夫死，廢一時之祭。
entries.en: By ritual, when a great officer dies, one season's sacrifice is suspended.
entries.literal: By ritual, when a great officer dies, one season's sacrifice is suspended.

entries.zh: 冬至唯可群下奉賀而已，未便小會。」

entries.literal: Winter solstice may only be an occasion for subordinates to offer congratulations—it is not yet fitting to convene a small assembly."

entries.zh: 詔以遠表示賀循，又曰：「武皇帝故事云『王公大臣薨，三朝發哀，逾月不舉樂，其一朝發哀，三日不舉樂』，此舊事明文。」
entries.en: The edict forwarded Xiong's statement to He Xun and added: "Emperor Wu's precedent reads: 'When princes, dukes, or great ministers die—three audiences of mourning, then no music for over a month; one audience, then no music for three days'—that old text is explicit."
entries.literal: The edict forwarded Xiong's statement to He Xun and added: "Emperor Wu's precedent reads: 'When princes, dukes, or great ministers die—three audiences of mourning, then no music for over a month; one audience, then no music for three days'—that old text is explicit."

entries.en: He Xun replied: "Reviewing the Rites, Miscellaneous Records: 'The lord toward a minister's or great officer's mourning—before burial does not eat meat, before the end of wailing does not raise music.

entries.en: In antiquity the bond between lord and minister was weighty: though the utmost honoring rites lowered the sovereign so he wore no full mourning, within three months he still dwelt in xi-cui and undertook no auspicious affairs.
entries.literal: In antiquity the bond between lord and minister was weighty: though the utmost honoring rites lowered the sovereign so he wore no full mourning, within three months he still dwelt in xi-cui and undertook no auspicious affairs.

entries.zh: 故春秋晉大夫智悼子未葬，平公作樂，為屠蒯所譏。
entries.en: Therefore the Spring and Autumn records that while Jin minister Zhi Ying lay unburied, Duke Ping ordered music and was rebuked by the blind musician Tu Kui.
entries.literal: Therefore the Spring and Autumn records that while Jin minister Zhi Ying lay unburied, Duke Ping ordered music and was rebuked by the blind musician Tu Kui.

entries.zh: 如遠所答，合于古義。
entries.en: Xiong Yuan's answer matches ancient meaning.
entries.literal: Xiong Yuan's answer matches ancient meaning.

entries.zh: 咸寧詔書雖不會經典，然隨時立宜，以為定制，誠非群下所得稱論。」，
entries.en: The Xianning edict may not tally with every classic, yet it set workable law for its day and became fixed statute—not something subordinates should reopen at will."
entries.literal: The Xianning edict may not tally with every classic, yet it set workable law for its day and became fixed statute—not something subordinates should reopen at will."

entries.zh: 升平元年，帝姑廬陵公主未葬，符問太常，冬至小會應作樂不。
entries.en: In Shengping 1, while Princess Luling still awaited burial, an official inquiry asked whether the winter-solstice dinner could have music.
entries.literal: In Shengping 1, the emperor's aunt, Princess Luling, had not yet been buried, and an official note asked the Chamberlain for Ceremonials whether music should be performed at the small winter-solstice gathering.

entries.zh: 博士胡訥議云：「君于卿大夫，比卒哭不舉樂。
entries.en: Erudite Hu Na argued: "The lord toward ministers and great officers does not raise music before the end of wailing.
entries.literal: Erudite Hu Na argued: "The lord toward ministers and great officers does not raise music before the end of wailing.

entries.zh: 公主有骨肉之親，宜闕樂。」
entries.en: The princess shares flesh-and-bone closeness—music ought to be omitted."
entries.literal: The princess shares flesh-and-bone closeness—music ought to be omitted."

entries.zh: 太常王彪之云：「案武帝詔，三朝舉哀，三旬乃舉樂；
entries.en: Chamberlain Wang Bianzhi said: "Reviewing Emperor Wu's edict—three audiences of mourning, then music only after three decad-days;
entries.literal: Chamberlain Wang Bianzhi said: "Reviewing Emperor Wu's edict—three audiences of mourning, then music only after three decad-days;

entries.zh: 其一朝舉哀者，三日則舉樂。
entries.en: those who hold one audience of mourning may raise music after three days.
entries.literal: those who hold one audience of mourning may raise music after three days.

entries.zh: 泰始十年春，長樂長公主薨，太康七年秋，扶風王駿薨，武帝並舉哀三日而已。
entries.en: In spring of the tenth year of Taishi, the Senior Princess of Changle died; in autumn of the seventh year of Taikang, Prince Jun of Fufeng died. For both, Emperor Wu held mourning for only three days.
entries.literal: In spring of the tenth year of Taishi, the Senior Princess of Changle died; in autumn of the seventh year of Taikang, Prince Jun of Fufeng died. For both, Emperor Wu held mourning for only three days.

entries.zh: 中興已後，更參論不改此制。
entries.en: Since the Eastern Restoration courts have debated again and never altered that system.
entries.literal: Since the Eastern Restoration courts have debated again and never altered that system.

entries.zh: 今小會宜作樂。」
entries.en: Therefore the small assembly ought use music."
entries.literal: Therefore the small assembly ought use music."

entries.zh: 二議竟不知所取。
entries.en: The ministries left the contradiction unresolved.
entries.literal: Between the two opinions the court never settled which to follow.

entries.zh: 宣帝豫自于首陽山為土藏，不填不樹，作《顧命終制》，斂以時服，不設明器。
entries.en: Sima Yi dug a plain shaft on Shouyang, left the hill unmarked, and left written orders for everyday clothes and no grave goods.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan in advance prepared an earthen burial chamber on Mount Shouyang—no mound, no trees—and composed the 'Charge at Gu' end testament: shroud in seasonal clothes only, with no ming vessels.

entries.zh: 景、文皆謹奉成命，無所加焉。
entries.en: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao kept Cao Pi's austere burial instructions to the letter.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing and Emperor Wen both scrupulously obeyed the completed testament and added nothing to it.

entries.zh: 景帝崩，喪事制度又依宣帝故事。
entries.en: Sima Shi's obsequies copied Sima Yi's lean model.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing died, the funeral regulations again followed Emperor Xuan's precedent.

entries.zh: 武帝泰始四年，文明王皇后崩，將合葬，開崇陽陵，使太尉司馬望奉祭，進皇帝密璽綬于便房神坐。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu, when Empress Wenming Wang died and was about to be jointly buried, Chongyang Mausoleum was opened, Grand Commandant Sima Wang was sent to present sacrifice, and the emperor's sealed jade seal and cords were advanced to the spirit seat in the side chamber.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu, when Empress Wenming Wang died and was about to be jointly buried, Chongyang Mausoleum was opened, Grand Commandant Sima Wang was sent to present sacrifice, and the emperor's sealed jade seal and cords were advanced to the spirit seat in the side chamber.

entries.zh: 魏氏金璽，此又儉矣。
entries.en: Even the golden seal bespoke restraint.
entries.literal: Wei's gold seal—another mark of frugality.

entries.zh: 江左初，元、明崇儉，且百度草創，山陵奉終，省約備矣。
entries.en: When the court fled across the Yangzi, Sima Rui and Sima Shao kept burials modest while institutions were new.
entries.literal: Early in the southward court, Emperors Yuan and Ming prized simplicity; the hundred offices were still being founded, so imperial tombs stayed spare yet adequate.

entries.zh: 成帝咸康七年，皇后杜氏崩。
entries.en: Empress Du of Cheng passed in 341.
entries.literal: In the seventh Xiankang year of Emperor Cheng, Empress Du died.

entries.zh: 詔外官五日一入臨，內官旦一入而已，過葬虞祭禮畢止。
entries.en: Courtiers could wail only on that thin schedule until the post-burial service closed mourning.
entries.literal: An edict ordered outer officials to enter condolence only once every five days and inner staff once at dawn, ending once burial and the Yu rite were finished.

entries.zh: 有司奏，大行皇后陵所作凶門柏歷門，號顯陽端門。
entries.en: The ministry wanted a formal death-gate and cypress lintel named like a palace portal.
entries.literal: The offices proposed building a funeral gate and cypress "calendar" portal for the late empress's mound, to be named the Xianyang gate.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「門如所處。
entries.en: The edict read: "Let the gate stand where proposed.
entries.literal: The edict read: "Let the gate stand where proposed.

entries.zh: 凶門柏歷，大為煩費，停之。」
entries.en: Funeral gates and cypress calendars are extravagantly costly—suspend them."
entries.literal: Funeral gates and cypress calendars are extravagantly costly—suspend them."

entries.zh: 案蔡謨說，以二瓦器盛始死之祭，繫於木，裹以葦席，置庭中，近南，名為重，今之凶門是其象也。
entries.en: Cai Mo traced the "death gate" to the temporary chong bundle hung south of the yard.
entries.literal: Cai Mo explains that two earthen jars holding the first-death offerings were lashed to a frame, wrapped in reed matting, and set in the courtyard toward the south as a chong; today's funeral gate imitates that form.

entries.zh: 禮，既虞而作主，今未葬，未有主，故以重當之。
entries.en: Until the tablet existed, the chong served as the spirit's lodging.
entries.literal: By ritual one fashions the spirit tablet after the Yu rite; before burial there is no tablet, so the chong stands in for it.

entries.zh: 禮稱為主道，此其義也。
entries.en: Classical glosses treat the chong as the spirit's interim path.
entries.literal: The canon calls this the "lord-of-the-spirit path"—that is the idea.

entries.zh: 范堅又曰：「凶門非禮，禮有懸重，形似凶門。
entries.en: Fan Jian adds: "The funeral gate is not canonical; ritual only suspends a chong that merely resembles a gate.
entries.literal: Fan Jian adds: "The funeral gate is not canonical; ritual only suspends a chong that merely resembles a gate.

entries.zh: 後人出之門外以表喪，俗遂行之。
entries.en: Later generations moved it outside the gate to advertise mourning, and vulgar custom adopted it.
entries.literal: Later generations moved it outside the gate to advertise mourning, and vulgar custom adopted it.

entries.zh: 薄帳，即古弔幕之類也。」
entries.en: Thin curtains belong to the ancient class of mourning screens."
entries.literal: Thin curtains belong to the ancient class of mourning screens."

entries.zh: 是時，又詔曰：「重壤之下，豈宜崇飾無用，陵中唯潔掃而已。」
entries.en: Another edict then declared: "Beneath double layers of earth one should not lavish useless ornament; only sweep the vault clean."
entries.literal: Another edict then declared: "Beneath double layers of earth one should not lavish useless ornament; only sweep the vault clean."

entries.zh: 有司又奏，依舊選公卿以下六品子弟六十人為挽郎，詔又停之。
entries.en: Officials wanted sixty noble sons as rope-pullers; the throne again said no.
entries.literal: The offices again asked to conscript sixty youths of sixth rank and below as catafalque pullers, as of old; the edict again refused.

entries.zh: 孝武帝太元四年九月，皇后王氏崩。
entries.en: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, Empress Wang died.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, Empress Wang died.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「終事唯從儉速。」
entries.en: An edict said: "Finish everything frugally and quickly."
entries.literal: An edict said: "Finish everything frugally and quickly."

entries.zh: 又詔：「遠近不得遣山陵使。」
entries.en: Another edict said, “Neither near nor distant officials may send envoys to the imperial tombs.”
entries.literal: Another edict said, “Neither near nor distant officials may send envoys to the imperial tombs.”

entries.zh: 有司奏選挽郎二十四人，詔停之。
entries.en: Even twenty-four rope-boys were denied.
entries.literal: When the ministry asked for twenty-four pullers, the edict stopped that as well.

entries.zh: 及宣帝，遺詔「子弟群官皆不得謁陵」。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan's testament commanded that "sons, younger kin, and all officials must not visit the imperial tombs."
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan's testament commanded that "sons, younger kin, and all officials must not visit the imperial tombs."

entries.zh: 於是景、文遵旨。
entries.en: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao complied.
entries.literal: Jing and Wen obeyed that order.

entries.zh: 至武帝，猶再謁崇陽陵，一謁峻平陵，然遂不敢謁高原陵，至惠帝復止也。
entries.en: Sima Yan alone made limited visits, never to Cao Cao's mound, and Hui abandoned the habit entirely.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu still visited Chongyang twice and Junping once, yet never dared approach Gaoling; under Emperor Hui the custom lapsed again.

entries.zh: 逮于江左，元帝崩後，諸公始有謁陵辭告之事。
entries.en: Eastern Jin nobles only began tomb pilgrimages after Sima Rui's death.
entries.literal: After the move south of the Yangzi, not until Emperor Yuan died did high nobles begin visiting mausoleums to announce their leave-takings.

entries.zh: 蓋由眷同友執，率情而舉，非洛京之舊也。
entries.en: The practice sprang from camaraderie's impulse, not old capital law.
entries.literal: They acted from private friendship among peers, not from Luoyang precedent.

entries.zh: 成帝時，中宮亦年年拜陵，議者以為非禮，於是遂止，以為永制。
entries.en: Cheng's harem stopped annual tomb trips once ritualists objected.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Cheng the inner palace yearly visited tombs until critics called it uncanonical; the court then banned it permanently.

entries.zh: 至穆帝時，褚太后臨朝，又拜陵，帝幼故也。
entries.en: Mu's regent mother revived the visits while the sovereign was a child.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Mu, Empress Dowager Chu regent, tombs were visited again because the boy emperor was young.

entries.zh: 至孝武崩，驃騎將軍司馬道子曰：「今雖權制釋服，至於朔望諸節，自應展情陵所，以一周為斷。」
entries.en: After Xiaowu died, Sima Daozi said: "Though we have shortened mourning by expedient rule, on new and full moons and festivals we should still show feeling at the tomb—take one round as the limit."
entries.literal: After Xiaowu died, Sima Daozi said: "Though we have shortened mourning by expedient rule, on new and full moons and festivals we should still show feeling at the tomb—take one round as the limit."

entries.zh: 於是至陵，變服單衣，煩黷無準，非禮意也。
entries.en: The result was slovenly dress and chaotic etiquette at every visit.
entries.literal: Thereupon courtiers went to the tombs in thin single garments—endless fuss with no standard, contrary to ritual intent.

entries.zh: 及安帝元興元年，尚書左僕射桓謙奏：「百僚拜陵，起于中興，非晉舊典，積習生常，遂為近法。
entries.en: In the first year of Yuanxing under Emperor An, Huan Qian, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, memorialized, "The hundred officials paying respects at the mausoleum began with the Restoration and was not an old Jin statute. Accumulated practice produced a norm, and it consequently became a recent rule.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing under Emperor An, Huan Qian, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, memorialized, "The hundred officials paying respects at the mausoleum began with the Restoration and was not an old Jin statute. Accumulated practice produced a norm, and it consequently became a recent rule.

entries.zh: 尋武皇帝詔，乃不使人主諸王拜陵，豈唯百僚！
entries.en: Review Emperor Wu's edict: he forbade even the sovereign and princes from tomb visits—let alone mere officials!
entries.literal: Review Emperor Wu's edict: he forbade even the sovereign and princes from tomb visits—let alone mere officials!

entries.zh: 謂宜遵奉。」
entries.en: We ought to obey that precedent."
entries.literal: We ought to obey that precedent."

entries.zh: 於是施行。
entries.en: The ban took effect.
entries.literal: The measure was implemented.

entries.zh: 及義熙初，又復江左之舊，
entries.en: Yixi reopened tomb pilgrimages for a time.
entries.literal: Early in the Yixi era the southern custom briefly returned.

entries.zh: 安豐太守程諒先已有妻，後又娶，遂立二嫡。
entries.en: Cheng Liang, prefect of Anfeng, already had a wife, then married again, thus setting up two principals.'
entries.literal: Cheng Liang, prefect of Anfeng, already had a wife, then married again, thus setting up two principals.'

entries.zh: 前妻亡，後妻子勳疑所服。
entries.en: When the first wife died, the later wife's son Xun doubted what to wear.'
entries.literal: When the first wife died, the later wife's son Xun doubted what to wear.'

entries.zh: 中書令張華造甲乙之問曰：「甲娶乙為妻，後又娶丙，匿不說有乙，居家如二嫡，無有貴賤之差。
entries.en: Prefect of the Masters of Writing Zhang Hua posed a paired question: "A took B as wife, later took C, hiding that B existed—he lived as if with two principals of equal rank.
entries.literal: Prefect of the Masters of Writing Zhang Hua posed a paired question: "A took B as wife, later took C, hiding that B existed—he lived as if with two principals of equal rank.

entries.zh: 乙亡，丙之子當何服？
entries.en: When B died, what should C's son wear?
entries.literal: When B died, what should C's son wear?

entries.zh: 本實並列，嫡庶不殊，雖二嫡非正，此失在先人，人子何得專制析其親也。
entries.en: In truth both stood coequal; principal and secondary were not distinguished—though two principals are irregular, the fault lies with the elders; how may a child on his own sever kin!
entries.literal: In truth both stood coequal; principal and secondary were not distinguished—though two principals are irregular, the fault lies with the elders; how may a child on his own sever kin!

entries.zh: 若為庶母服，又不成為庶。
entries.en: If he wears mourning for a concubine-mother, he cannot really be a concubine son.
entries.literal: If he wears mourning for a concubine-mother, he cannot really be a concubine son.

entries.zh: 進退不知所從。」
entries.en: He cannot decide whether to advance or retreat.'
entries.literal: He cannot decide whether to advance or retreat.'

entries.zh: 太傅鄭沖議曰：「甲失禮於家，二嫡並在，誠非人子所得正。
entries.en: Grand Tutor Zheng Chong answered: "A failed ritual at home—two principals present—is not something a child may correct.
entries.literal: Grand Tutor Zheng Chong answered: "A failed ritual at home—two principals present—is not something a child may correct.

entries.zh: 則乙丙之子並當三年，禮疑從重。」
entries.en: Then sons of both B and C should wear three years; when ritual doubts, follow the heavier.'
entries.literal: Then sons of both B and C should wear three years; when ritual doubts, follow the heavier.'

entries.zh: 車騎賈充、侍中少傅任愷議略與鄭同。
entries.en: General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong and Palace Attendant Junior Tutor Ren Kai largely agreed with Zheng.'
entries.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong and Palace Attendant Junior Tutor Ren Kai largely agreed with Zheng.'

entries.zh: 太尉荀顗議曰：「《春秋》並后匹嫡，古之明典也。
entries.en: Grand Commandant Xun Yi answered: "The Spring and Autumn treats two coequal empresses as a clear mirror of error.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant Xun Yi answered: "The Spring and Autumn treats two coequal empresses as a clear mirror of error.

entries.zh: 今不可以犯禮並立二妻，不別尊卑而遂其失也。
entries.en: Today one cannot break ritual to keep two wives; one must not blur noble and base and perpetuate the fault.
entries.literal: Today one cannot break ritual to keep two wives; one must not blur noble and base and perpetuate the fault.

entries.zh: 故當斷之以禮，先至為嫡，後至為庶。
entries.en: Therefore ritual must decide: first arrival is principal, later is secondary.
entries.literal: Therefore ritual must decide: first arrival is principal, later is secondary.

entries.zh: 丙子宜以嫡母服乙，乙子宜以庶母事丙。
entries.en: C's son should mourn B as principal mother; B's son should serve C as secondary mother.
entries.literal: C's son should mourn B as principal mother; B's son should serve C as secondary mother.

entries.zh: 昔屈建去芰，古人以為違禮而得禮。
entries.en: Formerly Qu Jian cast aside water caltrop—ancients thought him wrong on the letter yet right on ritual.
entries.literal: Formerly Qu Jian cast aside water caltrop—ancients thought him wrong on the letter yet right on ritual.

entries.zh: 丙子非為抑其親，斯自奉禮先後貴賤順敘之義也。」
entries.en: C's son is not belittling kin—he follows the sequence of ritual precedence.'
entries.literal: C's son is not belittling kin—he follows the sequence of ritual precedence.'

entries.zh: 中書監荀勖議曰：「昔鄉里鄭子群娶陳司空從妹，後隔呂布之亂，不復相知存亡，更娶鄉里蔡氏女。
entries.en: Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu answered: "Formerly Zheng Ziqun of the village married a cousin of Director Chen; later, separated by Lu Bu's chaos, he could not learn whether she lived, and remarried a Cai woman in the village.
entries.literal: Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu answered: "Formerly Zheng Ziqun of the village married a cousin of Director Chen; later, separated by Lu Bu's chaos, he could not learn whether she lived, and remarried a Cai woman in the village.

entries.zh: 徐州平定，陳氏得還，遂二妃並存。
entries.en: When Xuzhou was pacified, the Chen lady returned—then both consorts coexisted.
entries.literal: When Xuzhou was pacified, the Chen lady returned—then both consorts coexisted.

entries.zh: 蔡氏之子字元釁，為陳氏服嫡母之服，事陳公以從舅之禮。
entries.en: The Cai son, styled Yuanxin, wore principal mourning for the Chen lady and served Director Chen by the courtesy due a maternal uncle.
entries.literal: The Cai son, styled Yuanxin, wore principal mourning for the Chen lady and served Director Chen by the courtesy due a maternal uncle.

entries.zh: 族兄宗伯曾責元釁，謂抑其親，鄉里先達以元釁為合宜。
entries.en: A senior kinsman once reproached Yuanxin for belittling kin, yet village worthies approved him.
entries.literal: A senior kinsman once reproached Yuanxin for belittling kin, yet village worthies approved him.

entries.zh: 不審此事粗相似否。」，
entries.en: He asked whether the present case is broadly similar.'
entries.literal: He asked whether the present case is broadly similar.'

entries.zh: 《五經通義》以為有德則諡善，無德則諡惡，故雖君臣可同。
entries.en: "Tongyi of the Five Classics" holds that if one is virtuous, the posthumous title will be good, and if there is no virtue, the posthumous title will be evil, so although the emperor and his ministers can be the same.
entries.literal: "Tongyi of the Five Classics" holds that if one is virtuous, the posthumous title will be good, and if there is no virtue, the posthumous title will be evil, so although the emperor and his ministers can be the same.

entries.zh: 魏朝初諡''『宣帝為文侯，景王為武侯』''，文王表不宜與二祖同，於是改諡宣文、忠武。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Wei Dynasty, the posthumous titles were ""Emperor Xuan was Marquis Wen, and King Jing was Marquis Wu". It was inappropriate for King Wen to have the same title as his second ancestor, so the posthumous titles were changed to Xuanwen and Zhongwu.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Wei Dynasty, the posthumous titles were ""Emperor Xuan was Marquis Wen, and King Jing was Marquis Wu". It was inappropriate for King Wen to have the same title as his second ancestor, so the posthumous titles were changed to Xuanwen and Zhongwu.

entries.zh: 至文王受晉王之號，魏帝又追命宣文為宣王，忠武為景王。
entries.en: When King Wen received the title of King of Jin, Emperor Wei also appointed Xuanwen as King Xuan and Zhongwu as King Jing.
entries.literal: When King Wen received the title of King of Jin, Emperor Wei also appointed Xuanwen as King Xuan and Zhongwu as King Jing.

entries.zh: 太康八年十月，太常上諡故太常平陵男郭奕為景侯。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Taikang, in October, Taichang was given the posthumous title, so Guo Yi, the man from Pingling, Taichang, was given the title of Marquis of Jing.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Taikang, in October, Taichang was given the posthumous title, so Guo Yi, the man from Pingling, Taichang, was given the title of Marquis of Jing.

entries.zh: 有司奏云：「晉受命以來，祖宗號諡群下未有同者，故郭奕為景，與景皇同，不可聽，宜諡曰穆。」
entries.en: An official report said: "Since the Jin Dynasty, there has been no one with the same posthumous title for his ancestors. Therefore, Guo Yi is the king of Jing, and he is the same as Emperor Jing. It is not acceptable to listen to him, so it is appropriate to give him the posthumous title Mu."
entries.literal: An official report said: "Since the Jin Dynasty, there has been no one with the same posthumous title for his ancestors. Therefore, Guo Yi is the king of Jing, and he is the same as Emperor Jing. It is not acceptable to listen to him, so it is appropriate to give him the posthumous title Mu."

entries.zh: 王濟、羊璞等並云：「夫無窮之祚，名諡不一，若皆相避，于制難全。
entries.en: Wang Ji, Yang Pu, and the others all said: “In an endless imperial blessing, personal names and posthumous titles are not all the same; if all are mutually avoided, the system is hard to complete.
entries.literal: Wang Ji, Yang Pu, and the others all said: “In an endless imperial blessing, personal names and posthumous titles are not all the same; if all are mutually avoided, the system is hard to complete.

entries.zh: 如悉不避，復非推崇事尊之禮。
entries.en: If none are avoided, that again is not the rite of exalting and serving the honored.
entries.literal: If none are avoided, that again is not the rite of exalting and serving the honored.

entries.zh: 宜依諱名之義，但及七廟祖宗而已，不及遷毀之廟。」
entries.en: It is fitting to follow the meaning of name taboo only as far as the ancestors in the seven temples, and not extend it to temples whose tablets have been moved out or destroyed.”
entries.literal: It is fitting to follow the meaning of name taboo only as far as the ancestors in the seven temples, and not extend it to temples whose tablets have been moved out or destroyed.”

entries.zh: 成粲、武茂、劉訥並云：「同諡非嫌。
entries.en: Cheng Can, Wu Mao and Liu Na all said, "It is not inappropriate to have the same posthumous title.
entries.literal: Cheng Can, Wu Mao and Liu Na all said, "It is not inappropriate to have the same posthumous title.

entries.zh: 號諡者，國之大典，所以厲時作教，經天人之遠旨也。
entries.en: The person with the posthumous title is the grand ceremony of the country, so he teaches in a timely manner and obeys the distant decrees of heaven and man.
entries.literal: The person with the posthumous title is the grand ceremony of the country, so he teaches in a timely manner and obeys the distant decrees of heaven and man.

entries.zh: 固雖君父，義有所不隆，及在臣子，或以行顯。
entries.en: Even though you are a king and father, your righteousness is not upheld, and it may be shown by your actions to your ministers.
entries.literal: Even though you are a king and father, your righteousness is not upheld, and it may be shown by your actions to your ministers.

entries.zh: 故能使上下邁德，罔有怠荒。
entries.en: Therefore, it can bring great virtue to both the superiors and subordinates, without any laziness or neglect.
entries.literal: Therefore, it can bring great virtue to both the superiors and subordinates, without any laziness or neglect.

entries.zh: 臣願聖世同符堯舜，行周同諡之禮，舍漢魏近制相避之議。」
entries.en: I hope that the Holy World will be the same as Yao and Shun, and that the posthumous rites of Zhou Dynasty will be the same, and that the modern system of Han and Wei will be avoided.”
entries.literal: I hope that the Holy World will be the same as Yao and Shun, and that the posthumous rites of Zhou Dynasty will be the same, and that the modern system of Han and Wei will be avoided.”

entries.zh: 又引周公父子同諡曰文。
entries.en: He also cited Zhou Gong and his son as having the same posthumous title.
entries.literal: He also cited Zhou Gong and his son as having the same posthumous title.

entries.zh: 武帝詔曰：「非言君臣不可同，正以奕諡景不相當耳，宜諡曰簡。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu issued an edict: "It is not necessary to say that the emperor and his ministers cannot be the same. Since the posthumous title of Yi is not commensurate with the scenery, it is appropriate to give him the posthumous title of Jian."
entries.literal: Emperor Wu issued an edict: "It is not necessary to say that the emperor and his ministers cannot be the same. Since the posthumous title of Yi is not commensurate with the scenery, it is appropriate to give him the posthumous title of Jian."

entries.zh: 及太元四年，侍中王欣之表君臣之嫌同諡，尚書奏以欣之言為然。
entries.en: In Taiyuan 4, Palace Attendant Wang Xinzhi objected that ruler and minister should not share a posthumous title, and the Masters of Writing endorsed his view.
entries.literal: When it came to Taiyuan 4, Palace Attendant Wang Xinzhi memorialized that ruler and minister should avoid sharing the same posthumous title, and the Masters of Writing reported that Xinzhi's statement was correct.

entries.zh: 詔可。
entries.en: The edict can be issued.
entries.literal: The edict can be issued.

entries.zh: 五禮之別，二曰凶。
entries.en: Among the five canonical rituals, the second category is mourning for the dead.
entries.literal: Of the five kinds of ritual, the second is called 'inauspicious' (mourning).

entries.zh: 自天子至於庶人，身體髮膚，受之父母，其理既均，其情亦等，生則養，死則哀，故曰三年之喪，天下之達禮者也。
entries.en: From the sovereign to the humblest subject, flesh and hair come from one's parents; the duty is the same and the grief no different—while they live we sustain them, when they die we mourn them. Hence the canon calls three years' mourning the rite that runs through all the world.
entries.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, body, skin, and hair are received from father and mother; the principle is uniform and the feeling equal—in life they nurture, in death they mourn; therefore it is said that three years' mourning is the penetrating rite of the realm.

entries.zh: 漢禮，天子崩，自不豫至於登遐及葬，喪紀之制，與夫三代變易。
entries.en: Han court precedent for an emperor's death—from the first illness through the lying-in-state to interment—shifted its mourning code across the Xia, Shang, and Zhou models.
entries.literal: Under Han ritual, when the Son of Heaven collapsed, from the first illness through the final journey to burial, the mourning regulations changed with the Three Dynasties.

entries.zh: 魏晉以來，大體同漢。
entries.en: From the Wei through the Jin, the dynasty largely kept Han practice.
entries.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, the broad pattern matched Han.

entries.zh: 然自漢文革喪禮之制，後代遵之，無復三年之禮。
entries.en: Yet once Emperor Wen of Han pared the mourning statutes, every succeeding age copied his shortcut, and the full three-year observance disappeared.
entries.literal: Yet from Emperor Wen of Han's reform of mourning regulations, later ages followed it and no longer practiced three years' mourning.

entries.zh: 及魏武臨終，遺令「天下尚未安定，未得遵古。
entries.en: When Wei Wu was near death, he left a command: 'All under Heaven is not yet settled; I cannot follow antiquity.
entries.literal: When Wei Wu was near death, he left a command: 'All under Heaven is not yet settled; I cannot follow antiquity.

entries.zh: 百官當臨中者，十五舉音，葬畢便除。
entries.en: For the hundred officials who should attend at the central halt, raise the dirge fifteen times; when burial is finished, remove mourning at once.
entries.literal: For the hundred officials who should attend at the central halt, raise the dirge fifteen times; when burial is finished, remove mourning at once.

entries.zh: 其將兵屯戍者，不得離部。」
entries.en: Those who command troops on garrison may not leave their commands.'
entries.literal: Those who command troops on garrison may not leave their commands.'

entries.zh: 魏武以正月庚子崩，辛丑即殯，是月丁卯葬，是為不逾月也。
entries.en: Cao Cao died on the gengzi day of the first month; by xinchou the bier stood ready; dingmao that same month saw the interment—mourning lifted inside a single month.
entries.literal: Wei Wu died on gengzi in the first month; on xinchou he was encoffined; on dingmao that same month he was buried—this is what is meant by 'not exceeding one month.'

entries.zh: 武皇帝采漢魏之遺范，覽景文之垂則，鼎鼐唯新，前音不改。
entries.en: Jin’s Emperor Wu took Han–Wei patterns as his mold, reviewed precedents left by Emperors Jing and Wen, replaced the ritual vessels, yet kept the older musical substance intact.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin adopted Han and Wei survivals, surveyed the lasting norms left by Jing and Wen, renewed the tripod vessels of state, yet left earlier musical substance unchanged.

entries.zh: 泰始九年，光祿大夫荀勖始作古尺，以調聲韻，仍以張華等所制高文，陳諸下管。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Taishi, the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Xun Xu first fashioned ancient foot-rules to tune intervals, then still employed the majestic pieces Zhang Hua’s circle had written, presenting them beneath the standing pipes.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Taishi, Minister Guanglu Xun Xu first fashioned ancient foot-rules to regulate modes and pitches, then still employed the lofty compositions by Zhang Hua and others, presenting them beneath the pipes.

entries.zh: 永嘉之亂，伶官既減，曲台宣榭，咸變汙萊。
entries.en: The Yongjia disaster wiped out entire corps of musicians; Pattern Terrace and shuttered galleries alike turned to muddy ruin.
entries.literal: When the Yongjia turmoil struck, music officers were decimated; Terrace of Patterns and leaf-screened galleries alike sank into weed-choked wastes.

entries.zh: 雖復《象舞》歌工，自胡歸晉，至於孤竹之管，雲和之瑟，空桑之琴，泗濱之磬，其能備者，百不一焉。
entries.en: Even after “Elephant” dancers and choristers came south from the Hu domains, sets pairing Guzhu flutes, Yunhe zithers, hollow-sang lutes, and Siban stones survived intact perhaps once in a hundred cases.
entries.literal: Though dancers for the “Elephant” dance and singing craftsmen returned from the northern tribes to Jin, as for Guzhu pipes, Yunhe zithers, hollow-sang lutes, and Siban chimes, scarcely one ensemble in a hundred remained complete.

entries.zh: 夫人受天地之靈，蘊菁華之氣，剛柔遞用，哀樂分情。
entries.en: People inherit Heaven and Earth’s spiritual charge and store its distilled brilliance; yielding and firm forces trade places in turn, while sorrow and joy partition the heart.
entries.literal: Human beings receive the subtle powers of Heaven and Earth and harbor the condensed essence of brilliant vigor; hardness and softness alternate in application, grief and joy divide the feelings.

entries.zh: 經春陽而自喜，遇秋雕而不悅。
entries.en: Spring sunlight lifts them without prompting; autumn’s frost chills their mood unbidden.
entries.literal: Passing through spring sunshine they rejoice of themselves; meeting autumn’s stripping frost they lose cheer.

entries.zh: 游乎金石之端，出乎管弦之外，因物遷逝，乘流不反。
entries.en: They wander where bells and stones fade into silence and drift beyond strings and winds; as circumstance turns, feeling rides the current and never reverses.
entries.literal: They roam at the boundary of metal and stone, sail beyond strings and pipes; things shift with circumstance and time drifts downstream without turning back.

entries.zh: 是以楚王升輕軒于彭蠡，漢順聽鳴鳥于樊衢。
entries.en: So the Chu king raced his light car beside Pengli marsh, while Emperor Shundi of Han lingered over birdsong where Fan’s highways crossed.
entries.literal: Thus the king of Chu boarded his light carriage by Peng Lake, and Emperor Shun of Han listened to singing birds along the lanes of Fan.

entries.zh: 聖人功成作樂，化平裁曲，乃揚節奏，以暢中和，飾其歡欣，止於哀思者也。
entries.en: So the sage, achievements sealed and customs evenly ruled, fashions music and trims tunes—raising rhythm to release inner equipoise, heightening delight yet stopping short of mere lament.
entries.literal: Therefore when sages complete their work they create music; when transformation is balanced they trim melodies—only then do they lift beats and measures to vent centered harmony, adorn joy, and halt at mourning-thought.

entries.zh: 杜夔傳舊雅樂四曲，一曰《鹿鳴》，二曰《騶虞》，三曰《伐檀》，四曰《文王》，皆古聲辭。
entries.en: Du Kui handed down four former elegant-music pieces—“Deer Call,” “Zouyu,” “Cutting Sandalwood,” and “King Wen”—each preserving archaic lyrics and melody.
entries.literal: Du Kui transmitted former ritual music in four pieces—first “Deer Call,” second “Zouyu,” third “Cutting Sandalwood,” fourth “King Wen”—all antique tunes and texts.

entries.zh: 及太和中，左延年改夔《騶虞》、《伐檀》、《文王》三曲，更自作聲節，其名雖存，而聲實異。
entries.en: Mid-Taihe saw Zuo Yannian rework Du Kui’s settings for “Zouyu,” “Cutting Sandalwood,” and “King Wen,” drafting new beats under old names so hearing no longer matched tradition.
entries.literal: By mid-Taihe, Zuo Yannian revised three of Du Kui’s pieces—“Zouyu,” “Cutting Sandalwood,” and “King Wen”—making fresh rhythmic schemes himself; though titles survived, the actual sound changed.

entries.zh: 唯因夔《鹿鳴》，全不改易。
entries.en: Only “Deer Call” stayed exactly as Du Kui left it.
entries.literal: Only because of Du Kui’s “Deer Call” did they leave it wholly unchanged.

entries.zh: 每正旦大會，太尉奉璧，群後行禮，東廂雅樂常作者是也。
entries.en: Thus at each New Year’s dawn court, when the Grand Commandant presents the jade disk and regional lords perform the rites, the elegant ensemble of the eastern wing regularly performs these pieces.
entries.literal: Hence at each New Year’s court assembly, when the Grand Commandant presents the jade disk and regional lords perform ritual, the ritual music regularly performed from the eastern wing is this repertoire.

entries.zh: 後又改三篇之行禮詩。
entries.en: Later they again altered the three ceremonial procession poems.
entries.literal: Later they again altered the three procession hymns used during ritual.

entries.zh: 第一日《於赫篇》，詠武帝，聲節與古《鹿鳴》同。
entries.en: Piece one, “How Radiant,” hymned Emperor Wu to the old meter of “Deer Call.”
entries.literal: The first they titled “How Radiant”—praising Emperor Wu—its rhythm matched the ancient “Deer Call.”

entries.zh: 第二曰《巍巍篇》，詠文帝，用延年所改《騶虞》聲。
entries.en: Piece two, “How Towering,” praised Emperor Wen with Zuo Yannian’s revised “Zouyu” tune.
entries.literal: The second they titled “How Towering”—praising Emperor Wen—using the sound Zuo Yannian had refashioned for “Zouyu.”

entries.zh: 第三日《洋洋篇》，詠明帝，用延年所改《文王》聲。
entries.en: Piece three, “How Vast,” honored Emperor Ming with Zuo Yannian’s altered “King Wen” accompaniment.
entries.literal: The third they titled “How Vast”—praising Emperor Ming—using the sound Zuo Yannian had refashioned for “King Wen.”

entries.zh: 第四曰復用《鹿鳴》。
entries.en: The fourth slot reused “Deer Call” outright.
entries.literal: The fourth returned to employing “Deer Call.”

entries.zh: 《鹿鳴》之聲重用，而除古《伐檀》。
entries.en: Doubling “Deer Call” pushed out archaic “Cutting Sandalwood.”
entries.literal: Because “Deer Call” was employed twice, they dropped the ancient “Cutting Sandalwood.”

entries.zh: 及晉初，食舉亦用《鹿鳴》。
entries.en: Early Jin court dinners still opened with “Deer Call.”
entries.literal: When Jin began, banquets at imperial meals likewise used “Deer Call.”

entries.zh: 至泰始五年，尚書奏，使太僕傅玄、中書監荀勖、黃門侍郎張華各造正旦行禮及王公上壽酒、食舉樂歌詩。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Taishi the Secretariat memorialized, commissioning Minister Coachman Fu Xuan, Palace Secretariat Director Xun Xu, and Imperial Gate Gentleman Zhang Hua each to compose hymn texts for New Year ritual processions, princes' longevity toasts, and meal-accompaniment music.
entries.literal: By the fifth year of Taishi the Secretariat memorialized, ordering Minister Coachman Fu Xuan, Palace Secretariat Director Xun Xu, and Imperial Gate Gentleman Zhang Hua each to compose hymn texts for New Year ritual procession, for princes’ longevity toasts, and for meal-accompaniment music.

entries.zh: 荀勖云：「魏氏行禮、食舉，再取周詩《鹿鳴》以為樂章。
entries.en: Xun Xu argued, “Wei ceremonies and meal ensembles twice lifted Zhou’s ‘Deer Call’ wholesale.
entries.literal: Xun Xu stated: “Wei court ritual and meal music twice borrowed Zhou’s ‘Deer Call’ as its lyrics.

entries.zh: 又《鹿鳴》以宴嘉賓，無取於朝，考之舊聞，未知所應。」
entries.en: Yet ‘Deer Call’ belongs at banquets for noble visitors, not levee halls; antiquity gives no warrant for recycling it here.”
entries.literal: Moreover ‘Deer Call’ feasts honored guests—it offers nothing suited to court audiences; reviewing ancient precedent, I cannot see how it fits.”

entries.zh: 勖乃除《鹿鳴》舊歌更作行禮詩四篇，先陳三朝朝宗之義。
entries.en: So Xun Xu discarded the old “Deer Call” lyrics and composed four procession poems foregrounding the meaning of three-dawn court homage.
entries.literal: Xu therefore discarded the old “Deer Call” lyrics and wrote four new procession poems opening with the meaning of three-dawn court homage.

entries.zh: 又為正旦大會、王公上壽歌詩並食舉樂歌詩，合十三篇。
entries.en: He added lyrics for the dawn levee, royal toast stanzas, and dining suites—thirteen compositions altogether.
entries.literal: He further composed hymn texts for the great New Year assembly, princes’ longevity toasts, and meal music—thirteen pieces in all.

entries.zh: 又以魏氏歌詩或二言，或三言，或四言，或五言，與古詩不類，以問司律中郎將陳頎。
entries.en: Because Wei lyrics varied between two and five syllables unlike classical verse, he queried Pitch Colonel Chen Yi.
entries.literal: Moreover because Wei dynasty lyrics sometimes used two, three, four, or five characters per line—unlike ancient poems—he consulted Colonel Director of Pitch Chen Yi.

entries.zh: 頎曰：「被之金石，未必皆當。」
entries.en: Chen Yi answered, “Fit them to bells and lithophones—not every clause sits equally well.”
entries.literal: Yi replied: “Once married to bronze and stone, not every line necessarily fits.”

entries.zh: 故勖造晉歌，皆為四言，唯王公上壽酒一篇為三言五言焉。
entries.en: Thus Xun Xu’s Jin corpus stays strictly four-beat lines save the longevity stanza mingling triple and quintuple phrases.
entries.literal: Hence Xun Xu’s Jin hymns use four-character lines throughout, except one longevity toast mixing three- and five-character verses.

entries.zh: 張華以為「魏上壽、食舉詩及漢氏所施用，其文句長短不齊，未皆合古。
entries.en: Zhang Hua countered that “Wei toast and banquet lyrics, like Han precedents, stagger line lengths and violate classical meter.
entries.literal: Zhang Hua held that “Wei longevity and meal poems plus Han adaptations bear uneven line lengths—not all accord with antiquity.

entries.zh: 蓋以依詠弦節，本有因循，而識樂知音，足以制聲度曲，法用率非凡近之所能改。
entries.en: They stuck with instrumental phrasing by habit; yet masters who hear true pattern may forge regulated lines—standard practice should not yield to shallow edits.
entries.literal: Likely because following string rhythms originally allowed inertia; still, those who grasp music can craft measures and bend tunes—normative usage need not bow to vulgar tinkering.

entries.zh: 二代三京，襲而不變，雖詩章辭異，興廢隨時，至其韻逗留曲折，皆系於舊，有由然也。
entries.en: Han and Wei across Luoyang and Ye copied rather than innovated; lyrics rose and fell with politics, yet rhythmic pacing still hugged inherited grooves—and that stubborn continuity had cause.
entries.literal: Two dynasties and three capitals inherited without overhaul; although hymn wording shifted with rise and fall of reigns, cadence lingered and turns twisted along old grooves—and therein lay reason.

entries.zh: 是以一皆因就，不敢有所改易。」
entries.en: So every number hugged precedent—no editor dared novelty."
entries.literal: Therefore each piece kept inherited forms—none ventured rash alteration.”

entries.zh: 此則華、勖所明異旨也。
entries.en: Here Zhang Hua and Xun Xu laid bare how their aims diverged.
entries.literal: Thus Zhang Hua and Xun Xu disclosed differing intentions.

entries.zh: 時詔又使中書侍郎成公綏亦作焉。
entries.en: The court likewise commissioned Secretariat Vice Director Chenggong Sui to supply lyrics.
entries.literal: At the same time an edict also ordered Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat Chenggong Sui to compose texts.
