entries.zh: 今並采列之雲。
entries.en: What follows preserves both corpora together.
entries.literal: Now both sets are excerpted and recorded below.

entries.zh: 冬至初歲小會歌張華
entries.en: Early-Year Winter-Solstice Gathering Hymn—Zhang Hua
entries.literal: Minor Assembly Song for Winter Solstice and First Month—by Zhang Hua

entries.zh: 宴會歌張華
entries.en: Convivial Court Hymn—Zhang Hua
entries.literal: Banquet Song—by Zhang Hua

entries.zh: 命將出征歌張華
entries.en: Marching Host General’s Hymn—Zhang Hua
entries.literal: Song for Commanders Departing on Campaign—by Zhang Hua

entries.zh: 勞還師歌張華
entries.en: Homecoming Host after Punitive March—Zhang Hua
entries.literal: Song for Troops Returning from Labor Campaign—by Zhang Hua

entries.zh: 重華隆帝道，戎蠻或不賓。
entries.en: Chonghua exalted the imperial Way—martial margins sometimes spurned allegiance.
entries.literal: Chonghua raised the imperial Way—warlike tribes sometimes refused guesthood.

entries.zh: 徐夷興有周，鬼方亦違殷。
entries.en: Xu yi stirred under Zhou—Ghost Realm likewise insulted Shang.
entries.literal: Xu barbarians rose against Zhou—Guifang likewise defied Yin.

entries.zh: 今在盛明世，寇虐動四垠。
entries.en: In this brightest reign—raider savagery shakes four rims.
entries.literal: Now in this effulgent age—bandit cruelty stirs four borders.

entries.zh: 豺狼染牙爪，群生號穹旻。
entries.en: Beasts stain teeth and claws—creatures howl at vaulted heaven.
entries.literal: Wolves and hounds dye fangs and claws—myriad creatures wail at dome sky.

entries.zh: 元帥統方夏，出車撫涼秦。
entries.en: Chief commander rules central plain—chariots pacify Liang-Qin marches.
entries.literal: Grand marshal commands inner summer—war carts soothe Liang and Qin.

entries.zh: 眾貞必以律，臧否實在人。
entries.en: United resolve needs measured law—merit judgment lives in human hearts.
entries.literal: Mass loyalty must follow statutes—praise or blame truly rests in men.

entries.zh: 威信加殊類，疏逖思自親。
entries.en: Dread faith reaches stranger tribes—remote minds crave adoption as kin.
entries.literal: Prestige and trust touch alien kinds—distant folk wish kinship of themselves.

entries.zh: 單醪豈有味，挾纊感至仁。
entries.en: One cup of thin brew—no gourmet savor—yet quilted coats feel deepest grace.
entries.literal: Single jar of ale—how could it taste sweet?—yet padded coats sense utmost kindness.

entries.zh: 武功尚止戈，七德美安民。
entries.en: Warrior fame honors ending arms—seven virtues hymn soothing people.
entries.literal: Martial merit esteems halting spears—seven powers praise calming folk.

entries.zh: 遠跡由斯舉，永世無風塵。
entries.en: Distant tracks begin here—endless reign without battle haze.
entries.literal: Far footprints rise from this—eternal age without dust of strife.

entries.zh: 中宮所歌張華
entries.en: Empress Quarter Hymn—Zhang Hua
entries.literal: Song for the Inner Palace—by Zhang Hua

entries.zh: 宗親會歌張華
entries.en: Lineage Gathering Hymn—Zhang Hua
entries.literal: Song for Clan Kinsmen Assembly—by Zhang Hua

entries.zh: 先王統大業，玄化漸八維。
entries.en: Ancient sovereigns bound mega-work—subtle reform soaked eight poles.
entries.literal: Former kings threaded great enterprise—dark transformation seeped eight dimensions.

entries.zh: 儀刑孚萬邦，內訓隆壼闈。
entries.en: Pattern and statute swayed all realms—domestic teaching honored queen’s chambers.
entries.literal: Model and law won myriad states—inner instruction exalted inner palace.

entries.zh: 皇英垂帝典，《大雅》詠三妃。
entries.en: Huang and Ying draped dynastic standard—“Greater Ya” hymns three consorts.
entries.literal: Huang and Ying hung imperial canon—“Greater Elegantiae” sings three consorts.

entries.zh: 執德宣隆教，正位理厥機。
entries.en: Clutching merit they spread high doctrine—rightful seat tuned its gears.
entries.literal: Grasping virtue they broadcast lofty teaching—correct station ordered its pivots.

entries.zh: 含章體柔順，帥禮蹈謙祗。
entries.en: With inward pattern they wore yielding grace—guiding ceremony they walked shy reverence.
entries.literal: Holding culture they embodied supple obedience—leading ritual they trod humble awe.

entries.zh: 《螽斯》弘慈惠，《樛木》逮幽微。
entries.en: “Locusts” amplifies mercy—“Tumbling Branch” touches quiet depths.
entries.literal: “Locusts” magnifies kindness and grace—“Stooping Bough” reaches hidden subtlety.

entries.zh: 徽音穆清風，高義邈不追。
entries.en: Bright echoes ride fresh gale—lofty duty beyond chasing.
entries.literal: Fine voices breeze clear wind—high righteousness far beyond pursuit.

entries.zh: 遺榮參日月，百世仰餘暉。
entries.en: Yielding fame they match luminaries—centuries lift eyes to lingering glow.
entries.literal: Renouncing glory they rival sun and moon—hundred ages gaze up at afterglow.

entries.zh: 泰始九年，光祿大夫荀勖以杜夔所制律呂，校太樂、總章、鼓吹八音，與律呂乖錯，乃制古尺，作新律呂，以調聲韻。
entries.en: the ninth year of Taishi saw Xun Xu compare Du Kui’s pitch system with palace ensembles and martial bands; finding mismatch, he cast archaic rods and new tubes to true the scale.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Taishi, Minister Guanglu Xun Xu, because the pitch pipes Du Kui had devised—when checked against Grand Music, General Regulation, and Drum-and-Bugle eight timbres—clashed with standard lu, then fashioned ancient foot-rules and cast new pitch tubes to tune modes and intervals.

entries.zh: 事具《律曆志》。
entries.en: Full detail appears in the treatise on harmonics and calendrics.
entries.literal: The matter is fully recorded in the “Treatise on Pitch Pipes and the Calendar.”

entries.zh: 律成，遂班下太常，使太樂、總章、鼓吹、清商施用。
entries.en: Once the pitch-pipes were complete, they were promulgated to the Chamberlain of Ceremonial for Grand Music, General Regulation, Drum-and-Bugle, and Pure Shop to adopt them.
entries.literal: Once the pipes were complete, orders went down to the Chamberlain of Ceremonial for Grand Music, General Regulation, Drum-and-Bugle, and Pure Shop to adopt them.

entries.zh: 勖遂典知樂事，啟朝士解音律者共掌之。
entries.en: Xun Xu took charge of performance and asked literati who understood temperament to co-manage it.
entries.literal: Xun Xu then supervised musical affairs and memorialized that court gentlemen who grasped pitch theory should jointly administer them.

entries.zh: 使郭夏、宋識等造《正德》、《大豫》二舞，其樂章亦張華之所作雲。
entries.en: He tasked Guo Xia and Song Shi with choreography for “Zhengde” and “Dayu”—lyrics again from Zhang Hua.
entries.literal: He assigned Guo Xia, Song Shi, and others to create the two dances “Correct Virtue” and “Grand Ease”—their lyrics likewise composed by Zhang Hua.

entries.zh: 正德舞歌張華
entries.en: “Zhengde” Dance Hymn—Zhang Hua
entries.literal: Correct Virtue Dance Song—by Zhang Hua

entries.zh: 日皇上天，玄鑒惟光。
entries.en: Solar lord aloft—shadowy scrutiny alone shines.
entries.literal: Sun august, Heaven high—dark mirror alone sheds light.

entries.zh: 神器周回，五德代章。
entries.en: Divine tokens wheel—five virtues take rotating glory.
entries.literal: Sacred regalia cycles round—five powers replace in splendor.

entries.zh: 祚命于晉，世有哲王。
entries.en: Heaven’s lot settles on Jin—successions seat sagely rulers.
entries.literal: Fortune’s mandate rests with Jin—ages hold wise kings.

entries.zh: 弘濟區夏，陶甄萬方。
entries.en: They rescue central plain—they kiln-fire every quarter.
entries.literal: They broadly succor inner summer—they mold and fire myriad directions.

entries.zh: 大明垂曜，旁燭無疆。
entries.en: Grand splendor lowers gleam—peripheral torches know no bound.
entries.literal: Great brilliance hangs its glow—side lamps illumine without limit.

entries.zh: 蚩蚩庶類，風德永康。
entries.en: Teeming common folk—custom’s power ever robust.
entries.literal: Busy busy common kinds—wind virtue forever strong.

entries.zh: 皇道惟清，禮樂斯經。
entries.en: The royal way stays lucid—rites and song form its fixed threads.
entries.literal: Imperial path alone is pure—ritual and music are its warp.

entries.zh: 金石在懸，萬舞在庭。
entries.en: Bronze and jade hang ranked—countless dancers pack the yard.
entries.literal: Metal and stone hang suspended—myriad dancers fill courtyard.

entries.zh: 象容表慶，協律被聲。
entries.en: Figures display fortune—they wed mode and mantle tone.
entries.literal: Gestures image blessing—they harmonize pitch and cloak sound.

entries.zh: 軼《武》超《濩》，取節《六英》。
entries.en: Leaping past “Grand Wu,” vaulting “Grand Hu”—they steal rhythm from “Six Ying.”
entries.literal: Surpassing “Wu,” transcending “Hu”—they borrow beat from “Six Ying.”

entries.zh: 同進退讓，化漸無形。
entries.en: Joint charge, joint retreat—reform trickles past visible form.
entries.literal: Together advancing, together yielding—transformation seeps beyond shape.

entries.zh: 大和宣洽，通於幽冥。
entries.en: Supreme concord spreads—it threads silent shades.
entries.literal: Grand harmony proclaimed concord—it penetrates dim netherworld.

entries.zh: 大豫舞歌張華
entries.en: “Dayu” Dance Hymn—Zhang Hua
entries.literal: Grand Ease Dance Song—by Zhang Hua

entries.zh: 惟天之命，符運有歸。
entries.en: Thus runs celestial writ—omens and luck own their course.
entries.literal: Such is Heaven’s command—tally and fortune know their return.

entries.zh: 赫赫大晉，三後重暉。
entries.en: Resplendent mighty Jin—three successors stacked glory.
entries.literal: Blazing Great Jin—three later lords doubled splendor.

entries.zh: 繼明紹世，光撫九圍。
entries.en: Carrying flame, handing eras—gleam nurses nine peripheries.
entries.literal: Continuing brilliance, renewing ages—radiance soothes nine spheres.

entries.zh: 我皇紹期，遂在璿璣。
entries.en: Our sovereign takes timed mandate—therefore sits on polar hinge.
entries.literal: Our emperor inherits destined season—thus rests upon celestial pivot.

entries.zh: 群生屬命，奄有庶邦。
entries.en: Creatures hang fortunes—swiftly holding myriad states.
entries.literal: Myriad lives attach their fate—suddenly possessing hundred domains.

entries.zh: 慎徽五典，玄教遐通。
entries.en: Guardedly honoring five statutes—arcane doctrine bridges distance.
entries.literal: Carefully tracing five canons—dark teaching reaches far.

entries.zh: 萬方同軌，率土咸雍。
entries.en: Ten thousand regions ride shared gauge—every soil merges ease.
entries.literal: Myriad quarters share one track—all soils join harmony.

entries.zh: 爰制《大豫》，宣德舞功。
entries.en: Hence choreographed “Grand Ease”—spreading merit through swaying ode.
entries.literal: Thus they fashioned “Grand Ease”—broadcasting virtue through dance merit.

entries.zh: 醇化既穆，王道協隆。
entries.en: Distilled reform stands grave—royal course aligns with height.
entries.literal: Pure transformation already solemn—kingly Way coordinated lofty.

entries.zh: 仁及草木，惠加昆蟲。
entries.en: Mercy touches herb and timber—bounty sinks to creeping kin.
entries.literal: Kindness reaches grass and trees—grace adds even to crawling things.

entries.zh: 億兆夷人，悅仰皇風。
entries.en: Countless tribes beyond heartland—gladly crane toward sovereign wind.
entries.literal: Hundred millions of barbarian folk—joyfully lift eyes to royal breeze.

entries.zh: 丕顯大業，永世彌崇。
entries.en: Brightly shown mega-work—endless reigns heap reverence.
entries.literal: Brilliantly manifest great enterprise—forever ages it mounts revered.

entries.zh: 樂志上
entries.en: Treatise on Music: Part One
entries.literal: Music Treatise, Part One

entries.zh: 及武帝受禪，乃令傅玄制為二十二篇，亦述以功德代魏。
entries.en: After Emperor Wu took the abdicated throne he told Fu Xuan to write twenty-two lyrics chronicling Jin merit supplanting Wei.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted abdication, he ordered Fu Xuan to compose twenty-two pieces, likewise narrating merit and virtue replacing Wei.

entries.zh: 改《朱鷺》為《靈之祥》，言宣帝之佐魏，猶虞舜之事堯，既有石瑞之徵，又能用武以誅孟達之逆命也。
entries.en: 《Red Egret》 became 《Omen of the Spirits》, likening Sima Yi's service to Wei to Shun serving Yao: stone omens appeared and arms crushed Meng Da's revolt.
entries.literal: They changed 《Red Egret》 to 《Auspice of the Numina》, referring to how Emperor Xuan aided Wei as Yu Shun served Yao, having both the omen of stone talisman and the ability to use arms to execute Meng Da's treasonous command.

entries.zh: 改《思悲翁》為《宣受命》，言宣帝御諸葛亮，養威重，運神兵，亮震怖而死也。
entries.en: 《Thinking of the Old Man》 became 《Xuan Takes the Charge》, describing Sima Yi's stalemate with Zhuge Liang—stored dread majesty, maneuvered subtle hosts—until Zhuge Liang died of shock.
entries.literal: They changed 《Thinking of the Old Man》 to 《Xuan Receives the Mandate》, referring to how Emperor Xuan opposed Zhuge Liang, nurtured awe-inspiring weight, deployed spirit-like troops, and Liang trembled with terror and died.

entries.zh: 改《艾如張》為《征遼東》，言宣帝陵大海之表，討滅公孫氏而梟其首也。
entries.en: 《Spreading Mugwort》 was titled 《The Liaodong Expedition》, for Sima Yi's crossing of the sea, destruction of the Gongsuns, and display of Gongsun Yuan's head.
entries.literal: They changed 《Spreading Mugwort》 to 《Campaigning Liaodong》, referring to how Emperor Xuan crossed beyond the great sea, attacked and destroyed the Gongsun clan, and exposed their leader's head.

entries.zh: 改《上之回》為《宣輔政》，言宣帝聖道深遠，撥亂反正，網羅文武之才，以定二儀之序也。
entries.en: 《Ascending to the Turn》 became 《Xuan Orders the Realm》, praising deep sagely policy that righted disorder and ranked talented civil and martial officers.
entries.literal: They changed 《Ascending to the Turn》 to 《Xuan Assists the Government》, referring to how Emperor Xuan's sagely way ran deep, set chaos aright and restored order, netted civil and martial talents, and fixed the pattern of the Two Powers.

entries.zh: 改《雍離》為《時運多難》，言宣帝致討吳方，有征無戰也。
entries.en: 《Yong Leaves Part》 turned into 《Times of Many Perils》, noting punitive moves toward Wu that ended without pitched battle.
entries.literal: They changed 《Yong Leaves Part》 to 《The Age Harrows with Many Hardships》, referring to how Emperor Xuan carried punitive expedition to Wu's territory—campaigns without battle.

entries.zh: 改《戰城南》為《景龍飛》，言景帝克明威教，賞順夷逆，隆無疆，崇洪基也。
entries.en: 《South of the City We Fight》 became 《Soaring Dragon of Splendor》, celebrating Emperor Jing's awe-education, rewarding the loyal, punishing rebels, widening blessing, and deepening the great base.
entries.literal: They changed 《South of the City We Fight》 to 《Scenic Dragon Soars》, referring to how Emperor Jing clarified awesome instruction, rewarded compliance and chastised rebellion, elevated boundlessness, and enlarged the mighty foundation.

entries.zh: 改《巫山高》為《平玉衡》，言景帝一萬國之殊風，齊四海之乖心，禮賢養士，而纂洪業也。
entries.en: 《Mount Wu Is High》 was renamed 《Trueing the Jade Armillary》, for Emperor Jing's harmonizing every region, aligning distant hearts, honoring worthies, and advancing the great enterprise.
entries.literal: They changed 《Mount Wu Is High》 to 《Leveling the Jade Balance》, referring to how Emperor Jing unified the myriad nations' diverse customs, aligned the four seas' contrary hearts, honored the worthy and nurtured knights, and continued the great enterprise.

entries.zh: 改《上陵》為《文皇統百揆》，言文帝始統百揆，用人有序，以敷太平之化也。
entries.en: 《Ascending the Mausoleum》 became 《Emperor Wen Governs All Bureaus》, because Sima Zhao first superintended every office, ordered appointments, and spread great peace.
entries.literal: They changed 《Ascending the Mausoleum》 to 《Emperor Wen Commands All Offices》, referring to how Emperor Wen first presided over all bureaus, employed men in due order, and spread the transforming influence of great peace.

entries.zh: 改《將進酒》為《因時運》，言因時運變，聖謀潛施，解長蛇之交，離群桀之党，以武濟文，以邁其德也。
entries.en: 《Wine, Advance!》 was titled 《Seizing the Hour》, describing timely stratagem that broke Shu-Wu collusion, shattered rebel cliques, paired arms with culture, and heightened virtue.
entries.literal: They changed 《Wine, Advance!》 to 《Riding the Season's Fortune》, referring to how following fortune's seasons the sacred stratagem worked in secret, undid the long-serpent alliance, split the pack of fiends, aided culture with arms, and thereby advanced virtue.

entries.zh: 改《有所思》為《惟庸蜀》，言文帝既平萬乘之蜀，封建萬國，復五等之爵也。
entries.en: 《I Had Someone in Mind》 became 《That Shu Alone》, for Sima Zhao's reduction of the Shu empire, investiture of countless domains, and revival of the five noble ranks.
entries.literal: They changed 《I Had Someone in Mind》 to 《Only That Shu》, referring to how Emperor Wen pacified the Shu host of ten thousand chariots, enfeoffed myriad states, and restored the five grades of nobility.

entries.zh: 改《芳樹》為《天序》，言聖皇應曆受禪，弘濟大化，用人各盡其才也。
entries.en: 《Fragrant Trees》 turned into 《Heaven's Sequence》, celebrating the sage ruler's calendar-abdication, vast transformation, and each talent fully used.
entries.literal: They changed 《Fragrant Trees》 to 《Heaven's Ordering》, referring to how the sage emperor answered the calendar and received abdication, broadly aided great transformation, and employed each man to his full talent.

entries.zh: 改《上邪》為《大晉承運期》，言聖皇應籙受圖，化象神明也。
entries.en: 《Oh Heaven Above》 became 《Great Jin's Hour》, because the sage sovereign answered the tally-charts and merged his likeness with the divine.
entries.literal: They changed 《Oh Heaven Above》 to 《Great Jin Receives the Mandate's Season》, referring to how the sage emperor answered the tallies and received the charts, transforming likeness spirit-like.

entries.zh: 改《君馬黃》為《金靈運》，言聖皇踐阼，致敬宗廟，而孝道行於天下也。
entries.en: 《Your Horse Is Yellow》 was renamed 《Metal Virtue in Motion》, praising accession, ancestral devotion, and filial teaching across the land.
entries.literal: They changed 《Your Horse Is Yellow》 to 《The Metal Essence's Course》, referring to how the sage emperor ascended the throne, paid utmost homage at the ancestral shrine, and filial devotion ran through the realm.

entries.zh: 改《雉子班》為《于穆我皇》，言聖皇受禪，德合神明也。
entries.en: 《Pheasant Broods》 became 《How Majestic Our King》, for the abdicated accession and virtue mirroring the gods.
entries.literal: They changed 《Pheasant Broods》 to 《Oh Solemn Our Sovereign》, referring to how the sage emperor received abdication and virtue matched spirit luminaries.

entries.zh: 改《聖人出》為《仲春振旅》，言大晉申文武之教，畋獵以時也。
entries.en: 《The Sage Appears》 was titled 《Spring Hunt Drills the Troops》, recording Jin extension of civil-martial instruction and seasonal hunts.
entries.literal: They changed 《The Sage Appears》 to 《Second Month Drills the Host》, referring to how Great Jin extended civil and martial teaching and hunted according to season.

entries.zh: 改《臨高臺》為《夏苗田》，言大晉畋狩順時，為苗除害也。
entries.en: 《From the High Terrace》 became 《Summer Seedling Hunt》, when Jin drove off vermin in accord with the calendar.
entries.literal: They changed 《From the High Terrace》 to 《Summer Seedling Hunt》, referring to how Great Jin hunted in accord with season to rid the fields of harm.

entries.zh: 改《遠如期》為《仲秋獮田》，言大晉雖有文德，不廢武事，順時以殺伐也。
entries.en: 《Far as the Promised Day》 turned into 《Autumn Hunt in Order》, insisting that even with civil splendor Jin still struck punishments on schedule.
entries.literal: They changed 《Far as the Promised Day》 to 《Second Month Autumn Hunt》, referring to how Great Jin, though possessing civil virtue, did not neglect martial affairs, following season for punitive strikes.

entries.zh: 改《石留》為《順天道》，言仲冬大閱，用武修文，大晉之德配天也。
entries.en: 《Stone Stays》 was renamed 《Following Heaven's Road》, for midwinter grand reviews where arms perfected culture and Jin matched heaven.
entries.literal: They changed 《Stone Stays》 to 《Obeying Heaven's Way》, referring to how in mid-winter the grand review used arms to cultivate culture, Great Jin's virtue matching heaven.

entries.zh: 改《務成》為《唐堯》，言聖皇陟帝位，德化光四表也。
entries.en: 《Accomplishing Completion》 became 《Emperor Yao of Tang》, because the sage ruler mounted the throne and edifying virtue lit the four quarters.
entries.literal: They changed 《Accomplishing Completion》 to 《Tang Yao》, referring to how the sage emperor ascended the throne of emperor and moral transformation irradiated the four outer regions.

entries.zh: 《玄雲》依舊名，言聖皇用人，各盡其材也。
entries.en: 《Dark Clouds》 stayed unchanged, depicting every talent placed according to his gifts.
entries.literal: 《Dark Clouds》 kept its old name, referring to how the sage emperor employed men, each to his material.

entries.zh: 改《黃爵行》為《伯益》，言赤烏銜書，有周以興，今聖皇受命，神雀來也。
entries.en: 《Yellow Sparrow March》 became 《Helper Yi》, comparing the crimson crow's writ that launched Zhou to the spirit finches greeting Jin's charge.
entries.literal: They changed 《Yellow Sparrow March》 to 《Boy Yi》, referring to how the red crow bore writing—Zhou rose thereby—and now the sage emperor received the mandate and spirit magpies came.

entries.zh: 《釣竿》依舊名，言聖皇德配堯舜，又有呂望之佐，濟大功，致太平也。
entries.en: 《Fishing Rod》 remained, pairing Jin virtue with Yao-Shun and Lü Wang's aid to finish the great task of peace.
entries.literal: 《Fishing Rod》 kept its old name, referring to how the sage emperor's virtue matched Yao and Shun and he also had Lü Wang's assistance to accomplish great work and bring about great peace.

entries.zh: 其辭並列之於後雲。
entries.en: The texts follow in order.
entries.literal: Their lyrics are all listed below.

entries.zh: 靈之祥，石瑞章。
entries.en: Spirit blessing—stone portents blaze.
entries.literal: Auspice of the numina—stone omens bright.

entries.zh: 旌金德，出西方。
entries.en: Metal virtue revealed, rising from the west.
entries.literal: Displaying metal virtue, emerging from the west.

entries.zh: 天降命，授宣皇。
entries.en: Heaven sent its mandate, granting Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: Heaven dropped the charge, bestowed on Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 應期運，時龍驤。
entries.en: He rides the hour's luck; the dragon rears on high.
entries.literal: Answering timely fortune, for the moment the dragon rears.

entries.zh: 繼大舜，佐陶唐。
entries.en: He follows Great Shun, assists lofty Tang.
entries.literal: Continuing great Shun, assisting lofty Tang.

entries.zh: 贊武文，建帝綱。
entries.en: He upholds civil and martial, sets the royal span.
entries.literal: Praising civil and martial, establishing imperial norm.

entries.zh: 孟氏叛，據南疆。
entries.en: Meng Da rebelled, gripping the southern marches.
entries.literal: The Meng clan rebelled, holding the southern frontier.

entries.zh: 追有扈，亂五常。
entries.en: Like punishing You-Hu, he smashes the five norms.
entries.literal: Pursuing the You-Hu, disordering the five constants.

entries.zh: 吳寇叛，蜀虜強。
entries.en: Wu raiders rise; Shu hosts stay fierce.
entries.literal: Wu bandits rebelled; Shu captives strong.

entries.zh: 交誓盟，連遐荒。
entries.en: They swear dire alliances, chain the far frontiers.
entries.literal: Swearing leagues of alliance, linking distant wastes.

entries.zh: 宣赫怒，奮鷹揚。
entries.en: Xuan vents fierce wrath, lifts wings like hawks.
entries.literal: Xuan roused fierce wrath, soaring like the hawk.

entries.zh: 震乾威，曜電光。
entries.en: He shakes celestial awe, flashes lightning sheen.
entries.literal: Shaking heaven's majesty, flashing lightning's gleam.

entries.zh: 陵九天，陷石城。
entries.en: He climbs the nine tiers, storms Stone Fort hold.
entries.literal: Scaling the nine heavens, toppling Stone City.

entries.zh: 梟逆命，拯有生。
entries.en: He cuts the rebel charge, saves the breathing folk.
entries.literal: Beheading the traitor's mandate, saving the living throng.

entries.zh: 萬國安，四海寧。
entries.en: Ten thousand regions rest; four seas grow calm.
entries.literal: Ten thousand lands secure; the four seas at peace.

entries.zh: 宣受命
entries.en: Xuan Receives the Mandate
entries.literal: Xuan Receives the Mandate

entries.zh: 宣受命，應天機，風雲時動神龍飛。
entries.en: Xuan takes heaven's charge; clouds ride the hour—the dragon lifts.
entries.literal: Xuan receives the mandate, answers heaven's instrument; wind and clouds move in season—divine dragon flies.

entries.zh: 禦葛亮，鎮雍梁。
entries.en: He bars Zhuge Liang, shields Yong and Liang.
entries.literal: He fences off Zhuge Liang, guards Yong and Liang.

entries.zh: 邊境安，夷夏康。
entries.en: Frontiers lock tight; tribes and heartland easy.
entries.literal: Borderlands secure; barbarians and Xia at ease.

entries.zh: 務節事，勤定傾。
entries.en: He trims state affairs, labors to right the leaning throne.
entries.literal: He attends to modest duty, toils to steady the tipping scale.

entries.zh: 攬英雄，保持盈。
entries.en: He collects champions, guards surplus with care.
entries.literal: He gathers heroes, holds fullness in care.

entries.zh: 深穆穆，赫明明。
entries.en: Deep and still, blazingly bright.
entries.literal: Profound and solemn, radiant and bright.

entries.zh: 沖而泰，天之經。
entries.en: Supple and still—the warp of heaven.
entries.literal: Subtle and tranquil—heaven's constant warp.

entries.zh: 養威重，運神兵。
entries.en: He stores dread weight, drives spirit-like hosts.
entries.literal: He nurtures dread majesty, wields spirit-like troops.

entries.zh: 亮乃震斃，天下安寧。
entries.en: Liang dies of dread; the realm lies quiet.
entries.literal: Liang then quaked and perished; all under heaven secure and still.

entries.zh: 宣輔政
entries.en: Xuan Assists the Government
entries.literal: Xuan Assists the Government

entries.zh: 宣皇輔政，聖烈深。
entries.en: The Xuan emperor steered the realm; sacred power ran profound.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan aids governance; sagely merit runs deep.

entries.zh: 撥亂反正，順天心。
entries.en: He straightened the turmoil and matched heaven's mind.
entries.literal: He sets chaos aright and restores orthodoxy; he accords with heaven's heart.

entries.zh: 網羅文武才，慎厥所生。
entries.en: He gathered civil and martial talent and fostered each calling.
entries.literal: He nets civil and martial talents; cautiously he nurtures what they bear.

entries.zh: 所生賢，遺教施。
entries.en: Those nurtured proved worthy; his legacy spread as doctrine.
entries.literal: What they bear proves worthy; his bequeathed teaching spreads.

entries.zh: 安上治民，化風移。
entries.en: He steadied ruler and folk and shifted customs through reform.
entries.literal: He settles superiors and governs the people; transforming customs shift.

entries.zh: 肇創帝基，洪業垂。
entries.en: He founded the dynastic base and hung the great enterprise forth.
entries.literal: He begins creation of the imperial foundation; vast enterprise hangs down.

entries.zh: 于鑠明明，時赫戲。
entries.en: How radiant his gleam, how fierce his shining play.
entries.literal: Oh, blaze so bright, splendid and shining, momentous display.

entries.zh: 功濟萬世，定二儀。
entries.en: His work aids endless ages; he set heaven and earth aright.
entries.literal: Merit aids ten thousand generations; he fixes the Two Powers.

entries.zh: 定二儀，雲行雨施，海外風馳。
entries.en: Heaven and earth aligned: clouds rode, rain fell, winds raced overseas.
entries.literal: Fixing the Two Powers: clouds move and rain falls; beyond the seas winds gallop.

entries.zh: 時運多難，道教痡。
entries.en: Hard times exhausted the Way; instruction grew thin.
entries.literal: The age harrows with many hardships; the Way's teaching grows weary.

entries.zh: 天地變化，有盈虛。
entries.en: Sky and soil alternate between wax and wane.
entries.literal: Heaven and earth alter and shift; there is fullness and emptiness.

entries.zh: 蠢爾吳蠻，武視江湖。
entries.en: Those Wu savages eyed the rivers with martial greed.
entries.literal: You foolish Wu barbarians--martially you gaze on rivers and lakes.

entries.zh: 我皇赫斯，致天誅。
entries.en: Our sovereign rose in wrath to wield heaven's scourge.
entries.literal: Our emperor awesome thus--brings heaven's punishment upon you.

entries.zh: 有征無戰，弭其圖。
entries.en: Campaigns ended without pitched battle; their schemes collapsed.
entries.literal: Where there is campaign there is no battle; your plots are stilled.

entries.zh: 天威橫被，廓東隅。
entries.en: Heaven's awe swept outward and cleared the eastern march.
entries.literal: Heaven's majesty spreads horizontally; opens the eastern corner.

entries.zh: 征遼東，敵失據，威靈邁日域。
entries.en: The Liaodong war—foes lose footing; awe crosses the solar sphere.
entries.literal: Campaigning Liaodong—foe loses foothold; dread majesty crosses the sun's realm.

entries.zh: 公孫既授首，群逆破膽，咸震怖。
entries.en: Gongsun Yuan loses his head; rebels melt with fear.
entries.literal: Gongsun beheaded; crowd of rebels' gall melts—all shake in terror.

entries.zh: 朔北回應，海表景附。
entries.en: The northern wastes answer; overseas shores cling like shadows.
entries.literal: The northern north responds; beyond the seas gaze and cling like shadows.

entries.zh: 武功赫赫，德雲布。
entries.en: His martial glory blazes; kindness rains like clouds.
entries.literal: Martial prowess shines terrifying; virtue spreads like clouds.

entries.zh: 樂志下
entries.en: Treatise on Music, Part Two
entries.literal: Treatise on Music, Part Two

entries.zh: 《書》曰：「唐虞稽古，建官惟百。」
entries.en: The Book of Documents says: "When Tang and Yu looked back to antiquity, they created no more than a hundred offices."
entries.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Tang and Yu examined antiquity; they established offices numbering only one hundred."

entries.zh: 所以獎導民萌，裁成庶政。
entries.en: That was how they encouraged the people and gave shape to the affairs of state.
entries.literal: By this means they encouraged and guided the common people, and brought order to every branch of government.

entries.zh: 《易》曰：「天垂象，聖人則之。」
entries.en: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven displays signs; the sage patterns himself on them."
entries.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven hangs forth images; the sage takes them as his model."

entries.zh: 執法在南宮之右，上相處端門之外，而鳥龍居位，雲火垂名，前史詳之，其以尚矣。
entries.en: Justice lay to the right of the Southern Palace; the chief minister waited beyond the Duan Gate; bird and dragon offices held rank with cloud and fire as their emblems—prior histories lay it out clearly, and the grandeur speaks for itself.
entries.literal: Law sat to the right of the Southern Palace; the chief minister took station beyond the Duan Gate; the Bird and Dragon offices held their posts, cloud and fire lending their names—earlier histories spell this out in detail, and the dignity of it is plain.

entries.zh: 黃帝置三公之秩，以親黎元，少昊配九扈之名，以為農正，命重黎於天地，詔融冥於水火，則可得而言焉。
entries.en: The Yellow Emperor created the Three Dukes to draw near to the people; Shaohao aligned the Nine Hu titles with agricultural oversight; Chong and Li received Heaven and Earth; Zhu Rong and Ming received fire and water—and such patterns can be put into words.
entries.literal: The Yellow Emperor instituted the ranks of the Three Dukes to stay close to the black-haired masses; Shaohao paired the Nine Hu bird-names with the office of director of agriculture; Chong and Li were charged with Heaven and Earth; Zhu Rong and Ming were charged with fire and water—these arrangements can indeed be described.

entries.zh: 伊尹曰：「三公調陰陽，九卿通寒暑，大夫知人事，列士去其私。」
entries.en: Yi Yin said: "The Three Dukes harmonize yin and yang; the Nine Ministers track the seasons; grand officers attend to human affairs; ranked officers put private interest aside."
entries.literal: Yi Yin said: "The Three Dukes harmonize yin and yang; the Nine Ministers watch cold and heat; grand officers understand human affairs; ranked officers rid themselves of selfishness."

entries.zh: 而成湯居亳，初置二相，以伊尹、仲虺為之，凡厥樞會，仰承君命。
entries.en: When Tang of Shang made Bo his seat, he first set up two chancellors—Yi Yin and Zhong Hui—and on every pivot they carried out the sovereign's will.
entries.literal: When Cheng Tang ruled from Bo, he first created two chancellors and appointed Yi Yin and Zhong Hui to them; on every critical matter they looked upward to receive the ruler's commands.

entries.zh: 總及周武下車，成康垂則，六卿分職，二公弘化，咸樹司存，各題標準，苟非其道，人弗虛榮。
entries.en: Under King Wu and the models left by Cheng and Kang, the Six Ministers split the labor, the Two Dukes carried royal influence abroad, every bureau had its charter, and no one claimed idle honors without the right conduct.
entries.literal: Altogether, when King Wu of Zhou stepped down from his chariot to rule, Cheng and Kang handed down norms; the Six Ministers divided duties; the Two Dukes spread transformation; each office kept its place and measure; if it were not the proper Way, people did not vainly seek glory.

entries.zh: 貽厥孫謀，其固本也如此。
entries.en: They anchored the dynasty by planning for generations yet unborn.
entries.literal: They left plans for their descendants; thus they secured the foundation.

entries.zh: 及秦變周官，漢遵嬴舊，或隨時適用，或因務遷革，霸王之典，義在於斯，既獲厥安，所謂得其時制者也。
entries.en: Qin refashioned Zhou's bureaucracy; Han largely kept Qin's frame while tweaking it for the moment—the logic of strong rule was there—and stability meant institutions matched their age.
entries.literal: When Qin altered the Zhou offices and Han followed the Ying-clan precedent, sometimes adapting to the times, sometimes shifting with practical needs—the norms of hegemons and kings lay herein; once stability was gained, this is what is called obtaining timely institutions.

entries.zh: 四征興於漢代，四安起于魏初，四鎮通於柔遠，四平止於喪亂，其渡遼、淩江，輕車、強弩，式揚遐外，用表攻伐，興而復毀，厥號彌繁。
entries.en: Han invented the Four Expeditions; Wei at its outset the Four Pacifications; Four Garrisons stretched toward distant peoples; Four Peace posts vanished when chaos returned. Epithets like Crossing-the-Liao, River-Fording, light chariot, and strong crossbow brandished force beyond the borders for campaigns—created, scrapped, then multiplied until the catalogue grew tangled.
entries.literal: The Four Expeditions arose in Han; the Four Pacifications began at the start of Wei; the Four Garrisons reached outward to soothe the distant; the Four Peace offices ended with turmoil and disorder; as for Crossing-the-Liao, River-Fording, light chariot, and strong crossbow—they displayed might afar and signaled campaigns—raised up and then abolished, their titles grew ever more numerous.

entries.zh: 及當塗得志，克平諸夏，初有軍師祭酒，參掌戎律。
entries.en: Once the Cao regime triumphed and pacified the heartland, it introduced the army adviser libationer to share oversight of military law.
entries.literal: When the house at Dangtu achieved its ambition and subdued the Central Plain, there first appeared the army adviser libationer, who jointly handled military regulations.

entries.zh: 建安十三年，罷漢台司，更置丞相，而以曹公居之，用兼端揆。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an (208), the Han ministerial posts were abolished, the chancellorship was reinstated, and Lord Cao held it, thereby combining the highest civil authority.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an, the Han terrace ministers were abolished; the chancellor was reinstated, and Lord Cao held it, thereby combining the highest civil authority.

entries.zh: 孫吳、劉蜀，多依漢制，雖復臨時命氏，而無忝舊章。
entries.en: Wu and Shu largely kept Han models; occasional improvised titles notwithstanding, they stayed within the classical mold.
entries.literal: Eastern Wu and Liu Bei's Shu largely followed Han institutions; though they sometimes improvised titles on the spot, they did not shame the old statutes.

entries.zh: 世祖武皇帝即位之初，以安平王孚為太宰，鄭沖為太傅，王祥為太保，司馬望為太尉，何曾為司徒，荀顗為司空，石苞為大司馬，陳騫為大將軍，世所謂八公同辰，攀雲附翼者也。
entries.en: At his accession, Emperor Wu named Sima Fu Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang Grand Guardian, Sima Wang Minister of War, He Zeng Minister of Education, Xun Yi Minister of Works, Shi Bao Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian Grand General—the storied eight dukes of a single hour, men who rose by riding imperial favor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu the Shizu first ascended the throne, he appointed Prince Fu of Anping as Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong as Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang as Grand Guardian, Sima Wang as Minister of War, He Zeng as Minister of Education, Xun Yi as Minister of Works, Shi Bao as Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian as Grand General—what the age called the eight dukes sharing one hour, climbing clouds and attaching wings.

entries.zh: 若乃成乎棟宇，非一枝之勢；
entries.en: Raising the whole hall takes more than one timber;
entries.literal: As for completing roof-beams and rafters—it is not the strength of a single branch;

entries.zh: 處乎經綸，稱萬夫之敵。
entries.en: true stewardship of the realm earns the title match for ten thousand.
entries.literal: to dwell in ordering the realm is to be called a match for ten thousand men.

entries.zh: 或牽羊以葉於夢，或垂釣以申其道，或空桑以獻其術，或操版以啟其心。
entries.en: Some arrived through dreams of sheep and grain; some through fishing metaphors; some from humble soil with a craft to sell; some by presenting the royal tablet and winning trust.
entries.literal: Some led sheep and answered a leaf in a dream; some angled with a hook to proclaim their Way; some offered their arts from an empty mulberry; some grasped the tablet to open the ruler's mind.

entries.zh: 臥龍飛鴻，方金擬璧，秦奚、鄭產，楚材晉用，斯亦曩時之良具，其又昭彰者焉。
entries.en: Hidden dragons and soaring swans, talents weighed like gold against jade—Qin Xi, Zheng Chan, and Chu talent employed by Jin: these too were fine instruments of former times, and no less manifest.
entries.literal: The sleeping dragon, the soaring wild goose—square metal compared to round jade; the shepherd of Qin, the prodigy of Zheng; Chu talent employed by Jin—these too were fine instruments of former times, and no less manifest.

entries.zh: 宣王既誅曹爽，政由己出，網羅英俊，以備天官。
entries.en: After Sima Yi eliminated Cao Shuang, he ruled in his own name and stocked every court post with talent.
entries.literal: Once Prince Xuan had executed Cao Shuang, government proceeded from himself alone; he gathered capable men to fill the celestial offices.

entries.zh: 及蘭卿受羈，貴公顯戮，雖復策名魏氏，而乃心皇晉。
entries.en: When fine officers were seized and great nobles died in public execution, names might still stand with Wei but hearts had already turned to Jin.
entries.literal: When worthy ministers were placed under restraint and eminent dukes suffered public execution—though they still bore registration under the Wei, their hearts were with the august Jin.

entries.zh: 及文王纂業，初啟晉台，始置二衛，有前驅養由之弩；
entries.en: When Sima Zhao extended the family work and founded the Jin apparatus, he created the Two Guards with vanguard crossbows worthy of Yang Youji.
entries.literal: When King Wen continued the enterprise and first opened the Jin terrace, he began setting up the Two Guards, including front-vanguard crossbows like Yang Youji's.

entries.zh: 及設三部，有熊渠佽飛之眾。
entries.en: When the Three Corps were established, there were masses like those of Xiong Qu and Ci Fei.
entries.literal: When the Three Departments were established, there were masses like the royal swimmers of Xiong Qu.

entries.zh: 是以武帝龍飛，乘茲奮翼，猶武王以周之十亂而理殷民者也。
entries.en: Thus Emperor Wu's rise—vaulting on these preparations—matched King Wu deploying his ten able assistants to rule the former Shang subjects.
entries.literal: Therefore when Emperor Wu ascended like a dragon, riding this to beat his wings, it was like King Wu of Zhou using the Zhou's ten ministers to govern the Yin people.

entries.zh: 是以泰始盡于太康，喬柯茂葉，來居斯位；
entries.en: From the Taishi era through Taikang, imposing figures filled those ranks;
entries.literal: Thus from Taishi through Taikang, tall trees with lush foliage came to occupy these posts;

entries.zh: 自太興訖於建元，南金北銑，用處茲秩。
entries.en: from Daxing to Jianyuan, the finest metal south and north filled those offices.
entries.literal: from Daxing down to Jianyuan, southern gold and northern ore were employed in these ranks.

entries.zh: 雖未擬乎夔拊龍言，天工人代，亦庶幾乎任官惟賢，蒞事惟能者也。
entries.en: They fell short of the sage-kings' marriage of Heaven's work to human agency, yet they neared the ideal: office by virtue, tasks by competence.
entries.literal: Though they did not equal Kui's drumming and Long's pronouncements—Heaven's work and man's substitute—they approximated appoint officials only for worth, approach affairs only by ability.

entries.zh: 丞相、相國，並秦官也。
entries.en: The titles chancellor and minister of state both originated in Qin.
entries.literal: Chancellor and minister of state were both Qin offices.

entries.zh: 晉受魏禪，並不置，自惠帝之後，省置無恆。
entries.en: Jin left both vacant at the founding; after Emperor Hui the posts flickered in and out without a fixed rule.
entries.literal: When Jin received Wei's abdication, neither was established; from Emperor Hui onward, abolition and establishment were not constant.

entries.zh: 為之者，趙王倫、梁王肜、成都王穎、南陽王保、王敦、王導之徒，皆非復尋常人臣之職。
entries.en: When princes such as Sima Lun, Sima Rong, Sima Ying, Sima Bao, Wang Dun, and Wang Dao took these titles, they wielded power far beyond an ordinary subject's charge.
entries.literal: Those who held them—Zhao Wang Lun, Liang Wang Rong, Chengdu Wang Ying, Nanyang Wang Bao, Wang Dun, Wang Dao, and the like—were no longer the duties of ordinary ministers.

entries.zh: 光祿大夫假銀章青綬者，品秩第三，位在金紫將軍下，諸卿上。
entries.en: Silver-blue Splendid Luminaries ranked third—below gold-purple generals but above ordinary ministers.
entries.literal: Splendid luminaries grandees with silver seal and blue ribbon were grade three, below gold-purple generals and above the various ministers.

entries.zh: 漢時所置無定員，多以為拜假賵贈之使，及監護喪事。
entries.en: Han used them flexibly—often as ceremonial envoys or funeral supervisors.
entries.literal: In Han there was no fixed quota; they were often used as envoys for investitures, gifts, and funeral oversight.

entries.zh: 魏氏已來，轉復優重，不復以為使命之官。
entries.en: After Wei they became honorific rather than errand posts.
entries.literal: Since Wei they grew steadily weightier and ceased to be mere mission offices.

entries.zh: 其諸公告老者，皆家拜此位；
entries.en: Retiring dukes typically received this title by domestic edict;
entries.literal: When various dukes retired, they were all appointed to this rank at home;

entries.zh: 及在朝顯職，復用加之，及晉受命，仍舊不改，復以為優崇之制。
entries.en: Active ministers might earn it too; Jin kept the practice as a mark of esteem.
entries.literal: and for prominent posts at court it was again conferred; when Jin received the mandate it continued unchanged, again treating it as a system of honor.

entries.zh: 而諸公遜位，不復加之，或更拜上公，或以本封食公祿。
entries.en: Stepping-down dukes did not receive it again—some became upper dukes, others lived on fief income.
entries.literal: But when dukes yielded office they were not given it again; some were promoted to upper duke, some drew duke stipends from their original fiefs.

entries.zh: 其諸卿尹中朝大官年老致仕者，及內外之職加此者，前後甚眾。
entries.en: Many retired ministers and officials inside and outside received it.
entries.literal: Among ministers and capital officials who retired for age, and inner and outer posts given this rank, there were very many over time.

entries.zh: 由是或因得開府，或進加金章紫綬，又復以為禮贈之位。
entries.en: Some parlayed it into a headquarters appointment or gold-purple rank; it doubled as a ceremonial posthumous grade.
entries.literal: Hence some thereby gained headquarters, some advanced to gold seal and purple ribbon; it also served as a courtesy gift rank.

entries.zh: 泰始中，唯太子詹事楊珧加給事中光祿大夫。
entries.en: During Taishi only Yang Yao combined household supervisor with attendant-within and Splendid Luminaries.
entries.literal: In Taishi only Yang Yao, supervisor of the heir apparent's household, was additionally appointed attendant-within and splendid luminaries grandee.

entries.zh: 加兵之制，諸所供給依三品將軍。
entries.en: Military add-ons followed third-rank general perquisites.
entries.literal: For systems with added military authority, all provisions followed third-grade generals.

entries.zh: 其餘自如舊制，終武、惠、孝懷三世。
entries.en: The rest followed the old regulations through the three reigns of Wu, Hui, and Xiaohuai.
entries.literal: The rest followed old regulations through the reigns of Wu, Hui, and Xiaohuai.

entries.zh: 四征鎮安平加大將軍不開府、持節都督者，品秩第二，置參佐吏卒，幕府兵騎如常都督制，唯朝會祿賜從二品將軍之例。
entries.en: Expeditionary grand generals with credentials but no mansion ranked second; staffs matched normal commanders; court pay followed second-grade rules.
entries.literal: Four expeditions, garrisons, pacification, peace with added grand general title, without headquarters, credential-bearing commanders were grade second; staff and runners followed ordinary commander rules; only court assembly stipends followed second-grade general precedent.

entries.zh: 然則持節、都督無定員，前漢遣使始有持節。
entries.en: Area commanders had no fixed headcount; Former Han invented credential-bearing missions.
entries.literal: Thus credential-bearing commanders had no fixed quota; Former Han first had credential-bearing envoys.

entries.zh: 光武建武初，征伐四方，始權時置督軍御史，事竟罷。
entries.en: Guangwu's early campaigns used temporary army censors, then disbanded them.
entries.literal: At the start of Guangwu's Jianwu, campaigning in four directions, temporary army-supervising censors were first set up; when the task ended they were abolished.

entries.zh: 建安中，魏武為相，始遣大將軍督之。
entries.en: Mid-Jian'an Cao Cao as chancellor began assigning grand generals to oversee armies.
entries.literal: In Jian'an, Wei Wu as chancellor first dispatched grand generals to supervise.

entries.zh: 二十一年，征孫權還，夏侯惇督二十六軍是也。
entries.en: In 216, returning from the campaign against Sun Quan, Xiahou Dun supervised twenty-six armies; this is an instance.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year, returning from campaigning against Sun Quan, Xiahou Dun supervised twenty-six armies—this is an instance.

entries.zh: 魏文帝黃初三年，始置都督諸州軍事，或領刺史。
entries.en: 222 CE introduced provincial military commanders, often doubling as governors.
entries.literal: In Wei Wendi's third Huangchu year, commanders-in-chief of military affairs of various provinces were first established; some concurrently held inspector posts.

entries.zh: 又上軍大將軍曹真都督中外諸軍事、假黃鉞，則總統內外諸軍矣。
entries.en: Cao Zhen as senior grand general with the golden axe commanded every army at court and frontier.
entries.literal: Moreover Upper-army Grand General Cao Zhen commanded inner and outer armies with borrowed yellow axe—thus he commanded all armies within and without.

entries.zh: 魏明帝太和四年秋，宣帝征蜀，加號大都督。
entries.en: In the autumn of Emperor Ming of Wei's fourth Taihe year, Prince Xuan campaigned against Shu and added the title supreme commander.
entries.literal: Autumn of Wei Mingdi's fourth Taihe year, Prince Xuan campaigned against Shu and added the title supreme commander.

entries.zh: 高貴鄉公正元二年，文帝都督中外諸軍，尋加大都督。
entries.en: 254 CE Sima Zhao commanded all forces, then took supreme commander.
entries.literal: In Gaoguixiang Duke's second Zhenyuan year, Prince Wen commanded inner and outer armies; soon after he added supreme commander.

entries.zh: 及晉受禪，都督諸軍為上，臨諸軍次之，督諸軍為下；
entries.en: Jin ranked titles: commander-in-chief highest, overseer next, supervisor lowest;
entries.literal: When Jin received abdication, commander-in-chief of various armies was highest, overseeing various armies next, supervising various armies lowest;

entries.zh: 使持節為上，持節次之，假節為下。
entries.en: Full powers ranked above ordinary credential, which ranked above borrowed.
entries.literal: Bearer of full powers highest, credential-holder next, borrowed credential lowest.

entries.zh: 使持節得殺二千石以下；
entries.en: Full powers allowed executing officials through two-thousand-shi rank;
entries.literal: Bearer of full powers could execute officials down to two thousand shi;

entries.zh: 持節殺無官位人，若軍事，得與使持節同；
entries.en: Ordinary credentials covered commoners; in war matched full powers;
entries.literal: credential-holder could kill persons without office rank; in military matters could match bearer of full powers;

entries.zh: 假節唯軍事得殺犯軍令者。
entries.en: Borrowed credentials executed only military offenders.
entries.literal: borrowed credential only in military affairs could kill violators of military orders.

entries.zh: 江左以來，都督中外尤重，唯王導等權重者乃居之。
entries.en: South of the river, supreme command rarely fell except to figures as powerful as Wang Dao.
entries.literal: Since the Jiang left, commander-in-chief of inner and outer has been especially weighty; only men of heavy authority like Wang Dao have held it.

entries.zh: 散騎常侍，本秦官也。
entries.en: Elite cavalry standing attendant began under Qin.
entries.literal: Elite cavalry standing attendant—it was originally a Qin office.

entries.zh: 秦置散騎，又置中常侍，散騎騎從乘輿車後，中常侍得入禁中，皆無員，亦以為加官。
entries.en: Qin ran freelance riders behind the coach and inner-chamber standing attendants—both honorific and uncapped.
entries.literal: Qin established unattached cavalry and also palace standing attendants; unattached cavalry rode behind the imperial carriage; palace standing attendants could enter the forbidden quarters—both had no quota and served as supernumerary titles.

entries.zh: 漢東京初，省散騎，而中常侍用宦者。
entries.en: Later Han dropped freelance riders and staffed standing attendants with eunuchs.
entries.literal: Early Eastern Han cut unattached cavalry and palace standing attendants used eunuchs.

entries.zh: 魏文帝黃初初，置散騎，合之於中常侍，同掌規諫，不典事，貂榼插右，騎而散從，至晉不改。
entries.en: At the start of Huangchu, Emperor Wen of Wei restored unattached cavalry and merged them with palace standing attendants to offer counsel without managing affairs; marten-fur bags were tucked on the right as they rode in loose escort—unchanged through Jin.
entries.literal: Wei Wendi at the start of Huangchu restored unattached cavalry, merged them with palace standing attendants to jointly offer counsel without managing affairs; marten-fur bags tucked right, riding loosely escorting—unchanged through Jin.

entries.zh: 及元康中，惠帝始以宦者董猛為中常侍，後遂止。
entries.en: In Yuankang, Emperor Hui first made the eunuch Dong Meng a palace standing attendant; afterward the practice stopped.
entries.literal: In Yuankang under Emperor Hui the eunuch Dong Meng first became palace standing attendant; afterward it stopped.

entries.zh: 常為顯職。
entries.en: The post stayed an honor reserved for heavyweights.
entries.literal: It was normally an eminent post.

entries.zh: 秘書監，案漢桓帝延熹二年置秘書監，後省。
entries.en: Han Huan created a library director in 159 CE; the seat later vanished.
entries.literal: Director of the Palace Library—in tradition Emperor Huan of Han in the second year of Yanxi established a Palace Library director; later it was cut.

entries.zh: 魏武為魏王，置秘書令、丞。
entries.en: Cao Cao as Wei prince named a secretary director and deputy for archives.
entries.literal: Wei Emperor Wu as Prince of Wei established Palace Secretary director and assistant.

entries.zh: 及文帝黃初初，置中書令，典尚書奏事，而秘書改令為監。
entries.en: Huangchu split drafting from archives: Zhongshu handled memorials while the old secretary director became library supervisor.
entries.literal: When Wendi at the start of Huangchu established Palace Secretariat director to manage Secretariat memorial business, the Palace Secretary director title was changed to supervisor.

entries.zh: 後以何禎為秘書丞，而秘書先自有丞，乃以禎為秘書右丞。
entries.en: He Zhen became library deputy while a deputy already existed—so he took the new right-deputy slot.
entries.literal: Later He Zhen was appointed Palace Library assistant, but the library already had an assistant; therefore Zhen was made Right Assistant of the Palace Library.

entries.zh: 及晉受命，武帝以秘書並中書省，其秘書著作之局不廢。
entries.en: Wudi folded library staff into the Zhongshu apparatus but kept the historiography office alive.
entries.literal: When Jin received the mandate, Emperor Wu merged the Palace Library with the Palace Secretariat bureau, yet the library composition bureau was not abolished.

entries.zh: 惠帝永平中，復置秘書監，其屬官有丞，有郎，並統著作省。
entries.en: Huidi revived the library supervisor with deputies and gentlemen running the composition wing.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Hui in the Yongping era the Palace Library supervisor was restored; subordinate offices included assistants and gentlemen, jointly overseeing the Composition Bureau.

entries.zh: 著作郎，周左史之任也。
entries.en: The compiler post echoed Zhou's left historian.
entries.literal: Composition gentleman—it was the duty of Zhou's left historian.

entries.zh: 漢東京圖籍在東觀，故使名儒著作東觀，有其名，尚未有官。
entries.en: In Eastern Han, maps and registers were kept in the Eastern Observatory, so famed scholars wrote there; the title existed in name, but not yet as an office.
entries.literal: In Eastern Han, maps and registers were kept in the Eastern Observatory, so famed scholars were made to compose works in the Eastern Observatory; the name existed, but there was not yet an official post.

entries.zh: 魏明帝太和中，詔置著作郎，於此始有其官，隸中書省。
entries.en: Wei Mingdi minted the composition gentleman title under Zhongshu.
entries.literal: Wei Mingdi in the Taihe era issued an edict establishing composition gentlemen—here it first became an office, subordinate to the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 及晉受命，武帝以繆徵為中書著作郎。
entries.en: Wudi named Miao Zheng as Zhongshu compiler.
entries.literal: When Jin received the mandate, Emperor Wu appointed Miao Zheng as Palace Secretariat composition gentleman.

entries.zh: 元康二年，詔曰：「著作舊屬中書，而秘書既典文籍，今改中書著作為秘書著作。」
entries.en: In the second year of Yuankang an edict said: "Composition formerly belonged to the Palace Secretariat; since the Palace Library already manages documents, now change Palace Secretariat composition to Palace Library composition."
entries.literal: In the second year of Yuankang an edict said: "Composition formerly belonged to the Palace Secretariat; since the Palace Library already manages documents, now change Palace Secretariat composition to Palace Library composition."

entries.zh: 於是改隸秘書省。
entries.en: Compilers henceforth answered to the library bureau.
entries.literal: Thus they were reassigned to the Palace Library bureau.

entries.zh: 後別自置省而猶隸秘書。
entries.en: They eventually spun up a dedicated bureau still under library oversight.
entries.literal: Later they separately established a bureau yet still reported to the Palace Library.

entries.zh: 著作郎一人，謂之大著作郎，專掌史任，又置佐著作郎八人。
entries.en: One chief compiler ran history with eight assistants.
entries.literal: One composition gentleman was called senior composition gentleman, solely handling historical duty; eight assistant composition gentlemen were also appointed.

entries.zh: 著作郎始到職，必撰名臣傳一人。
entries.en: New compilers opened their tenure by drafting a notable minister biography.
entries.literal: When composition gentlemen first took office they had to compose one biography of a celebrated minister.

entries.zh: 晉初承魏制，置博士十九人。
entries.en: Early Jin kept nineteen classical chairs from Wei.
entries.literal: Early Jin inherited Wei regulations and established nineteen erudites.

entries.zh: 及咸甯四年，武帝初立國子學，定置國子祭酒、博士各一人，助教十五人，以教生徒。
entries.en: 278 CE launched the academy with one libationer, one professor, and fifteen assistants teaching disciples.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Xianning Emperor Wu first founded the Imperial Academy, fixing one libationer and one erudite each, fifteen teaching assistants, to instruct students.

entries.zh: 博士皆取履行清淳，通明典義者，若散騎常侍、中書侍郎、太子中庶子以上，乃得召試。
entries.en: Candidates needed pristine résumés and canonical mastery; only senior attendants and above sat the exam.
entries.literal: Erudites were all drawn from men of pure conduct who mastered canonical meaning; only those ranked elite cavalry standing attendant, Palace Secretariat deputy, heir-apparent household attendant or higher could be summoned to examination.

entries.zh: 及江左初，減為九人。
entries.en: South of the river the corps shrank to nine chairs.
entries.literal: Early east of the Yangzi it was reduced to nine.

entries.zh: 元帝末，增《儀禮》、《春秋公羊》博士各一人，合為十一人。
entries.en: Late Yuandi added Etiquette and Gongyang chairs—eleven professors.
entries.literal: At the end of Emperor Yuan's reign one Ceremonies erudite each was added for Etiquette and Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, totaling eleven.

entries.zh: 後又增為十六人，不復分掌《五經》，而謂之太學博士也。
entries.en: The roster grew to sixteen unified professors rather than one canon each.
entries.literal: Later it was increased to sixteen; they no longer split custody of the Five Classics but were called Imperial Academy erudites.

entries.zh: 孝武太元十年，損國子助教員為十人。
entries.en: 385 CE trimmed academy assistants to ten.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowu in the tenth year of Taiyuan cut Imperial Academy assistant posts to ten.

entries.zh: 太子太傅、少傅，皆古官也。
entries.en: Heir tutors were classical posts.
entries.literal: Grand tutor and junior tutor of the heir apparent—both were ancient offices.

entries.zh: 泰始三年，武帝始建官，各置一人，尚未置詹事，官事無大小，皆由二傅，並有功曹、主簿、五官。
entries.en: In the third year of Taishi (267), Emperor Wu first created these offices, one post each; before any household supervisor was appointed, all business, large or small, passed through the two tutors, who also had merit clerks, chief clerks, and gatekeeper officers.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taishi Emperor Wu first established the offices, each one post; not yet appointing a household supervisor—office business large or small all passed through the two tutors, who also had merit clerks, chief clerks, and gatekeeper officers.

entries.zh: 太傅中二千石，少傅二千石。
entries.en: Senior tutor drew near two thousand shi; junior tutor two thousand.
entries.literal: Grand tutor at salary comparable to two thousand shi; junior tutor at two thousand shi.

entries.zh: 其訓導者，太傅在前，少傅在後。
entries.en: Instruction lined up senior tutor forward, junior aft.
entries.literal: Those who instructed—grand tutor in front, junior tutor behind.

entries.zh: 皇太子先拜，諸傅然後答之。
entries.en: The crown prince bowed first; tutors returned the courtesy.
entries.literal: The imperial heir first bowed; the tutors then answered.

entries.zh: 武帝后以儲副體尊，遂命諸公居之；
entries.en: Once the heir's rank swelled, grandees filled those chairs;
entries.literal: Later Emperor Wu because the heir's station was august ordered various dukes to occupy the posts;

entries.zh: 以本位重，故或行或領。
entries.en: weight meant some served full-time, some doubled other posts.
entries.literal: because the posts were weighty, therefore some served in person and some held concurrent titles.

entries.zh: 時侍中任愷，武帝所親敬，復使領之，蓋一時之制也。
entries.en: Ren Kai briefly doubled duty—a court expedient.
entries.literal: At the time attendant Ren Kai, whom Emperor Wu personally favored and respected, was also made to oversee them—probably an arrangement of the moment.

entries.zh: 咸甯元年，以給事黃門侍郎楊珧為詹事，掌宮事，二傅不復領官屬。
entries.en: 275 CE Yang Yao became household supervisor so tutors shed staff.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xianning gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gates Yang Yao was made household supervisor handling palace business; the two tutors no longer supervised subordinates.

entries.zh: 及楊珧為衛將軍，領少傅，省詹事，遂崇廣傅訓，命太尉賈充領太保，司空齊王攸領太傅，所置吏屬復如舊。
entries.en: When Yang Yao became General of the Guards and concurrently Junior Tutor, the household supervisor was abolished and tutor instruction was expanded: Grand Commandant Jia Chong was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Guardian, and Minister of Works Prince You of Qi as Grand Tutor; the appointed clerical staff returned to the old pattern.
entries.literal: When Yang Yao became General of the Guards and concurrently Junior Tutor, the household supervisor was abolished; tutor instruction was then enlarged—Grand Commandant Jia Chong was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Guardian, and Minister of Works Prince You of Qi as Grand Tutor; the appointed clerical staff returned as before.

entries.zh: 二傅進賢兩梁冠，黑介幘，五時朝服，佩水蒼玉，食奉日三斛。
entries.en: Tutors wore two-ridged caps, black kerchiefs, seasonal robes, jade, three hu daily.
entries.literal: The two tutors wore two-beam advanced-worth caps, black scarves, five-seasons court dress, dark aquamarine jade, daily grain allowance three hu.

entries.zh: 太康二年，始給春賜絹五十匹，秋絹百匹，綿百斤。
entries.en: 281 CE added seasonal silk and cotton allotments.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taikang they began granting spring silk fifty bolts, autumn silk one hundred bolts, cotton one hundred jin.

entries.zh: 其後太尉汝南王亮、車騎將軍楊駿、司空衛瓘、石鑒皆領傅保，猶不置詹事，以終武帝之世。
entries.en: Afterward, the Grand Commandant Prince Liang of Runan, General of Chariots and Cavalry Yang Jun, Minister of Works Wei Guan, and Shi Jian all concurrently held tutor-guardian posts, but no household supervisor was appointed through the end of Emperor Wu's reign.
entries.literal: Afterward Grand Commandant Prince Liang of Runan, General of Chariots and Cavalry Yang Jun, Minister of Works Wei Guan, and Shi Jian all held tutor-guardian posts; still no household supervisor was appointed through Emperor Wu's reign.

entries.zh: 惠帝元康元年，復置詹事，二傅給菜田六頃，田騶六人，立夏後不及田者，食奉一年。
entries.en: 291 CE revived the supervisor and granted tutors vegetable plots like ministers.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui in the first year of Yuankang restored household supervisor; the two tutors received six qing vegetable land and six field runners; if after beginning of summer land had not been awarded, one year's salary instead.

entries.zh: 置丞一人，秩千石；
entries.en: One deputy at one thousand shi;
entries.literal: One assistant was placed at rank one thousand shi;

entries.zh: 主簿、五官掾、功曹史、主記門下史、錄事、戶曹法曹倉曹賊曹功曹書佐、門下亭長、門下書佐、省事各一人，給赤耳安車一乘。
entries.en: full tutor household staff plus a red-eared carriage.
entries.literal: chief clerk, gatekeeper officers, merit clerk, chief recorder, gate clerks, recorder, household office, law office, granary office, thieves office, merit clerk assistants, gate precinct chief, gate document clerks, miscellaneous clerks—one each; one red-eared secure carriage granted.

entries.zh: 及湣懷建官，乃置六傅，三太、三少，以景帝諱師，故改太師為太保，通省尚書事，詹事文書關由六傅。
entries.en: Minhuai's six tutors—taboo turned instructor into guardian—shared Secretariat oversight.
entries.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai established offices, six tutors were set—three senior and three junior—because of the taboo on Emperor Jing's name Shi, therefore Grand Instructor was changed to senior guardian, jointly overseeing Secretariat business; household paperwork passed through all six tutors.

entries.zh: 然自元康之後，諸傅或二或三，或四或六，及永康中復不置詹事也。
entries.en: Tutor counts fluctuated; Yongkang dropped the supervisor again.
entries.literal: Yet from Yuankang onward tutors numbered two, three, four, or six; by Yongkang household supervisor was again absent.

entries.zh: 自太安已來置詹事，終孝懷之世。
entries.en: Tai'an forward kept supervisors through the prince's fall.
entries.literal: From Tai'an onward household supervisor was set through Emperor Xiaohuai's reign.

entries.zh: 渡江之後，有太傅少傅，不立師保。
entries.en: South of the river kept grand and junior tutors only.
entries.literal: After crossing the Yangzi there were grand and junior tutors but no instructor or guardian titles.

entries.zh: 嘉平四年，關中饑，宣帝表徙冀州農夫五千人佃上邽，興京兆、天水、南安鹽池，以益軍實。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Jiaping, a Guanzhong famine drew Sima Yi’s memorial: shift five thousand Ji farmers to Shanggui and work the Jingzhao, Tianshui, and Nan’an brine pans for army stores.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaping, when Guanzhong suffered famine, Emperor Xuan memorialized to move five thousand farmers from Ji Province to colonize Shanggui and to develop the salt pools of Jingzhao, Tianshui, and Nan’an in order to enlarge military stores.

entries.zh: 青龍元年，開成國渠自陳倉至槐里；
entries.en: In the first year of Qinglong, they cut the Chengguo Canal between Chencang and Huaili.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qinglong, they opened the Chengguo Canal from Chencang to Huaili;

entries.zh: 築臨晉陂，引汧洛溉舄鹵之地三千餘頃，國以充實焉，
entries.en: The Linjin barrage steered the Qian and Luo onto thirty thousand acres of salty flats until the exchequer filled.
entries.literal: they built the Linjin weir, drew the Qian and Luo to irrigate more than three thousand qing of alkaline soil, and the state grew ample thereby.

entries.zh: 正始四年，宣帝又督諸軍伐吳將諸葛恪，焚其積聚，恪棄城遁走。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Zhengshi, Sima Yi next led the strike on Zhuge Ke—torched Wu supplies and drove Ke from his walls.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengshi, Emperor Xuan again supervised the various armies in attacking Wu general Zhuge Ke, burned Ke's stockpiled grain, and Ke abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 帝因欲廣田積穀，為兼併之計，乃使鄧艾行陳、項以東，至壽春地。
entries.en: Wishing to broaden fields and store grain for a strategy of piecemeal annexation, the emperor sent Deng Ai to survey east from Chen and Xiang as far as the Shouchun region.
entries.literal: The emperor therefore wished to broaden fields and pile grain for a strategy of piecemeal annexation, and sent Deng Ai to survey east from Chen and Xiang as far as the Shouchun region.

entries.zh: 艾以為田良水少，不足以盡地利，宜開河渠，可以大積軍糧，又通運漕之道。
entries.en: Deng Ai held that the soil was good but water scarce, not enough to exhaust the land's potential, and that rivers and canals should be opened to stockpile army grain in quantity and also to connect transport routes.
entries.literal: Ai held that the soil was good but water scarce—not enough to exhaust the land's potential—and that rivers and canals should be opened to stockpile army grain in quantity and also link transport routes.

entries.zh: 乃著《濟河論》以喻其指。
entries.en: He framed the argument in his 'Discourse on Channeling the Ji.'
entries.literal: He therefore composed the 'Treatise on the Ji River' to explain his meaning.

entries.zh: 又以為昔破黃巾，因為屯田，積穀許都，以制四方。
entries.en: He also argued that when the Yellow Turbans were crushed in former times, agricultural colonies were founded and grain piled at Xu so as to control the four quarters.
entries.literal: He also argued that when the Yellow Turbans were crushed in former times, agricultural colonies had been founded and grain piled at Xu so as to control the four quarters.

entries.zh: 今三隅已定，事在淮南。
entries.en: With three fronts quiet, only Huainan still mattered.
entries.literal: Now the three corners were settled; what remained lay in Huainan.

entries.zh: 每大軍征舉，運兵過半，功費巨億，以為大役。
entries.en: Each campaign burned logistics—half the effort was convoys—and bills ran into billions of cash.
entries.literal: Whenever great armies mobilized, more than half the burden was moving troops—costs ran to hundreds of millions and constituted a vast undertaking.

entries.zh: 陳蔡之間，土下田良，可省許昌左右諸稻田，並水東下。
entries.en: The Chen–Cai depression could soak up irrigation shed from the Xuchang rice plots if sluices turned east.
entries.literal: Between Chen and Cai the ground was low and fertile; one could retire the paddy fields around Xuchang and send all the water eastward.

entries.zh: 令淮北二萬人、淮南三萬人分休，且佃且守。
entries.en: He proposed fifty thousand men alternating guard duty with tillage on both banks of the Huai.
entries.literal: Order twenty thousand men north of the Huai and thirty thousand south of it to rotate rest with farming and guarding.

entries.zh: 水豐，常收三倍于西，計除眾費，歲完五百萬斛以為軍資。
entries.en: Wet years tripled western yields; after costs, five million hu a year could arm the campaigns.
entries.literal: With abundant water, harvests constantly tripled those west of the river; deducting all expenses, five million hu could be delivered yearly for military supply.

entries.zh: 六七年間，可積三千萬餘斛於淮北，此則十萬之眾五年食也。
entries.en: Six or seven harvests could stack thirty million hu north of the river—five years' rations for a hundred-thousand-man host.
entries.literal: In six or seven years one could stockpile over thirty million hu north of the Huai—food enough for an army of one hundred thousand for five years.

entries.zh: 以此乘敵，無不克矣。
entries.en: With this to strike the enemy, nothing would fail to be overcome.
entries.literal: With this to strike the enemy, nothing would withstand you.

entries.zh: 宣帝善之，皆如艾計施行。
entries.en: Sima Yi signed off and executed Deng Ai's blueprint.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan approved it and implemented everything according to Ai's plan.

entries.zh: 遂北臨淮水，自鐘離而南橫石以西，盡沘水四百餘里，五里置一營，營六十人，且佃且守。
entries.en: They lined the Huai from Zhongli past Hengshi—four hundred li of Bi River front—posting sixty-man camps every five li to plough under arms.
entries.literal: They therefore pressed north to the Huai River; from Zhongli south to west of Hengshi, and along the Bi River for over four hundred li, every five li they placed a camp of sixty men who farmed while they guarded.

entries.zh: 兼修廣淮陽、百尺二渠，上引河流，下通淮潁，大治諸陂于潁南、潁北，穿渠三百餘里，溉田二萬頃，淮南、淮北皆相連接。
entries.en: They dredged Huaiyang and Baichi, tied the Yellow River spill to Huai and Ying, refaced north–south Ying dikes, bored three hundred li of trench, and knitted Huai south and north across twenty thousand qing.
entries.literal: They also widened the Huaiyang and Baichi canals, drawing the great river above and linking Huai and Ying below, greatly repairing the various weirs south and north of the Ying, cutting channels over three hundred li and irrigating twenty thousand qing of fields; Huainan and north of the Huai linked into one network.

entries.zh: 自壽春到京師，農官兵田，雞犬之聲，阡陌相屬。
entries.en: Between Shouchun and Luoyang, garrison farms crowded the roads—chickens and dogs crowding the same dikes.
entries.literal: From Shouchun to the capital, military colonies lined the fields; the crowing of chickens and barking of dogs rose along paths that stretched unbroken.

entries.zh: 每東南有事，大軍出征，泛舟而下，達于江淮，資食有儲，而無水害，艾所建也。
entries.en: Whenever southeast campaigns launched, barges slid down safe channels to the Yangzi–Huai junction with grain to spare—Deng Ai's hydraulic shield.
entries.literal: Whenever trouble arose in the southeast and great armies marched out, boats floated downstream to reach the Yangzi and Huai; provisions lay stored and flood harm was avoided—this was what Ai built.

entries.zh: 昔者先王量地以制邑，度地以居民，因三才以節其務，敬四序以成其業，觀其謠俗而正其紀綱。
entries.en: The kings of old sized out territory to lay out towns, reckoned acreage to house the people, tuned their duties to the triad of Heaven, earth, and mankind, kept faith with the turning year to finish each season's work, and read popular sentiment so they could straighten what statute and custom required.
entries.literal: In antiquity the former kings measured land to regulate settlements, surveyed land to settle the people, guided their tasks according to the three powers (Heaven, Earth, and Man), honored the four seasons to complete their undertakings, and inspected local songs and customs to set right law and discipline.

entries.zh: 勖農桑之本，通魚鹽之利，登良山而采符玉，泛瀛海而罩珠璣。
entries.en: They promoted tillage and silk as the economy's foundation, extended trade in fish and salt, scaled high hills for ritual jade, and crossed the deep sea to harvest pearls.
entries.literal: They urged the root of farming and sericulture, opened access to the profit of fish and salt, climbed worthy hills to gather tally-jade, and sailed the Eastern Sea to seine pearls and precious beads.

entries.zh: 日中為市，總天下之隸，先諸布帛，繼以貨泉，貿遷有無，各得其所。
entries.en: When the sun stood at the meridian they opened the mart, drawing workers from across the land—first with bolts of cloth, then with coined cash—swapping abundance for scarcity until buyer and seller were matched.
entries.literal: They held market at midday, assembling all the laborers of the realm; first came cloth and silk, then currency; they traded surplus for want so that each found his proper place.

entries.zh: 《周禮》，正月始和，乃布教于象魏。
entries.en: The Zhouli records that with the new year's first month they proclaimed the royal teachings beneath the watch-towers flanking the palace gate.
entries.literal: The Rites of Zhou says: In the first month, when harmony begins, they promulgated instruction at the palace gate-towers (xiangwei).

entries.zh: 若乃一夫之士，十畝之宅，三日之徭，九均之賦，施陽禮以興其讓，命春社以勖其耕。
entries.en: Each farmer had his plot and homestead, a short stint of labor service, and the graded land tax; ritual taught humility, and the spring communal feast kept everyone at the plough.
entries.literal: Where one husbandman held his allotment, a homestead of ten mu, three days of corvée, and the ninefold equitable levy, they applied the 'yang' rites to encourage yielding deference and ordered the spring she sacrifice to spur plowing.

entries.zh: 天之所貴者人也，明之所求者學也，治《經》入官，則君子之道焉。
entries.en: Heaven prizes humanity; good government prizes scholarship; the path of the junzi runs through the canon and into service.
entries.literal: What Heaven esteems is human beings; what enlightened rule seeks is learning; mastering the Classics and entering office—that is the way of the gentleman.

entries.zh: 《詩》曰：「三之日於耜，四之日舉趾。」
entries.en: The Odes says: 'On the third month they sharpen the plough-shares; on the fourth month they raise their feet [to walk to the fields].'
entries.literal: The Odes says: 'On the third month they sharpen the plough-shares; on the fourth month they raise their feet [to walk to the fields].'

entries.zh: 是以農官澤虞，各有攸次，父兄之習，不玩而成，十五從務，始勝衣服，鄉無遊手，邑不廢時，所謂厥初生民，各從其事者也。
entries.en: Hence field overseers and marsh wardens stood in fixed posts; household instruction hardened young hands without play; at fifteen youths took up work and adult clothes; villages held no loafers and towns lost no farming window—that was the world in which, as the ode says, each newborn generation stuck to its calling.
entries.literal: Therefore the agricultural and forestry officials each held his station; the customs of fathers and elders were perfected without idle amusement; at fifteen they undertook labor and first wore full adult dress; in the hamlets none wandered idle, in the towns the seasons were not wasted—this is what is meant by 'when the people first arose, each followed his proper task.'

entries.zh: 是以太公通市井之貨，以致齊國之強；
entries.en: That is how Jiang Taigong turned ward and marketplace into strength for Qi.
entries.literal: Thus the Grand Duke opened the circulation of market goods and thereby brought strength to the state of Qi.

entries.zh: 鴟夷善發斂之居，以盛中陶之業。
entries.en: Fan Li, styled Lord Chiyi, knew how to marshal stores and levies, and so he built up the great pottery workshops of the interior.
entries.literal: Lord Chiyi excelled at the depots for fiscal collection; thereby he magnified the pottery industry of the central heartland.

entries.zh: 昔在金天，勤於民事，命春鳸以耕稼，召夏鳸以耘鋤，秋鳸所以收斂，冬鳸于焉蓋藏。
entries.en: Long ago, under Jin Tian, he was diligent in the people's tasks: he appointed the spring bird-officer for plowing and sowing, summoned the summer bird-officer for weeding and hoeing, used the autumn bird-officer for gathering the harvest, and assigned the winter bird-officer for covering and storing grain.
entries.literal: Long ago, in the reign associated with Jin Tian, he was diligent in the people's tasks: he appointed the spring bird-officer for plowing and sowing, summoned the summer bird-officer for weeding and hoeing, relied on the autumn bird-officer for gathering the harvest, and assigned the winter bird-officer for laying grain by.

entries.zh: 《書》曰：「曆象日月星辰，敬授民時。」
entries.en: The Documents says: 'We calculated and aligned the sun, moon, and stars, and reverently gave the people their seasons.'
entries.literal: The Documents says: 'We calculated and aligned the sun, moon, and stars, and reverently gave the people their seasons.'

entries.zh: 傳曰：「禹稷躬稼而有天下。」
entries.en: The tradition says: 'Yu and Hou Ji personally farmed and thereby gained the realm.'
entries.literal: The tradition says: 'Yu and Hou Ji personally farmed and thereby gained the realm.'

entries.zh: 若乃九土既敷，四民承范，東吳有齒角之饒，西蜀有丹沙之富，兗豫漆絲之廥，燕齊怪石之府，秦邠旄羽，迥帶琅玕，荊郢桂林，旁通竹箭，江幹橘柚，河外舟車，遼西旃罽之鄉，蔥右蒲梢之駿，殖物怪錯，於何不有。
entries.en: Once the nine domains were laid out and the four classes received their models, eastern Wu had abundance of ivory and horn, western Shu had cinnabar wealth, Yan and Yu stored lacquer and silk, Yan and Qi were treasuries of strange stone, Qin and Bin offered yak tails and feathers strung with carnelian, Jing, Ying, and Guilin connected bamboo arrows, riverbanks grew oranges and pomelos, beyond the Yellow River ran boats and carts, Liaoxi was a land of felts and rugs, and west of the Cong ranges came Pu-shao steeds—products multiplied in bewildering variety; what was there that could not be found?
entries.literal: When the nine provinces had been laid out and the four peoples received their models, eastern Wu had abundance in ivory and horn, western Shu hoarded cinnabar, Yan and Henan barns brimmed with lacquer and silk, Yan and Qi quarried strange stones, Qin and Bin offered yak tails and kingfisher feathers strung with carnelian, Jing, Ying, and Guilin shipped bamboo arrows, river terraces grew oranges and pomelos, beyond the Yellow River ran boats and carts, Liaoxi was home to felts and rugs, and past the Cong ranges came the famed Pu-shao horses—products multiplied bewilderingly; what was there that could not be found?

entries.zh: 若乃上法星象，下料無外，因天地之利，而總山海之饒，百畝之田，十一而稅，九年躬稼，而有三年之蓄，可以長孺齒，可以養耆年。
entries.en: Taking cues from the sky and leaving no acre unmeasured on earth, pooling hill and sea wealth, titheing one tenth off each hundred-mu farm, and insisting that nine harvest years include three years of reserves—that was how children grew strong and elders were fed.
entries.literal: When they took pattern from the stars above and omitted nothing in surveying below, relying on heaven-and-earth profit and gathering the bounty of mountains and seas, for fields of one hundred mu they levied one part in ten; after nine years of the ruler personally farming they laid up three years' surplus—thereby they could nurture the young and sustain the aged.

entries.zh: 因乎人民，用之邦國，宮室有度，旗章有序。
entries.en: Carried into hamlet and kingdom, it fixed how high halls might rise and how banners should march in order.
entries.literal: Applied among the people and deployed in the feudal states, palace chambers kept their degrees of rank, flags and emblems kept their proper sequence.

entries.zh: 朝聘自其儀，宴饗由其制，家殷國阜，遠至邇安。
entries.en: Embassies and banquets each had rule-books; wealth filled granaries while neighbors stayed calm.
entries.literal: Court audiences and diplomatic missions followed their ritual forms; feasts and communal drinks followed their regulations; households grew rich and the state prosperous, the distant submitted and the near rested secure.

entries.zh: 救水旱之災，恤寰瀛之弊，然後王之常膳，乃間笙鏞。
entries.en: They drained floods, eased drought, and patched every coastland hurt by scarcity—only then did the throne dine with leisure enough to hear bronze bells.
entries.literal: They relieved flood and drought disasters and aided distress throughout the realm; only after that did the king's ordinary meals occasionally include the music of mouth organs and bells.

entries.zh: 商周之興，用此道也。
entries.en: Shang and Zhou rose by walking this same road.
entries.literal: The rise of Shang and Zhou relied on this approach.

entries.zh: 辛紂暴虐，玩其經費，金鏤傾宮，廣延百里，玉飾鹿臺，崇高千仞，宮中九市，各有女司。
entries.en: King Zhou of Shang (Di Xin) wrecked the treasury through cruelty—gold sheathing for the tilted palace over endless leagues, jade facing for Deer Terrace up sheer cliffs, and nine separate markets inside the palace, each run by female clerks.
entries.literal: Xin Zhou was cruel and violent, squandering resources: the tilted palace was overlaid with gold and stretched a hundred li; the Deer Terrace was faced with jade and rose a thousand ren; inside the palace stood nine markets, each supervised by women.

entries.zh: 厚賦以實鹿臺之錢，大斂以增钜橋之粟，多發妖冶以充傾宮之麗，廣收珍玩以備沙丘之遊。
entries.en: Extortion stacked bronze at Deer Terrace, bulk grain at Juqiao, concubines for the leaning halls, and curios for the revels at Sand Dunes.
entries.literal: Heavy levies filled the coin stored at Deer Terrace; vast extractions swelled the grain at Great Bridge Granary; they collected hosts of seductive women to pack the tilted palace with beauty, and amassed rare treasures to supply the revels at Sand Dunes.

entries.zh: 懸肉成林，積醪為沼，使男女裸體相逐於其間，伏詣酒池中牛飲者三千餘人，宮中以錦綺為席，綾紈為薦。
entries.en: Carcasses hung like a forest, wine pooled like a pond; stripped revelers chased one another while thousands flopped at the pool's lip and sucked wine like oxen; chambers were carpeted in brocade and padded with figured silk.
entries.literal: They hung meat until it formed a forest and piled ale until it became a marsh; they made men and women chase one another naked within them; more than three thousand people lay prone along the ale pool and drank like cattle; inside the palace they used damask for mats and fine silk for cushions.

entries.zh: 及周王誅紂，肅拜殷墟，乃盡振鹿財，並頒橋粟，上天降休，殷人大喜。
entries.en: When King Wu smote the Shang king he emptied the Deer Terrace vaults, threw open Juqiao's granaries, and the conquered capital hailed heaven's mercy.
entries.literal: When the king of Zhou punished Zhou of Shang and reverently bowed amid the ruins of Yin, he shook out everything hoarded at Deer Terrace and distributed all the grain from Bridge Granary; Heaven sent its blessing, and the Yin people rejoiced greatly.

entries.zh: 王赧云季，徙都西周，九鼎淪沒，二南堙盡，貸于百姓，無以償之，乃上層臺以避其責，周人謂王所居為逃責臺者也。
entries.en: King Nan's late reign shifted the court west, lost the cauldrons, silenced the southern hymns, borrowed until bankruptcy, and hid on a platform locals mocked as the terrace for outrunning debt.
