entries.literal: In the closing years of King Nan he moved the capital to western Zhou; the Nine Tripods sank from sight and the 'two southern' odes fell silent; he borrowed from the hundred surnames and could not repay, so he climbed a high terrace to dodge his creditors—the Zhou people called the king's residence the Debt-Fleeing Terrace.

entries.zh: 昔周姬公制以六典，職方陳其九貢，頒財內府，永為不刊。
entries.en: Formerly the Duke of Zhou framed the six canons; the Office of Regions set out the nine tribute items; revenue entered the inner treasury and remained an unchanging statute.
entries.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou framed the six canons; the Office of Regions listed the nine tribute items; revenue entered the inner treasury and remained an unchanging statute.

entries.zh: 及刑政陵夷，菁茅罕至，魯侯初踐畝之稅，秦君收太半之入，前王之範，靡有孑遺。
entries.en: As government frayed, ritual bundles of thatch grew rare; Lu pioneered the acre tax, Qin seized over half the crop, and ancient fiscal norms vanished.
entries.literal: When punishments and government slackened, fine tribute grass seldom arrived; the lord of Lu first trod the tax on field yield; the lord of Qin took more than half the harvest; the models of former kings hardly survived.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：班固為《殖貨志》，自三代至王莽之誅，網羅前載，其文詳悉。
entries.en: The editors comment: Ban Gu's 'Huozhi zhi' runs from the Xia-Shang-Zhou age to Wang Mang's fall, netting prior sources in exhaustive detail.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Ban Gu composed the 'Treatise on Increasing Wealth,' spanning from the Three Dynasties down to the execution of Wang Mang; it gathers earlier records and its text is thorough.

entries.zh: 吳孫休時，烏程人有得困病，及差，能以響言者，言于此而聞於彼。
entries.en: During Sun Xiu's reign a Wucheng convalescent acquired ventriloquy that carried his voice miles from his lips.
entries.literal: Under Wu's Sun Xiu, a man of Wucheng fell deathly ill; after he recovered he could "resounding-speak" — speak here and be heard there.

entries.zh: 自其所聽之，不覺其聲之大也。
entries.en: Beside him it sounded no louder than ordinary speech.
entries.literal: From the listener's own place he did not notice the sound as particularly loud.

entries.zh: 自遠聽之，如人對言，不覺聲之自遠來也。
entries.en: From afar it seemed like conversation at arm's length, with no hint of distant projection.
entries.literal: From a distance it was like face-to-face talk; one did not sense that the voice came from far away.

entries.zh: 聲之所往，隨其所向，遠者所過十數里。
entries.en: He could steer the voice through a dozen leagues or more.
entries.literal: The sound went wherever he aimed it; those farthest heard it across more than ten li.

entries.zh: 其鄰人有責息于外，歷年不還，乃假之使為責讓，懼以禍福。
entries.en: A creditor used him to haunt a defaulter abroad with ghostly threats of blessing or woe.
entries.literal: A neighbor had money lent abroad that went unreturned for years; he borrowed the gift to have him deliver rebukes, threatening fortune or calamity.

entries.zh: 負物者以為鬼神，即傎倒畀之，其人亦不自知所以然也。
entries.en: The frightened borrower paid in full at once, while the wonder-worker himself hardly grasped the trick.
entries.literal: The debtor took it for a spirit, immediately turned everything over in payment; that man also did not know why it happened thus.

entries.zh: 言不從之咎也。
entries.en: The historians filed it under portents of distorted speech.
entries.literal: This was a fault arising from words not following their proper course.

entries.zh: 魏時起安世殿，武帝后居之。
entries.en: Wei builders raised Anshi Hall, later occupied by Sima Yan's empress.
entries.literal: In Wei they built Anshi Hall; later the empress of Emperor Wu resided there.

entries.zh: 安世，武帝字也。
entries.en: The hall bore Sima Yan's childhood name, Anshi.
entries.literal: Anshi was Emperor Wu's courtesy name.

entries.zh: 武帝每延群臣，多說平生常事，未嘗及經國遠圖。
entries.en: At court he dwelt on small talk, never on how to steer the empire.
entries.literal: Whenever Emperor Wu extended audiences to ministers he spoke mostly of trivial personal matters and never touched long-term state plans.

entries.zh: 此言之不從也。
entries.en: It marked another omen of rulers who would not voice the nation's business.
entries.literal: This was a case of words not following what duty required.

entries.zh: 何曾謂子遵曰：「國家無貽厥之謀，及身而已，後嗣其殆乎！
entries.en: He Ceng said to his son Zun: "The state has no plan to hand down its legacy; it will exhaust itself in this generation — will not posterity be endangered?
entries.literal: He Ceng said to his son Zun: "The state has no plan to hand down its legacy; it will exhaust itself in this generation — will not posterity be endangered?

entries.zh: 此子孫之憂也。」
entries.en: That is posterity's worry."
entries.literal: That is posterity's worry."

entries.zh: 自永熙後王室漸亂，永嘉中天下大壞，及何綏以非辜被殺，皆如曾言。
entries.en: From Yongxi onward the clan unraveled; Yongjia's catastrophe and He Sui's unjust death fulfilled his prophecy.
entries.literal: After Yongxi the royal house slid into disorder; in Yongjia the realm shattered; when He Sui was killed without guilt — all happened as Ceng had said.

entries.zh: 趙王倫廢惠帝于金墉城，改號金墉城為永安宮。
entries.en: Sima Lun cast Emperor Hui into Jinyong and cynically rebranded the prison Yong'an.
entries.literal: Prince Zhao Sima Lun deposed Emperor Hui at Jinyong fortress and renamed the fortress Yong'an Palace.

entries.zh: 帝尋復位而倫誅。
entries.en: Hui returned; Lun went to the block.
entries.literal: The emperor soon regained the throne and Lun was executed.

entries.zh: 惠帝永興元年，詔廢太子覃還為清河王，立成都王潁為皇太弟，猶加侍中、大都督，領丞相，備九錫，封二十郡，如魏王故事。
entries.en: Yongxing opened with a frantic rearrangement: Tan demoted to Qinghe, Ying named imperial heir while hoarding every title Cao Cao once held.
entries.literal: In Emperor Hui's first Yongxing year an edict deposed Crown Prince Tan, restoring him as Prince of Qinghe, and established Prince Ying of Chengdu as heir-apparent to the throne, still adding palace attendant, grand commander, chancellor, the full nine bestowals, enfeoffment over twenty commanderies, on the model of the Wei king.

entries.zh: 案周禮傳國以胤不以勳，故雖公旦之聖不易成王之嗣，所以遠絕覬覦，永一宗祧。
entries.en: Zhou law crowns the legitimate son, not the ablest man, which is why the Duke of Zhou never supplanted King Cheng — it blocks usurpation.
entries.literal: The Zhou ritual transmits the state by heir of the body, not by merit; therefore even the Duke of Zhou's sageness did not replace King Cheng's succession — thereby cutting off ambition far off and unifying the ancestral offering forever.

entries.zh: 後代遵履，改之則亂。
entries.en: Break that pattern, and turmoil follows.
entries.literal: Later ages observed this; altering it brings chaos.

entries.zh: 今擬非其實，僭差已甚。
entries.en: The court's scheme was a fiction and staggeringly presumptuous.
entries.literal: Now the arrangement did not match reality; presumption was already extreme.

entries.zh: 且既為國嗣，則不應復開封土，兼領庶職。
entries.en: An heir ought not also command twenty commanderies and a stack of ministries.
entries.literal: Moreover, once one is heir-apparent of the state, one should not again open feudal lands and concurrently hold miscellaneous offices.

entries.zh: 此言之不從，進退乖爽，故帝既播越，穎亦不終，是其咎僭也。
entries.en: When speech and policy twist so wildly, the sovereign flees and the favorite prince dies — classic "presumption" blame.
entries.literal: This was words unheeded and advance-and-retreat perverse; therefore the emperor was driven into exile and Ying met no good end — this was the fault of presumption.

entries.zh: 後猶不悟，又立懷帝為皇太弟。
entries.en: Still unrepentant, they repeated the error with Emperor Huai.
entries.literal: Later they still did not understand, and again set up Emperor Huai as heir-apparent in the same manner.

entries.zh: 懷終流弑，不永厥祚，又其應也。
entries.en: Huai perished as a fugitive pretender — another proof of the omen.
entries.literal: Huai in the end was murdered in exile; his line did not last — again the fulfillment.

entries.zh: 語曰，「變古易常，不亂則亡」，此之謂乎。
entries.en: The saying goes: "Change the archaic and alter the constant — without chaos comes ruin" — was it not this?
entries.literal: The saying goes: "Change the archaic and alter the constant — without chaos comes ruin" — was it not this?

entries.zh: 元帝永昌二年，大將軍王敦下據姑孰。
entries.en: During Yuan-di's Yongchang second year Wang Dun occupied Gushu.
entries.literal: In Emperor Yuan's second Yongchang year Grand General Wang Dun descended and seized Gushu.

entries.zh: 百姓訛言行蟲病，食人大孔，數日入腹，入腹則死；
entries.en: A panic spread of parasites burrowing through flesh and finishing their victim from within.
entries.literal: The people spread a rumor of a worm disease that ate large holes in people; in several days it entered the belly; once inside, death followed;

entries.zh: 療之有方，當得白犬膽以為藥。
entries.en: Charlatans prescribed gall from a white dog as the cure.
entries.literal: for treatment there was a recipe: one needed white dog gall as medicine.

entries.zh: 自淮泗遂及京都，數日之間，百姓驚擾，人人皆自云已得蟲病。
entries.en: The scare raced from the Huai-Si lowlands to Luoyang until every household insisted worms gnawed at them.
entries.literal: From Huai-Si it reached the capital; within days the populace was in turmoil; everyone claimed already to have the worm sickness.

entries.zh: 又云，始在外時，當燒鐵以灼之。
entries.en: The remedy was to brand oneself with red-hot iron before the creatures reached the gut.
entries.literal: They also said that while still outside the body one ought to heat iron and cauterize.

entries.zh: 於是翕然，被燒灼者十七八矣。
entries.en: In the frenzy seven or eight victims in ten scarred themselves.
entries.literal: Thereupon they rushed to comply; seventeen or eighteen in ten suffered burns.

entries.zh: 而白犬暴貴，至相請奪，其價十倍。
entries.en: White hounds soared in value as families outbid one another.
entries.literal: White dogs suddenly became costly; people begged and snatched for them until prices multiplied tenfold.

entries.zh: 或有自云能行燒鐵灼者，賃灼百姓，日得五六萬，憊而後已。
entries.en: Enterprising torturers rented their branding services for tens of thousands of cash a day.
entries.literal: Some claimed they could perform the iron burn, hiring themselves out to cauterize the people, earning fifty or sixty thousand a day until exhausted.

entries.zh: 四五日漸靜。
entries.en: Within a week the hysteria ebbed.
entries.literal: After four or five days it gradually quieted.

entries.zh: 說曰：「夫裸蟲人類，而人為之主。
entries.en: Exegesis states: "Hairless creatures are the human class, yet humans are their master.
entries.literal: Exegesis states: "Hairless creatures are the human class, yet humans are their master.

entries.zh: 今云蟲食人，言本同臭類而相殘賊也。
entries.en: Now it says worms eat humans — it means those of the same odor-class injuring one another.
entries.literal: Now it says worms eat humans — it means those of the same odor-class injuring one another.

entries.zh: 自下而上，明其逆也。
entries.en: From below to above shows inversion.
entries.literal: From below to above shows inversion.

entries.zh: 必入腹者，言害由中不由外也。
entries.en: That it must enter the belly means harm comes from within, not without.
entries.literal: That it must enter the belly means harm comes from within, not without.

entries.zh: 犬有守衛之性，白者金色，而膽，用武之主也。
entries.en: Dogs have guarding nature; white is the color of metal; gall is the lord of martial application.
entries.literal: Dogs have guarding nature; white is the color of metal; gall is the lord of martial application.

entries.zh: 帝王之運，王霸會於戌。
entries.en: The destiny of emperors and kings — hegemonic convergence meets at the branch xu.
entries.literal: The destiny of emperors and kings — hegemonic convergence meets at the branch xu.

entries.zh: 戌主用兵，金者晉行，火燒鐵以療疾者，言必去其類而來火與金合德，共除蟲害也。」
entries.en: Xu governs the use of arms; metal is Jin's phase; fire burning iron to treat disease means casting out the alien kind so fire and metal join virtues and together remove the worm scourge."
entries.literal: Xu governs the use of arms; metal is Jin's phase; fire burning iron to treat disease means casting out the alien kind so fire and metal join virtues and together remove the worm scourge."

entries.zh: 案中興之際，大將軍本以腹心受伊呂之任，而元帝末年，遂攻京邑，明帝諒闇，又有異謀，是以下逆上，腹心內爛也。
entries.en: At the Restoration, the grand general had been entrusted as an intimate minister in the manner of Yi Yin and Lü Wang, yet in Emperor Yuan's final years he attacked the capital, and while Emperor Ming was in mourning he again plotted rebellion. This was a case of inferiors turning against superiors, with the dynasty's own heart rotting from within.
entries.literal: Considering the restoration: the grand general had been a confidant trusted like Yi Yin or Lü Wang; yet in Emperor Yuan's last years he attacked the capital; under Emperor Ming's mourning veil there were new plots — subordinates rebelled against superiors and the belly-and-heart rotted within.

entries.zh: 及錢鳳、沈充等逆兵四合，而為王師所挫，逾月而不能濟水，北中郎劉遐及淮陵內史蘇峻率淮泗之眾以救朝廷，故其謠言首作於淮泗也。
entries.en: Qian Feng's ring around the capital failed; Su Jun and Liu Xia marched upriver from Huai-Si to lift the siege — matching where the rumor began.
entries.literal: When Qian Feng and Shen Chong's rebel hosts closed from four sides yet were broken by the imperial army, for over a month unable to ford the river, Northern Garrison Commander Liu Xia and Huailing prefect Su Jun led Huai-Si troops to rescue the court — therefore the rumor first arose in Huai-Si.

entries.zh: 朝廷卒以弱制強，罪人授首，是用白犬膽可救之效也。
entries.en: The throne survived by lesser force, heads rolled among rebels — the grotesque "cure" had served as metaphor.
entries.literal: The court ultimately used weakness to overcome strength; criminals surrendered their heads — this was the efficacy of "white dog gall could save."

entries.zh: 桓玄初改年為大亨，遐邇歡言曰「二月了」，故義謀以仲春發也。
entries.en: Huan Xuan first changed the era to Daheng; far and near gleefully said "the second month is over," therefore the loyal plot rose in mid-spring.
entries.literal: Huan Xuan first changed the era to Daheng; far and near gleefully said "the second month is over," therefore the loyal plot rose in mid-spring.

entries.zh: 玄篡立，又改年為建始，以與趙王倫同，又易為永始，永始復是王莽受封之年也。
entries.en: His usurpation recycled Sima Lun's Jianshi, then Wang Mang's Yongshi — compounding ill-omened names.
entries.literal: When Xuan usurped, he changed the era to Jianshi — the same as Prince Zhao Lun — then switched to Yongshi; Yongshi was likewise the year Wang Mang received his fief.

entries.zh: 始徙司馬道子于安成。
entries.en: Sima Daozi was packed off to Ancheng to clear the stage.
entries.literal: First Sima Daozi was banished to Ancheng.

entries.zh: 安帝遜位，出永安宮，封為平固王，琅邪王德文為石陽公，並使住尋陽城。
entries.en: An-di abdicated from Yong'an, won a hollow title at Pinggu, while Langya Wang Dewen became duke of Shiyang — both exiled to Xunyang.
entries.literal: Emperor An abdicated, left Yong'an Palace, was enfeoffed Prince of Pinggu; Langya Wang Dewen became Duke of Shiyang; both were ordered to reside in Xunyang city.

entries.zh: 識者皆以為言不從之妖僭也。
entries.en: Every augur read the clumsy reign titles as arrogance and deceitful speech.
entries.literal: Those who understood omens all deemed it demonic presumption — words again not obeyed.

entries.zh: 魏明帝太和二年五月，大旱。
entries.en: Wei's Ming-di recorded a crushing drought in Taihe 2's fifth month.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of Wei Emperor Ming's second Taihe year there was great drought.

entries.zh: 元年以来崇廣宮府之應也。
entries.en: Readers linked it to the endless new halls raised since Taihe began.
entries.literal: This answered the expansion of palaces and offices since the first year of the era.

entries.zh: 又，是春宣帝南擒孟達，置二郡，張郃西破諸葛亮，斃馬謖。
entries.en: The same season saw Sima Yi seize Meng Da, Zhang He rout Zhuge Liang, and Ma Su die for his defeat.
entries.literal: Moreover, that spring Emperor Xuan captured Meng Da in the south and set up two commanderies; Zhang He broke Zhuge Liang in the west and killed Ma Su.

entries.zh: 亢陽自大，又其應也。
entries.en: Another gloss: unchecked yang pride in the camp mirrored the weather.
entries.literal: Yang arrogantly supreme — again its omen.

entries.zh: 齊王正始元年二月，自去冬十二月至此月不雨。
entries.en: Cao Fang's Zhengshi opening saw another rainless span from deep winter into early spring.
entries.literal: In the second month of the Qi King's first Zhengshi year, from the twelfth month of last winter until this month it had not rained.

entries.zh: 去歲正月，明帝崩。
entries.en: Ming-di had fallen the previous new year.
entries.literal: The first month of last year Emperor Ming died.

entries.zh: 二月，曹爽白嗣主，轉宣帝為太傅，外示尊崇，內實欲令事先由已。
entries.en: Cao Shuang "promoted" Sima Yi to figurehead tutor while hoarding real power.
entries.literal: In the second month Cao Shuang informed the young lord, transferring Emperor Xuan to grand tutor, outwardly honoring him while in truth wishing every decision to pass through himself.

entries.zh: 是時宣帝功蓋魏朝，欲德不用之應也。
entries.en: Sima Yi's stature eclipsed the court — classic "latent virtue" portents.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan's achievements overshadowed the Wei court — an omen of desired virtue unused.

entries.zh: 武帝初，何曾薄太官御膳，自取私食，子劭又過之，而王愷又過劭。
entries.en: He Zeng snubbed the palace chefs for home cooking; He Shao and Wang Kai escalated the indulgence.
entries.literal: Early in Emperor Wu's reign He Zeng scorned the imperial kitchen and took private food; his son Shao exceeded him, and Wang Kai exceeded Shao.

entries.zh: 王愷、羊琇之儔，盛致聲色，窮珍極麗。
entries.en: Wang Kai and Yang Xiu bankrolled musicians, concubines, and luxuries without limit.
entries.literal: Wang Kai, Yang Xiu, and their ilk lavished music and women, exhausting treasures and utmost beauty.

entries.zh: 至元康中，誇恣成俗，轉相高尚，石崇之侈，遂兼王、何，而儷人主矣。
entries.en: Under Yuankang, ostentation turned into fashion until Shi Chong outspent even Wang Kai and He Zeng, shadowing the throne itself.
entries.literal: By the Yuankang years extravagance had become custom; people vied to outdo one another; Shi Chong's luxury surpassed Wang and He combined and rivaled the sovereign.

entries.zh: 崇既誅死，天下尋亦淪喪。
entries.en: Shi Chong's death presaged the empire's swift collapse.
entries.literal: After Chong was executed and killed, the realm soon also fell into ruin.

entries.zh: 僭逾之咎也。
entries.en: The historians chalked it up to rank-breaking excess.
entries.literal: This was the fault of presumption and overstepping.

entries.zh: 武帝泰始七年五月閏月旱，大雩。
entries.en: Sima Yan's Taihe 7 intercalary fifth month brought another da yu season.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu — intercalary fifth month drought; great yu.

entries.zh: 泰始八年五月，旱。
entries.en: the eighth year of Taishi's fifth month stayed rainless.
entries.literal: Fifth month of the eighth year — drought.

entries.zh: 是時帝納荀勖邪說，留賈充不復西鎮，而任愷漸疏，上下皆蔽之應也。
entries.en: Bad faith at court — Xun Xu's whispering, Jia Chong's stalled western posting, Ren Kai sidelined — mirrored blocked communication.
entries.literal: At that time the emperor accepted Xun Xu's vicious counsel, kept Jia Chong at court instead of sending him west again, and Ren Kai grew estranged — an omen of high and low both blocked.

entries.zh: 及李憙、魯芝、李胤等並在散職，近厥德不用之謂也。
entries.en: Worthy men languished in sinecures while mediocrities ran policy.
entries.literal: Moreover Li Xi, Lu Zhi, Li Yin and others all held idle posts — close to "desired virtue unused."

entries.zh: 惠帝元康七年七月，秦、雍二州大旱，疾疫，關中饑，米斛萬錢。
entries.en: Yuankang 7's seventh month left Guanzhong buying grain at ten thousand cash a hu.
entries.literal: Seventh month of Emperor Hui — great drought in Qin and Yong provinces, pestilence, Guanzhong famine, rice ten thousand cash per hu.

entries.zh: 因此氐羌反叛，雍州刺史解系敗績。
entries.en: Di and Qiang uprisings followed, crushing Inspector Jie Xi.
entries.literal: Thereupon Di and Qiang rebelled; Yongzhou inspector Jie Xi was defeated.

entries.zh: 而饑疫薦臻，戎晉並困，朝廷不能振，詔聽相賣鬻。
entries.en: Starvation and plague broke both barbarian and Chinese communities until the throne legalized selling kin to survive.
entries.literal: Famine and pestilence piled up; Rong and Jin alike were trapped; the court could not relieve them; an edict allowed mutual sale (of persons).

entries.zh: 其九月，郡國五旱。
entries.en: Five more jurisdictions reported drought that autumn.
entries.literal: That ninth month — five commanderies and states drought.

entries.zh: 永甯元年，自夏及秋，青、徐、幽、并四州旱。
entries.en: Yongning 1 scorched four provinces from midsummer into fall.
entries.literal: First Yongning year: from summer through autumn drought in Qing, Xu, You, and Bing provinces.

entries.zh: 十二月，又郡國十二旱。
entries.en: Winter brought a dozen more drought reports.
entries.literal: Twelfth month — again twelve commanderies and states drought.

entries.zh: 是年春，三王討趙王倫，六旬之中數十戰，死者十餘萬人。
entries.en: The war on Sima Lun killed over a hundred thousand in two months.
entries.literal: That spring the three kings campaigned against Prince Zhao Lun; within sixty days dozens of battles, more than a hundred thousand dead.

entries.zh: 景初初，童謠曰：「阿公阿公駕馬車，不意阿公東渡河，阿公來還當柰何！」
entries.en: Early Jingchu, a children's rhyme said: "Grandpa, grandpa, drives a horse cart; never thought grandpa would ford the river east; grandpa comes back — what then!"
entries.literal: Early Jingchu, a children's rhyme said: "Grandpa, grandpa, drives a horse cart; never thought grandpa would ford the river east; grandpa comes back — what then!"

entries.zh: 及宣帝遼東歸，至白屋，當還鎮長安。
entries.en: He should have turned west to Chang'an after the Liaodong campaign.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan returned from Liaodong to Baiwu, he was to go back and garrison Chang'an.

entries.zh: 會帝疾篤，急召之，乃乘追鋒車東渡河，終如童謠之言。
entries.en: A dying summons sent him racing east instead, matching the omen.
entries.literal: The emperor grew desperately ill and summoned him; he rode the "pursuit-blade" carriage east across the river — exactly as the rhyme said.

entries.zh: 孫休永安二年，將守質子群聚嬉戲，有異小兒忽來言曰：「三公鋤，司馬如。」
entries.en: Sun Xiu, Yong’an 2 — the hostage sons of the generals and garrison commanders had gathered to play when a strange child suddenly came and said, “The Three Dukes hoe; the Sima are like.”
entries.literal: Sun Xiu, Yong’an 2 — the hostage sons of the generals and garrison commanders had gathered to play when a strange child suddenly came and said, “The Three Dukes hoe; the Sima are like.”

entries.zh: 又曰：「我非人，熒惑星也。」
entries.en: It also said: "I am not human — I am the Planet Mars."
entries.literal: It also said: "I am not human — I am the Planet Mars."

entries.zh: 言畢上升，仰視若曳一匹練，有頃沒。
entries.en: The apparition shot upward like a comet and disappeared.
entries.literal: Finishing, it rose into the sky; looking up it seemed to trail a bolt of silk; soon it vanished.

entries.zh: 干寶曰：「後四年而蜀亡，六年而魏廢，二十一年而吳平。」
entries.en: Gan Bao said: "Four years later Shu perished, six years later Wei was cast off, twenty-one years later Wu was pacified."
entries.literal: Gan Bao said: "Four years later Shu perished, six years later Wei was cast off, twenty-one years later Wu was pacified."

entries.zh: 於是九服歸晉。
entries.en: The empire folded back under the Sima house.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Nine Domains returned to Jin.

entries.zh: 魏與吳蜀並戰國，「三公鋤，司馬如」之謂也。
entries.en: Wei fought Wu and Shu as warring states — that is what "The three dukes hoe, the Sima like" meant.
entries.literal: Wei fought Wu and Shu as warring states — that is what "The three dukes hoe, the Sima like" meant.

entries.zh: 孫皓天紀中，童謠曰：「阿童復阿童，銜刀游渡江。
entries.en: Under Sun Hao's Tianji years a rhyme said: "Atong again Atong, biting a blade he swims the river.
entries.literal: Under Sun Hao's Tianji years a rhyme said: "Atong again Atong, biting a blade he swims the river.

entries.zh: 不畏岸上獸，但畏水中龍。」
entries.en: Fear not beasts on the bank — only fear the dragon in the water."
entries.literal: Fear not beasts on the bank — only fear the dragon in the water."

entries.zh: 武帝聞之，加王浚龍驤將軍。
entries.en: Sima Yan ennobled Wang Jun as "dragon" general on cue.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu heard it, he promoted Wang Jun to Dragon-Loft general.

entries.zh: 及征吳，江西眾軍無過者，而王浚先定秣陵。
entries.en: Wang Jun's flotilla outran every rival to seize Nanjing.
entries.literal: When Wu was attacked, no western army surpassed his; Wang Jun first took Moling.

entries.zh: 武帝太康三年平吳後，江南童謠曰：「局縮肉，數橫目，中國當敗吳當復。」
entries.en: After Emperor Wu pacified Wu in Taikang 3, a children’s rhyme south of the Yangtze said, “Shriveled flesh, several horizontal eyes; the Middle Kingdom shall be defeated, Wu shall be restored.”
entries.literal: After Emperor Wu pacified Wu in Taikang 3, a children’s rhyme south of the Yangtze said, “Shriveled flesh, several horizontal eyes; the Middle Kingdom shall be defeated, Wu shall be restored.”

entries.zh: 又曰：「宮門柱，且當朽，吳當復，在三十年後。」
entries.en: It also said: "Palace gate pillars will rot; Wu returns in thirty years."
entries.literal: It also said: "Palace gate pillars will rot; Wu returns in thirty years."

entries.zh: 又曰：「雞鳴不拊翼，吳復不用力。」
entries.en: It also said: "Crows crow without folding wings — Wu needs hardly lift a finger."
entries.literal: It also said: "Crows crow without folding wings — Wu needs hardly lift a finger."

entries.zh: 于時吳人皆謂在孫氏子孫，故竊發為亂者相繼。
entries.en: Locals read the lines as Sun clan prophecy and rebelled in waves.
entries.literal: Then Wu people all thought it meant Sun heirs, so secret risings followed one another.

entries.zh: 案「橫目」者四字，自吳亡至元帝興幾四十年，元帝興于江東，皆如童謠之言焉。
entries.en: Note: "horizontal eyes" forms the graph for "four"; from Wu's fall to Yuan-di's rise in the east was nearly forty years — all matched the rhymes.
entries.literal: Note: "horizontal eyes" forms the graph for "four"; from Wu's fall to Yuan-di's rise in the east was nearly forty years — all matched the rhymes.

entries.zh: 元帝懦而少斷，「局縮肉」者，有所斥也。
entries.en: Yuan-di was timid and indecisive; "shriveled meat" rebukes that weakness.
entries.literal: Yuan-di was timid and indecisive; "shriveled meat" rebukes that weakness.

entries.zh: 惠帝永熙中，河內溫縣有人如狂，造書曰：「光光文長，大戟為牆。
entries.en: Under Emperor Hui's Yongxi years, a man in Wen county, Henan, raved like a madman and wrote: "Bright bright Wen-chang — halberds for walls.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Hui's Yongxi years, a man in Wen county, Henan, raved like a madman and wrote: "Bright bright Wen-chang — halberds for walls.

entries.zh: 毒藥雖行，戟還自傷。」
entries.en: Though poison runs its course, halberds wound themselves."
entries.literal: Though poison runs its course, halberds wound themselves."

entries.zh: 又曰：「兩火沒地，哀哉秋蘭。
entries.en: It also said: "Two fires sink into earth — alas, autumn orchid.
entries.literal: It also said: "Two fires sink into earth — alas, autumn orchid.

entries.zh: 歸形街郵，終為人歎。」
entries.en: Form returns to the roadside post — in the end men sigh over you."
entries.literal: Form returns to the roadside post — in the end men sigh over you."

entries.zh: 及楊駿居內府，以戟為衛，死時又為戟所害傷。
entries.en: Yang Jun's halberd corps foretold his own skewering.
entries.literal: When Yang Jun dwelt in the inner palace he used halberds for guards; at death he was again wounded by halberds.

entries.zh: 楊後被廢，賈后絕其膳八日而崩，葬街郵亭北，百姓哀之也。
entries.en: Consort Yang died of Jia Nanfeng's hunger strike and was dumped by the courier station.
entries.literal: Empress Yang was deposed; Empress Jia starved her eight days until she died; she was buried north of Jieyou post; the people pitied her.

entries.zh: 雨火，武帝諱，蘭，楊後字也。
entries.en: Commentators read the paired "fire" graphs as alluding to Emperor Wu's taboo name and "orchid" as Empress Yang Zhi's style name.
entries.literal: "Two fires" is Emperor Wu's taboo graph; "orchid" was Empress Yang's style name.

entries.zh: 其時又有童謠曰：「二月末，三月初，荊筆楊板行詔書，宮中大馬幾作驢。」
entries.en: Then another rhyme ran: "Late second month, early third — Jing brush and Yang tablet carry edicts; the palace's great horse nearly becomes a donkey."
entries.literal: Then another rhyme ran: "Late second month, early third — Jing brush and Yang tablet carry edicts; the palace's great horse nearly becomes a donkey."

entries.zh: 此時楊駿專權，楚王用事，故言「荊筆楊板」。
entries.en: At that time Yang Jun monopolized authority and the Prince of Chu held sway — hence "Jing brush and Yang tablet."
entries.literal: At that time Yang Jun monopolized authority and the Prince of Chu held sway — hence "Jing brush and Yang tablet."

entries.zh: 二人不誅，則君臣禮悖，故云「幾作驢」也。
entries.en: If the two were not executed, ruler-minister ritual would invert — hence "nearly a donkey."
entries.literal: If the two were not executed, ruler-minister ritual would invert — hence "nearly a donkey."

entries.zh: 元康中，京洛童謠曰：「南風起，吹白沙，遙望魯國何嵯峨，千歲髑髏生齒牙。」
entries.en: In Yuankang the capital children sang: "South wind rises, blows white sand; far off how steep the state of Lu — thousand-year skulls sprout teeth."
entries.literal: In Yuankang the capital children sang: "South wind rises, blows white sand; far off how steep the state of Lu — thousand-year skulls sprout teeth."

entries.zh: 又曰：「城東馬子莫嚨哅，此至來年纏女閤。」
entries.en: It also said: "East-city colt, don't whinny — by next year you'll tangle in women's boudoirs."
entries.literal: It also said: "East-city colt, don't whinny — by next year you'll tangle in women's boudoirs."

entries.zh: 南風，賈后字也。
entries.en: Nanfeng was the empress's sobriquet.
entries.literal: South wind" is Empress Jia's style name.

entries.zh: 白，晉行也。
entries.en: White stood for metal — Jin's element.
entries.literal: "White" is Jin's phase color.

entries.zh: 沙門，太子小名也。
entries.en: "Monkling" was Sima Zhong's pet name.
entries.literal: "Shamen" is the heir apparent's childhood name.

entries.zh: 魯，賈謐國也。
entries.en: Lu mapped onto Jia Mi's noble seat.
entries.literal: "Lu" is Jia Mi's princedom.

entries.zh: 言賈后將與謐為亂，以危太子，而趙王因釁咀嚼豪賢，以成篡奪，不得其死之應也。
entries.en: The gloss tied the verses to Jia's coup plot and Sima Lun's coming slaughter.
entries.literal: It means Empress Jia would riot with Mi to endanger the heir, while Prince Zhao would chew up great men and seize the throne — an omen of dying badly.

entries.zh: 元康中，天下商農通著大鄣日。
entries.en: Yuankang fashion made everyone don huge visors.
entries.literal: In Yuankang merchants and farmers all wore wide sun-hats.

entries.zh: 時童謠曰：「屠蘇鄣日覆兩耳，當見瞎兒作天子。」
entries.en: A rhyme said: "Tusu hat brim covers both ears — soon a blind boy will be Son of Heaven."
entries.literal: A rhyme said: "Tusu hat brim covers both ears — soon a blind boy will be Son of Heaven."

entries.zh: 及趙王倫篡位，其目實眇焉。
entries.en: Sima Lun's bad eye matched the "blind boy" line.
entries.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped, his eye was indeed blind.

entries.zh: 趙王倫既篡，洛中童謠曰：「獸從北來鼻頭汗，龍從南來登城看，水從西來河灌灌。」
entries.en: After Prince Zhao seized power, Luoyang sang: "Beasts come from the north with sweaty snouts; dragons from the south climb walls to look; water from the west makes rivers boil."
entries.literal: After Prince Zhao seized power, Luoyang sang: "Beasts come from the north with sweaty snouts; dragons from the south climb walls to look; water from the west makes rivers boil."

entries.zh: 數月而齊王、成都、河間義兵同會誅倫。
entries.en: The allied princes purged Sima Lun within the year.
entries.literal: Within months Qi, Chengdu, and Hejian righteous hosts jointly executed Lun.

entries.zh: 案成都西籓而在鄴，故曰「獸從北來。」
entries.en: Chengdu was a western fief but sat at Ye — hence "beasts from the north."
entries.literal: Chengdu was a western fief but sat at Ye — hence "beasts from the north."

entries.zh: 齊東籓而在許，故曰「龍從南來。」
entries.en: Qi was an eastern fief but camped at Xu — hence "dragons from the south."
entries.literal: Qi was an eastern fief but camped at Xu — hence "dragons from the south."

entries.zh: 河間水源而在關中，故曰「水從西來」。
entries.en: Hejian drew water from Guanzhong — hence "water from the west."
entries.literal: Hejian drew water from Guanzhong — hence "water from the west."

entries.zh: 齊留輔政，居於宮西，又有無君之心，故言「登城看」也。
entries.en: Qi stayed to assist government, dwelling west of the palace, yet nursed disloyalty — hence "climb walls to look."
entries.literal: Qi stayed to assist government, dwelling west of the palace, yet nursed disloyalty — hence "climb walls to look."

entries.zh: 武帝太康六年，南陽獻兩足猛獸，此毛蟲之孽也。
entries.en: In Taikang 6 under Emperor Wu, Nanyang offered a two-legged beast, classed here as a hairy-creature calamity.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu, Taikang 6 — Nanyang presented a two-legged fierce beast; this was a calamity from hairy creatures.

entries.zh: 識者為其文曰：「武形有虧，金獸失儀，聖主應天，期異何為！」
entries.en: Readers glossed its pattern: "Martial form is flawed; metal beast loses propriety; sage lord answers Heaven — why this strangeness?"
entries.literal: Readers glossed its pattern: "Martial form is flawed; metal beast loses propriety; sage lord answers Heaven — why this strangeness?"

entries.zh: 言兆亂也。
entries.en: They read it as rebellion brewing.
entries.literal: It spoke of impending chaos.

entries.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「足少者，下不勝任也。」
entries.en: Jing Fang's Treatise on the Changes says: "Too few feet — those below cannot bear the burden."
entries.literal: Jing Fang's Treatise on the Changes says: "Too few feet — those below cannot bear the burden."

entries.zh: 干寶以為：「獸者陰精，居於陽，金獸也。
entries.en: Gan Bao held: "Beasts are yin essences dwelling in yang — metal beasts.
entries.literal: Gan Bao held: "Beasts are yin essences dwelling in yang — metal beasts.

entries.zh: 南陽，火名也。
entries.en: Nanyang is a fire name.
entries.literal: Nanyang is a fire name.

entries.zh: 金精入火而失其形，王室亂之妖也。」
entries.en: Metal essence entering fire and losing shape is an omen of royal-house disorder."
entries.literal: Metal essence entering fire and losing shape is an omen of royal-house disorder."

entries.zh: 六，水數，言水數既極，火慝得作，而金受其敗也。
entries.en: Numerology linked six to water's end and fire's revenge on metal.
entries.literal: Six" is water's number — saying water's span is exhausted lets fire malice act while metal suffers defeat.

entries.zh: 至元康九年，始殺太子，距此十四年。
entries.en: Fourteen years later the heir died.
entries.literal: By Yuankang 9 they first killed the crown prince — fourteen years from this omen.

entries.zh: 二七十四，火始終相乘之數也。
entries.en: The arithmetic omen paired twos and sevens with fire phases.
entries.literal: Two times seven is fourteen — fire's beginning and end multiplied.

entries.zh: 自帝受命，至湣懷之廢，凡三十五年焉。
entries.en: Thirty-five years spanned Sima Yan to the ruined princes.
entries.literal: From the emperor's mandate to Min and Huai's deposition was thirty-five years.

entries.zh: 武帝太康九年，幽州有犬，鼻行地三百餘步。
entries.en: In Taikang 9 under Emperor Wu, a Youzhou dog was said to nose-walk more than three hundred paces.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu, Taikang 9 — in Youzhou there was a dog that walked more than three hundred paces with its nose to the ground.

entries.zh: 天戒若曰，是時帝不思和嶠之言，卒立惠帝，以致衰亂，是言不從之罰也。
entries.en: The freak dog echoed Sima Yan's refusal to change the heir.
entries.literal: Heaven's warning: then the emperor ignored He Jiao's advice, finally enthroned Emperor Hui, inviting decay — punishment for heedless words.

entries.zh: 武帝太康五年五月丁巳，隕石于溫及河陽各二。
entries.en: On dingsi in the fifth month of Taikang 5, two meteorites fell at Wen and two at Heyang.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu, Taikang 5, fifth month, dingsi — two meteorites each fell at Wen and Heyang.

entries.zh: 六年正月，隕石于溫，三。
entries.en: A second fall hit Wen commandery.
entries.literal: Sixth year first month — meteorites at Wen, three.

entries.zh: 惠帝元康中，吳郡婁縣人家聞地中有犬子聲，掘之，得雌雄各一。
entries.en: Subterranean barking yielded two pups in Wu commandery.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui Yuankang years a Lou county household heard puppy sounds underground; digging, they got a male and female.

entries.zh: 還置窟中，覆以磨石，經宿失所在。
entries.en: The pups vanished beneath the stone cover.
entries.literal: They returned them to the pit, covered it with millstones; by morning they were gone.

entries.zh: 天戒若曰，帝既衰弱，籓王相譖，故有犬禍。
entries.en: The omen matched frail sovereignty and princely intrigue.
entries.literal: Heaven warns: the emperor is weak; princes slander one another — hence dog disasters.

entries.zh: 魏明帝青龍三年正月乙亥，隕石于壽光。
entries.en: On yihai in the first month of Qinglong 3 under Wei Emperor Ming, a meteorite fell at Shouguang.
entries.literal: Wei Emperor Ming, Qinglong 3, first month, yihai — a meteorite fell at Shouguang.

entries.zh: 案《左氏傳》「隕石，星也」，劉歆說曰：「庶眾惟星隕于宋者，象宋襄公將得諸侯而不終也。」
entries.en: The Zuo Tradition says "falling stone is a star"; Liu Xin explained: "When many stars fell on Song it signified Duke Xiang gaining the hegemons yet not finishing."
entries.literal: The Zuo Tradition says "falling stone is a star"; Liu Xin explained: "When many stars fell on Song it signified Duke Xiang gaining the hegemons yet not finishing."

entries.zh: 秦始皇時有隕石，班固以為：「石，陰類也。
entries.en: Qin Shihuang had meteorites; Ban Gu thought: "Stone is yin class.
entries.literal: Qin Shihuang had meteorites; Ban Gu thought: "Stone is yin class.

entries.zh: 又白祥，臣將危君。」
entries.en: Also white omen — ministers will endanger the ruler."
entries.literal: Also white omen — ministers will endanger the ruler."

entries.zh: 是後宣帝得政云。
entries.en: Sima Yi followed the omen.
entries.literal: Thereafter Emperor Xuan seized power.

entries.zh: 吳孫亮五鳳二年五月，陽羨縣離裏山大石自立。
entries.en: In the fifth month of Wufeng 2 under Wu’s Sun Liang, a great stone at Lili Mountain stood upright on its own.
entries.literal: Wu Sun Liang, Wufeng 2, fifth month — a great stone at Lili Mountain in Yangxian county stood upright by itself.

entries.zh: 案京房《易傳》曰「庶士為天子之祥也」，其說曰：「石立於山同姓，平地異姓。」
entries.en: Jing Fang's Treatise says "commoners becoming Son of Heaven"; his gloss: "Stone on a mountain — same surname; on flat ground — different surname."
entries.literal: Jing Fang's Treatise says "commoners becoming Son of Heaven"; his gloss: "Stone on a mountain — same surname; on flat ground — different surname."

entries.zh: 干寶以為「孫皓承廢故之家得位，其應也。」
entries.en: Gan Bao thought it meant, "Sun Hao inherited a deposed old house and gained the throne; this was its response."
entries.literal: Gan Bao thought it meant, "Sun Hao inherited a deposed old house and gained the throne; this was its response."

entries.zh: 或曰孫休見立之祥也。
entries.en: Another reading favored Sun Xiu.
entries.literal: Others say it signified Sun Xiu's enthronement.

entries.zh: 武帝太康十年，洛陽宮西宜秋裏石生地中，始高三尺，如香鈩形，後如傴人，槃薄不可掘。
entries.en: In Taikang 10 under Emperor Wu, a stone sprouted in Yiqiu ward west of the Luoyang palace, changing from an incense-burner shape into something like a hunched man.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu, Taikang 10 — west of the Luoyang palace, in Yiqiu ward, a stone grew out of the ground; at first it was three chi high and shaped like an incense burner, later like a bent-over man, spreading thickly and impossible to dig out.

entries.zh: 案劉向說，此白眚也。
entries.en: Liu Xiang filed it under white shang.
entries.literal: Liu Xiang's doctrine calls this white ill-omen.

entries.zh: 明年宮車晏駕，王室始騷，卒以亂亡。
entries.en: Sima Yan died; turmoil followed.
entries.literal: Next year the imperial carriage halted; the royal house first stirred and ended in chaos.

entries.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「石立如人，庶士為天下雄。」
entries.en: Jing Fang says: "Stone stands like a man — commoners become heroes under heaven."
entries.literal: Jing Fang says: "Stone stands like a man — commoners become heroes under heaven."

entries.zh: 此近之矣。
entries.en: The annalist judged it apt.
entries.literal: This is close.

entries.zh: 武帝泰始八年五月，蜀地雨白毛，此白祥也。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu, white hair fell like rain in Shu, a white omen.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu, Taishi 8, fifth month — white hair rained down in Shu; this was a white omen.

entries.zh: 時益州刺史皇甫晏伐汶山胡，從事何旅固諫，不從，牙門張弘等困眾之怨，誣晏謀逆，害之。
entries.en: Huangfu Yan's western war brought mutiny and death.
entries.literal: Then Inspector Huangfu Yan campaigned against Wenshan Hu; aide He Lu counseled against it; ignored; gate officer Zhang Hong exploited troop hatred, slandered Yan as rebel, murdered him.

entries.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「前樂後憂，厥妖天雨羽。」
entries.en: Jing Fang says: "Joy before grief — its portent heaven rains feathers."
entries.literal: Jing Fang says: "Joy before grief — its portent heaven rains feathers."

entries.zh: 又曰：「邪人進，賢人逃，天雨毛。」
entries.en: Also: "Villains advance, worthies flee — heaven rains fur."
entries.literal: Also: "Villains advance, worthies flee — heaven rains fur."

entries.zh: 其《易妖》曰：「天雨毛羽，貴人出走。」
entries.en: His Omen Treatise says: "Heaven rains feather-fur — nobles flee."
entries.literal: His Omen Treatise says: "Heaven rains feather-fur — nobles flee."

entries.zh: 三占皆應。
entries.en: Every reading converged.
entries.literal: All three divinations fit.

entries.zh: 惠帝元康五年十二月，有石生於宜年裏。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of Yuankang 5 under Emperor Hui, a stone grew in Yinian ward.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui, Yuankang 5, twelfth month — a stone grew in Yinian ward.

entries.zh: 永康元年，襄陽郡上言，得鳴石，撞之，聲聞七八里。
entries.en: In Yongkang 1, Xiangyang Commandery reported finding ringing stones: when struck, their sound could be heard seven or eight li away.
entries.literal: Yongkang 1 Xiangyang reported singing stones — struck, heard seven or eight li.

entries.zh: 太安元年，丹陽湖熟縣夏架湖有大石，浮二百步而登岸，民驚噪相告曰：「石來。」
entries.en: Tai'an 1 a great stone in Danyang Hushu county's Xiajia Lake floated two hundred paces then beached; folk cried "The stone comes."
entries.literal: Tai'an 1 a great stone in Danyang Hushu county's Xiajia Lake floated two hundred paces then beached; folk cried "The stone comes."

entries.zh: 干寶曰：「尋有石冰入建鄴。」
entries.en: Gan Bao said: "Soon Shi Bing entered Jianye."
entries.literal: Gan Bao said: "Soon Shi Bing entered Jianye."

entries.zh: 惠帝永寧元年，齊王冏舉義軍。
entries.en: In Yongning 1 under Emperor Hui, Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, raised his righteous army.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui, Yongning 1 — Prince Jiong of Qi raised a righteous army.

entries.zh: 軍中有小兒，出於襄城繁昌縣，年八歲，發體悉白，頗能卜，于《洪范》，白祥也。
entries.en: An albino child divined in Jiong's host.
entries.literal: Among the troops a boy from Xiangcheng Fanchang, age eight, all white-haired, could divine — per Hong Fan, white omen.

entries.zh: 惠帝元康八年五月，郊禖壇石中破為二，此木沴金也。
entries.en: In the fifth month of Yuankang 8 under Emperor Hui, the fertility altar stone split in two, read as wood harming metal.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui, Yuankang 8, fifth month — the stone at the suburban fertility altar split in two; this was wood injuring metal.

entries.zh: 郊禖壇者，求子之神位，無故自毀，太子將危之象也。
entries.en: Broken altar spelled doom for the crown prince.
entries.literal: The suburban Subs altar is the god-seat for seeking sons; it broke without cause — image of the heir in peril.

entries.zh: 明年湣懷廢死。
entries.en: Sima Yu and Yu fell the next year.
entries.literal: Next year Min and Huai were deposed and died.

entries.zh: 惠帝元康二年二月，巴西郡界草皆生華，結子如麥，可食。
entries.en: In the second month of Yuankang 2 under Emperor Hui, Baxi grasses flowered and set edible wheat-like seed.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui, Yuankang 2, second month — grasses throughout Baxi commandery all flowered and bore seeds like wheat, which could be eaten.

entries.zh: 時帝初即位，楚王瑋矯詔誅汝南王亮及太保衛瓘，帝不能察。
entries.en: Sima Wei's coup caught the new throne blind.
entries.literal: The emperor had just mounted the throne; Prince Chu Wei forged edicts killing Prince Runan Liang and grand tutor Wei Guan — the emperor could not investigate.

entries.zh: 今非時草結實，此恆燠寬舒之罰。
entries.en: Untimely grain on weeds bespoke thermal slackness.
entries.literal: Now grass fruits out of season — punishment of constant heat and lax ease.

entries.zh: 惠帝元康二年春，巴西郡界竹生花，紫色，結實如麥，外皮青，中赤白，味甘。
entries.en: In spring of Yuankang 2 under Emperor Hui, Baxi bamboo flowered purple and fruited like sweet wheat.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui, Yuankang 2, spring — bamboo on the borders of Baxi commandery flowered purple and bore fruit like wheat, with green outer skin, red-white inside, and a sweet taste.

entries.zh: 元康九年六月庚子，有桑生東宮西廂，日長尺餘，甲辰枯死。
entries.en: On gengzi in the sixth month of Yuankang 9, a mulberry shot up in the Eastern Palace’s west wing, grew more than a chi a day, and died on jiachen.
entries.literal: Yuankang 9, sixth month, gengzi — a mulberry grew in the western wing of the Eastern Palace, lengthening more than a chi each day; on jiachen it withered and died.

entries.zh: 此與殷太戊同妖，太子不能悟，故至廢戮也。
entries.en: Like Shang precedent, the crown prince ignored the sign.
entries.literal: This matches Yin emperor Taiwu's portent; the heir could not understand — hence deposition and slaughter.

entries.zh: 班固稱「野木生朝而暴長，小人將暴居大臣之位，危國亡家之象，朝將為墟也。」
entries.en: Ban Gu said: "Wild wood in court growing wildly means petty men will usurp ministers' seats — image of state ruin; the court will be waste."
entries.literal: Ban Gu said: "Wild wood in court growing wildly means petty men will usurp ministers' seats — image of state ruin; the court will be waste."

entries.zh: 是後孫秀、張林用事，遂至大亂。
entries.en: Jia Nanfeng's minions fulfilled it.
entries.literal: Thereafter Sun Xiu and Zhang Lin held power until great chaos.

entries.zh: 永康元年四月，立皇孫臧為皇太孫。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongkang, Sima Zang became heir-apparent.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongkang, fourth month — imperial grandson Zang was made heir.

entries.zh: 五月甲子，就東宮，桑又生於西廂。
entries.en: The mulberry returned when Zang entered.
entries.literal: Fifth month jiazi — entering the Eastern Palace mulberry again grew in the west wing.

entries.zh: 明年，趙王倫篡位，鴆殺臧，此與湣懷同妖也。
entries.en: Lun's coup killed Zang like earlier heirs.
entries.literal: Next year Prince Zhao Lun usurped and poisoned Zang — same portent as Min and Huai.

entries.zh: 是月，壯武國有桑化為柏，而張華遇害。
entries.en: Mulberry-cypress shift coincided with Zhang Hua's death.
entries.literal: That month Zhuangwu princedom saw mulberry turn to cypress while Zhang Hua was murdered.

entries.zh: 壯武，華之封邑也。
entries.en: The omen struck his domain.
entries.literal: Zhuangwu was Hua's fief.

entries.zh: 景初元年，又有燕生巨鷇於衛國李蓋家，形若鷹，吻似燕，此羽蟲之孽，又赤眚也。
entries.en: A second freak hatchling augured Cao Wei's end.
entries.literal: Jingchu 1 — another swallow laid a giant chick at Li Gai's home in Wey; shaped like an eagle, beak like a swallow — feathered calamity, also red ill-omen.

entries.zh: 高堂隆曰：「此魏室之大異，宜防鷹揚之臣于蕭牆之內。」
entries.en: Gao Tang Long said: "This is Wei's great prodigy — guard against hawk-like ministers inside the screen wall."
entries.literal: Gao Tang Long said: "This is Wei's great prodigy — guard against hawk-like ministers inside the screen wall."

entries.zh: 其後宣帝起誅曹爽，遂有魏室。
entries.en: Sima Yi purged Shuang and seized power.
entries.literal: Thereafter Emperor Xuan rose and executed Cao Shuang, taking Wei.

entries.zh: 武帝泰始四年八月，有翟雉飛上閶闔門。
entries.en: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu, a long-tailed pheasant perched on Changhe Gate.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu, Taishi 4, eighth month — a long-tailed pheasant flew up onto Changhe Gate.

entries.zh: 天戒若曰，閶闔門非雉所止，猶殷宗雉登鼎耳之戒也。
entries.en: The gate omen recalled Shang dynasty precedent.
entries.literal: Heaven warns: Changhe Gate is no place for pheasants — like Shang's pheasant on the cauldron ear.

entries.zh: 武帝太康五年四月壬子，魯國池水變赤如血。
entries.en: In Emperor Wu's Taikang 5.4, on renzi, Lu's ponds turned blood-red.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of Taikang 5 under Emperor Wu, on renzi day, the pond water in Lu Principality turned red like blood.

entries.zh: 七年十月，河陰有赤雪二頃。
entries.en: Crimson snow covered Heyin fields.
entries.literal: Seventh year tenth month — Heyin had two qing of red snow.

entries.zh: 此赤祥也。
entries.en: The crimson fall matched chi portents.
entries.literal: This was red omen.

entries.zh: 是後四載而帝崩，王室遂亂。
entries.en: Sima Yan perished; turmoil followed.
entries.literal: Four years later the emperor died; the royal house then fell into chaos.

entries.zh: 惠帝永康元年，趙王倫既篡，京師得異鳥，莫能名。
entries.en: In Yongkang 1 under Emperor Hui, after Sima Lun’s usurpation, the capital captured an unnamed strange bird.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui, Yongkang 1 — after Prince Lun of Zhao had usurped, a strange bird was obtained in the capital, and no one could name it.

entries.zh: 倫使人持出，周旋城邑市以問人。
entries.en: Paraded the bird for identification.
entries.literal: Lun had it carried through city markets asking everyone.

entries.zh: 積日，宮西有小兒見之，遂自言曰：「服留鳥翳。」
entries.en: After days a western-slum boy saw it and said: "It is the 'stay-cloak' bird."
entries.literal: After days a western-slum boy saw it and said: "It is the 'stay-cloak' bird."

entries.zh: 持者即還白倫，倫使更求，又見之，乃將入宮，密籠鳥，並閉小兒戶中，明日視之，悉不見。
entries.en: Lun imprisoned bird and prophet — both disappeared.
entries.literal: The bearer reported to Lun; Lun sent to find him again, caged the bird with the boy locked in; next day both vanished.

entries.zh: 此羽蟲之孽。
entries.en: Another winged portent.
entries.literal: This was feathered calamity.

entries.zh: 時趙王倫有目瘤之疾，言服留者，謂倫留將服其罪也。
entries.en: The pun foretold Lun's execution.
entries.literal: Then Prince Zhao Lun had an eye tumor; "stay-cloak" meant Lun would soon suffer punishment.

entries.zh: 尋而倫誅。
entries.en: Sima Lun fell quickly.
entries.literal: Soon Lun was executed.

entries.zh: 惠帝元康五年三月，呂縣有流血，東西百餘步，此赤祥也。
entries.en: In the third month of Yuankang 5 under Emperor Hui, blood flowed across more than a hundred paces of Lü county, a red omen.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui, Yuankang 5, third month — there was flowing blood in Lü county, stretching more than a hundred paces east to west; this was a red omen.

entries.zh: 至元康末，窮凶極亂，僵屍流血之應也。
entries.en: The War of the Eight Princes fulfilled the sign.
entries.literal: By late Yuankang utmost villainy and chaos — answer of corpses and flowing blood.

entries.zh: 干寶以為「後八載而封雲亂徐州，殺傷數萬人」，是其應也。
entries.en: Gan Bao thought: "Eight years later Feng Yun ravaged Xuzhou, killing tens of thousands" — its answer.
entries.literal: Gan Bao thought: "Eight years later Feng Yun ravaged Xuzhou, killing tens of thousands" — its answer.

entries.zh: 趙王倫篡位，有鶉入太極殿，雉集東堂。
entries.en: Game birds invaded the throne hall.
entries.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped, quail entered Taiji Hall, pheasants gathered east hall.

entries.zh: 天戒若曰，太極東堂皆朝享聽政之所，而鶉雉同日集之者，趙王倫不當居此位也。
entries.en: Twin fowl barred his legitimacy.
entries.literal: Heaven warns: Taiji and east hall are where court meets — quail and pheasant the same day means Lun must not occupy that seat.

entries.zh: 《詩》云：「鵲之強強，鶉之奔奔，人之無良，我以為君。」
entries.en: The Book of Songs says: "Magpie strong-strong, quail darting — the man lacks goodness — I make him lord."
entries.literal: The Book of Songs says: "Magpie strong-strong, quail darting — the man lacks goodness — I make him lord."

entries.zh: 其此之謂乎！
entries.en: Editors applied the ode to Lun.
entries.literal: Did it not mean this?

entries.zh: 尋而倫誅。
entries.en: He died as foretold.
entries.literal: Soon Lun was executed.

entries.zh: 永康元年三月，尉氏雨血。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongkang, Blood showered on Weishi.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongkang, third month — Weishi rained blood.

entries.zh: 夫政刑舒緩，則有常燠赤祥之妖。
entries.en: Lax justice invites thermal and sanguinary signs.
entries.literal: When government and punishments are slack there are omens of constant heat and red freaks.

entries.zh: 此歲正月，送湣懷太子，幽于許宮。
entries.en: Sima Yu was caged in first month.
entries.literal: That year's first month they escorted Crown Prince Min-Huai, imprisoned him at Xu palace.

entries.zh: 天戒若曰，不宜緩恣奸人，將使太子冤死。
entries.en: Heaven rebuked Jia Nanfeng's plot against the heir.
entries.literal: Heaven warns: do not indulgently trust villains — it will make the heir die wronged.

entries.zh: 惠帝愚眊不寤，是月湣懷遂斃。
entries.en: Hui let his nephew be killed.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui was dull and did not wake; that month Min-Huai was murdered.

entries.zh: 於是王室成釁，禍流天下。
entries.en: Dynastic shame ignited civil war.
entries.literal: Thereupon the royal house bore scandal; disaster spread under heaven.

entries.zh: 淖齒殺齊湣王日，天雨血沾衣。
entries.en: Spring and Autumn parallel: blood rain on regicide.
entries.literal: The day Zhuo Chi killed King Min of Qi heaven rained blood staining clothes.

entries.zh: 天以告也，此之謂乎？
entries.en: The classic blood-rain trope applied.
entries.literal: Heaven announces — does it not mean this?

entries.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「歸獄不解，茲謂追非，厥咎天雨血。
entries.en: Jing Fang says: "When guilt is not cleared it is called pursuing wrong — its fault heaven rains blood.
entries.literal: Jing Fang says: "When guilt is not cleared it is called pursuing wrong — its fault heaven rains blood.

entries.zh: 茲謂不親，下有噁心，不出三年，無其宗。」
entries.en: This is called unfilial — below is malice — within three years the lineage ends."
entries.literal: This is called unfilial — below is malice — within three years the lineage ends."

entries.zh: 又曰：「佞人祿，功臣戮，天雨血也。」
entries.en: Also: "When sycophants have salary and merit ministers are slaughtered — heaven rains blood."
entries.literal: Also: "When sycophants have salary and merit ministers are slaughtered — heaven rains blood."

entries.zh: 言之不從，是謂不乂
entries.en: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.
entries.literal: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.

entries.zh: 文帝為晉王，患前代律令本注煩雜，陳群、劉邵雖經改革，而科網本密，又叔孫、郭、馬、杜諸儒章句，但取鄭氏，又為偏黨，未可承用。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen was King of Jin, he was troubled that the statutes and ordinances, root texts and notes of earlier generations were complicated and miscellaneous. Although Chen Qun and Liu Shao had revised them, the statutory net was basically dense, and the chapter-and-verse commentaries of Shusun, Guo, Ma, Du, and other classicists took only Zheng Xuan's school and were also partial and partisan, so they could not be adopted.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen was King of Jin, he was troubled that the statutes and ordinances, root texts and notes of earlier generations were complicated and miscellaneous. Although Chen Qun and Liu Shao had revised them, the statutory net was basically dense, and the chapter-and-verse commentaries of Shusun, Guo, Ma, Du, and other classicists took only Zheng Xuan's school and were also partial and partisan, so they could not be adopted.

entries.zh: 於是令賈充定法律，令與太傅鄭沖、司徒荀顗、中書監荀勖、中軍將軍羊祜、中護軍王業、廷尉杜友、守河南尹杜預、散騎侍郎裴楷、潁川太守周雄、齊相郭頎、騎都尉成公綏、尚書郎柳軌及吏部令史榮邵等十四人典其事，就漢九章增十一篇，仍其族類，正其體號，改舊律為《刑名》、《法例》，辨《囚律》為《告劾》、《系訊》、《斷獄》，分《盜律》為《請賕》、《詐偽》、《水火》、《毀亡》，因事類為《衛宮》、《違制》，撰《周官》為《諸侯律》，合二十篇，六百二十條，二萬七千六百五十七言。
entries.en: He therefore ordered Jia Chong to settle the laws and statutes, and ordered him together with Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Minister over the Masses Xun Yi, Palace Writer Director Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, Central Protector of the Army Wang Ye, Commandant of Justice Du You, Acting Governor of Henan Du Yu, Cavalier Attendant Pei Kai, Yingchuan Grand Administrator Zhou Xiong, Qi Chancellor Guo Qi, Cavalier Commandant Chenggong Sui, Secretariat Gentleman Liu Gui, Personnel Bureau Clerk Rong Shao, and the others, fourteen men in all, to manage the affair. Based on the Han Nine Chapters, they added eleven chapters, followed their categories, corrected their structures and titles, changed the old code into Penal Names and Legal Precedents, divided the Prisoners Code into Accusations and Impeachments, Detentions and Interrogations, and Deciding Prison Cases, divided the Robbery Code into Requests and Bribes, Fraud and Forgery, Water and Fire, and Destruction and Loss, made Palace Guards and Violations of Regulations according to the categories of affairs, and compiled the Zhou Offices into the Feudal Lords Code. Together these made twenty chapters, six hundred and twenty articles, and twenty-seven thousand six hundred fifty-seven words.
entries.literal: He therefore ordered Jia Chong to settle the laws and statutes, and ordered him together with Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Minister over the Masses Xun Yi, Palace Writer Director Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, Central Protector of the Army Wang Ye, Commandant of Justice Du You, Acting Governor of Henan Du Yu, Cavalier Attendant Pei Kai, Yingchuan Grand Administrator Zhou Xiong, Qi Chancellor Guo Qi, Cavalier Commandant Chenggong Sui, Secretariat Gentleman Liu Gui, Personnel Bureau Clerk Rong Shao, and the others, fourteen men in all, to manage the affair. Based on the Han Nine Chapters, they added eleven chapters, followed their categories, corrected their structures and titles, changed the old code into Penal Names and Legal Precedents, divided the Prisoners Code into Accusations and Impeachments, Detentions and Interrogations, and Deciding Prison Cases, divided the Robbery Code into Requests and Bribes, Fraud and Forgery, Water and Fire, and Destruction and Loss, made Palace Guards and Violations of Regulations according to the categories of affairs, and compiled the Zhou Offices into the Feudal Lords Code. Together these made twenty chapters, six hundred and twenty articles, and twenty-seven thousand six hundred fifty-seven words.

entries.zh: 蠲其苛穢，存其清約，事從中典，歸於益時。
entries.en: Editors stripped cruft, kept crisp rules, and tuned everything to contemporary needs.
entries.literal: They cut filth and kept essentials—matters follow central canons and aim to benefit the age.

entries.zh: 其餘未宜除者，若軍事、田農、酤酒，未得皆從人心，權設其法，太平當除，故不入律，悉以為令。
entries.en: Military, agrarian, and liquor rules stayed provisional edicts until a future peaceful reign could prune them.
entries.literal: Matters not yet fit for repeal—such as military affairs, farming, or liquor monopolies—could not all follow popular wishes; they provisionally set laws to be repealed in Great Peace, therefore not embedded in statutes but collected as edicts.

entries.zh: 施行制度，以此設教，違令有罪則入律。
entries.en: Administrative handbooks taught policy; breaching those edicts triggered codified penalties.
entries.literal: Institutions implementing policy used these for instruction—violating edicts became statutory crime.

entries.zh: 其常事品式章程，各還其府，為故事。
entries.en: Everyday paperwork stayed departmental precedent rather than criminal code.
entries.literal: Routine administrative forms and memorial templates returned to their bureaus as precedent dossiers.

entries.zh: 減梟斬族誅從坐之條，除謀反適養母出女嫁皆不復還坐父母棄市，省禁固相告之條，去捕亡、亡沒為官奴婢之制。
entries.en: Penal reform softened exposure executions, limited clan guilt for treason and adoption cases, scrapped denunciation prisons, and ended fugitive enslavement rules.
entries.literal: They reduced provisions on displaying heads, waist-cutting, clan execution, and accessory sitting; removed returning parents to marketplace execution for treason, adopted heirs, divorced daughters; dropped mutual denunciation imprisonment; abolished arrest fugitive statutes and enslavement of fugitives’ kin.

entries.zh: 輕過誤老少女人當罰金杖罰者，皆令半之。
entries.en: Fines and beatings for minors, seniors, women, and petty slips were automatically cut in half.
entries.literal: Light offenses, mistakes, old age, youth, or women liable for cash or cane had sentences halved.

entries.zh: 重奸伯叔母之令，棄市。
entries.en: Incest with uncles or aunts now meant immediate public execution.
entries.literal: They strengthened the statute on violating paternal uncles and aunts—marketplace execution.

entries.zh: 淫寡女，三歲刑。
entries.en: Seducing bereaved women earned three years penal labor.
entries.literal: Fornicating with widows brought three years labor.

entries.zh: 崇嫁娶之要，一以下娉為正，不理私約。
entries.en: Marriage validity rested solely on documented bride-price, not secret promises.
entries.literal: They elevated marriage essentials—only formal betrothal gifts counted; private pledges were ignored.

entries.zh: 峻禮教之防，准五服以制罪也。
entries.en: Law enforced mourning hierarchies when calibrating criminal guilt.
entries.literal: They fortified ritual barriers and matched punishments to the five mourning grades.

entries.zh: 凡律令合二千九百二十六條，十二萬六千三百言，六十卷，故事三十卷。
entries.en: The codex stacked 2,926 provisions across sixty volumes plus thirty precedent fascicles.
entries.literal: Statutes and edicts together numbered 2,926 articles, 126,300 characters, sixty scrolls; precedent dossiers thirty scrolls.

entries.zh: 泰始三年，事畢，表上。
entries.en: the third year of Taishi (267 CE) saw the finished code presented to the throne.
entries.literal: In Taishi third year the work finished and they memorialized it upward.

entries.zh: 武帝詔曰：「昔蕭何以定律令受封，叔孫通制儀為奉常，賜金五百斤，弟子百人皆為郎。
entries.en: Emperor Wu issued an edict, saying, "Formerly Xiao He received an enfeoffment for settling statutes and ordinances, and Shusun Tong made ritual regulations, became Chamberlain for Ceremonials, was granted five hundred jin of gold, and one hundred of his disciples all became gentlemen.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu issued an edict, saying, "Formerly Xiao He received an enfeoffment for settling statutes and ordinances, and Shusun Tong made ritual regulations, became Chamberlain for Ceremonials, was granted five hundred jin of gold, and one hundred of his disciples all became gentlemen.

entries.zh: 夫立功立事，古今之所重，宜加祿賞，其詳考差敘。
entries.en: Reward the compilers commensurate with their service.
entries.literal: Establishing merit has always mattered—add salaries and rewards; investigate ranks carefully.

entries.zh: 輒如詔簡異弟子百人，隨才品用，賞帛萬餘匹。」
entries.en: At once, according to the edict, one hundred exceptional disciples were selected, employed according to their talents and grades, and rewarded with more than ten thousand bolts of silk."
entries.literal: At once, according to the edict, one hundred exceptional disciples were selected, employed according to their talents and grades, and rewarded with more than ten thousand bolts of silk."

entries.zh: 武帝親自臨講，使裴楷執讀。
entries.en: Wudi presided while Pei Kai recited the new code.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu personally attended the lecture and had Pei Kai read aloud.

entries.zh: 四年正月，大赦天下，乃班新律。
entries.en: In the first month of year four he amnestied the realm and published the Jin code.
entries.literal: Fourth year, first month, he proclaimed a general amnesty and promulgated the new statutes.

entries.zh: 是時侍中盧珽、中書侍郎張華又表：「抄《新律》諸死罪條目，懸之亭傳，以示兆庶。」
entries.en: At this time Attendant Lu Ting and Palace Writer Attendant Gentleman Zhang Hua again memorialized: "Copy out the articles for the capital crimes in the New Code and hang them in stations and relay posts to show them to the common people."
entries.literal: At this time Attendant Lu Ting and Palace Writer Attendant Gentleman Zhang Hua again memorialized: "Copy out the articles for the capital crimes in the New Code and hang them in stations and relay posts to show them to the common people."

entries.zh: 有詔從之。
entries.en: The throne agreed.
entries.literal: An edict approved.

entries.zh: 至惠帝之世，政出群下，每有疑獄，各立私情，刑法不定，獄訟繁滋。
entries.en: Hui's court factionalized justice and docket chaos exploded.
entries.literal: By Emperor Hui's reign power scattered below; each doubtful case nursed private bias; punishments wavered; suits multiplied.

entries.zh: 尚書裴頠表陳之曰：
entries.en: Pei Wei then submitted:
entries.literal: Minister Pei Wei memorialized saying:

entries.zh: 去元康四年，大風之後，廟闕屋瓦有數枚傾落，免太常荀寓。
entries.en: Yuankang 4 windstorm tiles toppled; Xun Yu took the fall.
entries.literal: In fourth year of Yuankang, after great wind, several temple eaves-tiles fell—Minister of Ceremonies Xun Yu was dismissed.

entries.zh: 于時以嚴詔所譴，莫敢據正。
entries.en: Harsh edicts silenced dissent.
entries.literal: At the time harsh edict blame—none dared argue rectitude.

entries.zh: 然內外之意，僉謂事輕責重，有違于常。
entries.en: Everyone felt penalties disproportionate.
entries.literal: Court consensus judged fault light yet punishment heavy—contrary to precedent.

entries.zh: 會五年二月有大風，主者懲懼前事。
entries.en: Month-two winds next year made clerks paranoid.
entries.literal: When fifth year second month brought another gale, officials dreaded repeating prior ordeal.

entries.zh: 臣新拜尚書始三日，本曹尚書有疾，權令兼出，按行蘭台。
entries.en: Pei Wei briefly supervised inspections.
entries.literal: Your servant had just become Minister three days; chief minister fell ill so your servant temporarily inspected Orchid Terrace.

entries.zh: 主者乃瞻望阿棟之間，求索瓦之不正者，得棟上瓦小邪十五處。
entries.en: Teams counted fifteen slightly misaligned ridge tiles.
entries.literal: Inspectors stared between beams hunting crooked tiles—finding fifteen slightly skewed ridge tiles.

entries.zh: 或是始瓦時邪，蓋不足言，風起倉卒，台官更往，太常按行，不及得周，文書未至之頃，便競相禁止。
entries.en: Minor skew blamed on builders yet panic triggered blanket bans mid-inspection.
entries.literal: Perhaps masons laid them crooked originally—hardly worth mentioning—yet sudden winds sent Terrace officers and Minister of Ceremonies scrambling incomplete inspections while paperwork lagged—everyone raced to embargo repairs.

entries.zh: 臣以權兼暫出，出還便罷，不復得窮其事。
entries.en: Acting supervisors lost mandate once rotated.
entries.literal: Your servant held temporary duty—returning ended authority—could not pursue detail.

entries.zh: 而本曹據執，卻問無已。
entries.en: Permanent staff kept interrogating Ceremonies.
entries.literal: Yet home bureau clung stubbornly questioning endlessly.

entries.zh: 臣時具加解遣，而主者畏咎，不從臣言，禁止太常，復興刑獄。
entries.en: Despite Pei Wei's orders, terrified clerks prosecuted ritual ministers again.
entries.literal: Your servant explained dismissal yet chiefs feared blame—ignored advice—embargoed Minister of Ceremonies reopening trials.

entries.zh: 頠雖有此表，曲議猶不止。
entries.en: Even after Pei Wei’s paper, carping continued.
entries.literal: Although Pei had submitted this memorial, captious side-debates still did not cease.

entries.zh: 時劉頌為三公尚書，又上疏曰：
entries.en: Liu Song, serving as the Three Excellencies’ overseer, then added this argument:
entries.literal: At the time Liu Song, as Minister of the Three Dukes, again submitted a memorial saying:

entries.zh: 刑書之文有限，而舛違之故無方，故有臨時議處之制，誠不能皆得循常也。
entries.en: Because written law cannot cover every factual twist, judges need emergency procedures that sometimes break the usual rulebook.
entries.literal: Statute text is finite, yet causes of error know no limit—hence the system of ad hoc deliberation; one cannot in every case follow a constant rule.

entries.zh: 至於此等，皆為過當，每相逼迫，不得以理，上替聖朝畫一之德，下損崇禮大臣之望。
entries.en: These overreactions in tomb cases undercut the court’s commitment to one law for all and embarrass senior ministers who stand for proper ceremony.
entries.literal: As for these cases, all have exceeded the proper measure, each side pressing the other, unable to apply reason—above it undermines the sagely court’s virtue of uniform standards, below it injures the expectation that great ministers be honored in ritual.

entries.zh: 臣愚以為犯陵上草木，不應乃用同產異刑之制。
entries.en: Trampling graveyard growth should not trigger the same draconian kin-punishment statutes used for true desecration.
entries.literal: Your servant thinks that treading on plants above an imperial tumulus should not call forth the system of different punishments for those who share the same birth.

entries.zh: 按行奏劾，應有定準，相承務重，體例遂虧。
entries.en: Inspections and indictments need stable yardsticks, not an ever-harsher drift that warps precedent.
entries.literal: Investigations and impeachments ought to have fixed standards; generation after generation they pursued severity, and the body of precedent was thus injured.

entries.zh: 或因余事，得容淺深。
entries.en: Collateral issues can still adjust how heavy a sentence feels.
entries.literal: Sometimes, by way of other matters, one may accommodate lighter or deeper guilt.

entries.zh: 及帝即位，展為廷尉，又上言：「古者肉刑，事經前聖，漢文除之，增加大辟。
entries.en: When the emperor came to the throne, Wei Zhan became Commandant of Justice and again submitted words: "In antiquity, corporal punishments were matters passed through former sages; Emperor Wen of Han abolished them and increased capital penalties.
entries.literal: When the emperor came to the throne, Wei Zhan became Commandant of Justice and again submitted words: "In antiquity, corporal punishments were matters passed through former sages; Emperor Wen of Han abolished them and increased capital penalties.

entries.zh: 今人戶凋荒，百不遺一，而刑法峻重，非句踐養胎之義也。
entries.en: Depopulation clashes with Goujian-style mercy.
entries.literal: Now households are devastated—not one in a hundred survives—yet punishments stay harsh—this is not Goujian’s nurture-the-womb kindness.

entries.zh: 愚謂宜復古施行，以隆太平之化。」
entries.en: I foolishly think it fitting to restore antiquity and put it into effect, in order to exalt the transformation of Great Peace."
entries.literal: I foolishly think it fitting to restore antiquity and put it into effect, in order to exalt the transformation of Great Peace."

entries.zh: 詔內外通議。
entries.en: Court-wide deliberation ensued.
entries.literal: Edict ordered inner and outer courts deliberate.

entries.zh: 於是驃騎將軍王導、太常賀循、侍中紀瞻、中書郎庾亮、大將軍諮議參軍梅陶、散騎郎張嶷等議，以：「肉刑之典，由來尚矣。
entries.en: Thereupon General of Agile Cavalry Wang Dao, Chamberlain for Ceremonials He Xun, Attendant Ji Zhan, Palace Writer Gentleman Yu Liang, Great General's Advisory Army Consultant Mei Tao, Cavalier Gentleman Zhang Yi, and others deliberated, saying: "The canon of corporal punishments has long been honored in origin.
entries.literal: Thereupon General of Agile Cavalry Wang Dao, Chamberlain for Ceremonials He Xun, Attendant Ji Zhan, Palace Writer Gentleman Yu Liang, Great General's Advisory Army Consultant Mei Tao, Cavalier Gentleman Zhang Yi, and others deliberated, saying: "The canon of corporal punishments has long been honored in origin.

entries.zh: 肇自古先，以及三代，聖哲明王所未曾改也。
entries.en: Three-age kings kept mutilation.
entries.literal: From earliest ancestors through three dynasties sagely enlightened kings never altered them.

entries.zh: 豈是漢文常主所能易者乎！
entries.en: Han Wendi was no sage legislator.
entries.literal: How could mere Emperor Wen of Han alter them!

entries.zh: 時蕭曹已沒，絳灌之徒不能正其義。
entries.en: Early Han lacked wise ministers to defend classical law.
entries.literal: At that time Xiao He and Cao Shen had died—subordinates like Zhou Bo could not straighten principle.

entries.zh: 逮班固深論其事，以為外有輕刑之名，內實殺人。
entries.en: Ban Gu exposed Wen’s reform as bloodier.
entries.literal: When Ban Gu examined deeply he judged outwardly lighter punishments inwardly killed more.

entries.zh: 又死刑太重，生刑太輕，生刑縱於上，死刑怨於下，輕重失當，故刑政不中也。
entries.en: Wen’s imbalance caused penal dysfunction.
entries.literal: Further capital death weighs too heavy while living punishments weigh too light—living lax above, capital bitter below—imbalance misorders punishments.

entries.zh: 且原先王之造刑也，非以過怒也，非以殘人也，所以救奸，所以當罪。
entries.en: Classical mutilation targeted rehabilitation.
entries.literal: Moreover former kings crafting punishments acted not from excess anger nor desire to maim but to rescue society and match guilt.

entries.zh: 今盜者竊人之財，淫者好人之色，亡者避叛之役，皆無殺害也，則加之以刑。
entries.en: Non-capital crimes received death.
entries.literal: Now thieves steal lust seduces fugitives flee corvée—none kills yet punishments apply.

entries.zh: 刑之則止，而加之斬戮，戮過其罪，死不可生，縱虐於此，歲以巨計。
entries.en: Death sentences overshot proportion annually.
entries.literal: Punishment should stop yet waist-cutting adds killing—execution exceeds guilt—death cannot revive—such cruelty yearly tallies vast.

entries.zh: 此乃仁人君子所不忍聞，而況行之於政乎！
entries.en: Mass execution horrifies humane ears.
entries.literal: This benevolent gentlemen cannot bear hearing—how execute policy!

entries.zh: 若乃惑其名而不練其實，惡其生而趣其死，此畏水投舟，避坎蹈井，愚夫之不若，何取於政哉！
entries.en: Rejecting mutilation for killing is suicidal stupidity.
entries.literal: If deluded by reputation ignoring substance hating life rushing death—that fears water yet boards boat avoids pit yet leaps well—fools exceed such conduct—what governance values that!

entries.zh: 今大晉中興，遵復古典，率由舊章，起千載之滯義，拯百殘之遺黎，使皇典廢而復存，黔首死而更生，至義暢於三代之際，遺風播乎百世之後，生肉枯骨，惠侔造化，豈不休哉！
entries.en: Now in the Great Jin Restoration, the dynasty follows and restores the ancient canons and is guided by the old regulations. It raises up a meaning stalled for a thousand years, rescues the surviving people from a hundred ruins, makes the imperial canon exist again after being abolished, and makes the common people live again after death. Utmost righteousness will flourish in the age of the Three Dynasties, and its remaining influence will spread after a hundred generations. To make flesh grow on dry bones and make kindness equal to creation: is this not excellent!
entries.literal: Now in the Great Jin Restoration, the dynasty follows and restores the ancient canons and is guided by the old regulations. It raises up a meaning stalled for a thousand years, rescues the surviving people from a hundred ruins, makes the imperial canon exist again after being abolished, and makes the common people live again after death. Utmost righteousness will flourish in the age of the Three Dynasties, and its remaining influence will spread after a hundred generations. To make flesh grow on dry bones and make kindness equal to creation: is this not excellent!

entries.zh: 惑者乃曰，死猶不懲，而況于刑？
entries.en: Skeptics ask whether mutilation deters.
entries.literal: Critics say death still fails to deter—how much less mutilation?

entries.zh: 然人者冥也，其至愚矣，雖加斬戮，忽為灰土，死事日往，生欲日存，未以為改。
entries.en: Death’s abstraction fails deterrence.
entries.literal: Yet humans are benighted—most foolish—even executions vanish them to ash daily death dulls desire—few reform.

entries.zh: 若刑諸市朝，朝夕鑒戒，刑者詠為惡之永痛，惡者睹殘刖之長廢，故足懼也。
entries.en: Public mutilation educates better than hidden execution.
entries.literal: If executing in marketplace morning and evening offers mirror—criminals chant wicked pain forever villains glimpse lifelong maiming—then awe suffices.

entries.zh: 然後知先王之輕刑以禦物，顯誡以懲愚，其理遠矣。」
entries.en: Only then do we know that the former kings used light punishments to govern things and visible admonitions to discipline the foolish; their principle was far-reaching."
entries.literal: Only then do we know that the former kings used light punishments to govern things and visible admonitions to discipline the foolish; their principle was far-reaching."

entries.zh: 至安帝元興末，桓玄輔政，又議欲復肉刑斬左右趾之法，以輕死刑，命百官議。
entries.en: Yuanxing era Huan Xuan reopened corporal debate.
entries.literal: By Emperor An’s Yuanxing end Huan Xuan as regent again debated restoring foot-removal lightening capital death ordering hundred offices deliberate.

entries.zh: 蔡廓上議曰：「建邦立法，弘教穆化，必隨時置制，德刑兼施。
entries.en: Cai Kuo submitted a deliberation, saying: "In establishing a state and setting up laws, broadening instruction and harmonizing transformation, one must establish regulations according to the time and apply virtue and punishment together.
entries.literal: Cai Kuo submitted a deliberation, saying: "In establishing a state and setting up laws, broadening instruction and harmonizing transformation, one must establish regulations according to the time and apply virtue and punishment together.

entries.zh: 長貞一以閑其邪，教禁以檢其慢，灑湛露以流潤，厲嚴霜以肅威，雖復質文迭用，而斯道莫革。
entries.en: Moral education pairs with seasonal punishments.
entries.literal: Long rectitude fences evil teachings restrain slack sprinkling sweet dew nourishes harsh frost inspires awe—though substance and culture alternate this path never changes.

entries.zh: 肉刑之設，肇自哲王。
entries.en: Classical kings instituted mutilation.
entries.literal: Corporal punishments stemmed from wise kings.

entries.zh: 蓋由曩世風淳，人多惇謹，圖像既陳，則機心直戢，刑人在塗，則不逞改操，故能勝殘去殺，化隆無為。
entries.en: Pure ages needed only symbolic deterrence.
entries.literal: Because antiquity’s winds pure men mostly honest posted icons checked scheming punished walking roads deterred daring thus overcame cruelty eliminated killing elevated effortless rule.

entries.zh: 季末澆偽，設網彌密，利巧之懷日滋，恥畏之情轉寡。
entries.en: Decadent ages breed clever crime.
entries.literal: Late generations watered deceit denser nets crafty minds grew shame waned.

entries.zh: 終身劇役，不足止其奸，況乎黥劓，豈能反於善。
entries.en: Modern wickedness ignores corporal shame.
entries.literal: Lifetime hard labor cannot stop villainy—how much branding or nose-removal reforms goodness.

entries.zh: 徒有酸慘之聲，而無濟俗之益。
entries.en: Mutilation noise lacks social uplift.
entries.literal: Only sour misery echoes yet benefits customs nothing.

entries.zh: 至於棄市之條，實非不赦之罪，事非手殺，考律同歸，輕重均科，減降路塞，鐘陳以之抗言，元皇所為留湣。
entries.en: Equal sentencing blocked mercy Zhong Chen protested.
entries.literal: As for marketplace execution clauses truly not unforgivable crimes hands not killers yet statutes lump equal severity blocking mitigation paths—Zhong Chen remonstrated hence Yuan emperor pitied.

entries.zh: 今英輔翼贊，道邈伊周，誠宜明慎用刑，愛人弘育，申哀矜以革濫，移大辟于支體，全性命之至重，恢繁息於將來。」
entries.en: Now outstanding assistants give support and help, and their way is distant as Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. Truly they should be clear and cautious in using punishments, love the people and broadly nurture them, extend pity and compassion in order to reform excess, move capital penalties to the limbs, preserve the great weight of life and nature, and restore multiplication and growth for the future."
entries.literal: Now outstanding assistants give support and help, and their way is distant as Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. Truly they should be clear and cautious in using punishments, love the people and broadly nurture them, extend pity and compassion in order to reform excess, move capital penalties to the limbs, preserve the great weight of life and nature, and restore multiplication and growth for the future."

entries.zh: 而孔琳之議不同，用王朗、夏侯玄之旨。
entries.en: Kong Linzhi echoed Wang Lang opposing revival.
entries.literal: Yet Kong Linzhi disagreed adopting Wang Lang and Xiahou Xuan positions.

entries.zh: 時論多與琳之同，故遂不行。
entries.en: Majority sided Kong Linzhi—proposal stalled.
entries.literal: Contemporary debate mostly agreed with Linzhi therefore not enacted.

entries.zh: 刑法志
entries.en: Monograph: Criminal Law.
entries.literal: Treatise on Punishment and Law.

entries.zh: 孝武帝立，寧康二年，以后母裴氏為廣德縣君。
entries.en: After Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he titled the empress's mother, Lady Pei, Mistress of Guangde county in the second year of Ningkang.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was established, in the second year of Ningkang he made the empress's mother the Lady Pei Mistress of Guangde county.

entries.zh: 裴氏名穆，長水校尉綽孫，太傅主簿遐女，太尉王夷甫外孫。
entries.en: Lady Pei was named Mu—granddaughter of the Colonel of the Chang River Guard Pei Chuo, daughter of the Grand Tutor's registrar Pei Xia, and maternal granddaughter of Grand Commandant Wang Yan.
entries.literal: The Lady Pei had the name Mu; she was granddaughter of the Colonel of the Chang River Guard Chuo, daughter of the Registrar of the Grand Tutor Xia, and maternal granddaughter of Grand Commandant Wang Yan.

entries.zh: 中表之美，高於當世。
entries.en: Among her kin she stood out as one of the finest women of her generation.
entries.literal: The beauty among cousins was higher than in the contemporary age.

entries.zh: 遐隨東海王越遇害，無子。
entries.en: Pei Xia had followed Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, and was killed in the turmoil; he left no sons.
entries.literal: Xia followed the Prince of Donghai Yue and encountered harm and died; he had no sons.

entries.zh: 唯穆渡江，遂享榮慶，立第南掖門外，世所謂杜姥宅云。
entries.en: Only Lady Mu escaped south across the Yangzi and lived to see honor and ease; she built a mansion outside the southern side gate—the house later known as Old Lady Du's.
entries.literal: Only Mu crossed the Yangzi and thereupon enjoyed glory and felicity, erecting a mansion outside the southern Ye Gate—what the world calls Old Lady Du's house.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：方祇體安，儷乾儀而合德；
entries.en: The historians write: Earth holds still and mates with Heaven's pattern, sharing its virtue;
entries.literal: The historian's subject says: The square earth-spirit embodies tranquility; paired with Qian's model and joins virtue;

entries.zh: 圓舒循晷，配羲曜以齊明。
entries.en: the round moon follows the sundial's course and pairs with the solar splendor so both lights shine as one.
entries.literal: the round unfolds following sundial; paired with Xi radiance thereby equal brightness.'

entries.zh: 故知陽爍陰凝，萬物假其陶鑄；
entries.en: Thus yang's fire and yin's mold shape all things through their forge;
entries.literal: Therefore know yang melts yin congeals; the myriad things borrow their pottery-casting;

entries.zh: 火炎水潤，六氣由其調理。
entries.en: flame and flood temper the six cosmic breaths.
entries.literal: fire flames water moistens; the six qi by them are regulated and ordered.'

entries.zh: 取譬賢淑，作伉文思，靈根式固，實資於此。
