entries.zh: 吾不喜得幽州，喜獲二子。」
entries.en: I do not rejoice at obtaining Youzhou; I rejoice at obtaining these two men."
entries.literal: I do not rejoice at obtaining Youzhou; I rejoice at obtaining these two men."

entries.zh: 署從事中郎，出為長樂太守。
entries.en: Le named him staff adviser and governor of Changle.
entries.literal: He appointed him attendant for executive affairs and sent him out as Governor of Changle.

entries.zh: 及勒僭號，未遑制度，與王波為之撰朝儀，於是憲章文物，擬于王者。
entries.en: When Later Zhao began court ritual, Xian and Wang Bo drafted ceremonies fit for emperors.
entries.literal: When Le assumed a usurping title, before institutions were in place, he and Wang Bo drafted court ritual for him, whereupon statutes, regalia, and implements rivaled a true king's.

entries.zh: 勒大悅，署太中大夫，遷司徒。
entries.en: Le made him grand counselor, then minister of education.
entries.literal: Le was greatly pleased, appointed him Grand Palace Counselor, then Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 憲曆官無干績之稱，然在朝玄默，未嘗以物務經懷。
entries.en: He governed quietly without bustle while minds praised his virtue.
entries.literal: Though Xian earned no reputation for administrative feats in successive posts, at court he remained silent and never let mundane tasks burden his heart.

entries.zh: 但以德重名高，動見尊禮。
entries.en: Reputation alone won him ritual honor.
entries.literal: Yet by the weight of his virtue and fame he was everywhere received with deferential ceremony.

entries.zh: 竟卒于石氏，以族人峙子邁為嗣。
entries.en: In the end he died under the Shi clan; his clansman Zhi's son Mai was appointed heir.
entries.literal: In the end he died under the Shi clan; his clansman Zhi's son Mai was appointed heir.

entries.zh: 贊曰：世既順才，才膺世至。
entries.en: The verse praises timely union of talent and age.
entries.literal: The encomium runs: The age bows to talent; talent rises to meet the age.

entries.zh: 高平沈敏，蘊茲名器。
entries.en: It salutes Chen Qian's steady grasp of power.
entries.literal: Gaoping's Chen Qian was deep and astute, cherishing those vessels of fame.

entries.zh: 钜鹿自然，亦云經笥。
entries.en: It salutes Pei Xiu's effortless scholarship.
entries.literal: Julu's Pei Xiu moved with natural ease—another walking library of the classics.

entries.zh: 媧皇煉石，晉圖開秘。
entries.en: It invokes myth and charts to praise Jin mapping.
entries.literal: The goddess Nüwa smelted stone to mend heaven; Jin's charts unlocked hidden treasure.

entries.zh: 頠有清規，承家來媚。
entries.en: It closes by honoring Pei Yi's integrity.
entries.literal: Yi upheld pure standards, inheriting grace for his house.

entries.zh: 陳騫
entries.en: Chen Qian
entries.literal: Chen Qian

entries.zh: 安平獻王孚，字叔達，宣帝次弟也。
entries.en: Sima Fu, Prince Xian of Anping, styled Shuda, was the younger brother who followed Emperor Xuan (Sima Yi).
entries.literal: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu, courtesy name Shuda, was Emperor Xuan's next younger brother.

entries.zh: 初，孚長兄朗字伯達，宣帝字仲達，孚弟馗字季達，恂字顯達，進字惠達，通字雅達，敏字幼達，俱知名，故時號為「八達」焉。
entries.en: At first Fu's eldest brother Lang had courtesy name Boda; Emperor Xuan had courtesy name Zhongda; Fu's younger brothers were Kui, courtesy Jida; Xun, Xianda; Jin, Huida; Tong, Yada; and Min, Youda; all were renowned, so people at the time called them the 'Eight Worthies.'
entries.literal: At first Fu's eldest brother Lang had courtesy name Boda; Emperor Xuan had courtesy name Zhongda; Fu's younger brothers were Kui, courtesy Jida; Xun, Xianda; Jin, Huida; Tong, Yada; and Min, Youda; all were renowned, so people at the time called them the 'Eight Worthies.'

entries.zh: 孚溫厚廉讓，博涉經史。
entries.en: Warm, modest, and widely read in classical texts and history, he carried himself with unassuming grace.
entries.literal: Fu was warm and generous, honest and yielding, and broadly read the Classics and histories.

entries.zh: 漢末喪亂，與兄弟處危亡之中，簞食瓢飲，而披閱不倦。
entries.en: Through the Han collapse he and his brothers lived on the verge of ruin on the plainest fare, yet he never tired of his books.
entries.literal: At the end of the Han there was turmoil and disorder; with his brothers he dwelt amid peril and extinction, eating from bamboo baskets and drinking from gourd dippers, yet he wearied not of reading.

entries.zh: 性通恕，以貞白自立，未嘗有怨於人。
entries.en: Forgiving by temperament and upright in reputation, he kept himself blameless and bore no grudges.
entries.literal: By nature he was open and forgiving; by purity and integrity he established himself, and he never harbored resentment toward anyone.

entries.zh: 陳留殷武有名於海內，嘗罹罪譴，孚往省之，遂與同處分食，談者稱焉。
entries.en: When Yin Wu of Chenliu—a man celebrated empire-wide—was censured and punished, Fu called on him and stayed to share quarters and meals; observers admired his loyalty.
entries.literal: Yin Wu of Chenliu had renown throughout the realm; he once suffered condemnation for an offense. Fu went to visit him and shared lodging and divided food with him; those who spoke of it praised him.

entries.zh: 時孫權稱籓，請送任子，當遣前將軍于禁還，久而不至。
entries.en: Sun Quan had submitted as a tributary and offered to send a royal hostage and return the captive Yu Jin—but neither pledge appeared.
entries.literal: At that time Sun Quan declared himself a vassal and requested to send a hostage son; it was intended to send back former general Yu Jin, but after a long time he still had not arrived.

entries.zh: 天子以問孚，孚曰：「先王設九服之制，誠以要荒難以德懷，不以諸夏禮責也。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven asked Fu about it. Fu said, 'The former kings established the nine domains system—truly because the distant and wild regions are hard to win by virtue alone, and they did not hold them to Central States ritual.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven asked Fu about it. Fu said, 'The former kings established the nine domains system—truly because the distant and wild regions are hard to win by virtue alone, and they did not hold them to Central States ritual.

entries.zh: 陛下承緒，遠人率貢。
entries.en: Your Majesty carries on the succession; distant peoples all come bearing tribute.
entries.literal: Your Majesty carries on the succession; distant peoples all come bearing tribute.

entries.zh: 權雖未送任子，於禁不至，猶宜以寬待之，畜養士馬，以觀其變。
entries.en: Though Quan has not yet sent the hostage son and Yu Jin has not arrived, still it is fitting to treat him generously, nurture soldiers and horses, and observe how matters change.
entries.literal: Though Quan has not yet sent the hostage son and Yu Jin has not arrived, still it is fitting to treat him generously, nurture soldiers and horses, and observe how matters change.

entries.zh: 不可以嫌疑責讓，恐傷懷遠之義。
entries.en: One must not on account of suspicion reproach and blame him, lest one wound the principle of cherishing those far away.
entries.literal: One must not on account of suspicion reproach and blame him, lest one wound the principle of cherishing those far away.

entries.zh: 自孫策至權，奕世相繼，惟強與弱，不在一禁，禁之未至，當有他故耳。」
entries.en: From Sun Ce down to Quan, generations succeed one another; strength and weakness lie not in one Yu Jin; when Jin does not arrive, there ought to be another reason.'
entries.literal: From Sun Ce down to Quan, generations succeed one another; strength and weakness lie not in one Yu Jin; when Jin does not arrive, there ought to be another reason.'

entries.zh: 後禁至，果以疾遲留，而任子竟不至。
entries.en: Yu Jin eventually appeared, detained by illness as Fu predicted, yet the hostage never followed.
entries.literal: Afterward Jin arrived; indeed he had delayed because of illness, yet in the end the hostage son never came.

entries.zh: 大軍臨江，責其違言，吳遂絕不貢獻。
entries.en: Once imperial troops stood on the river and challenged Wu's breach of faith, tribute from the south stopped altogether.
entries.literal: When the great army reached the Yangzi they blamed Wu for breaking its word, and Wu then utterly ceased tribute.

entries.zh: 後出為河內典農，賜爵關內侯，轉清河太守。
entries.en: He later served as Henei agrarian director, received a secondary marquisate within the passes, then governed Qinghe.
entries.literal: Later he went out as Agrarian Director for Henei, was enfeoffed with rank of district marquis within the passes, and transferred to governor of Qinghe.

entries.zh: 初，魏文帝置度支尚書，專掌軍國支計，朝議以征討未息，動須節量。
entries.en: Emperor Wen had created the revenue ministry for military supply; court opinion stressed ongoing campaigns meant every outlay needed restraint.
entries.literal: At first Wei Emperor Wen established the Minister of Revenue to specialize in army and state expenditures; court discussion held that with expeditions still unfinished, movements constantly required moderation.

entries.zh: 及明帝嗣位，欲用孚，問左右曰：「有兄風不？」
entries.en: When Emperor Ming succeeded to the throne and wished to employ Fu, he asked those around him, "Does he have his elder brother's manner?"
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming succeeded to the throne and wished to employ Fu, he asked those around him, "Does he have his elder brother's manner?"

entries.zh: 答云：「似兄。」
entries.en: They answered, "He resembles his elder brother."
entries.literal: They answered, "He resembles his elder brother."

entries.zh: 天子曰：「吾得司馬懿二人，復何憂哉！」
entries.en: The Son of Heaven said, 'If I obtain two Sima Yis, what else need I worry about!'
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven said, 'If I obtain two Sima Yis, what else need I worry about!'

entries.zh: 轉為度支尚書。
entries.en: He was named minister of revenue.
entries.literal: Fu was transferred to Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 孚以為擒敵制勝，宜有備預。
entries.en: Fu insisted victory required planning ahead.
entries.literal: Fu held that to seize the enemy and achieve victory there ought to be preparedness beforehand.

entries.zh: 每諸葛亮入寇關中，邊兵不能制敵，中軍奔赴，輒不及事機，宜預選步騎二萬，以為二部，為討賊之備。
entries.en: Each time Zhuge Liang struck Guanzhong the border garrisons buckled while reinforcements arrived too late; Fu urged standing two corps of twenty thousand foot and horse in readiness.
entries.literal: Whenever Zhuge Liang invaded Guanzhong, the frontier troops could not check the enemy and the central army rushed to the rescue but always missed the moment; he proposed beforehand to select twenty thousand infantry and cavalry and divide them into two corps as preparations for punishing the rebels.

entries.zh: 又以關中連遭賊寇，穀帛不足，遣冀州農丁五千屯於上邽，秋冬習戰陣，春夏修田桑。
entries.en: With Guanzhong stripped by raids and short of grain and cloth, he relocated five thousand Ji cultivators to Shanggui to drill in winter and farm in summer.
entries.literal: Also because Guanzhong had repeatedly suffered bandit raids and grain and silk were insufficient, he sent five thousand farming households from Ji Province to garrison Shanggui; in autumn and winter they drilled battle formations, in spring and summer they tended fields and mulberries.

entries.zh: 由是關中軍國有餘，待賊有備矣。
entries.en: The western theater grew solvent while keeping the foe under watch.
entries.literal: By this means Guanzhong's army and state had surplus and awaited the enemy prepared.

entries.zh: 後除尚書右僕射，進爵昌平亭侯，遷尚書令。
entries.en: He rose to right vice director of the secretariat, marquis of Changping ting, then director.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, advanced in rank to Marquis of Changping precinct, and promoted Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 及大將軍曹爽擅權，李勝、何晏、鄧颺等亂政，孚不視庶事，但正身遠害而已。
entries.en: Under Cao Shuang's dictatorship and the cabal of Li Sheng, He Yan, and Deng Yang, Fu withdrew from daily administration and merely kept his head down.
entries.literal: When Grand General Cao Shuang monopolized power and Li Sheng, He Yan, Deng Yang, and others threw government into chaos, Fu did not attend to routine affairs but simply corrected himself and kept distant from harm.

entries.zh: 及宣帝誅爽，孚與景帝屯司馬門，以功進爵長社縣侯，加侍中。
entries.en: When Sima Yi struck down Shuang, Fu and Sima Shi sealed Sima Gate; for that service he became marquis of Changshe and palace attendant.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan executed Shuang, Fu together with Emperor Jing held Sima Gate; by merit he advanced to marquis of Changshe county and was additionally appointed palace attendant.

entries.zh: 及高貴鄉公遭害，百官莫敢奔赴，孚枕屍於股，哭之慟，曰：「殺陛下者臣之罪。」
entries.en: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang suffered violent death, none of the hundred officials dared go to the scene; Fu pillowed the corpse on his thigh, wept bitterly, and said, 'Those who killed Your Majesty are my crime.'
entries.literal: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang suffered violent death, none of the hundred officials dared go to the scene; Fu pillowed the corpse on his thigh, wept bitterly, and said, 'Those who killed Your Majesty are my crime.'

entries.zh: 奏推主者。
entries.en: He filed charges against the ringleaders.
entries.literal: He memorialized to pursue those responsible.

entries.zh: 會太后令以庶人禮葬，孚與群公上表，乞以王禮葬，從之。
entries.en: Though the empress dowager first demanded a commoner's funeral, Fu and his peers petitioned for kingly honors and won consent.
entries.literal: When it happened that the empress dowager ordered burial by commoner rites, Fu together with the dukes submitted a memorial begging burial by princely rites; she assented.

entries.zh: 孚性至慎。
entries.en: By temperament he was exceedingly careful.
entries.literal: Fu's nature was extremely cautious.

entries.zh: 宣帝執政，常自退損。
entries.en: Under Sima Yi's supremacy he habitually effaced himself.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan held power he often withdrew and diminished himself.

entries.zh: 後逢廢立之際，未嘗預謀。
entries.en: At every coup and enthronement thereafter he kept clear of the plotting.
entries.literal: Later when occasions of deposition and enthronement came, he never participated in plotting.

entries.zh: 景文二帝以孚屬尊，不敢逼。
entries.en: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao honored his seniority and never leaned on him.
entries.literal: Emperors Jing and Wen, because Fu's standing was venerable, did not dare coerce him.

entries.zh: 後進封長樂公。
entries.en: He was later advanced to duke of Changle.
entries.literal: Later he was advanced and enfeoffed as duke of Changle.

entries.zh: =義陽成王望，字子初，出繼伯父朗，寬厚有父風。
entries.en: Sima Wang, Prince Cheng of Yiyang, styled Zichu, was adopted into uncle Sima Lang's line—open-handed and steady like his father.
entries.literal: Prince Cheng of Yiyang, Wang, courtesy Zichu, went out to succeed uncle Lang; he was generous and mild and had his father's manner.

entries.zh: 仕郡上計吏，舉孝廉，辟司徒掾，曆平陽太守、洛陽典農中郎將。
entries.en: He rose from commandery accountant through filial-incorrupt recommendation and ministerial aide to Pingyang governor and Luoyang agrarian colonel.
entries.literal: He served the commandery as accounts clerk, was recommended Filial and Incorrupt, was summoned as aide to the Minister of Education, and successively held governor of Pingyang and Agrarian Commandant of Luoyang.

entries.zh: 從宣帝討王淩，以功封永安亭侯。
entries.en: Campaigning with Sima Yi against Wang Ling earned him the Yong'an ting marquisate.
entries.literal: He followed Emperor Xuan to punish Wang Ling and by merit was enfeoffed Marquis of Yong'an precinct.

entries.zh: 遷護軍將軍，改封安樂鄉侯，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: Promoted general who guards the army, he exchanged his fief for Anle township and received supernumerary cavalry attendant rank.
entries.literal: He was promoted General Who Guards the Army, changed enfeoffment to Marquis of Anle village, and added irregular cavalry attendant.

entries.zh: 時魏高貴鄉公好才愛士，望與裴秀、王沈、鍾會並見親待，數侍宴筵。
entries.en: Cao Mao cultivated writers and thinkers; Wang joined Pei Xiu, Wang Chen, and Zhong Hui in the emperor's intimate circle at countless banquets.
entries.literal: At that time Wei Duke of Gaoguixiang loved talent and cherished scholars; Wang together with Pei Xiu, Wang Chen, and Zhong Hui alike saw intimate favor and repeatedly attended banquets.

entries.zh: 公性急，秀等居內職，急有召便至。
entries.en: The sovereign's temper ran hot; men like Pei Xiu, holding palace posts, could answer an urgent summons immediately.
entries.literal: The duke was impatient by nature; Xiu and others held inner posts and when urgently summoned arrived at once.

entries.zh: 以望外官，特給追鋒車一乘，武賁五人。
entries.en: As an outsider he was granted a rapid courier cart and five household guards.
entries.literal: Because Wang was an outer official, specially there was given one swift-response carriage and five palace runners.

entries.zh: 時景文相繼輔政，未嘗朝覲，權歸晉室。
entries.en: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao ruled behind the curtain without formal audiences—effective authority already rested with the future Jin house.
entries.literal: At that time Jing and Wen succeeded each other as regents and never held court audience; power returned to the Jin house.

entries.zh: 望雖見寵待，每不自安，由是求出，為征西將軍、持節、都督雍涼二州諸軍事。
entries.en: Royal favor could not settle him; he won a western command as conquering-general with credentials over Yong and Liang.
entries.literal: Though Wang saw favor and treatment, often he was not at ease; on this account he sought to go out and became General Who Conquers the West, bearer of credentials, and supervisor of all military affairs of Yong and Liang provinces.

entries.zh: 在任八年，威化明肅。
entries.en: Across eight years his governance ran lucid and austere.
entries.literal: In office eight years, his awe-inspiring transformation was bright and stern.

entries.zh: 先是蜀將薑維屢寇關中，及望至，廣設方略，維不得為寇，關中賴之。
entries.en: After Jiang Wei's repeated strikes on Guanzhong, Wang's strategy stopped further incursions and steadied the northwest.
entries.literal: Earlier Shu general Jiang Wei repeatedly raided Guanzhong; when Wang arrived he broadly laid plans and measures so Wei could not raid; Guanzhong relied on him.

entries.zh: 進封順陽侯。
entries.en: His fief rose to marquis of Shunyang.
entries.literal: He was advanced and enfeoffed Marquis of Shunyang.

entries.zh: 徵拜衛將軍，領中領軍，典禁兵。
entries.en: Recalled as metropolitan guard, he headed the central army and commanded palace soldiers.
entries.literal: He was summoned and appointed General Who Guards the Metropolis, concurrently Central Army Supervisor, in charge of palace troops.

entries.zh: 尋加驃騎將軍、開府。
entries.en: He soon added champion-general rank with an independent staff.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Champion General and granted independent headquarters.

entries.zh: 頃之，代何曾為司徒。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he succeeded He Zeng as minister of education.
entries.literal: Before long he replaced He Zeng as Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 及武帝受禪，陳留王就金墉城，孚拜辭，執王手，流涕歔欷，不能自勝。
entries.en: When Sima Yan took the throne the Wei emperor withdrew to Jinyong; Fu clasped his hand in farewell and wept uncontrollably.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, the king of Chenliu went to Jinyong Fortress; Fu took leave of him, grasped the king's hand, wept and sobbed, and could not overcome himself.

entries.zh: 曰：「臣死之日，固大魏之純臣也。」
entries.en: He said, 'On the day I die I shall indeed be a pure minister of Great Wei.'
entries.literal: He said, 'On the day I die I shall indeed be a pure minister of Great Wei.'

entries.zh: 詔曰：「太傅勳德弘茂，朕所瞻仰，以光導弘訓，鎮靜宇內，願奉以不臣之禮。
entries.en: An edict said, 'The Grand Mentor's merit and virtue are vast and flourishing—what I look up to; by him brilliance guides instruction and calms the realm within the four seas—I wish to accord him rites that need not treat him as subject.
entries.literal: An edict said, 'The Grand Mentor's merit and virtue are vast and flourishing—what I look up to; by him brilliance guides instruction and calms the realm within the four seas—I wish to accord him rites that need not treat him as subject.

entries.zh: 其封為安平王，邑四萬戶。
entries.en: Enfeoff him as prince of Anping with forty thousand households.
entries.literal: Enfeoff him as prince of Anping with forty thousand households.

entries.zh: 進拜太宰、持節、都督中外諸軍事。」
entries.en: Advance him to Grand Preceptor, bearer of credentials, and commander-in-chief of all military affairs inside and outside."
entries.literal: Advance him to Grand Preceptor, bearer of credentials, and commander-in-chief of all military affairs inside and outside."

entries.zh: 有司奏，諸王未之國者，所置官屬，權未有備。
entries.en: Bureaus noted princes remaining at capital lacked complete households.
entries.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that for princes not yet gone to their fiefs the assigned staffs still lacked full appointments.

entries.zh: 帝以孚明德屬尊，當宣化樹教，為群後作則，遂備置官屬焉。
entries.en: The emperor ruled Fu's moral weight required a full household to model conduct for other royal uncles.
entries.literal: The emperor held that Fu's bright virtue and eminent standing ought to propagate transformation and establish instruction and serve as model for the host of kings; thereupon full staffs were completely appointed.

entries.zh: 又以孚內有親戚，外有交遊，惠下之費，而經用不豐，奉絹二千匹。
entries.en: Considering his kin, his hospitality, and modest stipend, the throne added two thousand rolls of silk.
entries.literal: Also because Fu had relatives within and friends without and expenses in showing kindness to subordinates yet regular income was not abundant, he was granted two thousand bolts of tribute silk.

entries.zh: 及元會，詔孚輿車上殿，帝於阼階迎拜。
entries.en: At court assembly his cart mounted the hall while Sima Yan bowed him in from the eastern stair.
entries.literal: At the New Year audience an edict ordered Fu's carriage onto the hall while the emperor greeted him with a bow on the eastern steps.

entries.zh: 既坐，帝親奉觴上壽，如家人禮。
entries.en: Seated, the emperor toasted him with familial warmth.
entries.literal: Once seated the emperor personally raised a cup and toasted him with family courtesy.

entries.zh: 帝每拜，孚跪而止之。
entries.en: Each time Sima Yan bowed, Fu dropped to his knees to forbid it.
entries.literal: Whenever the emperor bowed, Fu knelt to stop him.

entries.zh: 又給以雲母輦、青蓋車。
entries.en: He received a mica litter and an azure parasol carriage.
entries.literal: He was also granted a mica-canopied carriage and a blue-canopied coach.

entries.zh: 孚雖見尊寵，不以為榮，常有憂色。
entries.en: Yet privilege brought him no joy—his face stayed shadowed with worry.
entries.literal: Though Fu saw honor and favor he did not regard it as glory and often wore a troubled expression.

entries.zh: 臨終，遺令曰：「有魏貞士河內溫縣司馬孚，字叔達，不伊不周，不夷不惠，立身行道，終始若一，當以素棺單槨，斂以時服。」
entries.en: At his deathbed his testament said, 'There was a Wei loyalist of Henei Wen county, Sima Fu, courtesy Shuda—not acting Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou, neither withdrawing like Boyi nor compromising like Liuxiahui—who established himself and walked the Way from first to last as one; bury me in an unvarnished coffin with a single-layer outer shell and dress me in timely ordinary clothes.'
entries.literal: At his deathbed his testament said, 'There was a Wei loyalist of Henei Wen county, Sima Fu, courtesy Shuda—not acting Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou, neither withdrawing like Boyi nor compromising like Liuxiahui—who established himself and walked the Way from first to last as one; bury me in an unvarnished coffin with a single-layer outer shell and dress me in timely ordinary clothes.'

entries.zh: 泰始八年薨，時年九十三。
entries.en: He died in the eighth year of Taishi at ninety-three.
entries.literal: He died in the eighth year of Taishi at ninety-three.

entries.zh: 帝於太極東堂舉哀三日。
entries.en: Emperor Wu mourned three days in Taiji's east hall.
entries.literal: The emperor observed mourning three days in the eastern hall of Taiji Palace.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「王勳德超世，尊寵無二，期頤在位，朕之所倚。
entries.en: An edict said, 'The prince's merit and virtue surpass the age; honor and favor were without peer; he dwelt in office at a hundred years—what I relied upon.
entries.literal: An edict said, 'The prince's merit and virtue surpass the age; honor and favor were without peer; he dwelt in office at a hundred years—what I relied upon.

entries.zh: 庶永百齡，諮仰訓導，奄忽殂隕，哀慕感切。
entries.en: I hoped he would last forever to consult and look up to his instruction—suddenly he has fallen and passed away; grief and longing cut deep.
entries.literal: I hoped he would last forever to consult and look up to his instruction—suddenly he has fallen and passed away; grief and longing cut deep.

entries.zh: 其以東園溫明秘器、朝服一具、衣一襲、緋練百匹、絹布各五百匹、錢百萬，穀千斛以供喪事。
entries.en: Let there be supplied for the funeral the eastern park warming coffin and secret fittings, one set of court dress, one suit of clothes, one hundred bolts of crimson silk, five hundred bolts each of silk and cloth, a million cash, and a thousand hu of grain.
entries.literal: Let there be supplied for the funeral the eastern park warming coffin and secret fittings, one set of court dress, one suit of clothes, one hundred bolts of crimson silk, five hundred bolts each of silk and cloth, a million cash, and a thousand hu of grain.

entries.zh: 諸所施行，皆依漢東平獻王蒼故事。」
entries.en: All measures implemented shall follow the precedent of Han Prince Xian of Dongping, Liu Cang."
entries.literal: All measures implemented shall follow the precedent of Han Prince Xian of Dongping, Liu Cang."

entries.zh: 其家遵孚遺旨，所給器物，一不施用。
entries.en: The clan honored his will and refused every gifted token.
entries.literal: His family obeyed Fu's testamentary instructions; not one of the supplied implements was used.

entries.zh: 帝再臨喪，親拜盡哀。
entries.en: Sima Yan returned twice to bow in deepest sorrow.
entries.literal: The emperor twice attended the mourning and personally bowed in full grief.

entries.zh: 及葬，又幸都亭，望柩而拜，哀動左右。
entries.en: At interment he halted at the post station, bowed toward the catafalque, and moved every witness.
entries.literal: When it came to burial he also went to the courier station, gazed toward the bier and bowed, moving those around him to grief.

entries.zh: 給鑾輅輕車，介士武賁百人，吉凶導從二千餘人，前後鼓吹，配饗太廟。
entries.en: The cortège drew imperial hearses, a hundred household guards, two thousand ushers, full musical escort, and enshrinement beside the royal ancestors.
entries.literal: There were provided imperial escort carriages and light wagons, one hundred armored guards and palace runners, over two thousand attendants for auspicious and inauspicious processions, front and rear trumpets and drums, and joint sacrifice in the Grand Temple.

entries.zh: 九子：邕、望、輔、翼、晃、瑰、珪、衡、景。
entries.en: He had nine sons named Yong, Wang, Fu, Yi, Huang, Gui, Gui, Heng, and Jing—the fifth and sixth homophonous but written with different graphs.
entries.literal: Nine sons: Yong, Wang, Fu, Yi, Huang, Gui (lapis), Gui (jade tablet), Heng, Jing.

entries.zh: 武帝受禪，封義陽王，邑萬戶，給兵二千人，
entries.en: When Sima Yan took the throne Wang became prince of Yiyang at ten thousand households with a guard allotment of two thousand.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Yiyang with ten thousand households and two thousand troops granted.

entries.zh: 泰始三年，詔曰：「夫尚賢庸勳，尊宗茂親，所以體國經化，式是百辟也。
entries.en: In the third year of Taishi, an edict said, 'To esteem the worthy and employ the meritorious, to honor the clan and enrich kin—that is how one embodies the state and regulates transformation and serves as model for the hundred ministers.
entries.literal: In the third year of Taishi, an edict said, 'To esteem the worthy and employ the meritorious, to honor the clan and enrich kin—that is how one embodies the state and regulates transformation and serves as model for the hundred ministers.

entries.zh: 且台司之重，存乎天官，故周建六職，政典為首。
entries.en: Moreover the weight of the terrace ministers rests in Heaven's offices; therefore Zhou established six duties and governance statutes came first.
entries.literal: Moreover the weight of the terrace ministers rests in Heaven's offices; therefore Zhou established six duties and governance statutes came first.

entries.zh: 司徒、中領軍，以明德近屬，世濟其美；
entries.en: Minister of Education and Central Army Supervisor—by bright virtue as close kin across generations perfect their excellence;
entries.literal: Minister of Education and Central Army Supervisor—by bright virtue as close kin across generations perfect their excellence;

entries.zh: 祖考創業，翼佐大命，出典方任，入贊朝政，文德既著，武功宣暢。
entries.en: Grandfather and father founded enterprise, assisted the great mandate, went out to administer regional duty, entered to assist court governance; civil virtue was already manifest, martial merit widely displayed.
entries.literal: Grandfather and father founded enterprise, assisted the great mandate, went out to administer regional duty, entered to assist court governance; civil virtue was already manifest, martial merit widely displayed.

entries.zh: 逮朕嗣位，弼道惟明，宜登上司，兼統軍戎，內輔帝室，外隆威重，其進位太尉，中領軍如故。
entries.en: Down to Our succeeding the throne you have aided the Way with clarity; fittingly mount the high minister and concurrently command the army—within assist the imperial house, without raise mighty awe; We advance your rank to Grand Commandant; Central Army Supervisor as before.
entries.literal: Down to Our succeeding the throne you have aided the Way with clarity; fittingly mount the high minister and concurrently command the army—within assist the imperial house, without raise mighty awe; We advance your rank to Grand Commandant; Central Army Supervisor as before.

entries.zh: 置太尉軍司一人，參軍事六人，騎司馬五人。
entries.en: Establish one army aide to the Grand Commandant, six military staff advisers, five cavalry majors.
entries.literal: Establish one army aide to the Grand Commandant, six military staff advisers, five cavalry majors.

entries.zh: 又增置官騎十人，並前三十，假羽葆鼓吹。」
entries.en: Also additionally establish ten official mounted escorts—together with the former thirty—and confer feather-canopy band and drum.'
entries.literal: Also additionally establish ten official mounted escorts—together with the former thirty—and confer feather-canopy band and drum.'

entries.zh: 吳將施績寇江夏，邊境騷動。
entries.en: Wu general Shi Ji's strike on Jiangxia threw the frontier into alarm.
entries.literal: Wu general Shi Ji raided Jiangxia and the border was disturbed.

entries.zh: 以望統中軍步騎二萬，出屯龍陂，為二方重鎮，假節，加大都督諸軍事。
entries.en: Wang led twenty thousand central troops to Longpi as the brace between two theaters, credentials in hand as grand commander.
entries.literal: Wang was ordered to command twenty thousand infantry and cavalry of the central army, go out and encamp at Longpi as heavy garrison for two fronts, given credentials, and additionally promoted grand commander of all military affairs.

entries.zh: 會荊州刺史胡烈距績，破之，望乃班師。
entries.en: When Jing inspector Hu Lie routed Shi Ji, Wang stood down his army.
entries.literal: It happened that Inspector of Jing Province Hu Lie resisted Ji and defeated him; thereupon Wang withdrew the army.

entries.zh: 俄而吳將丁奉寇芍陂，望又率諸軍以赴之，未至而奉退。
entries.en: Ding Feng's raid on Quepi drew Wang east again, though the enemy slipped away before he arrived.
entries.literal: Soon Wu general Ding Feng raided Quepi; Wang again led the various armies to hurry there; before he arrived Feng withdrew.

entries.zh: 拜大司馬。
entries.en: He received appointment as grand marshal.
entries.literal: He was appointed Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 孫皓率眾向壽春，詔望統中軍二萬，騎三千，據淮北。
entries.en: Sun Hao's thrust toward Shouchun sent Wang to the north bank of the Huai with twenty thousand foot and three thousand horse.
entries.literal: Sun Hao led a host toward Shouchun; an edict ordered Wang to command twenty thousand central troops and three thousand cavalry and hold north of the Huai.

entries.zh: 皓退，軍罷。
entries.en: Sun Hao withdrew and the mobilization ended.
entries.literal: Hao withdrew and the army was disbanded.

entries.zh: 泰始七年薨，時年六十七，賻贈有加，望性儉吝而好聚斂，身亡之後，金帛盈溢，以此獲譏。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Taishi, he died at sixty-seven amid lavish obsequies yet earned ridicule for having hoarded treasure despite a miserly reputation.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi, he died at age sixty-seven; funeral gifts were generous in addition; Wang's nature was frugal and stingy yet fond of amassing; after his death gold and silk overflowed; on this account he incurred ridicule.

entries.zh: 四子：弈、洪、整、楙。
entries.en: Four sons survived him: Yi, Hong, Zheng, and Mao.
entries.literal: Four sons: Yi, Hong, Zheng, Mao.

entries.zh: 弈至黃門郎，先望卒。
entries.en: Yi rose to yellow-gate gentleman but died before his father.
entries.literal: Yi reached Yellow Gate Gentleman and died before Wang.

entries.zh: 整亦早亡。
entries.en: Zheng likewise died young.
entries.literal: Zheng also died young.

entries.zh: 以弈子奇襲爵。
entries.en: The title passed to Yi's son Qi.
entries.literal: By Yi's son Qi the noble rank was inherited.

entries.zh: 奇亦好畜聚，不知紀極，遣三部使到交廣商貨，為有司所奏，太康九年，詔貶為三縱亭侯。
entries.en: Qi also delighted in hoarding wealth without limit, sending three divisions of agents to trade in Jiao and Guang; after officials memorialized against him, an edict in Taikang year nine demoted him to Marquis of Sanzong Precinct.
entries.literal: Qi also delighted in hoarding wealth without limit, sending three divisions of agents to trade in Jiao and Guang; after officials memorialized against him, an edict in Taikang year nine demoted him to Marquis of Sanzong Precinct.

entries.zh: 更以章武王威為望嗣。
entries.en: The throne then named Sima Wei of Zhangwu as Wang's heir.
entries.literal: Next Prince Wei of Zhangwu was made Wang's successor.

entries.zh: 後威誅，復立奇為棘陽王以嗣望。
entries.en: After Wei's execution Qi was restored as Prince of Jiyang to continue Wang's line.
entries.literal: Later when Wei was executed, Qi was again established as Prince of Jiyang to succeed Wang.

entries.zh: 隨穆王整，兄弈卒，以整為世子。
entries.en: When Yi died Zheng became heir of the Yiyang house.
entries.literal: Prince Mu of Sui, Zheng—when elder brother Yi died Zheng was made heir apparent.

entries.zh: 曆南中郎將，封清泉侯，先父望薨，追贈冠軍將軍。
entries.en: He commanded southern gentlemen and held Qingquan marquis but predeceased Sima Wang; upon Wang's death the court posthumously named him Champion General.
entries.literal: He successively held General of the Southern Gentlemen, was enfeoffed Marquis of Qingquan; he died before his father Wang; when Wang died he was posthumously invested Champion General.

entries.zh: 武帝以義陽國一縣追封為隨縣王。
entries.en: Emperor Wu carved out Sui county from Yiyang for his posthumous princedom.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu used one county of the Yiyang state to posthumously enfeoff him as Prince of Sui county.

entries.zh: 子邁嗣。
entries.en: Mai succeeded him.
entries.literal: Son Mai succeeded.

entries.zh: 太康九年，以義陽之平林益邁為隨郡王。
entries.en: In 288 Yiyang's Pinglin canton enlarged Mai's domain to prince of Sui commandery.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Taikang Pinglin of Yiyang was added to enlarge Mai as Prince of Sui commandery.

entries.zh: 河間平王洪，字孔業，出繼叔父昌武亭侯遺。
entries.en: Sima Hong, Prince Ping of Hejian, styled Kongye, was adopted into uncle Yi's Changwu ting line.
entries.literal: Prince Ping of Hejian, Hong, courtesy Kongye, went out to succeed uncle Marquis of Changwu precinct Yi.

entries.zh: 仕魏，歷位典農中郎將、原武太守，封襄賁男。
entries.en: Under Wei he served as agrarian colonel, Yuanwu governor, and baron of Xiangben.
entries.literal: Serving Wei he successively held Agrarian Commandant, governor of Yuanwu, and was enfeoffed Baron of Xiangben.

entries.zh: 武帝受禪，封河間王。
entries.en: When Sima Yan took the throne Hong became prince of Hejian.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Hejian.

entries.zh: 立十二年，咸寧二年薨。
entries.en: After twelve years in the position, he died in Xianning year two.
entries.literal: After twelve years in the position, he died in Xianning year two.

entries.zh: 二子：威、混。
entries.en: He left two sons, Wei and Hun.
entries.literal: Two sons: Wei and Hun.

entries.zh: 威嗣，徙封章武。
entries.en: Wei inherited and moved the fief to Zhangwu.
entries.literal: Wei succeeded and was transferred enfeoffment to Zhangwu.

entries.zh: 其後威既繼義陽王望，更立混為洪嗣。
entries.en: Once Wei continued Sima Wang's Yiyang title, Hun was designated Hong's heir.
entries.literal: Later when Wei had succeeded Prince of Yiyang Wang, Hun was further established as Hong's successor.

entries.zh: 混歷位散常侍，薨。
entries.en: Hun served as supernumerary cavalry attendant and died.
entries.literal: Hun successively held irregular attendant posts and died.

entries.zh: 竟陵王楙，字孔偉，初封樂陵亭侯，起家參相國軍事。
entries.en: Sima Mao, styled Kongwei, began as marquis of Leling ting on the prince's military staff.
entries.literal: Prince of Jingling Mao, courtesy Kongwei, at first was enfeoffed Marquis of Leling precinct and began office as participant in princely-state military affairs.

entries.zh: 武帝受禪，封東平王，邑三千九十七戶。
entries.en: When Sima Yan took the throne Mao became prince of Dongping at 3,097 households.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Dongping with three thousand ninety-seven households.

entries.zh: 入為散騎常侍、尚書。
entries.en: He transferred to the capital as supernumerary cavalry attendant and ministry counselor.
entries.literal: He entered court as irregular cavalry attendant and minister.

entries.zh: 威字景曜，初嗣洪，
entries.en: Sima Wei, styled Jingyao, first inherited Hong.
entries.literal: Wei courtesy Jingyao at first succeeded Hong.

entries.zh: 咸寧三年，徙封章武。
entries.en: In Xianning year three, his fief was transferred to Zhangwu.
entries.literal: In Xianning year three, his fief was transferred to Zhangwu.

entries.zh: 太康九年，嗣義陽王望。
entries.en: In Taikang year nine, he continued Sima Wang's Yiyang princedom.
entries.literal: In Taikang year nine, he continued Sima Wang's Yiyang princedom.

entries.zh: 威凶暴無操行，諂附趙王倫。
entries.en: Savage and unscrupulous, he hitched himself to Sima Lun.
entries.literal: Wei was fierce and violent without moral conduct and flattered and attached himself to Prince Zhao Lun.

entries.zh: 元康末，為散騎常侍，倫將篡，使威與黃門郎駱休逼帝奪璽綬，倫以威為中書令。
entries.en: Late in Yuankang he helped Sima Lun wrench the seal from Emperor Hui alongside Luo Xiu, then took the palace secretariat.
entries.literal: At the end of Yuankang he was irregular cavalry attendant; when Lun was about to usurp he sent Wei together with Yellow Gate Gentleman Luo Xiu to coerce the emperor and seize the seal cords; Lun appointed Wei Palace Secretariat Director.

entries.zh: 倫敗，惠帝反正，曰：「阿皮捩吾指，奪吾璽綬，不可不殺。」
entries.en: When Lun was defeated Emperor Hui resumed right rule and said, 'Api twisted my fingers and seized my seal cords—cannot fail to kill him.'
entries.literal: When Lun was defeated Emperor Hui resumed right rule and said, 'Api twisted my fingers and seized my seal cords—cannot fail to kill him.'

entries.zh: 阿皮，威小字也。
entries.en: Api' was Wei's infant name.
entries.literal: Api was Wei's childhood name.

entries.zh: 於是誅威。
entries.en: Wei was put to death.
entries.literal: Thereupon Wei was executed.

entries.zh: 楙善諂諛，曲事楊駿。
entries.en: Sima Mao excelled at sycophancy and curried favor with Yang Jun.
entries.literal: Mao was skilled at flattery and fawning and bent his service to Yang Jun.

entries.zh: 及駿誅，依法當死，東安公繇與楙善，故得不坐。
entries.en: Jun's fall should have cost Mao his life, yet Sima You's friendship shielded him.
entries.literal: When Jun was executed, by law Mao ought to have died, but Duke of Dongan You was friendly with Mao, so he avoided punishment.

entries.zh: 尋遷大鴻臚，加侍中。
entries.en: He soon rose to grand herald with supernumerary palace attendant rank.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted Grand Herald and added palace attendant.

entries.zh: 繇欲擅朝政，與汝南王亮不平。
entries.en: Sima You grasped for centralized power and clashed with Prince Liang of Runan.
entries.literal: You wished to monopolize court government and was at odds with Prince Liang of Runan.

entries.zh: 帝托以繇討駿顧望，免繇、楙等官，遣楙就國。
entries.en: Emperor Hui blamed Sima You for half-hearted action against Jun, cashiered both men, and banished Mao to his domain.
entries.literal: The emperor on the pretext that You hesitated in attacking Jun removed You and Mao from office and sent Mao to his fief.

entries.zh: 楙殖財貨，奢僭逾制。
entries.en: He hoarded treasure and flouted sumptuary law with pretensions beyond his rank.
entries.literal: Mao amassed wealth and goods; extravagance and usurpation of ritual exceeded regulations.

entries.zh: 趙王倫篡位，召還。
entries.en: Sima Lun's coup brought Mao back to court.
entries.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne he recalled Mao.

entries.zh: 及義兵起，倫以楙為衛將軍、都督諸軍事。
entries.en: Once loyalist armies rose Lun named Mao metropolitan guard and overall commander.
entries.literal: When the righteous host rose, Lun appointed Mao General Who Guards the Metropolis and supervisor of all military affairs.

entries.zh: 倫敗，楙免官。
entries.en: Lun's fall stripped Mao of his posts.
entries.literal: When Lun was defeated Mao was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 齊王冏輔政，繇復為僕射，舉楙為平東將軍、都督徐州諸軍事，鎮下邳。
entries.en: Under Sima Jiong's regency Sima You returned as vice director and nominated Mao as pacifier-general for Xu based at Xiapi.
entries.literal: When Prince of Qi Jiong assisted government You again became vice director and recommended Mao as General Who Pacifies the East and supervisor of Xu military affairs, stationed at Xiapi.

entries.zh: 成都王穎輔政，進楙為衛將軍。
entries.en: Sima Ying's turn at power promoted Mao to metropolitan guard.
entries.literal: When Prince of Chengdu Ying assisted government Mao was advanced to General Who Guards the Metropolis.

entries.zh: 會惠帝北征，即以楙為車騎將軍，都督如故，使率眾赴鄴。
entries.en: The northern expedition made Mao chariot-and-cavalry general at Ye with unchanged theater command.
entries.literal: When Emperor Hui campaigned north Mao was at once made chariot-and-cavalry general with supervisory duties unchanged and ordered to lead troops toward Ye.

entries.zh: 蕩陰之役，東海王越奔於下邳，楙不納，越乃還國。
entries.en: After Dangyin Sima Yue sought refuge at Xiapi; Mao shut the gates and sent him home.
entries.literal: In the Dangyin fighting Prince of Donghai Yue fled to Xiapi; Mao refused him entry, so Yue returned to his state.

entries.zh: 帝既西幸，越總兵謀迎大駕，楙甚懼。
entries.en: After Emperor Hui had gone west, Sima Yue gathered troops and planned to welcome back the imperial carriage; Mao was greatly afraid.
entries.literal: Once the emperor had fled west Yue gathered troops planning to welcome the imperial carriage; Mao was greatly afraid.

entries.zh: 長史王修說曰：「東海宗室重望，今將興義，公宜舉徐州以授之，此克讓之美也。」
entries.en: Chief Clerk Wang Xiu advised saying, 'Prince of Donghai carries heavy prestige among the imperial clan; now he will raise righteous arms—you ought to yield Xu Province to him; this is the beauty of yielding precedence.'
entries.literal: Chief Clerk Wang Xiu advised saying, 'Prince of Donghai carries heavy prestige among the imperial clan; now he will raise righteous arms—you ought to yield Xu Province to him; this is the beauty of yielding precedence.'

entries.zh: 楙從之，乃自承制都督兗州刺史、車騎將軍，表于天子。
entries.en: Mao complied, seized Yan under emergency orders as chariot-and-cavalry chief, and reported to the throne.
entries.literal: Mao followed this; thereupon on his own authority under emergency regulations he acted as supervisor of Yan Province and chariot-and-cavalry general and memorialized the Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 時帝在長安，遣使者劉虔即拜焉。
entries.en: At Chang'an the court sent Liu Qian to seal the arrangement.
entries.literal: At that time the emperor was at Chang'an and dispatched envoy Liu Qian to confirm the appointment on the spot.

entries.zh: 晃孝友貞廉，謙虛下士，甚得宗室之稱。
entries.en: Filial, modest, and scrupulous, he won wide esteem among kinsmen.
entries.literal: Huang was filial, friendly, chaste, and honest, humble toward scholars, and greatly earned praise among the imperial clan.

entries.zh: 後為長水校尉、南中郎將。
entries.en: He later commanded long waters and southern gentlemen.
entries.literal: Later he was Colonel of Long Waters and General of the Southern Gentlemen.

entries.zh: 九年，詔曰：「南中郎將、下邳王晃清亮中正，體行明潔，才周政理，有文武策識。
entries.en: In the ninth year an edict said, 'Southern Gentlemen General Prince of Xiapi Huang is pure, bright, and upright; his conduct is lucid and clean; talent suffices for governance and he possesses civil and military stratagem.
entries.literal: In the ninth year an edict said, 'Southern Gentlemen General Prince of Xiapi Huang is pure, bright, and upright; his conduct is lucid and clean; talent suffices for governance and he possesses civil and military stratagem.

entries.zh: 其以晃為使持節，都督甯益二州諸軍事、安西將軍，領益州刺史。」
entries.en: Let Huang be credential-bearing commissioner supervising Ning and Yi military affairs, General Who Pacifies the West, and concurrently Inspector of Yi Province.'
entries.literal: Let Huang be credential-bearing commissioner supervising Ning and Yi military affairs, General Who Pacifies the West, and concurrently Inspector of Yi Province.'

entries.zh: 晃以疾不行，更拜尚書，遷右僕射。
entries.en: Pleading illness he stayed north and instead took minister of writing and right vice director.
entries.literal: Huang pleaded illness and did not go; he was further appointed Minister of Writing and promoted Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 久之，出為鎮東將軍、都督青徐二州諸軍事。
entries.en: Years later he commanded Qing and Xu from the east.
entries.literal: After a long while he went out as General Who Guards the East supervising Qing and Xu military affairs.

entries.zh: 惠帝即位，入為車騎將軍，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: Hui made him chariot-and-cavalry chief with supernumerary cavalry attendant.
entries.literal: When Emperor Hui ascended he entered as chariot-and-cavalry general with additional irregular cavalry attendant.

entries.zh: 將誅楊駿，以晃領護軍，屯東掖門，尋守尚書令。
entries.en: During Yang Jun's purge he guarded Dongye Gate then acting minister director.
entries.literal: When Yang Jun was to be executed Huang was put in charge of the guards encamped at Dongye Gate and soon held Minister Director.

entries.zh: 遷司空，加侍中，令如故。
entries.en: He rose to minister of works plus palace attendant, keeping director duties.
entries.literal: He was promoted Minister of Works with additional palace attendant while retaining minister director.

entries.zh: 元康六年薨，追贈太傅。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Yuankang, Death brought posthumous grand mentor.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Yuankang, he died and was posthumously invested Grand Mentor.

entries.zh: 楙慮兗州刺史苟晞不避己，乃給虔兵，使稱詔誅晞。
entries.en: Fearing Gou Xi, Mao armed Liu Qian with a forged warrant for Xi's death.
entries.literal: Mao feared Yan Inspector Gou Xi would not defer to him; therefore he supplied Qian troops and had him profess an edict executing Xi.

entries.zh: 晞時已避位，楙在州徵求不已，郡縣不堪命。
entries.en: Though Gou Xi had yielded, Mao's exactions broke the commanderies.
entries.literal: Xi had already stepped aside, yet Mao in the province demanded endlessly; commanderies and counties could not bear the orders.

entries.zh: 范陽王虓遣晞還兗州，徙楙都督青州諸軍事。
entries.en: Sima Xiao restored Gou Xi and shifted Mao to Qing theater.
entries.literal: Prince Xiao of Fanyang sent Xi back to Yan Province and transferred Mao to supervise Qing military affairs.

entries.zh: 楙不受命，背山東諸侯，與豫州刺史劉喬相結。
entries.en: Mao rejected the posting, broke with the eastern league, and joined Liu Qiao.
entries.literal: Mao refused the order, turned his back on the Shandong princes, and allied with Inspector Qiao of Yu Province Liu.

entries.zh: 虓遣將田徽擊楙，破之，楙走還國。
entries.en: Tian Hui routed Mao, who bolted for his fief.
entries.literal: Xiao dispatched general Tian Hui to strike Mao, defeated him, and Mao fled back to his state.

entries.zh: 帝還洛陽，楙乃詣闕。
entries.en: When Emperor Hui returned to Luoyang, Mao presented himself at the palace gates.
entries.literal: When the emperor returned to Luoyang Mao then presented himself at the palace gates.

entries.zh: 輔弟翼
entries.en: Yi—Fu's younger brother.
entries.literal: Fu di Yi.

entries.zh: 翼字子世，少曆顯位，官至武賁中郎將。
entries.en: Sima Yi, styled Zishi, rose young to major among the palace guards.
entries.literal: Yi courtesy Zishi in youth successively held eminent posts and reached Major of the Household Guards.

entries.zh: 武帝未受禪而卒，以兄邕之支子承為嗣，封南宮縣王。
entries.en: He died before the Wei-Jin transition; Yong's collateral heir Cheng took Nangong county.
entries.literal: Before Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he died; Yong's cadet son Cheng was appointed successor as Prince of Nangong county.

entries.zh: 薨，子祐嗣立，承遂無後。
entries.en: When Cheng died You continued the line, ending Cheng's branch.
entries.literal: He died; son You succeeded and Cheng thereby had no posterity.

entries.zh: 翼弟下邳獻王晃
entries.en: Huang, Prince Xian of Xiapi—Yi's younger brother.
entries.literal: Yi di Xiapi Offering Wang Huang.

entries.zh: 太原成王輔，魏末為野王太守。
entries.en: Late in Wei Sima Fu governed Yewang.
entries.literal: Prince Cheng of Taiyuan, Fu, at the end of Wei was governor of Yewang.

entries.zh: 武帝受禪，封渤海王，邑五千三百七十九戶，泰始二年之國。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, he enfeoffed him as Prince of Bohai with 5,379 households; in Taishi year two, he went to his domain.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, he enfeoffed him as Prince of Bohai with 5,379 households; in Taishi year two, he went to his domain.

entries.zh: 後為衛尉，出為東中郎將，轉南中郎將，咸寧三年，徙為太原王，監并州諸軍事。
entries.en: He later served as Commandant of Guards, went out as Gentlemen-General of the East, transferred to Gentlemen-General of the South, and in Xianning year three was moved to Prince of Taiyuan, supervising all military affairs in Bingzhou.
entries.literal: He later served as Commandant of Guards, went out as Gentlemen-General of the East, transferred to Gentlemen-General of the South, and in Xianning year three was moved to Prince of Taiyuan, supervising all military affairs in Bingzhou.

entries.zh: 太康四年入朝，五年薨，追贈鎮北將軍，
entries.en: In Taikang year four he entered court; in year five he died and was posthumously granted General Who Guards the North,
entries.literal: In Taikang year four he entered court; in year five he died and was posthumously granted General Who Guards the North,

entries.zh: 永平元年，更贈衛將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: and in Yongping year one he was further granted General of the Guards and the privileges of Opening an Office Equal to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: and in Yongping year one he was further granted General of the Guards and the privileges of Opening an Office Equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 子弘立，元康中為散騎常侍，後徙封中丘王。
entries.en: Heir Hong held supernumerary cavalry attendant then moved the title to Zhongqiu.
entries.literal: Son Hong succeeded; in Yuankang he was irregular cavalry attendant and later transferred enfeoffment to Prince of Zhongqiu.

entries.zh: 三年薨，子鑠立。
entries.en: Three years on Shuo inherited.
entries.literal: In the third year he died; son Shuo succeeded.

entries.zh: 下邳獻王晃字子明，魏封武始亭侯，拜黃門侍郎，改封西安男，出為東莞太守。
entries.en: Sima Huang, styled Ziming, began as Wushi ting marquis, yellow-gate gentleman, Xi'an baron, then Dongguan governor.
entries.literal: Prince Xian of Xiapi Huang courtesy Ziming was enfeoffed Marquis of Wushi precinct in Wei, appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman, changed to Baron of Xi'an, and went out as governor of Dongguan.

entries.zh: 武帝受禪，封下邳王，邑五千一百七十六戶，泰始二年就國。
entries.en: Sima Yan invested him at Xiapi with 5,176 households in 266.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiapi with five thousand one hundred seventy-six households and proceeded to his state in Taishi year two.

entries.zh: 太原烈王瓌，字子泉，魏長樂亭侯，改封貴壽鄉侯。
entries.en: Sima Gui, styled Ziquan, held Changle ting then Guishou township under Wei.
entries.literal: Prince Lie of Taiyuan Gui courtesy Ziquan was Marquis of Changle precinct in Wei and changed to Marquis of Guishou village.

entries.zh: 曆振威將軍，秘書監，封固始子。
entries.en: He rose through display-might general and palace librarian to Gushi viscount.
entries.literal: He successively held General Who Displays Might, Palace Library Supervisor, and was enfeoffed Viscount of Gushi.

entries.zh: 武帝受禪，封太原王，邑五千四百九十六戶，泰始二年就國。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, he enfeoffed him as Prince of Taiyuan with 5,496 households; in Taishi year two, he went to his state.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, he enfeoffed him as Prince of Taiyuan with 5,496 households; in Taishi year two, he went to his state.

entries.zh: 四年入朝，賜袞冕之服，遷東中郎將。
entries.en: Year four brought court robes and eastern gentleman-general rank.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he entered court and was granted robe and crown of state; he was promoted General of the Eastern Gentlemen.

entries.zh: 十年薨，詔曰：「瑰乃心忠篤，智器雅亮。
entries.en: In the tenth year he died; an edict said, 'Gui's heart was loyal and earnest; intellect and capacity were elegant and bright.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he died; an edict said, 'Gui's heart was loyal and earnest; intellect and capacity were elegant and bright.

entries.zh: 歷位文武，有幹事之績。
entries.en: He successively held civil and military posts and had achievements in handling affairs.
entries.literal: He successively held civil and military posts and had achievements in handling affairs.

entries.zh: 出臨封土，夷夏懷附，鎮守許都，思謀可紀。
entries.en: Going out he faced his enfeoffment lands and barbarians and Chinese cherished allegiance; guarding Xu capital his designs merit record.
entries.literal: Going out he faced his enfeoffment lands and barbarians and Chinese cherished allegiance; guarding Xu capital his designs merit record.

entries.zh: 不幸早薨，朕甚悼之。
entries.en: Unluckily he died young; We greatly mourn him.
entries.literal: Unluckily he died young; We greatly mourn him.

entries.zh: 今安厝在近，其追贈前將軍。」
entries.en: Now that burial is near, let him be posthumously invested as Former General."
entries.literal: Now that burial is near, let him be posthumously invested as Former General."

entries.zh: 子顒立，徙封河間王，別有傳。
entries.en: Heir Yong shifted the fief to Hejian—a fuller life appears in a separate biography.
entries.literal: Son Yong succeeded, transferred enfeoffment to Prince of Hejian; elsewhere there is a biography.

entries.zh: 高陽元王珪，字子璋，少有才望，魏高陽鄉侯。
entries.en: Sima Gui, Prince Yuan of Gaoyang, styled Zizhang, had talent and a good reputation in his youth. Under Wei he was Marquis of Gaoyang Village.
entries.literal: Prince Yuan of Gaoyang, Gui, courtesy name Zizhang, had talent and a good reputation in his youth and was Marquis of Gaoyang Township under Wei.

entries.zh: 曆河南令，進封湞陽子，拜給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: He governed Henan, rose to Zhenyang viscount, then serving yellow-gate gentleman.
entries.literal: He successively held magistrate of Henan, advanced to Viscount of Zhenyang, and was appointed Serving Yellow Gate Gentleman.

entries.zh: 武帝受禪，封高陽王，邑五千五百七十戶。
entries.en: Sima Yan invested Gaoyang at 5,570 households.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Gaoyang with five thousand five hundred seventy households.

entries.zh: 曆北中郎將、督鄴城守諸軍事。
entries.en: He commanded northern gentlemen and Ye defenses.
entries.literal: He successively held General of the Northern Gentlemen and supervised Ye city garrison affairs.

entries.zh: 泰始六年入朝，以父孚年高，乞留供養。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Taishi, Court duty moved him to ask leave to nurse elderly Sima Fu.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi, Entering court because father Fu was advanced in years he begged to remain and provide support.

entries.zh: 拜尚書，遷右僕射。
entries.en: He took the ministry then right vice director.
entries.literal: He was appointed Minister of Writing and promoted Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 十年薨，詔遣兼大鴻臚持節監護喪事，贈車騎將軍、儀同三司。
entries.en: Year ten brought supervised obsequies and posthumous chariot-and-cavalry honors matching three-dukes rites.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he died; an edict dispatched concurrent Grand Herald with credentials to supervise funeral affairs and posthumously invested chariot-and-cavalry general with ceremonies equal to the Three Dukes.

entries.zh: 常山孝王衡，字子平，魏封德陽鄉侯。
entries.en: Sima Heng, styled Ziping, held Deyang village under Wei.
entries.literal: Prince Xiao of Changshan Heng courtesy Ziping was Deyang village marquis in Wei.

entries.zh: 進封汝陽子，為駙馬都尉。
entries.en: Promotion brought Runyang viscount and commandant for princess consorts.
entries.literal: He advanced to Viscount of Runyang and became Commandant Steadfast for imperial sons-in-law.

entries.zh: 武帝受禪，封常山王，邑三千七百九十戶。
entries.en: Sima Yan named him Changshan prince at 3,790 households.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Changshan with three thousand seven hundred ninety households.

entries.zh: 二年薨，無子，以安平世子邕第四子敦為嗣。
entries.en: Childless after two years Yong's fourth son Dun succeeded.
entries.literal: In the second year he died without sons; Yong heir Yong's fourth son Dun was appointed successor.

entries.zh: 沛順王景，字子文，魏樂安亭侯。
entries.en: Sima Jing, styled Ziwen, began as Leyang ting marquis.
entries.literal: Prince Shun of Pei Jing courtesy Ziwen was Leyang precinct marquis in Wei.

entries.zh: 曆諫議大夫。
entries.en: He served as grand counselor of remonstrance.
entries.literal: He successively held Grand Counselor.

entries.zh: 武帝受禪，封沛王，邑三千四百戶。
entries.en: Sima Yan invested Pei at 3,400 households.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Pei with three thousand four hundred households.

entries.zh: 立十一年，咸寧元年薨，子韜立。
entries.en: After holding the title for eleven years, he died in Xianning year one, and his son Tao succeeded.
entries.literal: After holding the title for eleven years, he died in Xianning year one, and his son Tao succeeded.

entries.zh: 彭城穆王權，字子輿，宣帝弟魏魯相東武城侯馗之子也。
entries.en: Sima Quan, King Mu of Pengcheng and styled Ziyu, was the son of Sima Kui, Marquis of Dongwucheng and governor of Lu under Wei, who was Sima Yi's younger brother.
entries.literal: Prince Mu of Pengcheng Quan courtesy Ziyu was son of Emperor Xuan's younger brother Wei Lu governor East Wucheng Marquis Kui.

entries.zh: 初襲封，拜冗從僕射。
entries.en: He opened as supernumerary chariot master.
entries.literal: At first inheriting the enfeoffment he was appointed Supernumerary Master of Chariots.

entries.zh: 武帝受禪，封彭城王，邑二千九百戶。
entries.en: Sima Yan made him Pengcheng prince at 2,900 households.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng with two thousand nine hundred households.

entries.zh: 出為北中郎將、都督鄴城守諸軍事。
entries.en: He commanded Ye's northern gentleman garrison.
entries.literal: He went out as General of the Northern Gentlemen supervising Ye city garrison affairs.

entries.zh: 泰始中入朝，賜袞冕之服。
entries.en: Mid-Taishi brought court investiture robes.
entries.literal: In Taishi mid-years he entered court and was granted robe and crown of state.

entries.zh: 咸甯元年薨，子元王植立。
entries.en: 275 death; Yuan prince Zhi followed.
entries.literal: In Xianning year one he died; son Prince Yuan Zhi succeeded.

entries.zh: 歷位後將軍，尋拜國子祭酒、太僕卿、侍中、尚書。
entries.en: His offices ran rear general, academy libationer, coach minister, palace attendant, and ministry.
entries.literal: He successively held Later General, soon appointed Libationer of the Imperial Academy, Minister of Coachmanship, palace attendant, and minister of writing.

entries.zh: 出為安東將軍、都督揚州諸軍事，代淮南王允鎮壽春，未發。
entries.en: Named east-pacifier for Yangzhou replacing Yun at Shouchun, he never took up post.
entries.literal: He was going out as General Who Pacifies the East supervising Yangzhou military affairs replacing Prince Huainan Yun at Shouchun but did not depart.

entries.zh: 或云植助允攻趙王倫，遂以憂薨。
entries.en: Tradition claims he aided Yun against Sima Lun and died of anxiety.
entries.literal: Some say Zhi assisted Yun in attacking Prince Zhao Lun and therefore died of grief.

entries.zh: 贈車騎將軍，增封萬五千戶。
entries.en: The court added posthumous chariot-and-cavalry honors and boosted his fief by fifteen thousand households.
entries.literal: He was posthumously invested chariot-and-cavalry general and his enfeoffment was increased by fifteen thousand households.

entries.zh: 子康王釋立，官至南中郎將、持節、平南將軍，分魯國蕃、薛二縣以益其國，心二萬三千戶。
entries.en: Prince Kang Sima Shi rose to southern gentleman-general with pacifying-south command, annexed Fan and Xue from Lu, and held twenty-three thousand households.
entries.literal: Son Prince Kang Shi succeeded; he reached Southern Gentlemen General, credential-bearing, Pacifying South General; partitioned Fan and Xue counties of Lu to enlarge his state; total twenty-three thousand households.

entries.zh: 薨，子雄立，坐奔蘇峻伏誅，更以釋子紘嗣。
entries.en: After his death Xiong inherited but died with Su Jun's rebellion; Hong, son of Shi, continued the line.
entries.literal: He died; son Xiong succeeded; Xiong was executed for fleeing to Su Jun; Shi's son Hong was changed to succeed.

entries.zh: 珪有美譽於世，而帝甚悼惜之。
entries.en: Celebrated publicly, he won uncommon imperial grief.
entries.literal: Gui had fine reputation in the world yet the emperor deeply mourned and cherished him.

entries.zh: 無子，詔以太原王輔子緝襲爵。
entries.en: Without issue Taiyuan prince Fu's son Ji inherited.
entries.literal: Having no son an edict ordered Prince Fu of Taiyuan's son Ji to inherit the noble rank.

entries.zh: 緝立五年，咸寧四年薨，諡曰哀。
entries.en: Ji had held the title for five years when he died in Xianning year four, receiving the posthumous epithet Ai.
entries.literal: Ji had held the title for five years when he died in Xianning year four, receiving the posthumous epithet Ai.

entries.zh: 無子，太康二年詔以太原王瑰世子顒子訟為緝後，封真定縣侯。
entries.en: Having no son, in Taikang year two an edict made Song, son of Yong, heir of the heir apparent of Prince Gui of Taiyuan, continue Ji's line and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Zhending County.
entries.literal: Having no son, in Taikang year two an edict made Song, son of Yong, heir of the heir apparent of Prince Gui of Taiyuan, continue Ji's line and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Zhending County.

entries.zh: 恭王俊字道度，出嗣高密王略，官至散騎常侍。
entries.en: Prince Gong Sima Jun, styled Daodu, continued Lue of Gaomi and rose to supernumerary cavalry attendant.
entries.literal: Prince Gong Jun courtesy Daodu went out to succeed Prince of Gaomi Lue and reached irregular cavalry attendant.

entries.zh: 薨，子敬王純之立，曆臨川內史、司農少府卿、太宰右長史。
entries.en: When he died, his son Chunzhi, Prince Jing, succeeded him. He successively served as administrator of Linchuan, minister of agriculture, minister of the privy treasury, and right chief clerk to the Grand Steward.
entries.literal: He died; his son Chunzhi, Prince Jing, succeeded him and successively held the offices of administrator of Linchuan, minister of agriculture, minister of the privy treasury, and right chief clerk to the Grand Steward.

entries.zh: 薨，子恢之立。
entries.en: He died, and his son Huizhi succeeded him.
entries.literal: He died; son Huizhi succeeded.

entries.zh: 義熙末，以給事中兼太尉，修謁洛陽園陵。
entries.en: Late in Yixi he doubled as grand commandant tending western tombs.
entries.literal: At the end of Yixi he as consultant concurrently grand commandant repaired and visited Luoyang mausolea.

entries.zh: 宋受禪，國除。
entries.en: Liu Song shuttered the fief.
entries.literal: When Song accepted the abdication the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 泰性廉靜，不近聲色。
entries.en: Chaste and retiring, he shunned entertainment and concubines.
entries.literal: Tai's nature was honest and quiet; he did not draw near music and women.

entries.zh: 雖為宰輔，食大國之租，服飾肴膳如布衣寒士。
entries.en: Despite ministerial income he dressed and ate like a poor scholar.
entries.literal: Though he was chief minister eating great-state rents his dress and food were like a poor commoner scholar.

entries.zh: 任真簡率，每朝會，不識者不知其王公也。
entries.en: At audience strangers mistook him for a common official.
entries.literal: Straightforward and plain at court assemblies strangers did not know he was a prince duke.

entries.zh: 事視恭謹，居喪哀戚，謙虛下物，為宗室儀錶。
entries.en: Filial in mourning and deferential, he set clan standard.
entries.literal: Serving kin he was respectful and cautious; in mourning grief-stricken; humble toward others—he was model for the imperial clan.

entries.zh: 當時諸王，惟泰及下邳王晃以節制見稱。
entries.en: Only Tai and Sima Huang won esteem for self-control.
entries.literal: Among princes of the time only Tai and Prince of Xiapi Huang were praised for restraint.

entries.zh: 雖並不能振施，其餘莫得比焉。
entries.en: Neither dispensed charity widely yet none surpassed their discipline.
entries.literal: Though neither could relieve distress broadly none others matched them.

entries.zh: 泰四子：越、騰、略、模。
entries.en: Four sons: Yue, Teng, Lue, Mo.
entries.literal: Tai had four sons: Yue, Teng, Lue, Mo.

entries.zh: 越自有傳。
entries.en: Yue appears elsewhere.
entries.literal: Yue has his own biography.

entries.zh: 騰出後叔父，弟略立。
entries.en: Teng was adopted out; Lue inherited.
entries.literal: Teng went out to succeed uncle; younger brother Lue succeeded.

entries.zh: 子孝王略
entries.en: Prince Xiao Sima Lue.
entries.literal: Son Prince Xiao Lue.

entries.zh: 高密文獻王泰
entries.en: Sima Tai, Prince Wenxian of Gaomi.
entries.literal: Prince Wenxian of Gaomi Tai.

entries.zh: 高密文獻王泰，字子舒，彭城穆王權之弟，魏陽亭侯，補陽翟令，遷扶風太守。
entries.en: Sima Tai, styled Zishu, was Sima Quan's brother—Yang ting marquis, Yangdi magistrate, Fufeng governor.
entries.literal: Prince Wenxian of Gaomi Tai courtesy Zishu was younger brother of Prince Mu of Pengcheng Quan, Marquis of Yang precinct in Wei; supplied Yangdi magistrate; promoted governor of Fufeng.

entries.zh: 武帝受禪，封隴西王，邑三千二百戶，拜遊擊將軍。
entries.en: Sima Yan made him Longxi prince at 3,200 households with roving-strike command.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Longxi with three thousand two hundred households and appointed roving-strike general.

entries.zh: 出為兗州刺史，加鷹揚將軍。
entries.en: He shepherded Yan with hawk-banner general rank.
entries.literal: He went out as Inspector of Yan Province with additional general Who Displays Hawk banner.

entries.zh: 遷使持節、都督甯益二州諸軍事、安西將軍，領益州刺史，稱疾不行。
entries.en: Ning-Yi pacifying-west orders went unfulfilled on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: He was promoted credential-bearing supervisor of Ning and Yi military affairs and Pacifying West General concurrent Yi Inspector but pleaded illness and did not go.

entries.zh: 轉安北將軍，代兄權督鄴城守事。
entries.en: He succeeded brother Quan as pacifying-north chief at Ye.
entries.literal: He transferred to Pacifying North General replacing elder brother Quan supervising Ye garrison.

entries.zh: 安西將軍、都督關中事。
entries.en: He also held pacifying-west charge over Guanzhong.
entries.literal: Pacifying West General supervising Guanzhong affairs.

entries.zh: 太康初，入為散騎常侍、前將軍，領鄴城門校尉，以疾去官。
entries.en: Early Taikang brought palace posts and Ye gate command until illness retired him.
entries.literal: Early Taikang he entered as irregular cavalry attendant and former general concurrent colonel of Ye gates but resigned for illness.

entries.zh: 後代下邳王晃為尚書左僕射。
entries.en: He later succeeded Sima Huang as left vice director.
entries.literal: Later he replaced Prince of Xiapi Huang as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 出為鎮西將軍，領護西戎校尉、假節，代扶風王駿都督關中軍事，以疾還京師。
entries.en: He was sent out as General Who Guards the West, concurrently Colonel Protector of the Western Rong and Bearer of the Staff, replacing Prince Jun of Fufeng as commander of Guanzhong military affairs, but returned to the capital because of illness.
entries.literal: He went out as Guarding West General concurrent colonel of western tribes with credentials replacing Prince of Fufeng Jun supervising Guanzhong military affairs but returned to capital for illness.

entries.zh: 永熙初，代石鑒為司空，尋領太子太保。
entries.en: Yongxi opened with minister of works and heir-apparent junior tutor posts.
entries.literal: Early Yongxi he replaced Shi Jian as Minister of Works and soon concurrent junior tutor to heir apparent.

entries.zh: 及楊駿誅，泰領駿營，加侍中，給步兵二千五百人，騎五百匹。
entries.en: Jun's purge handed Tai the camp plus two thousand five hundred foot and five hundred horse.
entries.literal: When Yang Jun was executed Tai took over Jun's camp with additional palace attendant, two thousand five hundred infantry, and five hundred cavalry granted.

entries.zh: 泰固辭，乃給千兵百騎。
entries.en: He bargained the guard down to one thousand foot and one hundred horse.
entries.literal: Tai firmly declined so only one thousand troops and one hundred cavalry were given.

entries.zh: 楚王瑋之被收，泰嚴兵將救之，祭酒丁綏諫曰：「公為宰相，不可輕動。
entries.en: When Prince of Chu Wei was seized Tai drew up troops intending to rescue him; Libationer Ding Sui remonstrated saying, 'You are chief minister—you cannot move rashly.
entries.literal: When Prince of Chu Wei was seized Tai drew up troops intending to rescue him; Libationer Ding Sui remonstrated saying, 'You are chief minister—you cannot move rashly.

entries.zh: 且夜中倉卒，宜遣人參審定問。」
entries.en: Moreover midnight crisis requires sending men to investigate clearly.'
entries.literal: Moreover midnight crisis requires sending men to investigate clearly.'

entries.zh: 泰從之。
entries.en: Tai agreed.
entries.literal: Tai followed this.

entries.zh: 瑋既誅，乃以泰錄尚書事，遷太尉，守尚書令，改封高密王，邑萬戶。
entries.en: Wei's fall made Tai acting minister chief, then grand commandant with Gaomi at ten thousand households.
entries.literal: After Wei was executed Tai was put in charge of Ministry records, promoted Grand Commandant while holding Minister Director, changed enfeoffment to Prince of Gaomi with ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 元康九年薨，追贈太傅。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Yuankang, Posthumous grand mentor followed his death.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Yuankang, he died and was posthumously invested Grand Mentor.

entries.zh: 孝王略，字元簡，孝敬慈順，小心下士，少有父風。
entries.en: Sima Lue, styled Yuanjian, echoed his father's modest courtesy.
entries.literal: Prince Xiao Lue courtesy Yuanjian was respectful, mild, and obedient, humble toward scholars, having somewhat his father's manner.

entries.zh: 元康初，湣懷太子在東宮，選大臣子弟有名稱者以為賓友，略與華恆等並侍左右。
entries.en: Yuankang saw Lue among Minhuai's cultivated companions with Hua Heng.
entries.literal: Early Yuankang Crown Prince Minhuai was in the eastern palace and chose sons of eminent ministers with reputation as guests and friends; Lue together with Hua Heng and others attended left and right.

entries.zh: 曆散騎黃門侍郎、散騎常侍、秘書監，出為安南將軍、持節、都督沔南諸軍事，遷安北將軍、都督青州諸軍事。
entries.en: He successively served as Yellow-Gate Gentleman Attendant, Regular Palace Attendant, and Director of the Palace Library; then he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the South, Bearer of the Staff, and commander of the armies south of the Mian, before being promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and commander of Qing Province military affairs.
entries.literal: He successively held irregular cavalry yellow-gate gentleman, irregular cavalry attendant, palace library supervisor; went out Pacifying South General credential-bearing supervising Hannan military affairs; promoted Pacifying North General supervising Qing province military affairs.

entries.zh: 略逼青州刺史程牧，牧避之，略自領州。
entries.en: He bullied Cheng Mu aside and seized Qingzhou himself.
entries.literal: Lue pressured Qing Inspector Cheng Mu until Mu yielded and Lue personally headed the province.

entries.zh: 永興初，㡉令劉根起兵東萊，誑惑百姓，眾以萬數，攻略於臨淄，略不能距，走保聊城。
entries.en: Yongxing opened with Liu Gen's Donglai rising that drove Lue from Linzi to Liaocheng.
entries.literal: Early Yongxing Magistrate Liu Gen of Yi county raised troops in Donglai deluding commoners tens of thousands strong raiding Lue at Linzi; Lue could not resist and fled defending Liaocheng.

entries.zh: 懷帝即位，遷使持節、都督荊州諸軍事、征南大將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: Huai made him credential-bearing Jing commander with three-dukes parity staff.
entries.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended Lue was promoted credential-bearing supervisor of Jing military affairs, southern expedition grand marshal with independent headquarters matching Three Lords.

entries.zh: 京兆流人王逌與叟人郝洛聚眾數千，屯于冠軍。
entries.en: Wang You, a displaced person from Jingzhao, and Hao Luo of the Sou people gathered several thousand followers and encamped at Guanjun.
entries.literal: Wang You, a displaced person from Jingzhao, and Hao Luo of the Sou people gathered several thousand followers and encamped at Guanjun.

entries.zh: 略遣參軍崔曠率將軍皮初、張洛等討逌，為逌所譎，戰敗。
entries.en: Lue sent his military adviser Cui Kuang to lead the generals Pi Chu, Zhang Luo, and others against You, but You deceived them and they were defeated in battle.
entries.literal: Lue sent his military adviser Cui Kuang to lead the generals Pi Chu, Zhang Luo, and others against You, but You deceived them and they were defeated in battle.

entries.zh: 略更遣左司馬曹攄統曠等進逼逌。
entries.en: Lue then sent Left Sima Cao Shu to lead Kuang and the others in advancing against You.
entries.literal: Lue then sent Left Sima Cao Shu to lead Kuang and the others in advancing against You.

entries.zh: 將大戰，曠在後密自退走，攄軍無繼，戰敗，死之。
entries.en: As they were about to fight a major battle, Kuang, who was in the rear, secretly withdrew; Shu's army was left without support, was defeated, and Shu died in the fighting.
entries.literal: As they were about to fight a major battle, Kuang, who was in the rear, secretly withdrew; Shu's army was left without support, was defeated, and Shu died in the fighting.

entries.zh: 略乃赦曠罪，復遣部將韓松又督曠攻逌，逌降。
entries.en: Lue then pardoned Kuang's offense and again sent his subordinate Han Song to lead Kuang against Wang You, who surrendered.
entries.literal: Lue then pardoned Kuang's offense and again sent his subordinate general Han Song to command Kuang in attacking You; You surrendered.

entries.zh: 尋進開府，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: Soon he was advanced and allowed to establish his own office, with the additional appointment of Regular Mounted Attendant.
entries.literal: Soon he was advanced and allowed to establish his own office, with the additional appointment of Regular Mounted Attendant.

entries.zh: 永嘉三年薨，追贈侍中、太尉，子據立。
entries.en: He died in the third year of Yongjia and was posthumously granted the offices of Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant; his son Ju succeeded him.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongjia, he died and was posthumously granted the offices of Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant; his son Ju succeeded him.

entries.zh: 薨，無子，以彭城康王子紘為嗣。
entries.en: Childless, he passed to Hong from Pengcheng's Kang line.
entries.literal: He died without sons; Prince Kang of Pengcheng's son Hong was appointed successor.

entries.zh: 其後紘歸本宗，立紘子俊以奉其祀。
entries.en: Hong reverted to his birth house; Jun kept Lue's line alive.
entries.literal: Later Hong returned to root lineage; Hong's son Jun was established to maintain his sacrifices.

entries.zh: 略兄新蔡武哀王騰
entries.en: Lue's elder brother Sima Teng, Prince Wuai of Xincai.
entries.literal: Lue's elder brother Prince Wuai of Xincai Teng.

entries.zh: 略弟南陽王模
entries.en: Sima Mo, Prince of Nanyang—Lue's brother.
entries.literal: Younger brother of Lue Mo Prince of Nanyang.

entries.zh: 新蔡武哀王騰，字元邁，少拜冗從僕射，封東嬴公，曆南陽、魏郡太守，所在稱職，徵為宗正，遷太常，轉持節、寧北將軍、都督并州諸軍事、并州刺史。
entries.en: Sima Teng, Prince Wuai of Xincai, courtesy name Yuanmai, was appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant when young and enfeoffed as Duke of Dongying. He served successively as governor of Nanyang and Wei Commandery, was praised as competent wherever he served, was summoned as Director of the Imperial Clan, promoted to Minister of Ceremonies, and then transferred as Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, commander of all military affairs in Bing Province, and inspector of Bing Province.
entries.literal: Prince Wuai of Xincai Teng courtesy Yuanmai in youth was appointed supernumerary chariot master and enfeoffed Duke of Dongying; successively governor of Nanyang and Wei commandery where he was praised competent; summoned Grand Director of the Imperial Clan; promoted Minister of Ceremonies; transferred credential-bearing Pacifying North General supervising Bing military affairs and Bing Inspector.

entries.zh: 惠帝討成都王穎，六軍敗績。
entries.en: Hui's expedition against Sima Ying collapsed.
entries.literal: When Emperor Hui campaigned against Prince of Chengdu Ying the six armies were routed.

entries.zh: 騰與安北將軍王浚共殺穎所署幽州刺史和演，率眾討穎。
entries.en: Teng joined Wang Jun executing He Yan then marched on Ying.
entries.literal: Teng together with Pacifying North General Wang Jun jointly killed Inspector of You appointed by Ying—He Yan—and led hosts against Ying.

entries.zh: 穎遣北中郎將王斌距戰，浚率鮮卑騎擊斌，騰為後系，大破之。
entries.en: Xianbei cavalry under Wang Jun shattered Wang Bin while Teng held the rear.
entries.literal: Ying dispatched Northern Gentlemen General Wang Bin to resist; Jun led Xianbei horse striking Bin while Teng covered the rear routing them utterly.

entries.zh: 穎懼，挾帝歸洛陽，進騰位安北將軍。
entries.en: Ying was afraid and took Emperor Hui back to Luoyang; Teng was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.
entries.literal: Ying feared and escorted the emperor back to Luoyang; Teng was advanced Pacifying North General.

entries.zh: 永嘉初，遷車騎將軍，都督鄴城守諸軍事，鎮鄴。
entries.en: Yongjia named him chariot-and-cavalry chief at Ye.
entries.literal: Early Yongjia he was promoted chariot-and-cavalry general supervising Ye garrison stationed at Ye.

entries.zh: 又以迎駕之勳，改封新蔡王。
entries.en: Welcoming the throne earned the Xincai princedom.
entries.literal: Again for merit welcoming the imperial carriage his enfeoffment was changed Prince of Xincai.

entries.zh: 初，騰發并州，次於真定。
entries.en: Leaving Bing he paused at Zhending.
entries.literal: At first when Teng set out from Bing Province he halted at Zhending.

entries.zh: 值大雪，平地數尺，營門前方數丈雪融不積，騰怪而掘之，得玉馬，高尺許，表獻之。
entries.en: Snow melted oddly at his gate; digging revealed a jade horse sent to court.
entries.literal: It happened there was great snow several chi deep on level ground; before the camp gate several zhang of ground showed melted snow not accumulating; Teng wondered and dug obtaining a jade horse about a chi high which he memorialized and presented.

entries.zh: 其後公師籓與平陽人汲桑等為群盜，起於清河鄃縣，眾千餘人，寇頓丘，以葬成都王穎為辭，載穎主而行，與張泓故將李豐等將攻鄴。
entries.en: Ji Sang's gang marched under Ying's tablet to threaten Ye.
entries.literal: Later duke-lord Shi Fan with Pingyang men Ji Sang and others formed bandit gangs rising in Shu county of Qinghe over one thousand strong raiding Dunqiu using burying Prince of Chengdu Ying as pretext loading Ying's spirit tablet marching with Zhang Hong's old general Li Feng intending to attack Ye.

entries.zh: 騰曰：「孤在并州七年，胡圍城不能克。
entries.en: Teng said, 'I was at Bing seven years and barbarians besieging the city could not overcome it.
entries.literal: Teng said, 'I was at Bing seven years and barbarians besieging the city could not overcome it.

entries.zh: 汲桑小賊，何足憂也。」
entries.en: Ji Sang petty bandits—what worth worry.'
entries.literal: Ji Sang petty bandits—what worth worry.'

entries.zh: 及豐等至，騰不能守，率輕騎而走，為豐所害。
entries.en: The raid overwhelmed him; fleeing lightly armed he fell to Feng.
entries.literal: When Feng and others arrived Teng could not defend and led light horse fleeing and was killed by Feng.

entries.zh: 四子：虞、矯、紹、確。
entries.en: Four sons survived: Yu, Jiao, Shao, Que.
entries.literal: Four sons: Yu, Jiao, Shao, Que.
